properties.name: MainLoopThreadIsBackground
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether there is a GLib main-loop thread and it is a background thread. Pins the fix for issue #1448: a foreground loop thread blocks process exit until DestroyMainLoop quits it, and an AppDomain.ProcessExit teardown can never do that because ProcessExit runs only after every foreground thread has finished. A dead thread answers false rather than throwing. Reading IsBackground on a thread that has already exited raises ThreadStateException, and the field can outlive the thread - any quit of the loop outside DestroyMainLoop ends the thread and leaves the field set. An IsAlive test in front would not close that window: MainLoopSync serialises the writers of the field, not the loop thread's own termination, so the thread can still die between the two reads. One read, and the exception is the answer.

properties.name: CanWaitForMainLoopDispatch
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the caller may block waiting for something the GLib main loop has to dispatch to it.

properties.name: DefaultThreshold
properties.summary: The GStreamer default threshold every engine applies: DebugLevel, raised from errors to warnings once telemetry collects GStreamer's warnings - unless the customer chose another level.

methods.name: #cctor
methods.summary: Initializes static members of the GstInitializer class.

methods.name: DestroyMainLoop
methods.summary: Stops the GLib main loop and waits for its thread to exit.
methods.remarks: The loop thread is a background thread (see Init), so it cannot hold the process open by itself. What it does hold is the default main context: this method has to have actually brought the thread down — not merely asked it to stop — before gst_deinit runs, or the deinit tears GStreamer out from under a thread still dispatching. Two properties of GLib dictate the shape here (glib 2.74.4, gmain.c): g_main_loop_run sets is_running = TRUE on entry, so a quit issued before the thread got there is lost. Quitting once and trusting IsRunning therefore leaves the thread in the loop forever, and the process never exits. Quit is retried until the thread is out.g_main_loop_run only takes its own reference AFTER it is entered, so unreffing the loop while the thread is still on its way in can free it under that thread. The unref (MainLoop.Dispose) therefore happens only once the thread has confirmed its exit.

methods.name: EnableTelemetryWarnings
methods.summary: Starts collecting GStreamer's warnings and errors as telemetry breadcrumbs for the rest of the process, once an engine whose telemetry is on starts under a debugger. Every GStreamer engine calls it at start.

methods.name: EnsureLogFunctionAttached
methods.summary: Installs this domain's GStreamer debug log callback unless it is already attached. Used by the full ContextX) path, its IsInitialized fast path, and the InitSDK fast path in VisioForgeX - which a host reaches after StopMainLoop detached the callback mid-session without clearing the init state.

methods.name: DetachLogFunction
methods.summary: Detaches the GStreamer debug log callback registered by ContextX). MUST be called from the still-live managed domain on a Unity reload (via VisioForgeX.StopMainLoop on beforeAssemblyReload): the native GstDebug holds a function pointer + user_data tied to this domain, and after the domain unloads there is no managed state left to unregister it, so the entry would dangle and crash when the next GST message (default threshold = Error) fires. Both RemoveLogFunction flavors unregister by user_data from their registration registries, scoped to what this assembly added (the per-instance-wrapper path they replaced could not match by function pointer at all). A later Init in the SAME domain re-attaches through EnsureLogFunctionAttached, including via the InitSDK fast path.

methods.name: ResetState
methods.summary: Resets managed initialization bookkeeping after SDK teardown.

methods.name: SamePath
methods.summary: Compares two directory paths for equality, ignoring case and a trailing separator.

methods.name: IsMirrored
methods.summary: Whether a top-level file of <app>\<arch> is copied into the shared cache.

methods.name: IsKeyed
methods.summary: Whether a mirrored file is of a type the GStreamer packages deploy - a library, the certificate bundle, OpenCV's cascades - and so one the cache key is taken over: one key means one set of these files. A log written next to the natives at run time does not fork the key.

methods.name: IsOtherRedistFile
methods.summary: Whether a file of <app>\<arch> belongs to a redist other than GStreamer's, and so stays out of the shared cache (#3376). The FFMPEG redist's FFmpeg libraries are not matched: they are named on Libav's scheme (avcodec-NN.dll), so a name excluded today could be Libav's own after its next FFmpeg update.

methods.name: MirrorNativeFolder
methods.summary: Copies the application's native folder into the shared plugin cache the SDK loads from.
methods.remarks: A file is copied when the destination is missing or differs in either length or last-write time. Size alone is not enough: a rebuilt plugin of the same size was never refreshed, and the cached build kept loading (issue #1289). File.Copy carries the source's last-write time over, so the comparison is stable across runs. Files the source no longer has are left in place. GStreamer keys its registry on each plugin's absolute path, so this one canonical folder is what lets every application that deploys the same natives share a warm registry rather than each paying a full cold scan. The folder is keyed to the SDK version and to every library the mirror copies, so an application with a different native set gets a folder of its own and cannot add to this one. Two exceptions. gstaravis.dll, retired from the GenICam redist (#2307), is never mirrored and is removed from the cache, because its own Aravis breaks the SDK's GenICam. And the VC++ runtime () is never mirrored: Redist.Shared versions it apart from the key, and it is loaded from the application's own folder (#3337). Neither are the files of the other redists that share <app>\<arch> - VLC, Shared, MP4, LAV, XIPH and every DirectShow filter: the cache is first on PATH, so a copy here would win over the application's own, and libVLC's copy loads without its plugins\ (#3376). A copy of one an earlier build left in the SDK's own cache is removed when the application ships that file. Nothing is deleted from a folder the application chose: one holding a file of another redist, gstaravis.dll or a library the application does not ship is reported and not used, and the natives load in place. Other files in the destination are left alone.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.summary: The cache folder, created when missing.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: The context used to report a file that could not be copied.

parameters.name: ownsDestination
parameters.summary: false when destination is a folder the application chose rather than the SDK's own cache: nothing in it is deleted, and a file there that must not load is reported and makes it unusable, before anything is copied.

methods.returns: false when destination cannot be used: it cannot be created; it could not be probed, so it was left alone, and it does not hold what the application deployed; a library could not be copied into it, or a file that must not load could not be removed from it; or it is a folder the application chose and holds a file that must not load. The natives then load in place.

methods.name: CopyAndSwap
methods.summary: Copies one file into the cache through its temporary and swaps it over the destination, so a concurrent reader sees either the previous complete library or the new one, never a partial write.

methods.name: IsSameFolder
methods.summary: Whether destination is source under another name - a junction, a symbolic link, an 8.3, UNC or \\?\ alias - which a path comparison cannot tell. Mirroring onto itself would delete the application's own files of the other redists (#3376). null when the probe cannot be written, with the reason in error.

methods.name: ClearOwnTemporaries
methods.summary: Deletes temporaries in the cache that carry this process's id but were left by an earlier process that held the same id - a refresh killed between its copy and its swap.
methods.remarks: This process owns the id right now, so nothing alive can be writing them; and it is the whole of the collection story, which is why it can be this small. Temporaries left under some OTHER id are deliberately not touched: telling an abandoned one from a copy in flight needs a liveness rule, and a wrong answer there deletes a file another process is about to swap in. One such file survives until an id is reused, or forever if the application that deployed that plugin is uninstalled.

methods.name: MarkCacheInUse
methods.summary: Declares that this process is using a cache folder, so String) leaves it alone.
methods.remarks: Two signals, because a timestamp alone is not enough. The folder is stamped, which tells a later prune that something started here recently - its own timestamp never moves otherwise, since it only changes when its direct children do. And a marker file is opened and held for the life of the process, which is what protects a host that has been running for longer than UnusedCacheLifetime: its start is 45 days old and its stamp with it, but it is very much alive, and deleting its cache would take away every plugin it has not lazily loaded yet.

methods.name: OpenCacheInUseMarker
methods.summary: Opens this process's handle on the in-use marker of a version folder.
methods.remarks: FileShare.ReadWrite so that EVERY process using this folder can hold the marker at once - it is not a lock. Sharing Read alone would let only the first process on the machine take it and leave every later one unprotected, which is precisely the case the marker exists for. Delete is deliberately not shared: that is what makes String) fail while a holder is alive.

methods.name: IsCacheInUse
methods.summary: Whether some process still holds CacheInUseMarker in this version folder open.

methods.name: PruneUnusedCaches
methods.summary: Removes the cache folders of other deployments that have not been used for UnusedCacheLifetime.
methods.remarks: Only folders whose name starts with a version this scheme produces are considered. That deliberately spares the pre-#1289 unversioned x64 and x86 folders: applications built on an already-shipped SDK still load from those, and nothing stamps them - the old code wrote a file only when it was missing or a different size, and overwriting a file does not move its parent directory's timestamp, so a cache in daily use would look untouched for years. Deleting one out from under a running application removes every plugin it has not loaded yet.

parameters.name: cacheFolder
parameters.summary: The <version>\<arch> folder in use, which is kept.

methods.name: IsVersionedCacheFolder
methods.summary: Whether a child of the cache root was created by the versioned scheme, and is therefore ours to remove once unused. The name is <version> or <version>-<native-stamp>; anything else - notably the legacy x64 and x86 folders - is left alone.

methods.name: PrependToPath
methods.summary: Moves folder to the front of a search path, dropping any other copy of it: it must win over whatever else is on the path, and an Init retried after a failure must not grow the path.

classes.name: AppSrcTimestamp
classes.summary: Guards appsrc's do-timestamp against the moment it cannot stamp a buffer right.

methods.name: CannotStampYet
methods.summary: Whether an untimed buffer must be dropped because appsrc's do-timestamp cannot stamp it right yet.
methods.remarks: With do-timestamp, appsrc stamps an untimed buffer on the pushing thread as clock time minus its own base_time. The pipeline hands out its clock before that base_time reaches the appsrc, so a push in between is stamped with the clock's absolute time - days past the running time - and a syncing sink waits on that buffer for good: one buffer, then a silent stream (#2926, #2935). The base_time is set before the appsrc reaches PLAYING, so from then on the stamp is right. A live source therefore drops everything before PLAYING. A non-live one must keep its pushes to preroll, so it drops only once the clock is set, which leaves the moment between this check and appsrc's own.

parameters.name: appSrc
parameters.summary: The appsrc the buffer is about to be pushed to.

parameters.name: doTimestamp
parameters.summary: Whether the appsrc has do-timestamp set.

methods.returns: true if an untimed buffer must not be pushed now.

classes.name: BusMessageHelper
classes.summary: Reads a bus message's source without creating a managed wrapper for it.
classes.remarks: Gst.Message.Src runs GLib.Object.GetObject on the transfer-none source pointer, which takes a native reference and hands it to a ToggleRef. On a handler that runs for every element in the pipeline — state-changed, error, warning — that is an ownership claim over objects this SDK never created, given back much later on a ThreadPool worker. An element held past its owner's teardown is then finalized afterwards, and any library that registered a GWeakNotify closing over that owner dereferences freed memory: bugs.md #68, where a GES per-track gapfilter crashed the render pipeline. Every question those handlers actually ask — "did this come from the pipeline?", "what is the element called?" — is answerable from the raw pointer.

methods.name: GetSrcHandle
methods.summary: Reads the message's raw GstObject* source, creating no wrapper.
methods.returns: The raw source pointer, or Zero.

methods.name: SrcIs
methods.summary: Determines whether the message came from target.
methods.remarks: A NULL source is rejected before the comparison rather than compared. A disposed wrapper also reports Zero, so a plain equality test would answer "yes, from the pipeline" for a source-less message once the pipeline had been torn down — and the negated form of the same test would answer "no, keep going". Both are wrong.

parameters.name: target
parameters.summary: The expected sender, usually the pipeline. May be null.

methods.returns: true only when both are live and identical.

methods.name: GetSrcName
methods.summary: Reads the name of the message's source, creating no wrapper.

parameters.name: fallback
parameters.summary: Returned when there is no source or it has no name.

methods.returns: The source's name, or fallback.

methods.name: GetSrcElementHandle
methods.summary: Returns the native handle of the element that posted msg: the message source itself when it is an element, otherwise the parent element of the pad that posted it. Zero when there is neither.
methods.remarks: The caller owns one reference on the returned element on both paths: an element source is reffed here, a pad source comes from gst_pad_get_parent_element which is transfer-full. The pipeline records the handle for the whole session so a failed source can be skipped at stop time, and that reference is what keeps the element alive - and its native address unrecyclable by a later allocation - while the recorded set is still consulted. ClearErrorSrcHandles is the single place the reference is given back; a transient caller must unref the result itself.
methods.returns: The element's pointer, or Zero.

methods.name: GetSrcElementName
methods.summary: Reads the name of the message's source, but only when that source is an element.
methods.remarks: For handlers that used to write message.Src as Element and return early on null. A pad or a bus can post a message too, and matching such a name against a block's element name would be meaningless rather than merely useless.
methods.returns: The element's name, or null when the source is absent or not an element.

methods.name: GetSrcFactoryName
methods.summary: Reads the factory name of the message's source, creating no wrapper.
methods.returns: The factory name, or null when the source is not an element with a factory.

methods.name: ErrorReason
methods.summary: Joins an error message with the element's own reason from the debug string: the first line after the "file(line): function (): /element/path:" line GST_ELEMENT_ERROR puts first, or, in a debug string an element posted without that line, its first non-blank line. A udpsrc bind failure, for one, says only "Could not get/set settings from/on resource" in the message and "bind failed: ..." in the debug.

parameters.name: debug
parameters.summary: The error's debug string, or null.

methods.returns: The message, followed by the element's reason when it has one, credentials masked; null when neither exists.

methods.name: StartsWithReason
methods.summary: Tells whether a reason is another one, or that one continued: with a parenthesis ("Not Found (404), URL: ...", the shape String) joins in), a colon, comma or period after it. "Could not open resource for writing" does not continue "Could not open resource": it is a different failure.

parameters.name: start
parameters.summary: The reason it may start with.

methods.returns: true when reason is start or continues it.

methods.name: GetObjectName
methods.summary: Reads a GstObject's name from its raw pointer.
methods.returns: The name, or null.

methods.name: GST_IS_ELEMENT
methods.summary: The managed spelling of the GST_IS_ELEMENT macro, on a raw pointer.
methods.returns: true when the instance is a GstElement or a subclass of one.

methods.name: ClockTimeToTimeSpan
methods.summary: Reads a GST_TYPE_CLOCK_TIME (guint64 nanoseconds) field from a structure and converts it to a TimeSpan. Returns null when the field is absent or carries GST_CLOCK_TIME_NONE.
methods.returns: The time, or null.

methods.name: NanosecondsToTimeSpan
methods.summary: Converts GStreamer nanoseconds to a TimeSpan, rounded to the nearest tick. Not TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds: .NET Framework rounds that to whole milliseconds.
methods.returns: The time.

classes.name: CairoDrawWatcher
classes.summary: Connects a cairooverlay element's draw signal to managed code, in whichever shape the current runtime can actually call back into.
classes.remarks: Every consumer used to do this the same way: build a delegate over an instance method and hand it to g_signal_connect. That cannot work on a full-AOT runtime. Mono's AOT compiler cannot generate a native-to-managed thunk at run time, so the first emission of the signal faults, and [MonoPInvokeCallback] cannot rescue it because the attribute requires a static method. IL2CPP has the same requirement. So the callback here is always a static thunk, with the owner reached through a passed as user data. iOS gets [UnmanagedCallersOnly] function pointers, Unity gets [AOT.MonoPInvokeCallback] on a rooted static delegate, and JIT targets use the same rooted delegate without the marker.

constructors.summary: Connects to element's draw signal.

parameters.summary: Invoked on a GStreamer streaming thread for each emission.

parameters.name: context

classes.name: CapsHelper
classes.summary: Provides GStreamer capabilities (caps) manipulation and conversion utilities for media format handling. This internal static helper class handles caps type detection, media format conversions, and caps construction from video/audio information structures. Essential for managing media format negotiations and MediaBlocks pipeline pad type mappings in the GStreamer framework.

methods.name: SetCapsFromString
methods.summary: Sets the caps of an appsrc from a caps string. gst_app_src_set_caps takes its own reference, so the parsed caps are released here.

methods.name: CapsTypeFromString
methods.summary: Caps type from string.
methods.returns: CapsType.

methods.name: SetValueOwned
methods.summary: Sets one caps field and releases the value.
methods.remarks: gst_caps_set_value copies the GValue, so the caller's copy has to be unset or whatever its GType owns - a string's strdup, a boxed copy, a mini-object reference - is leaked. The name deliberately differs from SetValue: an extension method never wins against an instance method of the same name, so a same-named wrapper would silently never be called. Value) is the same contract for element properties. GitHub issue #954. Never hand it a value that came out of GetValue or GetProperty. Those return a borrowed GValue copied bytewise out of the owner's own storage, so unsetting it frees the field under its owner. Build the value here, or dispose it where it was read.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: The value. Owned by this method - it is released before returning.

methods.name: SetValueOwned
methods.summary: Sets one structure field and releases the value.
methods.remarks: gst_structure_set_value copies the GValue exactly as Value) describes, including its warning about values read back out of a structure or an object. GitHub issue #954.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: The value. Owned by this method - it is released before returning.

methods.name: IsVideoCaps
methods.summary: Whether a demuxer pad carries a video stream. Demuxers expose MJPEG as image/jpeg (avidemux, matroskademux, qtdemux) and JPEG 2000 as image/x-j2c / image/x-jpc, so video/ alone parks those streams (issue #2968).

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The caps structure name, e.g. image/jpeg.

methods.returns: true if the caps carry video.

methods.name: IsJpeg2000Caps
methods.summary: Whether caps carry JPEG 2000 (image/x-jpc, which also matches image/x-jpc-striped, image/x-j2c or image/jp2). The decoder blocks put jpeg2000parse in front of such a stream: openjpegdec takes J2C/JPC only with the sampling field the parser adds and demuxers do not set, and the parser also turns JP2 into J2C (issue #3113).
methods.returns: true if the caps carry JPEG 2000.

methods.name: IsSubtitleCaps
methods.summary: Whether a caps structure name carries subtitles or captions. Shared by the demuxer wrappers and the media info readers, so the families stay in one place: copies of this rule had drifted apart, and a family a copy did not know about was discarded to a null sink even when the caller had asked for subtitles (issue #1387). Subtitle families a plain decodebin cannot hand on are narrowed further by String), which DemuxerSource and DemuxerSourceBlock size their subtitle outputs by (issue #1414).
methods.remarks: Covers plain timed text (text/, subtitle/), DVD/DVB subpictures (subpicture/), CEA-608/708 closed captions carried as their own track (closedcaption/), the Matroska subtitle codecs (application/x-ass, application/x-ssa, application/x-usf), WebVTT (application/x-subtitle-vtt), TTML (application/ttml+xml) and DVB teletext (application/x-teletext).

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The caps structure name, e.g. closedcaption/x-cea-608.

methods.returns: true if the caps carry subtitles or captions.

methods.name: IsDecodableSubtitleCaps
methods.summary: Whether a subtitle stream is one a plain decodebin can hand on. This is the rule DemuxerSource sizes its subtitle decodebins by, the rule its pad router feeds them by, and the rule DemuxerSourceBlock publishes subtitle output pads by - all three have to agree, or a pad is published that nothing ever feeds (issue #1414).
methods.remarks: Deliberately narrower than String). The other families have no decoder a plain decodebin can auto-plug: for subpicture/x-dvb the shipped plugins carry dvbsubenc and dvbsuboverlay only, and neither is a decoder. Linking such a pad into a decodebin posts GST_STREAM_ERROR_CODEC_NOT_FOUND and takes the whole pipeline down, where parking it loses only that one stream - the finding that reverted PR #1405 round 1.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The caps structure name, e.g. text/x-raw.

methods.returns: true if the stream can be handed on by a plain decodebin.

methods.name: IsRawCaptionCaps
methods.summary: Whether a caps structure name carries a caption payload no subtitle consumer can render as it stands - CEA-608/708 closed captions and DVB teletext, which are binary service data rather than text.
methods.remarks: A subset of String), used to rank a stream when a block has a single subtitle slot: these families were parked before issue #1387 routed them, so a block that can carry only one subtitle stream gives the slot to a text-shaped one first and takes these only when it is still free. Without the ranking a caption track announced ahead of a tx3g track would take a slot the subtitles used to get.
methods.returns: true if the caps carry a raw caption or teletext payload.

methods.name: IsRawCaptionPad
methods.summary: String) for a pad, reading and releasing its caps.

parameters.name: pad
parameters.summary: The pad to inspect. A null pad reads as not a caption pad.

methods.returns: true if the pad carries a raw caption or teletext payload.

methods.name: IsMetadataCaps
methods.summary: Whether a caps structure name carries a metadata stream. Companion to String); call it only after that one, so a family belonging to both resolves to subtitles.
methods.remarks: Covers KLV and the other meta/ types an MPEG-TS carries, and the timed XML track an ONVIF recorder writes into MP4 (application/x-onvif-metadata) - which used to be discarded even with renderMetadata: true (issue #1387).

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The caps structure name, e.g. meta/x-klv.

methods.returns: true if the caps carry metadata.

classes.name: DeepElementAddedWatcher
classes.summary: Watches a bin's deep-element-added signal through a raw native callback and hands the caller a managed wrapper only for the elements produced by one named element factory.
classes.remarks: The managed DeepElementAdded event cannot be used for this. GLib's signal marshaller converts every GValue parameter into a managed object before the handler runs (SignalClosure.MarshalCallback), and wrapping a GObject takes a reference on it, so a subscription on a whole pipeline claims ownership of EVERY element added anywhere in the graph. Those references are released much later, off a ThreadPool worker, which lets an element outlive the owner a library expects it to die with: GES registers a GWeakNotify on its per-track gapfilter whose callback dereferences the already-freed GESTrack, and the render pipeline crashes (bugs.md #68). Matching on the raw pointer creates no wrapper at all.

constructors.name: DeepElementAddedWatcher
constructors.summary: Connects the watcher to bin, matching one element factory by name.

parameters.name: bin
parameters.summary: The bin (usually the pipeline) whose sub-bins are watched.

parameters.name: factoryName
parameters.summary: The element factory name to match, e.g. avenc_wmv1.

parameters.name: onMatch
parameters.summary: Invoked on a GStreamer thread with a wrapper for each matching element. The wrapper is valid only for the duration of the call and must not be kept.

constructors.name: DeepElementAddedWatcher
constructors.summary: Connects the watcher to bin, matching every factory matches accepts.

parameters.name: bin
parameters.summary: The bin (usually the pipeline) whose sub-bins are watched.

parameters.name: matches
parameters.summary: Tests one element factory name. Runs on a GStreamer thread for every element added anywhere below the bin, so it must be a pure name test - it may not block or touch element state. An exception thrown here is swallowed with the rest of the callback, which would silently skip the element rather than report anything.

parameters.name: onMatch
parameters.summary: Invoked on a GStreamer thread with a wrapper for each matching element. The wrapper is valid only for the duration of the call and must not be kept.

methods.name: Connect
methods.summary: Connects the handler, in whichever shape this flavour can call back into managed code.

methods.name: NameMatcher
methods.summary: The one-name test the string constructor is sugar for. Static so the argument check runs before the instance constructor body, and so the closure carries nothing but the name.

methods.name: ReleaseWatcher
methods.summary: Called by GLib when the signal closure is finalized, which is after the handler has been disconnected and no emission of it is running.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Disconnects the signal handler. Must be called while the watched bin is still alive.

classes.name: DeepElementAddedNative
classes.summary: The native signature of deep-element-added: void (GstBin *bin, GstBin *sub_bin, GstElement *element, gpointer user_data).

classes.name: ClosureNotifyNative
classes.summary: GClosureNotify: void (gpointer data, GClosure *closure).

classes.name: DeferredCaptionPads
classes.summary: Holds a demuxer's raw caption and teletext pads back until the demuxer has exposed every stream, so a block hands its subtitle slots to the text-shaped tracks first.
classes.remarks: Issue #1387 routed CEA-608/708 closed captions and DVB teletext to the subtitle output; before that they were parked. A block assigns its subtitle slots in the order the pads arrive, and a muxer writes the caption track first often enough - qtmux always does - that the captions would take a slot the subtitles used to get. Deferring the raw-caption families fixes the order without ranking machinery in every block. The wait always ends before a buffer flows: qtdemux_expose_streams adds every pad and then calls gst_element_no_more_pads in straight-line code, and gst_ts_demux_program_started does the same after activating every stream of a program - its one early return is the !have_pads case, where nothing was deferred. Pads are held by name rather than as the the signal handed over: that wrapper is non-owned, so nothing keeps the native pad alive across signal emissions.

methods.name: Open
methods.summary: Accepts deferrals again and drops anything left over from a previous run. Call from the owning block's build.

methods.name: Close
methods.summary: Refuses further deferrals and drops what is held. Call from the owning block's cleanup.

methods.name: TryDefer
methods.summary: Holds the pad back when it carries a raw caption or teletext payload.

parameters.name: pad
parameters.summary: The pad the demuxer has just added.

methods.returns: true when the pad was taken over and the caller must not link it now; false when the caller should handle it as usual - including while the block is being torn down, where linking it to a sink beats leaving it with no peer.

methods.name: Drain
methods.summary: Takes back the pads held so far, resolved against the element that owns them.

parameters.name: element
parameters.summary: The demuxer element. A null element yields nothing.

methods.returns: The pads to link now, in the order they arrived. A pad the demuxer has taken away again is left out.

classes.name: ElementHelper
classes.summary: Provides GStreamer element availability and factory utilities for plugin discovery and validation. This static helper class handles GStreamer element factory operations including checking for element availability, validating plugin existence, and managing element factory resources. Essential for ensuring required GStreamer plugins are available before pipeline construction.

methods.name: IsAvailable
methods.summary: Determines whether the specified element is available, meaning it is both listed in the GStreamer registry and still provided by its plugin once that plugin is loaded.
methods.remarks: This loads the plugin that owns the element, which is a side effect of asking the question: only a loaded plugin can say which elements it really provides. Media Foundation is the exception, because registering that plugin activates NVIDIA's encoder MFTs and kills every later NVENC session in the process (issue #842). The plugin the SDK ships does not, and it is not always the one on the load path: initialization does not fail when the redist is missing, it logs and carries on against whatever GStreamer resolved from PATH, and a runtime refresh can drop a stock plugin into the SDK's own directory. So an mf* element is load-probed only when the plugin file GStreamer would load is verified to carry the patch, and answered from the registry alone otherwise - the pre-#1175 behaviour, which over-reports but cannot take NVENC down with it.
methods.returns: true if the specified element is available; otherwise, false.

methods.name: IsDecoderAvailable
methods.summary: Determines whether a decoder decodebin could plug for caps is available: a decoder factory of at least marginal rank whose sink accepts the caps and that String) confirms, so a hardware decoder the GPU does not provide (a stale registry entry) does not count.

parameters.name: caps
parameters.summary: The encoded caps, for example video/x-h265.

methods.returns: true when at least one such decoder exists.

methods.name: FindDecoders
methods.summary: Lists the decoders decodebin would try for caps, highest rank first: decoder factories of at least marginal rank whose sink accepts the caps and that String) confirms. Lazy - each candidate's plugin is loaded only when the enumeration reaches it.

parameters.name: caps
parameters.summary: The encoded caps, for example audio/x-adpcm, layout=(string)microsoft.

parameters.name: loadableOnly
parameters.summary: Skip decoders whose plugin may not be loaded (a stock mediafoundation, #842). True for a caller that instantiates the result; String) answers those from the registry alone.

methods.returns: The element factory names; none when no such decoder exists or the caps do not parse.

methods.name: SinkRefuses
methods.summary: Whether a registered element's sink template cannot take caps, so linking it would fail with NOFORMAT. An element that is not registered does not count: creating it fails on its own.

parameters.name: caps
parameters.summary: The caps the element would be linked with.

methods.name: CanLoadSafely
methods.summary: Whether the plugin owning a feature may be loaded just to answer an availability question.
methods.remarks: True for every plugin but mediafoundation, and true for that one only when the plugin file GStreamer would load carries the #842 patch. Two weaker tests were tried and rejected: a non-empty GST_PLUGIN_SYSTEM_PATH proves nothing, because a machine-wide GStreamer installation or the application itself may have set it before the SDK ran; and "the redist directory is there" proves nothing either, because a GStreamer runtime refresh can copy a stock plugin over the patched one inside that very directory. See the remarks on String) for why Media Foundation is special.

methods.name: MediaFoundationIsPatched
methods.summary: Whether the mediafoundation plugin GStreamer would load carries the #842 patch.
methods.remarks: The file is taken from the registry rather than composed from a directory, so this asks about the plugin that will actually be loaded. Checking a directory instead would miss the case this repository has already been bitten by: a GStreamer runtime refresh copying a stock plugin over the patched one inside the SDK's own tree, which is why _SETUP/NuGet/verify-patched-plugins.ps1 exists. Anything unreadable or unrecognised answers "not patched" - the conservative direction, since being wrong the other way costs the process its NVENC.

methods.name: ContainsAscii
methods.summary: Whether a byte buffer contains the given ASCII text.

methods.name: LoadIfSafe
methods.summary: Returns the factory as the loaded plugin registers it, for a caller that already holds one and needs its metadata to describe the real element rather than the cached registry entry.
methods.remarks: Returns null when the loaded plugin no longer provides the factory - a stale entry that String) could not create (issue #1175). When the plugin must not be loaded (see String)) the caller's own factory comes back unchanged, which is the pre-#1175 answer from the cached registry.

parameters.name: factory
parameters.summary: The factory taken from the registry.

methods.returns: The loaded factory, the original one, or null.

methods.name: EnsurePluginLoaded
methods.summary: Loads a plugin by name so that the registry's feature list for it describes what the plugin registers on this host, not what an earlier scan cached.
methods.remarks: Enumerating factories reads the registry, so an enumeration that starts before the plugin is loaded cannot see a feature the plugin registers only now - dropping stale entries afterwards is not enough (issue #1175). Call this first when enumerating the elements of a plugin whose feature set is decided at load time. Carries the same plugin-load side effect as String).

parameters.name: pluginName
parameters.summary: Name of the plugin, e.g. mediafoundation.

methods.name: CreateFallbackSrc
methods.summary: Creates a fallbacksrc element if available.
methods.returns: The created fallbacksrc element, or null if not available.

methods.name: IsFallbackSrcAvailable
methods.summary: Checks if the fallbacksrc element is available in the current GStreamer installation.
methods.returns: True if fallbacksrc is available; otherwise, false.

methods.name: IsFallbackSwitchAvailable
methods.summary: Checks if the fallbackswitch element is available in the current GStreamer installation.
methods.returns: True if fallbackswitch is available; otherwise, false.

classes.name: FontConfigBootstrap
classes.summary: Generates a fontconfig configuration file at runtime and points fontconfig at it.
classes.remarks: GStreamer's text elements (textoverlay, subtitle overlays, the trial watermark) render through Pango, which on iOS, Android and Apple desktop builds resolves font families through fontconfig. Those redists ship neither a fonts.conf nor any font, so fontconfig starts with an empty font set ("Cannot load default config file") and every glyph comes out as .notdef — a row of empty boxes. This helper writes a minimal configuration into a writable app directory listing whatever font directories actually exist on the device (fonts imported from the app bundle, platform font directories, and a font extracted from the SDK's own resources) so the generic Sans / sans-serif family customers pass in a font description resolves to a real face.

methods.name: Configure
methods.summary: Writes a generated fontconfig configuration and exports FONTCONFIG_FILE / FONTCONFIG_PATH so fontconfig picks it up.
methods.remarks: Must run before anything performs a font lookup through Pango — fontconfig loads its configuration once, lazily, on first use. Note that the trigger is the first Pango font map, which the SDK also materializes outside a pipeline (a parameterless FontSettings enumerates the installed families on desktop), so an application that builds font UI before InitSDK can still latch an unconfigured fontconfig.

parameters.name: writableRoot
parameters.summary: A writable directory owned by the app.

parameters.name: fontDirs
parameters.summary: Candidate font directories. Non-existing entries are dropped.

parameters.name: importFontsFrom
parameters.summary: Optional directory whose top-level font files are copied into the generated configuration's own font directory. Used for the application bundle: handing fontconfig the bundle root instead would make it scan the entire application payload recursively on every first run.

parameters.name: cacheRoot
parameters.summary: Optional separate root for fontconfig's own cache. The cache is regenerable, so on platforms with a reclaimable cache location it belongs there rather than next to the configuration and the extracted face, which must survive. Defaults to writableRoot.

methods.name: SweepStagingFiles
methods.summary: Deletes scratch files a previous run may have left behind after a crash. They live next to the configuration rather than in the scanned font directory, but a stale one is still clutter that would accumulate for the life of the installation.
methods.remarks: Only files older than StagingMaxAge are swept. The lock serializing this helper is per-process, while the directory is not: on macOS two instances of the same application share it, and deleting a scratch file the other one is mid-write through would make its publish throw and abort its whole setup. Nothing here writes for minutes, so age separates a live scratch file from an abandoned one without any cross-process coordination.

methods.name: IsConfiguredByApplication
methods.summary: Returns true when the application configured fontconfig itself, which the SDK must not override. A value this helper exported on an earlier init does not count — the environment is process-scoped and survives an SDK restart, so treating it as customer-owned would make every init after the first a no-op.

methods.name: BuildConfigXml
methods.summary: Builds the fontconfig configuration document.
methods.remarks: No DOCTYPE is emitted: fonts.dtd is not part of the mobile redists and fontconfig does not need it.

parameters.name: fontDirs
parameters.summary: Font directories to scan. Expected to exist.

parameters.name: cacheDir
parameters.summary: Writable directory for the fontconfig cache.

methods.returns: The configuration file content.

classes.name: GSignalHandlerId
classes.summary: Normalizes a GLib signal handler id returned through a UIntPtr P/Invoke.
classes.remarks: A handler id is a gulong: 8 bytes on the 64-bit Linux, macOS, iOS and Android ABIs, but **4 bytes on Windows and on the 32-bit Android ones** (GLIB_SIZEOF_LONG in each bundled glibconfig.h). Declaring the return as is what makes one declaration work on all of them — it is the gulong width everywhere except Windows x64, where it is over-wide and the callee only defines the low 32 bits of the return register, and the Microsoft x64 ABI leaves the upper half undefined rather than zero. In practice a 32-bit register write on x86-64 and AArch64 does zero the upper half, which is why this has never been seen to misbehave — but "has never been seen" is not the same as "cannot". If it ever did, a failed connect returning 0 with dirt above it would read as a non-zero id: the caller would believe it was connected, never free its GCHandle, and later hand garbage to g_signal_handler_disconnect for a GLib critical. Masking costs one branch on a path that runs once per connection.

methods.name: Normalize
methods.summary: Discards the undefined upper half of a handler id on platforms where gulong is 32 bits wide.

parameters.name: handlerId
parameters.summary: The value as returned by g_signal_connect_data.

methods.returns: The handler id, with any undefined high bits removed.

methods.remarks: Decoders allowed to change their output stride between frames take a different branch and are not affected - this mirrors gst_ffmpegviddec_decoder_can_change_stride(), whose AV_CODEC_ID_HEVC and AV_CODEC_ID_VVC gst-libav registers as h265 and h266. Audio decoders share the prefix and are rejected later, by Element), which is the only place that can tell them apart.

methods.name: DisableBrokenDirectRendering
methods.summary: Disables gst-libav direct rendering on the video decoders that hit the broken pool-negotiation path, leaving H.264/H.265/H.266 (and every non-libav element) untouched.
methods.remarks: In GStreamer 1.28 gst_ffmpegviddec_try_pool() may adopt a downstream buffer pool for direct rendering while keeping the libav-aligned GstVideoInfo (extra stride alignment plus one extra bottom row). When the pool does not allocate for that alignment, the GstVideoMeta on the buffer points past the end of the memory and the decoder aborts the stream with "Cannot access memory for read and write operation" - measured on macOS with avdec_dvvideo (yuv411p 720x480 -> plane 1 at offset 768 * 481) rendering through glimagesink. Turning direct rendering off costs one av_frame_copy per frame. For decoders GStreamer auto-plugs rather than the SDK creating by name, use instead.

methods.name: WatchAutoplugged

methods.remarks: One watcher per root is enough and one per root is required: GStreamer re-emits deep-element-added up the whole parent chain, so this sees elements added inside every descendant bin, but the walk stops at a bin with no parent. Do not add a second watcher on a sub-bin that is already in a watched pipeline. The returned watcher MUST be disposed while the pipeline wrapper is still alive, and therefore before that wrapper is disposed - see .

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.summary: The root pipeline. null yields null.

methods.returns: The installed watcher, or null when there was no pipeline to watch.

methods.name: Apply
methods.summary: Turns direct rendering off on one decoder that has already been matched by factory name.
methods.remarks: Runs on a GStreamer thread when it is reached from ContextX). Audio decoders share the avdec_ prefix but derive from a different base class and have no direct-rendering property, so the element class is what separates them - the factory name cannot. On the auto-plug path that costs one managed wrapper per libav audio decoder the graph builds - one or two per pipeline - because the element has to be wrapped before the gate can run. Reading the class off the factory instead would avoid those wrappers at the price of a second klass gate that could drift from this one; at this volume it is not worth the second copy.

classes.name: NDIRuntimeHelper

properties.name: WindowsArm64Hint
properties.summary: Appended to an NDI-unavailable error. Nothing NDI loads into a native Windows ARM64 process: gst-plugins-rs has no Windows ARM64 library name, so the ARM64 redist carries no NDI plugin, and the NDI SDK bindings load only the x86/x64 libraries (issue #3161).

methods.name: IsAvailable
methods.summary: Determines whether the NDI runtime can be loaded.
methods.remarks: Mirrors what the plugin itself does (gst-plugins-rs net/ndi/src/ndisys.rs, load()): try the directory in NDI_RUNTIME_DIR_V6, then the one in NDI_RUNTIME_DIR_V5, then the bare library name through the OS loader. That last step matters - on Linux and macOS the NDI installers export neither variable, so treating the variables as the whole answer reports a correctly installed runtime as missing. The probe needs NativeLibrary. Where it does not exist - net461/net472/netcoreapp3.1, and the netstandard2.1 assembly Unity ships to Windows, macOS, iOS and Android alike - the answer is the env-var route, and when neither variable is set: not being able to look is not evidence of absence, and a false negative would refuse a working installation. A runtime that is genuinely missing then fails inside the NDI element, which is how it behaved before this check existed.
methods.returns: true if the NDI runtime is present, or cannot be probed; otherwise, false.

methods.name: BlockPad
methods.summary: Block a pad using a probe that drops all data until removed.
methods.returns: The probe id to pass to UInt64), or 0 if the pad was null. The caller owns the id: blocking the same pad twice installs two probes and each one needs its own unblock.

methods.name: WaitForPadIdle
methods.summary: Wait until pad is out of dataflow, so the element behind it can be taken to the NULL state.
methods.remarks: Pad) is gst_pad_add_probe and nothing else - it installs the probe and returns, so a streaming thread already inside gst_pad_push keeps running and keeps the stream lock. SetState(State.Null) then deactivates the pads and gst_base_transform_activate waits on that lock forever. Waiting for the block probe itself to fire is not the answer: it returns rather than blocking, and on a PAUSED pipeline no further buffer arrives to fire it. An IDLE probe is the wait that works. gst_pad_add_probe runs an IDLE callback synchronously when the pad's using count is zero, and otherwise leaves it to the last thread to leave the push; block probes run before that counter is raised (gst_pad_push_data), so once the surrounding calls are in place the only thing left to wait for is the push already in flight.

parameters.name: pad
parameters.summary: The pad to wait on, and it has to be a src pad: only gst_pad_push_data / gst_pad_pull_range / gst_pad_push_event_unchecked raise the pad's using count, and all three run on the pushing side. An idle probe on a sink pad therefore fires at once in push mode and answers nothing. Which src pads a caller has to name is Pad[])'s remarks.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.summary: How long to wait before giving up.

methods.returns: True when the pad is idle, and when pad is null - an element with no pad on that side has no dataflow to wait for. False on timeout, when the probe could not be installed, and when the wrapper's handle is zeroed: a pad another holder disposed cannot be asked anything, and "could not check" must not read as "safe". On false the caller must NOT take the element to NULL - that is the deadlock of GitHub issue #838.

methods.name: WaitForPadsIdle
methods.summary: Wait until every pad in pads is out of dataflow, sharing one budget between them.
methods.remarks: One pad is rarely the whole answer. The peer of an element's sink pad covers every thread that entered through the chain, but says nothing about an element driving its own GstTask on its src pad, or about an element whose upstream peer is already gone - and that element's own src pad is blind to a thread that has not reached the push yet. Asking both is two cheap calls: a pad that is already idle answers from inside gst_pad_add_probe without blocking.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.summary: The budget for the whole set, not per pad.

parameters.name: pads
parameters.summary: The src pads a thread could be inside. Nulls are skipped, and naming the same pad twice is harmless - the second wait answers at once.

methods.returns: True when all of them are idle; false as soon as one is not.

methods.name: UnblockPad
methods.summary: Unblock a pad by removing the probe added by Pad).

parameters.name: probeId
parameters.summary: The probe id returned by Pad).

methods.name: SpecialRemoveElementRange
methods.summary: Take a whole run of chained elements out of the pipeline as one unit: one block at the run's boundary, one bypass edge around it, and either all of them leave the bin or none of them do.
methods.remarks: A filter built from several elements used to take them out one at a time, which is three or four separate edits of a live graph with no rollback across them. When one failed and the rest succeeded, "the filter is in the chain" stopped being a single fact: the two things VideoEffectsBlock tests for it - Filter != null and Filter.Out != null - disagreed, and neither field policy could make them agree. One verdict for the whole run is what makes them agree again. GitHub issue #942.

methods.remarks: No neighbour is named, so nothing is linked across the gap: the neighbours belong to other blocks. With nothing feeding the run, the edit runs inside an idle probe on the run's own downstream end - the src of its last member that has one, which a thread rendering into a sink behind it is still inside - so no thread is in the run, none can leave it, and no flush reaches a neighbour: a flush into the next block's sink in PLAYING loses its state and holds the pipeline in PAUSED. GitHub issue #2139.
methods.returns: true when every element left the bin, false when the run is untouched.

methods.remarks: Duplicates are the normal case, not a caller error: a filter hands over In, Element, Out and in a two-element filter one of them is an alias of another, in a one-element filter all three are the same wrapper. Compared by Handle rather than by reference because that is the identity the bin uses.

methods.name: RemoveElementAfterIdle
methods.summary: Unlink, stop, and unparent every element of run once the run's pads are idle.
methods.remarks: A bare SetState(Null) before gst_bin_remove deadlocks: going to NULL deactivates the pads, and gst_base_transform_activate waits on the stream lock the streaming thread already holds inside gst_pad_push. A PAUSED pipeline still has that thread — often blocked in sink preroll, still inside this element's chain. Flush-start unblocks preroll so the chain can return; an idle probe then waits until the pad is actually out of chain. SetState(Null) runs on this thread, never from the probe callback. See GitHub issue #838. A run of one is the single-element removal, unchanged: the boundary pads below are that element's own, and there is no internal edge to cut. A longer run costs the same one flush cycle and one 2 s wait, not one per element - and it is either all out or all back, which is what issue #942 needs.

GStreamer holds the pad for as long as an idle callback runs, so nothing crosses it during the edit; and the callback fires at once, on this thread, when the pad is already idle - a starved branch included - or on the streaming thread right after the item in flight. Not a blocking probe that is waited on and then released: an idle probe lets data through again the moment its callback returns (gstpad.c, do_probe_callbacks), and a blocking one never fires on a branch that receives nothing.

methods.remarks: The peers are read from the graph rather than assumed from the run's order, because two members of a run need not be adjacent, and a caller cannot promise that they are. gst_element_link_filtered is how that used to happen without anyone meaning it: it creates a capsfilter, adds it to the bin and links through it, and the two effect filters that called it had one nobody held sitting between them until they were given their own (GitHub issue #943). Recording both ends of every member is what lets the rollback put those edges back too - gst_bin_remove unlinks everything it removes, so an edge left unrecorded is an edge silently lost for the rest of the run. An edge through a request pad stays invisible here, as it is to the whole chain-walking side of this helper, and is left to gst_bin_remove - exactly what a per-element removal did with it.

An edge between two run members is named twice, once from each end, so the src pass skips it - but only when the downstream member recorded that same edge on its sink side. Being a member is not enough: GetConnectedToInput reads the static sink and video_sink pads and nothing else, so a member fed through any other pad recorded nothing, and then the src pass is the only one that can put the edge back. A rollback that fails is louder than the failure that caused it: at that point nothing short of a rebuild puts the chain back together.

Each pad therefore restores its own segment: read immediately before that pad is flushed, pushed straight back after. The restore is not conditional on the flush-stop's return value - the sticky is gone either way, so a rejected flush must still get its segment back.
