methods.name: IsEosOnAllSinks
methods.summary: Answers whether the pipeline has already reached End-Of-Stream, by asking the sinks instead of tracking it in a flag. GStreamer EOS is sticky: once the event has travelled the graph it sits on every sink pad until a flush drops it (a flushing seek, a trip through READY, a rebuild), and the pipeline never posts a second EOS message for it. A shadow flag would have to be cleared by hand in every one of those places, and a single miss costs a muxer its trailer - an unplayable file - so the sticky event itself is read instead. Only leaf elements count as sinks. A bin's ghost sink pad latches the sticky EOS the moment the event ENTERS the bin, which is before a muxer inside it has written anything; the filesink downstream of that muxer only sees EOS after the trailer has gone out. Bins are therefore skipped - their children are walked anyway. A sink inside a splitmuxsink is the exception to "a sticky EOS means the end": it gets one at every segment boundary (see Element)).

parameters.name: except
parameters.summary: Leaf sinks to leave out: those behind a muxer that can never finish (IntPtr}@)). When every sink found is one of them, the answer is true.

methods.returns: true when at least one leaf sink was found and every one of them holds a sticky EOS on every one of its sink pads - and, for one inside a splitmuxsink, that EOS is the stream's own - or when every leaf sink found is in except; false otherwise - including when no sink was found at all, so an unrecognized graph falls back to whatever the caller does without this answer.

methods.name: EosUnfedQueues
methods.summary: Sends End-Of-Stream into every top-level queue no stream can reach (Boolean)): the branch of a source block whose stream never appeared - an SRT source stopped before its first byte, or an audio output connected to a stream without audio. The source's own EOS cannot reach such a branch, so its sink would never post EOS and a graceful stop would wait out its whole budget; a sink that never prerolled also holds the pipeline in PAUSED, which backs up the other branches until the source's streaming thread blocks and the stop's EOS with it (issue #1798). A queue takes the event without blocking the caller - it only enqueues it - which is why only queues are EOSed here and why only the SDK's own top-level elements are walked, never the internals of a bin.

parameters.name: muxerBranches
parameters.summary: The cut-off queues left alone because they feed a muxer: see Element). Such a muxer can never finish.

parameters.name: stuckSinks
parameters.summary: The leaf sinks behind those muxers, for IntPtr}) to leave out: no EOS will ever reach them, and the other outputs must not wait for them.

methods.returns: The number of cut-off queues that now hold EOS, plus the muxer inputs released without a queue: either may let a sink preroll.

methods.name: SettleEmptyMuxerInputs
methods.summary: Settles the muxer inputs no stream can reach and that never had one, on a muxer with another input that can or did. Such a muxer waits for them forever, as for a cut-off queue in front of it: it holds a pipeline short of PLAYING, and the End-Of-Stream sent to a source then blocks the stop for good (issue #3634). An input the muxer drops cleanly is released, as in Element), one it can end empty is ended (Element)), and the others are counted. A muxer with nothing but such inputs or none at all is a cut-off output (IntPtr})) on a pipeline settled in PLAYING; on any other it counts, as its sink may be what holds the pipeline there and a source's End-Of-Stream can then hang the stop. No other output on such a pipeline gets one: measured beside an MP4 recording stopped from a pause, that file lacked its moov in 3 of 4 runs with the End-Of-Stream sent as well, after a 10 s wait.

parameters.name: stuck
parameters.summary: Receives the leaf sinks behind the muxers with an input counted.

parameters.name: released
parameters.summary: The number of inputs released or ended.

methods.returns: The number of inputs counted.

methods.name: CollectSourcesOfHeldMuxers
methods.summary: The elements upstream of the inputs of every splitmuxsink with an input that has had no stream and another that has. It holds the fed inputs at their next keyframe until every input reaches it, even in PLAYING, and a source behind them then never takes an End-Of-Stream sent to it (issue #4019). Any input without caps counts, as every input the stop counts as never fed has none. Only read: nothing is ended or released.

parameters.name: cutOffOnly
parameters.summary: Count only an input no stream can reach (Boolean)), not one whose stream has not arrived yet.

methods.returns: The handles found, compared by pointer only; empty when there is no such muxer; null when the walk could not tell, so that every source is treated as held.

methods.name: CollectUpstream
methods.summary: Adds every element upstream of sink to elements: out of a bin through its ghost pads, as Boolean) walks, and up every input of an element with more than one.

parameters.name: elements
parameters.summary: The elements found, which also stop the walk where it has been.

methods.returns: false when a pad walk failed, so an element upstream may be missing.

methods.name: CollectSinksBehindPad
methods.summary: Adds the leaf sinks downstream of pad to sinks: every sink behind the element it belongs to, inside a bin when it is the bin's ghost pad.

parameters.name: pad
parameters.summary: A pad the caller holds a reference on.

parameters.name: sinks
parameters.summary: The set the sinks are added to.

methods.name: CollectCutOffSinks
methods.summary: Fills sinks with every leaf sink no stream can reach now: its sink pad is cut off (Boolean)) - the sink of a block added with AddBlockLive and never linked, or one disconnected while the pipeline ran. No EOS can reach it, so the graceful stop does not wait for it (issue #3616); the stop reports a file such a sink writes.

parameters.name: sinks
parameters.summary: An empty set to fill. It is cleared when the walk starts over.

methods.name: CollectFedCutOffInputs
methods.summary: Ends the inputs that carried a stream and were then cut off with DisconnectLive: an unlinked sink pad with sticky caps, on anything but a leaf sink. Nothing upstream can end them, so the stop does, which gives a muxer behind one its trailer (issue #3634). An input with no caps is never ended (issue #1798). Only the SDK's own top-level elements are walked, as in IntPtr}@): never the internals of a bin.

parameters.name: sinks
parameters.summary: Filled with the leaf sinks that get an End-Of-Stream this way, which are waited for, not left out: every unlinked input in front of them carried a stream. An input EosUnfedQueues has ended already counts. A sink that also has an input in front of it that never carried one is not among them.

parameters.name: end
parameters.summary: Sends the End-Of-Stream into a pad; null to send nothing yet, as the caller will try again.

methods.name: IsSettledInPlaying
methods.summary: Whether the pipeline is in PLAYING with no state change pending. Any other answer, a failed query included, means a sink may still be waiting in preroll.
methods.remarks: A FAILURE return does not count against it: any child error sets the bin's return to FAILURE for good (gstbin.c 1.28 gst_bin_handle_message_func), while the state and pending state are still read - and a state change that really failed leaves the state short of PLAYING.

methods.name: IsHeldByFailure
methods.summary: Whether a failure holds the pipeline short of PLAYING until the next state change: a child's error, which sets the bin's state return to FAILURE, or a state change that failed. From then on the bin drops every ASYNC_DONE (gstbin.c 1.28 bin_handle_async_done, had_error): the sinks stay in preroll and none of them posts an EOS.

methods.name: IsLockedOut
methods.summary: Whether the pipeline child holding element is locked out of the state changes.

methods.name: IsFedBy
methods.summary: Whether a sink pad of element is linked to one of elements.

methods.name: ForEachSinkPad
methods.summary: Runs visit on the borrowed sink pads of element until it answers false.
methods.returns: false if visit did, or if the pads could not be walked.

methods.name: FreezeNewUnfedSinks
methods.summary: Freezes every new pipeline child holding a leaf sink nothing feeds - the elements of a block added with AddBlockLive and not linked yet. GstBin counts every child flagged SINK: each state change through PAUSED - a pause, a resume, a flushing seek - waited for that sink's preroll, the pipeline's EOS for its EOS, and a seek failed because the sink could not pass it upstream (issue #3635). The child loses its SINK flag and the leaf sink gets async off, so a state change of the pipeline takes it along without waiting for a preroll. The walk upstream goes through queues and leaves bins through their ghost pads, so an audio renderer's queue and a renderer's bin are covered. The first data or event to reach the child gives both back (PadProbeInfo)). An auto sink (autovideosink) is only half covered: the sink it creates on its way to READY comes with async on.

parameters.name: childrenBefore
parameters.summary: The pipeline's children before the new elements were added; left as they are.

methods.name: FreezeUnfedSinksBehind
methods.summary: Freezes the leaf sinks nothing feeds behind inputs, the unlinked inputs a build finds with no connection recorded - one DisconnectLive unlinked, or never connected. A start would wait for those sinks' preroll forever (issue #3936). A sink also fed from elsewhere - through a mixer, or a muxer with a fed input - is left alone. The first data to reach such a sink through a link brings it back (PadProbeInfo)). Called in NULL, where no sink waits in preroll.
methods.returns: The inputs behind which a sink is frozen.

methods.name: FreezeCutBranch
methods.summary: Freezes the leaf sinks behind input that output fed until it was just unlinked from it, as Pad}) does at a build, so a pause, a seek or the end of stream does not wait for them (#3936). A pause or a start still running may already have taken such a sink along and wait for its preroll: an async-done is posted for it, which the pipeline ignores when it waits for none (gstbin.c 1.28, ASYNC_DONE). Then lets a push still inside the branch come back out (IntPtr})).

methods.name: CollectUnfedLeaves
methods.summary: Adds the leaf sinks nothing feeds behind input and not frozen yet to leaves, those frozen already to frozen, and the pipeline children holding either to tops - those of the frozen ones only when frozen is given. Each with a ref.

parameters.name: leaves
parameters.summary: The leaves found not frozen yet.

parameters.name: frozen
parameters.summary: The leaves found frozen already, or null.

methods.returns: Whether a sink behind it is frozen already.

methods.name: ReleaseInFlight
methods.summary: Lets a push output began before its unlink come back out of the branch it fed. It sits in a sink there - waiting on the clock, or held in preroll by a pause - on the output's own thread, and while it does, a pause or a flushing seek waits for that thread, the queue behind the output fills and the outputs beside it starve (#3936). The sinks the branch ends in play, out of the pipeline's state changes, until the push has come back; then they follow the pipeline again. Nothing to do when the output is idle; a child locked by someone else is left as it is.

parameters.name: tops
parameters.summary: The pipeline children holding the branch's sinks. Borrowed.

methods.name: FreezeLeaves
methods.summary: Freezes leaves and the pipeline children tops holding them: see IntPtr}). Both borrowed.

parameters.name: settle
parameters.summary: Whether a child may be waiting in preroll right now, and is taken back to NULL.

methods.name: ThawOnData
methods.summary: Gives back what IntPtr}) took from the pipeline child data has just reached: its SINK flag and its leaf sinks' async. Runs once, on the streaming thread. Every frozen sink inside the child counts again, a second one nothing feeds too (ponytail: a child holding two sinks fed apart is not one any block builds). Data reaching a child still cut off - the tail a queue inside the branch held when its input was unlinked, or a push begun before the unlink - leaves it frozen: only a route that feeds it again thaws it (#3936).

methods.name: CollectNewUnfedSinks
methods.summary: Collects, with a reference on each, the leaf sinks nothing feeds whose pipeline child is not in childrenBefore, and those children.

methods.name: TopChild
methods.summary: The child of the top-level bin (the pipeline) that holds element - the element itself when it is one - with a reference the caller releases, or Zero when it has no parent.

methods.name: TakeMarks
methods.summary: Clears bits and returns those of them that were set.

methods.name: IsCutOff
methods.summary: Whether no stream can reach sink: it is unlinked, or linked only through elements Boolean) lets the walk pass, the first of which is unlinked. A source block may put a converter in front of its queue, and the link it never made is then the converter's: an NDI sender whose audio never arrived left the audio queue linked to an unlinked audioconvert, and the branch held the pipeline in PAUSED (issue #2877). The walk leaves a bin through its ghost pad (issue #3616).

parameters.name: sink
parameters.summary: The queue's sink pad. May be null.

parameters.name: throughQueues
parameters.summary: Walk on through a queue too: nothing reaches a queue nothing feeds (#3635).

parameters.name: throughMuxers
parameters.summary: Walk on through a muxer too, which is cut off when all of its inputs are, and when it has none (#3634).

methods.name: IsPlainSingleInput
methods.summary: Whether Boolean) may walk on through element: one sink pad, no source of its own (a bin carries the flag of a source inside it), and not a queue, which is judged on its own.

parameters.name: throughQueues
parameters.summary: A queue counts as plain as well.

methods.name: FeedsMuxer
methods.summary: Whether a branch starting at element reaches a muxer input that must not be ended empty (issue #1798). Measured with an input that gets EOS and never caps, beside a fed video input: mp4mux writes a track with no sample description (mdhd time scale 0, empty stsd) that no player opens, and matroskamux/webmmux never finish at all; mpegtsmux writes a valid file without that track, and so does splitmuxsink running it (every segment valid across rotation), so those are the ones a branch may be ended into (Element)). Any other factory class containing Muxer is treated as unsafe - a muxer bin is judged by its own class, since the pads inside it may not exist yet. The walk stops at a mixer (Element)) another input of which already carries a stream (sticky caps): an ended input of a mixer is dropped, and the muxer behind it gets the mixer's stream. Before any stream has reached the mixer the walk goes on to the muxer, so a branch is never ended into a mix that may end up with no stream at all. It follows each link, entering a bin through its ghost pad; a walk that fails answers true, the side that ends nothing.

parameters.name: element
parameters.summary: The element to start from. Borrowed.

methods.name: ReleaseMuxerInputs
methods.summary: Releases every muxer input a branch starting at element reaches and must not end empty (Element)), so the muxer writes its other inputs instead of waiting for this one forever (issue #1929); removing a pad unlinks it. All or none: every input is checked before any is released. Only through elements with one input - a tee fans out, but a mixer none of whose inputs has a stream yet, or any other element with more inputs, would carry more than this branch into that muxer input. A mixer that already has a stream ends the path, as in Element): it drops the ended input. Only on a muxer measured to drop the input cleanly (Pad)), and only while it keeps another input: with none left it could not finish either. Serialized process-wide, so two branches cannot each leave the other's muxer input as its last. The sink blocks keep these pads as the internal pads of their inputs but never release them, so nothing releases them a second time.

parameters.name: element
parameters.summary: The element to start from. Borrowed.

methods.returns: true if the branch no longer reaches such an input.

methods.name: CollectMuxerInputs
methods.summary: Adds the muxer inputs downstream of element that must not be ended empty to inputs. A mixer another input of which already carries a stream (sticky caps) ends the path: an ended input of a mixer is dropped, and the muxer behind it gets the mixer's stream. Before any stream has reached the mixer the walk goes on to the muxer, so a branch is never ended into a mix that may end up with no stream at all - or, when strict, gives up, as it does at any other element with more than one input (Element)).
methods.returns: false when a strict walk gave up; a lenient one always returns true.

methods.name: CollectFromMuxerPeer
methods.summary: The downstream side of a link. Into a bin through its ghost sink pad: a muxer bin (splitmuxsink, hlssink2) is judged as a whole - the pads inside it are made as streams arrive, so a walk through it could find nothing and read that as safe; any other bin is walked inside. Out of a bin through the internal proxy pad of its ghost src pad, which has no parent element: on to the ghost pad's own peer.

methods.name: DropsReleasedInputCleanly
methods.summary: The muxers measured to write a valid file with the other inputs once an unfed request pad is released (issue #1929): matroskamux, webmmux, and splitmuxsink over mp4mux, which restarts its muxer for the first fragment and so rebuilds the moov from the pads left. Not the qtmux family itself: it adds a pad's track to its moov when the pad is requested and release_pad does not take it out again (gstqtmux.c 1.28), so mp4mux still wrote that track, with mdhd time scale 0 and an empty stsd. Any muxer not measured is left alone. Nor is splitmuxsink's reference stream, its video pad: release_pad leaves reference_ctx NULL, which the fragment logic dereferences unchecked (gstsplitmuxsink.c 1.28). With no video pad the reference is the first input, which cannot be told from here, so nothing is released there.

methods.name: FeedsQtMuxer
methods.summary: Whether a branch starting at element reaches an input of a qtmux-family muxer - mp4mux, qtmux and the others gst_qt_mux_register makes - or of a splitmuxsink running one, that must not end empty (Element)). Such a muxer writes nothing while that input has no stream, and neither ending nor releasing the input saves the recording (Pad)), so the failure can be reported as soon as it is known rather than at the stop (issue #1962). Strict, like Element): past a mixer with no stream yet, another of its inputs may still feed the muxer. A walk that gives up or fails answers false: the stop still reports the input.

parameters.name: element
parameters.summary: The element to start from. Borrowed.

methods.name: CollectLeafSinks
methods.summary: Adds every leaf sink downstream of element to sinks, following links the way Boolean) does: into a bin through its ghost sink pad, out of it through the internal proxy pad of its ghost src pad.

parameters.name: sinks
parameters.summary: The set the sinks are added to.

parameters.name: follow
parameters.summary: When set, only the src pads of element itself it accepts are followed; past them every link is.

parameters.name: throughMerges
parameters.summary: When false, the walk does not go past an element with more than one sink pad (a mixer, a muxer, an input-selector): another of its inputs may still carry the stream on.

parameters.name: stopAt
parameters.summary: When set, no src pad it accepts is followed, anywhere on the walk.

methods.name: CollectSinksBehindFlowError
methods.summary: Adds to sinks the leaf sinks behind each src pad of element whose streaming task paused on a flow error. Such a pad passes nothing on until it is restarted, and an EOS sent toward it is dropped - a queue holding a flow error refuses it (gstqueue.c 1.28, gst_queue_handle_sink_event) - so no EOS will reach those sinks (issue #1781). A pad with no task (a chain-based element, which forwards EOS whatever its last push returned) or with a running one is left alone, and so is a paused pad an EOS has already gone past: the stop pushes it beyond an errored source (issue #825), and the sinks behind it can still finalize. The walk stops at a merge - a mixer that ignores inactive inputs or an input-selector still ends on the EOS of its other inputs - so a sink behind one is waited for, as before.

parameters.name: element
parameters.summary: A GstElement* kept alive by its owner for the call.

parameters.name: sinks
parameters.summary: The set the sinks are added to.

methods.name: CollectSinksBehindAnyFlowError
methods.summary: Adds to sinks the leaf sinks behind every src pad in the pipeline whose streaming task paused on a flow error, as IntPtr}) does for one element. For a stop that cannot wait for the error to be recorded: the bus delivers it to Bus_Error only later (issue #4021).

parameters.name: sinks
parameters.summary: The set the sinks are added to.

methods.name: PushEosPastFlowError
methods.summary: Pushes an EOS onto the peer of each src pad of the queue element whose streaming task paused on a flow error, past the task that would drop it (issue #2272) - as the stop does for an errored source (issue #825). Queues only: a queue reports its flow error only when an EOS reaches it, so its paused task is still there when the stop runs, while an element that reports the error at once (a source, a mixer) has the graph restarted by the error recovery; and past a muxer's paused task the EOS would reach the file sink without the trailer, and the stop would report a clean end. For the same reason a pad with a failed sink the EOS would reach is left alone, until that sink's own branch pauses. A peer no stream reached (no caps) is left alone too: ending it would write an empty track into a muxer (issue #1798). Past a peer that has caps the muxer inputs are not asked: an encoder still holding its first frames (x264enc lookahead) gives its muxer input caps only with its first output, which the EOS drains out. The EOS runs downstream on the calling thread, so the caller must know no sink there is waiting in preroll.

parameters.name: element
parameters.summary: A GstElement* kept alive by its owner for the call.

parameters.name: failed
parameters.summary: Every element that posted an error.

parameters.name: pushed
parameters.summary: The pads the EOS was sent past: a peer that refused it stores none, and is not sent another.

methods.returns: true when a peer took the EOS.

methods.name: SinksBehindFailed
methods.summary: Whether a failed sink is among those an EOS sent to peer would reach. A pad paused on a flow error drops the EOS, so the sinks behind one - a failed sink on another tee branch - do not count. A walk that fails counts as a failed sink: the pad is then left cut off, as before.

methods.name: HasEosBeyond
methods.summary: Whether an EOS sits downstream of pad: on its peer, or - when the peer is the way out of a bin - on the peer of the bin's ghost pad, where the stop puts it for an errored source bin (issue #825).

methods.name: EndsCleanlyWithAnEmptyInput
methods.summary: The muxers measured to write a valid file when one input ends with no caps (issue #1798): mpegtsmux, and a splitmuxsink running it. hlssink2 always runs splitmuxsink over mpegtsmux.

methods.name: SplitMuxerFactory
methods.summary: The factory of the muxer a splitmuxsink runs: its muxer element when one was set, else its muxer-factory name (default mp4mux).

methods.name: IsMixer
methods.summary: A video compositor (any factory class containing Compositor) or an audio mixer (audiomixer, liveadder, adder): an aggregator that drops an input which ends, whatever the others carry. Not every aggregator does - audiointerleave builds its channel layout from every input.

methods.name: IsCompositorKlass
methods.summary: Every video aggregator shipped here advertises .../Compositor (compositor, glvideomixer, d3d11compositor, and vfmetalcompositor per a measured macOS run); see FixesFrameSizeDownstream.

methods.name: AnySinkPadHasCaps
methods.summary: Whether any sink pad of the element holds sticky caps - some input of it has had a stream.

methods.name: HasFileWritingSink
methods.summary: Whether the graph holds a sink that writes its output somewhere it has to be finalized - the only case in which a stop that never saw End-Of-Stream costs the user anything. A muxer writes its trailer/index when EOS reaches it, so a recording cut short without EOS is an unplayable file; a renderer, a null sink or a live network sink has nothing to finalize and its missing EOS is not a defect to report (issue #1464). The question is asked of the graph rather than of the block list because a single output block can expand into a bin of its own. Bins are skipped and their children walked instead, so a splitmuxsink, hlssink2, hlssink3 or dashsink is found through the leaf sink it builds, not through its own properties. A leaf sink is asked for its factory class first. Sink/File is what GStreamer gives a sink that writes to a file or a descriptor, and it separates exactly the right way - read off gst-inspect-1.0 on the shipped 1.28.6 rather than assumed: filesink, multifilesink and fdsink carry it, while the renderers do not (directsoundsink and autoaudiosink are Sink/Audio, d3d11videosink and kmssink are Sink/Video) and neither do the live network sinks (rtmpsink, udpsink and the curl*sink family are Sink/Network, rtmp2sink and fakesink a bare Sink). That class is what keeps an RTMP or YouTube broadcast stopped mid-stream from being told its file may be unplayable. Two sinks the class does not reach are asked for a property instead, in : awss3sink, which upstream labels Source/Network and which completes its multipart upload on End-Of-Stream, is found by bucket; and giostreamsink, which hlssink2, hlssink3 and dashsink write their fragments through, is found by close-on-stop. That sink is a bare Sink, and so is nicesink inside the webrtcbin of a WHIP output; close-on-stop is what separates them, where the more obvious stream does not - nicesink has one too, holding a NICE stream ID, and matching it put the false positive back on a WHIP stop (measured). Its sibling giosink needs neither: it is Sink/File and the class branch already has it. A sink this recognizes as neither loses the warning. In a graph whose every end is a renderer it also loses the graceful EOS wait (issue #4062): there this answer is the only sign of a writer hidden behind a block's output pad. Every other graph waits for all its outputs as before.

parameters.name: only
parameters.summary: When set, only these leaf sinks are considered.

parameters.name: except
parameters.summary: When set, these leaf sinks are left out.

methods.returns: true when a leaf sink that writes something to be finalized was found, and when the walk could not answer at all - a graph this cannot read must not lose its warning.

methods.name: WritesSomethingToFinalize
methods.summary: Whether the leaf sink writes something that has to be finalized.
methods.returns: true for a Sink/File factory class, or for one of DestinationProperties.

methods.name: FeedsFixedFrameSizeMuxer
methods.summary: Walks downstream from a sink pad and answers whether the frame size arriving at that pad is written into the track header of a muxer that cannot change it again (FixedFrameSizeMuxers).
methods.remarks: The question is deliberately "does this pad's size reach the muxer", not "is a muxer reachable". A VideoResizeBlock or a ResizeVideoEffect ends in a capsfilter pinned to a fixed width and height, and a VideoMixerBlock input pad is one sink of a compositor that composes onto an output of its own size: in both the muxer never sees the change, and answering true there would kill a recording that was working.

parameters.name: sinkPad
parameters.summary: The pad to walk from. Borrowed.

methods.returns: true only when such a muxer was actually found AND nothing on the way re-fixes the frame size. Everything else - a preview branch, a live streaming branch, a scaler or a compositor in between, a request-pad element on the way (a tee has no static src) or an unrecognized muxer - answers false, so a walk that cannot see far enough leaves the previous behaviour in place rather than inventing an error. A branch that crosses an appsink/appsrc boundary, as PreEventRecordingBlock does, is one of those: the walk ends at the appsink and the muxer on the far side is never reached.

methods.name: FixesFrameSizeDownstream
methods.summary: Whether this element re-fixes the frame size for everything downstream of it, so a change arriving upstream of it never reaches a muxer.

parameters.name: element
parameters.summary: The element on the walk. Borrowed.

parameters.name: factoryName
parameters.summary: Its factory name, already resolved by the caller. May be null.

methods.returns: true when the walk must stop and answer "not affected".

methods.name: FixesBothDimensions
methods.summary: Whether every structure of a capsfilter's caps carries a fixed width and height.
methods.remarks: caps is a BOXED property: the wrapper GLib.Value.Val hands back is transfer-none and dies with the GValue, so everything is read inside the using and no wrapper escapes it. See the remarks on BaseElement.GetElementProperty.
methods.returns: true when the caps pin the frame size.

methods.name: GetStringProperty
methods.summary: Reads a string property, or null when the element does not have a readable one by that name. A string comes out of the GValue copied, so it outlives the value.
methods.returns: The value, or null.

methods.name: GetFactoryName
methods.summary: The element's factory name, read without creating a managed wrapper for the factory.
methods.remarks: Deliberately not Element.Factory: wrapping that transfer-none pointer claims ownership of the factory - the same trap BusMessageHelper.GetSrcFactoryName documents (bugs.md #69). Both pointers here are borrowed, so neither is unreffed.
methods.returns: The factory name, or null when the element has no factory or a zero handle.

methods.name: GetFactoryKlass
methods.summary: The element's factory class metadata (GST_ELEMENT_METADATA_KLASS), read without creating a managed wrapper. Both pointers are transfer-none - gst_element_get_factory borrows the factory and gst_element_factory_get_metadata returns a const gchar * owned by it - so neither is unreffed or freed here, and the string is copied out.
methods.returns: The class string, or null when the element has no factory or a zero handle.

methods.name: HasStickyEosOnEverySinkPad
methods.summary: Whether every sink pad of the element carries a sticky EOS. An element with no sink pads answers false - it is not something that can have finished.

parameters.name: element
parameters.summary: The element to inspect. Pads come from the iterator and are borrowed, so none of them is disposed here.

methods.returns: true when the element has at least one sink pad and all of them hold a sticky EOS.

methods.name: IsStreamEosInSplitMuxSink
methods.summary: For a leaf sink inside a splitmuxsink, whether its sticky EOS ends the stream rather than one segment. At every segment boundary splitmuxsink sends EOS straight into its muxer's sink pads, drops the sink's EOS message, and only then resets the muxer and sink for the next file - so for that moment the sink holds a sticky EOS while the stream goes on, and a stop reading it forces NULL before the last segment is written (issue #2226). The stream's own EOS is the one that comes out of splitmuxsink's input queues, so it is the only one stored on their src pads: the sink's EOS counts once every other element in the splitmuxsink holds a sticky EOS on all of its src pads. In the default mode that cannot be a boundary EOS still on the sink: the reference stream's queue thread is the one that resets the sink, inside its own output probe, so it pushes the stream's EOS only after the reset. With async-finalize the old muxer and sink stay in the bin until they finish, and the new muxer's src pad without an EOS keeps the answer false - the safe direction. The ancestors are walked on raw pointers and the factory compared by pointer, so a sink outside a splitmuxsink costs the stop's poll no wrapper and no allocation. A bin set as splitmuxsink's sink property puts the leaf below it, which is why the walk goes up more than one level.

A top-down DIB stores a negative height, so the product wraps and the caps carry e.g. -1/1 for a 4:3 640x480 stream; a sink then fails negotiation in gst_video_calculate_display_ratio. classes.name: RefusedDecoderWatch
classes.summary: Notices a VideoToolbox decoder that refuses a stream. It fails every frame with a log line and posts nothing on the bus until EOS, and a live stream has no EOS, so the application sees PLAYING and no video (issue #3709).
classes.remarks: The verdict is nothing out 2 seconds after 2 key frames and 32 frames went in. The first key frame alone can be damaged by joining a stream mid-packet, 32 frames exceed the longest reorder delay (16), and the wait covers a file fed faster than the decoder's first output, which is asynchronous. It runs on a timer because a source backed up behind the prerolled sinks delivers no further buffer to count on. The check repeats until a frame comes out, so the EOS is sent again after a flush takes it away. ponytail: only the start of a stream is watched, a decoder that starts and then refuses is not seen. A source that backs up before the counts are reached (a key frame every few seconds, a low frame rate) gets no verdict. Add a stall check when either is seen in the field.

classes.name: RtspPayloadFilter
classes.summary: Keeps each rtspsrc stream on its main RTP payload type (issue #2158).
classes.remarks: rtpbin adds a pad per SSRC and payload type, and rtspsrc ghosts each one; from then on it pushes all of that stream's data - every payload type - out of the newest pad (gstrtspsrc.c 1.26 and newer: new_manager_pad replaces stream->srcpad; gst_rtspsrc_handle_src_sink_chain and _event push every older pad's buffers and events there). A single comfort-noise (RFC 3389) or DTMF (RFC 4733) packet therefore moves the whole stream to a pad whose caps a depayloader rejects, and returning to the main payload type raises no new pad. Before 1.26 each pad keeps carrying its own data, so there the stream stays on its main payload type's pad. A source that follows the newest pad of a stream calls for each one, and to put an admitted pad in its stream's place. From 1.26 on, every admitted pad but the stream's first gets a probe passing only the stream's main payload type - its buffers, and its caps events - so the newest pad can be linked to the stream's depayloader whatever payload type it was created for. The caps of another payload type also reach the pad as an ACCEPT_CAPS query - rtspsrc's internal pad asks downstream before it takes the caps event - which the probe answers itself, or the depayloader's refusal fails the stream with not-negotiated. The probe runs per RTP packet and works on raw pointers only: no managed wrapper, no allocation. One instance per rtspsrc element.

Freeing them on Dispose() requires the owned/elements_owned ctor flags - the typed-only GLib.List ctor leaves both false and frees nothing (GitHub issue #1208). The event names the complete set of streams to activate; anything omitted is deactivated (GitHub issue #1216). After STREAMS_SELECTED the tracked set already has the real subtitle.

A text stream counts as text only when it can come out as text/x-raw (Stream)): a DVB/DVD/PGS subpicture, a closed-caption, a teletext stream or a payload no decoder decodebin3 could auto-plug (TTML) is typed text but no raw-text output takes it. Never: a DVB/DVD/PGS subpicture, or a closed-caption / teletext payload (String)) - parked regardless of the registry. Everything else needs a decoder decodebin3 can auto-plug: a decoder-classified factory at rank above NONE that sinks the stream's caps and sources text/x-raw. methods.summary: Parses the GStreamer image-orientation tag value (e.g. rotate-90, flip-rotate-180, flip-horizontal) into its rotation component in degrees (0/90/180/270) and a flag indicating whether a horizontal flip should be applied before the rotation.
methods.remarks: GStreamer's canonical values are rotate-0, rotate-90, rotate-180, rotate-270, flip-rotate-0 (= horizontal mirror), flip-rotate-90, flip-rotate-180 (= vertical mirror), and flip-rotate-270. Some producers emit the friendlier aliases flip-horizontal / flip-vertical — we map flip-horizontal to (0°, flipped) and flip-vertical to (180°, flipped), matching GStreamer's own alias handling. Composition convention: consumers must apply the horizontal flip FIRST, then the rotation clockwise. Under that order, (rot=180, flipped=true) is equivalent to a vertical mirror (horiz-flip-then-rotate-180 ≡ vert-flip). The returned IsHorizontallyFlipped flag is therefore NOT "is this a horizontal mirror?" on its own — see for the full (rotation, flipped) → videoflip-method table.

Both properties are writable only in NULL/READY state, which is exactly when deep-element-added fires: decodebin adds the element before syncing its state. GstDiscoverer exposes no handle to that uridecodebin (its only hook is source-setup), but by the time this signal runs the source is already parented to it, and deep-element-added bubbles up from every descendant bin - so watching the source's owner sees every decoder decodebin creates.

methods.remarks: Only a single JPEG video stream is completed: rtspsrc exposes pads in the order packets arrive, so with two there is no telling which read belongs to which declared stream, and the size stays unknown rather than guessed. The read runs over the RTSP TCP connection and gives up after VideoFrameRate); a failure leaves info as it was.

methods.name: GetPad
methods.summary: Reads the pad at padIndex off Element.
methods.remarks: Call it - and use what it returns - inside lock (SyncRoot). A pad is not one of the fields the lock protects, so it is the element read here plus the push or read that have to be under it together: outside the lock a teardown can zero the pad wrapper's handle between the two, and g_object_set_property on a zeroed handle is a GLib critical - one log line and a silent no-op rather than an exception; a read gets back an empty value, and its cast throws. GitHub issues #1366, #3286.

parameters.name: padIndex
parameters.summary: The index into the element's pad list.

methods.returns: The pad, or null when the element is gone or has no such pad.

methods.name: SetInputPadProperty
methods.summary: Pushes one property onto the pad at padIndex, resolving the pad and pushing under SyncRoot.

methods.name: UpdateAspectRatio
methods.summary: Updates the aspect ratio.
methods.remarks: Call it inside lock (SyncRoot): it both reads the pad's property list and pushes onto it, and neither is safe against a teardown zeroing the wrapper's handle otherwise. GitHub issue #1366. The letterbox is computed here and stretched into - which compensates its width for the input PAR as well - when the pad has no sizing-policy, or when the input is cropped: glvideomixer's keep-aspect-ratio sizes from the uncropped frame. The size is 's; a cropped input with none keeps the pad's policy. Which way the pad went is recorded for , and a CAPS event of the input or the output lays it out again. GitHub issue #3675.

parameters.name: pad
parameters.summary: The pad. Resolved by the caller under SyncRoot.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.summary: The rectangle to lay the input out in: the stream's own, or a step of Double}).

parameters.name: followsCaps
parameters.summary: Whether the layout depends on the input's caps and the output PAR: a letterbox computed here.

methods.returns: Whether the letterbox could be computed: not without an input size - negotiated caps or SourceInfo - larger than the crop. The caller reports it once SyncRoot is released (#1711, #3435).

methods.name: GetInputSize
methods.summary: The input's size and pixel aspect ratio: from its caps, as StretchPadGeometry follows them - what glvideomixer draws, and the PAR it compensates for - and from info until the pad has caps. A size of 0 when neither gives one. GitHub issue #3675.

methods.name: ReportLetterbox
methods.summary: Reports what Boolean@) could not do. Call it after SyncRoot is released: a log call runs the application's OnError handler (#1711, #3435).

methods.name: OnCapsChanged
methods.summary: Called by StretchPadGeometry when the caps of the input on pad, or the output PAR, change. It runs under a stream lock, so the layout, which needs SyncRoot, goes to a thread of _animations, which Dispose waits for (#948). Static with a weak owner: the listener the pad keeps would otherwise keep the mixer alive. GitHub issue #3675.

methods.name: Relayout
methods.summary: Lays stream out again on the pad handle names - only while that pad still holds the stream's layout. Another stream object in its place, or the stream at another position, is a SetSettings or Input_Update that has laid the pad out since, or is about to, from the caps as they are.

methods.name: ApplyStream
methods.summary: Pushes a stream's layout, crop and blend onto its pad - for a plain stream, no crop and the default blend. The caller holds SyncRoot.
methods.remarks: Shared by SetSettings and Input_Update: only the first used to push crop and blend, so an Input_Update left them as they were. GitHub issue #3663.
methods.returns: What Boolean@) could do, for the caller to report.

methods.name: SetAlphaFilterSettings
methods.summary: Sets the alpha filter settings for chroma keying.
methods.remarks: The filter is resolved inside the lock rather than handed in: the map is cleared under SyncRoot by ChromaKeyElementsDispose and the filters are disposed just after, so a caller that read the entry outside the lock would push onto a wrapper whose handle had been zeroed - the silent GLib critical of issue #1366. It reports rather than logs: Input_Update reaches it for every chroma-key input, including a position built with a plain stream and so with no filter at all, and logging there would be one error line per animation tick.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The input's position in the stream list, which is also its pad's.

methods.returns: false when the input has no alpha filter, so the caller can report it.

methods.name: SetAlphaFilterPassthrough
methods.summary: Switches the input's alpha filter off - gstalpha's SET method at an alpha of 1.0 - under SyncRoot.
methods.remarks: SET still applies the filter's alpha, so an input keyed at 0.5 and switched off stayed translucent. prefer-passthrough stays off, so the filter still processes every frame of an input that is not keyed. Measured with it on: with a source in GL memory the input stayed un-keyed when keying went on. It goes first because PreferPassthrough may have put it on. GitHub issue #3665.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The input's position in the stream list, which is also its pad's.

methods.returns: false when the input has no alpha filter.

methods.name: ApplyChromaKeyState
methods.summary: Puts the input's alpha filter into the state its stream asks for.
methods.remarks: Nothing in this class unlinks or removes an alpha element once it is in the bin, so a disabled input is one whose filter sits in gstalpha's SET method - passthrough at the default alpha of 1.0 - and not one whose filter is gone. Without this, chroma key could be turned on through SetSettings and never off again. GitHub issue #1366.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The input's position in the stream list, which is also its pad's.

methods.returns: false when keying was asked for and is not on: the input has no alpha filter or no settings.

methods.name: TrackChromaKeyRefusal
methods.summary: Records whether the input's chroma key request is met.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The input's position in the stream list, which is also its pad's.

methods.returns: true when the request is unmet and this reason has not been reported yet.

methods.name: ApplyChromaKeyStateOrReport
methods.summary: Puts the input's alpha filter into the state its stream asks for and reports a request that cannot be met, once until the request is withdrawn or met.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The input's position in the stream list, which is also its pad's.

parameters.name: method
parameters.summary: The calling method, for the log.

methods.name: ChromaKeyElementsDispose
methods.summary: Chroma key elements dispose.
methods.remarks: Unpublishes the filters under SyncRoot and disposes them outside it - the same split BaseElement makes for Element. A settings push holds that lock while it writes to these filters, so unpublishing under it is what makes the push either land on a live wrapper or find nothing at all, rather than on a wrapper whose handle was zeroed halfway through. GitHub issue #1366.

classes.name: ManagedElementConstruction
classes.summary: Process-wide serialization for constructing VisioForge managed GStreamer elements.
classes.remarks: Constructing a managed GObject subclass runs the gtk-sharp construction path (GLib.Object.CreateNativeObject → g_object_newv → ConstructorCallback / SetPropertyCallback), which mutates process-global, non-thread-safe static state: the lazy per-type GType registration and the shared PropertiesToSet deferred-property dictionary. When several pipelines start at once (e.g. multiple RTSP cameras), concurrent first constructions race that state and fail non-deterministically — the loser either throws "Unable to register managed GObject type ..." or corrupts the property dictionary (IndexOutOfRangeException). Both surface to the caller as "Unable to create sample grabber element." The callbacks run synchronously on the constructing thread inside g_object_newv, so holding this single shared lock around each plugin's CreateNativeObject call fully serializes the risky window across all managed element types. Construction is infrequent (pipeline build only), so the contention cost is negligible. This is deliberately shared by ALL managed plugin types — the corrupted PropertiesToSet state is global, so a per-type lock would not prevent two different element types from racing it.

classes.name: OwnedElementHandles
classes.summary: Tracks the native handles of plugin elements created by their managed constructors, so a wrapper rebuilt by a vfunc trampoline after its original was disposed can be recognized.
classes.remarks: Disposing a managed wrapper drops it from the GLib object table while the native GObject may still be alive (the pipeline bin holds its own reference). The next vfunc on that native object then rebuilds a fresh wrapper through the single IntPtr constructor, which starts from field defaults: per-instance state set by the owner is gone (issue #1784). A handle present here marks such a recreation: the owner's managed constructor recorded it, and GLib.Object.GetObject would have returned the original wrapper instead of constructing a new one if that wrapper were still alive. Entries are never pruned: one IntPtr per element ever built, and a pruned entry could not tell a recreated wrapper from a factory-created one. The ceiling is that an element created through the element factory on a recycled address of a dead owner-built element would be flagged as recreated; this codebase never creates these elements through the factory, and a subsequent owner construction at the same address overwrites the entry.

parameters.name: raw
parameters.summary: Native GObject handle of the new element.

methods.name: WasOwned
methods.summary: Reports whether the wrapper being constructed from a raw handle is a recreation of an owner-built element, and logs once when it is.

parameters.name: raw
parameters.summary: Raw GObject handle passed to the IntPtr constructor.

parameters.name: wrapper
parameters.summary: The wrapper under construction, for the log line.

methods.returns: true when this wrapper is a recreation and has lost the owner's state.

classes.name: NDIStreamWatch
classes.summary: Watches the start of an NDI connection whose sender has both video and audio, and says when to drop it and open a new one because one of the two streams is not arriving (issue #2904).
classes.remarks: NDI's reliable-UDP transport (libndi 6.3.2) sometimes carries only one of a sender's streams on a connection, or stops one of them right after its first frames: measured against the lab sender, 4 to 10 of 20 connections. The branch that gets nothing never prerolls, and the pipeline then plays neither stream. A new connection brings the missing stream back - the probe does the same (NDIInfoX.ShouldReconnect, #2871) and uses these constants. Only the start is watched: once both streams have flowed together for the watch is done (each start of the source builds a new one), so a sender that pauses one stream later (audio only while there is sound, video only on change) is never reconnected. A stream's grace runs from the first frame after both were silent, not from the connect - a connection that takes seconds to come up, is not a missing stream. Both falling silent before the watch is done is: a connection that brought a frame or two and then nothing. A pause of the pipeline ends the watch (): ndisrc's own timeouts do not pause, so silence could no longer be timed against them. asks once, frames are ignored until , and that times the new connection afresh. Thread-safe.

parameters.summary: Whether a connection silent after its frames may be replaced.

parameters.summary: Whether a connection that brought nothing at all may be replaced.

properties.name: IsDone
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether there is nothing left to decide: both streams flowed together for ReconnectAfterMs, or the reconnects ran out and each stream has arrived on some connection of this start - either way every branch has had a buffer to preroll on. Lock-free.

methods.name: ShouldReconnect
methods.summary: Decides from the age of each stream's last frame (or grace start). Pure, so the decision is unit-testable.

parameters.summary: Milliseconds since the last video frame, or since its grace started.

parameters.name: msSinceAudio

methods.summary: Initializes in Samba/UNC mode using filesrc + decodebin instead of uridecodebin. GStreamer's uridecodebin cannot handle UNC file:// URIs correctly on Windows, but filesrc handles UNC paths natively via Win32 file APIs.

methods.name: WatchForTsDemux
methods.summary: Starts watching the decoder's internals for a tsdemux.
methods.remarks: This replaces a managed ElementAdded subscription that re-subscribed itself to every decodebin / parsebin / sourcebin it saw. GLib's signal marshaller converts every GObject parameter into a managed object before the handler body runs, and a wrapper takes a native reference - so that scheme claimed ownership of every element uridecodebin builds, at every depth, on the hot path of every player and capture graph in the SDK - 511 Element wrappers in one measured four-class run, 110 after this change (bugs.md #69). The recursion is also gone with it, because deep-element-added is emitted recursively by GStreamer itself (gst_bin_do_deep_add_remove), which the old code was hand-rolling with subscriptions on sub-bins it kept no reference to and never disconnected.

classes.name: TSBitReader
classes.summary: A small MSB-first bit reader over a byte buffer, used to parse codec sequence/parameter-set headers (H.264/HEVC SPS, MPEG-2 sequence header). Supports single-bit and multi-bit reads plus unsigned (ue) and signed (se) Exp-Golomb codes. All reads are bounds-checked: a read past the end of the buffer throws EndOfStreamException so the (defensive) caller can catch it and leave the parsed fields at their defaults rather than emitting garbage.

constructors.name: TSBitReader
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the TSBitReader class over a region of a byte buffer.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.summary: The byte offset to start reading from.

parameters.name: length
parameters.summary: The number of bytes available to read.

properties.name: BitLength
properties.summary: Gets the total number of bits available in the reader's window. Computed as Int64 so a window wider than 256 MB does not overflow the multiply (the reader only ever wraps small codec headers, but the wider type costs nothing and removes the latent overflow).

properties.name: BitsRemaining
properties.summary: Gets the number of bits not yet consumed.

methods.name: ReadBit
methods.summary: Reads a single bit, returning 0 or 1.
methods.returns: The bit value.

methods.name: ReadBits
methods.summary: Reads count bits MSB-first into an unsigned value.

parameters.name: count
parameters.summary: The number of bits to read (0..32).

methods.returns: The value, with the first-read bit as the most significant.

methods.name: ReadUe
methods.summary: Reads an unsigned Exp-Golomb code (ue(v)).
methods.returns: The decoded value.

methods.name: ReadSe
methods.summary: Reads a signed Exp-Golomb code (se(v)).
methods.returns: The decoded signed value.

methods.name: SkipBits
methods.summary: Skips count bits.

parameters.name: count
parameters.summary: The number of bits to skip.

methods.name: RemoveEmulationPrevention
methods.summary: Removes H.264/HEVC emulation-prevention bytes (the 0x03 in a 00 00 03 sequence) from an RBSP-encoded payload, returning the de-escaped bytes.

parameters.name: data
parameters.summary: The source buffer (NAL payload, after the NAL header).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.summary: The byte offset to start at.

parameters.name: length
parameters.summary: The number of bytes to process.

methods.returns: A new array with emulation-prevention bytes removed.

classes.name: TSPacketParser
classes.summary: Parses raw MPEG transport-stream bytes (188 or 192 byte packets) and accumulates analysis statistics: PAT/PMT discovery, per-PID bitrate and continuity-counter errors, and PCR timing. Thread-safe: Int32) runs on the GStreamer streaming thread, while Boolean) may be called from the statistics timer thread, the streaming thread (final report on end-of-stream), or an arbitrary caller thread (GetReport). All access is guarded by an internal lock.

constructors.name: TSPacketParser
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the TSPacketParser class.

methods.name: Feed
methods.summary: Feeds a chunk of raw transport-stream bytes into the parser.

parameters.name: length
parameters.summary: The number of valid bytes in data.

methods.name: DecodeH264SpsNal
methods.summary: Decodes one H.264 SPS NAL unit (header byte included, emulation prevention bytes still in) - the form an RTSP sprop-parameter-sets value carries. Returns null when it cannot be decoded. The pixel aspect ratio comes from the VUI; both values are 0 when the SPS does not carry one, or when the VUI is cut off - the size is still returned then.

parameters.name: parNumerator
parameters.summary: The pixel aspect ratio numerator, or 0.

parameters.name: parDenominator
parameters.summary: The pixel aspect ratio denominator, or 0.

methods.returns: The decoded details, or null.

methods.name: ParseH264DimensionsFromCodecData
methods.summary: Returns the H.264 dimensions carried by an AVCDecoderConfigurationRecord - the codec_data flvdemux publishes on a compressed AVC pad, which carries no width/height of its own. Returns null when the record is too short or the SPS cannot be decoded.
methods.returns: The decoded details, or null.

methods.name: Snapshot
methods.summary: Produces a report snapshot. Per-PID and total bitrate are running averages over the whole stream so far: total bytes seen on each PID divided by the PCR-derived elapsed time (so the value is independent of how fast the source is read and converges to the nominal rate). Only when no PCR span is available yet does it fall back to the supplied per-interval delta.

parameters.name: intervalSeconds
parameters.summary: Seconds elapsed since the previous snapshot (fallback only).

parameters.name: resetInterval
parameters.summary: When true (the timer-driven cadence) the per-interval accounting is rolled over: each PID's instant/peak bitrate is recomputed from the bytes accumulated this interval and the interval byte counter is reset. When false (a read-only probe such as GetReport) the last computed instant/peak values are reported as-is and the interval counter is left intact, so an out-of-cadence reader cannot steal bytes from the next interval and report a spuriously low instant rate.

methods.returns: A fresh TSAnalyzerReport.

methods.name: RemoveOwnedRangeWithDrawWatcher
methods.summary: Take an In -> Element -> Out run out of the graph as one unit, with the cairooverlay draw handler detached across the attempt and reconnected if the run stays.
methods.remarks: The watcher has to be disposed while the element wrapper is still alive: after the wrapper goes, CairoDrawWatcher.Dispose cannot disconnect the handler and its GCHandle roots the watcher, the callback and this filter for the life of the process. So it goes first - and it has to come back if the removal is refused, because a refusal now leaves the whole filter in the graph. A cairooverlay sitting in a running chain with no draw handler renders nothing while the block still reports the effect as applied, and the reachable refusal is the ordinary one: the removal's 2 s idle probe timing out on a loaded pipeline. GitHub issue #942. internal rather than protected: this class is public and CairoDrawWatcher is not, so a protected signature naming it does not compile. Every caller is an internal filter in this assembly.

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.summary: The pipeline the run is in.

parameters.name: watcher
parameters.summary: The filter's draw watcher field. Nulled on success, reconnected on failure.

parameters.name: onDraw
parameters.summary: The filter's draw callback, used to reconnect.

methods.returns: What Element[]) answered.

methods.name: ResolveText
methods.summary: Resolves the text to draw for this frame: the per-frame provider when one is set and still healthy, otherwise the static text. Shared by every filter that renders an OverlayManagerText, so the desktop and Android paths cannot drift apart.
methods.remarks: A provider that throws is logged once and then not called again - retrying it every frame would unwind an exception 50 times a second on the streaming thread while the overlay lock is held, which costs far more than the failure being reported. Assigning to TextProvider again gives the mechanism another go.
methods.returns: The text to lay out and draw. Never null.

methods.name: ApplyConverterThreads
methods.summary: Lets a converter element spread a frame across several worker threads.
methods.remarks: videoconvert defaults to n-threads=1. The Cairo-based effects wrap cairooverlay, which only accepts BGRx/BGRA/RGB16, so every YUV source pays for two full-frame conversions per frame - single-threaded that does not keep up with 1080p50 and the recording branch starves. A fixed small cap rather than n-threads=0: the auto setting sometimes picks a single worker, the same reason VideoRendererBlock pins it. Silently skipped when the element has no such property.

parameters.name: element
parameters.summary: The converter element. Ignored when null.

classes.name: ChromaKey
classes.summary: ChromaKey video effect filter for green screen compositing. Implements the BaseElement.
classes.remarks: The six elements live inside a private bin with three ghost pads - background and chroma in, src out - and only that bin is added to the pipeline: videoconvertscale → capsfilter → compositor.sink_0 videoconvert → alpha → compositor.sink_1 compositor → videoconvert → src That is a Y-graph through request pads, not a run, so it has no atomic removal as a set of loose elements: SpecialRemoveElementRange describes a chain with one bypass edge and there is no single bypass that reconnects a two-input compositor's neighbours. As one bin it is one element to the pipeline, the removal is one edit, and the request pads live and die inside a bin nobody else touches. GitHub issue #944.

constructors.name: ChromaKey
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the ChromaKey class.

methods.name: IsAvailable
methods.summary: Determines whether this element is available. NuGet SDK redist should be included in your project.
methods.returns: true if this element is available; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Init
methods.summary: Initializes the specified pipeline.
methods.remarks: The bin is parented before it is filled, so a failure anywhere after that would leave an orphan bin in the pipeline for the rest of the run - the callers answer a failed Init with Dispose(), which releases the wrappers and never touches the pipeline. This wrapper takes it back out. Nothing outside is linked to it yet and it has never left the NULL state, so unparenting it here is the plain gst_bin_remove and not the graph edit Pipeline) has to do. In a finally rather than on the false return, because a refusal is not the only way out: a ChromaColor outside the three defined values throws from SetAlphaSettings, on the element created right after the bin is parented.
methods.returns: true if successful, false otherwise.

methods.name: BuildBin
methods.summary: Builds the bin and everything in it. See ChromaKeySettingsX), which owns the failure path.
methods.returns: true if successful, false otherwise.

methods.name: GetBackgroundPad
methods.summary: Gets the background input pad for connecting background video source.
methods.returns: The bin's background ghost pad.

methods.name: GetChromaPad
methods.summary: Gets the chroma input pad for connecting chroma video source (goes through chroma converter).
methods.returns: The bin's chroma ghost pad.

methods.name: SetSettings
methods.summary: Sets the chroma key settings.

methods.name: SetAlphaSettings
methods.summary: Configures the alpha filter settings based on chroma key parameters.
methods.remarks: Under SyncRoot for the whole push, not just the null check. ChromaKeyBlock's ten public setters all land here from the application's thread while its own CleanUp may be disposing this filter, and what teardown zeroes is the wrapper's handle rather than only the field - a zeroed handle in SetProperty is a silent GLib critical, not an exception. GitHub issues #948 and #951.

methods.name: SyncStateWithParent
methods.summary: Synchronizes the state with parent.

methods.name: RemoveFromPipeline
methods.summary: Removes from pipeline.
methods.remarks: One removal for the whole filter, because the pipeline holds one element: the bin. Six separate removals were six edits of a live graph with no rollback across them, and a partial failure left the filter half in. Refused here, nothing was removed and every field is still where it was. GitHub issue #944. One edit, not one blocked branch: SpecialRemoveElement finds its peers through static pads named sink / src, and this bin deliberately has no sink, so the flush and the idle probe both land on the output while the two input branches are only unlinked. On a live pipeline that can cut them mid-push. Blocking both inputs first is what a live removal would need; no caller does one today.
methods.returns: true if successful, false otherwise.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases unmanaged and - optionally - managed resources.
methods.remarks: Unpublish everything under SyncRoot, release outside it - the same three phases Boolean) uses, and for the same reasons. The flag is the base's to set, not this override's. Testing and setting it here left both halves outside the lock while the base sets it inside, so two concurrent Dispose() calls both passed the check and both released all six elements. The base's check-and-set is atomic with its own claim, so calling through and reading the answer is what makes one of them win; the early return below only skips work the base would skip too. Element, In and Out all alias _effectBin, so they have to be dropped before the base runs or it calls SetState(Null) on a wrapper this method already zeroed - "assertion 'GST_IS_ELEMENT (element)' failed". They are dropped inside the lock for the same reason unpublishes them inside it: a reader honouring the lock must not see them change under it. GitHub issue #948.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources.

methods.name: SetupMessageHandler
methods.summary: Subscribes to the pipeline bus messages to receive video mark detection notifications.
methods.remarks: A GStreamer bus supports a single watch source, and the owning MediaBlocksPipeline already holds it (AddSignalWatch in CreatePipeline), so a callback watch installed here always fails silently - the watch never attaches and detection never fires (GitHub issue #1052). Subscribe to the async "message" signal instead: it is delivered by the pipeline's signal watch on the GLib main loop, and each subscriber receives its own borrowed message wrapper, so no native source is owned here and nothing needs gst_bus_remove_watch.

methods.name: DetachMessageHandler
methods.summary: Unsubscribes from the pipeline bus messages, exactly once per successful attach.

methods.name: OnBusMessage
methods.summary: Handles bus messages from the simplevideomarkdetect element. The element posts messages with structure name "GstSimpleVideoMarkDetect" containing fields: have-pattern (boolean), timestamp/stream-time/running-time/duration (uint64) and data (uint64) - the detected pattern value.
methods.remarks: All managed handlers connected to one GLib signal share a single closure and a single per emission (Signal.AddDelegate combines them), and the pipeline's own handler - connected first, in CreatePipeline - disposes that wrapper in its finally. Running in the default (after) phase would therefore hand this filter a wrapper whose native handle is already zeroed: reading it raises NullReferenceException inside the marshalled call and aborts the whole handler chain. [ConnectBefore] puts this handler into the run-first phase, ahead of the pipeline's teardown of the wrapper. The message is only read here, never disposed.

parameters.name: o
parameters.summary: The bus object that raised the message signal.

parameters.name: args
parameters.summary: The message arguments. The wrapped message is borrowed - the bus dispatch owns its lifetime, so it must not be disposed here.

methods.remarks: The lock spans the build, which is more than SyncRoot asks of a teardown, and deliberately so: it is what keeps a concurrent ResizeVideoEffect) from reading a half-published filter. The failure path under it does reach SetState(State.Null), but not the unbounded kind - these elements were created a few lines earlier and were never linked into a running chain, so there is no streaming thread for it to wait on. That is the whole difference from the #838 wedge.

methods.name: ApplyVideoScaleProperties
methods.summary: Pushes the current _settings values onto the videoscale element. Safe to call while the pipeline is playing.

methods.name: ApplyCapsFilter
methods.summary: Builds a fresh single-structure caps from the current _settings width and height and assigns it to the capsfilter. This avoids the template-caps mutation pattern that fails on adaptive (DASH/HLS) sources whose downstream features include DMA/GL memory variants. PAR must be frozen. videoscale rewrites it to keep DAR on a size change even with add-borders=false (measured 1/1 → 9/16 on a 90° rotate); a live H.264 encoder and mp4mux then not-negotiate and the recording dies at one frame. GitHub issue #1514. Letterbox pins 1/1 so bars stay inside W×H. Stretch freezes the PAR from the first caps event so anamorphic sources keep theirs.

methods.name: FreezeStretchPar
methods.summary: On the first stretch caps event, remember that PAR and pin it on the capsfilter from the thread pool. Must not take SyncRoot here: this runs with the pad stream lock held, and ResizeVideoEffect) takes the lock then calls into GStreamer — the inverted order of issue #948.

methods.name: RemoveFromPipeline
methods.summary: Removes from pipeline.
methods.remarks: The lock is taken twice and held across nothing that can block, which is the contract SyncRoot asks for: the removal waits up to 2 s for the run to go idle, and holding the lock across that would stall every ResizeVideoEffect) push and the finalizer thread with it. _capsFilter is unpublished up front rather than after the removal, because releases it together with the rest of the run and a field still pointing at a released wrapper is exactly the zeroed handle this is meant to keep readers away from. A refusal puts it back, so the "on false every field is still where it was" promise holds; the only thing lost in that window is a caps push, and _settings keeps it for the next one. What dropping the lock across the removal does allow, and what holding it used to prevent, is a landing while the run is being taken out. That is not the defect being fixed here: the wrappers are alive for the whole of it, so the push reaches a real element rather than a zeroed handle. It does re-arm videoscale on its way out of the graph, which is wasted work and nothing worse. Buying that back would mean holding the lock across the 2 s idle probe, and stalling every push and the finalizer queue behind a removal is the trade #947 already made and had to revert.
methods.returns: true if successful, false otherwise.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases unmanaged and - optionally - managed resources.
methods.remarks: Only the capsfilter: the base already covers In, Element and Out, and this is the one member of the run it does not know about. Every owner that disposes this filter does so having never called Pipeline) - VideoRendererBlock.CleanUp, VideoResizeBlock.CleanUp, DecklinkVideoSink.Dispose, and VideoEffectsBlock when it builds one through VideoEffectsProcessor - so without this the wrapper was left to its finalizer and ToggleRef.QueueUnref's ThreadPool drain, which is issue #841's crash site. (A removal that was attempted and refused is not one of those paths: VideoEffectsBlock.RetireFilter returns before it disposes anything, and its gate-timeout path drops the filter without disposing it at all.) Safe while the element is still parented: the wrapper owns one reference and the bin a second, so this drops the count to one and cannot reach gst_element_dispose. The lock covers the field and nothing else, and the base call stays outside it: the base sets In, Element and Out to NULL state, and on an element that is still parented - which is every owner above - that is the unbounded call of the #838 trap. Holding across it would put that wedge in front of every other user of the lock, including on Android's view thread by way of VideoRendererBlock.SetOutputSize. It does not need to: the base takes the same lock itself to unpublish the three fields before it touches GStreamer, so a settings push can no longer reach a wrapper this is about to release. GitHub issue #948. is a convention here, matching the base class, and not a statement about the calling thread: nothing in this hierarchy declares a finalizer, so Dispose(false) never arrives - while the finalizer route that does reach this filter arrives as true, because ~MediaBlock runs the renderer block's CleanUp outside its own disposing guard and that calls the parameterless Dispose(). Do not read the guard as protection against the finalizer thread.

parameters.summary: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources.

classes.name: WmvOutputPtsRebaser
classes.summary: Zero-bases the output of an avenc_wmv1 encoder so its PTS/DTS align with the sibling audio stream before the ASF muxer.
classes.remarks: avenc_wmv1 is a GstVideoEncoder; gst-libav calls gst_video_encoder_set_min_pts with a large fixed min-pts guard, so the base class shifts every OUTPUT buffer's PTS/DTS forward by a fixed amount (observed as a ~1 hour offset on GStreamer 1.28.x) while the output segment stays 0-based. asfmux writes ASF presentation time straight from the buffer PTS and, unlike mp4mux/qtmux/matroskamux, does NOT re-base to running-time-zero, so video lands ~1 h ahead of the 0-based WMA audio and the two PTS ranges never overlap. A src-pad buffer probe strips the offset from each buffer's PTS/DTS, deriving the base from the first buffer so it survives any change to the gst-libav guard constant. NOTE: an identity single-segment or gst_pad_set_offset only shifts the segment/running-time, not the raw buffer PTS asfmux reads verbatim, so neither strips this offset — the buffer timestamps must be rewritten directly.

methods.name: Attach
methods.summary: Attaches the zero-basing buffer probe to the encoder's src pad.

methods.name: Detach
methods.summary: Removes the probe, releases the retained pad reference and resets the rebase origin so a subsequent Attach starts from a clean state.

methods.name: ProbeMethod
methods.remarks: info.Buffer is a transfer-none wrapper around the in-flight GstBuffer owned by the pipeline; we mutate its PTS/DTS in place and must NOT Dispose it. This runs on a native streaming thread, so any leaked managed exception would abort the process — the body is wrapped in try/catch.

methods.name: IsInvertibleScale
methods.summary: Whether cairo_scale can apply these factors to an identity-like CTM: cairo rejects a zero or non-finite determinant (_cairo_gstate_scale, then _cairo_matrix_is_invertible), and a finite non-zero product also means each factor is finite. A rejected scale leaves cr in INVALID_MATRIX, and every later draw on it is a no-op. A negative factor is valid and mirrors.

classes.name: CircularBuffer`1
classes.summary: A generic circular buffer implementation that allows efficient insertion and removal of elements at both ends of the buffer. When the buffer reaches full capacity, adding new elements will automatically remove elements from the opposite end.
classes.remarks: When writing to a full buffer:PushBack() removes the element at Front() (this[0])PushFront() removes the element at Back() (this[Size-1])This implementation is inspired by the Boost circular_buffer library: http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_53_0/libs/circular_buffer/doc/circular_buffer.html

constructors.name: CircularBuffer`1

parameters.summary: The maximum number of elements that the buffer can hold. Must be positive.

parameters.name: capacity
parameters.summary: The maximum number of elements that the buffer can hold. Must be positive.
