parameters.summary: Initial items to fill the buffer with. The length must not exceed the capacity. Tip: Use Skip(x).Take(y).ToArray() to build this parameter from any enumerable.

properties.name: Capacity
properties.summary: Gets the maximum capacity of the circular buffer.
properties.value: The maximum number of elements that can be stored in the buffer.

properties.name: IsFull
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the circular buffer is at full capacity.
properties.value: true if the buffer contains the maximum number of elements; otherwise, false.

properties.name: IsEmpty
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the circular buffer is empty.
properties.value: true if the buffer contains no elements; otherwise, false.

properties.name: Size
properties.summary: Gets the current number of elements contained in the circular buffer.
properties.value: The number of elements currently stored in the buffer.

properties.name: Item
properties.summary: Gets or sets the element at the specified index in the buffer.

methods.name: Front
methods.summary: Returns the element at the front of the buffer without removing it.
methods.returns: The element at the front of the buffer (equivalent to this[0]).

methods.name: Back
methods.summary: Returns the element at the back of the buffer without removing it.
methods.returns: The element at the back of the buffer (equivalent to this[Size - 1]).

methods.name: PushBack
methods.summary: Adds an element to the back of the circular buffer.
methods.remarks: After this operation, Back() and this[Size-1] will return the newly added element. If the buffer is full, the element at the front (Front()/this[0]) will be removed to make room for the new element.

parameters.name: item
parameters.summary: The element to add to the back of the buffer.

methods.name: PushFront
methods.summary: Adds an element to the front of the circular buffer.
methods.remarks: After this operation, Front() and this[0] will return the newly added element. If the buffer is full, the element at the back (Back()/this[Size-1]) will be removed to make room for the new element.

parameters.name: item
parameters.summary: The element to add to the front of the buffer.

methods.name: PopBack
methods.summary: Removes and discards the element at the back of the circular buffer.
methods.remarks: This operation decreases the buffer size by 1.

methods.name: PopFront
methods.summary: Removes and discards the element at the front of the circular buffer.
methods.remarks: This operation decreases the buffer size by 1.

methods.name: Clear
methods.summary: Removes all elements from the circular buffer.
methods.remarks: After this operation, Size will be 0 but Capacity remains unchanged. All elements in the internal buffer are set to their default values.

methods.name: ToArray
methods.summary: Copies all elements from the circular buffer to a new array.
methods.remarks: The returned array preserves the logical order of elements (from front to back), regardless of their physical arrangement in the internal buffer.
methods.returns: A new array containing copies of the elements in the buffer, ordered from front to back.

methods.name: ToArraySegments
methods.summary: Gets the contents of the buffer as two ArraySegment instances without copying the elements.
methods.remarks: This method provides a zero-copy view of the buffer contents, which is useful for performance-critical scenarios such as network operations (e.g., Send(IList<ArraySegment<byte>>)).The segments preserve the logical order of elements from front to back. Either or both segments may be empty depending on the buffer state.
methods.returns: An IList containing two ArraySegment instances that represent the buffer contents.

methods.name: GetEnumerator
methods.summary: Returns an enumerator that iterates through the circular buffer.
methods.remarks: The enumeration preserves the logical order of elements regardless of their physical arrangement in the internal buffer.
methods.returns: An enumerator that can be used to iterate through the buffer from front to back.

methods.name: System#Collections#IEnumerable#GetEnumerator
methods.summary: Returns a non-generic enumerator that iterates through the circular buffer.
methods.returns: An IEnumerator that can be used to iterate through the buffer.

methods.name: ThrowIfEmpty
methods.summary: Throws an InvalidOperationException if the buffer is empty.

parameters.name: message
parameters.summary: The error message to include in the exception. Defaults to "Cannot access an empty buffer."

methods.name: Increment
methods.summary: Increments the specified index by one, wrapping around to 0 when it reaches capacity.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: A reference to the index variable to increment.

methods.name: Decrement
methods.summary: Decrements the specified index by one, wrapping around to capacity-1 when it reaches 0.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: A reference to the index variable to decrement.

methods.name: InternalIndex
methods.summary: Converts a logical index (0 to Size-1) to the corresponding physical index in the internal buffer.
methods.returns: The corresponding physical index in the internal buffer array.

methods.name: ArrayOne
methods.summary: Gets the first contiguous segment of the circular buffer.
methods.remarks: The circular buffer may be split into two segments due to wrapping. This method returns the first segment, which starts at the logical front of the buffer.
methods.returns: An ArraySegment representing the first contiguous portion of the buffer contents.

methods.name: ArrayTwo
methods.summary: Gets the second contiguous segment of the circular buffer.
methods.remarks: The circular buffer may be split into two segments due to wrapping. This method returns the second segment, which contains any wrapped-around elements. May return an empty segment if all elements are contiguous in the first segment.
methods.returns: An ArraySegment representing the second contiguous portion of the buffer contents.

classes.name: CommandLineHelper

classes.remarks: This class handles complex command line parsing scenarios including quoted arguments, escaped quotes, and proper space handling within quoted strings.

methods.name: SplitCommandLineArgument
methods.summary: Splits a command line string into individual arguments, respecting quoted strings and escaped quotes.
methods.remarks: This method properly handles: - Arguments enclosed in double quotes that contain spaces - Escaped quotes (\") within arguments - Multiple consecutive spaces between arguments - Removal of enclosing quotes from quoted arguments

parameters.name: argumentString
parameters.summary: The command line string to be parsed. Can contain arguments separated by spaces, with support for quoted strings containing spaces and escaped quotes (\")

methods.returns: An array of strings where each element represents a single command line argument. Empty entries are automatically removed from the result.

methods.name: RemoveMatchingQuotes
methods.summary: Removes matching pairs of double quotes from a string, starting from the outermost pair.
methods.remarks: This method iteratively removes matching quote pairs from outside to inside. It preserves unmatched quotes and stops when no more matching pairs are found.

parameters.name: stringToTrim
parameters.summary: The string from which to remove matching quote pairs. May contain multiple pairs of quotes.

methods.returns: The input string with all matching pairs of double quotes removed. If quotes are unmatched, they are left in the string.

classes.name: ContextPropagator
classes.summary: Reflection-based helper that wires the SDK's BaseContext into UI views and other objects that expose a settable Context property. The mechanism is intentionally non-invasive: it does not require IVideoView (or any other public interface) to declare Context. Implementations that happen to have a settable Context property of a compatible type get it set; everything else is a no-op.
classes.remarks: Engine classes (MediaPlayerCoreX, VideoCaptureCoreX, classic Windows engines, renderer blocks) call this when a video view / handler is attached so the view's logging flows through the same Serilog pipeline as the engine, instead of dangling on a never-set property and falling back to Trace.

methods.name: Propagate
methods.summary: If target exposes a public, settable instance property named Context whose type is assignable from context, sets it. Otherwise no-op. Reflection failures are swallowed (best-effort wiring).

parameters.name: target
parameters.summary: The object to receive the context (e.g. an IVideoView implementation, a handler, or anything else with a Context property). Null is allowed.

classes.summary: Provides helper methods for working with Blackmagic DeckLink professional video hardware. This class contains extension methods and utilities for converting between DeckLink-specific formats and the framework's internal format representations.

methods.summary: Converts a DeckLink audio format to the framework's internal AudioFormatX representation.

parameters.summary: The DeckLink audio format to convert.

methods.returns: The corresponding AudioFormatX format. Returns S16LE as the default if the format is not recognized.

methods.name: GetVideoInfoFromMode
methods.summary: Extracts video format information from a DeckLink video mode. This method parses the DeckLink mode enumeration and returns the corresponding video resolution (width and height) and frame rate for the specified mode.
methods.remarks: Supports standard definition (NTSC/PAL), HD (720p/1080i/1080p), 2K DCI, and UHD 4K formats. For Unknown and unrecognized modes, returns width=0, height=0 and Empty. The values follow the display mode table of the DeckLink SDK, and an interlaced mode reports its frame rate, not its field rate: HD1080i50 is 25 fps. A DeckLink source block in an interlaced mode delivers twice that rate when its auto deinterlacing is enabled with DeinterlaceFields.All, which is the default. That includes NTSC2398_Widescreen but not NTSC2398, which is not deinterlaced. In the NTSC_P and PAL_P modes, including their widescreen variants, the caps of the GStreamer DeckLink plugin announce half of the rate returned here. SD modes report the stored size: their non-square pixel aspect ratio is not part of the result.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.summary: The DeckLink video mode to parse.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains the horizontal resolution in pixels for the specified mode.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains the vertical resolution in pixels for the specified mode.

parameters.name: framerate
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains the frame rate information for the specified mode.

classes.name: EncodedFrameRingBuffer
classes.summary: Thread-safe circular buffer specialized for encoded media frames. Stores the most recent N seconds of encoded video/audio frames in memory. Evicts frames based on time duration. When draining for recording, starts from the nearest video keyframe to ensure decodable output.

constructors.name: EncodedFrameRingBuffer
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the EncodedFrameRingBuffer class.

parameters.name: maxDuration
parameters.summary: Maximum duration of frames to keep in the buffer.

parameters.name: maxBytes
parameters.summary: Maximum buffer size in bytes. 0 for unlimited (time-based eviction only).

properties.name: TotalBytes
properties.summary: Gets the total bytes currently stored in the buffer.

properties.name: VideoFrameCount
properties.summary: Gets the number of video frames in the buffer.

properties.name: AudioFrameCount
properties.summary: Gets the number of audio frames in the buffer.

properties.name: BufferedDuration
properties.summary: Gets the buffered duration based on the oldest and newest video frame timestamps.

methods.name: PushVideoFrame
methods.summary: Pushes an encoded video frame into the buffer. Evicts oldest frames if the buffer exceeds the configured duration or byte limit.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: The encoded video frame to add.

methods.name: PushAudioFrame
methods.summary: Pushes an encoded audio frame into the buffer. Evicts audio frames that fall outside the video frame time window.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: The encoded audio frame to add.

methods.name: DrainFromKeyframe
methods.summary: Drains the buffer starting from the earliest video keyframe. Returns all video and audio frames from that keyframe forward, interleaved by PTS. The buffer is cleared after draining.
methods.returns: A list of encoded media frames (video + audio interleaved by PTS) starting from the nearest keyframe. Returns an empty list if no keyframe is found.

methods.name: DrainFromKeyframeSeparate
methods.summary: Drains the buffer starting from the earliest video keyframe. Returns video and audio frames separately, each in their original arrival order (decode order for video, which is critical for H264 with B-frames). The buffer is cleared after draining.

methods.name: ClearVideo
methods.summary: Drops the buffered video frames. Audio frames stay, so a video format change does not throw away the audio span the next file can still mux.

methods.name: ClearAudio
methods.summary: Drops the buffered audio frames. Video frames stay.

methods.name: Clear
methods.summary: Clears all frames from the buffer and releases their data.

methods.name: ClearFrameList
methods.summary: Disposes one stream's frames and subtracts them from the byte total. Must be called under _lock.

methods.name: EvictOldVideoFrames
methods.summary: Evicts video frames older than the configured maximum duration. Measured relative to the newest video frame's PTS.

methods.name: EvictOldAudioFrames
methods.summary: Evicts audio frames that fall outside the video frame time window.

methods.name: EvictByByteLimit
methods.summary: Evicts oldest video and audio frames when byte limit is exceeded. Evicts video first (keeping at least 1), then audio if still over.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases all resources used by the buffer.

methods.name: Redact
methods.summary: Masks the credentials of every URL in text, each as String) does, a password= value outside a URL, and the value of an HTTP Authorization header.
methods.remarks: A URL is a scheme, :// and everything up to whitespace, a quote or an angle bracket. Bounding the greedy userinfo mask to one URL keeps it from running on to an e-mail address later in the text. A URL whose authority holds a : and no @ - a password with a space or quote, rtsp://admin:my pass@cam - runs on to the next @ on its line; past a port (host:554) only when that @ is within the next word. The scheme is found by walking back from each ://, which stays linear on long alphanumeric runs and finds a scheme glued to the text before it (source_rtsp://, 1.rtsp://).

methods.name: RedactUrl

Both err towards masking more than the credential, except a path value that itself contains _word=. Credentials under other key names are not recognized.

classes.name: ObservableCollectionHelper

parameters.name: collection

parameters.name: items

parameters.name: collection

parameters.name: items

methods.summary: Removes all occurrences of the specified items from the ObservableCollection`1.

parameters.summary: The collection to remove items from.

parameters.name: items

parameters.name: index

parameters.name: count

parameters.name: index

methods.name: ToObservableCollection``1
methods.summary: Converts an array to an ObservableCollection`1.
methods.remarks: This method creates a new ObservableCollection and copies all items from the source array. The original array remains unchanged.
methods.returns: A new ObservableCollection`1 containing all items from the source array.

classes.name: PathHelper
classes.summary: Provides utility methods for file path operations and directory management.
classes.remarks: This internal helper class contains static methods for common path-related operations such as creating directory structures, extracting file extensions, and determining the executing assembly's path.

methods.name: CreateAllPath
methods.summary: Creates all directories in the path of the specified filename if they don't already exist.
methods.remarks: This method extracts the directory path from the provided filename and creates all necessary directories in the hierarchy. If the directory already exists, no action is taken. If the filename parameter contains no directory information, no directories are created.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The full path of the file for which to create the directory structure.

methods.name: ValidateOutputPath
methods.summary: Validates that the output file path is writable by creating the directory structure and performing a non-destructive write test. This catches path issues early with a clear exception rather than letting GStreamer fail later with hard-to-diagnose errors.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The full path of the output file to validate.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: Optional context for error logging and diagnostics.

methods.name: CheckWindowsWriterPath
methods.summary: Checks an output path against the MaxWindowsWriterPath limit of the Windows writer named by writerName, which otherwise fails only at Run, with no hint of the cause.

parameters.name: writerName
parameters.summary: The Windows writer behind the output format; null for any other writer.

methods.returns: The error to report when the path is too long; otherwise null.

methods.name: GetAssemblyPath
methods.summary: Determines and returns the directory path of the currently executing assembly.
methods.remarks: This method attempts to retrieve the assembly path using multiple fallback strategies: First attempts to get the location of the executing assemblyFalls back to AppContext.BaseDirectory if the first attempt returns null or emptyFinally attempts to get the entry assembly location if previous attempts fail This approach ensures compatibility across different hosting scenarios including single-file deployments, self-contained applications, and traditional deployments. If none of the strategies succeed, an empty string is returned to keep the contract uniform for callers (no null sentinel).
methods.returns: The directory path where the executing assembly is located, or an empty string if unable to determine. This method never returns null.

classes.name: PermissionsHelper
classes.summary: Cross-platform helper for permissions that are required for media capture.

methods.name: CheckScreenRecordingPermission
methods.summary: Checks whether the running app has Screen Recording permission on macOS / Mac Catalyst.
methods.remarks: macOS caches the TCC decision per process. If the user grants the permission after the app has already started, the process must be relaunched before CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess reports true. Without the permission, AVCaptureScreenInput initWithDisplayID: returns nil, which makes AVCaptureSession addInput: throw NSInvalidArgumentException and terminate the process.
methods.returns: Granted when the app can capture the screen, Denied when the user has not allowed it, or NotApplicable on platforms that do not require this permission.

methods.name: RequestScreenRecordingPermission
methods.summary: Requests Screen Recording permission on macOS / Mac Catalyst. The first call presents the system TCC dialog; subsequent calls return the cached state without reprompting.
methods.remarks: The system dialog must be posted from the main thread; this method marshals the call as needed. A false return value immediately after a grant is normal — macOS only reevaluates TCC state at process start. Ask the user to relaunch the app and re-check with BaseContext).
methods.returns: true if permission is already granted for the current process, false otherwise (the user must relaunch the app after approving in System Settings).

classes.name: PhotoGalleryHelper
classes.summary: Provides helper methods for adding media files (photos and videos) to device galleries on mobile platforms. This class contains platform-specific implementations for Android and iOS to save media files to the device's photo/video gallery, making them accessible through the native gallery applications.

classes.name: ProcessHelper
classes.summary: Provides utility methods for process execution and management. This class contains helper methods for running processes with elevated privileges.

methods.name: RunProcessAsAdmin
methods.summary: Runs a process with administrator privileges.
methods.remarks: This method uses the "runas" verb to request administrator privileges through UAC (User Account Control). The calling process must have permission to elevate, and the user must approve the UAC prompt. The method will wait for the process to complete before returning.

parameters.name: exeName
parameters.summary: The full path or name of the executable file to run.

parameters.name: workingDir
parameters.summary: The working directory for the process. This is where the process will start execution.

parameters.name: parameters
parameters.summary: Command-line parameters to pass to the executable.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: Optional logging context. When null, errors fall through to Trace.

methods.returns: The exit code of the process if successful; 1223 if the user cancelled the UAC elevation prompt; -1 if an error occurred during process execution.

classes.name: RandomHelper
classes.summary: Provides utility methods for generating random values and unique identifiers.
classes.remarks: This class offers thread-safe methods for generating random integers and timestamp-based unique identifiers useful for file naming, logging, or tracking purposes.

methods.name: GetWithDate
methods.summary: Generates a unique string identifier combining the current timestamp with a random number.
methods.remarks: This method is useful for generating unique file names, log entries, or any identifier that requires both temporal ordering and uniqueness. The timestamp ensures chronological sorting while the random number helps prevent collisions when called multiple times within the same millisecond.
methods.returns: A string in the format "YYYY_M_D_H_m_s_ms_randomNumber" where each component represents the current date/time values and a random integer. For example: "2022_2_4_14_30_45_123_456789".

methods.name: Get
methods.summary: Generates a non-negative random integer.
methods.remarks: This method uses the shared Random instance to generate values. For thread-safe operations in multi-threaded scenarios, consider implementing additional synchronization if needed.
methods.returns: A 32-bit signed integer greater than or equal to 0 and less than MaxValue.

classes.name: SambaHelper
classes.summary: Helper class for SMB/CIFS share authentication using Windows networking APIs.

methods.name: ConnectToShare
methods.summary: Connects to an SMB share with credentials.
methods.remarks: The argument is a managed and therefore cannot be reliably zeroed (the CLR is free to copy or relocate string instances during GC). This is a known limitation — callers that need stronger guarantees should hold the password in a or pinned char[] upstream and pass the decoded form only at the lowest level. We minimize residual exposure by dropping our local references as soon as WNetAddConnection2 returns and not stashing any credential field on this helper.

parameters.name: username
parameters.summary: The username. When null/empty, the call is a no-op (the caller is expected to access the share anonymously / as the current user).

parameters.name: password
parameters.summary: The password. When non-empty, username must also be supplied — otherwise the call is rejected so a half-configured credential pair can't silently fall through to anonymous access.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: Optional logging context. When null, errors fall through to Trace.

methods.returns: true if the share was authenticated successfully or no credentials were supplied (anonymous path). false when authentication was attempted and failed, or when only a password (no username) was supplied.

methods.name: DisconnectFromShare
methods.summary: Disconnects from an SMB share.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: Optional logging context. When null, warnings fall through to Trace.

classes.name: SentryHelper
classes.summary: Provides helper functionality for Sentry error reporting integration. This class manages a list of error messages that should be ignored and not reported to Sentry.

methods.name: #cctor
methods.summary: Initializes static members of the SentryHelper class. Populates the ignore list with predefined error messages that should not be reported to Sentry. These include license-related messages, connection errors, codec issues, and expected operational messages.

methods.name: IsIgnored
methods.summary: Determines whether the specified error message should be ignored by Sentry error reporting.

parameters.name: msg
parameters.summary: The error message to check against the ignore list.

methods.returns: true if the message is in the ignore list and should not be reported to Sentry; otherwise, false.

methods.name: ContainsIgnoredFragment
methods.summary: Determines whether the specified error message contains any of the ignored fragments.
methods.remarks: This is the test the list was written for. Every entry in it is a fragment or a prefix ("[tcp @", "mpeg4", "Access to the path "), so String), which compares whole strings, can essentially never match one. String) is left alone because it is a public member on a shipped surface; new callers should use this.

parameters.name: msg
parameters.summary: The error message to check against the ignore list.

methods.returns: true when the message contains an ignored fragment; otherwise, false.

classes.name: SerilogConverters
classes.summary: Provides extension methods for converting between Serilog log levels and VisioForge debug levels. This internal utility class facilitates interoperability between the Serilog logging framework and VisioForge's internal debugging system.

methods.name: To
methods.summary: Converts a Serilog LogEventLevel to a corresponding VisioForge DebugLevel. This extension method maps multiple Serilog verbosity levels to a simplified three-tier debug level system.

parameters.name: level
parameters.summary: The Serilog log event level to convert.

methods.returns: A DebugLevel value corresponding to the input Serilog level: - Verbose, Debug, and Information map to Info - Warning maps to Warning - Error and Fatal map to Error

classes.name: SizeHelper
classes.summary: Provides extension methods for converting between System.Drawing.Size and VisioForge.Core.Types.Size types. methods.summary: Converts a System.Drawing.Size object to a VisioForge.Core.Types.Size object.

methods.returns: A new VisioForge.Core.Types.Size object with the same width and height values as the input System.Drawing.Size object.

methods.name: ToSize
methods.summary: Converts a VisioForge.Core.Types.Size object to a System.Drawing.Size object.

parameters.name: sz

methods.returns: A new System.Drawing.Size object with the same width and height values as the input VisioForge.Core.Types.Size object.

classes.name: SkiaHelper

parameters.summary: The width of the image in pixels.

parameters.name: height

parameters.name: stride

methods.summary: Copies the rows of 4-byte pixels that fit in dataSize bytes into a new bitmap of the platform colour type, swapping red and blue when the source byte order differs from it.

parameters.name: width

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: The height of the image in pixels.

methods.returns: A new SKBitmap containing the converted image data.

methods.summary: Copies rows rows of 4-byte pixels into the bitmap as they are when the bitmap's colour type already has the source byte order, and with red and blue swapped otherwise. methods.name: VideoFrameRGBToSKBitmap
methods.summary: Converts a VideoFrameX containing RGB data to an SKBitmap with the platform colour type.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: The VideoFrameX containing RGB pixel data.

methods.returns: A new SKBitmap containing the converted image data.

methods.name: VideoFrameBGRAToSKBitmap
methods.summary: Converts a VideoFrameX containing BGRA data to an SKBitmap with the platform colour type. Padded rows are copied honouring Stride.

parameters.name: frame

methods.returns: A new SKBitmap containing the image data.

classes.name: TrialHelper
classes.summary: Cross-platform trial period enforcement with dual-location file storage. Stores trial start date in two files to prevent bypass via deletion of a single file. Both files live under %LocalApplicationData%\VisioForge\ on every platform — the registry-based primary on Windows was removed because MSIX/AppX-deployed apps (MAUI Windows, WinUI) virtualize HKCU through Helium, so each packaged app sees its own private registry hive that survives the global wipe and silently keeps the trial timer alive across "reset" attempts.
classes.remarks: Tamper resistance: each file payload is "filetime|HMAC-SHA256(filetime)" using a fixed obfuscation key. A reader who edits the FileTime without recomputing the MAC produces a payload whose HMAC no longer matches; String@) fails closed on it with TamperedMessage instead of failing open. Genuine read errors (file missing, permissions, IO) still fail-open so legitimate users aren't locked out by transient disk problems. Path choice: LocalApplicationData resolves to the global %LocalAppData% for sideloaded MAUI MSIX apps with FullTrust (Win32 file APIs are NOT virtualized for those, only HKCU is). On mobile (iOS / Android) the same call returns the per-app sandbox — that's an OS-level constraint, the trial is necessarily per-app there. On Mac Catalyst it is ~/Documents, where opening a file raises a privacy prompt and blocks until it is answered, so Application Support is used.

methods.name: CheckTrialDate
methods.summary: Checks whether the application trial period is still active. Uses dual-location storage — deleting one location does not reset the trial. Returns false if the trial has expired, clock backdating is detected, or the stored trial state has been tampered with (HMAC mismatch). Returns true on transient errors (fail-open) so legitimate users with disk glitches aren't locked out.

methods.name: CheckTrialDate
methods.summary: Same as BaseContext); on false, failureMessage is the error to report: ExpiredMessage, TamperedMessage or ClockBehindMessage. It is null when the check passes.

classes.name: UriHelper
classes.summary: Provides extension methods for Uri objects to simplify common URI operations such as extracting credentials, checking URI types, and formatting URI strings.

methods.name: ResolveHostInUri
methods.summary: Resolves the DNS hostname inside the given URI string to a literal IP address (IPv4 preferred) and substitutes it in place. This is a workaround for a race in the GLib threaded resolver (gthreadedresolver.ccancelled_cb assertion on g_cancellable_is_cancelled) that fires when multiple in-flight async DNS lookups are cancelled simultaneously — typical when several network sinks/sources running with AutoReconnect lose connectivity at once. The assertion calls abort() and kills the host process. Passing a pre-resolved IP to the native element skips the GIO resolver entirely.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.summary: URI in string form (for example srt://host:1234?mode=caller).

methods.returns: The URI with hostname replaced by a resolved IP, or the original URI unchanged when the host is already an IP literal, when parsing fails, when DNS resolution fails, or when only IPv6 results are available (we deliberately do not substitute IPv6 — that would require teaching String) about bracketed authorities, and in the SRT crash scenario that motivated this helper the targets are always reachable over IPv4). In all skipped cases the native element gets a chance to try again itself.

methods.name: ReplaceHostInUri
methods.summary: Pure-string substitution of the host portion of a URI. Handles scheme://user:pass@host:port/path?q#f correctly — in particular, userinfo (with a colon between user and password) is preserved rather than being mis-detected as a port separator. Internal so the substitution logic can be unit-tested independently of Dns.

parameters.name: newHost
parameters.summary: Replacement host (IP literal or another hostname).

methods.returns: The URI with the host substring replaced, or the original string when the URI has no scheme:// prefix.

methods.name: InsertUserInfo
methods.summary: Inserts a URL-escaped login:password@ userinfo prefix into the authority of a root URI string (right after the scheme://). The login and password are percent-encoded with String) so reserved characters (@ : / ? # % space, ...) in a credential do not corrupt the URI that the native IP-camera filters (VLC/LAV/FFMPEG/NDI/MJPEG/RTSP) parse. Internal so the substitution can be unit-tested independently of a live capture graph.

parameters.name: rootUri
parameters.summary: Credential-free root URI string, e.g. rtsp://cam.local:554/stream.

parameters.name: login
parameters.summary: The login as a literal (un-pre-encoded) credential; the method percent-encodes it, preserving leading/trailing whitespace as %20 rather than trimming it.

parameters.name: password
parameters.summary: The password as a literal (un-pre-encoded) credential; percent-encoded the same way.

methods.returns: The URI string with the escaped userinfo inserted, or the original string unchanged when it has no :// authority marker.

methods.name: ApplyCredentials
methods.summary: Returns the URL an engine that reads credentials only from the URL opens: url with the login and password as its userinfo. A blank password is sent as login:@, because FFmpeg answers a challenge only when the userinfo has the colon.

parameters.name: login
parameters.summary: The literal login. Empty or whitespace uses the login in the URL, if any.

methods.returns: The root URI string to open. A URL with its own password, with no host, with an empty userinfo, or on a UDP or RTP scheme, where VLC reads the part before @ as a source address, is returned as it is. A login with no password or a blank one in the URL is replaced.

methods.name: GetNetworkHost
methods.summary: Host string suitable for a GStreamer address/host property or a .NET socket connect: IPv6 brackets stripped, zone id unescaped. Host keeps the brackets and drops the zone; DnsSafeHost keeps the zone percent-escaped. Only %25 is decoded to % — String) would also decode a Windows numeric zone such as %12 into a raw byte.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.summary: The URI to take the host from. Null yields an empty string.

methods.returns: The unbracketed host, or an empty string when the URI has no host.

methods.name: GetUsername
methods.summary: Extracts the username from the URI's UserInfo component.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.summary: The URI from which to extract the username.

methods.returns: The username portion of the UserInfo, or an empty string if no username is present.

methods.name: GetPassword
methods.summary: Extracts the password from the URI's UserInfo component.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.summary: The URI from which to extract the password.

methods.returns: The password portion of the UserInfo (after the colon), or an empty string if no password is present.

methods.summary: Determines whether the specified URI is null or represents an empty URI string.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.summary: The URI to check for emptiness.

methods.returns: true if the URI is null or its string representation is empty; otherwise, false.

methods.summary: Converts the URI to a string representation, removing trailing slashes for non-HTTP URIs. HTTP and HTTPS URIs are returned as-is to maintain standard web URL formatting.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.summary: The URI to convert to a root URI string.

The temporary bitmap is disposed after conversion. If the source array is null, the jpeg output parameter will be set to null.

The caller is responsible for freeing the memory using Marshal.FreeCoTaskMem when done. If the source pointer is null, both output parameters will be set to zero/IntPtr.Zero.

parameters.name: source

parameters.name: sourceSize

parameters.name: srcArray

parameters.name: srcWidth

parameters.name: srcHeight

parameters.name: pixelFormat
parameters.summary: The pixel format of the source data.

parameters.name: destBmp
parameters.summary: A pre-existing destination bitmap that must match the specified dimensions and pixel format.

methods.name: BitmapToIntPtrFlip
methods.summary: Converts a bitmap to raw image data with vertical flip.
methods.remarks: This method flips the bitmap vertically before copying the data, then restores the original orientation. The destination pointer must be pre-allocated with sufficient memory. If parameters don't match or destPtr is null, the method returns without modification.

parameters.name: width

parameters.name: height

methods.name: ResizeImage
methods.summary: Extension method that resizes an image to the specified dimensions.
methods.remarks: The method uses different Graphics settings based on the fast parameter: - Fast mode: Uses NearestNeighbor interpolation, HighSpeed smoothing, and SourceCopy compositing for maximum performance. - Quality mode: Uses HighQualityBicubic interpolation, HighQuality smoothing, and proper pixel offset for best visual quality. The original image is disposed after the operation, so ensure you don't need it afterwards.

parameters.name: image
parameters.summary: The source image to resize. This image will be disposed after resizing.

parameters.name: fast
parameters.summary: If set to true, uses fast but lower quality resizing (NearestNeighbor interpolation); if false, uses high quality resizing (HighQualityBicubic interpolation).

methods.returns: A new Bitmap containing the resized image.

methods.name: SaveFrame
methods.summary: Saves raw image data to a bitmap file.
methods.remarks: This method converts the raw image data to a bitmap and saves it in BMP format. The bitmap is automatically disposed after saving.

methods.remarks: This method creates a new bitmap with dimensions matching the crop rectangle and copies the specified region from the source. The source bitmap is not modified or disposed.

parameters.name: cropRect
parameters.summary: The rectangle defining the crop area in the source bitmap.

methods.returns: A new Bitmap containing only the cropped area.

methods.name: Convert
methods.summary: Converts a bitmap to a different pixel format.
methods.remarks: This method creates a new bitmap with the target pixel format and copies the image data from the source using GDI+ Graphics drawing. The source bitmap is not modified or disposed.
methods.returns: A new Bitmap with the specified pixel format containing the same image data.

methods.name: RGBBitmapToRAWImage
methods.summary: Converts an RGB bitmap to a RAWImage object.
methods.remarks: This method allocates a new RAWImage structure, copies the bitmap data in RGB24 format, and sets the appropriate width, height, stride, and colorspace properties. The returned RAWImage must be properly disposed to free unmanaged memory.
methods.returns: A new RAWImage object containing the bitmap data in RGB format.

methods.name: RGBBitmapToRAWVideoFrame
methods.summary: Converts an RGB bitmap to a RAWVideoFrame object.
methods.remarks: This method allocates a new RAWVideoFrame structure with initialized RAWBaseVideoInfo, copies the bitmap data in RGB24 format, and sets the appropriate properties. The returned RAWVideoFrame must be properly disposed to free unmanaged memory.
methods.returns: A new RAWVideoFrame object containing the bitmap data in RGB format.

methods.name: RGBBitmapToVideoFrame
methods.summary: Converts an RGB bitmap to a VideoFrame object.
methods.remarks: This method allocates a new VideoFrame structure with initialized RAWBaseVideoInfo, copies the bitmap data in RGB24 format, and sets the appropriate properties. The returned VideoFrame must be properly disposed to free unmanaged memory.
methods.returns: A new VideoFrame object containing the bitmap data in RGB format.

methods.name: RGBBitmapToVideoFrameX
methods.summary: Converts an RGB bitmap to a VideoFrameX object.
methods.remarks: This method allocates a new VideoFrameX structure, copies the bitmap data in RGB24 format, and sets the appropriate width, height, stride, and format properties. The returned VideoFrameX must be properly disposed to free unmanaged memory.
methods.returns: A new VideoFrameX object containing the bitmap data in RGB format.

methods.name: ARGBBitmapToVideoFrameX
methods.summary: Converts an ARGB bitmap to a VideoFrameX object.
methods.remarks: This method allocates a new VideoFrameX structure, copies the bitmap data in ARGB32 format, and sets the appropriate width, height, stride, and format properties. The returned VideoFrameX must be properly disposed to free unmanaged memory.

parameters.name: bitmap
parameters.summary: The source bitmap to convert (must be in ARGB format).

methods.returns: A new VideoFrameX object containing the bitmap data in ARGB format.

methods.name: RGBABitmapToRAWImage
methods.summary: Converts an RGBA bitmap to a RAWVideoFrame object.
methods.remarks: This method allocates a new RAWVideoFrame structure with initialized RAWBaseVideoInfo, copies the bitmap data in RGBA32 format, and sets the appropriate properties. The returned RAWVideoFrame must be properly disposed to free unmanaged memory.

parameters.name: bitmap
parameters.summary: The source bitmap to convert (must be in RGBA format).

methods.returns: A new RAWVideoFrame object containing the bitmap data in RGBA format.

methods.name: MeasureTextFake
methods.summary: Measures the size of text when rendered with the specified font.
methods.remarks: This method creates a temporary 100x100 bitmap and Graphics object to measure the text size. It's called "fake" because it uses a temporary bitmap rather than measuring against an actual target surface. The method is useful for pre-calculating text dimensions before rendering.

parameters.name: font
parameters.summary: The font to use for measurement.

methods.returns: A Size structure representing the dimensions of the rendered text.

methods.name: GenerateImageWithText
methods.summary: Generates a bitmap image containing the specified text.
methods.remarks: This method uses Arial 24pt font to render black text on a white background. The bitmap size is automatically calculated to fit the text dimensions. The caller is responsible for disposing the returned bitmap when no longer needed.

parameters.name: text
parameters.summary: The text to render in the image.

methods.returns: A new Bitmap containing the rendered text on a white background.

classes.name: DPIHelper
classes.summary: Provides utility methods for retrieving DPI (dots per inch) information for monitors.
classes.remarks: This helper class wraps Windows API calls to query monitor DPI settings, which is essential for proper scaling and rendering on high-DPI displays. It supports different DPI awareness modes including Effective, Angular, and Raw DPI measurements.

methods.name: GetDpi
methods.summary: Retrieves the DPI values for the monitor containing the specified bounds.
methods.remarks: This method determines which monitor contains the specified bounds by checking a point within the bounds, then queries the DPI information for that monitor. If no monitor is found at the specified location, the nearest monitor is used.

parameters.name: monitorBounds
parameters.summary: The rectangle defining the monitor bounds to query.

parameters.name: dpiType
parameters.summary: The type of DPI measurement to retrieve (Effective, Angular, or Raw).

parameters.name: dpiX
parameters.summary: Output parameter that receives the horizontal DPI value.

parameters.name: dpiY
parameters.summary: Output parameter that receives the vertical DPI value.

methods.name: EnterOwnerDpiContext
methods.summary: Puts the calling thread into the DPI awareness context of owner, so that every window created and every coordinate read or written through user32 from here on speaks that window's coordinates rather than the process's.
methods.remarks: The window's own context is taken as it is, rather than mapped through GetAwarenessFromDpiAwarenessContext the way DSScreenSource does: that one wants to read in physical pixels, this one wants to match the owner exactly. A context read off a live window is by definition one this OS supports.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.summary: The window whose context to adopt.

methods.returns: The thread's previous context, to hand back to IntPtr), or Zero when nothing was changed.

methods.name: LeaveDpiContext
methods.summary: Restores what IntPtr) returned.

parameters.summary: The context to go back to; Zero does nothing.

methods.summary: Retrieves a handle to the monitor that contains a specified point.

parameters.summary: Determines the function's return value if the point is not contained within any monitor.

methods.returns: A handle to the monitor.

methods.summary: Queries the DPI of a display.

parameters.summary: The type of DPI being queried.

parameters.summary: The DPI in the X direction.

parameters.summary: The DPI in the Y direction.

classes.name: ProcessExitHelper

properties.name: IsProcessExiting
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the process is exiting. .NET Framework finalizes reachable objects then, while a graph left running may still use what they own; the OS reclaims everything, so a finalizer that sees this releases nothing. False on AppDomain unload, where the process lives on (HasShutdownStarted is true there as well, measured on net472), and always false for a finalizer on .NET (Core).

classes.name: RegistryHelper
classes.summary: Provides utility methods for managing application trial period information in the Windows Registry.
classes.remarks: This helper class stores and validates trial period information by reading and writing to the Windows Registry under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\VisioForge. It is used internally to track when a trial period begins and whether it has expired.

methods.name: CheckTrialDate
methods.summary: Checks whether the application trial period is still active.
methods.remarks: This method reads or creates a trial date registry entry under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\VisioForge\TrialDate. If the entry doesn't exist, it creates it with the current date and time. The method then compares the stored date with the current UTC time to determine if more than 30 days have elapsed. Any exceptions during registry access are caught and the method returns true (allowing the trial to continue).
methods.returns: true if the trial is active (less than 30 days have passed since the trial start date); otherwise, false.

classes.name: WindowHelper
classes.summary: Provides utility methods for working with Windows windows and processes.
classes.remarks: This helper class contains methods for enumerating window handles associated with processes and retrieving window titles. It wraps Windows API calls to interact with the window management system.

methods.name: EnumerateProcessWindowHandles
methods.summary: Enumerates all window handles associated with a specific process.
methods.remarks: This method iterates through all threads in the specified process and enumerates the windows associated with each thread using the Windows API EnumThreadWindows function. It collects all window handles into a list and returns them.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.summary: The process identifier to enumerate windows for.

methods.returns: An IEnumerable`1 containing all window handles belonging to the process.

methods.name: GetWindowNamesByProcessName
methods.summary: Retrieves the titles of all windows associated with a process by its name.
methods.remarks: This method finds the first process matching the specified name, enumerates all its windows, and retrieves the window title for each window by sending a WM_GETTEXT message. Empty or untitled windows will return empty strings in the array.

parameters.name: processName
parameters.summary: The name of the process (without .exe extension) to query windows for.

methods.returns: An array of strings containing the titles of all windows belonging to the specified process.

classes.name: ISkin
classes.summary: Defines the contract for UI skin implementations that provide theming and styling capabilities. Implementations of this interface supply visual assets and styling data for media player and capture control UI elements.
classes.remarks: Skins provide visual customization by defining images and styles for various UI elements such as buttons, sliders, and control panels. The skin system supports multiple visual states (base, hover, pressed, disabled) for interactive elements, enabling rich visual feedback during user interaction.

methods.name: GetName
methods.summary: Gets the display name of the skin for identification purposes.
methods.remarks: The name should be unique across all loaded skins to allow proper identification and retrieval via String).
methods.returns: A string containing the human-readable name of the skin used for selection and display in user interfaces.

methods.name: GetElement
methods.summary: Retrieves the skin element data for a specific UI element type.
methods.remarks: The returned SkinElementData contains image data for multiple visual states (base, hover, pressed, disabled) and indicates whether the images are in SVG or raster format.

parameters.name: element
parameters.summary: The type of UI element to retrieve skin data for.

methods.returns: A SkinElementData object containing the styling information for the specified element type, or null if the element is not defined in this skin.

classes.name: Skin
classes.summary: Represents a complete skin theme for the UI, containing styling information for various UI elements. Implements the ISkin interface.
classes.remarks: A skin encapsulates all visual assets needed to theme media player and capture control interfaces, including button images, slider styles, control panel layouts, and color schemes. Skins can be loaded from various sources: Embedded resources in assemblies (.vfskin files)ZIP archives containing skin elementsFile system directories with individual element filesByte arrays with compressed skin data Each UI element can have multiple visual states (base, hover, pressed, disabled) and supports both SVG and raster image formats. The skin also defines color schemes for backgrounds, text, playlists, and hover effects.

constructors.name: Skin
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the Skin class with empty element collection.
constructors.remarks: After construction, the skin must be populated with element data using the Byte[]) method or loaded through SkinManager utility methods.

properties.name: Context
properties.summary: SDK logging context. Set by SkinManager when a skin is loaded. When null, parse failures fall back to Trace.

properties.name: BackgroundColor
properties.summary: Gets or sets the primary background color for the UI.
properties.value: An SKColor value representing the main background color, or null if not defined in the skin. This color is typically used for the main control panel and UI container backgrounds.

properties.name: TextColor
properties.summary: Gets or sets the primary text color for UI labels and text elements.
properties.value: An SKColor value representing the text color, or null if not defined in the skin. This color applies to labels, time displays, and other textual information in the UI.

properties.name: PlaylistItemBackgroundColor
properties.summary: Gets or sets the background color for individual playlist items.
properties.value: An SKColor value for playlist item backgrounds, or null if not defined. This color is used for each media item entry in playlist views.

properties.name: PlaylistBackgroundColor
properties.summary: Gets or sets the background color for the playlist container.
properties.value: An SKColor value for the overall playlist background, or null if not defined. This color provides the backdrop behind all playlist items.

properties.name: PlaylistTextColor
properties.summary: Gets or sets the text color for playlist item labels.
properties.value: An SKColor value for playlist text, or null if not defined. This color is applied to media titles, durations, and other text within playlist items.

properties.name: ButtonHoverColor
properties.summary: Gets or sets the fallback color applied to buttons on hover when no hover image is available.
properties.value: An SKColor value used as a color overlay or tint on buttons during hover state, or null if not defined. This provides visual feedback when a specific hover image is not included in the skin element data.

properties.name: WPFSeekingSliderStyle
properties.summary: Gets or sets the XAML style data for WPF seeking slider controls.
properties.value: A byte array containing the UTF-8 encoded XAML style definition for video seeking sliders, or null if not defined. This style customizes the appearance and behavior of the timeline scrubber.

properties.name: WPFSliderStyle
properties.summary: Gets or sets the XAML style data for WPF volume slider controls.
properties.value: A byte array containing the UTF-8 encoded XAML style definition for volume sliders, or null if not defined. This style customizes the appearance of audio volume adjustment controls.

properties.name: WPFPlayerControls
properties.summary: Gets or sets the XAML template data for WPF media player control panel.
properties.value: A byte array containing the UTF-8 encoded XAML control template for the complete player UI, or null if not defined. This template defines the layout and structure of all player controls.

properties.name: WPFCaptureControls
properties.summary: Gets or sets the XAML template data for WPF capture control panel.
properties.value: A byte array containing the UTF-8 encoded XAML control template for capture/recording interfaces, or null if not defined. This template defines the layout of camera and recording controls.

properties.name: WPFPlaylist
properties.summary: Gets or sets the XAML template data for WPF playlist control.
properties.value: A byte array containing the UTF-8 encoded XAML control template for playlist displays, or null if not defined. This template defines how playlist items are displayed and organized.

methods.name: GetElement
methods.summary: Retrieves the skin element data for the specified UI element type.
methods.remarks: If an element is not defined in the skin, controls should fall back to default styling or hide the element. The returned SkinElementData contains image data for base, hover, pressed, and disabled states, though some states may be undefined if not provided by the skin.

parameters.name: element
parameters.summary: The type of UI element to retrieve skin data for.

methods.returns: A SkinElementData object containing the styling information including images for all visual states, or null if the element is not defined in this skin.

methods.name: GetName
methods.summary: Gets the display name of the skin.
methods.remarks: This name is used for display in UI selection lists and for programmatic retrieval via String). The name should be unique across all loaded skins to avoid ambiguity.
methods.returns: The skin's display name as defined in the Settings.json file within the skin package.

methods.name: ParseElement
methods.summary: Parses and loads skin element data from a file.
methods.remarks: This method supports multiple file types: Settings.json - Contains skin metadata (name, colors)*.svg - SVG vector graphics for UI elements*.png - Raster images for UI elements*.xaml - WPF-specific XAML templates and styles (Windows only) Element filenames follow a naming convention: ElementType[_state].extension where state can be: No suffix - Base/normal state_h - Hover state_p - Pressed state_d - Disabled state

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The filename of the element resource (e.g., "Settings.json", "Play.svg", "WPFSliderStyle.xaml").

parameters.name: data
parameters.summary: The raw byte data of the element resource.

methods.returns: true if the element was successfully parsed and loaded; false if the element type was not recognized or parsing failed.

methods.name: UpdateElement
methods.summary: Updates or creates a skin element with the specified state data.

parameters.name: elementType
parameters.summary: The type of UI element being updated.

parameters.name: state
parameters.summary: The visual state for which the data applies (base, hover, pressed, or disabled).

parameters.name: data
parameters.summary: The raw image or SVG data for the element state.

parameters.name: svg
parameters.summary: Indicates whether the data is SVG format (true) or raster image format (false).

methods.name: ParseInfo
methods.summary: Parses the skin settings from JSON configuration data.

parameters.name: json
parameters.summary: The JSON string containing skin settings including name and color definitions.

methods.returns: true if the settings were successfully parsed and a name was found; false if parsing failed or no name was specified.

methods.name: LoadColor
methods.summary: Converts a hex color string to an SKColor value.

parameters.name: color
parameters.summary: The hex color string with or without '#' prefix (e.g., "#FF0000" or "FF0000").

methods.returns: The parsed SKColor value, or 0 (transparent black) if parsing fails.

classes.name: SkinActionEventArgs
classes.summary: Provides event data for skin-related UI actions, allowing event handlers to identify the UI element involved and control event propagation.
classes.remarks: This event args class is used when users interact with skinned UI elements such as buttons and controls. Event handlers can use the Type property to determine which element was clicked and set HandleAndIgnore to prevent default behavior and implement custom actions. This is particularly useful for overriding standard control behavior or implementing custom command handling.

constructors.name: SkinActionEventArgs
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the SkinActionEventArgs class with the specified element type.

parameters.name: elementType
parameters.summary: The type of UI element that triggered the action.

properties.name: Type
properties.summary: Gets the type of UI element that triggered the skin action.
properties.value: The SkinElementType indicating which UI element was involved in the action.

properties.name: HandleAndIgnore
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the action has been handled externally and should be ignored by the control panel's default handling.
properties.value: true if the event has been handled and should not be processed further; otherwise, false.

classes.name: SkinElementData
classes.summary: Contains visual state data for a single UI element within a skin, supporting multiple states (base, hover, pressed, disabled).
classes.remarks: Each UI element can have up to four visual states, each represented by separate image data: - The default appearance when not interacting - Appearance when mouse cursor is over the element - Appearance during active click or touch - Appearance when the element is not available Not all states are required; if a state is not defined (null), the control should fall back to the base state or apply alternative visual feedback. The IsSVG property indicates whether the images are vector (SVG) or raster (PNG, etc.), which affects rendering and scaling behavior.

constructors.name: SkinElementData
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the SkinElementData class with the specified image format.
constructors.remarks: The image format should be consistent across all states (base, hover, pressed, disabled) for a single element. Mixing SVG and raster formats within a single element is not supported.

parameters.name: svg
parameters.summary: if set to true, indicates that the element images are in SVG format; otherwise, they are raster images.

properties.name: IsSVG
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the element images are in SVG format.
properties.value: true if images are SVG vector graphics; false if they are raster images (PNG, etc.).

properties.name: Base
properties.summary: Gets or sets the image data for the element's default/normal state.
properties.value: Raw byte array containing the image data in either SVG or raster format.

properties.name: Pressed
properties.summary: Gets or sets the image data displayed when the element is pressed (mouse down or touch active).
properties.value: Raw byte array containing the image data for the pressed state, or null if not defined.

properties.name: Hover
properties.summary: Gets or sets the image data displayed when the mouse hovers over the element.
properties.value: Raw byte array containing the image data for the hover state, or null if not defined.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets the image data displayed when the element is in a disabled state.
properties.value: Raw byte array containing the image data for the disabled state, or null if not defined.

methods.name: GetByState
methods.summary: Retrieves the appropriate image data based on the specified element state.
methods.remarks: This method ensures that a valid image is always returned by falling back to the base state when specific state images are not defined. This allows partial skin definitions where only the most important states are provided.

parameters.name: state
parameters.summary: The visual state of the element to retrieve image data for.

methods.returns: The byte array containing the image data for the specified state. If the requested state is not available (null), returns the Base image as a fallback.

classes.name: SkinManager
classes.summary: Manages the loading, storage, and retrieval of UI skins from various sources including embedded resources, files, and folders.
classes.remarks: The SkinManager serves as the central repository for all loaded skins in the application. It provides multiple loading mechanisms: Automatic loading of embedded .vfskin resources during static initializationLoading from .vfskin files on disk via Loading from directories containing skin element files via Loading from byte arrays via All loading methods support ZIP-compressed skin packages (.vfskin files) which contain: Settings.json - Skin metadata and color definitionsElement images (.svg or .png) - Visual assets for UI elements in various statesXAML files (.xaml) - WPF-specific templates and styles (Windows only) Once loaded, skins can be retrieved by name using String) or enumerated using Skins and SkinNames. This class is thread-safe for read operations after initialization, but loading operations should be performed during application startup.

Returns a snapshot copy — mutating the returned list does not affect the skin manager (previous behavior of returning the live internal list was unsafe across threads and let callers corrupt state).

classes.name: CallbackVideoView
classes.summary: A headless video view implementation that provides frame callbacks without visual rendering. This class serves as a callback-based video sink that receives video frames and forwards them to event handlers for custom processing, analysis, or forwarding to other systems, without performing any UI rendering operations. It's ideal for scenarios requiring frame access without a visual display component, such as video analytics, streaming to external systems, or custom image processing pipelines. Key features: - Receives video frames in configurable pixel formats (RGB, RGBA, NV12, etc.) - Implements IVideoView for standard video view integration - Implements IVideoViewPushFrame for receiving frame data - Provides OnFrame event for frame processing subscribers - Supports both VideoFrame and VideoFrameX frame formats - No-op implementations of UI-specific methods (rendering, mouse events, etc.) - Platform-independent operation without UI dependencies - Minimal overhead for maximum processing performance Common use cases: - Video analytics and computer vision processing without display - Frame extraction and image capture operations - Video streaming to custom network protocols - Integration with third-party processing libraries - Headless video recording and transcoding scenarios - Multi-stream processing without rendering overhead Threading considerations: - Frame callbacks occur on the media pipeline thread - Subscribers should handle frames quickly or queue for background processing - No UI thread synchronization overhead Performance characteristics: - Minimal memory allocation per frame - No rendering overhead for maximum throughput - Configurable pixel format to match processing requirements - Zero-copy frame delivery when possible

properties.name: Format
properties.summary: Gets or sets the pixel format for video frames received by this callback view. This property determines the pixel format that will be used when video frames are delivered to the OnFrame event. The format affects frame data layout, stride calculation, and memory usage. Choose the format that best matches your processing requirements. Supported formats include: - RGB: 24-bit RGB (8 bits per channel, no alpha) - RGBA: 32-bit RGBA (8 bits per channel with alpha) - BGRA: 32-bit BGRA (8 bits per channel with alpha) - NV12: YUV 4:2:0 planar format (efficient for video encoding) - I420: YUV 4:2:0 planar format - And other formats supported by VideoFormatX enumeration Performance considerations: - RGB/RGBA formats are CPU-intensive but easy to process - YUV formats (NV12, I420) are more efficient for encoding pipelines - Choose the format matching your target processing to avoid conversions - Format conversion happens in the media pipeline before callback delivery Thread safety: Can be set before starting the media pipeline. Changing during playback may not take effect until restart.
properties.value: The pixel format for frame callbacks. Default is RGB.

For Windows-specific implementations requiring parent attachment, use platform-specific video view classes such as WinForms or WPF VideoView.

methods.name: PushFrame
methods.summary: Pushes a video frame to the view for processing and event notification. This method receives video frames from the media pipeline and converts them to VideoFrameX format before raising the OnFrame event. It's called internally by the media framework to deliver frames to callback subscribers. Frame conversion process: - Converts legacy VideoFrame format to modern VideoFrameX format - Preserves frame data, dimensions, and timing information - Applies format conversions based on the Format property - Raises OnFrame event with converted frame data The conversion parameter (false) indicates whether to copy frame data. In this context, no copying occurs to maximize performance. Threading: Called on the media pipeline thread. Synchronous operation - blocks until OnFrame handlers complete. Performance: Minimal overhead conversion with direct frame forwarding.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: The video frame to process in legacy VideoFrame format.

methods.name: PushFrame
methods.summary: Pushes a video frame to the view for processing and event notification. This method receives video frames in VideoFrameX format and directly raises the OnFrame event for subscribers. This is the preferred method for modern media pipelines using VideoFrameX format. Frame delivery: - Direct event notification without format conversion - Zero-copy operation for maximum performance - Frame data pointer remains valid only during event handler execution - Subscribers must copy data if processing will occur asynchronously Threading: Called on the media pipeline thread. Synchronous operation - blocks until OnFrame handlers complete. Performance: Most efficient frame delivery path with no conversions.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: The video frame to process in VideoFrameX format.

events.summary: Occurs when a mouse button is released on the video view. Note: This event is never raised in CallbackVideoView as it has no visual representation. events.name: OnFrame
events.summary: Occurs when a new video frame is available for processing. This event is the primary mechanism for receiving video frames in CallbackVideoView. Subscribers receive VideoFrameX objects containing frame data, dimensions, format, and timing information. The event is raised on the media pipeline thread. Event handling guidelines: - Process frames quickly or queue for background processing to avoid blocking the pipeline - Frame data pointers are valid only during the event handler execution - Copy frame data if processing will occur asynchronously - Do not perform heavy processing directly in the event handler - Consider using a producer-consumer pattern for complex frame processing The VideoFrameX parameter provides: - Frame data pointer and size - Frame dimensions (width, height, stride) - Pixel format information - Timestamp and frame number - Additional metadata depending on source Thread safety: Event is raised on media pipeline thread, not UI thread. Subscribers must handle thread synchronization if updating UI components. Performance: Minimize processing time in handlers to maintain real-time performance. For 30fps video, each frame handler should complete within ~33ms.

classes.name: JPEGCallbackVideoView
classes.summary: A headless video view implementation that provides JPEG-encoded frame callbacks without visual rendering. This class serves as a specialized callback-based video sink that receives video frames pre-encoded as JPEG images and forwards them to event handlers. Unlike CallbackVideoView which delivers raw pixel data, JPEGCallbackVideoView provides ready-to-use JPEG byte arrays, eliminating the need for frame encoding in subscriber code. Ideal for scenarios requiring JPEG images without UI rendering, such as motion JPEG streaming, snapshot systems, or web-based video delivery. Key features: - Receives pre-encoded JPEG frame data as byte arrays - Implements IVideoView for standard video view integration - Provides OnJPEGFrame event for JPEG data processing - No-op implementations of UI-specific methods (rendering, mouse events, etc.) - Platform-independent operation without UI dependencies - Zero encoding overhead - frames arrive already JPEG-compressed - Memory-efficient delivery of compressed frame data Common use cases: - Motion JPEG (MJPEG) streaming servers - Snapshot capture and storage systems - Web-based video monitoring dashboards - Network camera integration with JPEG output - Thumbnail generation for video content - Low-bandwidth video transmission scenarios - REST API video frame endpoints Threading considerations: - Frame callbacks occur on the media pipeline thread - JPEG data is ready for immediate network transmission or file storage - Subscribers should handle data quickly or queue for background processing - No UI thread synchronization overhead Performance characteristics: - Minimal memory allocation per frame - No rendering or encoding overhead - Compressed data reduces memory and network bandwidth requirements - JPEG quality and compression ratio configured at source level

events.name: OnJPEGFrame
events.summary: Occurs when a new JPEG-encoded video frame is available for processing. This event is the primary mechanism for receiving JPEG-compressed video frames in JPEGCallbackVideoView. Subscribers receive byte arrays containing complete JPEG image data, ready for storage, transmission, or further processing. The event is raised on the media pipeline thread. Event handling guidelines: - JPEG data is complete and valid for immediate use - Frame data can be directly written to files, network streams, or HTTP responses - Process frames quickly or queue for background processing to avoid blocking the pipeline - Byte array remains valid only during the event handler execution - Copy data if processing will occur asynchronously The byte array parameter contains: - Complete JPEG file data including headers - Compressed image data ready for storage or transmission - Quality and compression configured at the media source level - No additional encoding required Common usage patterns: - Stream to HTTP response for web viewing - Save to file for snapshot capture - Transmit over network for MJPEG streaming - Queue for batch processing or archival - Forward to REST API endpoints Thread safety: Event is raised on media pipeline thread, not UI thread. Subscribers must handle thread synchronization if updating UI components. Performance: JPEG data is pre-encoded by the media pipeline. Frame size varies based on content complexity and configured quality settings.

classes.name: DesignModeHelper
classes.summary: Shared helpers for WinForms custom controls.
classes.remarks: The own Control.DesignMode property only reports true on the immediate control being designed. A custom control hosted inside *another* user control (which is being designed) reports false and runs its real-mode paint path — that path can touch initialization that crashes the VS designer (e.g. assembly preloading in the 32-bit VS designer process). Walking the parent chain catches that case.

methods.name: IsAnyParentInDesignMode
methods.summary: Returns true if control or any of its ancestors is currently being hosted in design mode. Use in custom OnPaint overrides to skip work that would crash the Visual Studio designer.
methods.returns: true if any ancestor (including control itself) is in design mode.

classes.name: GlobalKeyboardHook
classes.summary: Provides system-wide keyboard hook functionality using Windows Low-Level Keyboard Hook API. Enables monitoring of global keyboard events across all applications with optional key filtering. This class implements a low-level keyboard hook that captures keyboard events before they reach the target application.
classes.remarks: This class uses Windows API SetWindowsHookEx with WH_KEYBOARD_LL to install a low-level keyboard hook. The hook procedure receives keyboard events system-wide and can optionally filter specific keys. Proper disposal is critical to ensure the hook is removed when no longer needed.

constructors.name: GlobalKeyboardHook
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the GlobalKeyboardHook class. Sets up the low-level keyboard hook and loads the required User32 library.
constructors.remarks: This constructor performs the following operations: 1. Loads User32.dll library for Windows API access 2. Installs a low-level keyboard hook using SetWindowsHookEx 3. Stores the hook procedure delegate to prevent garbage collection The hook remains active until the object is disposed.

parameters.name: registeredKeys
parameters.summary: Array of keys that should trigger the KeyboardPressed event. Pass null to capture all keyboard events system-wide.

properties.name: LowLevelKeyboardInputEvent.Key

These events are associated either with a specific thread or with all threads in the same desktop as the calling thread.
methods.returns: If the function succeeds, the return value is the handle to the hook procedure.

methods.remarks: This method: 1. Extracts keyboard event data from the lParam structure 2. Checks if the key matches the registered keys filter 3. Determines modifier key states (Ctrl, Shift) 4. Raises the KeyboardPressed event if criteria are met 5. Suppresses the event if the event handler sets Handled = true

parameters.name: lParam

methods.name: FFEXEDisableVideoMode
methods.summary: Disables all video encoding mode options and related controls. Resets the UI state for video encoding mode selection.
methods.remarks: This method is called before enabling specific video encoding modes to ensure a clean state. It disables all mode radio buttons and their associated controls such as quality slider and bitrate text boxes.

methods.name: FFEXEEnableVideoCBR
methods.summary: Enables Constant Bitrate (CBR) video encoding mode. Activates CBR mode and enables the target bitrate control.
methods.remarks: CBR mode maintains a constant bitrate throughout the video stream, useful for streaming scenarios where consistent bandwidth is required.

methods.name: FFEXEEnableVideoABR
methods.summary: Enables Average Bitrate (ABR) video encoding mode. Activates ABR mode and enables bitrate range controls.
methods.remarks: ABR mode allows bitrate variation within specified limits while maintaining an average target bitrate. This provides better quality than CBR while keeping file size predictable.

methods.name: FFEXEEnableVideoQuality
methods.summary: Enables quality-based video encoding mode. Activates quality mode and enables the quality slider control.
methods.remarks: Quality mode (CRF/quantizer) encodes video to maintain consistent quality rather than bitrate. This typically provides the best quality-to-size ratio but results in variable file sizes.

methods.name: cbFFEXEProfile_SelectedIndexChanged
methods.summary: Handles the SelectedIndexChanged event of the profile combobox. Applies predefined encoding settings based on the selected profile.
methods.remarks: This method configures output format, video codec, and audio codec settings based on predefined profiles such as MPEG-1, MP4 H.264/AAC, WebM, etc. It provides quick configuration for common encoding scenarios.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The source of the event (profile combobox).

methods.name: FFEXEDisableAudioMode
methods.summary: Disables all audio encoding mode options and related controls. Resets the UI state for audio encoding mode selection.
methods.remarks: This method is called before enabling specific audio encoding modes to ensure a clean state. It disables all mode radio buttons and their associated controls such as quality slider and bitrate dropdown.

methods.name: FFEXEEnableAudioCBR
methods.summary: Enables Constant Bitrate (CBR) audio encoding mode. Activates CBR mode and enables the bitrate selection control.
methods.remarks: CBR mode maintains a constant bitrate for audio streams, providing predictable file sizes and compatibility with streaming.

methods.name: FFEXEEnableAudioQuality
methods.summary: Enables quality-based audio encoding mode. Activates quality mode and enables the quality slider control.
methods.remarks: Quality mode encodes audio based on perceptual quality rather than fixed bitrate, providing better quality-to-size ratio for formats that support it (e.g., MP3, Vorbis, Opus).

methods.name: FFEXEEnableAudioLossless
methods.summary: Enables lossless audio encoding mode. Activates lossless mode for codecs that support it.
methods.remarks: Lossless mode preserves the original audio quality perfectly at the cost of larger file sizes. Available for codecs like FLAC, ALAC, and WavPack.
