classes.name: WindowCaptureForm
classes.summary: A specialized WinForms dialog for interactively selecting and capturing application windows. This borderless, semi-transparent form provides a visual interface for selecting windows to capture by hovering over them with the mouse cursor. When activated via a global hotkey, it displays a camera crosshair overlay and allows users to click on any window to capture its handle and properties. The selected window can then be used as a capture source for screen recording or streaming applications. Key features: - Global hotkey activation (default: Ctrl+Shift+Q) - Semi-transparent camera icon cursor overlay - Real-time window information display - Parent window capture support - Configurable border color for selection feedback - Mouse drag repositioning capability - Non-intrusive fuchsia transparency key Architecture: - Borderless form with transparency for overlay effect - Global keyboard hook for hotkey detection - Real-time cursor position tracking - Win32 API integration for window enumeration Usage workflow: 1. Form is created and positioned 2. User presses configured hotkey (Ctrl+Shift+Q) 3. OnCaptureHotkey event fires 4. User moves cursor over target window 5. InfoLabel displays window information 6. User clicks to capture window handle 7. CapturedWindowHandle and CapturedWindowText properties are set Threading: All operations should occur on the UI thread. Global keyboard hook events are marshaled appropriately.

classes.name: PeakMeterCtrl
classes.summary: Professional multi-band audio peak meter control for real-time audio level visualization in WinForms applications. This highly customizable control provides broadcast-quality audio metering with support for multiple bands, LED-style visualization, and professional color-coded level indication. It implements smooth falloff effects, peak hold functionality, and flexible styling options suitable for audio recording, mixing, and monitoring applications. Key features: - Multi-band metering support (1-1000 bands configurable) - LED-style segmented display (1-1000 LEDs per band) - Three-zone color coding: Normal (green), Medium (yellow), High (red) - Smooth level falloff with configurable speed - Peak hold indicators with optional decay - Grid visualization for reference levels - Horizontal and vertical orientation support - Optimized double-buffered rendering - Customizable colors and appearance Technical specifications: - Default ranges: Normal (0-60%), Medium (60-80%), High (80-100%) - Configurable falloff speed with smooth animation - Efficient GDI+ rendering with minimal CPU usage - Automatic scaling based on control dimensions - Thread-safe level update mechanism Performance characteristics: - Double-buffered rendering to prevent flicker - Optimized paint routines for multiple bands - Timer-based falloff animation - Minimal memory allocation during operation Common use cases: - Audio recording and playback level monitoring - Multi-track mixing console interfaces - Broadcast audio monitoring systems - Live sound reinforcement applications - Audio analysis and measurement tools - Multi-channel audio processing visualization Usage pattern: 1. Set BandsCount and LEDCount for desired resolution 2. Configure color scheme and ranges 3. Call Start() to begin metering 4. Update levels using SetData() method 5. Call Stop() to pause metering Thread safety: SetData() and related methods can be called from any thread. Visual updates are automatically marshaled to the UI thread.

classes.name: VideoView
classes.summary: High-performance video view control for Windows Forms applications providing comprehensive video display capabilities. This control serves as the primary video rendering component for WinForms applications, supporting multiple rendering modes including hardware-accelerated Direct2D, EVR (Enhanced Video Renderer), and software rendering. It integrates seamlessly with VisioForge media components for video capture, playback, and editing scenarios. Key features: - Multiple rendering modes: Direct2D, EVR, MadVR, and software rendering - Hardware acceleration support for GPU decoding and high-resolution video - Picture box overlay for picture-in-picture functionality - Status overlay system for connection progress and notifications - Comprehensive error handling with debug log dialog - Mouse event forwarding for interactive video applications - Automatic aspect ratio handling and video transformations - Integration with MediaPlayer, VideoCapture, and VideoEdit components Rendering modes: - Software: CPU-based rendering using GDI+ (compatible but slower) - Direct2D: Hardware-accelerated 2D rendering (recommended for most scenarios) - EVR: Windows Enhanced Video Renderer (excellent for video playback) - MadVR: High-quality video renderer for advanced video processing Architecture: - Extends System.Windows.Forms.Panel for WinForms integration - Implements INotifyPropertyChanged for data binding support - Implements IVideoView for VisioForge framework integration - Provides event-driven architecture for media pipeline integration Threading considerations: - UI operations must occur on the UI thread - Media events are marshaled to the UI thread automatically - Supports InvokeRequired pattern for cross-thread calls Performance characteristics: - Hardware-accelerated rendering when available - Efficient frame delivery with minimal overhead - Automatic resource cleanup and disposal - Support for high-resolution video (4K/8K) with hardware acceleration Common use cases: - Live video preview from capture devices - Video file playback applications - Video editing and processing tools - Security and surveillance systems - Video conferencing applications - Multi-camera monitoring systems

properties.summary: Gets or sets the status overlay displayed during connection establishment and before video streaming begins. The status overlay provides visual feedback to users during network connection establishment, particularly useful for IP cameras, RTSP streams, and other network-based video sources that require connection negotiation time. The overlay appears immediately after calling Start/StartAsync and remains visible until the first video frame is received or an error occurs. Key features: - Appears automatically after Start/StartAsync call - Disappears when first video frame arrives - Supports custom text, positioning, and styling - Thread-safe property setting - No performance impact on video rendering Common usage: Use TextStatusOverlay for text-based overlays with customizable: - Font and size - Text color and background - Position (center, top-left, etc.) - Text alignment - Custom messages ("Connecting...", "Loading...", etc.) Custom implementations can provide: - Progress bars or spinners - Animated connection indicators - Branded loading screens - Multi-line status information Thread safety: This property can be set from any thread. The overlay rendering occurs on the UI thread automatically. Performance: Overlay rendering is lightweight and optimized. No impact on video performance once streaming begins.

methods.summary: Retrieves a handle to the display monitor that contains a specified point.
methods.remarks: This is a wrapper for the Windows API MonitorFromPoint function. The dwFlags parameter value of 2 corresponds to MONITOR_DEFAULTTONEAREST, which returns the nearest monitor when the point is not contained in any monitor.

parameters.name: pt

classes.summary: Represents a WPF page for configuring AMD AMF H.264 encoder settings. This page provides UI controls for setting various H.264 encoding parameters such as bitrate, GOP size, quantization parameters, rate control mode, encoder preset, profile, level, and usage mode. Implements INotifyPropertyChanged for data binding and IOutputFormatPageType for integration with the output format dialog system.

properties.name: Bitrate

properties.value: The bitrate in kilobits per second.

properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum bitrate for encoding in kilobits per second. Used in variable bitrate modes to cap the maximum bitrate.
properties.value: The maximum bitrate in kilobits per second.

properties.name: GOPSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Group of Pictures (GOP) size. Defines the maximum distance between I-frames (keyframes). A value of -1 uses encoder default.
properties.value: The GOP size in frames, or -1 for default.

properties.name: QPI
properties.summary: Gets or sets the quantization parameter for I-frames. Lower values mean higher quality and higher bitrate. Typical range is 0-51.
properties.value: The quantization parameter for I-frames.

properties.name: QPP
properties.summary: Gets or sets the quantization parameter for P-frames. Lower values mean higher quality and higher bitrate. Typical range is 0-51.

properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum quantization parameter allowed during encoding. Prevents the encoder from using quantization values above this threshold. A value of -1 uses encoder default.
properties.value: The maximum QP value, or -1 for default.

classes.name: NVENCHEVCEncoderPage
classes.summary: Configuration page for the NVIDIA NVENC HEVC (H.265) hardware video encoder.
classes.remarks: The NVENC HEVC encoder provides hardware-accelerated H.265/HEVC video encoding on compatible NVIDIA graphics cards. HEVC offers improved compression efficiency compared to H.264, typically achieving 25-50% better compression at the same quality level. This encoder is ideal for 4K and high-resolution video encoding where bandwidth efficiency is critical. Key features of the NVENC HEVC encoder: - Multiple rate control modes including constant QP, CBR, VBR, and quality-based VBR - Support for Main and Main10 profiles for standard and 10-bit encoding - Hardware acceleration with minimal CPU usage - Optimized presets for different use cases (quality, performance, low latency) - Zero-latency mode for real-time streaming applications - Configurable GOP size and quantization parameters Hardware requirements: - NVIDIA GPU with NVENC support (GTX 10 series or newer for HEVC) - Updated NVIDIA graphics drivers - Sufficient GPU memory for encoding resolution This page allows configuration of all major NVENC HEVC encoding parameters including bitrate control, quality settings, encoding presets, and advanced options for professional video production workflows.

constructors.name: NVENCHEVCEncoderPage
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the NVENCHEVCEncoderPage class.

properties.name: Bitrate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the target bitrate for encoding in kilobits per second.
properties.value: The target bitrate in kbps. Typical values range from 1000-50000 kbps depending on resolution and quality requirements. Used when rate control mode is set to bitrate-based modes like CBR, VBR, or QVBR. Higher values produce better quality but larger files.

properties.name: MaxBitrate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum bitrate limit for variable bitrate encoding modes.
properties.value: The maximum bitrate in kbps. Should be set higher than the target bitrate (typically 1.5-2x). Used with VBR and QVBR modes to prevent bitrate spikes. For streaming, this ensures bandwidth limits are respected.

properties.name: GOPSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Group of Pictures (GOP) size in frames.
properties.value: The number of frames between keyframes (I-frames). Default is -1 (auto). Common values: 30-300 frames. Smaller values improve seeking and error recovery but reduce compression. For streaming, use 1-2 seconds worth of frames.

properties.name: QP
properties.summary: Gets or sets the constant Quantization Parameter for quality-based encoding.
properties.value: The QP value ranging from 0-51. Lower values mean better quality but larger files. Typical values: 18-23 for high quality, 24-28 for medium quality, 29-35 for lower quality. Used only in ConstQP mode.

properties.name: MinQP
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum Quantization Parameter allowed during encoding.
properties.value: The minimum QP value (0-51). Default is -1 (disabled). Lower values allow better quality in low-motion scenes. Used with bitrate-based modes to prevent excessive quality. Setting too low may cause bitrate overshoot.

properties.name: MaxQP
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum Quantization Parameter allowed during encoding.
properties.value: The maximum QP value (0-51). Default is -1 (disabled). Higher values allow more compression in complex scenes. Used with bitrate-based modes to maintain target bitrate. Setting too high may cause visible quality degradation.

properties.name: ZeroLatency
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether zero latency mode is enabled for real-time encoding.
properties.value: true if zero latency is enabled; otherwise, false. When enabled, disables B-frames and reduces lookahead to minimize encoding delay. Essential for live streaming and video conferencing but may reduce compression efficiency.

properties.name: RateControl
properties.summary: Gets or sets the rate control algorithm used for encoding.
properties.value: The rate control mode. ConstQP for consistent quality, CBR for streaming, VBR for file encoding, QVBR for quality-based VBR. Each mode offers different trade-offs between quality consistency and bitrate control.

properties.name: RateControlStr
properties.summary: Gets or sets the rate control (as string).
properties.value: The rate control.

properties.name: RateControlModes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the rate control mode list.

properties.name: Preset
properties.summary: Gets or sets the encoding preset that balances quality and performance.
properties.value: The preset mode. Options range from fastest (P1) to slowest (P7). Default provides balanced performance. Higher presets improve quality through better motion estimation but require more GPU resources and encoding time.

properties.value: The HEVC profile. Main for 8-bit video (most compatible), Main10 for 10-bit HDR content. Main profile supports most devices while Main10 enables higher color depth for professional workflows.

classes.summary: Configuration page for the OpenH264 video encoder.
classes.remarks: OpenH264 is an open-source H.264/AVC video encoder developed by Cisco and released under the BSD license. It provides a royalty-free implementation of the H.264 standard, making it suitable for applications where licensing costs are a concern. The encoder is optimized for real-time communication scenarios. Key features of the OpenH264 encoder: - Baseline, Main, and High profile support - Optimized for real-time video conferencing - Background detection for bandwidth optimization - Denoising filter for improved quality in noisy environments - Frame skipping for maintaining real-time performance - Flexible rate control with bitrate and quality modes Common use cases: - WebRTC video communication - Video conferencing applications - Real-time streaming with low latency requirements - Applications requiring royalty-free H.264 encoding - Cross-platform video encoding solutions This page allows configuration of encoding parameters including bitrate control, quality settings, GOP structure, and special features like denoising and background detection that enhance video quality in communication scenarios.

properties.name: MaxBitrate

properties.name: QPMin

properties.value: The minimum QP value (0-51). Default is 12. Lower values improve quality but increase bitrate. Used in quality mode to set the upper quality bound. Values below 10 provide minimal quality improvement.

properties.name: GOPSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Group of Pictures size determining keyframe interval.

Key features of the Opus encoder: - Hybrid codec combining SILK (speech) and CELT (music) technologies - Wide bitrate range from 6 to 510 kbps - Support for mono and stereo audio - Multiple rate control modes (VBR, CBR, constrained VBR) - Low latency suitable for real-time communication - Excellent quality at low bitrates for voice applications Common use cases: - VoIP and video conferencing (WebRTC) - Streaming audio over limited bandwidth - Podcast and audiobook encoding - Game audio and interactive applications - Internet radio broadcasting This page provides configuration options for bitrate and rate control mode selection, allowing optimization for different audio content types and network conditions.

classes.name: QSVH264EncoderPage
classes.summary: Configuration page for the Intel Quick Sync Video (QSV) H.264 hardware encoder.
classes.remarks: The QSV H.264 encoder leverages Intel's integrated graphics hardware to provide high-performance H.264/AVC video encoding with minimal CPU usage. Quick Sync Video is Intel's dedicated media processing technology built into Intel processors with integrated graphics. Key features of the QSV H.264 encoder: - Hardware-accelerated encoding using Intel GPU - Multiple rate control modes including CQP, CBR, VBR, AVBR, and LA (lookahead) variants - Support for all H.264 profiles (Baseline, Main, High) - Low latency mode for real-time streaming - Per-frame type QP control (I, P, B frames) - CABAC entropy coding support - Efficient power consumption compared to CPU encoding Rate control modes: - CQP: Constant Quantization Parameter for consistent quality - CBR: Constant Bitrate for streaming with fixed bandwidth - VBR: Variable Bitrate for optimal quality/size balance - AVBR: Average Variable Bitrate with better rate control - ICQ/LA_ICQ: Intelligent Constant Quality modes - LA: Lookahead modes for improved quality and rate control Hardware requirements: - Intel processor with HD Graphics 2000 or newer - Intel Media SDK or oneVPL runtime installed - Sufficient system memory for encoding resolution

constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the QSVH264EncoderPage class.

properties.name: Bitrate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the target bitrate for video encoding in kilobits per second.
properties.value: The target bitrate in kbps. Default is 2000 kbps. Typical values: 500-1500 kbps for 720p, 2000-5000 kbps for 1080p, 8000-15000 kbps for 4K. Used with CBR, VBR, AVBR, and lookahead modes.

properties.name: MaxBitrate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum bitrate limit for variable bitrate modes.
properties.value: The maximum bitrate in kbps. Default is 3000 kbps. Should be 20-50% higher than target bitrate. Prevents bitrate spikes in VBR/AVBR modes. Critical for streaming to ensure bandwidth limits are respected.

properties.name: GOPSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Group of Pictures size defining keyframe interval.
properties.value: The GOP size in frames. Default is 0 (auto, typically 250 frames). Common values: 30-60 for live streaming, 120-300 for VOD. Smaller values improve seeking but reduce compression. Match to framerate for time-based intervals.

properties.name: QPI
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Quantization Parameter for I-frames (keyframes).
properties.value: The QP value for I-frames (1-51). Default is 22. Lower values improve keyframe quality. Used in CQP mode. I-frames typically use lower QP than P/B frames for better quality reference frames.

properties.name: QPP
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Quantization Parameter for P-frames (predicted frames).
properties.value: The QP value for P-frames (1-51). Default is 22. Controls quality of forward-predicted frames. Used in CQP mode. Typically equal to or slightly higher than I-frame QP for consistent quality.

properties.name: QPB
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Quantization Parameter for B-frames (bidirectional frames).
properties.value: The QP value for B-frames (1-51). Default is 22. Controls quality of bidirectional predicted frames. Used in CQP mode. Often set 1-3 points higher than P-frames as B-frames are less critical.

properties.name: MinQPI
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum Quantization Parameter allowed for I-frames.
properties.value: The minimum QP for I-frames (1-51). Default is 0 (no limit). Prevents excessive bitrate on keyframes. Used with bitrate-based modes to control quality range. Setting too low may cause bitrate spikes.

properties.name: MaxQPI
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum Quantization Parameter allowed for I-frames.
properties.value: The maximum QP for I-frames (1-51). Default is 0 (no limit). Ensures minimum quality for keyframes. Used with bitrate-based modes. Important for maintaining seekable reference frame quality.

properties.name: MinQPB
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum Quantization Parameter allowed for B-frames.
properties.value: The minimum QP for B-frames (1-51). Default is 0 (no limit). Controls maximum quality for B-frames. Used with bitrate-based modes. B-frames can typically use higher minimum QP than I/P frames.

properties.name: MaxQPB
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum Quantization Parameter allowed for B-frames.
properties.value: The maximum QP for B-frames (1-51). Default is 0 (no limit). Controls minimum quality for B-frames. Higher values allow more aggressive compression on B-frames to save bitrate.

properties.name: MinQPP
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum Quantization Parameter allowed for P-frames.
properties.value: The minimum QP for P-frames (1-51). Default is 0 (no limit). Controls maximum quality for predicted frames. Used with bitrate-based modes to prevent quality from becoming too high at the expense of bitrate.

properties.name: MaxQPP
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum Quantization Parameter allowed for P-frames.
properties.value: The maximum QP for P-frames (1-51). Default is 0 (no limit). Ensures minimum quality for predicted frames. P-frames are important for motion quality, so limit carefully to avoid motion artifacts.

properties.name: LowLatency
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether low latency mode is enabled for real-time encoding.
properties.value: true if low latency is enabled; otherwise, false. Reduces encoding delay by limiting lookahead and B-frame usage. Essential for video conferencing and live streaming but may reduce compression efficiency.

properties.name: CABAC
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether CABAC entropy coding is enabled.
properties.value: true if CABAC is enabled; otherwise, false. CABAC (Context-Adaptive Binary Arithmetic Coding) provides 10-15% better compression than CAVLC but requires more processing. Disable only for baseline profile compatibility.

properties.value: The rate control mode. CQP for constant quality, CBR for streaming, VBR for files, AVBR for better VBR, ICQ/LA_ICQ for intelligent quality, LA modes use lookahead for improved decisions. Each mode optimizes different scenarios.

classes.name: QSVHEVCEncoderPage
classes.summary: Configuration page for the Intel Quick Sync Video (QSV) HEVC/H.265 hardware encoder.
classes.remarks: The QSV HEVC encoder provides hardware-accelerated H.265/HEVC video encoding using Intel's integrated graphics processors. HEVC offers approximately 50% better compression efficiency compared to H.264, making it ideal for 4K video and bandwidth-constrained streaming scenarios. Key features of the QSV HEVC encoder: - Hardware acceleration on Intel 6th generation (Skylake) processors and newer - Support for Main and Main10 profiles (8-bit and 10-bit encoding) - Multiple rate control modes including CQP, CBR, VBR, and ICQ - Per-frame type quantization control - Low latency mode for real-time applications - Efficient encoding for 4K and high-resolution content - Power-efficient encoding using dedicated hardware Rate control modes: - CQP: Constant QP for predictable quality - CBR: Constant bitrate for streaming - VBR: Variable bitrate for storage - AVBR: Average VBR with better stability - ICQ: Intelligent constant quality - QVBR: Quality-defined VBR mode Hardware requirements: - Intel 6th Gen Core processors (Skylake) or newer for HEVC encoding - Intel Graphics driver with HEVC support - Intel Media SDK or oneVPL runtime

constructors.name: QSVHEVCEncoderPage

properties.name: Bitrate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the target bitrate for encoding in kilobits per second (Kbps).
properties.value: The target bitrate in Kbps. Default is 2000 Kbps (2 Mbps). Typical ranges: - SD content (480p): 1000-2500 Kbps - HD content (720p): 2500-5000 Kbps - Full HD (1080p): 5000-10000 Kbps - 4K content: 15000-40000 Kbps Used with CBR, VBR, AVBR, and QVBR rate control modes.

properties.name: MaxBitrate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum bitrate for variable bitrate modes in kilobits per second (Kbps).
properties.value: The maximum bitrate in Kbps. Default is 3000 Kbps (3 Mbps). Should be 1.5-2x the target bitrate for VBR modes. Helps prevent quality spikes during complex scenes. Only used with VBR and AVBR rate control modes.

properties.name: GOPSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Group of Pictures (GOP) size in frames.
properties.value: The number of frames between keyframes (I-frames). Default is 0 (auto). Common values: - 0: Automatic (typically 2-10 seconds worth of frames) - 30-60: Low latency streaming (1-2 second intervals at 30fps) - 120-300: Standard streaming (4-10 second intervals) - 300+: High compression for storage Smaller values improve seek performance but reduce compression.

properties.name: QPI
properties.summary: Gets or sets the quantization parameter for I-frames (keyframes).
properties.value: The QP value for I-frames. Default is 22. Range: 0-51 (lower values = higher quality/bitrate). Typical values: - 16-20: High quality - 20-26: Standard quality - 26-32: Lower quality/high compression I-frames are reference frames, so lower QP improves overall quality. Used only with CQP rate control mode.

properties.name: QPP
properties.summary: Gets or sets the quantization parameter for P-frames (predicted frames).
properties.value: The QP value for P-frames. Default is 22. Range: 0-51 (lower values = higher quality/bitrate). Typically set equal to or 1-2 points higher than QP-I. P-frames reference previous frames for compression. Used only with CQP rate control mode.

properties.name: QPB
properties.summary: Gets or sets the quantization parameter for B-frames (bidirectional predicted frames).
properties.value: The QP value for B-frames. Default is 22. Range: 0-51 (lower values = higher quality/bitrate). Typically set 2-4 points higher than QP-P as B-frames are less important. B-frames reference both past and future frames. Used only with CQP rate control mode.

properties.name: MinQPI
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum quantization parameter allowed for I-frames.
properties.value: The minimum QP value for I-frames. Default is 0. Prevents the encoder from using too much bitrate on easy content. Range: 0-51 (must be less than MaxQPI). Used with VBR and AVBR rate control modes.

properties.name: MaxQPI
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum quantization parameter allowed for I-frames.
properties.value: The maximum QP value for I-frames. Default is 51. Prevents quality from dropping too low during complex scenes. Range: 0-51 (must be greater than MinQPI). Used with VBR and AVBR rate control modes.

properties.name: MinQPB
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum quantization parameter allowed for B-frames.
properties.value: The minimum QP value for B-frames. Default is 0. Range: 0-51 (must be less than MaxQPB). Used with VBR and AVBR rate control modes.

properties.name: MaxQPB
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum quantization parameter allowed for B-frames.
properties.value: The maximum QP value for B-frames. Default is 51. Range: 0-51 (must be greater than MinQPB). Used with VBR and AVBR rate control modes.

properties.name: MinQPP
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum quantization parameter allowed for P-frames.
properties.value: The minimum QP value for P-frames. Default is 0. Range: 0-51 (must be less than MaxQPP). Used with VBR and AVBR rate control modes.

properties.name: MaxQPP
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum quantization parameter allowed for P-frames.
properties.value: The maximum QP value for P-frames. Default is 51. Range: 0-51 (must be greater than MinQPP). Used with VBR and AVBR rate control modes.

properties.name: LowLatency
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether low latency mode is enabled.
properties.value: true if low latency is enabled; otherwise, false. Low latency mode: - Reduces encoding delay for real-time applications - Disables B-frames - Uses smaller lookahead buffers - Ideal for video conferencing and live streaming - May slightly reduce compression efficiency

properties.name: RateControl

properties.value: The rate control mode. Default is CQP. Available modes: - CQP: Constant QP for predictable quality - CBR: Constant bitrate for streaming - VBR: Variable bitrate for optimal quality/size - AVBR: Average VBR with smoother bitrate - ICQ: Intelligent constant quality - QVBR: Quality-defined VBR (best quality mode)

properties.value: The ICQ quality level. Default is 0. Range: 1-51 (lower values = higher quality). ICQ mode automatically adjusts bitrate to maintain consistent quality. Similar to CRF in x264/x265 encoders. Used only with ICQ rate control mode.

properties.name: QPI
properties.summary: Gets or sets the quantization parameter for I-frames (keyframes).
properties.value: The QP value for I-frames. Default is 0. Range: 0-255 for VP9 (lower values = higher quality/bitrate). Typical values: 10-50 I-frames are complete reference frames that don't depend on other frames. Used only with CQP rate control mode.

properties.name: QPP
properties.summary: Gets or sets the quantization parameter for P-frames (predicted frames).
properties.value: The QP value for P-frames. Default is 0. Range: 0-255 for VP9 (lower values = higher quality/bitrate). Typically set equal to or slightly higher than QP-I. P-frames use previous frames as references for compression. Used only with CQP rate control mode.

properties.name: MaxBitrate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum bitrate for variable bitrate modes.
properties.value: The maximum bitrate as a string (can include units like "5M" for 5 Mbps). Should be 1.5-2x the target bitrate for VBR mode. Prevents bitrate spikes during complex scenes. Only used with VBR rate control mode.

properties.name: GOPSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Group of Pictures (GOP) size.
properties.value: The GOP size as a string (number of frames between keyframes). Common values: - "0" or empty: Automatic GOP size - "30"-"60": Low latency streaming - "120"-"300": Standard streaming - "300+": High compression for storage VP9 supports dynamic GOP sizes for better compression.

properties.name: LowLatency
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether low latency mode is enabled.
properties.value: true if low latency is enabled; otherwise, false. Low latency mode: - Reduces encoding delay for real-time applications - Limits frame reordering and lookahead - Ideal for video conferencing and live streaming - May reduce compression efficiency by 10-20%

classes.name: SpeexEncoderPage
classes.summary: Configuration page for the Speex audio encoder.
classes.remarks: Speex is an open-source audio codec specifically designed for speech compression. It was developed as part of the Xiph.org project and is optimized for Voice over IP (VoIP) and other speech applications. Speex provides excellent compression for speech while maintaining intelligibility at very low bitrates. Key features of the Speex encoder: - Optimized for speech compression (8-32 kHz sampling rates) - Multiple encoding modes (narrowband, wideband, ultra-wideband) - Variable bitrate (VBR) encoding for optimal quality/size ratio - Voice Activity Detection (VAD) to reduce bandwidth during silence - Adjustable quality settings (0-10 scale) - Low computational complexity - Patent-free and royalty-free codec Encoding modes: - Narrowband (8 kHz): Telephone quality speech - Wideband (16 kHz): Higher quality speech, comparable to AM radio - Ultra-wideband (32 kHz): Very high quality speech - Auto: Automatically selects mode based on input Common use cases: - VoIP applications and softphones - Podcast recording and distribution - Voice messaging systems - Speech recording and archival - Low-bandwidth communication systems Note: While Speex excels at speech compression, it's not suitable for music or general audio. For music encoding, consider using Vorbis or Opus instead.

classes.name: VP8EncoderPage
classes.summary: Configuration page for the VP8 video encoder.
classes.remarks: VP8 is an open-source, royalty-free video codec developed by On2 Technologies and later acquired by Google. It was designed to provide high-quality video compression for web video while avoiding patent licensing fees. VP8 is the predecessor to VP9 and forms part of the WebM project. Key features of the VP8 encoder: - Completely royalty-free and patent-unencumbered - Excellent browser support through WebM container - Good compression efficiency (better than H.263, comparable to H.264 baseline) - Multiple rate control modes (CBR, VBR, CQ) - Adjustable quantization parameters - Suitable for real-time encoding - Lower complexity than VP9 or H.264 Common use cases: - WebRTC video conferencing - HTML5 web video delivery - YouTube video streaming (legacy) - Cross-platform video applications - Embedded systems with limited resources Rate control modes: - CQ (Constrained Quality): Maintains consistent quality - CBR: Constant bitrate for streaming - VBR: Variable bitrate for optimal quality/size

It provides compression efficiency comparable to HEVC/H.265 while remaining completely free from patent licensing fees. VP9 is widely used for YouTube, web video, and various streaming platforms. Key features of the VP9 encoder: - Royalty-free alternative to HEVC with similar compression efficiency - 30-50% better compression than VP8 - Excellent support for 4K and higher resolutions - Multiple rate control modes (CBR, VBR, CQ) - Adaptive quantization and advanced coding tools - Widely supported in modern browsers and devices - Suitable for both VOD and live streaming Common use cases: - YouTube video streaming (primary codec) - WebRTC video conferencing - HTML5 web video delivery - 4K/8K video distribution - HDR video content (Profile 2) - Cross-platform video applications Rate control modes: - CQ (Constrained Quality): Best for archival and high-quality encoding - CBR: Constant bitrate for live streaming - VBR: Variable bitrate for optimal quality/size balance VP9 offers excellent quality but requires more computational resources than VP8 or H.264. For real-time applications, consider hardware requirements carefully.

classes.summary: Configuration page for WAV (Waveform Audio File Format) encoder settings.
classes.remarks: WAV is an uncompressed audio format developed by Microsoft and IBM. It stores audio data in raw PCM (Pulse Code Modulation) format, providing perfect quality reproduction at the cost of large file sizes. WAV files are the standard for professional audio production. Key features of WAV format: - Uncompressed audio with no quality loss - Support for various bit depths (8, 16, 24, 32-bit) - Multiple sample formats (integer and floating-point) - Industry standard for audio editing and mastering - Universal compatibility across all platforms - Metadata support through INFO and BWF chunks Common audio formats: - S16LE: 16-bit signed integer, little-endian (CD quality standard) - S24LE: 24-bit signed integer (professional audio) - S32LE: 32-bit signed integer (high-end audio) - F32LE: 32-bit floating-point (audio processing) - U8: 8-bit unsigned (legacy/low quality) Use cases: - Professional audio recording and editing - Audio mastering and archival - Intermediate format in production workflows - High-quality audio playback - Audio analysis and processing File size calculation: Size = Sample Rate × Bit Depth × Channels × Duration Example: 44.1kHz × 16-bit × 2ch × 60s = ~10MB per minute

classes.remarks: WMV (Windows Media Video) is a proprietary video compression format developed by Microsoft. It was designed as part of the Windows Media framework and was widely used for streaming video content and media distribution on Windows platforms during the 2000s. Key features of WMV: - Multiple codec versions (WMV7, WMV8, WMV9) - VC-1 codec (WMV9) is standardized by SMPTE - Good compression for its era (comparable to MPEG-4 Part 2) - DRM support through Windows Media DRM - Integrated with Windows Media Player - Hardware acceleration on some older devices Common use cases (legacy): - Windows Media streaming services - Corporate video distribution - Video content for Windows-based systems - HD-DVD format (VC-1 codec) - Xbox 360 video playback Limitations: - Limited cross-platform support - Inferior compression compared to modern codecs (H.264, HEVC) - Declining usage in favor of open standards - May require Windows Media Foundation on non-Windows platforms Note: This encoder page is currently a placeholder. WMV encoding is considered legacy, and modern applications should use H.264, HEVC, or VP9 for better compatibility and efficiency.

classes.name: IVideoSurfaceProvider
classes.summary: Exposed by WPF VideoView when it runs in the D3D11Composable mode. The provider owns a single BGRA8 D3D11 shared texture; its handle (SharedTextureHandle) is stable for the lifetime of the current internal texture and may be reset to Zero on resize, device-removed / TDR, unsupported pixel format upstream, or disposal. See SharedTextureHandle for the full list.
classes.remarks: Typical use: subscribe to FrameReady, open the shared handle on your own ID3D11Device, run a compute or pixel shader that reads from and writes to the texture, then return. The mutated frame is what WPF presents this compose cycle.

properties.name: SharedTextureHandle
properties.summary: DXGI shared handle of the current frame's GPU texture, BGRA8. Stable for the lifetime of the current internal texture and reset to Zero when: no frame has been pushed yet,the source resolution changed (a new texture is allocated and the published handle is replaced),frame upload failed (e.g. device removed / TDR, driver crash, unsupported pixel format) — the pipeline tears down the texture and the next successful upload publishes a new handle,the view was disposed. Consumers must re-read this property per frame; do not cache.

properties.name: SurfaceWidth
properties.summary: Width of the current shared texture, in pixels.

properties.name: SurfaceHeight
properties.summary: Height of the current shared texture, in pixels.

events.name: FrameReady
events.summary: Raised after each frame has been uploaded to the shared texture and before WPF presents it. Subscribers may mutate the texture in place (within an Acquire/Release pair on their own ID3D11Device); the modified pixels are what the user will see this compose cycle.

events.name: RenderError
events.summary: Raised when the underlying D3D11 render pipeline encounters a non-fatal error: shared-texture upload failure, device-removed / TDR, D3DImage bridge construction failure, dispatcher rejection during teardown, or a consumer-supplied FrameReady handler throwing. Subscribers can log, surface a UI banner, or reset their own state without attaching a debugger. Consumer exceptions thrown from this handler are swallowed so a misbehaving subscriber cannot break the pipeline.

classes.name: MultiscreenVideoView
classes.summary: A WPF UserControl providing high-performance video rendering for multiscreen and multi-stream display scenarios. This control is optimized for displaying multiple video streams simultaneously in WPF applications, such as surveillance systems, video walls, and multi-camera monitoring interfaces. It renders raw video frames directly to a WPF Image control using WriteableBitmap for efficient software-based video playback. Key features: - Software-based RGB24 video frame rendering - Thread-safe frame processing with background operations - Automatic UI thread marshaling for safe WPF updates - Dynamic frame size adaptation without flickering - Native memory operations for optimal performance - Minimal overhead for multi-stream scenarios - Automatic aspect ratio handling Architecture: - Uses WriteableBitmap for efficient pixel buffer updates - Employs native memcpy for high-speed frame data copying - Implements double-buffering pattern with _rendering flag - Dispatcher.BeginInvoke for thread-safe UI updates - Grid-based layout with Image control for display Performance characteristics: - Native memory copy operations (memcpy) for maximum speed - Minimal GC pressure through reusable WriteableBitmap - Thread-safe frame queueing prevents UI blocking - Efficient handling of frame dimension changes - Optimized for multiple concurrent video streams Common use cases: - Video surveillance dashboards with multiple camera feeds - Video conferencing applications with participant grids - Multi-camera video editing interfaces - Video wall displays - Split-screen video playback - Picture-in-picture implementations Threading considerations: - Frame data can be pushed from any thread - Rendering operations are marshaled to UI thread automatically - _rendering flag prevents concurrent frame updates - Safe for high-frequency frame delivery Memory management: - WriteableBitmap is reused when possible - Frame data is copied using unsafe native operations - Minimal managed allocations per frame - Automatic cleanup on control disposal Technical notes: - Supports only RGB24/BGR24 pixel format - Handles line stride calculation for proper alignment - Uses 72 DPI for bitmap creation - Black background by default
classes.remarks: This control is designed to handle RGB24 video frames and provides thread-safe frame rendering through the use of background frame processing and UI thread marshalling. It supports dynamic frame size changes and provides methods for clearing the display. The control uses unsafe memory operations for optimal performance when copying video frame data, making it suitable for high-resolution video playback scenarios.

methods.name: CopyMemory
methods.summary: Managed memory copy used for video frame data. Replaces the previous [DllImport("msvcrt.dll", "memcpy")] which truncated lengths above 2 GB silently (int parameter) and is not available on every Windows SKU (e.g. Server Core). Buffer.MemoryCopy is a BCL primitive that accepts long counts and is implemented against the same underlying optimized memmove.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.summary: Pointer to the destination memory buffer.

parameters.name: source
parameters.summary: Pointer to the source memory buffer.

methods.name: NewFrameDelegateMethod
methods.summary: Processes and displays a new video frame on the UI thread with optimized bitmap handling. This method is the core rendering function called via Dispatcher.BeginInvoke to ensure thread-safe execution on the WPF UI thread. It manages the WriteableBitmap lifecycle, handles frame dimension changes, and performs efficient pixel data updates. Processing workflow: 1. Validates WPFScreen control availability 2. Creates or recreates WriteableBitmap if dimensions changed 3. Calculates proper line stride for BGR24 format alignment 4. Writes pixel data to bitmap using WritePixels 5. Clears rendering flag for next frame Bitmap management: - Reuses existing bitmap when frame dimensions match - Creates new bitmap only when dimensions change - Sets proper DPI (72) and pixel format (Bgr24) - Uses BeginInit/EndInit for efficient property updates Line stride calculation: - Formula: (((width * 24) + 31) / 32) * 4 - Ensures proper 32-bit alignment for performance - Accounts for BGR24 pixel format (3 bytes per pixel) - Matches Windows bitmap row alignment requirements Error handling: - Try-catch block prevents exceptions from crashing UI thread - Always clears _rendering flag even on error - Silent error handling to maintain stability Performance notes: - WritePixels performs native memory copy - BeginInit/EndInit batch property updates - Minimal allocations when bitmap is reused - Optimized for high frame rates Threading: This method must execute on the UI thread. Always called via Dispatcher.BeginInvoke from PushFrame.
methods.remarks: This method is called via Dispatcher.BeginInvoke to ensure it runs on the UI thread. It automatically handles bitmap recreation when frame dimensions change and calculates the proper line step for BGR24 pixel format.

methods.name: RenderFrame
methods.summary: Renders a video frame from a VideoFrameBufferEventArgs event.
methods.remarks: This method extracts the frame data from the event arguments and delegates to the main RenderFrame method for actual rendering.

parameters.summary: The VideoFrameBufferEventArgs containing the video frame data and metadata from a video processing event.

methods.name: RenderFrame
methods.summary: Renders a video frame in RGB24 format to the display.
methods.remarks: This method performs thread-safe frame rendering by: 1. Checking if a rendering operation is already in progress 2. Copying frame data to an internal buffer if needed 3. Marshalling the actual rendering to the UI thread The method handles dynamic frame size changes by reallocating the internal frame buffer when dimensions change.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: The VideoFrame containing the raw video data, dimensions, and format information to be displayed.

methods.summary: Clears the video display by removing the current frame and resetting the image source.
methods.remarks: This method immediately clears the displayed video content and resets the Image control to show a blank (black) background. It's typically called when stopping video playback or when transitioning between video sources.

classes.name: SkinHelper
classes.summary: Provides utility methods for working with the VisioForge skinning system in WPF. This static class contains helper methods for loading XAML styles, converting colors, and applying skin-specific styling to WPF controls.
classes.remarks: The SkinHelper class bridges the gap between the VisioForge skin system and WPF by providing methods to: - Load XAML resource dictionaries from byte arrays - Convert between SkiaSharp and WPF color formats - Apply skin-specific styles to WPF controls This class is essential for the WPF skin system integration and is used by various skin controls to apply consistent styling across the application.

methods.name: LoadStyleDictionaryFromData
methods.summary: Dynamically loads a WPF ResourceDictionary from a byte array containing XAML data.
methods.remarks: This method is used to load dynamic styles from skin files at runtime. The loaded ResourceDictionary can then be applied to WPF controls to change their appearance according to the active skin. The method includes error handling and will return null if the XAML data cannot be parsed, logging any errors to the debug output.

parameters.name: data
parameters.summary: The byte array containing XAML ResourceDictionary data. This data typically comes from skin files and contains style definitions for WPF controls.

methods.returns: A ResourceDictionary containing the loaded styles and resources, or null if the data is invalid or cannot be parsed.

methods.name: ToColor
methods.summary: Converts a SkiaSharp SKColor to a WPF Color.
methods.remarks: This extension method provides seamless conversion between SkiaSharp and WPF color formats, which is essential for maintaining consistent colors across the different rendering systems used in the skinning framework.
methods.returns: A WPF Color with the same ARGB values as the input SKColor.

methods.name: UpdateSliderStyle
methods.summary: Updates a WPF Slider control with styles from a skin's ResourceDictionary.
methods.remarks: This method searches through the provided ResourceDictionary for a Style that targets the Slider type and applies it to the specified slider control. This allows sliders to be dynamically restyled based on the active skin. The method safely handles null parameters and will only apply styles if both the skin and style dictionary are valid.

parameters.name: skin
parameters.summary: The skin instance containing styling information.

parameters.name: slider
parameters.summary: The WPF Slider control to update with new styling.

parameters.name: styleDict
parameters.summary: The ResourceDictionary containing style definitions loaded from the skin.

classes.name: SkinLoader
classes.summary: Provides methods for loading WPF UserControls from skin XAML data. This static class is responsible for creating WPF controls from XAML content stored in skin files, enabling dynamic UI generation based on skin definitions.
classes.remarks: The SkinLoader class handles the creation of various UI components from skin data: - Player controls for media playback interfaces - Capture controls for video capture interfaces - Playlist controls for media library interfaces All methods use XamlReader to parse XAML content from memory streams, allowing for dynamic UI generation at runtime based on the active skin. Error handling is included to gracefully handle invalid XAML data.

methods.name: LoadPlayerControls
methods.summary: Loads WPF player controls from skin XAML data.
methods.remarks: This method creates a complete player control interface from XAML data stored in the skin file. The resulting UserControl typically contains buttons, sliders, and other UI elements needed for media playback control. The method will log a debug message if the skin doesn't contain the required XAML data and return null, allowing calling code to handle the absence gracefully.

parameters.name: skin
parameters.summary: The skin instance containing the WPFPlayerControls XAML data.

methods.returns: A UserControl containing the loaded player interface, or null if the skin doesn't contain player controls XAML or if loading fails.

methods.name: LoadCaptureControls
methods.summary: Loads WPF capture controls from skin XAML data.
methods.remarks: This method creates a complete capture control interface from XAML data stored in the skin file. The resulting UserControl typically contains buttons and controls needed for video capture operations such as record, stop, and settings. The method will log a debug message if the skin doesn't contain the required XAML data and return null, allowing calling code to handle the absence gracefully.

parameters.name: skin
parameters.summary: The skin instance containing the WPFCaptureControls XAML data.

methods.returns: A UserControl containing the loaded capture interface, or null if the skin doesn't contain capture controls XAML or if loading fails.

methods.name: LoadPlaylist
methods.summary: Loads WPF playlist controls from skin XAML data.
methods.remarks: This method creates a complete playlist control interface from XAML data stored in the skin file. The resulting UserControl typically contains a list view or similar container for displaying and managing media items in a playlist. The method will log a debug message if the skin doesn't contain the required XAML data and return null, allowing calling code to handle the absence gracefully.

parameters.name: skin
parameters.summary: The skin instance containing the WPFPlaylist XAML data.

methods.returns: A UserControl containing the loaded playlist interface, or null if the skin doesn't contain playlist XAML or if loading fails.

classes.name: VideoView
classes.summary: High-performance video view control for WPF applications providing multiple rendering modes and comprehensive video display capabilities. Supports software rendering via WriteableBitmap, hardware-accelerated rendering via Direct2D/EVR, and native rendering for optimal performance. This control handles video frame display, UI event forwarding, background image management, status overlays, and video transformations. Key features: - Multiple rendering modes: FrameCallback (software), Direct2D, EVR, MadVR, and native rendering - Hardware acceleration support for GPU decoding and high-resolution video (4K/8K) - Thread-safe frame delivery with efficient pixel format handling - Video rotation and transformation capabilities - Status overlay system for connection progress and custom notifications - Comprehensive mouse and keyboard event handling - Background image support with stretch modes - Picture-in-picture overlay functionality - DPI awareness for high-DPI displays - Memory-efficient frame buffering with automatic cleanup Threading considerations: - Frame rendering is performed on the UI thread via Dispatcher.BeginInvoke for thread safety - All UI operations are properly marshaled to the UI thread - Event handlers are invoked on the UI thread - Native rendering components require proper disposal to prevent memory leaks - Window minimize/restore events are handled with proper synchronization to prevent race conditions Performance optimizations: - WriteableBitmap reuse to minimize memory allocations - Efficient pixel format detection and stride calculation - Hardware-accelerated rendering paths for supported configurations - Frame dropping capability to maintain smooth playback

constructors.name: VideoView
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VideoView class. Sets up the video view with default configuration: - Black background for professional video display - Automatic size change handling for responsive layout - Event handlers for UI component resizing - Thread-safe operations using exception handling The constructor prepares the control for video rendering but does not create the actual rendering surface until a parent component is attached and a rendering mode is specified. Thread safety: Must be called from the UI thread as it initializes WPF controls.

properties.name: Context
properties.summary: SDK logging context. Set by the engine via ContextPropagator when the view is attached. When null, render/lifecycle exceptions fall back to Trace.

properties.name: StatusOverlay
properties.summary: Gets or sets the status overlay displayed during connection establishment and before video streaming begins. This overlay is particularly useful for IP cameras, network streams, and other sources that require connection negotiation time. The overlay appears immediately after Start/StartAsync is called and remains visible until the first video frame is received or an error occurs. Use TextStatusOverlay for text-based overlays with customizable fonts, colors, positioning, and alignment. Custom overlay implementations can provide progress bars, animations, or other visual feedback. Thread safety: This property can be set from any thread, but the overlay rendering occurs on the UI thread. Performance: Overlay rendering is lightweight and does not impact video performance once streaming begins.
properties.value: The status overlay implementation or null to disable status overlays.

properties.name: RotationAngle
properties.summary: Gets or sets the video rotation angle in degrees for WPF software rendering. Applies geometric transformations to rotate video frames by any angle. Uses WPF's RenderTransform system for efficient GPU-accelerated rotation. Automatically adjusts scaling based on the RotateCrop property. Supported values: - 0: No rotation applied (default) - Positive values: Clockwise rotation (e.g., 90, 120, 180, 270) - Negative values: Counter-clockwise rotation (e.g., -90, -45) - Any decimal value is supported (e.g., 73.5, 120.25) Examples: - 90: 90-degree clockwise rotation - 180: Upside down - 270 or -90: 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation - 73: 73-degree clockwise rotation - -45.5: 45.5-degree counter-clockwise rotation Performance: Rotation is hardware-accelerated when possible and has minimal impact on rendering performance. Thread safety: Can be set from any thread; UI updates are marshaled to the UI thread. Note: This property only affects WPF software rendering (FrameCallback mode). Native rendering modes handle rotation through the video renderer configuration.
properties.value: The rotation angle in degrees to apply to video frames.

properties.name: RotateCrop
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether video rotation should crop the image to fill the view. This property controls the scaling behavior when rotation is applied: - When true: The rotated video is scaled to fill the entire view area, which may result in cropping the edges. This is useful when you want to maintain a filled view without black bars. - When false: The rotated video is scaled to fit entirely within the view without cropping. This ensures the entire video content is visible but may show black bars. This property only affects 90-degree and 270-degree rotations where the aspect ratio changes. 180-degree rotation is not affected as the aspect ratio remains the same. Performance: Uses WPF's GPU-accelerated transforms for efficient rendering. Thread safety: Can be set from any thread; UI updates are marshaled to the UI thread. Note: This property only affects WPF software rendering (FrameCallback mode).
properties.value: True to crop the rotated video to fill the view; false to fit without cropping. Default is false.

properties.name: RotationStretch
properties.summary: Gets or sets the stretch mode to use when video rotation is applied. This property controls how the video content is stretched within the Image control before rotation: - Stretch.Fill: Video fills the entire Image bounds, may distort aspect ratio (default for rotation) - Stretch.Uniform: Video maintains aspect ratio, may show letterboxing (black bars) - Stretch.UniformToFill: Video maintains aspect ratio and fills bounds, may crop content When RotationAngle is 0 (no rotation), this property is ignored and the Video_Renderer.StretchMode is used. When RotationAngle is non-zero, this property determines the stretch behavior before rotation transform. Common scenarios: - Stretch.Fill: Best for videos that match the view aspect ratio or when distortion is acceptable - Stretch.Uniform: Best for maintaining video aspect ratio during rotation (shows black bars) - Stretch.UniformToFill: Best for filling the view while maintaining aspect ratio Performance: Stretch mode is a WPF property and has minimal performance impact. Thread safety: Can be set from any thread; UI updates are marshaled to the UI thread. Note: This property only affects WPF software rendering (FrameCallback mode) when rotation is active.
properties.value: The stretch mode to use during rotation. Default is Stretch.Fill.

properties.name: Video_Renderer
properties.summary: Gets the video renderer configuration used for displaying video content. This property provides access to the video rendering settings that control how video frames are displayed, including rendering mode, stretch behavior, and hardware acceleration options. For native rendering mode, returns a fixed EVR configuration. For standard mode, returns the parent component's renderer settings and automatically synchronizes WPF stretch modes with the renderer configuration. Supported stretch mode mappings: - Letterbox → Stretch.Uniform (maintains aspect ratio) - Stretch → Stretch.Fill (fills entire area) - LetterboxToFill → Stretch.UniformToFill (maintains aspect ratio, may crop) Thread safety: Can be accessed from any thread, but WPF property updates are automatically marshaled to the UI thread.
properties.value: The video renderer settings, or null if no parent is attached.

properties.summary: Gets or sets background image stretch.

methods.name: GetImageLayer
methods.summary: Gets the primary image layer used for WPF software rendering. This method provides access to the underlying WPF Image control that displays video frames in FrameCallback rendering mode. The returned Image control can be used to apply custom WPF transforms, animations, or effects. Common use cases: - Applying custom RenderTransform animations - Setting opacity or visibility effects - Accessing ActualWidth/ActualHeight for measurements - Adding custom attached properties Thread safety: Must be called from the UI thread. Note: Returns null if native rendering is enabled or if the control hasn't been initialized with a software rendering mode.
methods.returns: The WPF Image control used for video display, or null if not available.

methods.name: Core_OnVideoFrameBufferWPF
methods.summary: Handles incoming video frames from the media core for WPF rendering. This event handler is the primary entry point for video frame processing in software rendering mode. It receives raw video frames from the media pipeline and routes them to the appropriate rendering mechanism (Direct2D managed panel or WPF WriteableBitmap). Frame processing flow: 1. Checks if frame processing is stopped to avoid unnecessary work 2. Converts the frame to VideoFrameX format for internal processing 3. Routes to Direct2DPanel for hardware-accelerated rendering, or 4. Dispatches to UI thread for WPF WriteableBitmap rendering Performance considerations: - Uses BeginInvoke with Render priority for non-blocking UI thread marshaling - Implements frame dropping when UI thread is busy to prevent backlog - Handles exceptions gracefully to prevent frame delivery interruption Thread safety: Called from media processing thread, marshals UI operations appropriately.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The media core component sending the frame.

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: Event arguments containing the video frame data and metadata.

methods.name: UpdateTransform
methods.summary: Updates the video rotation transform applied to the WPF image layer. This method applies geometric transformations to rotate video frames according to the current RotationAngle property value. It uses WPF's RenderTransform system for hardware-accelerated rotation with automatic scaling adjustments. Transform calculations: - Applies rotation by the specified angle in degrees - Sets the Image Stretch mode based on RotationStretch property (Fill, Uniform, or UniformToFill) - Calculates scaling factors based on RotateCrop property: - With crop: scales to fill the view area (may crop edges) - Without crop: scales to fit entire rotated image (may show black bars) - For non-90-degree increments, calculates the bounding box of the rotated rectangle - Sets transform origin to center point for natural rotation - Combines rotation and scaling in a TransformGroup Performance: Uses hardware acceleration when available and caches transform objects to minimize memory allocations. Thread safety: Must be called from the UI thread.

methods.name: DetectPixelFormat
methods.summary: Detects and maps video pixel format to WPF PixelFormat for WriteableBitmap rendering. This method converts from the media framework's internal video format enumeration to WPF's PixelFormat enumeration, enabling proper pixel data interpretation during WriteableBitmap operations. Supported format mappings: - RGB → Rgb24 (24-bit RGB) - BGR → Bgr24 (24-bit BGR, common for Windows) - BGRA → Bgr32 (32-bit BGR with alpha) - Other formats → null (unsupported, logged as error) Performance: Called once per format change to avoid repeated format detection.

parameters.name: format
parameters.summary: The video format to map to WPF PixelFormat.

methods.name: GetStride
methods.summary: Calculates the memory stride (row pitch) for a given pixel format and width. The stride represents the number of bytes per row in the pixel data, which may be larger than width * bytes_per_pixel due to memory alignment requirements. Proper stride calculation is essential for correct image rendering and preventing memory access violations. Supported formats: - 3 bits per pixel (RGB24/BGR24): Uses ImageHelper.GetStrideRGB24 - 4 bits per pixel (BGRA32): Uses ImageHelper.GetStrideRGB32 - Other formats: Returns 0 (unsupported) Performance: Static method with minimal overhead, called during format changes.
methods.returns: The stride in bytes, or 0 if the format is unsupported.

methods.name: DrawWPFFrame
methods.summary: Renders a video frame to the WPF display using WriteableBitmap. This is the core rendering method for WPF software rendering mode. It handles: - WriteableBitmap creation and reuse for efficient memory management - Pixel format detection and DPI-aware bitmap creation - Frame data copying with proper stride handling - Automatic format changes and bitmap recreation - Error handling to prevent rendering pipeline failures Rendering pipeline: 1. Validates frame data and stopped state 2. Checks if bitmap needs recreation (size/format changes) 3. Creates new WriteableBitmap with appropriate pixel format and DPI 4. Copies frame data using WritePixels for efficient pixel transfer 5. Updates WPF Image control with the new bitmap Performance optimizations: - Reuses WriteableBitmap objects when possible - Uses DPI-aware bitmap creation for high-DPI displays - Efficient pixel data transfer via WritePixels - Graceful error handling without exceptions Thread safety: Must be called from the UI thread (typically via Dispatcher.BeginInvoke).

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: The video frame containing pixel data and metadata.

parameters.name: force
parameters.summary: True to render even when stopped (for overlays), false to respect stopped state.

This method establishes the connection between the video view and a media processing component (MediaPlayer, VideoCapture, or VideoEdit). The parent component provides video frames and controls the rendering pipeline. The attachment process: 1. Stores the parent reference for renderer access 2. Should be called before disposing the parent component or switching to a new parent. Cleanup operations: 1. Disconnects video frame buffer events 2. Clears the parent reference 3. Stops frame delivery and rendering 4. Maintains UI state for potential reattachment Thread safety: Can be called from any thread.

methods.name: SetNativeRendering
methods.summary: Enables or disables native rendering mode for optimal video performance. Native rendering bypasses WPF's software rendering pipeline and provides direct access to hardware-accelerated video renderers. This mode is recommended for: - GPU-accelerated video decoding - High-resolution video (4K/8K) - Performance-critical applications - Multiple concurrent video streams When enabled: - Uses native window handles for Direct2D, EVR, or MadVR rendering - Provides maximum performance with minimal CPU usage - Reduces memory usage compared to software rendering - Enables hardware deinterlacing and post-processing When disabled: - Uses WPF WriteableBitmap for software rendering - Provides full WPF integration and transformation support - Enables custom overlays and effects - Works on systems without hardware acceleration Thread safety: Can be called from any thread, but should be set before attaching a parent component for consistent behavior.

methods.name: PushFrame
methods.summary: Pushes a video frame for display through the external frame delivery interface. This method is part of the IVideoViewPushFrame interface and provides external components with the ability to deliver video frames directly to the video view. It handles both Direct2D managed rendering and WPF software rendering modes. Frame delivery process: 1. Checks rendering mode (Direct2D managed vs WPF software) 2. For Direct2D: Pushes frame directly to Direct2DPanel 3. For WPF: Creates Image control if needed and marshals to UI thread 4. Handles thread safety and error conditions gracefully Performance considerations: - Direct2D rendering provides hardware acceleration - WPF rendering uses efficient WriteableBitmap operations - Frame delivery is asynchronous to prevent blocking - Error handling prevents pipeline failures Thread safety: Can be called from any thread, automatically marshals UI operations.

Works with every supported backend: MediaPlayerCore / VideoCaptureCore / VideoEditCore (DirectShow) — frames arrive via OnVideoFrameBufferWPF and are routed to the D3D11 panel; the engine is automatically switched to on its renderer settings. MediaPlayerCoreX / VideoCaptureCoreX / VideoEditCoreX (GStreamer) — frames arrive via IVideoViewPushFrame.PushFrame and are routed to the D3D11 panel.

methods.name: D3D11Panel_RendererUnavailable

Drop the panel, build the software surface and let the WriteableBitmap path take over, so the customer sees frames instead of a black rectangle. The request is cleared too, or the next start would install the panel again. The transition is one-way for the life of this view: a tier that recovers later (an RDP reconnect, a hybrid-GPU switch) does not bring the composable panel back — call again for that.

classes.name: SpectrumAnalyzer
classes.summary: Real-time audio spectrum analyzer control for WPF applications providing frequency domain visualization. This control displays audio frequency content as a dynamic spectrum graph, converting FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) results into a visual representation of audio frequency distribution over time. It's designed for professional audio applications, music software, and diagnostic tools requiring frequency analysis. Key features: - Real-time FFT visualization with configurable bin resolution - Logarithmic frequency scaling for natural audio perception - Automatic scaling and normalization for optimal display - Performance optimized for real-time audio processing - Customizable appearance with professional styling - Frame rate limiting to prevent excessive GPU usage Technical specifications: - Supports 512-bin FFT input (from 1024-point FFT) - Logarithmic amplitude scaling with -90dB minimum threshold - Point reduction for smoother visual representation - Automatic X-axis scaling based on control width - Yellow polyline visualization on black background Performance characteristics: - Efficient canvas-based rendering using WPF Polyline - Frame rate limiting (every 2nd frame) to reduce CPU usage - Minimal memory allocation through point reuse - Optimized for continuous real-time operation Usage pattern: 1. Call Start() to begin spectrum analysis 2. Feed FFT results via Update(Complex[] fftResults) 3. Call Stop() to pause analysis 4. Call Clear() to reset the display Thread safety: All methods should be called from the UI thread as this control manipulates WPF visual elements.

constructors.name: SpectrumAnalyzer
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the SpectrumAnalyzer class. Sets up the spectrum analyzer with professional appearance and optimal performance settings: - Creates a black canvas background for professional audio visualization - Initializes a yellow polyline for frequency curve rendering - Calculates initial X-axis scaling based on default bin count - Registers size change handlers for responsive layout The control is created in a stopped state and requires Start() to begin processing.

methods.name: Start
methods.summary: Starts the spectrum analyzer to begin processing and displaying FFT data. Once started, the analyzer will process FFT results provided via Update() method and display the frequency spectrum in real-time. The control remains active until Stop() is called. Thread safety: Must be called from the UI thread.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops the spectrum analyzer and pauses FFT data processing. When stopped, the analyzer ignores Update() calls and maintains the last displayed spectrum until Start() is called again. The display is not cleared automatically - use Clear() if needed. Thread safety: Must be called from the UI thread.

methods.name: SpectrumAnalyser_SizeChanged
methods.summary: Handles the control size change event to recalculate scaling parameters.
methods.remarks: This event handler ensures the spectrum display adapts properly to control resizing, maintaining correct frequency bin to pixel coordinate mapping.

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: The SizeChangedEventArgs containing size change information.

methods.name: CalculateXScale
methods.summary: Calculates the horizontal scaling factor for frequency bin to pixel conversion.
methods.remarks: This method computes the X-axis scaling based on the control width and the effective number of display points (bins divided by BinsPerPoint). The scaling ensures that the full frequency spectrum fits within the control's width while maintaining proper aspect ratio for the visualization.

methods.name: Update
methods.summary: Updates the spectrum display with new FFT results. This method processes FFT data and updates the visual representation of the frequency spectrum. It performs the following operations: 1. Checks if the analyzer is started and applies frame rate limiting 2. Adapts to FFT size changes by adjusting bin count and scaling 3. Processes frequency bins with point reduction for smoother visualization 4. Converts complex FFT data to logarithmic amplitude values 5. Updates the polyline points for rendering Performance optimizations: - Frame rate limiting (processes every 2nd frame) to reduce CPU usage - Point averaging across multiple bins for smoother curves - Efficient polyline point management Thread safety: Must be called from the UI thread.

parameters.name: fftResults
parameters.summary: Complex FFT results array, typically from audio processing pipeline.

methods.name: Clear
methods.summary: Clears the spectrum display by removing all frequency curve points. This method resets the visualization to a blank state while maintaining the analyzer's started/stopped state. Useful for clearing the display when switching audio sources or resetting the visualization. Thread safety: Must be called from the UI thread.

methods.name: GetYPosLog
methods.summary: Converts a complex FFT result to a Y-axis position using logarithmic scaling.
methods.remarks: This method performs logarithmic amplitude conversion suitable for audio visualization: 1. Calculates magnitude from complex components 2. Converts to decibels using 10*log10 (power spectrum) 3. Clamps to -90dB minimum threshold 4. Normalizes and inverts for display (0dB at top) The 10x multiplier is used for power spectrum (magnitude squared) rather than 20x which would be used for amplitude spectrum, following standard audio practices.

parameters.name: c
parameters.summary: The complex number from FFT containing real and imaginary components.

methods.returns: The Y-coordinate position for the amplitude display (0 at top for 0dB).

methods.name: AddResult
methods.summary: Adds or updates a frequency bin result in the polyline visualization.
methods.remarks: This method efficiently manages polyline points by either adding new points or updating existing ones, minimizing memory allocations during continuous spectrum updates. Points are positioned using calculated X coordinates and provided Y power values.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The bin index in the reduced point set.

parameters.name: power
parameters.summary: The power/amplitude value for the Y-coordinate.

methods.name: CalculateXPos
methods.summary: Calculates the X-axis position for a frequency bin.
methods.remarks: Currently uses linear scaling for frequency representation. The commented logarithmic scaling option (Math.Log10) can be enabled for perceptually uniform frequency distribution, which better matches human hearing characteristics.
methods.returns: The X-coordinate position for the bin.

classes.name: VolumeMeter
classes.summary: Professional audio volume meter control for WPF applications providing real-time VU-style level indication. This control displays audio signal levels as a traditional VU meter with customizable appearance, orientation, and dynamic response characteristics. It's designed for audio monitoring applications, mixing consoles, and broadcast equipment requiring accurate level visualization. Key features: - Horizontal and vertical orientation support - Configurable decibel range with professional audio standards - Real-time level indication with smooth visual response - Boost functionality for gain visualization - Minimal update interval control for performance optimization - Professional gray/green color scheme Technical specifications: - Default range: -60dB to +18dB (professional audio standard) - Configurable boost multiplier for gain indication - Automatic scaling based on control dimensions - Efficient rectangle-based rendering - Update rate limiting to prevent excessive redraws Performance characteristics: - Lightweight canvas-based rendering - Efficient rectangle reuse to minimize allocations - Configurable update intervals for CPU optimization - Smooth level transitions with minimal flickering Usage pattern: 1. Set MinDb, MaxDb, and Orientation properties 2. Call Start() to begin level monitoring 3. Update Amplitude property with current level 4. Call Update() to refresh the display 5. Call Stop() to pause monitoring Thread safety: All methods should be called from the UI thread as this control manipulates WPF visual elements.

constructors.name: VolumeMeter
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VolumeMeter class.
constructors.remarks: Sets up the volume meter with default professional audio standards: - Range: -60dB to +18dB for standard VU meter operation - Gray background with black foreground for professional appearance - Vertical orientation matching traditional VU meters - 100ms update interval for smooth visual response - Creates internal canvas for efficient rectangle-based rendering

methods.remarks: This method sets the amplitude to 0.0 and immediately redraws the control to provide a clean slate for new level readings. Useful for resetting the display when switching audio sources or clearing stale data.

methods.name: Update
methods.summary: Updates the volume meter display with the current amplitude value.
methods.remarks: This method performs rate-limited updates based on the MinimalUpdateInterval to optimize performance and prevent excessive redraws. The meter is only redrawn if sufficient time has passed since the last update and the control is in started state.

methods.name: Start
methods.summary: Starts the volume meter and enables level display updates.
methods.remarks: This method activates the volume meter for receiving amplitude updates. Once started, the meter will respond to Update() calls and display level changes based on the current amplitude value.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops the volume meter and disables level display updates.
methods.remarks: This method deactivates the volume meter, causing it to ignore Update() calls. The current display state is preserved until Start() is called again.

methods.name: DrawLevel
methods.summary: Draws or updates the level indicator rectangle on the canvas.
methods.remarks: This method efficiently manages the level visualization by reusing a single rectangle instance and only updating properties that have changed. The green fill color provides standard VU meter appearance. Position and size updates use a 0.1 pixel threshold to avoid unnecessary property changes.

parameters.summary: The X-coordinate position for the rectangle.

parameters.name: y
parameters.summary: The Y-coordinate position for the rectangle.
