methods.name: Redraw
methods.summary: Redraws the volume meter display based on current amplitude and settings.
methods.remarks: This method performs the core volume meter rendering logic: 1. Clamps the amplitude to the configured dB range (MinDb to MaxDb) 2. Converts the dB value to a percentage of the display range 3. Applies boost multiplier for visual gain adjustment 4. Calculates rectangle dimensions based on orientation: - Horizontal: Level extends from left to right - Vertical: Level rises from bottom to top (traditional VU meter) 5. Updates the level rectangle position and size The BeginInit/EndInit calls optimize canvas updates by batching changes. The 2-pixel margin provides visual padding from control edges.

classes.name: VolumeMeterLED
classes.summary: Segmented LED-bar VU meter for WPF. Each segment is independently coloured per its dB position on the scale (green / yellow / red zones) and lit only when the current Amplitude reaches its anchor dB.

Optional features (peak hold, scale labels, RMS bar) are gated by individual dependency properties so the control can scale from a compact 90x14 strip to a full mixer-style indicator.

methods.name: Stop

methods.remarks: The peak-hold sample is captured on every call (so a transient peak that lands between rate-limit ticks is not lost), while the visual redraw itself is rate-limited to MinimalUpdateInterval.

classes.name: WaveformPainter
classes.summary: Professional real-time audio waveform painter control for WPF applications providing time-domain visualization. This control displays audio waveform data as a continuous oscilloscope-style visualization, showing the time-domain representation of audio signals. It's designed for audio editing applications, monitoring systems, and diagnostic tools requiring waveform analysis. Key features: - Real-time waveform visualization with scrolling display - Dual-channel support (top and bottom values for stereo or min/max) - Automatic scaling and centering for optimal display - Continuous scrolling with wraparound functionality - Configurable blank zone for visual separation - Professional bisque fill with black outline Technical specifications: - Polygon-based rendering for smooth waveform curves - Automatic vertical scaling based on control height - Configurable horizontal scaling (default 2 pixels per sample) - Blank zone system for visual continuity - Center-line reference for zero-crossing indication Performance characteristics: - Efficient polygon point management with reuse - Smooth scrolling without flicker - Minimal memory allocation through point recycling - Optimized for continuous real-time operation Rendering architecture: - Uses WPF Polygon for anti-aliased waveform rendering - Maintains dual point arrays for top and bottom envelope - Automatic point insertion and position management - Responsive layout with size change handling Usage pattern: 1. Call Start() to begin waveform painting 2. Feed audio samples via AddValue(float maxValue, float minValue) 3. Call Stop() to pause painting 4. Call Clear() to reset the display Thread safety: All methods should be called from the UI thread as this control manipulates WPF visual elements.

constructors.name: WaveformPainter
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the WaveformPainter class. Sets up the waveform painter with professional appearance and optimal performance settings: - Creates a gray canvas background with black foreground - Initializes a bisque-filled polygon with black outline for the waveform - Sets up size change handling for responsive scaling - Positions the waveform at the control center The control is created in a stopped state and requires Start() to begin processing.

methods.name: Stop

methods.name: AddValue
methods.summary: Adds a new audio sample value to the waveform display. This method processes audio amplitude data and updates the waveform visualization. It handles both the top and bottom envelope values to create a filled waveform shape. The method performs the following operations: 1. Checks if painting is active and calculates visible pixel width 2. Creates polygon points for the current sample position 3. Handles wraparound scrolling when reaching the right edge 4. Maintains a blank zone for visual separation 5. Updates polygon points for smooth waveform rendering Performance optimizations: - Efficient polygon point management with reuse - Automatic wraparound for continuous display - Minimal memory allocation through point recycling Thread safety: Must be called from the UI thread.

parameters.name: minValue

This method resets the waveform visualization to a blank state while maintaining the painter's started/stopped state. The rendering position is reset to the beginning, and all polygon points are cleared for a fresh start. Useful for: - Clearing the display when switching audio sources - Resetting the visualization after long pauses - Starting fresh waveform capture Thread safety: Must be called from the UI thread.

classes.name: WPFImageHelper
classes.summary: Static utility class providing image format conversion between WinForms and WPF image types. This helper class bridges the gap between System.Drawing.Bitmap (WinForms) and WPF's BitmapSource, enabling seamless image data exchange between different UI frameworks within the same application. Essential for mixed-mode applications using both WinForms and WPF components. Key features: - Bidirectional conversion between Bitmap and BitmapSource - Proper native resource management with automatic cleanup - Performance-optimized conversion using native Windows APIs - Memory-safe operations with proper handle disposal - Support for various pixel formats and color depths Performance characteristics: - Uses native GDI+ and WPF interop for optimal performance - Minimizes memory allocations through efficient resource handling - Proper disposal of native handles to prevent memory leaks - Optimized for frequent conversions in real-time applications Thread safety: All methods are thread-safe and can be called from any thread. Native resource management ensures proper cleanup regardless of calling thread.

methods.name: DeleteObject
methods.summary: Deletes a GDI object from memory to prevent resource leaks. This native Windows API function releases GDI resources such as bitmaps, brushes, and pens. Critical for proper memory management when converting between image formats as GDI+ bitmap handles must be explicitly released. Used internally by the conversion methods to clean up native bitmap handles after creating WPF BitmapSource objects.

parameters.name: hObject
parameters.summary: Handle to the GDI object to delete.

methods.returns: True if the object was successfully deleted, false otherwise.

methods.name: ToBitmapSource
methods.summary: Converts a WinForms Bitmap to WPF BitmapSource with proper resource management. This extension method provides efficient conversion from System.Drawing.Bitmap to WPF's BitmapSource format, enabling display of GDI+ images in WPF controls. Conversion process: 1. Extracts the native bitmap handle from the GDI+ Bitmap 2. Creates a WPF BitmapSource using CreateBitmapSourceFromHBitmap 3. Properly disposes of the native handle to prevent memory leaks 4. Returns the WPF-compatible BitmapSource Performance considerations: - Uses native Windows APIs for optimal conversion speed - Automatic resource cleanup prevents memory leaks - Supports all common pixel formats and bit depths - Preserves image quality and metadata Thread safety: Safe to call from any thread.

parameters.name: bitmap
parameters.summary: The source WinForms bitmap to convert, or null.

methods.returns: A WPF BitmapSource containing the converted image data, or null if input is null.

methods.name: ToBitmap
methods.summary: Converts a WPF BitmapSource to WinForms Bitmap with efficient memory management. This extension method provides reverse conversion from WPF's BitmapSource to System.Drawing.Bitmap format, enabling use of WPF images in GDI+ operations. Conversion process: 1. Creates a BMP encoder for lossless format conversion 2. Encodes the BitmapSource to a memory stream 3. Creates a new Bitmap from the encoded stream data 4. Leaves the memory stream open: the bitmap reads it for as long as it lives Performance considerations: - Uses BMP format for lossless conversion - Memory stream provides efficient in-memory conversion - Preserves all pixel data and format information - The stream is released with the bitmap; do not dispose it separately Thread safety: Safe to call from any thread.

parameters.name: bitmapSource
parameters.summary: The source WPF BitmapSource to convert, or null.

methods.returns: A WinForms Bitmap containing the converted image data, or null if input is null.

classes.name: WPFUIHelper
classes.summary: Static utility class providing WPF visual tree manipulation and search functionality. This helper class offers essential tools for navigating and manipulating the WPF visual tree, which is crucial for finding child controls, implementing custom behaviors, and performing runtime UI analysis. Particularly useful for control templating, theming, and dynamic UI scenarios. Key features: - Recursive visual tree traversal with generic type filtering - Efficient enumeration of specific control types - Deep searching through complex visual hierarchies - Support for finding controls within templates and data templates - Performance-optimized iteration with yield return Common use cases: - Finding specific controls within complex UI hierarchies - Implementing custom behaviors that need to locate child controls - Theming and styling operations that require control enumeration - Debugging and diagnostics for UI structure analysis - Dynamic UI generation requiring control discovery Performance characteristics: - Uses yield return for memory-efficient iteration - Recursive traversal with early termination support - Minimal memory allocation during traversal - Optimized for both shallow and deep tree searches Thread safety: All methods should be called from the UI thread as they manipulate WPF visual elements.

methods.name: FindVisualChildren``1
methods.summary: Recursively finds all visual children of a specific type within the WPF visual tree. This method performs a depth-first search through the visual tree starting from the specified dependency object, returning all child objects that match the generic type constraint. Uses yield return for memory-efficient iteration over large visual trees. Search behavior: - Performs recursive depth-first traversal - Filters results by generic type constraint - Includes the starting object if it matches the type - Searches through all visual children and their descendants - Handles null references gracefully Performance characteristics: - Lazy evaluation through yield return - Memory-efficient for large trees - Early termination support when used with LINQ - Minimal allocation overhead Common usage patterns: - Finding all Button controls: FindVisualChildren<Button>(panel) - Locating TextBox controls: FindVisualChildren<TextBox>(form) - Enumerating custom controls: FindVisualChildren<MyControl>(container) Thread safety: Must be called from the UI thread as it traverses WPF visual elements.

parameters.name: depObj
parameters.summary: The root dependency object to start searching from.

methods.returns: An enumerable collection of all visual children matching the specified type.

classes.name: WPFWindowWrapper
classes.summary: Window handle wrapper enabling WinForms dialog display in WPF applications. This class provides a bridge between WPF and WinForms by implementing the IWin32Window interface, allowing WinForms dialogs and controls to be properly parented to WPF windows. Essential for mixed-mode applications that need to display WinForms dialogs (like file dialogs, message boxes, or third-party controls) within a WPF application context. Key features: - Implements IWin32Window interface for WinForms compatibility - Extracts native window handle from WPF windows - Provides proper parent-child relationship for dialogs - Ensures correct Z-order and focus behavior - Enables modal dialog functionality across UI frameworks Common use cases: - Displaying WinForms dialogs from WPF applications - Embedding WinForms controls that require parent handles - Third-party component integration requiring Win32 handles - Legacy code integration in modernized WPF applications Technical implementation: - Uses WindowInteropHelper to extract native window handle - Maintains handle reference for dialog lifetime - Provides seamless interop between WPF and WinForms Thread safety: Should be created and used on the UI thread as it accesses WPF window handles.

constructors.name: WPFWindowWrapper

The constructor extracts the native window handle from the WPF window using WindowInteropHelper, which provides the Win32 handle needed for WinForms interop. The extracted handle is stored and exposed through the IWin32Window interface, allowing WinForms dialogs to be properly parented to the WPF window. Thread safety: Must be called from the UI thread as it accesses WPF window properties.

parameters.name: wpfWindow

properties.name: Handle
properties.summary: Gets the native window handle for the wrapped WPF window. This property implements the IWin32Window interface requirement and provides the Win32 window handle that WinForms dialogs and controls need for proper parent-child relationships. The handle is extracted once during construction and remains valid for the lifetime of the wrapper object. This handle can be used with any WinForms API that requires a parent window handle. Thread safety: Safe to access from any thread once initialized.

classes.name: WPFWindowWrapperHelper
classes.summary: Static helper class providing extension methods for seamless WinForms dialog integration in WPF applications. This utility class extends WinForms Form objects with convenient extension methods that automatically handle the complexity of showing WinForms dialogs from WPF applications. It eliminates the need for manual window handle extraction and wrapper creation. Key features: - Extension methods for natural API usage - Automatic window handle extraction and wrapper creation - Proper parent-child relationship establishment - Seamless integration between WPF and WinForms modal dialogs - Clean, fluent API that hides interop complexity Benefits: - Simplified syntax for showing WinForms dialogs from WPF - Automatic resource management for window handles - Consistent modal dialog behavior across UI frameworks - Reduced boilerplate code for mixed-mode applications Thread safety: Extension methods should be called from the UI thread as they access WPF window handles.

methods.name: ShowDialog

This extension method provides a convenient way to display WinForms dialogs from WPF applications while maintaining proper parent-child relationships. It automatically creates a WPFWindowWrapper to handle the Win32 interop and ensures the dialog appears modal to the parent WPF window. The method handles: - Automatic window handle extraction from the WPF parent - Creation of the appropriate wrapper object - Proper modal dialog behavior - Correct Z-order and focus management - Standard WinForms dialog result handling Usage example: OpenFileDialog dialog = new OpenFileDialog(); if (dialog.ShowDialog(this) == DialogResult.OK) { ... } Thread safety: Must be called from the UI thread.

classes.name: DmtxImageNative

classes.summary: Dynamic Live Source Switch block with proper support for runtime input add/remove. Unlike LiveSourceSwitchBlock, this version uses slot-based management where each slot has a fixed bridge name. When an input is removed, the slot becomes empty but the bridge remains ready for a new input.

methods.name: Switch
methods.summary: Switches both video and audio to the specified slot.
methods.remarks: This method synchronously switches both video and audio streams to the same slot. A slot holding a video-only input is the one exception: nothing feeds that slot's audio pad, and the input is a deliberate choice of picture without sound, so the audio switch stays where it was and the audio that was playing continues. An empty slot is not that case - switching to nothing switches the audio to nothing too. Use Int32) and Int32) for independent control. One limit is structural: an empty slot can only take the audio to silence while the audio switch has a pad at that index. On a switcher configured with smaller than there is no such pad above the audio limit, so switching to an empty slot there leaves the audio that was playing under a black picture. Give the audio switch as many pads as the video one if that matters.

properties.summary: Gets or sets the synchronization mode for the input selector. Default is Clock for better live switching performance.

properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether inactive streams should be synced. Default is false for faster switching without synchronization delay.

Default is null (inherits from CacheBuffers), which typically favors smoother audio over the lowest latency.

methods.name: Input_FirstFreeVideoSlot
methods.summary: Picks the first video slot no other input claims.
methods.remarks: Ids used to be positional - GetVideoInputsCount() - 1 - so removing an input left a hole and handed the next add an id a live input was still using: two inputs on one bridge name, one of them permanently black. A free slot is not automatically a usable one: a file input removed after the graph was built leaves its buffered bridge behind, and pairing a frame-based sink with it produces a black input that reports success. classes.name: LiveVideoCompositor
classes.summary: Real-time live video and audio compositor: mixes several inputs into one composition and routes it to any number of outputs, with inputs and outputs added and removed while the composition runs. Video mixing runs on the CPU, OpenGL or Direct3D 11 (Windows) depending on MixerType. Use it for live production, multi-camera switching and streaming.
classes.remarks: This is version 2 of the compositor and the one to use in new code; the V1 type in VisioForge.Core.LiveVideoCompositor is obsolete. Each input and each output runs in its own MediaBlocks pipeline, bridged into the main mixing pipeline, so one failing source cannot stall the composition. The compositor is created from a LiveVideoCompositorSettings describing the composition frame size, frame rate and audio format.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases the unmanaged resources used by the LiveVideoCompositor and optionally releases the managed resources.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources.

methods.name: WaitForGraphLock
methods.summary: Takes _graphLock for a teardown, bounded, and reports whether it got it.
methods.remarks: Callers raise _tearingDown BEFORE calling this, not after: an add suspended at an await then learns about the teardown at its next IsTearingDown checkpoint and bails on its own, which is the only thing that helps when the wait cannot succeed. That case is real and worth naming rather than hiding. SDK code does not use ConfigureAwait(false), so an add suspended at an await resumes on the caller's synchronization context - and a Dispose() called from a UI thread while an add is in flight blocks the very thread that add needs to continue on. The wait then cannot succeed and burns its whole budget. That is why it is bounded, why _tearingDown is raised before it rather than after, and why DisposeAsync exists: on that path the wait is asynchronous and the add does get to run. Which is also why _graphLock is never disposed. Disposing it after a wait that gave up would pull it out from under the thread still holding it - that thread's Release throws ObjectDisposedException out of a public API, and because it never releases, anything parked in WaitAsync waits for good. It would also turn every call arriving after the disposal from the logged false those methods promise into a throw, since the wait comes before the IsTearingDown guard. A whose AvailableWaitHandle is never touched holds no unmanaged resource, so there is nothing to reclaim and nothing is lost by leaving it.
methods.returns: true when the lock was taken and must be released.

methods.name: DisposeCore
methods.summary: Contains the core logic for disposing unmanaged and managed resources. This method is called by both synchronous and asynchronous Dispose methods.
methods.remarks: Callers detach the handlers and stop the main pipeline first (issue #2359) - Dispose() synchronously, DisposeAsync() awaited. The pipeline is not disposing yet, so that is its restart-preserving stop: no block is disposed, and TearDownBuild finds it Free and takes the caller's audio renderer out undisposed. Left to the pipeline's own Dispose, the stop disposed every block still in its collection, that renderer included. The stop is unconditional: a pipeline still starting reads Free, and a stop landing during its probe pass makes it abandon; one past the probe pass is not cancelled.

parameters.name: graphLockHeld
parameters.summary: Whether the caller took _graphLock and this method must release it. The caller acquires it, not this method, so the asynchronous path can await the gate where the synchronous one has to block on it.

methods.name: DetachHandlersForDispose
methods.summary: Stops the render-statistics timer and unsubscribes the compositor's pipeline and VU meter handlers. Runs before the dispose-path stop, so nothing that stop raises reaches the caller's events. Idempotent: the handler fields are nulled. Never throws, so a failure here cannot skip the stop that follows it.

methods.name: RetireBlock
methods.summary: Takes one block the compositor built out of the pipeline's block collection and disposes it.
methods.remarks: Both halves matter, and both are best-effort because this only ever runs from a teardown. A block left in the pipeline's collection is rebuilt by the next Start — disposed, so the start fails — and a block removed but not disposed leaks its native elements. Blocks the live add paths attached with SetPipeline were never in that collection (it stores a weak reference only), so RemoveBlockLive simply answers false for them.

parameters.name: block
parameters.summary: The block to retire. null is ignored.

methods.name: DisposeAndClear``1
methods.summary: Retires each block of the list (tolerating nulls and exceptions) and clears it.

methods.name: Finalize
methods.summary: Finalizes an instance of the LiveVideoCompositor class. This finalizer is called by the .NET runtime to release unmanaged resources if the Dispose method was not called explicitly.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Performs application-defined tasks associated with freeing, releasing, or resetting unmanaged resources. This is the public synchronous Dispose method, implementing the IDisposable interface.

methods.name: DisposeAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously releases the unmanaged and managed resources used by the LiveVideoCompositor. This method is part of the IAsyncDisposable pattern, allowing for asynchronous resource cleanup.
methods.returns: A ValueTask that represents the asynchronous dispose operation.

methods.name: SetLicenseCertificateAsync

methods.remarks: This is the only public licensing API. The file-path and stream overloads and every license-key method were removed in 2026.5.2, so an application reads the .vflicense file itself and passes the bytes here. The certificate belongs to this instance: call it on every instance you create, before starting it -- licensing one instance does not license another. Without a certificate the instance runs in the 30-day trial.

methods.returns: A task that completes once the certificate has been loaded and any required activation has run.

methods.summary: Gets the context object for this compositor.
methods.remarks: The context provides centralized logging and error management functionality for the compositor and all its components.
methods.returns: The ContextX instance used for logging and error handling.

methods.name: GetPipeline
methods.summary: Gets the main processing pipeline of the compositor.
methods.remarks: This pipeline contains the video mixer, audio mixer, effects processors, and output distribution. It is separate from the individual input and output pipelines.
methods.returns: The main MediaBlocksPipeline that manages the compositor's core processing.

methods.name: GetVideoMixer
methods.summary: Gets the video mixer component of the compositor.
methods.remarks: The video mixer is the core component that performs the actual video composition. Its type (CPU, OpenGL, D3D11) is determined by the MixerType setting. It exists only between StartAsync() and StopAsync(): the composition graph is built on start and retired on stop, so the instance can be started again.
methods.returns: The VideoMixerBlock that combines multiple video inputs into a single output, or null while the compositor is stopped.

methods.name: Build
methods.summary: Builds the internal pipeline structure of the compositor.
methods.remarks: This private method constructs the entire compositor pipeline including: - Video and audio mixers with appropriate settings - Bridge sources and sinks for all inputs and outputs - Fake sources for mixer stability - Tee elements for output distribution - Effects and overlay managers This method is called automatically by StartAsync().
methods.returns: true if the build was successful; false if an error occurred.

methods.name: ResolveVideoMixerStream
methods.summary: Gets the mixer stream for an input, keeping the one a previous run already has.
methods.remarks: VideoMixerStream is a settings object with no native state, so the one the caller has been mutating through LVCInput) / Input_VideoStream_Update is re-added to the rebuilt mixer as it stands. Creating a fresh one from input.Rectangle/ZOrder would silently undo every live layout change on a restart — and Alpha has no counterpart on LVCVideoInput at all, so it could not be restored by the caller either.

parameters.name: rectangle
parameters.summary: The rectangle to start from when there is no stream yet.

parameters.name: zOrder
parameters.summary: The z-order to start from when there is no stream yet.

parameters.name: resizePolicy
parameters.summary: The resize policy to start from when there is no stream yet.

parameters.name: sourceInfo
parameters.summary: The input's frame info, refreshed on every build.

methods.returns: The stream to hand to _videoMixerSettings.AddStream.

methods.name: TearDownBuild
methods.summary: Returns the compositor to the state the constructor left it in: everything Build created is taken out of the pipeline and disposed, and every per-build map is cleared, so the next Build constructs a fresh graph instead of stacking a second one on top of the first.
methods.remarks: Needed because MediaBlocksPipeline's stop is restart-preserving: ClearData tears down everything GStreamer-side but deliberately keeps the block objects in its collection and the logical pad graph, so a restart can rebuild them. , however, creates a whole new set of mixers, tees and bridge blocks every time it runs, and it calls AddStream on the constructor-owned _videoMixerSettings once per video input. Without this teardown a second Start produced a doubled graph whose video tee was sized 2N+1 and whose first N branches fed the previous run's bridge sinks — GitHub issue #1377. On the stop path it runs AFTER _pipeline.StopAsync(true), so the native pipeline is already at NULL, the elements are out of the bin, every block's CleanUp has run and the Gst.Pipeline itself is gone. Nothing is streaming and there is no bin, which is why none of the live-removal machinery belongs here: no PadHelper.BlockPad, no TeeBlock.RemovePadLive (which refuses on a null element anyway), and neither the non-leaky tee-queue ordering documented in nor the "never SetState(Null) before gst_bin_remove" rule of issue #838 — both of those are about a live pipeline. Do not add them back. Dispose() and DisposeAsync() stop the main pipeline before DisposeCore calls this too (issue #2359). It can still arrive with a live graph after a stop that did not take, which is why nothing here may assume the pipeline is quiescent, and why every step is best-effort. Every step is best-effort and null-safe: this also runs on a compositor that was never started, on a second stop, and from DisposeCore.

methods.name: DisconnectPad
methods.summary: Clears one pad's logical connection, tolerating a pad whose peer is already gone.

parameters.name: pad
parameters.summary: The pad to disconnect. null is ignored.

methods.name: RemoveAudioRenderer
methods.summary: Takes the caller's audio renderer out of the pipeline's collection without disposing it, and forgets it.

methods.name: DurationAsync
methods.summary: Gets the current playback position of the compositor.
methods.remarks: For live compositing, this typically represents the elapsed time since the compositor started. The position is determined by the main pipeline's clock.
methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with the current position.

methods.name: StartAsync
methods.summary: Starts the compositor and all configured inputs and outputs.
methods.remarks: This method performs the following operations: 1. Applies license keys to all pipelines 2. Builds the internal pipeline structure 3. Preloads all inputs and outputs for synchronized startup 4. Configures clock synchronization across all pipelines 5. Starts all components in the correct order Inputs and outputs with AutoStart=true will begin processing immediately. Others must be started manually after the compositor is running.
methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with true if startup was successful; otherwise, false.

methods.name: RollbackStartAsync
methods.summary: Tears down pipelines that were successfully preloaded in StartAsync when a later preload step fails. Without this rollback a partial preload leaves inputs and/or outputs stuck in PAUSED while StartAsync returns false, and the caller's only recourse (Dispose) would tear them down via the bulk-disposal path rather than gracefully.

parameters.name: preloadedInputs
parameters.summary: Inputs already preloaded, in preload order.

parameters.name: mainPreloaded
parameters.summary: Whether the main pipeline reached preload before failure.

parameters.name: preloadedOutputs
parameters.summary: Outputs already preloaded, in preload order (may be null).

parameters.name: retireGraph
parameters.summary: true when the failed start is also the one that built the composition graph, so the graph is this call's to undo. false for a start that arrived while a composition was already running: Build short-circuits on _built, every input is already at Play so nothing is preloaded, and the main pipeline refuses a second start - which lands here with a LIVE graph that must be left exactly as it is.

methods.name: StopAsync
methods.summary: Stops the compositor and all active inputs and outputs.
methods.remarks: This method stops all components in the reverse order of startup: 1. Stops all inputs 2. Stops the main pipeline 3. Stops all outputs 4. Retires the composition graph, so the instance can be started again File outputs are properly finalized to ensure valid output files. The compositor can be restarted: call StartAsync() again on the same instance, with the inputs and outputs it still holds, plus any added or removed while it was stopped. Note that the composition graph exists only between StartAsync() and StopAsync(), so GetVideoMixer() and GetAudioMixer() return null on a stopped compositor.
methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous stop operation.

methods.name: Input_VideoStream_Get
methods.summary: Gets the video mixer stream configuration for a specific input.
methods.remarks: Use this method to retrieve the current configuration of a video input stream, which can then be modified and updated using Input_VideoStream_Update(). It answers on a stopped compositor too, and returns the same object a run left behind: the stream survives a stop, so an input can be repositioned between StopAsync() and the next StartAsync(), which picks the change up as it rebuilds the mixer. Mutating the object is enough there — Input_VideoStream_Update() pushes to a live mixer and does nothing while the composition is stopped. It returns null for an input without a video leg, and otherwise only before the input's first build. Up to that point the layout is the input's own Rectangle/ZOrder/ResizePolicy, which seed the stream; afterwards the stream is the layout and those properties are no longer read.

parameters.name: input
parameters.summary: The input to get the stream for.

methods.returns: The VideoMixerStream containing position, size, and other properties; null if the input is not found.

methods.name: IsTearingDown
methods.summary: Answers whether a teardown has started, for an add to check between its awaits.
methods.remarks: This narrows the window rather than closing it: the native work an add does after the check cannot be held under _listsLock without queueing every other caller behind it, so a teardown starting one instruction later still meets a nulled _videoMixer or _pipeline. What it removes is the common shape - a Dispose() that ran to completion while the add sat in a multi-second StartAsync on a camera or a network source - which without it comes back out of a public API as a NullReferenceException instead of a false. What slips through is caught by each rollback step's own try/catch.
methods.returns: true when the compositor is being disposed and the add must give up.

methods.name: RefuseInputAdd
methods.summary: Refuses an input add, through the log, which raises OnError later, on the thread pool.

parameters.name: error
parameters.summary: Why the add is refused - an input's UnknownFrameSizeError(), say; null lets the add go on.

methods.returns: true when the add must be refused.

methods.name: InputLimitReached
methods.summary: Answers whether an input add would take the compositor past its configured limits.
methods.remarks: Called twice per add, and both are needed. The first, at the entry, refuses before a camera is opened or a file is read. The second, inside the lock that registers the input, is the one that actually holds: two concurrent adds can both pass the entry check on the last free slot, and only a check under the registering lock can tell the second one apart. A refusal there leaves added false, so the rollback in the finally undoes the work the add had already done. Monitor is reentrant, so this is safe to call from inside that lock.

parameters.name: video
parameters.summary: true to weigh the add against MaxVideoInputsCount.

parameters.name: audio
parameters.summary: true to weigh it against MaxAudioInputsCount.

methods.returns: true when the add must be refused; the reason is already logged.

methods.name: OutputLimitReached
methods.summary: Answers whether an output add would take the compositor past its configured limits.
methods.remarks: See Boolean) - same two call sites, same reason.

parameters.name: video
parameters.summary: true to weigh the add against MaxVideoOutputsCount.

parameters.name: audio
parameters.summary: true to weigh it against MaxAudioOutputsCount.

methods.returns: true when the add must be refused; the reason is already logged.

methods.name: StopRolledBackInputAsync
methods.summary: Stops and disposes an input whose add is being rolled back.
methods.remarks: A rolled-back input never entered _inputs - it is registered only once the add has fully succeeded - and both StopAsync and Dispose iterate that list, so an input left running here is one nothing can ever reach again, holding its camera or file for the life of the process. Its pool ID is also the bridge channel name it publishes on, which is why a failed stop withholds the ID: the next input would otherwise open a second sink on a channel the abandoned one still owns.

parameters.name: started
parameters.summary: true when this add called StartAsync on it. When it did not there is nothing to stop, and a stop asked of a pipeline that never ran could only cost the pool ID and the dispose.

methods.returns: true when the input's pipeline is stopped - by this call or already; false when the stop threw, in which case the input is left undisposed and its pool ID must not be returned.

methods.name: LinkBridgeToMixer
methods.summary: Links a bridge source's output pad to a mixer input pad, telling apart the three ways it can fail before gst_pad_link is ever reached.
methods.remarks: Neither operand may be dereferenced by the caller. Both are null on ordinary failures - a bridge channel that could not be opened, a stop in flight - and a NullReferenceException there would be reported to the caller as a crash where a link refusal is the honest answer; the rollback runs either way. The refusals are logged apart because Refused alone reads as a caps refusal and sends triage to negotiation instead of to the teardown race that actually happened.

parameters.name: bridgePad
parameters.summary: The bridge source's output pad. Null when its Build failed.

parameters.name: mixerInput
parameters.summary: The pad the mixer handed out. Null when the mixer is not built or was torn down.

methods.returns: What gst_pad_link answered, or Refused when it was not reached - either way the caller's link-failure rollback is what runs.

methods.name: Input_VideoStream_Update
methods.summary: Updates the configuration of a video input stream in the mixer.
methods.remarks: Use this method to dynamically change properties of a video input during playback, such as position, size, opacity, or z-order. The stream object should be obtained from Input_VideoStream_Get() and modified before passing to this method. It pushes the change to the running mixer, so it does nothing while the composition is stopped — there, mutating the object Input_VideoStream_Get() returned is the whole of it, and the next StartAsync() builds the mixer from it.

methods.name: GetVideoInputsCount
methods.summary: Gets video input count.
methods.returns: int.

methods.name: GetVideoOutputsCount
methods.summary: Gets the video outputs count.
methods.returns: System.Int32.

methods.name: GetAudioInputsCount
methods.summary: Gets audio input count.
methods.returns: int.

methods.name: GetAudioOutputsCount
methods.summary: Gets the audio outputs count.
methods.returns: System.Int32.

methods.name: Input_AddAsync
methods.summary: Adds a video-only input to the compositor.
methods.remarks: On anything but true - a false and a throw alike - the input was not added and the wrapper is the caller's. Nothing the attempt installed survives: an add that had got far enough to build or start anything rolls all of it back and stops and disposes the input on the way out, while one refused before it touched the input at all - a null argument, a settings check - leaves it as it was. Either way the caller disposes it, and disposing an already-disposed one is harmless (LVCInput.Dispose is idempotent), so a caller that owns it through a finally needs no special case. A retry builds a fresh input rather than re-submitting this one. An input whose video frame size is unknown - a width or height of 0 in its info - is refused with false, and the reason is raised through . So is an input whose source cannot be connected, such as one with no video output, or is known to send no video through the output it has: an RTSP source or UniversalSourceBlock whose camera or file info was read, with no video stream, or a UniversalSourceBlock with video rendering off. This method can be called before or after the compositor is started. If called after startup, the input is dynamically added to the running pipeline. The input's AutoStart property determines whether it begins processing immediately. Each input is assigned a unique ID for bridge connections.
methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with true if the input was added successfully; otherwise, false.

methods.name: RollbackInputAddAsync
methods.summary: Rolls back an input add that did not reach true, tearing down exactly the parts that were installed and handing the pool IDs back when they are safe to reuse.
methods.remarks: Called from the finally of every Input_AddAsync overload, so it runs for a false and for a throw alike, and every step reports rather than throws - an exception here would replace the one in flight. The input is registered only after the add has fully succeeded, so there is nothing to take out of _inputs or the ID maps: a failed add is invisible to every other member, and the wrapper stays the caller's. A pool ID goes back only when the mixer actually took its pad off AND the input's own pipeline stopped - the ID also names the bridge channel the input publishes on, and reusing it would name a slot something is still feeding.

parameters.name: input
parameters.summary: The input being rolled back. Stopped and disposed here.

parameters.name: inputStarted
parameters.summary: true when this add started the input.

parameters.name: videoId
parameters.summary: Its video pool ID, or -1 when the overload has no video leg.

parameters.name: videoBridge
parameters.summary: The video bridge source, or null when it was never created.

parameters.name: videoMixerPad
parameters.summary: The video mixer pad, or null when the mixer never handed one out.

parameters.name: videoStream
parameters.summary: The mixer stream, or null when it was never added.

parameters.name: audioId
parameters.summary: Its audio pool ID, or -1 when there is no audio leg.

parameters.name: audioBridge
parameters.summary: The audio bridge source, or null when it was never created.

parameters.name: audioMixerPad
parameters.summary: The audio mixer input pad, or null when the mixer never handed one out.

methods.name: Input_RemoveAsync
methods.summary: Removes an input from the compositor by its unique ID.
methods.remarks: This method can be called during playback to dynamically remove inputs. It properly: - Stops the input pipeline - Blocks and removes mixer pads - Cleans up bridge connections - Releases IDs back to the pool for reuse - Disposes of all resources The removal is performed safely without interrupting other inputs or the main pipeline.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The unique identifier of the input to remove.

methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with true if the input was removed successfully; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Output_AddAsync
methods.summary: Adds a video-only output to the compositor.
methods.remarks: On anything but true - a false and a throw alike - the output was not added and the wrapper is the caller's. Nothing the attempt installed survives: an add that had got far enough to build or start anything rolls all of it back and stops and disposes the output on the way out, while one refused before it touched the output at all - a null argument, a settings check - leaves it as it was. Either way the caller disposes it, and disposing an already-disposed one is harmless (LVCOutput.Dispose is idempotent), so a caller that owns it through a finally needs no special case. A retry builds a fresh output rather than re-submitting this one. This method can be called before or after the compositor is started. If called after startup, the output is dynamically added to the running pipeline using a tee element. The start parameter overrides the output's AutoStart property for immediate activation.

parameters.name: start
parameters.summary: If true, starts the output immediately; otherwise, it must be started manually. Default is false.

methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with true if the output was added successfully; otherwise, false.

methods.name: StartTeeSinkPad
methods.summary: Transitions the GStreamer queue element created by AddNewPadLive to PLAYING state. We look up the parent element by the pad we just received rather than indexing into the tee's internal Sinks collection, whose order is not guaranteed to match add order (and shifts after any output remove).

methods.name: Output_RemoveAsync
methods.summary: Removes an output from the compositor by its unique ID.
methods.remarks: This method stops the output pipeline gracefully and removes it from the compositor. For file outputs, this ensures proper file finalization. The output is disposed after removal.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The unique identifier of the output to remove.

methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with true if the output was removed successfully; otherwise, false.

methods.name: TearDownOutputBridges
methods.summary: Tears down the tee branches and bridge sinks an output add installed, symmetrically with Output_AddAsync.
methods.remarks: Without this the pre-fix code left _videoBridgeSinks/_audioBridgeSinks entries live, left the tee sink pad attached, and let the (ordinal) slot name lvc{key}video{N}_sink collide with a subsequent add using the same N. Combined with the slot-ID pool fix, bridge-sink names now recycle cleanly. Every step is best-effort and reports rather than throws - this also runs from the finally of an add, where an exception would replace the one in flight.

parameters.name: record
parameters.summary: What the add recorded. Every field is optional: an add that failed part-way leaves the parts it never reached null, and each step here is skipped for them.

parameters.name: method
parameters.summary: The calling member, for the log lines.

parameters.name: releaseSlotIds
parameters.summary: true to hand the slot IDs back to their pools. A rollback whose output would not stop passes false: that output's own bridge source is still live on the slot's name, and the next add must not derive the same one.

parameters.name: outputWasRegistered
parameters.summary: true when the output had been registered, so a build may have created a bridge sink for it. false from an add's rollback: that output never reached _outputs, so no build ever saw it and a missing sink means exactly that - nothing holds its channel name.

methods.name: RollbackOutputAddAsync
methods.summary: Rolls back an output add that did not reach true.
methods.remarks: Called from the finally of every Output_AddAsync overload, so it runs for a false and for a throw alike and must never throw itself - an exception here would replace the one in flight. The output is registered only after the add has fully succeeded, so there is nothing to take out of _outputs or _outputBridges: a failed add is invisible to every other member, and the wrapper stays the caller's.

parameters.name: output
parameters.summary: The output being rolled back. Stopped and disposed here.

parameters.name: record
parameters.summary: The slot IDs it claimed and whatever it managed to install.

parameters.name: outputStarted
parameters.summary: true when this add called StartAsync on the output. When it did not there is nothing to stop, and a stop asked of a pipeline that never ran could only cost the slot and the dispose.

methods.name: ProbeNDISourceAsync
methods.summary: Probes the sender of an input's NDI source before the input is added, outside the gate: whether it has audio is decided from what the probe found (GitHub issues #2112, #2192). A failed probe is left to the start, which probes again and reports it.

parameters.name: input
parameters.summary: The input being added; anything but an NDI source is left alone.

methods.name: Input_AddAsync
methods.summary: Adds an audio-only input to the compositor.
methods.remarks: On anything but true - a false and a throw alike - the input was not added and the wrapper is the caller's. Nothing the attempt installed survives: an add that had got far enough to build or start anything rolls all of it back and stops and disposes the input on the way out, while one refused before it touched the input at all - a null argument, a settings check - leaves it as it was. Either way the caller disposes it, and disposing an already-disposed one is harmless (LVCInput.Dispose is idempotent), so a caller that owns it through a finally needs no special case. A retry builds a fresh input rather than re-submitting this one. An input whose source cannot be connected, such as one with no audio output, is refused with false, and the reason is raised through . So is one whose source is known to send no audio through the output it has: an RTSPSourceBlock or RTSPRAWSourceBlock with AudioEnabled off, a file or an RTSP camera whose info was read, with no audio stream, or an NDI sender found to have no audio when it is probed here. This method requires audio to be enabled in the compositor settings. Like video inputs, audio inputs can be added dynamically during playback. Each input is assigned a unique ID for bridge connections and mixed into the main audio output.
methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with true if the input was added successfully; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Output_AddAsync
methods.summary: Adds an audio-only output to the compositor.
methods.remarks: On anything but true - a false and a throw alike - the output was not added and the wrapper is the caller's. Nothing the attempt installed survives: an add that had got far enough to build or start anything rolls all of it back and stops and disposes the output on the way out, while one refused before it touched the output at all - a null argument, a settings check - leaves it as it was. Either way the caller disposes it, and disposing an already-disposed one is harmless (LVCOutput.Dispose is idempotent), so a caller that owns it through a finally needs no special case. A retry builds a fresh output rather than re-submitting this one. Audio outputs receive the mixed audio from all audio inputs. Multiple audio outputs can be active simultaneously, each receiving the same audio mix. This is useful for recording while streaming or monitoring. A compositor with set to false has no audio mix, so this method returns false there, before and after start alike.

parameters.name: start
parameters.summary: If true, starts the output immediately; otherwise, it must be started manually. Default is false.

methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with true if the output was added successfully; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Output_AddAsync
methods.summary: Adds a combined video and audio output to the compositor.
methods.remarks: On anything but true - a false and a throw alike - the output was not added and the wrapper is the caller's. Nothing the attempt installed survives: an add that had got far enough to build or start anything rolls all of it back and stops and disposes the output on the way out, while one refused before it touched the output at all - a null argument, a settings check - leaves it as it was. Either way the caller disposes it, and disposing an already-disposed one is harmless (LVCOutput.Dispose is idempotent), so a caller that owns it through a finally needs no special case. A retry builds a fresh output rather than re-submitting this one. This method creates separate bridge connections for video and audio streams to the output. Both streams remain synchronized through the output pipeline. Common uses include recording files with both video and audio or streaming to services that require both components. With set to false only the video bridge is created, and the output receives video alone.

parameters.name: start
parameters.summary: If true, starts the output immediately; otherwise, it must be started manually. Default is false.

methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with true if the output was added successfully; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Output_VideoAudio_Get
methods.summary: Gets a video/audio output by its index in the output list.
methods.remarks: This method performs type checking and will return null if the output at the specified index is not a combined video/audio output.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the output.

methods.returns: The LVCVideoAudioOutput at the specified index; null if the index is out of range or the output is not a video/audio type.

methods.summary: Gets a video/audio output by its unique identifier.
methods.remarks: This is the preferred method for retrieving outputs as IDs are guaranteed to be unique and stable throughout the output's lifetime.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The unique identifier of the output.

methods.returns: The LVCVideoAudioOutput with the specified ID; null if not found or the output is not a video/audio type.

methods.name: Input_AddAsync
methods.summary: Adds a combined video and audio input to the compositor.
methods.remarks: On anything but true - a false and a throw alike - the input was not added and the wrapper is the caller's. Nothing the attempt installed survives: an add that had got far enough to build or start anything rolls all of it back and stops and disposes the input on the way out, while one refused before it touched the input at all - a null argument, a settings check - leaves it as it was. Either way the caller disposes it, and disposing an already-disposed one is harmless (LVCInput.Dispose is idempotent), so a caller that owns it through a finally needs no special case. A retry builds a fresh input rather than re-submitting this one. An input that renders video with an unknown frame size - a width or height of 0 in its video info - is refused with false, and the reason is raised through . So is an input whose source cannot be connected, such as one with no output for a leg it has. This method handles inputs that provide both video and audio streams. The video and audio components are processed separately but remain synchronized. Special handling is provided for file sources to ensure proper preloading when added to a running compositor. Both video and audio IDs are assigned from their respective pools; an input without an audio leg - no audio info, a UniversalSourceBlock or UniversalSourceBlockV2 with audio rendering off, an RTSPSourceBlock or RTSPRAWSourceBlock with AudioEnabled off, a file, or an RTSP camera whose info was read, with no audio stream, or a source with no audio output such as an NDI sender found to have no audio when it is probed - takes no audio ID and no audio slot. The same holds for video, except that an NDI source given video info always has a video leg. An NDI source is probed here, before its audio leg is decided. An input with neither leg is refused with false, and the reason is raised through .

parameters.name: start
parameters.summary: If true, starts the input after adding; otherwise uses the input's AutoStart property. Default is false.

methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with true if the input was added successfully; otherwise, false.

methods.name: InstallRenderStatisticsProbe
methods.summary: Attaches a buffer pad probe to the compositor's video tee input and starts the render-statistics timer. Called after the main pipeline has been preloaded so the tee's internal GStreamer pad is available.

methods.name: RenderStatsProbeCallback
methods.summary: Buffer pad probe that counts frames leaving the compositor and records the most recent PTS. Runs on the GStreamer streaming thread; must stay allocation-free and fast.
methods.remarks: The buffer returned by info.Buffer is a transfer-none wrapper around an in-flight GstBuffer owned by the pipeline. Do NOT call Dispose() on it — doing so risks decrementing the native refcount while the buffer is still being passed downstream, leading to use-after-free crashes or subtle corruption. This matches the convention used by MotionDetectionBlock.ProbeCallback.

methods.name: RenderStatsTimerTick
methods.summary: Timer callback that converts the frame counter into a frames-per-second reading and raises OnRenderStatistics. Uses a stopwatch so the reading stays accurate even if the timer tick is delayed by threadpool scheduling.

methods.name: StopRenderStatisticsTimer
methods.summary: Stops the render-statistics timer and drains any in-flight callback via WaitHandle). Safe to call multiple times and when the timer was never started.
methods.remarks: A bare Timer.Dispose() returns immediately even while RenderStatsTimerTick is running, which means OnRenderStatistics subscribers could fire after the compositor has been torn down. Using the WaitHandle overload blocks until the pending tick drains.

methods.name: RemoveRenderStatisticsProbe
methods.summary: Stops the render-statistics timer and removes the buffer probe from the video tee input. Safe to call multiple times and when no probe was ever installed.
methods.remarks: Callers must ensure the upstream pipeline has transitioned out of PLAYING before invoking this method from a context that holds the pad stream-lock (e.g. from a streaming thread), otherwise Pad.RemoveProbe can deadlock while waiting for in-flight probe callbacks.

methods.name: Video_Overlay_Add
methods.summary: Adds a new overlay element to the video stream.
methods.remarks: The overlay will be rendered on top of the video according to its position and properties. Multiple overlays can be added and will be rendered in the order they were added.

parameters.name: overlay
parameters.summary: The overlay element to add, such as text, image, or shape overlay.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.summary: The channel number for multi-channel support. Currently not used but reserved for future use. Default is 0.

methods.name: Video_Overlay_Remove
methods.summary: Removes a specific overlay element from the video stream.
methods.remarks: If the specified overlay is not found in the current overlay list, no action is taken.

parameters.name: overlay

parameters.name: channel
parameters.summary: The channel number for multi-channel support. Currently not used but reserved for future use. Default is 0.

methods.name: Video_Effects_AddOrUpdateAsync
methods.summary: Adds a new video effect or updates an existing one on the composed output.
methods.remarks: This method can be called during playback to dynamically add or modify effects. If the video effect manager is not initialized, this method will return without doing anything. A ResizeVideoEffect, crop effect or box cannot be added or updated through this call while the composition is running with at least one video output: the outputs were built for the frame size that reached them. The call is refused through OnError, and the effect stays registered, so the next start applies it. Without outputs it applies live, as the renderer follows a frame-size change. Setting a property on an effect object that is already applied is not intercepted and takes effect live.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.summary: The video effect to add or update. If an effect with the same name exists, it will be updated.

methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous operation.

methods.name: HasVideoOutputBridges
methods.summary: Determines whether any video output's bridge is in the composition.
methods.returns: true when at least one video output bridge exists; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Video_Effects_Get
methods.summary: Retrieves a video effect by its name.
methods.remarks: Use this method to retrieve an effect instance for modification or inspection. If the video effect manager is not initialized, this method will return null.

parameters.name: effectName
parameters.summary: The unique name of the effect to retrieve.

methods.returns: The IBaseVideoEffect instance if found; otherwise, null.

methods.name: Video_Effects_RemoveAsync
methods.summary: Removes a video effect from the composed output.
methods.remarks: This method pauses the pipeline during effect removal to ensure smooth operation. The pipeline will automatically resume after the effect is removed. If the video effect manager or pipeline is not initialized, this method will return without doing anything. Before the first successful start, and after the composition has been stopped, the effect is removed as configuration without changing the pipeline state; the next start builds the composition from the effects that remain.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.summary: The video effect instance to remove.

methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous operation.

methods.name: Video_Effects_RemoveAsync
methods.summary: Removes a video effect from the composed output by its name.
methods.remarks: This method first looks up the effect by name, then removes it if found. The pipeline is paused during removal and automatically resumed afterwards. If the effect is not found or the video effect manager is not initialized, this method will return without doing anything. Before the first successful start, and after the composition has been stopped, the effect is removed as configuration without changing the pipeline state; the next start builds the composition from the effects that remain.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name of the effect to remove.

methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous operation.

methods.name: Video_Effects_Clear
methods.summary: Removes all video effects from the composed output.
methods.remarks: A playing composition is paused for the clear and resumed afterwards. A composition left in Pause is cleared in place and stays paused. A frame-size effect present on a live composition refuses the clear - stop the composition first. A clear that cannot take the pause - the pipeline is already stopping - is reported and skipped. Before the first start, and after the composition has been stopped, the effects are only configuration and are removed without touching the pipeline state.

methods.name: IsCompositionLive
methods.summary: Determines whether the composition has a live graph that effect removal must respect.
methods.returns: true when the pipeline has started and is not stopped; otherwise, false.

methods.name: TryGetFrameSizeEffect
methods.summary: Finds a frame-size effect registered on the composed output by ID, custom names included.
methods.returns: The effect instance, or null when none is registered.

methods.name: PauseForEffectRemovalAsync
methods.summary: Pauses the composition before an effect is unplugged from the running graph.
methods.remarks: Outside a run - before the first successful StartAsync and again after StopAsync - the effects are only configuration: there is no live graph to protect, so removal proceeds without changing the pipeline state. Only a running composition is paused before an effect is unplugged from it. The stopped case is the reason StopAsync clears _hasStarted. Without that, this asked a released pipeline to pause - ClearData has already let it go, so Pause returned early without touching the state - and then refused the removal on the strength of a pause that was never going to land.
methods.returns: true when the effect may be removed; false when the pause did not land.

classes.name: LVCHelpers
classes.summary: Provides helper methods for the Live Video Compositor.
classes.remarks: This internal static class contains utility methods used by the Live Video Compositor for various calculations and transformations, particularly related to video scaling and aspect ratio handling.

methods.name: UnknownFrameSizeError
methods.summary: Returns why a video input with this frame info cannot be added, or null when it can.
methods.remarks: The input's bridge is built for the declared width and height, so without them it would be accepted and then fail at start with nothing naming the cause. Call it only for an input that builds a video bridge: an input with no video leg decides that before asking.

methods.name: CalculateUniformToFillRect
methods.summary: Calculates the source rectangle coordinates for UniformToFill scaling mode.
methods.remarks: UniformToFill scaling ensures that the entire target area is filled while maintaining the source aspect ratio. This may result in cropping parts of the source image. The method calculates which portions of the source should be cropped to achieve this effect, centering the visible area both horizontally and vertically.

parameters.name: sourceWidth
parameters.summary: The width of the source image in pixels. Must be greater than zero.

parameters.name: sourceHeight
parameters.summary: The height of the source image in pixels. Must be greater than zero.

parameters.name: targetWidth
parameters.summary: The width of the target control or display area in pixels. Must be greater than zero.

parameters.name: targetHeight
parameters.summary: The height of the target control or display area in pixels. Must be greater than zero.

methods.returns: A Rect representing the portion of the source image that will be displayed, with coordinates specifying the crop area.

classes.name: LiveVideoCompositorSettings
classes.summary: Contains configuration settings for the Live Video Compositor. This class defines all the parameters needed to initialize and configure a live video compositing session, including video dimensions, frame rate, audio settings, and output destinations.
classes.remarks: The settings control both video and audio parameters for the compositor, as well as specify the mixer type and output targets. Video parameters are immutable once set through the constructor. The audio settings are read once, when the LiveVideoCompositor is constructed; changing them afterwards has no effect. Output destinations can be modified after initialization.

constructors.name: LiveVideoCompositorSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the LiveVideoCompositorSettings class with the specified video dimensions and frame rate.
constructors.remarks: The constructor sets the video parameters which are immutable after initialization. The mixer type is automatically set to OpenGL for cross-platform compatibility. Audio settings are initialized to default values and can be changed until this object is passed to the LiveVideoCompositor constructor.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: The width of the output video in pixels.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: The height of the output video in pixels.

parameters.name: frameRate
parameters.summary: The frame rate for the output video.

properties.name: MixerType
properties.summary: Gets or sets the type of video mixer to use for compositing.
properties.value: The mixer type that determines the rendering backend. Common values include OpenGL for cross-platform support and D3D11 for Windows-specific hardware acceleration.

properties.name: AudioEnabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio stream processing is enabled in the compositor.
properties.value: true if audio processing is enabled; otherwise, false. When disabled, the compositor will process video only. Default value is true. Read once, when the LiveVideoCompositor is constructed; changing it afterwards has no effect.

properties.name: VideoWidth
properties.summary: Gets the width of the output video in pixels.
properties.value: The video width in pixels. This value is immutable and must be set through the constructor.

properties.name: VideoHeight
properties.summary: Gets the height of the output video in pixels.
properties.value: The video height in pixels. This value is immutable and must be set through the constructor.

properties.name: VideoFrameRate
properties.summary: Gets the frame rate for the output video.
properties.value: The video frame rate as a VideoFrameRate object, which typically represents frames per second. This value is immutable and must be set through the constructor.

properties.name: AudioFormat
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio sample format for the compositor's audio output.
properties.value: The audio format that determines the bit depth and encoding of audio samples. Default value is S16LE (16-bit signed little-endian). Read once, when the LiveVideoCompositor is constructed.

properties.name: AudioSampleRate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio sample rate in Hz.
properties.value: The number of audio samples per second. Common values include 44100 Hz (CD quality) and 48000 Hz (professional audio). Default value is 48000 Hz. Read once, when the LiveVideoCompositor is constructed.

properties.name: AudioChannels
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of audio channels.
properties.value: The number of audio channels. Common values are 1 for mono and 2 for stereo. Default value is 2 (stereo). Read once, when the LiveVideoCompositor is constructed.

properties.name: AudioMixerLatency
properties.summary: Gets or sets how long the audio mixer waits for late input before it mixes without it. See Latency.
properties.value: Default: 100 ms. Zero gives the behaviour before this setting existed. Read once, when the LiveVideoCompositor is constructed.

properties.name: VideoView
properties.summary: Gets or sets the video view control for direct rendering output.
properties.value: The IVideoView implementation that will display the compositor's video output. This is typically a UI control where the video will be rendered. Can be null if no direct video display is needed.

properties.name: AudioOutput
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio renderer block for audio playback.
properties.value: The AudioRendererBlock that handles audio output to the system's audio device. Can be null if audio playback is not required or if audio is disabled.

properties.name: InputFrameHoldTimeout
properties.summary: Gets or sets the timeout after which an input's bridge switches from repeating its last received frame to producing black frames when no new buffers arrive.
properties.value: Default is 24 hours, which effectively holds the last frame for the entire duration of any pause. Reduce this (e.g. TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)) if you prefer the legacy bridge-source behavior where a stalled input visibly blacks out after a short delay. Must be strictly positive and must not exceed MaxInputFrameHoldTimeout.

properties.name: MaxVideoInputsCount
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of video input sources that can be connected to the compositor.
properties.value: The maximum video inputs count. Default is 10.

properties.name: MaxVideoOutputsCount
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of video output destinations that can receive the composed video.
properties.value: The maximum video outputs count. Default is 10.

properties.name: MaxAudioInputsCount
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of audio input sources that can be connected to the compositor.
properties.value: The maximum audio inputs count. Default is 10.

properties.name: MaxAudioOutputsCount
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of audio output destinations that can receive the mixed audio.
properties.value: The maximum audio outputs count. Default is 10.

classes.name: LVCAudioInput
classes.summary: Represents an audio input for the Live Video Compositor that can receive and process audio streams. This class provides functionality to connect audio sources, apply processing blocks, and route audio to the compositor pipeline. Implements the LVCInput.

constructors.name: LVCAudioInput
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the LVCAudioInput class.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name identifier for this audio input.

parameters.name: autostart

properties.name: BridgeInfo
properties.summary: Gets the format the input's bridge sink was built at, a copy taken by String). The compositor builds its side of the bridge at this format, and AudioInfoX) refuses a change once it is set (GitHub issue #2102).

methods.name: UpdateInfo
methods.summary: Updates the audio information for this input with new format specifications.
methods.remarks: Any format is accepted: the compositor's audio mixer converts every input to its own format. The format is set before the input is added to a compositor; the input's bridge is built at it then.

parameters.name: info
parameters.summary: The new audio information containing updated format, channels, or sample rate.

parameters.name: uniqueName2

methods.returns: true if every connection was made; otherwise, false.

classes.name: LVCAudioOutput
