classes.name: LVCInput
classes.summary: Base class for all Live Video Compositor input sources.
classes.remarks: This abstract base class provides the common functionality for all input types in the Live Video Compositor. It manages the input pipeline, bridge connections, and lifecycle operations. Derived classes implement specific input types such as video-only, audio-only, or combined video/audio inputs. Each input maintains its own pipeline for processing before sending data to the main compositor.

constructors.name: LVCInput
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the LVCInput class.
constructors.remarks: This protected constructor is called by derived classes to initialize the base input functionality. It creates a separate pipeline for this input and configures clock synchronization.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: A descriptive name for this input.

parameters.name: compositor
parameters.summary: The compositor this input belongs to. Can be null if adding later.

parameters.name: mainBlock
parameters.summary: The source block that provides the media stream.

parameters.name: mediaType
parameters.summary: The type of media this input provides (video, audio, or both).

parameters.name: autostart
parameters.summary: If true, starts automatically when the compositor starts.

parameters.name: processingBlock
parameters.summary: Optional processing block for applying effects. Default is null.

parameters.name: live
parameters.summary: If true, indicates a live source requiring real-time processing. Default is true.

properties.name: MainBlock
properties.summary: Gets or sets the main source block that provides media data for this input.
properties.value: The primary MediaBlock that generates or provides the media stream.

properties.name: MediaType
properties.summary: Gets the type of media this input provides.
properties.value: The LVCMediaType indicating whether this input provides video, audio, or both.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets the descriptive name of this input.
properties.value: A string identifying this input. Used for logging and user interface display.

properties.name: ID
properties.summary: Gets the unique identifier for this input.
properties.value: A Guid that uniquely identifies this input instance.

properties.name: UniqueName
properties.summary: Gets or sets the unique bridge identifier for the primary media stream.
properties.value: A string used to identify the bridge connection for video or primary audio streams.

properties.name: UniqueName2
properties.summary: Gets or sets the unique bridge identifier for the secondary media stream.
properties.value: A string used to identify the bridge connection for secondary audio streams in video/audio inputs.

properties.name: Pipeline
properties.summary: Gets the media processing pipeline for this input.
properties.value: The MediaBlocksPipeline that manages this input's processing chain.

properties.name: IsSeekable
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this input supports seeking operations.
properties.value: true if the input can seek to different positions; otherwise, false.

properties.name: AutoStart
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this input starts automatically with the main compositor.
properties.value: true if the input should start when the compositor starts; otherwise, false.

properties.name: BuildError
properties.summary: Gets why the last MediaBlockPadMediaType) found no pad, for the refusal message; null when it found one.

properties.name: BuildRefusal
properties.summary: Gets the error Input_AddAsync reports for a String) that returned false.

properties.name: UnreadDemuxerSettings
properties.summary: Gets why a DemuxerSourceBlock source has no outputs at all, when that is the case; otherwise null. The block's own "Unable to get media info" goes to a context it does not have yet.

methods.name: UnknownFrameSizeError
methods.summary: Returns why this input cannot be added because the frame size of the video bridge it builds is unknown, or null - always null for an input that builds no video bridge from its info.

methods.name: Build
methods.summary: Builds the internal pipeline structure for this input.
methods.remarks: This virtual method is called when the input is added to a compositor. Derived classes must override this method to create their specific pipeline structure, including bridge connections and any necessary processing blocks.

parameters.name: uniqueName
parameters.summary: The unique bridge identifier for the primary stream.

parameters.name: uniqueName2
parameters.summary: The unique bridge identifier for the secondary stream (if applicable).

methods.returns: true if every connection was made; false if one failed and the input feeds nothing.

methods.name: GetSourceOutput
methods.summary: Looks up the source's output of the given type for String); the reason there is none goes to BuildError.

parameters.name: type
parameters.summary: The media type of the output to look up.

methods.returns: The output pad, or null when the source has none of that type.

methods.name: SourceMissingStream
methods.summary: Tells why the source is known to send no stream of the given kind through an output it has. An RTSPSourceBlock has no stream the camera info its settings have read, if any, lacks - in compatibility mode it creates both outputs whatever the camera carries - and with audio off sends the camera's audio to a fakesink. An RTSPRAWSourceBlock builds the paths Boolean) describes. A UniversalSourceBlock goes by its render setting, then the stream count of the file info its settings have read: CreateAsync turns the setting off for a file with no such stream, settings built with the constructor and read with ReadInfoAsync keep it. An NDI source has audio when the sender info its settings have probed, if any, has an audio stream: its pads exist whatever the sender carries.

parameters.name: video
parameters.summary: true for video, false for audio.

methods.returns: Why the source has no such stream, or null - also when that is unknown, or for any other source.

methods.name: RTSPRAWMissingStream
methods.summary: Tells why an RTSPRAWSourceBlock's source builds no stream of the given kind, decided the way RTSPRAWSource.Init builds its paths from the camera info its settings have read: video for a video RTP stream, audio for an audio stream with audio enabled. No info read: the content is unknown.
methods.returns: Why the source has no such stream, or null - also when that is unknown.

methods.name: InfoHasStream
methods.summary: Answers whether the info read from a source has a stream of the given kind; no info means unknown.

methods.name: ResumeAsync
methods.summary: Resumes playback of this input after it has been paused.
methods.remarks: This virtual method can be overridden by derived classes to perform additional operations when resuming. The base implementation simply resumes the pipeline.
methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous resume operation.

methods.name: PauseAsync
methods.summary: Pauses playback of this input.
methods.remarks: The input can be resumed later using ResumeAsync(). The input maintains its current position and state while paused.
methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous pause operation.

methods.name: StartAsync
methods.summary: Starts this input's pipeline and begins processing media.
methods.remarks: For certain source types (UniversalSourceBlock, DecklinkVideoSourceBlock), this method waits for the pipeline to reach a ready state before returning. This ensures proper initialization of complex sources. The preloadOnly parameter is useful for preparing inputs without immediately starting playback.

parameters.name: preloadOnly
parameters.summary: If true, only preloads the pipeline without starting playback. Default is false.

methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with true if the start was successful; otherwise, false.

methods.name: StopAsync
methods.summary: Stops this input's pipeline and releases processing resources.
methods.remarks: This method performs a forced stop of the pipeline to ensure quick shutdown. After stopping, the input would need to be restarted using StartAsync() to resume processing.
methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with true if the stop was successful; otherwise, false.

methods.name: SafeDispose
methods.summary: Disposes one child, reporting rather than throwing.
methods.remarks: A teardown that throws - a caller's processing block, say - must not cost the remaining children their release, nor let the exception escape Boolean).

parameters.name: item
parameters.summary: The child to dispose. Ignored when null.

parameters.name: what
parameters.summary: What is being disposed, for the log line.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases the unmanaged and optionally managed resources used by this input.
methods.remarks: This method disposes of the main block, pipeline, and bridge sink block if they exist. Derived classes should override this method to dispose of their specific resources, ensuring to call the base implementation.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources.

methods.name: Finalize
methods.summary: Finalizes an instance of the LVCInput class.
methods.remarks: The finalizer calls Dispose(false) to release unmanaged resources. This ensures resources are cleaned up even if Dispose() is not called explicitly.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Performs application-defined tasks associated with freeing, releasing, or resetting resources.
methods.remarks: Call this method when you are finished using the input. This method calls Dispose(true) and suppresses finalization to improve performance.

classes.name: LVCOutput
classes.summary: Base class for all Live Video Compositor output destinations.
classes.remarks: This class provides the common functionality for all output types in the Live Video Compositor. It manages the output pipeline, bridge connections from the main compositor, and lifecycle operations. Derived classes implement specific output types such as video files, streams, or display outputs. Each output maintains its own pipeline separate from the main compositor for independent control.

constructors.name: LVCOutput
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the LVCOutput class.
constructors.remarks: This constructor initializes the output pipeline and configures clock synchronization with the main compositor. The main block typically represents a file sink, stream sink, or display renderer.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: A descriptive name for this output.

parameters.name: compositor
parameters.summary: The compositor this output belongs to.

parameters.name: mainBlock
parameters.summary: The sink block that will receive and process the media stream.

parameters.name: mediaType
parameters.summary: The type of media this output handles (video, audio, or both).

parameters.name: autostart
parameters.summary: If true, starts automatically when the compositor starts.

properties.name: Pipeline
properties.summary: Gets the media processing pipeline for this output.
properties.value: The MediaBlocksPipeline that manages this output's processing chain.

properties.name: AutoStart
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this output starts automatically with the main compositor.
properties.value: true if the output should start when the compositor starts; otherwise, false.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets the descriptive name of this output.
properties.value: A string identifying this output. Used for logging and user interface display.

properties.name: ID
properties.summary: Gets the unique identifier for this output.
properties.value: A Guid that uniquely identifies this output instance.

methods.name: Build
methods.summary: Builds the internal pipeline structure for this output.
methods.remarks: This virtual method creates the bridge source blocks that receive data from the main compositor and connects them to the output's main block. It can be overridden by derived classes for custom pipeline configurations. The method handles dynamic input creation for blocks that support it.

parameters.name: uniqueName
parameters.summary: The unique bridge identifier for the primary stream (video or audio).

parameters.name: uniqueName2
parameters.summary: The unique bridge identifier for the secondary stream (used for video/audio outputs).

methods.name: SetAndConnectMainBlock
methods.summary: Sets a new main block and connects it to the existing bridge source.
methods.remarks: This protected method allows derived classes to change the output destination dynamically. The bridge source must already be created before calling this method.

parameters.name: mainBlock
parameters.summary: The new sink block to use as the main output destination.

methods.returns: true if the connection was successful; false if the block is null or connection failed.

methods.name: StartAsync
methods.summary: Starts this output's pipeline and begins processing media from the compositor.
methods.remarks: This method should be called after the output has been added to the compositor. If AutoStart is true, this method is called automatically when the compositor starts.
methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with true if the start was successful; otherwise, false.

methods.name: StopAsync
methods.summary: Stops this output's pipeline and finalizes any pending operations.
methods.remarks: For file outputs, using force=true may result in incomplete files or corrupted endings. Always use force=false (default) for file outputs to ensure proper finalization. For display or streaming outputs, force=true can be used for immediate shutdown.

parameters.name: force
parameters.summary: If true, forces immediate pipeline shutdown without waiting for pending data. If false, performs a graceful shutdown using end-of-stream messages. Default is false.

methods.returns: A Task`1 that completes with true if the stop was successful; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases the unmanaged and optionally managed resources used by this output.
methods.remarks: This method disposes of the main block, pipeline, and bridge source block if they exist. Derived classes should override this method to dispose of their specific resources, ensuring to call the base implementation.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources.

methods.name: Finalize
methods.summary: Finalizes an instance of the LVCOutput class.
methods.remarks: The finalizer calls Dispose(false) to release unmanaged resources. This ensures resources are cleaned up even if Dispose() is not called explicitly.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Performs application-defined tasks associated with freeing, releasing, or resetting resources.
methods.remarks: Call this method when you are finished using the output. This method ensures proper cleanup of all resources and should be called before removing the output from the compositor.

methods.name: GetFilenameOrURL
methods.summary: Gets the filename or URL associated with this output.
methods.remarks: This method delegates to the main block's implementation of IMediaBlockSink. It's typically used for file or stream outputs to retrieve the destination path or URL.
methods.returns: The filename or URL if the main block implements IMediaBlockSink; otherwise, null.

methods.name: SetFilenameOrURL
methods.summary: Sets the filename or URL for this output.
methods.remarks: This method delegates to the main block's implementation of IMediaBlockSink. It's typically used for file or stream outputs to set the destination path or URL. The actual behavior depends on the specific sink implementation in the main block.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: The filename or URL to set as the output destination.

classes.name: LVCVideoAudioInput
classes.summary: Represents a combined video and audio input source for the Live Video Compositor.
classes.remarks: This class handles input streams that contain both video and audio components. It provides separate processing pipelines for video and audio, allowing independent effects and transformations on each stream while maintaining synchronization. Like video-only inputs, it supports positioning, resize policies, and preview rendering.

constructors.name: LVCVideoAudioInput
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the LVCVideoAudioInput class with a compositor reference.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: A descriptive name for this input.

parameters.name: compositor
parameters.summary: The LiveVideoCompositor instance this input belongs to.

parameters.name: mainBlock
parameters.summary: The source media block that provides both video and audio streams.

parameters.name: videoInfo
parameters.summary: The video frame information. Width and height are required; the frame rate is a preference, and a source at another or a variable rate is accepted. null if video is disabled. Any other value gives the input a video leg unless its source - a UniversalSourceBlock, UniversalSourceBlockV2, DemuxerSourceBlock, BluRaySourceBlock or RTSPSourceBlock - renders no video, or the file or camera it has read has no video stream.

parameters.name: audioInfo
parameters.summary: The audio information, or null if audio is disabled. Any other value enables audio when the compositor mixes audio, unless its source - a UniversalSourceBlock, UniversalSourceBlockV2, DemuxerSourceBlock, BluRaySourceBlock or RTSPSourceBlock - renders no audio, or the file or camera it has read has no audio stream - or any other source has no audio output of its own; the input then carries the compositor's audio format.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.summary: The position and size of the video component within the compositor output.

parameters.name: autostart
parameters.summary: If true, the input will start automatically when the compositor starts.

parameters.name: processingVideoBlock
parameters.summary: An optional processing block for the video stream. Default is null.

parameters.name: processingAudioBlock
parameters.summary: An optional processing block for the audio stream. Default is null.

parameters.name: live
parameters.summary: If true, indicates this is a live source requiring real-time processing. Default is true.

parameters.name: customSyncFlag
parameters.summary: Optional custom synchronization flag for advanced timing control. Default is null.

constructors.name: LVCVideoAudioInput

constructors.remarks: This constructor is typically used when creating inputs that will be added to a compositor later.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: A descriptive name for this input.

parameters.name: mainBlock
parameters.summary: The source media block that provides both video and audio streams.

parameters.name: videoInfo
parameters.summary: The video frame information. Width and height are required; the frame rate is a preference, and a source at another or a variable rate is accepted. null if video is disabled. Any other value gives the input a video leg unless its source - a UniversalSourceBlock, UniversalSourceBlockV2, DemuxerSourceBlock, BluRaySourceBlock or RTSPSourceBlock - renders no video, or the file or camera it has read has no video stream.

parameters.name: audioInfo
parameters.summary: The audio information. Format, channels, and sample rate are required. Can be null if audio is disabled.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.summary: The position and size of the video component within the compositor output.

parameters.name: autostart
parameters.summary: If true, the input will start automatically when added to a compositor.

parameters.name: processingVideoBlock
parameters.summary: An optional processing block for the video stream. Default is null.

parameters.name: processingAudioBlock
parameters.summary: An optional processing block for the audio stream. Default is null.

parameters.name: live
parameters.summary: If true, indicates this is a live source requiring real-time processing. Default is true.

parameters.name: customSyncFlag
parameters.summary: Optional custom synchronization flag for advanced timing control. Default is null.

properties.name: Rectangle
properties.summary: Gets or sets the position and size of the video component within the compositor output.
properties.value: A Rect defining the position (x, y) and size (width, height) in pixels.

properties.name: ZOrder
properties.summary: Gets or sets the z-order (layer position) of the video component.
properties.value: The z-order value. Higher values appear on top of lower values. Default is 0.

properties.name: ResizePolicy
properties.summary: Gets or sets the resize policy for the video component.
properties.value: The LVCResizePolicy that determines how the video is scaled to fit its rectangle. Default is Stretch.

properties.name: ProcessingVideoBlocks
properties.summary: Gets the list of video processing blocks applied to the video stream.
properties.value: A list of MediaBlock instances that process the video stream. Processing blocks should not change the video dimensions.

properties.name: VideoInfo
properties.summary: Gets the video stream information for this input.
properties.value: The video frame information containing width, height, format, and frame rate. May be null if this input was configured without video.

properties.name: AudioInfo
properties.summary: Gets the audio stream information for this input.
properties.value: The audio information containing format, sample rate, and channel configuration. May be null if this input was configured without audio. For an input created with a compositor and audio, a copy of the compositor's audio format.

properties.name: VideoView
properties.summary: Gets or sets an optional video view for previewing the video component of this input.
properties.value: An IVideoView instance for rendering a preview of the video stream, or null if no preview is needed.

methods.name: UnknownFrameSizeError
methods.remarks: Asked only for an input with a video leg: one without it has no video bridge to size.

methods.name: HasVideoLeg
methods.summary: Answers whether this input has a video leg: video info, and a source with video to render.
methods.remarks: The compositor claims a video slot and builds a video bridge only for such an input. Decided the way HasAudioLeg is, except that an NDI source with video info always has one.

methods.name: HasAudioLeg
methods.summary: Answers whether this input has an audio leg: audio info, and a source with audio to render.
methods.remarks: The compositor claims an audio slot and builds an audio bridge only for such an input. Decided before the source is built: from the outputs of a block that creates them in its constructor, from the settings and file info of a UniversalSourceBlock, from the settings and camera info of an RTSPSourceBlock or RTSPRAWSourceBlock, from the probed sender info of an NDI source, and for any other block from its outputs - an audio output the video leg does not take (GitHub issue #2112).

methods.name: SourceHasStream
methods.summary: Answers whether the source renders a stream of the given kind. A source Boolean) knows to send none has none. A UniversalSourceBlockV2, DemuxerSourceBlock or BluRaySourceBlock is asked for the outputs it created in its constructor from its render settings, an RTSPSourceBlock for the ones it created from the camera info its settings have read (in compatibility mode it creates both, info or not). An RTSPRAWSourceBlock, UniversalSourceBlock or NDI source has every stream Boolean) does not rule out. Any other source is taken at its word for video, and has audio when String) would find an audio output to connect.

parameters.name: video
parameters.summary: true for video, false for audio.

methods.returns: false only when the source is known to have no such stream.

methods.name: Build
methods.summary: Builds the internal pipeline structure for this video/audio input.
methods.remarks: This internal method constructs separate pipelines for video and audio: - Video pipeline: bridge sink, optional tee/renderer for preview, optional crop/resize for LetterboxToFill - Audio pipeline: bridge sink with optional processing block A leg the compositor passes no channel name for is not built: it has decided, through HasVideoLeg and HasAudioLeg, that the input has none. This method is called automatically when the input is added to a compositor.

parameters.name: uniqueName
parameters.summary: A unique identifier for the video bridge sink connection.

parameters.name: uniqueName2
parameters.summary: A unique identifier for the audio bridge sink connection.

methods.returns: true if every connection was made; otherwise, false.

methods.name: ResumeAsync
methods.summary: Resumes playback of this input after it has been paused.
methods.remarks: This override ensures that the video stream's alpha channel is restored to full opacity when resuming, in case it was set to zero during initialization. This is particularly important for inputs that were added while the compositor was already running.
methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous operation.

methods.name: UpdateLetterboxFillRectangle
methods.summary: Updates the crop settings when using LetterboxToFill resize policy.
methods.remarks: This private method recalculates and applies the crop area needed to implement the LetterboxToFill resize policy when the rectangle dimensions change. It ensures the video fills the entire rectangle while maintaining aspect ratio. Only applies to the video component; audio is unaffected.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases the unmanaged and optionally managed resources used by this video/audio input.
methods.remarks: This method properly disposes of both video and audio bridge sinks, as well as any preview components that were created. It ensures all resources are cleaned up in the correct order before calling the base class disposal logic.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources.

classes.name: LVCVideoAudioOutput
classes.summary: Represents a video and audio output component for the Live Video Compositor. This class handles the creation and management of both video and audio bridge sources that connect to the main processing pipeline, supporting optional processing blocks for both media streams.
classes.remarks: This output type is used when both video and audio streams need to be processed and output from the compositor. It creates separate bridge sources for video and audio, allowing for independent processing of each stream before they are connected to the main output block.

constructors.name: LVCVideoAudioOutput

classes.name: LiveVideoCompositor
classes.summary: Provides real-time live video composition and mixing capabilities for multiple video and audio inputs. This class creates a complex MediaBlocks pipeline that can mix multiple video sources in real-time, apply video effects, manage overlay graphics, and route the composed output to multiple destinations. Supports CPU-based mixing, GPU-accelerated OpenGL mixing, Direct3D 11 composition (Windows), and input switching modes. Essential for live streaming, video production, broadcast applications, and multi-camera setups. Implements the IDisposable. Implements the IAsyncDisposable.
classes.remarks: The Live Video Compositor manages multiple pipelines: - Main pipeline: Handles video/audio mixing and effects processing - Input pipelines: Each input source runs in its own pipeline for isolation - Output pipelines: Multiple outputs can be configured for different destinations The compositor uses bridge blocks to connect these separate pipelines efficiently.

Video and audio mixers 2. Tee blocks for splitting signals 3. Overlay managers (if not on Android) 4. All input sources 5. All output sinks

methods.summary: Finalizes an instance of the LiveVideoCompositor class.

methods.name: Dispose

methods.remarks: This method should be called when the Live Video Compositor is no longer needed. It releases all resources including MediaBlocks pipelines, mixers, effects, and overlays. After disposal, the object cannot be used and should be discarded.

The certificate belongs to this instance: call it on every instance you create, before starting it -- licensing one instance does not license another. Without a certificate the instance runs in the 30-day trial.

methods.returns: The main pipeline instance.

methods.name: GetVideoMixer
methods.summary: Gets the video mixer block if it's a VideoMixerBlock type (not a switcher).
methods.returns: The video mixer block, or null if using switcher mode or another mixer type.

methods.name: GetAudioMixer
methods.summary: Gets the audio mixer block if it's an AudioMixerBlock type (not a switcher).
methods.returns: The audio mixer block, or null if using switcher mode.

methods.name: Build
methods.summary: Builds the internal pipeline by creating and connecting all blocks (mixers, tees, bridges, effects).
methods.remarks: Runs once. Every later call - a restart - reuses the graph it built and does no layout work: every add and removal lays its own slot out as it happens, whatever the pipeline state, so the mixer settings are already current and only Background has to be carried across here. The shape of the graph is fixed at the first build: turning Video_Overlay_Enabled on or off afterwards does not add or remove the overlay manager (a change is reported on the restart rather than silently ignored; the property does not exist on Android). Settings.VideoChannelCount is fixed even earlier - the bridge sink array and the per-channel effects are sized from it in the constructor.
methods.returns: true if the pipeline was built successfully, false otherwise.

methods.name: Input_SlotRectanglesLocked
methods.summary: Maps every video bridge slot to the rectangle of the input that claims it.
methods.remarks: Keyed by the input's own slot, not by its position in the input list: the two agree only while every slot from 0 up is taken in order, and neither a removal nor a slot skipped as unusable leaves them agreeing. Keyed by position, an input's rectangle landed on another input's picture, or on the hidden placeholder. GitHub issue #1383. Call with _listsLock held, and hold it until the streams have been written: an add landing between the snapshot and the write claims a slot the snapshot does not have, and its own layout call finds no stream yet - the input ends up claimed, wired and invisible.
methods.returns: An array sized to the bridge array, holding null for a slot no input claims.

methods.name: Input_ApplyVideoSlot
methods.summary: Puts a video bridge slot's layout onto the mixer stream that serves it.
methods.remarks: The streams sit in slot order, one per bridge slot, so slot i is stream i. It writes the rectangle and the alpha together: an unclaimed slot carries a fully transparent placeholder, so an input landing on one has to raise the alpha back or it stays invisible whatever its rectangle says, and a slot an input leaves has to go transparent again. Z-order and everything else are left alone. The callers are the adds and the removals, which own the slot's layout at that moment; nothing writes a slot afterwards, so a layout the caller sets through stands until it changes it again - a restart included. A no-op in switcher mode, whose settings object is never created and which has no mixer streams at all. The stream comes from the settings rather than from VideoMixerBlock.Input_List(): the block answers that from its native element, which exists only between a pipeline start and the matching stop, so on the restart path - Build() runs before the pipeline starts - the list is empty and every update would be silently dropped. Only the push to the pad needs the element, and it is skipped while there is none: the element is built from these settings and reads the values out of them at start.

parameters.name: rectangle
parameters.summary: The rectangle of the input claiming the slot, or null when no input claims it.

methods.name: HiddenSlotRectangle
methods.summary: The rectangle a video slot no input claims carries: a 16x16 square at the origin, which together with an alpha of 0 keeps it out of the composition.
methods.returns: A new rectangle - never a shared instance, since a stream's rectangle is mutable.

methods.name: DurationAsync
methods.summary: Gets the current playback position of the main pipeline.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains the current position.

methods.name: StartAsync
methods.summary: Starts the compositor, including all input pipelines, the main pipeline, and auto-start outputs.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if started successfully, false otherwise.

methods.name: StopAsync
methods.summary: Stops the compositor, including all input pipelines, the main pipeline, and all outputs.
methods.remarks: The input and output lists are snapshotted at the start, so an input added while the stop is running is not stopped by it - teardown is not serialized against the adds. Stop the compositor and add afterwards, rather than the other way round.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous stop operation.

methods.summary: Reports whether an add has to be refused because teardown has begun, and hands back the pipeline and bridge array the caller will use if it may proceed.

So an add is either refused, or it holds references that stay valid for the rest of its body - reading the fields again further down is what a concurrent Dispose could turn into a null.

methods.remarks: Audio slots shift independently of video ones - an audio-only input takes an audio slot and no video slot - so they need their own scan. Call with _listsLock held.

parameters.name: except
parameters.summary: An input to ignore - the one being added or removed.

methods.returns: true when another input still reports that slot as its own.

methods.name: Input_FirstFreeVideoSlot
methods.summary: Picks the first video slot no other input claims.
methods.remarks: Ids used to be positional - GetVideoInputsCount() - 1 - so removing an input left a hole and handed the next add an id a live input was still using: two inputs on one bridge name, one of them permanently black. Taking the first free slot instead makes that impossible; with no removals it returns exactly what the old expression did. A free slot is not automatically a usable one: a file input removed after the graph was built leaves its buffered bridge behind, and pairing a frame-based sink with it produces a black input that reports success. Such a slot is skipped, so the inputs that can use the remaining ones still get them. Bounded by the bridge array rather than by Settings.MaxVideoInputsCount, which has a public setter and can be raised after the array was sized from it. Call with _listsLock held.

parameters.name: bufferedBridge
parameters.summary: true for a file input, which feeds the buffered bridge; false for every other input, which feeds the frame-based one.

methods.returns: The slot index, or -1 when no usable slot is left.

methods.name: Input_FirstFreeAudioSlot
methods.summary: Picks the first audio slot no other input claims.
methods.remarks: Call with _listsLock held. See Boolean).
methods.returns: The slot index, or -1 when every slot is taken.

methods.name: Input_RestoreVideoBridgeSlot
methods.summary: Puts the frame-based bridge back into a video slot a file input had swapped for a buffered one, so the slot can take an ordinary video/audio input again.
methods.remarks: Only while the graph has never been built: after Build() the block in the slot is linked to the mixer and replacing it would break that link. A file input added before the first start and removed before it is therefore fully undone; one removed after the graph was built leaves its buffered bridge behind, and a later video/audio input landing on that index is refused with a message rather than crashing.

methods.name: Input_AddFailedAsync
methods.summary: Takes an input back out after a failed add: removes it from the input list and stops it if it was started, so a failed add leaves no slot occupied.
methods.remarks: The input is not disposed: an add that returns false never takes ownership, whatever the reason, and disposing here would leave the caller holding an object whose pipeline is already gone. The list entry goes first - across the await below the compositor's own StopAsync would otherwise walk this input.

parameters.name: method
parameters.summary: The calling method, for the log entry.

parameters.name: started
parameters.summary: Whether the input was already started and has to be stopped first.

methods.returns: Always false, so a caller can return the result of this call directly.

methods.summary: Adds a video-only input source to the compositor.

parameters.summary: The video input configuration to add.

The task result contains true if added successfully, false if max inputs reached or the input's video frame size is unknown (a width or height of 0; the reason is raised through OnError). On false the input was not added and is not disposed - it stays the caller's to dispose; if it had already been started it is stopped first.

methods.name: Output_AddRefusedByTeardown
methods.summary: Reports whether an output add has to be refused because teardown has begun, and hands back the pipeline and sink arrays the caller will use if it may proceed.
methods.remarks: The output twin of MediaBlock[]@), and safe for the same reason: DisposeCore raises _tearingDown under _listsLock before it releases anything, so an add is either refused or holds references that stay valid for the rest of its body. Reading the fields again further down is what a concurrent Dispose could turn into a null - the captured locals are what the caller must use.

parameters.name: method
parameters.summary: The calling method, for the log entry.

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.summary: The main pipeline, captured while it was still there.

methods.returns: true when the compositor is disposed or being disposed.

methods.name: Output_SinkNameIsClaimed
methods.summary: Reports whether a bridge sink name is still bound to one of the outputs in the list.
methods.remarks: Binding a second output to the name a live one uses puts both on one entry in BridgeSinkSourceCache: whichever registers second overwrites the other, which then silently receives nothing. Removal there is identity-checked, so the displaced output's own Dispose takes nothing out - but the winner's does, and the name is then registered by neither. Call with _listsLock held.
methods.returns: true when an output still holds that name.

methods.name: Output_FirstFreeSinkName
methods.summary: Picks the first bridge sink name no output claims.
methods.remarks: Ids used to be positional - GetVideoOutputsCount() - 1 - so removing an output left a hole and handed the next add a name a live output was still bound to. Taking the first free one instead makes that impossible; with no removals it returns exactly what the old expression did. The claim is the name and not the index because the video name carries the channel: two outputs on different channels share an index and still cannot collide. Bounded by the sink arrays rather than by Settings.Max*OutputsCount, which have public setters and can be raised after the arrays were sized from them. Call with _listsLock held.

methods.name: Video_Effects_AddOrUpdateAsync
methods.summary: Adds a new video effect or updates an existing effect on the specified channel.
methods.remarks: If an effect with the same name already exists, it will be updated with the new parameters. Effects are applied in the order they are added to the channel. A ResizeVideoEffect, crop effect or box cannot be added or updated through this call while the composition is running: every channel feeds the output bridges built for one frame size. The call is refused through OnError, and the effect stays registered, so the next start applies it. Setting a property on an effect object that is already applied is not intercepted and takes effect live.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.summary: The video effect to add or update. Must implement IBaseVideoEffect interface.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.summary: The video channel index to apply the effect to. Default is 0.

methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous operation.

methods.name: Video_Effects_Get
methods.summary: Retrieves a video effect by name from the specified channel.
methods.remarks: Effect names are matched without regard to case.

parameters.name: effectName
parameters.summary: The unique name identifier of the effect to retrieve.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.summary: The video channel index to search for the effect. Default is 0.

methods.returns: The video effect instance if found; otherwise, null.

methods.name: Video_Effects_RemoveAsync
methods.summary: Removes a video effect instance from the specified channel.
methods.remarks: The pipeline is temporarily paused during effect removal to ensure thread safety. If the effect is not found on the channel, the method returns without error. Before the first successful start, the effect is removed as configuration without changing the pipeline state. After the composition has stopped, a failed pause is logged and the effect is left in place rather than the call hanging.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.summary: The video effect instance to remove.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.summary: The video channel index to remove the effect from. Default is 0.

methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous operation.

methods.name: Video_Effects_RemoveAsync
methods.summary: Removes a video effect by name from the specified channel.
methods.remarks: The pipeline is temporarily paused during effect removal to ensure thread safety. If no effect with the given name exists, the method returns without error. Before the first successful start, the effect is removed as configuration without changing the pipeline state. After the composition has stopped, a failed pause is logged and the effect is left in place rather than the call hanging.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name identifier of the effect to remove.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.summary: The video channel index to remove the effect from. Default is 0.

methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous operation.

methods.name: PauseForEffectRemovalAsync
methods.summary: Pauses the composition before an effect is unplugged from the running graph.
methods.remarks: Before the first successful StartAsync, the effects are only configuration: they have no live graph to protect, so removal proceeds without changing the pipeline state. A compositor which has run at least once still pauses before removing a live effect. It cannot pause once the composition has been stopped: ClearData releases the GStreamer pipeline, so Pause returns early without touching the state. That case is reported and the effect is left in the list, where the next start picks it up.
methods.returns: true when the effect may be removed; false when the pause did not land.

methods.name: EffectsFor
methods.summary: Resolves the effects block for a channel, reporting an invalid call instead of throwing.

parameters.name: method
parameters.summary: The public method name to report the failure under.

methods.returns: The channel's effects block, or null when the compositor was disposed or the channel index is out of range.

methods.name: Video_Effects_Clear
methods.summary: Removes all video effects from the specified channel.
methods.remarks: A playing composition is paused for the clear and resumed afterwards. A composition left in Pause is cleared in place and stays paused. A frame-size effect present on a live composition refuses the clear - stop the composition first. A clear that cannot take the pause - the pipeline is already stopping - is reported and skipped. Before the first start the effects are only configuration and are removed without touching the pipeline state.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.summary: The video channel index to clear effects from. Default is 0.

methods.name: IsCompositionLive
methods.summary: Determines whether the composition has a live graph that effect removal must respect.
methods.remarks: V1 never resets _hasStarted on stop, so the pipeline state clause is what keeps removal-after-stop working as configuration.
methods.returns: true when the pipeline has started and is not stopped; otherwise, false.

methods.name: TryGetFrameSizeEffect

methods.returns: The effect instance, or null when none is registered.

classes.name: LiveVideoCompositorSettings
classes.summary: Configuration settings for the Live Video Compositor, defining video/audio format parameters, mixer technology, resource limits, and processing capabilities for real-time composition. These settings determine the compositor's output quality, performance characteristics, and capacity for handling multiple inputs and outputs.
classes.remarks: The settings are immutable for video dimensions and frame rate once created, as these fundamental parameters affect the entire composition pipeline. Other settings like mixer type and capacity limits can be adjusted based on the target platform and performance requirements. Default values are optimized for common live streaming scenarios with balanced quality and performance.

classes.name: LVCInput
classes.summary: Base class for Live Video Compositor input sources that feed media content into the composition pipeline. Each input runs in its own isolated MediaBlocks pipeline and connects to the main compositor via bridge blocks. This architecture allows for independent control of each input source (start, stop, pause) while maintaining synchronized output from the main composition pipeline. Supports video-only, audio-only, or combined video/audio inputs. Implements the IDisposable.
classes.remarks: Input types include: - Video capture devices (cameras, capture cards) - Audio capture devices (microphones, audio interfaces) - Network streams (RTSP, NDI, HTTP) - File-based sources (video files, image sequences) - Virtual sources (test patterns, screen capture) Each input maintains its own processing pipeline for isolation and independent lifecycle management.

classes.name: LVCOutput
classes.summary: Base class for Live Video Compositor output destinations that receive composed media content from the main composition pipeline. Each output runs in its own isolated MediaBlocks pipeline and connects to the main compositor via bridge blocks. This architecture allows for independent control of each output destination (start, stop, pause) while receiving synchronized content from the main composition pipeline. Supports video-only, audio-only, or combined video/audio outputs. Implements the IDisposable.
classes.remarks: Output types include: - File encoders (MP4, AVI, MOV recordings) - Streaming encoders (RTMP, SRT, UDP streaming) - Network outputs (NDI, RTP) - Display outputs (preview windows, fullscreen) - Hardware outputs (DeckLink, NDI hardware) Each output maintains its own processing pipeline for isolation and independent lifecycle management.

methods.name: StartAsync
methods.summary: Starts the output pipeline and begins receiving composed media from the compositor.

methods.name: StopAsync
methods.summary: Stops the output pipeline and finalizes any pending operations.

classes.name: LVCVideoAudioInput
classes.summary: Live Video Compositor combined video and audio input that feeds synchronized video/audio content into the composition pipeline. Handles sources with both video and audio streams, maintaining synchronization between streams while providing independent processing capabilities for video positioning/effects and audio mixing/effects. This is the most common input type for camera sources, media files, and streaming inputs. Implements the LVCInput.

methods.name: PublishChain
methods.summary: Points the block's output at output and claims the built latch, unless CleanUp has run since this build started. GitHub issue #957.
methods.remarks: The compare and the _isBuilt write are one critical section: the give-up path in CleanUp does its work while this thread still holds the gate, so without the compare its two writes are undone right here and every later Build() short-circuits on a block that owns nothing. The pad publish stays outside that lock. SetInternalPad blocks on RemoveProbe, which waits for an in-flight EOS probe, and that probe raises OnEOS on the streaming thread - a handler reading the effect count would take this lock. It does not make such a handler free to mutate the block: everything that mutates waits on _mutationGate, which this build holds. Attach reaches its chain under the same gate. It also stays ahead of the latch, where it has always been. Both orders were tried and neither has a reachable failure - AddProbe reports a failed install by returning 0 rather than throwing, and a discarded build leaving the pad on a chain it disowns costs nothing _inputPad does not already cost on every build. Do not move it again.

parameters.summary: The filters this build created, for the discard.

methods.name: MarkTornDown
methods.summary: Records that a teardown happened: the block is not built, and a build in flight has to discard rather than publish. GitHub issue #957.
methods.remarks: One critical section because the two writes are one fact. CleanUp reaches it from both paths - the give-up one, which runs while a build still holds the gate and is why the generation exists, and the ordinary one, which cannot race a build but has to mean the same to a build that started before either.

methods.name: TornDownSince
methods.summary: Whether a teardown has moved the block on since generation was read, so an insertion still in flight has to stop instead of reaching the graph. GitHub issue #960.
methods.remarks: Read without _audioEffectsLock on purpose: AudioConverter) asks this from inside an entry's monitor, and taking the list lock under one is the nesting no path in this class does - see EventArgs). The volatile read is not what makes the answer trustworthy, and it is worth being clear about which half is: the give-up path in CleanUp moves the generation BEFORE it sweeps the entries, and that sweep needs the same monitor the splice holds, so an AudioConverter) that takes the monitor after the sweep released it acquires the lock the sweeper exited - a barrier both threads passed through - and cannot miss the bump. What the volatile read adds is only that the value is re-read at all rather than cached in a register. != rather than >, the same as : the question is whether this is still the same run, not how many have been since.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.summary: The generation the caller snapshotted before it started.

methods.returns: true when MarkTornDown has run since.

methods.name: DiscardBuild
methods.summary: Gives back the filters a build published into the entries, for a build that lost the race with CleanUp's give-up path. GitHub issue #957.
methods.remarks: Exactly what the give-up path in CleanUp does and no more: drop the entries' filter references, touch no element. The elements belong to the pipeline, which is being disposed and releases its own children. The converter reference is kept, as that path also keeps it. The pipeline calls a second time from its dispose, while the pipeline is still alive - ClearData disposes it only after the per-block loop - and that call is what takes the converter to NULL and releases its wrapper. The pads likewise keep pointing at the discarded chain; the next build re-points them.

methods.name: AddOrUpdate
methods.summary: Adds a new audio effect to the processing chain or updates an existing effect with the same name. If an effect with the same name already exists, it will be replaced with the new configuration. Effects can be added dynamically during playback, and the block will reconfigure the processing chain to include the new effect. The effect will be automatically initialized and configured.
methods.remarks: Supported audio effects include: - Volume control and amplification - Stereo balance adjustment - Echo and reverb effects - Multi-band and parametric equalizers - Audio compression and expansion - Tempo scaling without pitch change Effects are applied in the order they were added to the chain. Reconfiguring a running graph is synchronous work, and this call does it on the thread it is called on. An effect added while the pipeline is not Playing stays registered without a filter, and the next build puts it in the graph. An effect added to a running graph keeps the stream's channel count: a outputs the format already playing, and its applies from the next start. This method, , and take one non-reentrant gate between them, and BaseAudioEffect.OnUpdate is raised from under it. A handler on that event must therefore not call back into any of them: doing so blocks the calling thread on a gate that same thread already holds. Change effect properties from the handler freely - that path takes only the effect's own monitor - but do the adding and removing elsewhere.

methods.remarks: Every field on the way to the state can be nulled by a teardown running on another thread - MediaBlock.Dispose nulls the context itself, and ClearData nulls the pipeline - so each is read once into a local rather than re-read per dereference. The handle is checked before the state because CurrentState is an unchecked read at an offset from it: on a disposed wrapper that is an access violation, which cannot be caught, while Handle is a plain field read that is IntPtr.Zero by then.
methods.returns: The current state, or null when there is no pipeline to read.

methods.name: Remove
methods.summary: Removes an audio effect from the processing chain. This method safely removes the effect from both the high-level effect list and the underlying GStreamer processing chain, cleaning up resources and event handlers.
methods.remarks: An effect whose filter changes the channel count of a running stream - a mono WeightedChannelMixAudioEffect on a stereo source - is not removed, or replaced through BaseAudioEffect), until the pipeline stops: the stream would switch channel count under an encoder or a muxer that has already negotiated it. The refusal is reported as an error.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.summary: The audio effect to remove from the processing chain.

methods.name: TryRemove
methods.summary: BaseAudioEffect), reporting whether the effect's filter really left the graph.
methods.returns: true when the effect is removed and its filter was in the graph - a removal that flushed.

methods.name: Clear
methods.summary: Removes all audio effects from the processing chain. This method clears both the high-level effects list and the underlying GStreamer processing elements, returning the block to a pass-through state with no effects applied - except an effect that changes the channel count of a running stream.
methods.remarks: An effect that changes the channel count of a running stream stays, as BaseAudioEffect) describes, and an error is reported for each such effect.

methods.name: ClearCore
methods.summary: Clear, reporting how many effects were removed.
methods.returns: The number of removed effects whose filter was in the graph - removals that flushed.

methods.name: DropFilter
methods.summary: Forgets the filter of entry without touching the element - for the cases where the element belongs to a pipeline that is already gone, so removing or disposing it would be a call on freed memory. The element dies with its pipeline; the wrapper's toggle ref keeps it alive until then.
methods.returns: true when there was a filter to forget.

methods.name: RetireFilter
methods.summary: Takes the filter of entry out of the graph and releases it. The caller holds _mutationGate.
methods.remarks: The entry's own lock spans the removal AND the dispose, and that is the whole point of this method. Splitting them is what let a teardown land inside the removal's 2 s idle probe and zero the wrappers that removal was working through, after which it edited the graph through IntPtr.Zero and still returned true. The one thing this can hold up is a settings push for this same effect, and only for as long as the removal takes; the streaming thread never takes this lock unless the application sets a property from a sample callback. GitHub issue #949.
methods.returns: true when the entry has no filter afterwards; false when the filter could not be removed and is still in the graph.

methods.name: RefuseChannelChange
methods.summary: Refuses taking the filter of entry out of a running stream when its input and output channel counts differ: the stream downstream would switch channel count under an encoder or a muxer that has already negotiated it, and the recording stops (not-negotiated). The effect stays until the pipeline stops. GitHub issue #3431.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.summary: The entry about to lose its filter.

parameters.name: method
parameters.summary: The public method, for the error.

methods.returns: true when the change is refused and reported.

methods.name: CurrentChannels
methods.summary: The channel count negotiated on a pad of element.
methods.returns: The channel count, or 0 when nothing is negotiated.

methods.name: RefreshOutputPad
methods.summary: Points _outputPad at the src pad of the last filter in the graph - or the converter's when there is none - after a live edit changed the tail of the chain. The caller holds _mutationGate and must not hold any entry's lock. A block that is not built keeps its pads: the next Build sets them itself, and teardown deliberately leaves them pointing at the old run. GitHub issue #955.

methods.name: GuardTailRemoval
methods.summary: Arms an on-demand output's drop probe ahead on the pad that is the chain's tail once entry has left - a no-op unless entry is the tail. Same contract as RefreshOutputPad.

methods.name: TailSrcPad
methods.summary: The src pad of the chain's tail - the last filter in the graph, or the converter when there is none - with skip left out. RefreshOutputPad and GuardTailRemoval both go by it; a live add anchors its splice on its own.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.summary: An entry to leave out, or null.

methods.returns: The pad, or null when the tail has none.

methods.name: LastFilterInChainBefore
methods.summary: The last filter before stop - or in the whole list when it is null - whose elements are still in the graph: a retirement that failed after already nulling the filter's output element must yield neither a splice anchor nor the chain's tail, or the walk dereferences null. This is a field test, not a linkage test - a filter stuck in the bin with a severed link is still returned, and deliberately so: anchoring on it makes the next splice fail loudly, where skipping it would splice at the wrong position and silently invert the order.

parameters.name: stop
parameters.summary: The entry to stop in front of, or null for the whole list.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.summary: An entry whose filter is leaving, or null; only its Retiring one counts.

methods.returns: The filter, or null when only the converter is left.

methods.summary: Finds the entry carrying name.
methods.returns: The entry, or null.

methods.summary: Copies the entries under _audioEffectsLock so a caller can walk them while a reader is looking at the list.
methods.returns: A snapshot of the entries, in order.

methods.name: HasFilter
methods.summary: Whether the entry currently has a filter in the graph.
methods.returns: true when a filter is attached.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases unmanaged and optionally managed resources used by the audio effects block. Properly disposes of all audio effects, the effects processor, and audio converter components.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources.

methods.name: ForgetEffects
methods.summary: Drops every effect and unsubscribes its handler, so a disposed block leaves no delegate behind in effects the application still holds.
methods.remarks: Takes only _audioEffectsLock, never the gate: the filters are CleanUp's to retire, and this has to stay reachable when the gate is wedged - see Boolean). The whole drain is one critical section, and the latch is set inside it. Draining a snapshot and then unsubscribing outside the lock is not enough, and neither is subscribing atomically on the other side: on the very path this method exists for - a mutation holding the gate past CleanUpGateTimeout, so gave up and returned - that mutation is still running, and it publishes its effect *after* this drain has been and gone. The entry was never in the snapshot, so nothing unsubscribes it, and the application is left holding a delegate into a disposed block. Only a latch the publisher also reads closes that, which is why the two share this lock rather than being ordered against each other. Unsubscribing under the lock is free: OnUpdate is a field-like event, so -= is an interlocked delegate remove and runs no application code.

methods.name: CleanUp
methods.summary: Cleans up the audio effects block by disposing of all internal processing components. This method takes every filter back out of the graph and disposes the audio converter, resetting the block to an unbuilt state. The effects themselves stay registered, so a rebuild restores the chain.

methods.name: ReportUnmappedRunningTime
methods.summary: Logs, once per run, that the element has stopped reporting a running time, and narrows the cause as far as the message itself allows.
methods.remarks: A single unmapped message is ordinary: it is what the element reports right after a seek or a flush. A whole run of them is issue #1491, and narrowing that needs the other fields of the same message, which the event does not carry. ebur128level derives all three times from the same segment and the same buffer presentation timestamp, so: all undefined means the buffers arrived with no presentation timestamp; a defined timestamp with an undefined stream-time means the element could not map that timestamp - either it holds no TIME segment at all, or the window falls outside the segment it holds, which the message cannot tell apart; and a defined stream-time alongside an unmapped running time narrows no further, because the two lookups do not fail together in every case - gst_segment_to_running_time also answers NONE for a position inside the segment's offset and for a negative-rate segment with no stop, both of which leave the stream time mappable. Ahead of all of that, this re-reads running-time itself: the caller read it off this same structure, so a value that reads back fine here says the element mapped the window and the loss is in the reading, not in the stream.

parameters.summary: The running time already read from it, or null.

properties.summary: Gets all output pads for this remove silence block. This block has a single output for processed audio.
properties.value: Array containing the single output pad for processed audio.

properties.name: Threshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the silence detection threshold. Audio levels below this threshold will be considered as silence. Values range from 0.0 (clamped to the element's -70 dB floor - only near-digital silence is removed) to 1.0 (full scale - every sample counts as silence). Lower values are more permissive; higher values remove more audio.
properties.value: The silence threshold as a linear value from 0.0 to 1.0. Default: 0.001 (-60 dB).

properties.name: Squash
properties.summary: Gets or sets the squash mode. Silent sections are always dropped; squash controls what happens to the timeline afterwards. When enabled (true), the timestamps of the surviving buffers are pulled back by the dropped duration, so the output is shorter and gapless - which also means the audio no longer lines up with the video of the same recording. When disabled (false), the gap is left in place and the surviving buffers keep their original timestamps, which keeps A/V sync.
properties.value: true to close the gap left by removed silence; false to keep the original timeline. Default: false, matching the element.

classes.name: SilenceDetectorBlock
classes.summary: Silence detector block that analyzes uncompressed audio streams to detect periods of silence based on a configurable threshold level. This block monitors audio in real-time, identifies when audio levels drop below the specified threshold, and tracks the duration of silence periods. Features include real-time callbacks for silence start/end events, collection of all silence periods with precise timestamps, and JSON export functionality for detailed analysis and reporting. Essential for audio editing applications, speech processing, podcast production, and any scenario requiring automatic silence detection and analysis. Implements the MediaBlock. Implements the IMediaBlockInternals. Implements the IDisposable.

Values are typically negative (e.g., -40.0 dB for fairly quiet audio, -60.0 dB for very quiet). Lower (more negative) values are less sensitive and require quieter audio to trigger silence detection. Higher (less negative) values are more sensitive and will detect silence at louder levels.

events.name: OnSilenceStarted
events.summary: This event occurs when a silence period starts (audio level drops below the threshold). Provides immediate notification with timestamp and audio level information, enabling applications to respond in real-time to silence detection.

events.name: OnSilenceEnded
events.summary: This event occurs when a silence period ends (audio level rises above the threshold). Provides notification with timestamp, audio level, and the completed silence period - start time, end time and duration - for recording or analysis purposes. The period is null whenever it could not be formed: one of its ends was not on the timeline, or the two were out of order. The Timestamp is null only when this event is itself the unplaceable one, so on an event from FinalizeSilencePeriods - which always carries the end time the caller passed - a non-null Timestamp does not imply a non-null Period. The crossing itself still happened.

classes.name: VolumeBlock
classes.summary: Audio volume control block that provides precise control over audio levels and muting. This block allows dynamic adjustment of audio volume using a linear scale where 1.0 represents the original volume level. It supports both volume scaling (0.0 to 10.0 or higher) and instant muting without changing the volume setting. Unlike the AmplifyBlock which focuses on gain with clipping control, the VolumeBlock provides simple, direct volume control suitable for user-facing volume controls and audio mixing scenarios. The block processes audio in real-time with minimal latency and CPU overhead. Implements the MediaBlock. Implements the IMediaBlockInternals. Implements the IDisposable.

classes.name: BridgeAudioSinkBlock
classes.summary: Audio sink block that bridges audio data between different pipelines or applications using a channel-based communication system. This block acts as an endpoint that receives audio data and makes it available to other pipelines or processes through a named channel. It enables inter-pipeline communication for audio streams, allowing complex architectures where audio processing is distributed across multiple pipelines. The bridge uses an efficient in-memory transport mechanism with minimal latency and supports real-time audio streaming. Common use cases include splitting audio processing across multiple pipelines, implementing modular audio processing chains, and creating reusable audio processing components. Pair this sink with a BridgeAudioSourceBlock using the same channel name to establish a complete audio bridge connection. Implements the MediaBlock. Implements the IMediaBlockInternals. Implements the IDisposable.

properties.value: The audio input pad that accepts audio streams to be bridged.

properties.value: An array containing the single audio input pad.

properties.name: Output
properties.summary: Gets the output pad. Bridge sinks do not have outputs as they are terminal blocks.
properties.value: Always returns null as this is a sink block.

properties.name: Outputs
properties.summary: Gets all output pads. Bridge sinks have no outputs as they are terminal blocks.
properties.value: Always returns an empty array as this is a sink block.

classes.name: BridgeBufferSinkBlock
classes.summary: Buffer sink block that bridges raw buffer data between different pipelines using a pair-based communication system. This block acts as an endpoint that receives buffer data and makes it available to a corresponding BridgeBufferSourceBlock through a unique pair identifier. Unlike channel-based bridges, this uses direct buffer passing for lower latency and supports any media type including video, audio, or custom data. The bridge maintains a cache of sink/source pairs for efficient lookup and connection. Common use cases include zero-copy data transfer between pipelines, implementing custom processing chains with raw buffers, and creating high-performance media routing systems. The video information parameter helps optimize buffer handling for video streams but the block can handle any buffer type. Implements the MediaBlock. Implements the IMediaBlockInternals.

classes.name: BridgeSubtitleSinkBlock
classes.summary: Subtitle sink block that bridges subtitle data between different pipelines or applications using a channel-based communication system. This block acts as an endpoint that receives subtitle data (text, SSA/ASS, WebVTT, or other formats) and makes it available to other pipelines or processes through a named channel. It enables inter-pipeline communication for subtitle streams, allowing complex architectures where subtitle processing is distributed across multiple pipelines. The bridge supports various subtitle formats and maintains timing synchronization. Common use cases include subtitle extraction and routing, implementing subtitle processing chains, overlaying subtitles from different sources, and creating subtitle broadcasting systems. Pair this sink with a BridgeSubtitleSourceBlock using the same channel name to establish a complete subtitle bridge. Implements the MediaBlock. Implements the IMediaBlockInternals. classes.name: InterPipeSinkBlock
classes.summary: InterPipe sink block that enables high-performance inter-pipeline communication using the GStreamer interpipe plugin. This block acts as an endpoint that publishes data to a named pipe, making it available to InterPipeSourceBlock instances with the same pipe name. InterPipe provides zero-copy data transfer between pipelines running in the same process, with support for multiple listeners, dynamic connection/disconnection, and automatic format negotiation. The sink maintains compatibility with standard GStreamer elements while providing enhanced performance for local pipeline communication. Common use cases include splitting processing across multiple pipelines for modularity, implementing one-to-many data distribution, creating reusable processing components, and building complex media processing graphs. The video information parameter helps optimize buffer handling for video streams but the block can handle any media type. Implements the MediaBlock. Implements the IMediaBlockInternals.

classes.name: ProxySinkBlock
classes.summary: Proxy sink block that enables direct element-to-element communication within the same pipeline using GStreamer's proxy elements. This block acts as a sink that pairs with a ProxySourceBlock to create an internal bridge within a single pipeline, allowing dynamic pipeline reconfiguration and data routing without traditional pad connections. The proxy mechanism provides a way to decouple pipeline sections, making it easier to implement dynamic pipeline topologies, switchable processing paths, and modular pipeline designs. Unlike InterPipe which works across pipelines, proxy elements work within the same pipeline with minimal overhead.
