classes.name: MediaBlockCatalog
classes.summary: A read-only catalog of every built-in Media Block known to the loaded SDK assemblies. Descriptors are generated once, by reflection: block identity from the Type property override (read from its IL - the getters are constant expressions and blocks are never instantiated for this), category from the diagram categorizer, factories from the settings CreateBlock() convention or a parameterless constructor, availability from the block's static IsAvailable(), and property metadata from the settings CLR type. Custom third-party block assemblies are not supported.

properties.name: All
properties.summary: Gets every registered descriptor, ordered by type name. The scan runs once per process.

methods.name: Get
methods.summary: Gets the descriptor for one block type, or null when no concrete block reports it.

methods.name: ByCategory
methods.summary: Filters descriptors by visual category.

methods.name: Search
methods.summary: Searches descriptors across display name, type name and keywords, case-insensitively.

parameters.name: text
parameters.summary: The search text; null or whitespace returns everything.

methods.name: SerializeSettings
methods.summary: Serializes a settings object of this descriptor's settings type into the JSON shape used in documents.

parameters.name: descriptor
parameters.summary: The descriptor whose settings type is serialized.

methods.returns: A raw JSON element, or null when the block has no settings.

methods.name: DeserializeSettings
methods.summary: Deserializes document JSON back into a settings object of this descriptor's settings type.

parameters.name: descriptor
parameters.summary: The descriptor whose settings type is materialized.

parameters.name: json
parameters.summary: The raw settings JSON stored in a document.

methods.returns: The settings instance, or null when the block has no settings and the payload is empty.

methods.name: IncludedProperties
methods.summary: Every property carrying [JsonInclude]. These are written by Object) against IgnoreReadOnlyProperties, which would otherwise drop them; the ones that are also mandatory constructor arguments are then enforced by JsonElement).

methods.name: ValidateIncludedProperties
methods.summary: Enforces the required-property gate on a settings payload. Internal because VideoMixerSourceJsonConverter deserializes a mixer's nested sources itself and has to apply the same rule - without it a mixer entry omitting a mandatory reference-type argument binds null and fails at pipeline start instead of being reported.

parameters.name: settingsType
parameters.summary: The settings type the payload is for.

methods.name: MandatoryConstructorArguments
methods.summary: The parameter names, without a default, of the constructor System.Text.Json would use for this settings type: the [JsonConstructor] one (which it also honours on a non-public constructor), else the parameterless one (which has none), else the only public one. A type with several candidates and no [JsonConstructor] cannot be deserialized at all, so it has no mandatory arguments to speak of.

methods.name: TryGetProperty
methods.summary: Looks a property up the way the deserializer does - PropertyNameCaseInsensitive is on, and documents are hand-editable, so a payload the deserializer accepts must not fail here.

methods.name: ReadDiscriminator
methods.summary: Reads the constant returned by the block's Type getter straight from its IL, without instantiating the block: the override compiles to ldc.i4.N; ret.

methods.name: FindSettingsType
methods.summary: Resolves the settings CLR type from the block constructors: the first parameter of a concrete type whose name ends with "Settings". Interface-typed parameters are resolved to their uniquely-named default implementation (IFooSettings to FooSettings) when exactly one loaded SDK class implements the interface; otherwise the block gets no settings type and behaves as runtime-configured. Constructors are ordered deterministically (most parameters first), so the result never depends on reflection enumeration order. When no parameter is named that way, the block's own Settings property is asked instead - see Type).

methods.name: FindSettingsPropertyType
methods.summary: Resolves the settings CLR type from the block's own public Settings property, for the block families whose settings class is not named *Settings. The video and audio effects are the large one - VideoBalanceBlock takes a VideoBalanceVideoEffect, VideoResizeBlock a ResizeVideoEffect - and the name convention alone left every one of them without a settings type, so a document naming one failed MBS032. This is the property the live-pipeline snapshot already reads back, so a block the catalog can build from a document is now exactly a block the snapshot can capture into one.
methods.remarks: Only a property a constructor will actually accept qualifies: the settings have to reach the block somehow, and a read-only or unrelated Settings property would produce a descriptor promising a payload nothing consumes. A bare value - an enum, a string, a number - is rejected: it carries no editable property surface and no JSON object, so those blocks get a settings class of their own instead of a scalar masquerading as one. So is a settings class with no public constructor - UniversalSourceSettingsV2 is built by an async factory that probes the media - because naming it here would report a block as constructible that neither the deserializer nor the catalog can ever build, turning a clean MBS032 at validation into an MBS050 halfway through materialization.
methods.returns: The settings CLR type, or null when the block has no such property.

methods.name: TakesSettingsInConstructor
methods.summary: Reports whether the block has a public constructor that takes settingsType and nothing else that is mandatory - the shape both the catalog factory and the materializer need to hand a settings instance to a block.

parameters.name: exact
parameters.summary: true to require the parameter type to be settingsType itself, false to accept a base-typed parameter as well - the two passes the materializer makes, in that order. Ownership of a settings class is decided on the exact match only: a block taking a base type does not lay claim to every subclass of it.

methods.returns: true when such a constructor exists.

methods.name: FindCreateBlockMethod
methods.summary: The settings class's own CreateBlock() factory, or null when it has none. One definition for the catalog factory, the materializer and MediaBlockDescriptor) alike: three copies of the lookup is how the validator came to promise a construction path the materializer did not have.

parameters.name: settingsType
parameters.summary: The settings CLR type, or null.

methods.returns: The CreateBlock() method, or null.

methods.name: SettingsCanBuildTheBlock
methods.summary: Reports whether a settings payload alone can produce this descriptor's block, by the same two routes MediaBlocksPipelineMaterializer.TryCreateWithSettings takes: the settings' own CreateBlock() when it is this block's factory, and otherwise a constructor that takes the settings with every other parameter optional.
methods.returns: true when a settings payload is a construction path.

methods.name: OwnsItsSettingsClass
methods.summary: Reports whether blockType is the only concrete block a settings class can build, which is what makes that class's own CreateBlock() safe to call for this descriptor. Two pairs share one: SRTSourceSettings across SRTSourceBlock and SRTRAWSourceBlock, NDISourceSettings across NDISourceBlock and NDISourceXBlock. CreateBlock() is declared to return MediaBlock, so no return-type check can tell which of a pair it names - and the two differ in their pads, so building the wrong one turns a document's SRT decoding source into a raw one whose connections then fail to resolve. A shared settings class reaches its block through the block's own constructor instead, which cannot pick the sibling.

parameters.name: settingsType
parameters.summary: The settings CLR type, or null.

methods.returns: true when no other concrete block takes the same settings class.

methods.name: ResolveUniqueImplementation
methods.summary: Maps IFooSettings to the single loaded SDK class named FooSettings that implements it. Returns null when there is no such class or more than one - an ambiguous interface has no single default representation to persist. Known limitation: interfaces whose implementations do not follow the name convention (for example IH264EncoderSettings, implemented by many encoder backends under different names) resolve to nothing; those blocks are treated as runtime-configured until materialization learns to pick a backend explicitly.

methods.name: CanCreateDefaultSettings
methods.summary: Reports whether Object@) has a constructor to work with, without building an instance.
methods.returns: true when a default instance can be created.

methods.name: TryCreateDefaultSettings
methods.summary: Creates a settings instance carrying nothing but its own defaults. A parameterless constructor is used when there is one; otherwise a constructor whose parameters are all optional is invoked with every argument omitted - the same allowance the block constructors already get, and the only way settings such as VirtualAudioSourceSettings(wave = Ticks, sampleRate = 48000, ...) can be built by the catalog or restored from a document that carries no payload for them.
methods.remarks: False means "no usable constructor". A constructor that exists and throws is not swallowed: its own exception is rethrown, because a settings type that cannot initialize is a different failure from one that cannot be constructed, and both call sites report it as a diagnostic rather than letting it escape.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The created instance, or null when no usable constructor exists.

methods.returns: true when an instance was created.

methods.name: FindDefaultSettingsConstructor
methods.summary: Picks the constructor Object@) uses: the parameterless one, or the shortest all-optional one. Ties break on the ordinal parameter type names so the choice never depends on reflection enumeration order.
methods.returns: The constructor, or null.

methods.name: InstallSettingsConstructorFactory
methods.summary: Last factory path: build the settings with their own defaults and hand them to the constructor that takes them. It covers every block whose only constructor is Block(FooSettings settings) and whose settings carry no CreateBlock() of their own - the video and audio effects, the overlays, the OpenCV filters and the muxing sinks among them. Without it those descriptors report HasFactory = false and a caller with nothing but a descriptor cannot produce the block at all, though the materializer builds the very same one from a document.

parameters.name: descriptor
parameters.summary: The descriptor whose factory is installed.

classes.name: MediaBlockDescriptor
classes.summary: Describes one built-in block for the catalog: identity, CLR types, display metadata, category, factory, availability probe and settings property metadata. The catalog constructs descriptors from reflection over the SDK assemblies; consumers treat them as read-only.

constructors.name: MediaBlockDescriptor
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MediaBlockDescriptor class. Only descriptors produced by MediaBlockCatalog have working factories and availability probes; hand-built instances are inert shells.

properties.name: Type
properties.summary: Gets the stable MediaBlockType discriminator. This is the value stored in JSON documents.

properties.name: TypeName
properties.summary: Gets the enum member name, kept for readability and diagnostics only.

properties.name: BlockType
properties.summary: Gets the concrete block CLR type.

properties.name: SettingsType
properties.summary: Gets the settings CLR type, or null when the block takes no settings object.

properties.name: SettingsFactoryIsAuthoritative
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether SettingsType.CreateBlock() produces this block rather than a sibling that shares the same settings class. SRTSourceSettings serves both SRTSource and SRTRAWSource and NDISourceSettings both NDISource and NDISourceX, while CreateBlock() names exactly one of each pair - so a shared settings class must reach its block through the block's own constructor instead, or a document naming one source materializes the other.

properties.name: DisplayName
properties.summary: Gets or sets the human-readable display name.

properties.name: Description
properties.summary: Gets or sets the English description of what the block does.

properties.name: Keywords
properties.summary: Gets or sets lowercase search keywords (display name, enum name and extras).

properties.name: Category
properties.summary: Gets or sets the visual category used by editors and diagrams.

properties.name: IsSink
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the block is a sink - the end of a branch, writing somewhere outside the pipeline. Not the same question as Category: the MP4/MKV/WebM output blocks are categorised Output and the GIF encoder as an encoder, and every one of them ends a branch exactly as a sink does. A sink is not necessarily a file: RTMP, SRT, UDP, NDI, WHIP and the platform live sinks are all sinks that write to a network endpoint. A host preparing output directories, or keeping two copies of a block from opening one path, has to ask this and whether the settings name a file - the flag alone would have it creating a folder for an RTMP URL.

properties.name: AcceptsDynamicInputs
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the block creates an input pad on demand - what the muxing sinks do, one pad per stream. An editor drawing such a block has to leave a free indexed pad for the next connection instead of a single fixed one.

properties.name: IsRuntimeConfigured
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the block is configured through factory-built settings (devices, files and models resolved at creation time, async Create methods) rather than an editable POCO. Such settings expose no editable property surface and are represented in JSON documents as resource references instead of payloads.

properties.name: HasFactory
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether a factory delegate is present. The delegate itself is internal to keep third parties from re-binding it; use CreateBlock.

properties.name: CanConstruct
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the block has any document-level construction path: either a default factory exists (HasFactory) or the block takes a settings object that a settings payload in the JSON document can populate. Note that some settings types additionally require a payload to be present - they cannot be default-created.

properties.name: AvailabilityProbe
properties.summary: Gets or sets the availability probe. Never null: blocks without an explicit probe report available.

properties.name: Properties
properties.summary: Gets or sets the per-property settings metadata, ordered by property name.

methods.name: CreateBlock
methods.summary: Creates a new block instance using its default settings path. Throws when the block's settings cannot be default-constructed - create the settings yourself and use the block constructor.
methods.returns: A new block instance.

methods.name: SetFactory
methods.summary: Installs the factory delegate. Internal so the catalog remains the single place that binds factories.

constructors.name: MediaBlockPropertyDescriptor

methods.name: LinkStreamPad
methods.summary: Links a demuxer output pad to the queue prepared for that stream, or parks it on a null sink when there is no free slot left - either because the stream is surplus, or because the caller switched that media type off and no queue was prepared for it at all. A pad left unlinked pushes not-linked back into the demuxer's flow combiner, so it is given a sink of its own.
methods.remarks: The slot is resolved before the link rather than under a lock covering both: tsdemux and qtdemux raise pad-added from one streaming task, so two of these cannot run at once and no second caller can take the slot in between.

methods.name: LinkStreamPad
methods.summary: Links one newly arrived demuxer pad into the element that is next in line for its stream type. The demuxer is free to produce more streams of a type than MediaFileInfo reported — an extra program in an MPEG-TS, a stream parsebin only discovers while running — and those get a null sink created on the spot rather than an index past the end of the list, which used to throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException straight into the GStreamer streaming thread. UniversalAutoDemuxerBlock has always guarded this.

methods.name: CleanUp

methods.remarks: Tear-down order per element is the canonical GStreamer sequence: SetState(NULL) — stop dataflow gracefully so any in-flight push returns and the streaming task exits.pipeline.Remove(element) — detach from the parent bin so the bin no longer holds a ref. Without this, Dispose only drops the managed wrapper while the unmanaged GstElement stays alive (parented by the bin) and shows up as a leak when the pipeline itself is reused or disposed later. Wrapped in try/catch — Remove is a no-op + warning if the element is not actually parented (defensive against partial Build()s).Dispose() — release the managed wrapper and the final unmanaged ref. QueueElement.Dispose handles SetState internally; we only need explicit Remove on the queue's underlying Element before disposing the wrapper.

Settings that are not about the connection are not applied: on the RTSP and RTMP settings that is AudioEnabled, CompatibilityMode, UseGPUDecoder and CustomVideoDecoder, and on RTSP also EnableRAWVideoAudioEvents and ForceCustomKeepAlive. Which outputs exist follows EnableVideo and EnableAudio. The output takes the size and format of whichever source is active, so the caps change on every switch. A consumer that needs fixed caps - an encoder feeding a file - should put a scaler and converter with fixed caps after the block.

methods.name: UseNdiSource
methods.summary: Builds an unparented ndisrc ! ndisrcdemux bin for fallbacksrc's source.
methods.remarks: fallbacksrc wraps a custom source and needs raw streams on pads that exist before it starts: a plain bin has no sometimes-pad template, so the wrapper never listens for a pad added later. Each stream's convert ! tee branch and its ghost pad are therefore built here, and the demuxer's pad is only linked into it. The tee allows not-linked: the wrapper exposes a stream only once fallbacksrc selects it, and ndisrcdemux pushes at once - the not-linked answer would stop ndisrc and make fallbacksrc restart it in a loop (gsttee.c, single-pad push). The audio branch exists whenever audio is enabled: the sender's audio cannot be probed while it is offline. A branch that never carries data leaves only the audio output on silence: ndisrc is live, so fallbacksrc does not hold the video back for it, and it restarts the source only when every output is on its fallback (all_pads_fallback_activated). Set EnableAudio off for a video-only sender.
methods.returns: true on success.

classes.name: NDISourceBlock
classes.summary: NDI (Network Device Interface) source block for professional IP-based video streaming. Provides low-latency, high-quality video and audio streaming over IP networks for broadcast production, live events, and multi-camera setups with automatic source discovery and synchronization capabilities. Implements the SourceMediaBlock. Implements the IMediaBlockInternals. Implements the IDisposable.
classes.remarks: Each stream the sender carries gets an output, and a caller that wants one stream alone simply leaves the other unconnected - hence IParksUnconnectedOutputs. Without it the unused leg pushes into an unlinked queue. The queue's not-linked reaches the demuxer, and when no other pad of the demuxer is linked by then - the connected stream has not started - the pipeline dies with "Internal data stream error ... not-linked" before it reaches PLAYING (issue #3024).

The previous behaviour silently accepted null and allocated VideoOutput, AudioOutput, and the _outputs cache for a block that Build would later refuse to initialise — wasting work and leaving the block in an obviously unusable state with no early failure signal. methods.name: Reconnect
methods.summary: Drops ndisrc to READY, which shuts its NDI receiver down, and brings it back to the pipeline's state with a new one. ndisrcdemux keeps its pads: it removes them only on its own PAUSED to READY.
methods.remarks: All of it under _reconnectLock, so a stop or a cleanup waits for a reconnect in flight and none starts after them. The drop to READY cannot wait on a full queue: the branch queues leak while the start is watched. A refused reconnect - stopped, an older run, or the source gone - leaves the watch waiting for ConnectionOpened, so it decides nothing more; every stop tears the block down and the next start builds a new watch. A connection that goes silent brings no buffer to decide on, so a poller asks until the next reconnect.

classes.name: NDISourceXBlock
classes.summary: NDI (Network Device Interface) source block that receives through the NDI SDK directly.
classes.remarks: Windows only. drives the GStreamer ndisrc element and is the cross-platform path; this block runs the NDI SDK receiver itself and feeds the frames into an internal live . Teardown contract. Pushes are gated by a flag that and clear, followed by a handshake on the push barrier - after that handshake no push can be in flight, so the mixer is safe to dispose even if the NDI capture thread refuses to exit. The receiver is disconnected before the mixer goes away. A live NDI capture thread at process exit is what left the host alive after Stop-Process -Force, wedged in libndi's DllMain(DLL_PROCESS_DETACH) under the loader lock (issue #1490), so nothing here may return while that thread is still running by choice. BlockOnPush stays false on the mixer. Flipping it to true would let a push block on downstream while holding the push barrier, and the disconnect below would then wait on a thread that is waiting on us. The audio output exists only when the sender has audio, and a caller that wants video alone simply leaves it unconnected - hence IParksUnconnectedOutputs. Without it the audio appsrc pushes into an unlinked queue and the pipeline dies with "Internal data stream error" before it reaches PLAYING.

classes.name: SourceMediaBlock
classes.summary: Abstract base class for all media source blocks in the MediaBlocks pipeline framework. This foundational class provides the essential infrastructure for blocks that originate media data from various sources including file systems, capture devices, network streams, and synthetic generators. Source blocks represent the entry points of media processing pipelines, responsible for acquiring raw or encoded media data and making it available to downstream processing blocks. Key responsibilities: - Defining the common interface for all media source implementations - Providing base functionality for source lifecycle management - Establishing contracts for subtitle availability and source control - Serving as the starting point for media processing chains Common derived implementations: - File sources (MP4, AVI, MKV, WebM, etc.) - Device sources (cameras, microphones, capture cards) - Network sources (RTSP, RTMP, HTTP streams) - Synthetic sources (test patterns, tone generators) - Screen capture sources (desktop, window, region) - Industrial camera sources (GenICam, machine vision) Source blocks typically have no input pads and one or more output pads depending on the media streams they provide (video, audio, subtitles). They are responsible for format detection, stream initialization, and maintaining synchronization between multiple output streams. Implements the MediaBlock.

methods.name: IsSubtitlesAvailable
methods.summary: Determines whether subtitle streams are available from this media source. This method allows downstream blocks to query the availability of text-based subtitle tracks that may be embedded in media files or provided as separate streams. Subtitle support includes various formats such as SRT, SSA/ASS, WebVTT, TTML, and embedded formats like DVD/Blu-ray subtitles.
methods.remarks: Override this method in derived classes that implement subtitle extraction capabilities. The base implementation returns false, indicating no subtitle support by default. Sources that support subtitles should also implement the corresponding subtitle output pad.
methods.returns: true if one or more subtitle streams are available and can be extracted; false if no subtitles are present or the source doesn't support subtitle extraction.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops the media source from generating or reading data and releases associated resources. This method provides a controlled shutdown mechanism for source blocks, ensuring proper cleanup of system resources, device handles, network connections, and file descriptors.
methods.remarks: Override this method in derived classes to implement source-specific stopping logic: - File sources: Close file handles and release memory buffers - Device sources: Stop hardware devices and release exclusive access - Network sources: Close connections and cleanup network resources - Thread sources: Signal and wait for worker threads to terminate The base implementation returns true, allowing simple sources to use default behavior. Complex sources should ensure all resources are properly released to prevent leaks. This method may be called multiple times and should be idempotent.
methods.returns: true if the source was successfully stopped and all resources were released; false if an error occurred during shutdown.

classes.name: StreamSourceBlockWithDecoder
classes.summary: Composite media source block that combines stream reading with automatic decoding for complete media playback. This high-level block encapsulates the complexity of reading from .NET Stream objects, automatically detecting media formats, demuxing container formats, and decoding compressed streams into raw video and audio data. Provides a simplified API for applications that need to play media from memory without manual pipeline construction. Key features: - Automatic format detection for all supported container formats - Integrated demuxing of multi-stream containers (MP4, MKV, AVI, etc.) - Hardware-accelerated decoding when available - Support for any .NET Stream implementation (MemoryStream, FileStream, NetworkStream) - Seamless handling of variable bitrate and adaptive streams - Automatic audio/video synchronization - Zero-copy streaming from memory buffers when possible Common use cases: - Playing media from memory buffers or byte arrays - Streaming from encrypted or compressed archives - Processing media from network streams without temporary files - Embedding media playback in memory-constrained environments - Custom stream implementations for DRM or proprietary formats The block internally manages a StreamSourceBlock for reading and a DecodeBinBlock for automatic format detection and decoding, presenting a simple interface with separate video and audio outputs ready for rendering or further processing. Implements the SuperMediaBlock

classes.name: UDPRAWSourceBlock
classes.summary: UDP RAW source block. Receives a live UDP stream (MPEG-TS, RTP, or raw elementary) and exposes parsed but still-encoded video (and optional audio) without decoding. Intended for passthrough recording or remuxing — for example, splitting a UDP feed into MP4/MKV files without re-encoding.
classes.remarks: Pipeline construction by :Auto / MPEGTS: udpsrc → parsebin. parsebin auto-detects the container (MPEG-TS is the common "UDP video" case), demuxes and parses every stream, and exposes them still encoded via dynamic pads.RTP: udpsrc(caps=application/x-rtp …) → rtpXdepay → parser. The video codec is taken from (a bare UDP socket carries no SDP); optional RTP audio () arrives on a separate port ().Raw: udpsrc(caps=video/… ) → parser for a single elementary video stream selected by .The exposed video/audio output pads carry encoded data, so connecting them to a muxer sink (such as MP4SinkBlock / MKVSinkBlock) records without re-encoding.In Auto/MPEGTS mode every common codec is exposed. When a codec maps to a timestamp-inferring GstBaseParse parser (video: h264parse/h265parse/vp9parse/av1parse/mpegvideoparse/mpeg4videoparse/jpegparse; audio: aacparse/mpegaudioparse/ac3parse/opusparse/flacparse) the parser is inserted so every passthrough buffer carries a PTS — a strict muxer such as mp4mux/qtmux otherwise aborts with "Buffer has no PTS". Any codec without a matching parser (for example VP8, raw PCM) is linked through unparsed as a passthrough rather than dropped, since dropping a connected pad would starve a downstream muxer.

methods.name: HandleParsebinPad
methods.summary: Routes a newly added parsebin pad to the matching parser/queue. Always called under _padLock with _tornDown already checked. Every failure branch routes the incoming pad to a fakesink so the demuxer streaming thread can never block on an unconsumed src pad (which would stall the whole pipeline), and any half-added parser is removed so a later pad does not create a second orphaned parser.

methods.name: SelectAudioParser
methods.summary: Maps an audio caps structure to the matching timestamp-inferring GstBaseParse parser. aacparse and mpegaudioparse both accept audio/mpeg, so they are distinguished by mpegversion (1 = MP1/MP2/MP3 → mpegaudioparse; 2/4 = AAC → aacparse). AC-3 maps to ac3parse, Opus to opusparse, FLAC to flacparse. Returns null for any codec this block cannot timestamp through a parser (it is then linked through unparsed as passthrough).

methods.name: SelectVideoParser
methods.summary: Maps a video caps structure to the matching timestamp-inferring GstBaseParse parser, and reports whether that parser exposes the config-interval property (only h264parse, h265parse and mpeg4videoparse do — setting it on the others throws). Returns null for any codec without a dedicated parser (for example VP8, which has no vp8parse), in which case the caller links the already-framed parsebin pad through unparsed as passthrough.

methods.name: RemoveOrphanedVideoParse
methods.summary: Removes and disposes a half-added _videoParse after a failed link so a later video pad does not allocate a second parser and orphan this one. Called under _padLock.

methods.name: RemoveOrphanedAudioParse

classes.name: UniversalSourceBlockMini
classes.summary: Lightweight universal media source block with integrated format detection and decoding capabilities. This mini version of UniversalSourceBlock provides a streamlined implementation optimized for common media playback scenarios, offering automatic format detection, demuxing, and decoding in a single block. Designed for applications requiring simple media playback without the complexity of manual pipeline construction. Key features: - Automatic format detection for 100+ container and codec combinations - Integrated demuxing and decoding with hardware acceleration support - Dynamic pad creation based on available streams (video/audio/subtitle) - Support for local files, HTTP/HTTPS URLs, and custom URI schemes - Optimized memory usage for embedded and mobile applications - Selective stream rendering (video-only, audio-only, or both) - Built-in buffering and synchronization management Supported sources: - Local files: All major formats (MP4, AVI, MKV, MOV, WebM, etc.) - Network streams: HTTP, HTTPS, RTSP, RTMP, HLS, DASH - Device URIs: Custom schemes for platform-specific sources - Memory streams: Via custom URI protocols Common use cases: - Media player applications with basic playback needs - Video preview and thumbnail generation - Audio-only playback for music applications - Embedded systems with limited resources - Quick media format validation and analysis The "Mini" designation indicates this block uses simplified internal processing compared to the full UniversalSourceBlock, trading some advanced features for reduced complexity and resource usage while maintaining compatibility with most common media formats and use cases. Implements the SourceMediaBlock. Implements the IMediaBlockInternals. Implements the IDisposable.

classes.remarks: Pipeline construction algorithm (Build):Create a GStreamer source element based on URI scheme (filesrc, souphttpsrc, rtspsrc, etc.).For RTSP sources: connect through parsebin which auto-discovers and decodes streams via dynamic pads (, ).For file/HTTP sources: use typefind to detect container format, then select an explicit demuxer () and parsers ().If the demuxer has static pads, link them immediately via ; otherwise, wait for dynamic pad-added signals ().For each media stream, create an output chain: queue → optional parser → decoder → converter → output pad (, , ).Decoder selection () considers hardware acceleration availability and falls back to software decoding when hardware is unavailable.Key responsibilities: source element creation, format detection, demuxer/parser/decoder selection, output chain assembly, dynamic pad negotiation, hardware decoder fallback, and multi-stream output management.This class delegates to GStreamer elements for the actual media processing. methods.summary: Links an announced RTSP pad to the parsebin of its stream. rtspsrc raises pad-added once per stream from its own streaming threads, and again whenever a stream gets a new SSRC - a camera restarting its encoder - or payload type - comfort noise, DTMF, a codec switch. It keeps the older pads, but from then on pushes all of that stream's data out of the newest one (gstrtspsrc.c: new_manager_pad replaces stream->srcpad, and gst_rtspsrc_handle_src_sink_chain pushes every pad's buffers there). So a new pad takes the older one's place at the stream's parsebin, whose chain holds the output, behind a filter that passes only the stream's main payload type (issue #2158). An already linked pad is ignored.

classes.summary: Video mixer source block for combining multiple video sources into a single composite output. Provides real-time video mixing with positioning, scaling, alpha blending, and chroma key support for creating picture-in-picture effects, video walls, live production, and multi-stream compositing using CPU, OpenGL, or D3D11 acceleration. Implements the SuperMediaBlock. Implements the IMediaBlockInternals. Implements the IDisposable.
classes.remarks: Mixing algorithm:Constructor: Select mixer backend based on VideoMixerType (CPU via , OpenGL via GLVideoMixerBlock, or D3D11 via D3D11VideoCompositorBlock on Windows).For each input in , create a child source block (e.g. VirtualVideoSourceBlock) and a corresponding mixer stream with rectangle and z-order.Connect each child source output to the corresponding mixer input pad via the pipeline.Build: Build the mixer first (creates the GStreamer compositor element), then build each child source block so data flows into the mixer.Runtime operations: Input streams can be repositioned (), faded in/out (/), reordered (), and have chroma key toggled () while the pipeline is running.

constructors.remarks: This is the constructor a settings payload reaches the block through: it is what VideoMixerSourceSettings.CreateBlock() calls, and the pipeline-document materializer puts the result into the pipeline with an explicit AddBlock, so the block is present in the build loop and its runs.Internal on purpose, though no longer for safety: names this block as the owner of the mixer and of every child, and AddBlockIfRequired walks that link, so connecting the composed output alone does register this block and its does run. It stays internal because the public way to build a mixer source from settings is VideoMixerSourceSettings.CreateBlock(), and the public way to build one against a known pipeline is the overload above, which links immediately.

methods.summary: Creates the mixer backend, one child source block per configured input, and the matching mixer stream layout.

methods.name: AttachSources
methods.summary: Links every child source output to its mixer input pad. Idempotent - the second call is a no-op, so the pipeline-taking constructor and Build cannot link twice.

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.summary: The pipeline the links are made in.

methods.name: Register
methods.summary: Puts a child into this block's Blocks collection and names this block as its owner.
methods.remarks: The ownership is what makes the block reachable. Its Output pad belongs to the inner mixer, so pipeline.Connect(mixerSource.Output, sink.Input) hands AddBlockIfRequired the mixer, not this block - and without the owner link the pipeline would never hold this block, never call its Build, and never link the child sources. AddBlockIfRequired walks Owner and then registers every entry of the owner's Blocks, so one connection to the composed output brings the whole composition in.

methods.name: DisposePartiallyBuilt
methods.summary: Releases the mixer and every child source after a failed construction or link pass. On such a failure the caller never sees this, so nothing else will ever dispose them and every created block would leak its native GStreamer element. Each inner Dispose is guarded so a secondary failure never masks the original exception the caller should see.

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.summary: The pipeline the failed pass ran in, or null when there was none. A piece the pipeline has already taken is left to it: the pipeline's own teardown releases it, and disposing it here would hand the next start a dead block. The collections are emptied either way - this instance is being abandoned, and a piece the pipeline holds is in its block list, where teardown reaches it without this one.

classes.name: D3D11H264DecoderBlock
classes.summary: Direct3D 11/DXVA H.264/AVC hardware-accelerated video decoder block.
classes.remarks: This decoder block provides hardware-accelerated H.264/AVC video decoding using Direct3D 11 and DirectX Video Acceleration (DXVA) 2.0 on Windows platforms. It leverages the GPU for efficient decoding of H.264 video streams, significantly reducing CPU usage compared to software decoders. Key Features:Hardware-accelerated H.264/AVC decoding (Baseline, Main, High profiles)Support for resolutions up to 4K and beyond (hardware dependent)Low CPU usage through GPU offloadingDirect3D 11 surface output for efficient renderingZero-copy decoding pipeline when used with D3D11 renderersUse Cases:High-performance video playback applicationsMulti-stream video surveillance systemsReal-time video processing pipelinesLow-latency streaming applicationsVR/AR video applications requiring minimal CPU overheadRequirements:Windows 7 or later with Direct3D 11 supportGPU with H.264 DXVA2 decoding capabilitiesCompatible graphics drivers with DXVA supportPerformance Considerations: The decoder automatically utilizes the GPU for decoding operations. For optimal performance, ensure your graphics drivers are up to date and the GPU supports the H.264 profile and level of your input video. The decoder outputs D3D11 surfaces which can be directly rendered without additional memory copies when used with D3D11-based video renderers.

classes.name: D3D11H265DecoderBlock
classes.summary: Direct3D 11/DXVA H.265/HEVC hardware-accelerated video decoder block.
classes.remarks: This decoder block provides hardware-accelerated H.265/HEVC video decoding using Direct3D 11 and DirectX Video Acceleration (DXVA) 2.0 on Windows platforms. It leverages the GPU for efficient decoding of H.265/HEVC video streams, offering superior compression efficiency compared to H.264 while maintaining low CPU usage. Key Features:Hardware-accelerated H.265/HEVC Main and Main 10 profile decodingSupport for 8-bit and 10-bit color depthsUltra HD 4K, 8K resolution support (hardware dependent)HDR video support with Main 10 profileExtremely low CPU usage through GPU offloadingDirect3D 11 surface output for zero-copy renderingUse Cases:4K/8K video playback applicationsHDR video streaming and playbackProfessional video editing with HEVC footageDigital signage and video wall applicationsNext-generation video surveillance systemsVR/AR applications with high-resolution videoRequirements:Windows 10 or later (recommended for full HEVC support)GPU with H.265/HEVC DXVA2 decoding capabilities (Intel 6th gen+, NVIDIA GTX 960+, AMD RX 400+)HEVC Video Extensions from Microsoft Store (for some Windows versions)Latest graphics drivers with HEVC decode supportPerformance Considerations: HEVC decoding is more computationally intensive than H.264, requiring newer GPU hardware for smooth playback. The decoder automatically utilizes GPU resources and outputs D3D11 surfaces for efficient rendering. For 4K/8K content, ensure your GPU has sufficient video memory and decode capabilities.

classes.name: D3D11MPEG2DecoderBlock
classes.summary: Direct3D 11/DXVA MPEG-2 hardware-accelerated video decoder block.
classes.remarks: This decoder block provides hardware-accelerated MPEG-2 video decoding using Direct3D 11 and DirectX Video Acceleration (DXVA) 2.0 on Windows platforms. It leverages the GPU for efficient decoding of MPEG-2 video streams commonly found in DVD, broadcast television, and legacy video content. Key Features:Hardware-accelerated MPEG-2 Main Profile decodingSupport for standard definition (SD) and high definition (HD) resolutionsInterlaced and progressive video supportLow CPU usage through GPU offloadingDirect3D 11 surface output for efficient renderingDVD-Video and ATSC/DVB broadcast compatibilityUse Cases:DVD playback applicationsDigital TV and broadcast video decodingLegacy video archive systemsVideo surveillance systems using MPEG-2 encodingProfessional video editing with MPEG-2 footageSet-top box and media center applicationsRequirements:Windows 7 or later with Direct3D 11 supportGPU with MPEG-2 DXVA2 decoding capabilitiesCompatible graphics drivers with DXVA supportMPEG-2 Video Decoder may require separate licensing on some Windows versionsPerformance Considerations: MPEG-2 is a mature codec with excellent hardware support across all modern GPUs. The decoder handles both interlaced and progressive content, automatically deinterlacing when necessary. For optimal performance with interlaced content, ensure your rendering pipeline supports proper field handling.

classes.name: D3D11VP8DecoderBlock
classes.summary: Direct3D 11/DXVA VP8 hardware-accelerated video decoder block.
classes.remarks: This decoder block provides hardware-accelerated VP8 video decoding using Direct3D 11 and DirectX Video Acceleration (DXVA) 2.0 on Windows platforms. VP8 is an open-source video codec developed by Google, primarily used in WebM containers and WebRTC video communications. Key Features:Hardware-accelerated VP8 decoding for WebM and WebRTC contentSupport for resolutions up to Full HD (1920x1080) and beyondLow CPU usage through GPU offloadingDirect3D 11 surface output for efficient renderingReal-time decoding capabilities for video conferencingRoyalty-free codec implementationUse Cases:WebRTC video conferencing applicationsWebM video playback in browsers and media playersYouTube and streaming platform video playbackVideo chat and collaboration toolsOpen-source video streaming solutionsCross-platform video applicationsRequirements:Windows 10 or later (VP8 hardware support is limited on older versions)GPU with VP8 DXVA2 decoding capabilities (Intel HD Graphics 4000+, NVIDIA GTX 600+, AMD GCN+)Compatible graphics drivers with VP8 decode supportGStreamer VP8 plugins properly installedPerformance Considerations: VP8 hardware acceleration support varies significantly across GPU vendors and models. Intel GPUs generally provide the best VP8 hardware support due to WebRTC requirements. The decoder automatically falls back to software decoding if hardware support is unavailable. For WebRTC applications, this decoder provides low-latency decoding suitable for real-time communication.

classes.name: D3D11VP9DecoderBlock
classes.summary: Direct3D 11/DXVA VP9 hardware-accelerated video decoder block.
classes.remarks: This decoder block provides hardware-accelerated VP9 video decoding using Direct3D 11 and DirectX Video Acceleration (DXVA) 2.0 on Windows platforms. VP9 is Google's successor to VP8, offering better compression efficiency than H.264 while competing with H.265/HEVC. It's widely used in YouTube, WebM containers, and is a mandatory codec for WebRTC. Key Features:Hardware-accelerated VP9 Profile 0 and Profile 2 decodingSupport for 8-bit and 10-bit color depths (HDR support with Profile 2)4K, 8K, and beyond resolution support (hardware dependent)YouTube HDR and 4K/8K video playbackExtremely efficient compression with low CPU usageDirect3D 11 surface output for zero-copy renderingRoyalty-free alternative to HEVCUse Cases:YouTube and streaming platform video playback (4K/8K/HDR)WebRTC video conferencing with high qualityWebM video playback and editingNext-generation video streaming applicationsHDR video playback systemsOpen-source video platformsRequirements:Windows 10 version 1709 or later (for full VP9 support)GPU with VP9 DXVA2 decoding capabilities (Intel Kaby Lake+, NVIDIA GTX 1050+, AMD RX 400+)Compatible graphics drivers with VP9 decode supportGStreamer VP9 plugins properly installedPerformance Considerations: VP9 provides excellent compression efficiency but requires modern GPU hardware for acceleration. Intel 7th gen and newer CPUs provide excellent VP9 support. NVIDIA and AMD GPUs from 2016 onwards typically include VP9 hardware decoding. The decoder supports both SDR and HDR content, automatically handling 10-bit decoding when Profile 2 content is detected. For optimal YouTube playback performance, ensure your GPU drivers are up to date.

classes.name: UniversalAutoDemuxerBlock
classes.summary: Represents a universal automatic demuxer block that dynamically selects the appropriate demuxer based on the input stream format detected by typefind element.
classes.remarks: The UniversalAutoDemuxerBlock is a MediaBlocks component that automatically detects the format of an incoming stream and creates the appropriate demuxer dynamically. It uses GStreamer's typefind element to identify the media format and then instantiates the correct demuxer element on the fly. Key features: - Automatic format detection using typefind - Dynamic demuxer creation based on detected format - Support for all common container formats (MP4, MKV, AVI, WebM, etc.) - Pre-created output pads based on constructor parameters - Configurable output stream selection (video, audio, subtitle, metadata) Output pads are pre-created based on constructor parameters: - If renderVideo is true, creates 1 video output pad - If renderAudio is true, creates 1 audio output pad - If renderSubtitle is true, creates 1 subtitle output pad - If renderMetadata is true, creates 1 metadata output pad

classes.name: PadConnector
classes.summary: PadConnector helper class for establishing connections between MediaBlock pads. This static helper provides functionality to connect GStreamer pads between different media blocks in a pipeline. It handles the low-level pad linking operations, validates pad compatibility, manages on-demand connections, and provides comprehensive error reporting. Essential for the MediaBlocks framework's automatic pipeline construction capabilities.

methods.returns: The hint, or an empty string when neither block is a GL-memory peer.

methods.name: ConnectPads
methods.summary: Connects all specified media block pads to their configured destinations. This method iterates through the provided pads, validates their connections, retrieves the internal GStreamer pads, and establishes the links. Handles on-demand connections by skipping them for later dynamic linking.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: The pipeline context for error reporting and logging.

parameters.name: pads
parameters.summary: Array of MediaBlockPad instances to be connected.

parameters.name: refused
parameters.summary: Receives each link GStreamer refused as src -> sink (reason), keyed by the source pad's handle, so a pair tried from both of its ends is recorded once.

classes.name: IAudioProcessingBlock
classes.summary: Marks a media block as an in-graph audio processing block: a single audio input pad and a single audio output pad that passes audio through unchanged (while tapping it for analysis).
classes.remarks: This is the contract the X engines (VideoCaptureCoreX, MediaPlayerCoreX, VideoEditCoreX) accept when inserting a user-supplied processing block into their audio chain. The Whisper speech-to-text block implements this interface so it can be plugged into the engine pipeline without the engine (in VisioForge.Core) referencing the AI assemblies. A block exposes its connection pads through Input and Output.

classes.name: IMediaBlock
classes.summary: Main Media Block interface that defines the contract for all media processing blocks in the pipeline system. Media blocks are the fundamental building blocks of media processing pipelines, representing individual processing units such as sources, filters, encoders, decoders, and sinks. Each block can have input and output pads for connecting to other blocks, forming a directed graph of media processing operations.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets or sets the unique name identifier for this media block within the pipeline. The name is used for debugging, logging, and referencing the block in pipeline operations. Names should be descriptive and unique within a pipeline to avoid confusion.
properties.value: A string representing the unique name of this media block.

properties.name: Type
properties.summary: Gets or sets the type of media block, indicating its primary function in the pipeline. The type determines the block's role (source, filter, encoder, decoder, sink, etc.) and helps in categorizing blocks for pipeline validation and optimization.
properties.value: The MediaBlockType enumeration value representing this block's functional category.

properties.name: Input
properties.summary: Gets the primary input pad for this media block, if it has a single input. For blocks with multiple inputs, this returns the default or primary input pad. Returns null for source blocks that have no inputs.
properties.value: The primary MediaBlockPad for input connections, or null if no inputs exist.

properties.name: Inputs
properties.summary: Gets an array of all input pads available on this media block. Input pads are connection points where this block can receive media data from other blocks. Source blocks typically return an empty array as they generate data rather than receive it.
properties.value: An array of MediaBlockPad objects representing all available input connection points.

properties.name: Output
properties.summary: Gets the primary output pad for this media block, if it has a single output. For blocks with multiple outputs, this returns the default or primary output pad. Returns null for sink blocks that have no outputs.
properties.value: The primary MediaBlockPad for output connections, or null if no outputs exist.

properties.name: Outputs
properties.summary: Gets an array of all output pads available on this media block. Output pads are connection points where this block can send media data to other blocks. Sink blocks typically return an empty array as they consume data rather than produce it.
properties.value: An array of MediaBlockPad objects representing all available output connection points.

methods.name: GetPipelineContext
methods.summary: Gets the pipeline context associated with this media block. The pipeline context provides access to shared resources, pipeline state, and coordination mechanisms used by all blocks within the same pipeline instance.
methods.returns: The BlockPipelineContext object containing pipeline-wide state and resources.

classes.name: IMediaBlockAsyncPrepare
classes.summary: Optional interface for blocks whose synchronous Build() needs data that only an asynchronous probe of a live source can supply - the RTSP RAW and NDI sources pick their GStreamer elements from the probed stream layout, so they cannot be built blind the way RTSPSourceBlock can with its compatibility mode. Boolean) probes for this interface with as and awaits CancellationToken) on every block that implements it, once, before the pipeline is built. A settings object that was configured by hand or restored from a pipeline document therefore gets its media information without any blocking call on the build path.
classes.remarks: Implementations MUST be idempotent (a second call with the information already cached is a no-op), MUST NOT throw - a cancelled probe returns false rather than raising - and MUST tolerate a context. The synchronous Boolean) and AddBlockLive paths have no place to await and do not call this - the block's own Build() guard still reports the missing information there.

methods.name: PrepareAsync
methods.summary: Probes whatever the block needs before Build() can run.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: The pipeline context used for logging. May be .

parameters.name: cancellationToken
parameters.summary: Cancelled when a stop or a dispose arrives while the pass is running. Honour it where the underlying probe accepts one; where it does not, the probe's own timeout is the ceiling and the pipeline still abandons the start at the next block.

methods.returns: true when the block is ready to be built; false when the source could not be probed and starting the pipeline should be abandoned.

classes.name: IMediaBlockDynamicInputs
classes.summary: Interface for MediaBlocks that support dynamic creation of input pads at runtime. This interface enables blocks like mixers and multiplexers to create new input connections on demand, allowing for flexible pipeline topologies that can change during execution.

methods.name: CreateNewInput
methods.summary: Creates a new input pad of the specified media type on this block. This allows for runtime expansion of the block's input capabilities, useful for scenarios like adding new video streams to a mixer or new audio tracks to a multiplexer.

parameters.name: mediaType
parameters.summary: The type of media content the new input pad will accept (video, audio, subtitle, or data).

methods.returns: A new MediaBlockPad configured as an input with the specified media type, or null if creation fails.

methods.name: GetInput
methods.summary: Retrieves an existing input pad that handles the specified media type. This method searches for an already created input pad matching the requested media type, useful for reusing existing connections rather than creating new ones.

parameters.name: mediaType
parameters.summary: The type of media content to search for among existing input pads.

methods.returns: An existing MediaBlockPad that accepts the specified media type, or null if no matching pad is found.

classes.name: IMediaBlockInternals
classes.summary: Internal interface providing low-level access to MediaBlock implementation details. This interface exposes the underlying GStreamer elements and pipeline management methods that are used internally by the MediaBlocks framework for pipeline construction and lifecycle management. Not intended for direct use in application code.

methods.name: SetContext
methods.summary: Associates this MediaBlock with a pipeline and initializes its internal context. This method is called automatically when the block is added to a pipeline, providing access to shared resources and pipeline-wide configuration.

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.summary: The MediaBlocksPipeline instance that will manage this block.

methods.name: Build
methods.summary: Constructs and initializes the underlying GStreamer elements for this MediaBlock. This method creates the necessary GStreamer components, configures their properties, and prepares the block for integration into the pipeline. Must be called before the block can process media.
methods.returns: True if the block was successfully built and all required elements were created; false if construction failed.

methods.name: CleanUp
methods.summary: Releases the GStreamer elements this MediaBlock created in Build and returns the block to a re-buildable state. Called automatically during pipeline teardown.
methods.remarks: A stopped pipeline can be started again on the same instance, in which case Build runs a second time on this very block. So the contract is: clear the build latch, so does not short-circuit;release everything created, since will create it again;do NOT release anything cannot recreate - state built in the constructor, user configuration, and event subscriptions belong to Dispose(bool). Releasing constructor-owned state here makes the second run silently produce no data: the null-conditional code in Build succeeds while owning nothing.

methods.name: GetElement
methods.summary: Retrieves the primary GStreamer element that represents this MediaBlock in the pipeline. This element is the main component that performs the actual media processing and is connected to other elements in the GStreamer pipeline.
methods.returns: The GStreamer Element instance, or null if the block hasn't been built yet.

methods.name: GetCore
methods.summary: Retrieves the core BaseElement wrapper that provides additional functionality around the GStreamer element. This wrapper adds VisioForge-specific features and simplifies common operations on the underlying GStreamer element.
methods.returns: The BaseElement wrapper instance that encapsulates the GStreamer element.

classes.name: IParksUnconnectedOutputs
classes.summary: Implemented by a block that publishes one output pad per stream, where a pad the caller leaves unconnected would otherwise push into nothing: gst_queue_loop answers not-linked by pausing its task, the queue fills, and a full queue blocks the block's shared streaming thread - starving the streams the caller did connect (issue #1415). The pipeline parks such a pad on a discard-mode null sink when the graph is built.
classes.remarks: Opt-in on purpose: a tee's spare outputs are handed out later by TeeBlock.GetFreeOutputPad and connected live, and parking one would make that connection fail. To connect a covered block's output after the build, set OnDemandConnect on the pad before building - the parking skips it.

classes.name: IMediaBlockInternals2
classes.summary: Extended internal interface for MediaBlocks that require post-connection initialization. This interface provides additional lifecycle hooks for blocks that need to perform configuration or setup after their pads have been connected in the pipeline.

methods.name: PostConnect
methods.summary: Called after all pad connections have been established for this block. This method allows blocks to perform initialization that depends on knowing the connected blocks or negotiated media formats. Common uses include configuring filters based on input format or setting up dynamic processing chains.
methods.returns: True if post-connection initialization was successful; false if an error occurred.

classes.name: IMediaBlockRenderer
classes.summary: Interface for MediaBlocks that perform rendering operations (audio playback, video display, etc.). This interface provides control over synchronization behavior for blocks that present media to users, ensuring proper timing and smooth playback of multimedia content.

properties.name: IsSync
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to synchronize media streams for real-time playback. When enabled, the renderer will maintain proper timing relationships between audio and video, ensuring lip-sync and smooth playback. Should typically be true for playback and live capture scenarios, but false for transcoding or processing operations where speed is more important than timing.
properties.value: True if synchronization is enabled for real-time playback; false for maximum processing speed.

classes.name: IMediaBlockSettings
classes.summary: Interface for configuration objects that can create and configure MediaBlock instances. This interface enables a factory pattern where settings objects encapsulate all necessary configuration parameters and can instantiate properly configured MediaBlocks on demand.

methods.name: CreateBlock
methods.summary: Creates a new MediaBlock instance configured with the settings contained in this object. This factory method allows for separation of configuration from instantiation, making it easier to serialize settings or create multiple blocks with the same configuration.
methods.returns: A new MediaBlock instance configured according to this settings object.

classes.name: IMediaBlockSink
classes.summary: Interface for media blocks that serve as data sinks (outputs) in the MediaBlocks pipeline. Sink blocks consume media data and output it to destinations such as files, streams, or hardware devices. Examples include file writers, streaming encoders, and display renderers.

methods.name: GetFilenameOrURL
methods.summary: Gets the output destination filename or URL where the media data will be written. This could be a local file path, network URL, or device identifier depending on the sink type.
methods.returns: The filename, URL, or destination identifier as a string.

methods.name: SetFilenameOrURL
methods.summary: Sets the output destination filename or URL where the media data should be written. This configures where the sink block will send its processed media data.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: The filename, URL, or destination identifier to set.

classes.name: IMediaBlockSinkAllInOne
classes.summary: Interface for comprehensive media sink blocks that can handle multiple media types (audio, video, subtitles) in a single output destination. These are typically container-format sinks like MP4, MKV, or AVI that can multiplex different media streams into one output file or stream. Extends the IMediaBlockSink interface.

classes.name: IMediaBlockSource
classes.summary: Common shape for blocks the player treats as "the source". Implemented by both the classic SourceMediaBlock hierarchy and composite wrappers like StreamSourceBlockWithDecoder (a SuperMediaBlock) so that MediaPlayerContext.Source consumers can dispatch through a single interface instead of pattern-matching every concrete shape. Internal because both the consumer (MediaPlayerCoreX) and the implementers ship in this assembly.

methods.name: IsSubtitlesAvailable
methods.summary: Indicates whether this source exposes a subtitle stream.
methods.returns: true when subtitles are available; otherwise false.

classes.name: IMediaBlocksPipeline
classes.summary: Defines the core interface for the modern MediaBlocks pipeline system, enabling flexible, cross-platform media processing workflows. This interface provides the foundation for building modular media processing applications by composing reusable media blocks (sources, effects, encoders, sinks) into complete processing pipelines. Built on GStreamer, it delivers high-performance media handling across Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android platforms with a unified API.
classes.remarks: The MediaBlocks pipeline architecture allows developers to: - Build custom media workflows from pre-built blocks (camera capture, file playback, video encoding, streaming, etc.) - Connect blocks dynamically to create processing chains - Control pipeline lifecycle (build, start, pause, resume, stop) - Handle errors and monitor pipeline state - Process multiple media streams simultaneously This is the most flexible and powerful approach in the VisioForge Media Framework ecosystem.

properties.name: State
properties.summary: Gets the current playback state of the pipeline (stopped, playing, paused, etc.).
properties.value: The current PlaybackState indicating the pipeline's operational status.

methods.name: AddBlock
methods.summary: Adds a media block to the pipeline for processing. The block will be automatically integrated into the pipeline's lifecycle management and can be connected to other blocks.

parameters.name: block
parameters.summary: The media block to add to the pipeline (source, effect, encoder, sink, etc.).

methods.returns: true if the block was successfully added, false otherwise.

methods.name: GetBlock
methods.summary: Retrieves a media block from the pipeline by its unique name identifier.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name of the block to retrieve.

methods.returns: The media block with the specified name, or null if not found.

methods.name: GetBlock
methods.summary: Retrieves the first media block of the specified type from the pipeline. Useful for finding blocks by their functional category (source, sink, effect, etc.).

parameters.name: type_
parameters.summary: The type of media block to search for.

methods.returns: The first media block of the specified type, or null if not found.

methods.name: Build
methods.summary: Builds the complete pipeline by creating and configuring all underlying GStreamer elements and establishing the connections between media blocks. This must be called before starting playback.
methods.returns: true if the pipeline was successfully built, false if an error occurred.

methods.name: Start
methods.summary: Starts the pipeline execution, beginning media processing and playback. The pipeline must be built before calling this method.

parameters.name: onlyPreload
parameters.summary: If set to true, only preloads the pipeline and sets it to paused state without starting playback.

methods.returns: true if the pipeline started successfully, false otherwise.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops the pipeline execution and halts all media processing. This will bring the pipeline to a complete stop and free up resources.

parameters.name: force
parameters.summary: If set to true, forces an immediate stop without waiting for graceful shutdown.

methods.returns: true if the pipeline stopped successfully, false otherwise.

methods.name: Pause
methods.summary: Pauses the pipeline execution, temporarily halting media processing while maintaining the current state. The pipeline can be resumed from the current position using Resume().
methods.returns: true if the pipeline was successfully paused, false otherwise.

methods.name: Resume
methods.summary: Resumes pipeline execution from a paused state, continuing media processing from the current position.
methods.returns: true if the pipeline was successfully resumed, false otherwise.

methods.name: Connect
methods.summary: Connects two media blocks by linking an output pad from one block to an input pad of another block. This establishes the data flow path in the media processing pipeline.

parameters.name: output
parameters.summary: The output pad from the source media block.

parameters.name: input
parameters.summary: The input pad of the destination media block.

methods.returns: true if the connection was established successfully, false otherwise.

methods.name: GetContext
methods.summary: Gets the GStreamer context that provides access to the underlying pipeline infrastructure, including the GStreamer pipeline object, bus, and other low-level components.
methods.returns: The ContextX instance containing GStreamer pipeline infrastructure.

events.name: OnError
events.summary: Event raised when an error occurs during pipeline execution. Provides detailed error information for debugging and error handling.

events.name: OnNetworkSourceDisconnect
events.summary: Event raised when a network source (RTSP, HTTP, SRT, NDI, RTMP, etc.) disconnects or encounters a connection error. Provides details about the disconnected source element, error message, and source URI when available.

classes.name: IMediaBlockStoppable
classes.summary: Optional lifecycle hook for blocks that run a background worker or apply upstream backpressure (block the GStreamer streaming thread) and therefore need an early, before-state-NULL signal to release that thread and cancel in-flight work. The pipeline probes for this interface with as and calls RequestStop at the very start of its stop sequence — before EOS is sent and before the blocking transition to the NULL state — so a block that is backpressuring can unblock the streaming thread in time for EOS/NULL to proceed without a deadlock.
classes.remarks: Implementations MUST be non-blocking (do not join the worker here — that still happens later in CleanUp/Dispose), idempotent, and safe to call when the block is not running.

methods.name: RequestStop
methods.summary: Signals the block that the pipeline is stopping. Releases any producer blocked for backpressure and cancels in-flight work so the streaming thread can exit promptly.

classes.name: IMediaBlockStreamsSelected
classes.summary: A block whose outputs are fed by a decoder's dynamic pads, told when that decoder has settled its stream selection so it can end the outputs no selected stream will feed. An output left waiting never prerolls its sink, and that holds the whole pipeline in PAUSED (issue #1798).

methods.name: OnStreamsSelected
methods.summary: Called on the bus thread for every GST_MESSAGE_STREAMS_SELECTED.

parameters.name: srcName
parameters.summary: The name of the element that posted the message.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.summary: The types of the selected streams, combined.

classes.name: IVideoProcessingBlock
classes.summary: Marks a media block as an in-graph video processing block: a single video input pad and a single video output pad that passes frames through (optionally modifying them or drawing overlays).
classes.remarks: This is the contract the X engines that expose Video_Processing_AddBlock() - VideoCaptureCoreX and MediaPlayerCoreX - accept when inserting a user-supplied processing block into their video chain. (VideoEditCoreX has no such entry point.) AI blocks such as object detection, OCR, face recognition, ANPR, object analytics, background removal and generic ONNX inference implement this interface so they can be plugged into the engine pipeline without the engine (in VisioForge.Core) referencing the AI assemblies. A block exposes its connection pads through Input and Output.

classes.name: LicenseWatermark
classes.summary: Shared helper that burns the trial-license "UNREGISTERED" watermark into the video stream by inserting a textoverlay element in front of a sink element when the owning pipeline is unregistered (trial/blocked).
classes.remarks: Used by both VideoRendererBlock (on-screen rendering) and the frame-callback sinks (BufferSinkBlock / VideoSampleGrabberBlock) so that the watermark reaches every video output path, including the headless / callback paths used by the Unity samples (the SDK's text message is otherwise only shown on a native IVideoView, which Unity does not have). Implemented as a textoverlay (not a cairo chain): it negotiates RGBA/BGRA/ARGB directly and sits passthrough on an RGBA pipeline, avoiding an RGBA→BGRA→RGBA round-trip on every frame.

methods.name: WrapSink
methods.summary: Returns the sink pad to use as the block's input entry point. When pipeline reports a non-zero license state (trial/blocked), a textoverlay watermark is inserted in front of downstreamElement and its video_sink pad is returned (with the created element exposed via overlayElement so the caller can dispose it). Otherwise the downstream element's sink pad is returned and overlayElement is null.

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.summary: The owning pipeline (provides the license state). May be null.

parameters.name: pipelineCtx
parameters.summary: The pipeline context used to add the overlay element. May be null.

parameters.name: downstreamElement
parameters.summary: The sink element the watermark output links to.

parameters.name: overlayElement
parameters.summary: Outputs the created watermark element, or null when no watermark was inserted.

methods.returns: The pad to assign as the block's input pad. Never null unless the downstream element has no sink pad.

methods.name: TryInsertLicenseTextOverlay
methods.summary: Inserts a textoverlay element with the trial-license watermark text between the input pad and downstreamElement, returning the textoverlay's video sink pad. Returns null (with overlayElement = null) when creation/linking fails so the caller can fall back to a direct downstream connection.

classes.name: MediaBlock
classes.summary: Base implementation of a media processing block in the VisioForge MediaBlocks pipeline system. This abstract base class provides core functionality for all media blocks including pipeline management, context handling, and basic lifecycle operations. Media blocks are the fundamental building blocks that can be connected together to create complex media processing pipelines. Implements the IMediaBlock interface.

properties.name: _pipeline
properties.summary: Gets the pipeline that owns this block, or null if the pipeline has been collected. Protected property for derived classes to safely access the pipeline.

properties.name: Pipeline

methods.name: GetPipelineContext
methods.summary: Gets the pipeline context that contains shared resources and configuration for the entire MediaBlocks pipeline. This context provides access to GStreamer objects, logging, licensing information, and other pipeline-wide resources.
methods.returns: The BlockPipelineContext instance associated with this block's pipeline.
