parameters.summary: The EOS message indicating stream completion.

methods.name: DispatchStreamsSelected
methods.summary: Hands a GST_MESSAGE_STREAMS_SELECTED to the blocks fed by a decoder's dynamic pads, so an output no selected stream will feed is ended instead of holding the pipeline in PAUSED (issue #1798).

methods.name: ReapplyBridgeRenderDelays
methods.summary: Re-applies the configured render-delay on every BridgeAudioSinkBlock in the pipeline. interaudiosink.start() overwrites render-delay with the inter-surface default when the sink side starts before its paired source (the common case with separate input/output pipelines); calling this once the pipeline has reached PAUSED restores the configured value. No-op when there are no bridge audio sinks.

methods.name: Bus_StateChanged
methods.summary: Handles pipeline state change messages to track playback state and trigger appropriate events. Monitors transitions between Null, Ready, Paused, and Playing states to fire OnStart, OnPause, OnResume, and OnReady events. Also handles automatic seeking to start/stop positions when configured.

parameters.name: bus
parameters.summary: The bus that sent the state change message.

parameters.name: msg
parameters.summary: The state change message containing old state, new state, and pending state information.

methods.name: Position_SetRange
methods.summary: Sets the playback range by seeking to a specific start and stop position in the media. Playback ends at the stop position the way it ends at the end of the media: it stops, or, when Loop is set, every later pass plays this range again - until another range is set, StartPosition or StopPosition is assigned, or playback starts anew.

parameters.name: startPosition
parameters.summary: The position where playback should begin.

parameters.name: stopPosition
parameters.summary: The position where playback should end.

parameters.name: seekToKeyframe
parameters.summary: If true, seeks to the nearest keyframe (faster, less precise); if false, seeks to the exact position.

methods.name: SeekRange
methods.summary: Boolean)'s seek, at the current Rate and under RateLock. Returns the error for the caller to report outside the lock, or null once the seek is sent or skipped for a stop in progress.

parameters.name: startPosition
parameters.summary: The position where playback should begin.

parameters.name: stopPosition
parameters.summary: The position where playback should end.

parameters.name: seekToKeyframe
parameters.summary: If true, seeks to the nearest keyframe (faster, less precise); if false, seeks to the exact position.

parameters.name: loopRange
parameters.summary: Whether Loop passes replay this range: true for Boolean), false for the start seek, after which they read StartPosition/StopPosition.

methods.name: Position_SetRangeAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously sets the playback range by seeking to a specific start and stop position in the media. This method limits playback to the specified time range without blocking the calling thread.

parameters.name: startPosition
parameters.summary: The position where playback should begin.

parameters.name: stopPosition
parameters.summary: The position where playback should end.

parameters.name: seekToKeyframe
parameters.summary: If true, seeks to the nearest keyframe (faster, less precise); if false, seeks to the exact position.

methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous seek operation.

methods.name: WaitForStopAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously waits for the pipeline to reach the stopped (Free) state without blocking the calling thread. This method polls the pipeline state and completes when playback has fully stopped.
methods.remarks: This method is useful for coordinating pipeline shutdown with other application logic. It polls the State property every 50 milliseconds until PlaybackState.Free is reached. For applications that need to perform cleanup after the pipeline stops, await this method before proceeding with cleanup operations.
methods.returns: A Task that completes when the pipeline transitions to the Free state.

methods.name: WaitForStop
methods.summary: Synchronously waits for the pipeline to reach the stopped (Free) state, blocking the calling thread. This method polls the pipeline state and returns when playback has fully stopped.
methods.remarks: This method blocks the calling thread while waiting for the pipeline to stop. It polls the State property every 50 milliseconds until PlaybackState.Free is reached. For UI applications, consider using WaitForStopAsync() instead to avoid blocking the UI thread.

methods.name: GstButtonToMouseButton
methods.summary: Converts a GStreamer navigation event button number to a MouseButton enum value. GStreamer on Windows (d3d11videosink) uses: 1=Left, 2=Right, 3=Middle.

methods.name: ConnectLive
methods.summary: Dynamically connects two media block pads while the pipeline is already running (live connection). This method enables runtime modification of the pipeline by establishing new connections between blocks without stopping playback. Useful for dynamic routing scenarios like switching between video sources.
methods.remarks: Live connections allow for dynamic pipeline reconfiguration without interrupting playback. This is more complex than pre-built connections and may cause brief disruptions in data flow. Both pads must be in a compatible state for live linking to succeed. The link is recorded as a connection, so a stop and start of the pipeline links the pads again - unless either pad has OnDemandConnect, which leaves the link to the caller after every start.

parameters.name: output
parameters.summary: The source pad that will provide media data (the two pads may also be given the other way round).

parameters.name: input
parameters.summary: The destination pad that will receive media data.

methods.returns: true if the live connection was established, or output is already linked to input; false if the operation failed, including when output is linked to another pad. Same result as MediaBlockPad); like it, this overload takes the two pads in either order and links the output to the input.

methods.name: IsParked
methods.summary: Whether output was left unconnected at build time and parked on a null sink (#3024).

methods.name: FreezeSinksBehind
methods.summary: Freezes the sinks input fed until DisconnectLive or Disconnect unlinked it from output: nothing reaches them now, and a pause, a seek or the end of stream would wait for them (#3936). The first data across the input brings them back.

methods.name: AddBlockIfRequired
methods.summary: Adds the block if required.
methods.returns: true when every block this one needs is in the pipeline; false when AddBlock refused one - it does while the pipeline is running, and while StartAsync is probing its sources. The result used to be discarded, so a refusal produced a connection to a block the pipeline never held and never built, and Connect still reported success.

methods.name: Connect
methods.summary: Connects two media blocks by linking an output pad to an input pad. This method establishes a data flow connection between blocks, automatically adding blocks to the pipeline if needed. The connection enables media data to flow from the output block to the input block during processing.

parameters.name: output
parameters.summary: The source pad that will provide media data.

parameters.name: input
parameters.summary: The destination pad that will receive media data.

methods.returns: true if the connection was successfully established; false if the operation failed due to null pads, null blocks, or connection errors.

methods.name: Connect
methods.summary: Connects two media blocks using their default output and input pads. This is a convenience method that automatically uses the primary output pad of the source block and the primary input pad of the destination block to establish the connection. When either block has no primary pad on its side - a custom block implementing only Outputs or Inputs - the first free output and input pads of the same media type are connected instead, each block's free primary pad first.

parameters.name: output
parameters.summary: The source media block that will provide data from its default output pad.

parameters.name: input
parameters.summary: The destination media block that will receive data on its default input pad.

methods.returns: true if the blocks were successfully connected; false if the operation failed due to null blocks or connection errors.

methods.name: TryPairFreePads
methods.summary: Pairs an output and an input pad for MediaBlock) when a block has no primary pad on its side - it overrides only Outputs or Inputs.
methods.remarks: Each block offers its primary pad first and then its other pads, as the by-type lookup Connect does for a source, and only pads not connected yet - so a second Connect takes the block's next free pad rather than re-pointing one already in use. A pad flagged OnDemandConnect, a primary one included, is tried after the unflagged ones (see MediaBlockPad)). The media types must match, except that the Auto input of a DecodeBinBlock accepts any output - the same rule as Connect's.

parameters.name: outputPad
parameters.summary: The source's primary output pad, or null; the paired output on success.

parameters.name: inputPad
parameters.summary: The destination's primary input pad, or null; the paired input on success.

methods.returns: true when a pair was found; the pads are left unchanged otherwise.

methods.name: FreePads
methods.summary: The output or input pads of a block that are not connected yet.
methods.remarks: A pad flagged OnDemandConnect goes last rather than out: the flag may keep it for a later MediaBlockPad), but a block such as UniversalSourceBlockMini flags every output because it links them itself. When a flagged pad is the only match it is still paired, and a start links it only if its block does so itself.

parameters.name: outputs
parameters.summary: true for the outputs; false for the inputs.

parameters.name: primary
parameters.summary: A pad to put first among the pads with the same OnDemandConnect flag - the block's primary pad, which need not be in its array.

methods.returns: The free pads; empty when the block has none.

methods.name: Connect
methods.summary: Connects multiple media block pad pairs in a batch operation. This method allows connecting several output pads to input pads in a single call, useful for establishing multiple connections efficiently in complex pipelines.

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.summary: An array of pad pair arrays, where each inner array contains exactly 2 elements: [output_pad, input_pad].

methods.returns: true if all connections were successful; false if any connection failed.

methods.name: GetDiagramAsImage
methods.summary: Renders the pipeline diagram as a raster image using SkiaSharp. In mode, only the logical nodes and their connections are shown. This works at any time after blocks have been added and connected (even before ). In mode, every pad is labelled with its media type and, when available, the underlying GStreamer pad name. For full GStreamer-level detail the pipeline should have been built.

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary: Rendering options controlling mode, scale, spacing, colors, and orientation. Pass null to use defaults (HighLevel, scale 1.0, left-to-right).

methods.returns: An SKImage containing the rendered diagram. The caller owns the image and must dispose it.

methods.name: GetDiagramAsSvg
methods.summary: Renders the pipeline diagram as an SVG string. In mode, only the logical nodes and their connections are shown. In mode, every pad is labelled with its media type and GStreamer pad name when available.

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary: Rendering options controlling mode, scale, spacing, colors, and orientation. Pass null to use defaults.

methods.returns: A complete SVG document as a string.

methods.name: GetDiagramGraph
methods.summary: Extracts the diagram graph model from the current pipeline state. Acquires _mediaBlocksLock to snapshot the block list, then releases the lock before layout/rendering.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases unmanaged and - optionally - managed resources.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources.

methods.name: SetNativePipelineNull
methods.summary: Takes the native pipeline to the NULL state and waits, bounded, for it to get there.
methods.remarks: Bounded rather than CLOCK_TIME_NONE: a teardown can be issued from an application handler running on the pipeline's own bus thread, and a blocking state change from there waits for a message that same thread is responsible for delivering. Mirrors the polling wait the stop path uses after its forced SetState.

methods.name: IsLive
methods.summary: Whether pipeline still holds resources - anything other than NULL.
methods.remarks: Takes the pipeline rather than reading the field so a caller can hold one consistent view across a sequence of calls. The handle is checked before the state because CurrentState is an unchecked read at an offset from it: on a disposed wrapper that is an access violation, which no try/catch can see, while Handle is a plain field read that is Zero by then.

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.summary: A pipeline the caller already snapshotted; may be null.

methods.returns: true when it is live and a teardown still has work to do.

methods.name: DisposeAsync
methods.summary: Disposes the asynchronous.
methods.returns: System.Threading.Tasks.ValueTask.

methods.name: WaitForStart
methods.summary: Waits for a start in flight - its probe pass and its build - to finish, so the stop and the block disposal that follow do not run under it (#2322). State is Free for the whole of a start, so without this the dispose would skip its stop and dispose blocks the start is still building. Once the start has finished, a pipeline it took to PLAYING reads non-Free and is stopped as usual.
methods.remarks: Bounded: the Windows NDI probe takes no token and keeps its own deadline, and a start on a WPF/WinForms view marshals into the UI thread a synchronous Dispose may be blocking - the start then sees _disposing before its build and abandons. Once a wait has given up, later ones are skipped: DisposeAsync's own wait and the Dispose(true) it ends with must not add up to 20 s on a stuck start. Never reached on the start's own thread - Dispose(bool) defers to the start's exit there.

parameters.name: caller
parameters.summary: The caller name used in the log message.

methods.name: Finalize
methods.summary: Finalizes an instance of the MediaBlocksPipeline class.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Performs application-defined tasks associated with freeing, releasing, or resetting unmanaged resources.
methods.remarks: This method is thread-safe. Multiple calls are guarded by _disposedValue and internally delegates to Boolean) which is serialized via _stopLock.

methods.name: DisposeBlockPads
methods.summary: Disconnects (optionally) and disposes every pad a block exposes.
methods.remarks: Call this while the elements owning the static pads are still alive and the pipeline is already at NULL - see Boolean) for why the pads have to be released at all. A failure is logged rather than thrown: teardown continues.

parameters.name: block
parameters.summary: The block whose pads are released.

parameters.name: caller
parameters.summary: The caller name used in the log message.

parameters.name: disconnect
parameters.summary: When true, a connected pad is unlinked before it is disposed.

methods.name: DisposeParkedNullRenderers
methods.summary: Releases the null sinks the park pass stood up. Called on every teardown of the native graph: ClearData disposes the pipeline wrapper on every stop, so a sink left in the list would point into a freed GstPipeline, and the next run would add a second one.

parameters.name: caller
parameters.summary: The calling path, for the log line.

methods.name: ClearData
methods.summary: Clears the data.

parameters.name: forRestart
parameters.summary: true when the pipeline instance stays alive and may be started again (the stop path). The GStreamer side is torn down exactly as for disposal — elements are removed from the pipeline, every block's CleanUp() runs and the Gst.Pipeline object is disposed — but the two things a restart needs are preserved: the block objects themselves (not disposed) and the logical pad graph the caller built with Connect (_connectedTo is what ConnectPads relinks from, and nothing else records the topology). Each block's build latch is cleared instead, so the next Start rebuilds every element from scratch. false is the disposal path: pads are disconnected and blocks disposed as before.

parameters.name: deferNativeRelease
parameters.summary: The value Bus) returned for THIS teardown. When true the native pipeline must not be freed on this thread and is handed to Pipeline) instead. Passed in rather than read from a field: teardown paths are not mutually exclusive (Stop holds _stopLock, Close holds it only off the bus thread, Dispose does not), so a shared flag lets one teardown clear the answer another one is about to act on - and acting on a cleared true means freeing the pipeline from inside its own live bus dispatch. Deliberately has no default value. There is no safe one: false means "free it here", which is the dangerous direction, and true would silently change teardown behaviour for a caller that simply forgot. Both existing callers pass it, so requiring it costs nothing and makes a third caller state its intent.

methods.returns: true if successful, false otherwise.

methods.name: DisposeLibAVDirectRenderingWatcher
methods.summary: Disconnects the libav direct-rendering watcher and the refused decoder watch, which must happen while the pipeline wrapper still has a handle - each needs it to remove its native signal handler. Issues #1121, #3709.

parameters.name: caller
parameters.summary: The teardown path calling in, for the log line.

methods.name: ForceGPUDecodersUsage
methods.summary: Forces the pipeline to prioritize GPU hardware decoders over software decoders. This method adjusts decoder element rankings to prefer hardware-accelerated decoding for better performance. Note: Hardware decoder availability varies by platform and installed drivers. An explicit false is remembered: pipelines created afterwards skip the automatic raise (see ApplyDefaultGPUDecodersUsage), so the disable holds until an explicit true call. The method is not synchronized - call it before pipelines start being created on other threads.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: True to force GPU decoders to high priority; false to disable hardware decoding - every hardware decoder (Direct3D 11/12, NVDEC, Quick Sync, VideoToolbox, VA / VA-API, V4L2, Vulkan, Jetson) drops to None. The switch is process-wide and does nothing on iOS and Android. A later true re-enables the usual set; decoders outside it, such as the Direct3D 12 ones and VideoToolbox's vtdec, are not re-ranked by it and stay off until the process restarts.

methods.name: ApplyDefaultGPUDecodersUsage
methods.summary: Applies the automatic GPU decoder raise every pipeline construction performs. A call with no explicit Boolean) state, or after an explicit true, raises the usual decoder list; after an explicit false it does nothing - the disable is a process-wide intent and pipeline construction must not undo it (#2977).

methods.name: GetHardwareDecoders
methods.summary: Retrieves a list of available hardware decoders filtered by the specified criteria. This method queries the media framework registry for hardware-accelerated decoder elements that match the given filters.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.summary: Array of filter strings to match against decoder names (e.g., "H264", "H265", "VP9").

methods.returns: Array of tuples containing decoder element names and their descriptions for matching hardware decoders.

methods.name: GetSoftwareH264Decoders
methods.summary: Gets the list of available software-based H.264 decoders. Returns the standard FFmpeg-based H.264 decoder that provides reliable software decoding capabilities.
methods.returns: Array of tuples containing H.264 software decoder element names and descriptions.

methods.name: GetSoftwareH265Decoders
methods.summary: Gets the list of available software-based H.265/HEVC decoders. Returns the standard FFmpeg-based H.265 decoder that provides reliable software decoding capabilities.
methods.returns: Array of tuples containing H.265 software decoder element names and descriptions.

methods.name: ComputeInternalLicenseToken
methods.summary: Generates the internal license token. Uses a compile-time constant that's harder to extract via reflection.

methods.name: SetInternalLicenseState
methods.summary: Sets the internal license state. INTERNAL USE ONLY - Called by SDK classes after certificate validation.

parameters.name: state
parameters.summary: The license state (0 = licensed, 1 = trial, -1 = blocked).

parameters.name: token
parameters.summary: Security token - must match internal token.

methods.name: GetInternalLicenseToken
methods.summary: Gets the internal license token for SDK use. INTERNAL USE ONLY.

methods.name: LoadJsonAsync
methods.summary: Loads a pipeline JSON document into this pipeline: parses and validates it, clears the current contents, materializes every block through the block catalog, applies settings and resources, and restores the connections. The pipeline must be in the Free (not running) state. When the document fails to parse or validate, or the pipeline is running, nothing is changed; when materialization itself fails midway, the pipeline is left empty.

parameters.name: resolver
parameters.summary: Resolves logical resource ids referenced by the document.

parameters.name: baseDirectory
parameters.summary: Directory that relative file paths inside settings resolve against, or null.

methods.returns: The combined load and materialization result with diagnostics and block mapping.

methods.name: ToDocument
methods.summary: Captures the pipeline's current graph into a document, together with everything that could not be read off it - the reverse of String). Safe while the pipeline is running: the block list is taken under its own lock and nothing is changed, which makes this the save-during-Run path. Use it rather than when the result has to be a faithful copy - says whether it is, because a block that does not expose its settings contributes its position and not its configuration.
methods.returns: The captured document and its diagnostics.

methods.name: ToJson
methods.summary: Captures the pipeline's current graph as JSON. Whatever could not be captured goes to the log; call ToDocument when the caller has to act on it.
methods.returns: The document as JSON.

methods.name: SaveJsonAsync
methods.summary: Captures the pipeline's current graph and writes it to a file. As with ToJson, what could not be captured goes to the log.
methods.returns: A task that completes once the file is written.

methods.name: SetLicenseCertificateAsync
methods.summary: Loads a license certificate into this instance and activates it if the certificate requires activation.
methods.remarks: This is the only public licensing API. The file-path and stream overloads and every license-key method were removed in 2026.5.2, so an application reads the .vflicense file itself and passes the bytes here. The certificate belongs to this instance: call it on every instance you create, before starting it -- licensing one instance does not license another. Without a certificate the instance runs in the 30-day trial.

parameters.name: certificateData
parameters.summary: The bytes of a .vflicense certificate file issued by VisioForge.

methods.returns: A task that completes once the certificate has been loaded and any required activation has run.

methods.name: ValidateLicense
methods.summary: Validates the license and returns the dsVMREventID (0 = licensed, >0 = trial). Called from Start() method.

methods.name: GetLicenseState
methods.summary: Gets the current license state.
methods.returns: 0 = licensed, 1 = trial, -1 = blocked.

methods.name: GetContext
methods.summary: Gets the logging context that provides centralized logging services for this pipeline instance. The context manages the Serilog logger and provides structured logging methods for all pipeline operations.
methods.remarks: The logging context provides: - Structured logging with Serilog - Log level filtering (Debug, Info, Warning, Error) - File output when debug mode is enabled - Observable logging for event processing Blocks and pipeline components use this context for consistent logging throughout the framework.
methods.returns: The ContextX instance containing the configured logger and logging infrastructure.

methods.name: _loggerSink_OnErrorX
methods.summary: Handles log events from the Serilog observable sink and converts them to pipeline error events. This method processes log entries, formats them appropriately, and triggers error event handlers. Also handles automatic error reporting to Sentry when telemetry is enabled.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The logger sink that generated the log event.

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: The Serilog log event containing the log data and metadata.

methods.name: LoggerClose
methods.summary: Safely closes and disposes of the current logger instance. This method replaces the active logger with a silent logger to prevent logging during shutdown.

methods.name: LoggerConfigure
methods.summary: Configures the Serilog logger with appropriate sinks and settings based on debug mode and error event requirements. This method sets up file logging, console output, Sentry telemetry, and observable sinks for error event processing.

parameters.name: errorEvent
parameters.summary: True to enable error event processing through the observable sink; false to disable error events.

methods.name: LoggerSentryOnStartConfigure
methods.summary: Configures Sentry telemetry with detailed diagnostic information when pipeline starts. This method attaches pipeline settings, system information, environment variables, and other diagnostic data to Sentry reports for comprehensive error analysis during development.

methods.name: DeliverError
methods.summary: Queues args so OnError runs on the thread pool, after every error queued before it.
methods.remarks: The log that reaches this method often runs on a GStreamer streaming thread or the bus thread. Raising OnError there lets a handler's synchronous Stop() join that thread from itself and crash the process (issue #1991). The continuation is never ExecuteSynchronously, and this method does not wait for it: waiting would deadlock a handler that stops or disposes the pipeline, and an inline run would put the handler back on the logging thread. ErrorsEventArgs) reads OnError when it runs, so an event still queued after Dispose clears the handler does nothing. One handler throwing does not drop the rest of the queue.

parameters.name: args
parameters.summary: The error already formatted on the logging thread.

methods.name: ErrorDeliveryForTests
methods.summary: The OnError deliveries queued so far; completes once each of them has run. For tests.

methods.name: InvokeErrorHandler
methods.summary: Invokes the appropriate error handler for pipeline errors, with special handling for common SDK issues. This method processes error events and either triggers the OnError event or displays default error messages depending on the configuration and error type.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The object that generated the error.

parameters.name: args
parameters.summary: The error event arguments containing error details and severity level.

methods.name: ReportMissingNativeLibrary
methods.summary: Tells the developer that a native library the SDK needs is missing, without going back through the logger that is currently reporting the error (see ErrorsEventArgs)).
methods.remarks: The hint is not a copy of the error already in the log - it is the actionable half - so it goes to Trace as well as to the video view. A pipeline with no renderer block, which is every console and service pipeline, has no view to show it on.

parameters.name: library
parameters.summary: File name of the missing native library.

methods.name: SettingsGetJSON
methods.summary: Serializes the current pipeline settings to JSON format for diagnostic purposes. This method is used by the telemetry system to include configuration information in error reports.
methods.returns: JSON string representation of the pipeline settings, or empty string if serialization fails.

methods.name: Debug_SavePipeline
methods.summary: Saves the current media pipeline structure to a DOT file for visualization and debugging. The DOT file can be rendered into a graph image using Graphviz tools to visualize the complete pipeline structure.
methods.remarks: Pipeline graphs show: - All media elements in the pipeline - Pad connections between elements - Element properties and states - Caps (capabilities) negotiated between elements To view the graph: 1. Install Graphviz (https://graphviz.org/) 2. Run: dot -Tpng graph.dot -o graph.png 3. Open the resulting PNG file This is invaluable for debugging pad linking issues, caps negotiation problems, and understanding pipeline structure.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The base filename for the DOT file (without extension). The .dot extension will be added automatically. The file will be saved to the Debug_Dir directory.

methods.name: Debug_GetPipeline
methods.summary: Gets the current media pipeline structure as a DOT format string for programmatic analysis or visualization. This method returns the DOT graph data without writing to a file; credentials in it are masked.
methods.remarks: The returned DOT string includes: - All media elements with their properties - Pad connections and caps - Element states - Data flow directions Use this method when you need to: - Programmatically analyze pipeline structure - Send pipeline graphs over network - Store graphs in databases - Generate custom visualizations The DOT format can be processed by Graphviz or other graph visualization libraries.
methods.returns: DOT format string representing the complete pipeline structure with all elements, pads, and connections, or empty string if the pipeline is not available or DOT generation fails.

methods.name: GetPipelineDotData
methods.summary: The pipeline graph in DOT format, read under a pipeline use so a concurrent stop cannot release the pipeline mid-walk (issue #1899).
methods.returns: The graph, or null if there is no pipeline.

methods.name: GetTelemetryPipelineSnapshot
methods.summary: The pipeline graph for the error event telemetry reports, until one has been sent in this run, and only while a debugger is attached (#2430). Caps and states only: without NonDefaultParams GStreamer leaves out element properties, which carry the customer's URIs and file paths.

parameters.name: errorText
parameters.summary: The error the graph would ride on; an error telemetry drops gets none.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.summary: The run the error belongs to.

methods.returns: The raw graph, or null when none is due.

methods.name: TAG
methods.summary: Creates a logging tag that includes the pipeline instance name for more specific log identification.
methods.returns: A formatted string containing the class tag and instance name.

methods.name: ThrowIfDisposed
methods.summary: Throws an ObjectDisposedException if the pipeline has been disposed.

methods.name: GetSpecialBlocksSnapshot
methods.summary: Returns a snapshot of _specialBlocks taken under _mediaBlocksLock. Bus message handlers call this before iterating so a concurrent AddBlock / ClearBlocks / Dispose on another thread can't invalidate the enumerator and throw InvalidOperationException ("Collection was modified").

methods.name: IsSpecialBlock
methods.summary: Whether this block's events are delivered through _specialBlocks. The bus handlers dispatch element messages over that list alone, so every path that adds a block has to register the same set of types - AddBlock was the only one that did, and a detector or meter added with AddBlockLive never raised its event (issue #1473).
methods.returns: true when the block needs a place in _specialBlocks.

methods.name: ContainsBlock
methods.summary: Whether the pipeline already holds this block, tested under _mediaBlocksLock. A bare _mediaBlocks.Contains can walk the backing array while a concurrent AddBlock resizes it.

methods.name: CanAcceptBlocks
methods.summary: Whether AddBlock would accept a block right now - the same predicate it applies. Lets Connect ask once instead of discovering a refusal half way through adding two blocks.

methods.name: GetMediaBlocksSnapshot
methods.summary: Returns a snapshot of _mediaBlocks taken under _mediaBlocksLock. Used by bus message handlers that must locate the owning block of a message (for example the splitmuxsink fragment messages) without racing a concurrent AddBlock / ClearBlocks.

methods.name: UsePipeline
methods.summary: Starts a use of the current pipeline: until it is disposed, TakePipeline does not hand the pipeline over for release. Nothing inside a use should log or reach user code, and nothing inside may wait on a thread that is releasing the pipeline.

parameters.name: teardown
parameters.summary: Whether the caller is the teardown BeginPipelineRelease started.

methods.returns: The use; its pipeline is null if there is none, or its teardown has begun.

methods.name: BeginPipelineRelease
methods.summary: Marks the start of the current pipeline's teardown, before it goes to NULL: a Pause or Resume that comes later must not raise it again.

methods.name: IsPipelineReleased
methods.summary: Gets whether pipeline is no longer the current one, or its teardown has begun.
methods.returns: true if it is released or being released.

methods.name: IsStartStopped
methods.summary: Gets whether a stop or a dispose ended the start that is pausing or playing pipeline.

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.summary: The pipeline the start used; null if it had none.

methods.returns: true if the start must give up as stopped rather than report a failure.

methods.name: TakePipeline
methods.summary: Clears the pipeline field and hands the pipeline back for the caller to release. Once this returns, no query holding _pipelineReleaseLock and no Boolean) use is still using it. The wait is short - every caller has set the pipeline to NULL first, so a seek or a state change in flight on it returns - and bounded: a use that outlives it, or one this thread holds, leaves the pipeline unreleased, to the garbage collector.
methods.returns: The pipeline, or null if there was none or it must not be released now.

methods.name: AddBlock
methods.summary: Adds a media processing block to the pipeline. The block will be included in the pipeline's processing chain and can be connected to other blocks. This method is thread-safe and can only be called when the pipeline is in the Free state.
methods.remarks: Special blocks like barcode detectors, face detection, and VU meters are automatically tracked separately for event handling. The pipeline must be in Free state to add blocks. Attempting to add the same block twice will result in a warning but return true.

parameters.name: block
parameters.summary: The media block to add to the pipeline. Cannot be null.

methods.returns: true if the block was successfully added; false if the operation failed (e.g., null block, pipeline not in Free state, or block already exists).

methods.name: AddBlockLive
methods.summary: Adds a media block to a running pipeline and builds it without changing the element state. Unlike IMediaBlock), this method does not require the pipeline to be in the Free state. After calling this method, connect the block's pads using MediaBlockPad), then call IMediaBlock) to transition the block's elements to the Playing state.
methods.remarks: A block with outputs and no inputs - a source - does not follow the pipeline's state changes until IMediaBlock) starts it or a later pause, resume or play finds an output connected, so it cannot start with nothing connected. A sink of the block that nothing feeds yet is not counted as a sink - a pause, a resume or a seek does not wait for it and the end of the file raises OnStop without it - until data reaches it. A build that fails part way has already added some of its elements to the running pipeline. This method takes those back - the elements the failed build added are removed from the pipeline live-safely (issue #1409) - and the block is reset, so adding it again builds it afresh (issue #2695). The block object itself is left to the caller to dispose. An element that cannot be removed is reported as an error and stays in the pipeline, and the block is then not reset and this method refuses it for the life of this pipeline object - use a new block - and nothing releases it; dispose it only after the pipeline has stopped - releasing its elements while one of them still runs is the deadlock of issue #838. Do not add a block again when its clean-up after the failure logged a warning: it may be half released.

parameters.name: block
parameters.summary: The media block to add and build.

methods.returns: true if the block was successfully added and built; false otherwise.

methods.name: CollectBinChildHandles
methods.summary: The native handles of the pipeline bin's direct children.
methods.remarks: Each handle carries a reference, so no child can be freed and its address reused by a new element while the snapshot is in use. Release them with IntPtr}). No wrapper is made: one made here would never be released (#2062).

methods.name: HoldNewElements
methods.summary: Records what IMediaBlock) has to start for a block just added live, and keeps a source block out of the pipeline's state changes until then. StartAsync returns with the pipeline still on its way to PLAYING, and that change takes new children along: a source taken along before ConnectLive pushes into a pad with no peer and fails with not-linked, and the error parks the whole pipeline in READY (issue #3666).
methods.remarks: A pipeline that has not started takes the block along when it starts, so nothing is recorded then. A block with a core that is not a source starts through its core, so nothing is recorded for it either, except the source elements a mixer builds for its PNG inputs, held the same way (#4017). A block with neither a core nor a main element - a composite such as an output or an effects chain - has only these elements to start. ponytail: a state change reaching an element between the build's add and this lock still starts it (gst_element_set_locked_state is documented as racy against the parent). Usually that element is left unlocked, so the pipeline can stop it; a change already past the bin's check of the flag leaves it running and locked until the teardown lets go of it. Closing the window means locking inside every block's build.

parameters.name: childrenBefore
parameters.summary: The pipeline's children before the build.

methods.name: LockIfNotStarted
methods.summary: Locks the element's state, unless a state change has already started it.
methods.returns: true when the element is left locked.

methods.name: LockSinkIfNotStarted
methods.summary: Element) for a sink too.
methods.returns: true when the element is left locked.

methods.name: TakeHeldElements
methods.summary: Gives a held block back to the pipeline's state changes.
methods.returns: The elements that were held, with the references the caller now releases; empty when none were.

methods.name: UnlockConnectedHeldBlocks
methods.summary: Lets the state change the caller is about to make take along every held block with an output connected, as it takes any other child, for a caller that does not use IMediaBlock). A source with nothing connected stays held: it would fail with not-linked, or discard its data on a parked output. So does one the caller has removed, and a block IMediaBlock) refuses.

methods.name: ReleaseHeldElementsOutOfBin
methods.summary: Drops the held elements that have left the pipeline, and the blocks left with none. A removed block stays held only for what it left in the pipeline, which a state change would start.

methods.name: ReleaseHeldLiveBlocks
methods.summary: Gives every held block back and drops the references. Called before every teardown of the native graph, whose state change to NULL would skip an element still locked.

methods.name: RollBackFailedLiveAdd
methods.summary: Undoes a failed IMediaBlock) build: takes its elements back out of the bin, then resets the block so a retry builds it again instead of returning early on the state the failed build left (issue #2695).

methods.name: RemoveFailedLiveAddOrphans
methods.summary: Takes back the elements a failed IMediaBlock) build already added to the running pipeline: everything that is in the bin now and was not in childrenBefore.
methods.remarks: Removal goes through Element), whose idle-probe order keeps a live pipeline out of the issue #838 deadlock. An element a sub-build rolled back on its own is no longer in the bin and simply drops out of the diff. The wrappers stay valid here; IntPtr}) releases them through the block's CleanUp once this returns true.
methods.returns: true when every such element left the bin.

methods.name: RemoveBlockLive
methods.summary: Removes a media block from a running pipeline's block collection. This is the counterpart to IMediaBlock) for live removal. The caller is responsible for disconnecting pads and calling RemoveElementsFromPipeline, before or after this. Every connection recorded to the block's pads is forgotten, so a restart does not link to it; after this call MediaBlockPad.Disconnect has nothing left to unlink, and DisconnectLive does it. An input the block fed is then treated on a restart as after MediaBlockPad.DisconnectLive (#3976).
methods.returns: true if the block was found and removed; false otherwise.

methods.name: SyncBlockStateLive
methods.summary: Transitions a block's elements to the Playing state in a running pipeline. Call this after IMediaBlock) and MediaBlockPad) to start the block once all pads are properly connected.
methods.remarks: When several blocks are added as a chain, sync them from the sink end first. An output linked with MediaBlockPad) drops what it pushes until the block it feeds is started, so a block synced before its consumer loses that data - an encoder's first keyframe, the head of a file - rather than stopping. A block with no core and no main element that ends the chain or has several inputs - an output block, an NDI sink - is refused while one of its inputs is not linked: link it and call this again.

parameters.name: block
parameters.summary: The media block whose elements should be set to Playing.

methods.returns: true if the state was successfully synced; false otherwise.

methods.name: SyncElements
methods.summary: Starts the elements of a list that data enters through - the source elements and inputs - or the others. An element that has left the pipeline is passed over: it has no parent to sync with, which is not a failure of the block.

methods.name: LockHeldElements
methods.summary: Keeps what a refused block built out of the pipeline's state changes, its sinks too: behind a muxer they are not frozen as unfed, and a resume would wait for their preroll. A sink that neither takes one of the block's inputs nor is fed by the block is left alone, as it may be another block's.

parameters.name: inputs
parameters.summary: The elements owning the block's inputs.

methods.name: MissesAnInput
methods.summary: Whether a block with no core and no main element cannot start yet: it ends the chain or has several inputs, and one of them is not linked. A muxer or a combiner waits for every input it has, which would stall the running pipeline and then the stop, and an unfed sink would hold up a resume (#3734).

methods.name: HasNoOutputs
methods.summary: Whether the block is terminal - it has no output pads, so the elements downstream of its tail, up to another block's input, belong to it (a muxer sink's filesink). GitHub issues #1688, #2369.

methods.name: OtherBlocksInputPads
methods.summary: The input pads of every block but block, where the walk past a terminal block's tail has to stop: a custom block declaring no output may still expose one through a pad property of its own, linked to another block. GitHub issue #2369.

methods.name: RemoveBlockElements
methods.summary: The default RemoveElementsFromPipeline: takes the block's elements out of the running pipeline and leaves the block as if it had never been built.
methods.remarks: All or nothing. The elements are the ones a closed pad walk places inside the block - see IntPtr}) - plus the discard sinks parked on its output, and the neighbours are not linked across the gap. The block has to be fed from upstream and cut loose there (its inputs disconnected), and have at most one output: the removal then holds one pad, its own downstream end, and no thread is inside it. A block with several independent chains (an RTSP server's video and audio inputs, #3476) is removed chain by chain, each under its own held pad; a chain that fails logs an error and leaves the block built, with any chain already removed left out, and a retry removes the rest. Anything else - no BaseElement core, a source, a branch, a request pad, a connected input, several outputs, a block declaring no output whose tail still leads into another block's input (#2369) - leaves the block as it is, with a warning: removing part of it would leave the rest in the bin with its wrappers released. A sink prerolling in PAUSED keeps the held pad busy, so such a removal fails after the idle wait and leaves the block whole. Without this a live-removed branch stayed in the bin, its sink never got EOS, and a graceful stop waited out its whole budget. Nothing is done while ClearData runs: the pipeline is already in NULL and releases its children itself. GitHub issue #2139.

methods.name: RefuseRemoval
methods.summary: Says that MediaBlock) left block as it was.

methods.name: RemoveRun
methods.summary: Takes one run out of the pipeline through wrappers that are released afterwards.

methods.name: InternalPads
methods.summary: The GStreamer pads behind pads.

methods.name: ParkedOn
methods.summary: The discard sinks String) linked to any of outputs, each with its own sink pad.

methods.name: UseElements
methods.summary: Calls use with a wrapper for every handle, none of them left to the finalizer (#2079).

methods.name: Build
methods.summary: Builds and prepares the media pipeline for execution. This method configures the internal pipeline structure, initializes logging and telemetry, and prepares all added media blocks for connection and playback.
methods.remarks: This method should be called after adding all required media blocks but before starting playback. It performs essential initialization including Sentry telemetry configuration for error reporting. The pipeline must be successfully built before calling Start() or other playback methods.
methods.returns: true if the pipeline was successfully built; false if the build process failed.

methods.name: GetBlock
methods.summary: Retrieves a media block from the pipeline by its name. The search is case-insensitive and returns the first block with a matching name. This method is thread-safe and can be called at any time.
methods.remarks: Block names are assigned when creating media blocks and should be unique within a pipeline for best results. This method performs a case-insensitive string comparison to find the matching block.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The name of the block to retrieve. Cannot be null or empty.

methods.returns: The IMediaBlock with the specified name, or null if no block is found or the name is invalid.

methods.name: GetBlock
methods.summary: Retrieves the first media block from the pipeline that matches the specified block type. This method is useful for finding blocks by their functional type when the exact name is unknown. This method is thread-safe and can be called at any time.
methods.remarks: If multiple blocks of the same type exist in the pipeline, this method returns the first one found. For pipelines with multiple blocks of the same type, consider using GetBlock(string name) with specific names.

parameters.name: type_
parameters.summary: The MediaBlockType to search for (e.g., VideoRenderer, AudioEncoder, etc.).

methods.returns: The first IMediaBlock of the specified type, or null if no matching block is found.

methods.name: ClearBlocks
methods.summary: Removes all media blocks from the pipeline. This method clears both regular media blocks and special blocks (detectors, analyzers). The pipeline must be in the Free state to perform this operation.
methods.remarks: This method is thread-safe and will only execute if the pipeline state is Free. Both the main media blocks collection and special blocks collection are cleared. Use this method to reset the pipeline before adding a new set of blocks. The removed blocks are disposed: the pipeline is their owner and they are unreachable afterwards. Do not call it for blocks you intend to reuse - a stopped pipeline can be restarted with the same blocks by calling StartAsync again.

methods.name: FindVideoRenderer
methods.summary: Finds the video renderer.
methods.returns: VideoRenderer.

methods.name: FindVideoView
methods.summary: Finds the video view.

methods.name: FindOtherVideoViews
methods.summary: Collects the other renderers' views. Called at start only, so the stop reaches the views that start started.

methods.name: InvokeVideoViewStop
methods.summary: Stops the video view, unless another pipeline owns it now (#2656).

methods.name: StartAsync
methods.summary: Starts the media pipeline asynchronously for playback or recording. This method builds the media pipeline, connects all media blocks, and transitions to the playing state. Optionally, the pipeline can be preloaded to a paused state for faster subsequent playback.
methods.remarks: This method handles the complete pipeline initialization process: - Validates pipeline state and prevents multiple simultaneous start operations - Builds the internal media pipeline from added media blocks - Connects all block inputs and outputs according to their media types - Configures bus message handling for events and errors - Transitions the pipeline to playing state (or paused if onlyPreload is true) If the pipeline is already in paused state, this method will resume playback instead of rebuilding. The method is thread-safe and prevents concurrent start operations.

parameters.name: onlyPreload
parameters.summary: If set to true, the pipeline will be built and preloaded but remain in paused state instead of playing. This allows for faster playback startup later.

methods.returns: A Task`1 that represents the asynchronous start operation. The task result is true if the pipeline started successfully; otherwise, false - including when the link between two connected blocks is refused while the pipeline is built, for example because their formats do not match (OnError names the pair and the reason). A pad a block publishes once media flows, such as a demuxer's stream pad, is linked outside the build, and a refused link there is reported through OnError only.

methods.name: PrepareBlocksAsync
methods.summary: Awaits CancellationToken) on every block that implements it, so a source whose synchronous Build() needs probed media information has it by the time CreatePipeline runs.

parameters.name: cancellationToken
parameters.summary: Cancelled by a stop or a dispose arriving mid-pass.

methods.returns: true when every block is ready; false when one could not be prepared.

methods.name: Start
methods.summary: Starts this instance.

parameters.name: onlyPreload
parameters.summary: if set to true only preload and set to Pause.

methods.returns: true if successfull, false otherwise.

methods.name: StartIntl
methods.summary: Performs the start with the starting latch already claimed by the caller (Boolean) or Boolean)), and releases that claim on every exit.

parameters.name: onlyPreload
parameters.summary: if set to true only preload and set to Pause.

methods.returns: true if successful, false otherwise.

methods.name: TearDownFailedBuild
methods.summary: Tears down a graph a failed start built (wholly or in part) while it is still in NULL, so a retried start rebuilds every block from scratch.
methods.remarks: _stopping as Boolean) holds it, so the bus workers that gate on it stand down. Not Boolean): the graph never left NULL, and its source Stop() calls would reach blocks that never built; CleanUp reaches them too, as on every Dispose of a pipeline that never started. A Dispose in flight waits for the start to finish and disposes the blocks itself, so this one stands down.

methods.name: GetPipelineContext
methods.summary: Gets the internal pipeline context containing low-level media pipeline infrastructure and shared resources. This method provides access to the underlying pipeline implementation for advanced scenarios that require direct interaction with media components.
methods.remarks: The pipeline context includes: - The media pipeline instance - Pipeline-wide callbacks and error handlers - Shared resources accessible by all media blocks - Pipeline state information This is intended for advanced scenarios. Most applications should use the higher-level MediaBlocksPipeline API.
methods.returns: The BlockPipelineContext instance containing the media pipeline, callbacks, and pipeline-wide state.

methods.name: ParkUnconnectedOutputs
methods.summary: Gives a null sink to every output pad of block that no block connected to and that has no peer. The queue behind such a pad pushes into nothing, gst_queue_loop gets not-linked and pauses its task without posting an error, the queue fills, and a full queue blocks the block's shared streaming thread - starving the streams the caller did connect (issue #1415). Runs once per build, after every block is built, connected and post-connected, and again for a block added to a live pipeline.
methods.remarks: Only pads of a block implementing IParksUnconnectedOutputs are parked. A pad left for a later ConnectLive (OnDemandConnect on it or on its peer) stays connectable on any block, and drops its data until it is linked (issue #2056). An output whose input was dropped (LostItsInput, #3948) drops its data too, and on a parking block is parked as well. Idempotent: a pad parked on an earlier run is still linked, so the predicate skips it, and an output keeps one drop probe.

parameters.name: block
parameters.summary: The block whose outputs are checked.

parameters.name: caller
parameters.summary: The calling pass, for the log line.

methods.name: FreezeUnfedInputs
methods.summary: Freezes the sinks behind every input left with no connection - one DisconnectLive unlinked, one a ConnectLive of its output moved to another block, or one never connected - as IMediaBlock) does for a block not linked yet. Their preroll would hold the start, and the next stop, forever (issue #3936). The first data to reach such a sink brings it back. An on-demand input is left for the caller to link.

methods.name: CreatePipeline
methods.summary: Creates the pipeline.
methods.returns: true if successful, false otherwise.

methods.name: CreateEditingPipeline
methods.summary: Creates a specialized MediaBlocksPipeline configured for non-linear video editing workflows. This factory method initializes a pipeline with timeline editing engine support for timeline-based editing.
methods.remarks: The editing pipeline uses the timeline editing engine which provides: - Timeline-based editing with multiple layers - Non-linear editing capabilities - Transition and effect support - Project management This is distinct from the standard playback/recording pipeline and is intended for video editing applications.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: Optional pipeline name for identification in logs and debugging.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: Optional logging context for centralized logging.

methods.returns: A new MediaBlocksPipeline instance configured with editing capabilities.

methods.name: InitIntl
methods.summary: Initializes core.

methods.name: ErrorCallbackHandler
methods.summary: Error callback handler.

methods.name: Close
methods.summary: Closes the pipeline and releases all resources including media elements and bus connections. This method transitions the pipeline to a stopped state and performs cleanup operations.
methods.remarks: This method: - Disconnects bus message handlers to prevent memory leaks - Marks the pipeline context as closed - Clears internal data structures - Transitions the pipeline state to Free Consider using Dispose() or DisposeAsync() instead for complete resource cleanup.

methods.name: PauseAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously pauses the media pipeline playback without blocking the calling thread. This is the recommended method for pausing from UI threads to maintain responsiveness.
methods.returns: A Task that represents the asynchronous pause operation.

methods.name: Pause
methods.summary: Pauses the media pipeline playback. This method transitions the pipeline from playing state to paused state, maintaining the current position. Playback can be resumed later using Resume() or ResumeAsync() methods.
methods.remarks: This method immediately changes the pipeline state to Pause and pauses the media pipeline. The method will return false if the pipeline is null or not properly initialized. Use PauseAsync() for asynchronous pause operations. This method is thread-safe; the underlying GStreamer state change is atomic.
methods.returns: true if the pipeline was successfully paused; false if the operation failed or the pipeline is not available.

methods.name: SendEOS
methods.summary: Sends an End-of-Stream (EOS) event to the pipeline for graceful playback termination. This method allows the pipeline to finish processing any remaining data before stopping, ensuring proper file closure and resource cleanup. This is the recommended way to stop recording or playback.
methods.remarks: The EOS event propagates through the entire pipeline, allowing each element to flush remaining data. This is particularly important for file outputs to ensure proper file structure and prevent corruption. After sending EOS, the pipeline will transition to the stopped state once all data is processed. Use this method instead of Stop() when you need to ensure all data is properly written.

methods.name: ResumeAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously resumes media pipeline playback from a paused state without blocking the calling thread. This is the recommended method for resuming from UI threads to maintain responsiveness.
methods.returns: A Task that completes with a boolean value: true if resume was successful, false otherwise.

methods.name: Resume
methods.summary: Resumes media pipeline playback from a paused state. This method transitions the pipeline from paused state back to playing state, continuing from the current position without seeking.
methods.remarks: This method immediately changes the pipeline state to Play and resumes the media pipeline. The method will return false if the pipeline is null or not properly initialized. Use ResumeAsync() for asynchronous resume operations that return a Task. This method is thread-safe; the underlying GStreamer state change is atomic.
methods.returns: true if the pipeline was successfully resumed; false if the operation failed or the pipeline is not available.

methods.name: Duration
methods.summary: Gets the total duration of the media content in the pipeline. This method queries the pipeline for the total duration of the media being processed. Duration is only available for seekable sources like files; live sources will return TimeSpan.Zero.
methods.remarks: Duration information is only available for seekable sources such as media files. Live sources (cameras, network streams) typically return TimeSpan.Zero as they have no defined end. The pipeline must be in a playing or paused state for duration queries to be reliable. This method performs a duration query internally.
methods.returns: A TimeSpan representing the total duration of the media, or Zero if duration cannot be determined.

methods.name: Segment
methods.summary: The range _segment records for the current epoch; the whole media otherwise.

methods.name: RecordSegment
methods.summary: Records the range a position seek set. Called under RateLock.

parameters.name: stop
parameters.summary: The range stop, in nanoseconds; -1 for the end.

parameters.name: epoch
parameters.summary: The _rateEpoch read before the seek: a stop or park that raced it leaves the range already expired.

methods.name: StepSeek
methods.summary: MediaPlayerCoreX's step one frame against the playback direction: an accurate seek within the playback range. Forward playback steps back at 1.0, after which Rate says 1.0; reverse playback steps forward and keeps its rate. Refused, like a direct Double), before the start seek and during a stop, so a rate stored for the next start stays. A step that would cross the range end it moves towards from inside the range lands on it; one from that end itself - within half a step on either side - is refused. A reverse step from outside the range lands on the range's nearest frame; a forward one from below the range start goes where it was asked. Reports why itself, after releasing RateLock (issue #1711): a lifecycle refusal at Debug, a refusal at the range end at Info, a failed seek as an error.

parameters.name: expected
parameters.summary: The GStreamer pipeline the caller read the position from; the step is refused if a rebuild replaced it since.

parameters.name: current
parameters.summary: The position the step starts from, in nanoseconds.

parameters.name: frameDuration
parameters.summary: The duration of one frame, in nanoseconds.

methods.returns: true if the seek was sent; false otherwise.

methods.name: CanSeekNow
methods.summary: Whether a rate or frame-step seek may go to pipeline now: it exists, the start seek has run, and no stop is under way. Read under RateLock.

methods.name: RearmStartSeek
methods.summary: Puts the start seek ahead again. Lock-free, so a stop or a park holding _stopLock never waits on RateLock.
methods.returns: The new epoch.

methods.name: DurationAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously queries the total duration of the media content in the pipeline without blocking the calling thread. This is the recommended method for duration queries from UI threads.
methods.returns: A Task that completes with a TimeSpan representing the total duration, or TimeSpan.Zero if unavailable.

methods.name: Position_GetAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously queries the current playback position in the media timeline without blocking the calling thread. This is the recommended method for position queries from UI threads.
methods.returns: A Task that completes with a TimeSpan representing the current position, or TimeSpan.Zero if unavailable.

methods.name: Position_Get
methods.summary: Gets the current playback position in the media timeline. This method queries the pipeline for the current position during playback or recording. Position information is only meaningful for seekable sources like media files.
methods.remarks: Position queries work best with seekable sources like local files. Live sources and non-seekable network streams may return zero or invalid positions. For UI progress bars or time displays, consider calling this method periodically (e.g., every 100-500ms) rather than on every frame.
methods.returns: A TimeSpan representing the current position, or Zero if position cannot be determined or pipeline is not available.

methods.name: Position_SetAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously sets the playback position (seeking) without blocking the calling thread. This is the recommended method for seeking from UI threads to maintain responsiveness.

parameters.name: position
parameters.summary: The target position to seek to in the media timeline.

parameters.name: seekToKeyframe
parameters.summary: If true, seeks to the nearest keyframe for faster seeking but potentially less precise positioning. If false, seeks to the exact position which may be slower but more accurate.

methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous seek operation.

methods.name: Position_Set
methods.summary: Sets the playback position in the media timeline (seeking operation). This method performs a seek operation to jump to a specific time position in the media. Seeking is only supported for seekable sources like media files, not live streams.

parameters.name: position
parameters.summary: The target position to seek to in the media timeline.

parameters.name: seekToKeyframe
parameters.summary: If set to true, seeks to the nearest keyframe for faster seeking but potentially less precise positioning. If false, seeks to the exact position which may be slower but more accurate.

methods.name: SeekPosition
methods.summary: Boolean)'s seek, at the current Rate and under RateLock.

parameters.name: position
parameters.summary: The target position to seek to in the media timeline.

parameters.name: seekToKeyframe
parameters.summary: If true, seeks to the nearest keyframe (faster, less precise); if false, seeks to the exact position.

parameters.name: userSeek
parameters.summary: Whether the seek takes a pending PauseOnStop park: Boolean)'s does, the start seek does not (issue #1828).

parameters.name: error
parameters.summary: Why the seek failed, for the caller to report outside the lock (issue #1711); null when it was sent, there is no pipeline to seek or a stop is in progress.

methods.returns: true if the seek was sent; false otherwise.

methods.name: Rate_GetAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously gets the current playback rate (speed) without blocking the calling thread.
methods.returns: A Task that completes with a double value representing the playback rate (1.0 = normal speed).

methods.name: Rate_Get
methods.summary: Gets the current playback rate (speed) of the media pipeline. The rate determines how fast the media plays relative to normal speed (1.0 = normal, 2.0 = double speed, 0.5 = half speed).
methods.returns: A Double value representing the current playback rate, where 1.0 is normal speed.

methods.name: Rate_SetAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously sets the playback rate (speed) without blocking the calling thread. This is the recommended method for rate changes from UI threads to maintain responsiveness.

parameters.name: rate
parameters.summary: The playback rate where 1.0 is normal speed, values greater than 1.0 are faster, and values less than 1.0 are slower. Negative values enable reverse playback if supported by the media format.

methods.returns: A Task that completes with true if the rate change was successful, false otherwise.

methods.name: Rate_Set
methods.summary: Sets the playback rate (speed) of the media pipeline. This method changes how fast the media plays back relative to normal speed. Rate changes require a video renderer to be present in the pipeline.
methods.remarks: A positive rate set while the pipeline is not playing - before StartAsync, while it is starting, or after a stop - is stored and applied when playback next starts. A PauseOnStop replay keeps a forward rate. A reverse rate is not carried into a replay that has no start position; Rate_Get reports 1.0 while that replay is still ahead. A start position assigned before the replay seeks in reverse. A zero, NaN or infinite rate is rejected; use Pause to stop playback.

parameters.name: rate
parameters.summary: The playback rate where 1.0 is normal speed, values greater than 1.0 are faster, and values less than 1.0 are slower. Negative values enable reverse playback if supported.

methods.returns: true if the rate was successfully changed; false if the operation failed due to missing video renderer or other errors.

methods.name: ConfiguredRange
methods.summary: The range StartPosition and StopPosition describe, checked the same way for the start seek and every Loop pass: a zero stop counts as unset, a stop alone plays from the beginning, a negative start plays from the beginning, and a stop not after the start is dropped. A null start means no start seek; a null stop, play to the end.

parameters.name: errors
parameters.summary: Receives why a value was ignored; null to ignore it silently.

methods.name: ApplyStartSeek
methods.summary: The bus's Ready->Paused step: seeks to StartPosition when seekStart is set, at Rate - the rate stored before the start, or the one kept across a park - so a StopPosition range survives it. With no start position seek it sends a forward rate on its own; a reverse one kept across a park it does not apply, and records 1.0 in Rate instead. Runs on the bus thread, where a throw would skip the state bookkeeping after it.

methods.name: ResetRateAfterStop
methods.summary: Sets Rate_Get back to 1.0 after a stop, unless a rate is stored for the next start.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.summary: The run the stop tore down; skipped once a newer run has begun.

methods.name: NextFrame
methods.summary: Advances video playback by one frame in frame-by-frame stepping mode. This method pauses the pipeline and then steps by exactly one video frame in the current playback direction, useful for precise video analysis, editing, or frame extraction scenarios.
methods.remarks: Frame stepping requires a video renderer to be present in the pipeline. The pipeline will be automatically paused before stepping to the next frame. During reverse playback the step goes one frame backwards; the playback rate is not changed. Frame stepping precision depends on the video codec and whether frames are keyframes or predictive frames.
methods.returns: true if the frame step was successful; false if the operation failed or video renderer is unavailable.

Video renderer blocks with VR-capable video views VR video control enables features like equirectangular projection, viewing angle adjustment, and stereoscopic modes.
