classes.name: IDiscovery
classes.summary: Provides functionality to discover ONVIF compliant devices on the network using the WS-Discovery protocol.
classes.remarks: This interface defines methods for discovering ONVIF devices through multicast UDP probes. Implementations should handle network communication and parse discovery responses according to the ONVIF specification.

methods.name: Discover
methods.summary: Discovers ONVIF devices on the network and invokes a callback for each device found.
methods.remarks: This method provides real-time notifications as devices are discovered, making it suitable for UI scenarios where you want to display devices as they are found rather than waiting for all devices to respond.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.summary: The maximum time in seconds to wait for device responses before completing the discovery process.

parameters.name: onDeviceDiscovered
parameters.summary: A callback action that is invoked for each discovered device as responses are received.

parameters.name: cancellationToken
parameters.summary: An optional cancellation token to cancel the discovery operation.

methods.returns: A task representing the asynchronous discovery operation.

methods.name: Discover
methods.summary: Discovers all ONVIF devices on the network and returns them as a collection.
methods.remarks: This method waits for the specified timeout period to collect all device responses before returning. Use the CancellationToken) overload if you need real-time notifications as devices are discovered.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.summary: The maximum time in seconds to wait for device responses before completing the discovery process.

parameters.name: cancellationToken
parameters.summary: An optional cancellation token to cancel the discovery operation.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation, containing a collection of discovered DiscoveryDevice instances.

classes.name: IOnvifUdpClient
classes.summary: Provides an abstraction over UDP client functionality for ONVIF device discovery.
classes.remarks: This interface wraps the UdpClient to enable easier testing and to provide ONVIF-specific functionality for sending discovery probes and receiving responses.

methods.name: SendProbeAsync
methods.summary: Sends a WS-Discovery probe message to discover ONVIF devices on the network.
methods.remarks: The probe message follows the WS-Discovery specification and includes the provided message ID to enable matching of probe responses to their corresponding requests. A failed send ends discovery on this client; discovery fails with a DiscoveryException only when the probe could not be sent on any client.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.summary: A unique identifier for the probe message, used to correlate responses with the original probe request.

parameters.name: endPoint
parameters.summary: The target endpoint for the probe message, typically a multicast address (239.255.255.250:3702 for WS-Discovery).

methods.returns: A task representing the asynchronous operation, containing the number of bytes sent.

methods.name: ReceiveAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously receives a UDP datagram from a remote host.
methods.remarks: This method blocks until data is received or the operation is cancelled. The returned result contains both the received byte array and the remote endpoint information. A failed receive faults the returned task rather than returning an empty result: an ObjectDisposedException ends discovery on this client, any other failure makes discovery pause briefly and receive again. A result with no remote endpoint, or from port 0, is treated as a failed receive.
methods.returns: A task representing the asynchronous receive operation, containing the UdpReceiveResult with the received data and sender information.

methods.name: Close
methods.summary: Closes the UDP client and releases all associated resources.
methods.remarks: This method should be called when the client is no longer needed to ensure proper cleanup of network resources. After calling this method, the client instance should not be used.

classes.name: IUdpClientFactory
classes.summary: Factory interface for creating IOnvifUdpClient instances for ONVIF device discovery.
classes.remarks: This factory pattern allows for flexible creation of UDP clients, supporting both single endpoint scenarios and multi-interface discovery where clients are created for each available network interface.

methods.name: CreateClient
methods.summary: Creates an IOnvifUdpClient configured for the specified endpoint.
methods.remarks: The endpoint parameter typically specifies a local IP address and port. For ONVIF discovery, this is often a specific network interface address with port 0 (any available port).

parameters.name: endpoint
parameters.summary: The local endpoint to bind the UDP client to, determining which network interface and port to use.

methods.returns: A new instance of IOnvifUdpClient bound to the specified endpoint.

methods.name: CreateClientForeachInterface
methods.summary: Creates UDP clients for all available network interfaces to enable comprehensive device discovery.
methods.remarks: This method is useful for discovering devices across all network segments when a system has multiple network interfaces. It typically excludes loopback interfaces and creates clients only for active, up interfaces that support IPv4. Each client can independently send and receive discovery messages on its respective network interface.
methods.returns: A collection of IOnvifUdpClient instances, one for each valid network interface.

classes.name: DiscoveryDevice
classes.summary: Represents a discovered ONVIF-compliant device on the network.
classes.remarks: This class encapsulates all information obtained from an ONVIF device during the WS-Discovery probe process. It provides a strongly-typed, developer-friendly representation of the device data extracted from WS-Discovery probe match responses. The class contains parsed and processed information including network addressing, device identification (manufacturer and model), service endpoints, device capabilities (types), and detailed metadata (scopes). This information is essential for connecting to and managing ONVIF devices. All properties are set internally during the discovery process and should be treated as read-only by consumers of this class.

properties.name: Types
properties.summary: Gets or sets the collection of ONVIF device types that describe the device's capabilities and supported profiles.
properties.value: An enumerable collection of device type identifiers such as: "NetworkVideoTransmitter" - IP cameras and video encoders"NetworkVideoDisplay" - Video displays and decoders"NetworkVideoAnalytics" - Video analytics devices"NetworkVideoStorage" - Network video recorders and storage devices

properties.name: XAdresses
properties.summary: Gets or sets the collection of service endpoint URLs where the device's ONVIF web services are accessible.
properties.value: An enumerable collection of URLs, typically in the format "http://{IPAddress}:{Port}/onvif/device_service" or "https://{IPAddress}:{Port}/onvif/device_service" for secure connections. Multiple URLs may be present if the device is accessible through different network interfaces.

properties.name: Model
properties.summary: Gets or sets the model name or identifier of the ONVIF device.
properties.value: The device model string as reported by the manufacturer, typically extracted from the hardware scope in the format "onvif://www.onvif.org/hardware/{model}". May be an empty string if not provided by the device.

properties.name: Mfr
properties.summary: Gets or sets the manufacturer name of the ONVIF device.
properties.value: The manufacturer's name, typically extracted from manufacturer or name scopes in the format "onvif://www.onvif.org/mfr/{manufacturer}" or "onvif://www.onvif.org/name/{name}". May be an empty string if not provided by the device.

properties.name: Address
properties.summary: Gets or sets the IP address of the discovered device on the network.
properties.value: The IPv4 or IPv6 address as a string, representing the network location from which the device responded to the discovery probe. This is the address of the network interface that sent the response.

properties.name: Scopes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the collection of scope URIs that contain detailed metadata about the device.
properties.value: An enumerable collection of scope URI strings containing device metadata such as: onvif://www.onvif.org/type/{type} - Device type classificationonvif://www.onvif.org/hardware/{model} - Hardware model informationonvif://www.onvif.org/name/{name} - User-configurable device nameonvif://www.onvif.org/location/{location} - Physical location descriptiononvif://www.onvif.org/Profile/{profile} - Supported ONVIF profiles (e.g., S, T, G)onvif://www.onvif.org/mfr/{manufacturer} - Manufacturer identification

classes.name: XmlProbeReponse
classes.summary: Represents a WS-Discovery probe match response message received from an ONVIF device.
classes.remarks: This class serves as the root element for deserializing SOAP 1.2 envelope responses that conform to the WS-Discovery specification. It is used with to parse XML responses received over UDP during the ONVIF device discovery process. The structure follows the SOAP 1.2 envelope format with WS-Addressing and WS-Discovery namespaces, containing metadata in the header and actual discovery results in the body. Note: The class name contains a legacy typo ("Reponse" instead of "Response") that is maintained for backward compatibility with existing code.

properties.name: Header
properties.summary: Gets or sets the SOAP header section containing message routing, identification, and correlation metadata.
properties.value: A Header object containing WS-Addressing elements such as MessageID, RelatesTo, To, and AppSequence used for message correlation and duplicate detection.

properties.name: Body
properties.summary: Gets or sets the SOAP body section containing the actual probe match results.
properties.value: A Body object containing an array of ProbeMatch instances, each representing a discovered ONVIF device with its endpoint, types, scopes, and service addresses.

classes.name: Header
classes.summary: Represents the header section of a WS-Discovery probe match response message.
classes.remarks: The header contains WS-Addressing elements that provide essential metadata for message processing, including unique message identification, correlation with the original probe request, routing information, and sequence data for duplicate detection. These elements conform to the WS-Addressing specification and enable proper message correlation and handling in the WS-Discovery protocol.

properties.name: MessageID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the unique identifier for this probe match response message.
properties.value: A unique message identifier string, typically in the format "uuid:{guid}", that uniquely identifies this particular response message from the device.

properties.name: RelatesTo
properties.summary: Gets or sets the message ID of the original probe request that this response correlates to.
properties.value: The message ID from the probe request (in the format "uuid:{guid}"), used to match responses with their corresponding requests. This enables proper correlation when multiple discovery sessions are active simultaneously.

properties.name: To
properties.summary: Gets or sets the destination address for this message as specified in WS-Addressing.
properties.value: The target address URI for the message. For probe match responses, this typically contains the anonymous reply address defined by WS-Addressing.

properties.name: AppSequence
properties.summary: Gets or sets the application sequence information used for message ordering and duplicate detection.
properties.value: A string containing instance ID and message number attributes that help identify the sequence of messages from a device and detect duplicate transmissions.

classes.name: Body
classes.summary: Represents the body section of a WS-Discovery probe match response message.
classes.remarks: The body contains the actual discovery results in the form of probe matches, where each match represents an ONVIF device that responded to the probe request and matched the specified device types.

properties.name: ProbeMatches
properties.summary: Gets or sets the collection of devices that matched the WS-Discovery probe request.
properties.value: An array of ProbeMatch instances, each representing a discovered ONVIF device with its endpoint reference, types, scopes, service addresses, and metadata version. May be empty if no devices matched the probe criteria.

classes.name: ProbeMatch
classes.summary: Represents a single ONVIF device match from a WS-Discovery probe operation.
classes.remarks: This class contains all the information provided by an ONVIF device in response to a discovery probe, including its unique identifier, supported device types, metadata scopes (containing manufacturer, model, location, and other device information), and the service endpoint addresses where the device's ONVIF web services can be accessed. The data is structured according to the WS-Discovery specification with ONVIF-specific extensions and conventions for encoding device metadata in scope URIs.

properties.name: EndpointReference
properties.summary: Gets or sets the endpoint reference containing the device's unique identifier.
properties.value: An EndpointReference object containing the device's unique address, typically a UUID in the format "urn:uuid:{guid}" that persistently identifies the device.

properties.name: Types
properties.summary: Gets or sets the device types as a space-separated string of qualified names.
properties.value: A space-separated list of QName values indicating the device types (e.g., "tdn:NetworkVideoTransmitter" for cameras, "tdn:NetworkVideoDisplay" for displays). These types describe the ONVIF capabilities and profiles supported by the device.

properties.name: Scopes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the device scopes as a space-separated string of URIs.
properties.value: A space-separated list of scope URIs containing device metadata such as manufacturer, model, hardware version, location, name, and ONVIF profile compliance. These scopes follow the ONVIF scope URI format (e.g., "onvif://www.onvif.org/name/{devicename}", "onvif://www.onvif.org/hardware/{model}").

properties.name: XAddrs
properties.summary: Gets or sets the transport addresses where the device's ONVIF web services are accessible.
properties.value: A space-separated list of URLs, typically HTTP endpoints in the format "http://{IP}:{Port}/onvif/device_service", where the device's ONVIF-compliant web services are hosted. Multiple addresses may be provided if the device is accessible through different network interfaces or supports multiple protocols.

properties.name: MetadataVersion
properties.summary: Gets or sets the metadata version number for change detection and caching.
properties.value: An integer (as a string) indicating the current version of the device's metadata. This value is incremented whenever the device's metadata changes (e.g., configuration updates), allowing clients to detect when cached device information may be stale.

classes.name: EndpointReference
classes.summary: Represents a WS-Addressing endpoint reference that uniquely identifies a device endpoint.
classes.remarks: The EndpointReference provides a stable, unique identifier for a device that persists across network changes and reboots. In ONVIF discovery, this is typically a UUID-based URN that serves as the canonical identifier for the device. This identifier is distinct from the device's IP address and remains constant even if the device's network configuration changes, making it useful for device tracking and management.

properties.name: Address
properties.summary: Gets or sets the unique address identifier for the endpoint.
properties.value: A unique identifier string in the format "urn:uuid:{guid}" that persistently identifies the device across discovery sessions and network changes.

classes.name: BindingParameterCollectionExtensions
classes.summary: Lets several endpoint behaviors wrap the HTTP message handler WCF builds for a channel.

methods.name: WrapHttpMessageHandler
methods.summary: Wraps the HTTP message handler around whatever handler an earlier behavior already set.
methods.remarks: WCF takes a single Func<HttpClientHandler, HttpMessageHandler> and refuses a second one, so each behavior chains onto the previous.

parameters.name: bindingParameters
parameters.summary: The binding parameters of the endpoint.

parameters.name: wrap
parameters.summary: Builds the new handler around the inner one.

classes.name: DisableExpect100ContinueBehavior
classes.summary: WCF endpoint behavior that disables the HTTP Expect: 100-continue header for ONVIF compatibility.
classes.remarks: Some ONVIF devices have issues with the HTTP Expect: 100-continue mechanism, which is enabled by default in .NET for POST requests with content. This behavior intercepts HTTP requests and disables the Expect header to ensure compatibility with these devices. The Expect: 100-continue header causes the client to wait for a 100 Continue response before sending the request body. Some ONVIF devices don't handle this properly, causing timeouts or communication failures. This behavior should be added to WCF client endpoints when experiencing timeout issues or when devices are known to have problems with the Expect header.

methods.name: AddBindingParameters
methods.summary: Adds a custom HTTP message handler factory to the binding parameters.
methods.remarks: This method injects a factory function that creates the custom HTTP message handler when the WCF channel is built. The handler will disable the Expect: 100-continue header on all outgoing requests.

parameters.name: bindingParameters
parameters.summary: Collection of binding parameters where the HTTP handler factory is added.

methods.name: ApplyClientBehavior
methods.summary: Not used. Required by IEndpointBehavior interface.

methods.name: ApplyDispatchBehavior
methods.summary: Not used. Required by IEndpointBehavior interface.

methods.name: Validate
methods.summary: Not used. Required by IEndpointBehavior interface.

classes.name: DisableExpect100ContinueBehaviorExtensions
classes.summary: Provides extension methods for applying the DisableExpect100Continue behavior to WCF clients.
classes.remarks: This class contains convenience extension methods that simplify the process of adding the DisableExpect100ContinueBehavior to WCF client channels. This is useful when configuring ONVIF service clients that need to communicate with devices that have issues with the HTTP Expect: 100-continue header.

methods.name: SetDisableExpect100Continue``1
methods.summary: Applies the DisableExpect100Continue behavior to a WCF client channel if provided.
methods.remarks: This method adds the provided behavior to the client's endpoint behaviors collection if it's not already present. This ensures that the Expect: 100-continue header is disabled for all requests made through this client. Usage example: var deviceClient = new DeviceClient(binding, endpoint); var disableBehavior = new DisableExpect100ContinueBehavior(); deviceClient.SetDisableExpect100Continue(disableBehavior);

parameters.name: channel
parameters.summary: The WCF client instance to configure.

parameters.name: disableExpect100Continue
parameters.summary: The endpoint behavior that disables the Expect: 100-continue header. If null, no action is taken.

classes.name: DisableExpect100ContinueMessageHandler
classes.summary: HTTP message handler that disables the Expect: 100-continue header on outgoing requests.
classes.remarks: This handler intercepts all HTTP requests and removes the Expect: 100-continue header before they are sent to the ONVIF device. This is necessary for compatibility with devices that don't properly handle the 100-continue protocol. The handler works by setting the ExpectContinue property to false on the request headers, which prevents .NET from adding the Expect header to POST requests. This handler is typically used in conjunction with DisableExpect100ContinueBehavior to configure WCF clients for ONVIF communication.

constructors.name: DisableExpect100ContinueMessageHandler
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the DisableExpect100ContinueMessageHandler class.

parameters.name: innerHandler
parameters.summary: The inner handler which is responsible for processing the HTTP request messages.

methods.name: SendAsync
methods.summary: Sends an HTTP request with the Expect: 100-continue header disabled.
methods.remarks: This method overrides the base implementation to disable the Expect: 100-continue header before forwarding the request to the inner handler. This ensures that ONVIF devices that don't support the 100-continue protocol can process the requests without timing out.

parameters.name: request
parameters.summary: The HTTP request message to send.

parameters.name: cancellationToken
parameters.summary: The cancellation token to cancel the operation.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains the HTTP response message.

classes.name: NetworkHelpers
classes.summary: Provides static helper methods for network interface discovery and information retrieval.
classes.remarks: This utility class helps ONVIF clients determine network configuration details needed for device communication and event listener setup. It focuses on IPv4 networking and provides methods to discover: - Primary network interface IP address - DNS server addresses - MAC addresses - Gateway addresses - NTP server addresses These utilities are particularly useful when: - Setting up event listeners that need to know the local IP - Configuring device network settings - Determining network topology for camera discovery The class automatically filters out loopback and tunnel interfaces to find the primary physical network interface.

methods.name: GetPrimaryNetworkInterface
methods.summary: Gets the primary network interface excluding loopback and tunnel interfaces.
methods.remarks: This method filters out virtual interfaces to find physical network adapters. It's used internally by other methods to ensure they operate on actual network hardware rather than virtual adapters.
methods.returns: The first available network interface that is not a loopback or tunnel interface, or null if no suitable interface is found.

methods.name: GetIPv4NetworkInterface
methods.summary: Gets the IPv4 address of the primary network interface.
methods.remarks: This method is commonly used when setting up ONVIF event listeners to determine the local IP address that should be provided to devices for callbacks. It returns the first IPv4 unicast address found on the primary network interface.
methods.returns: The IPv4 address as a string (e.g., "192.168.1.100"), or null if no IPv4 address is found.

methods.name: GetIPv4NetworkInterfaceDns
methods.summary: Gets the IPv4 DNS server address configured for the primary network interface.
methods.remarks: This method retrieves the first IPv4 DNS server from the network interface configuration. It can be useful when configuring ONVIF devices to use the same DNS settings as the client.
methods.returns: The IPv4 DNS server address as a string, or null if no IPv4 DNS server is configured.

methods.name: GetPrimaryNetworkInterfaceMAC
methods.summary: Gets the MAC address of the primary network interface.
methods.remarks: The MAC address is returned as a continuous string of hexadecimal digits without colons or hyphens. This format may need to be reformatted depending on the requirements of the ONVIF device or service being configured.
methods.returns: The MAC address as a string without separators (e.g., "001122334455"), or null if the primary network interface cannot be determined.

methods.name: GetIPv4NTPAddress
methods.summary: Resolves an NTP server hostname to its IPv4 address.
methods.remarks: This method is useful when configuring ONVIF devices with NTP settings, as some devices require IP addresses rather than hostnames for NTP configuration. DNS resolution is performed synchronously and may block if the server is unreachable.

parameters.name: ntp
parameters.summary: The NTP server hostname to resolve. Default is "time.windows.com". Common alternatives include "pool.ntp.org", "time.google.com", or "time.nist.gov".

methods.returns: The IPv4 address of the NTP server, or null if resolution fails or no IPv4 address is found.

methods.name: GetIPv4NetworkInterfaceGateway
methods.summary: Gets the IPv4 default gateway address of the primary network interface.
methods.remarks: The gateway address is typically the router or switch that provides access to other networks. This information can be useful when: - Determining network topology for camera discovery - Configuring static routes on ONVIF devices - Troubleshooting connectivity issues Note that some network configurations may have multiple gateways; this method returns only the first IPv4 gateway found.
methods.returns: The IPv4 gateway address as a string (e.g., "192.168.1.1"), or null if no IPv4 gateway is configured.

classes.name: OnvifAuthenticationExtensions
classes.summary: Provides extension methods for configuring ONVIF authentication on WCF clients.
classes.remarks: This class simplifies the process of applying authentication to auto-generated ONVIF service clients. It handles the complexity of configuring both HTTP Digest and WS-Security authentication, including platform-specific workarounds. The extension method can configure: - HTTP Digest authentication through WCF client credentials - WS-Security UsernameToken through custom endpoint behaviors - Platform-specific impersonation level settings - Proper behavior attachment for legacy authentication

methods.name: SetOnvifAuthentication``1
methods.summary: Configures ONVIF authentication for a WCF client channel.
methods.remarks: This method configures the appropriate authentication based on the device's requirements. It handles platform-specific issues such as impersonation levels on .NET Standard vs .NET Framework. For HTTP Digest authentication, the method sets up WCF's built-in support; on Android, where the platform HTTP handler does not answer the challenge, it also adds AndroidHttpDigestBehavior. For WS-Security, it adds the provided behavior to the endpoint if not already present. Example usage: var deviceClient = new DeviceClient(binding, endpoint); // HTTP Digest only deviceClient.SetOnvifAuthentication( OnvifAuthentication.HttpDigest, new NetworkCredential("admin", "password")); // WS-Security only var wsAuth = new WsUsernameTokenBehavior("admin", "password"); deviceClient.SetOnvifAuthentication( OnvifAuthentication.WsUsernameToken, new NetworkCredential("admin", "password"), wsAuth); // Both authentication methods deviceClient.SetOnvifAuthentication( OnvifAuthentication.HttpDigest | OnvifAuthentication.WsUsernameToken, new NetworkCredential("admin", "password"), wsAuth);

parameters.name: channel
parameters.summary: The WCF client instance to configure.

parameters.name: authentication
parameters.summary: Authentication method(s) to apply. Can be a combination of flags to support devices that accept multiple authentication types.

parameters.name: credentials
parameters.summary: Network credentials containing username and password.

parameters.name: legacyAuth
parameters.summary: Optional endpoint behavior for WS-Security authentication. Required when using WsUsernameToken. Typically an instance of WsUsernameTokenBehavior.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: Optional context for error logging and diagnostics.

classes.name: OnvifBindingFactory
classes.summary: Factory class for creating WCF bindings configured for ONVIF communication.
classes.remarks: This factory provides pre-configured WCF bindings optimized for ONVIF services. ONVIF has specific requirements for SOAP messaging that differ between service types: - Most services use SOAP 1.2 without WS-Addressing - Event services require WS-Addressing for proper subscription handling - Some devices may require SOAP 1.1 for compatibility All bindings are configured with: - HTTP Digest authentication (standard for ONVIF) - Large message size limits (10MB) for video metadata - Appropriate XML reader quotas for complex ONVIF messages These bindings are used by the auto-generated WCF client proxies to ensure proper communication with ONVIF-compliant devices. Transport security: the parameterless overloads default to plain HTTP. Although Digest authentication hashes the password challenge, the SOAP body – which can contain stream URIs, snapshot URIs, NTP server names, etc. – still transits in cleartext. For TLS-protected ONVIF endpoints (URLs starting with https://) call the useHttps: true overload (e.g. ) so the binding uses .

methods.name: CreateBinding
methods.summary: Creates a standard ONVIF binding without WS-Addressing for most ONVIF services.
methods.remarks: This binding configuration is used for the majority of ONVIF services including: - Device Management Service - Media Service (profiles, stream URIs) - PTZ Service (pan/tilt/zoom control) - Imaging Service (brightness, contrast, etc.) - Analytics Service Key configuration: - SOAP 1.2 without WS-Addressing headers - HTTP Digest authentication - 10MB message size limits - Optimized XML reader quotas for large metadata
methods.returns: A configured CustomBinding suitable for ONVIF device, media, imaging, analytics, and PTZ services.

methods.name: CreateBinding
methods.summary: Creates a standard ONVIF binding without WS-Addressing for most ONVIF services, optionally over HTTPS.

parameters.name: useHttps
parameters.summary: When true, the binding uses HttpsTransportBindingElement for TLS-protected ONVIF endpoints. When false (default), plain HTTP is used – credentials transit in cleartext (apart from Digest hashing of the challenge), so callers should pass true for any endpoint URL that starts with https://.

methods.returns: Configured CustomBinding.

methods.name: CreateEventBinding
methods.summary: Creates an ONVIF binding with WS-Addressing enabled for event services.
methods.remarks: This binding is specifically configured for ONVIF event-related services: - Event Service (subscriptions, pull-points) - Notification Producer/Consumer interfaces The key difference from the standard binding is the inclusion of WS-Addressing headers which are mandatory for event subscriptions and notifications per the ONVIF specification. Configuration: - SOAP 1.2 with WS-Addressing 1.0 - HTTP Digest authentication - 10MB message size limits - Support for complex event metadata
methods.returns: A configured CustomBinding with WS-Addressing support required for ONVIF event and notification services.

methods.name: CreateEventBinding
methods.summary: Creates an ONVIF binding with WS-Addressing enabled for event services, optionally over HTTPS.

parameters.name: useHttps
parameters.summary: When true, the binding uses HttpsTransportBindingElement for TLS-protected ONVIF event endpoints.

methods.name: CreateEventBindingSoap11
methods.summary: Creates an ONVIF binding with SOAP 1.1 and WS-Addressing for legacy device compatibility.
methods.remarks: Some older ONVIF devices or non-standard implementations may require SOAP 1.1 instead of the standard SOAP 1.2. This binding provides compatibility for such devices while maintaining WS-Addressing support needed for event services. Use this binding when: - Standard event binding fails with SOAP version errors - Device documentation specifies SOAP 1.1 requirement - Dealing with early ONVIF implementations (pre-2.0) Configuration: - SOAP 1.1 with WS-Addressing 1.0 - HTTP Digest authentication - Same message size limits as standard bindings
methods.returns: A configured CustomBinding using SOAP 1.1 with WS-Addressing for devices that don't fully support SOAP 1.2.

methods.name: CreateEventBindingSoap11
methods.summary: Creates an ONVIF binding with SOAP 1.1 + WS-Addressing for legacy device compatibility, optionally over HTTPS.

classes.name: ONVIFClientX
classes.summary: Provides a comprehensive client implementation for ONVIF (Open Network Video Interface Forum) compliant devices. This client supports device discovery, configuration, media streaming, PTZ control, event handling, and other ONVIF services.
classes.remarks: The ONVIFClientX class serves as the main entry point for interacting with ONVIF devices such as IP cameras, video encoders, and other network video equipment. It provides a simplified API that abstracts the complexity of the underlying ONVIF web services. Key features include: - Device connection and authentication (WS-UsernameToken and HTTP Digest) - Media profile management and stream URI retrieval - PTZ (Pan-Tilt-Zoom) control for compatible devices - Event subscription and notification handling - Time synchronization and device configuration - Network configuration and device maintenance operations The client automatically manages service endpoints and provides error handling for common scenarios. All methods are async-enabled for non-blocking operations.

constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the ONVIFClientX class.
constructors.remarks: The context parameter allows integration with existing logging infrastructure. After creating an instance, use String) to establish a connection to an ONVIF device.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: Optional base context for logging and error handling. If not provided, a default context will be created.

properties.value: true to disable the Expect: 100-continue header; otherwise, false. The default is false.

properties.value: The default is one minute; MaxValue or InfiniteTimeSpan disables the timeout.

methods.name: ConnectAsync
methods.summary: Connects to an ONVIF device using the specified credentials with default authentication methods.
methods.remarks: This method uses both WS-UsernameToken and HTTP Digest authentication by default, which provides compatibility with most ONVIF devices. When both the user name and the password are empty, it connects without authentication (None), for devices that need no credentials. The connection process includes retrieving device information to validate the connection.

parameters.name: userName
parameters.summary: The username for authentication. Leave it and password empty for a device that needs no credentials.

parameters.name: password
parameters.summary: The password for authentication. Leave it and userName empty for a device that needs no credentials.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if the connection was successful; otherwise, false.

methods.name: ConnectAsync
methods.summary: Connects to an ONVIF device using the specified credentials and authentication method.
methods.remarks: This method establishes a connection to an ONVIF device and retrieves basic device information. The authentication parameter allows fine-grained control over the authentication mechanism: - None: No authentication (for devices that don't require credentials) - WsUsernameToken: WS-Security UsernameToken (most common for ONVIF) - HttpDigest: HTTP Digest authentication - Both can be combined for maximum compatibility The connection is validated by retrieving device information. If this fails, the method returns false. Each call drops what the previous connection cached (the device's service list and service clients), so the same instance can be connected to another device; clients returned earlier by String,``0}) are aborted, and event polling started with CancellationToken) stops. Don't call other methods of this instance while it runs. When the method returns false the client is not connected, and service calls report "Not connected" until a later call succeeds.

parameters.name: userName
parameters.summary: The username for authentication. Can be empty if authentication is None.

parameters.name: password
parameters.summary: The password for authentication. Can be empty, for an account with a blank password.

parameters.name: authentication
parameters.summary: The authentication method(s) to use. Can be combined using bitwise OR.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if the connection was successful; otherwise, false — also when onvifUri is empty, or userName is empty while authentication is not None. The method does not throw; the reason is logged as an error.

methods.name: AdjustForCameraClockAsync
methods.summary: Shifts the WS-UsernameToken timestamps by the difference between the camera's clock and this machine's.
methods.remarks: The token digest covers its creation time, which the camera checks against its own clock, so a camera whose clock is off rejects every authenticated request with ter:NotAuthorized. The ONVIF Core specification has the client read the clock with GetSystemDateAndTime, which needs no credentials, and correct for it; the request goes out on a client without authentication for that reason. When the clock cannot be read the timestamps stay on this machine's clock. TimeSpan) after connecting replaces the offset set here.
methods.returns: false when the device did not answer at all (unreachable or timed out), so the connect can fail at once instead of waiting for the same timeout again; true otherwise.

methods.name: IsNoAnswer
methods.summary: Returns whether a request failed because the device never answered: a timeout, or a connection that could not be made (WCF on .NET reports that as a CommunicationException over a socket error). A SOAP fault, an HTTP error status or a connection the device reset is an answer: the device was reached.

methods.name: SetCameraUtcNowOffset
methods.summary: Sets the UTC-now offset applied when computing WS-UsernameToken timestamps.

parameters.name: utcNowOffset
parameters.summary: The offset to add to DateTime.UtcNow for token generation. Use this when the camera clock differs from the host clock.

methods.remarks: This method returns comprehensive time information including: - UTC date and time - Local date and time - Time zone configuration - Daylight saving time status - Time source (manual or NTP) The SystemDateTime object provides raw time data as returned by the device. For a simplified UTC DateTime, use GetSystemDateAndTimeUtcAsync. This information is critical for: - Event timestamp correlation - Recording synchronization - Forensic analysis - Multi-device coordination

methods.summary: Sets the system date and time manually on the ONVIF device.
methods.remarks: This method sets the device time manually, which disables NTP synchronization. The device will maintain time using its internal clock, which may drift over time. For better time accuracy, consider using: - Boolean) to enable NTP synchronization - Boolean) for devices with specific NTP requirements The timezone parameter should be a POSIX timezone string. Common formats: - Simple offset: "UTC", "GMT", "EST5", "PST8" - With DST: "EST5EDT", "PST8PDT", "CST6CDT" - Full POSIX: "Europe/London-0BST-1,M3.5.0/01:00:00,M10.5.0/02:00:00" Time synchronization is critical for: - Accurate event timestamps - Recording correlation - Multi-device synchronization - Forensic analysis

methods.name: SetSynchronizationPointAsync
methods.summary: Sets a synchronization point (I-frame) in the video stream.
methods.remarks: A synchronization point forces the encoder to generate an I-frame (keyframe) in the video stream. This is useful for: - Ensuring a clean starting point for new stream consumers - Recovering from transmission errors - Improving stream quality after network issues - Starting recording at a proper frame boundary I-frames are complete images that don't depend on previous frames, allowing decoders to start decoding from that point. Note: This only affects video streams with inter-frame compression (H.264, H.265). MJPEG streams don't need synchronization points as every frame is independent.

methods.name: AbsoluteMoveAsync
methods.summary: Performs an absolute zoom movement to a specific position.
methods.remarks: Absolute movement commands position the PTZ unit to specific coordinates. The zoom range is typically -1.0 (wide) to 1.0 (telephoto), with 0 being the middle position. Speed values range from 0.0 (slowest) to 1.0 (fastest).

parameters.name: profileToken
parameters.summary: The token of the media profile that contains PTZ configuration.

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.summary: The absolute zoom position (-1.0 to 1.0, where 0 is center).

methods.returns: A task whose result is true when the camera accepted the command, or false when the command did not reach the camera or the camera rejected it (the failure is logged).

methods.name: AbsoluteMoveAsync
methods.summary: Performs an absolute pan and tilt movement to specific positions.
methods.remarks: Absolute movement positions the camera to exact coordinates: - Pan: -1.0 (full left) to 1.0 (full right) - Tilt: -1.0 (full down) to 1.0 (full up) - Speed: 0.0 (slowest) to 1.0 (fastest) The actual range depends on the camera's physical capabilities.

parameters.name: profileToken
parameters.summary: The token of the media profile that contains PTZ configuration.

parameters.name: pan
parameters.summary: The absolute pan position (-1.0 to 1.0, where 0 is center).

parameters.name: tilt
parameters.summary: The absolute tilt position (-1.0 to 1.0, where 0 is center).

methods.returns: A task whose result is true when the camera accepted the command, or false when the command did not reach the camera or the camera rejected it (the failure is logged).

methods.name: AbsoluteMoveAsync
methods.summary: Performs an absolute PTZ movement to specific pan, tilt, and zoom positions.
methods.remarks: This method moves all three axes simultaneously to their absolute positions: - Pan: -1.0 (full left) to 1.0 (full right) - Tilt: -1.0 (full down) to 1.0 (full up) - Zoom: -1.0 (wide) to 1.0 (telephoto) - Speed: 0.0 (slowest) to 1.0 (fastest) for each axis The camera will move all axes simultaneously, arriving at the target position based on the individual axis speeds.

parameters.name: profileToken
parameters.summary: The token of the media profile that contains PTZ configuration.

parameters.name: pan
parameters.summary: The absolute pan position (-1.0 to 1.0, where 0 is center).

parameters.name: tilt
parameters.summary: The absolute tilt position (-1.0 to 1.0, where 0 is center).

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.summary: The absolute zoom position (-1.0 to 1.0, where 0 is center).

methods.returns: A task whose result is true when the camera accepted the command, or false when the command did not reach the camera or the camera rejected it (the failure is logged).

methods.name: RelativeMoveAsync
methods.summary: Performs a relative zoom movement from the current position.
methods.remarks: Relative movement commands move the PTZ unit by a specified distance from its current position. Positive values zoom in (telephoto), negative values zoom out (wide angle). The actual movement distance depends on the camera's current position and physical limits.

parameters.name: profileToken
parameters.summary: The token of the media profile that contains PTZ configuration.

methods.returns: A task whose result is true when the camera accepted the command, or false when the command did not reach the camera or the camera rejected it (the failure is logged).

methods.name: RelativeMoveAsync
methods.summary: Performs a relative pan and tilt movement from the current position.
methods.remarks: Moves the camera relative to its current position: - Positive pan values move right, negative move left - Positive tilt values move up, negative move down - Movement distance is relative to the total range - Camera stops at physical limits

parameters.name: profileToken
parameters.summary: The token of the media profile that contains PTZ configuration.

methods.returns: A task whose result is true when the camera accepted the command, or false when the command did not reach the camera or the camera rejected it (the failure is logged).

methods.name: RelativeMoveAsync
methods.summary: Performs a relative PTZ movement from the current position.
methods.remarks: Moves all three axes relative to their current positions: - Pan: positive = right, negative = left - Tilt: positive = up, negative = down - Zoom: positive = zoom in, negative = zoom out All movements are simultaneous. The camera stops at physical limits. Use smaller values for fine adjustments, larger values for bigger movements.

parameters.name: profileToken
parameters.summary: The token of the media profile that contains PTZ configuration.

methods.returns: A task whose result is true when the camera accepted the command, or false when the command did not reach the camera or the camera rejected it (the failure is logged).

methods.name: GotoHomePositionAsync
methods.summary: Moves the PTZ camera to its home position.
methods.remarks: Sends the ONVIF GotoHomePosition command, which moves the camera to the home position stored in the camera itself. Only when the camera refuses it (no home position configured, or the operation is not supported) does the method fall back to a preset named "Home", then a preset with token "1"; with neither, it returns false.

parameters.name: profileToken
parameters.summary: The token of the media profile that contains PTZ configuration.

methods.returns: A task whose result is true when the camera accepted the command, or false when the command did not reach the camera or the camera rejected it (the failure is logged).

methods.name: GotoHomePositionAsync
methods.summary: Moves the PTZ camera to its home position.
methods.remarks: Sends the ONVIF GotoHomePosition command, which moves the camera to the home position stored in the camera itself. Only when the camera refuses it (no home position configured, or the operation is not supported) does the method fall back to a preset named "Home", then a preset with token "1"; with neither, it returns false.
methods.returns: A task whose result is true when the camera accepted the command, or false when the command did not reach the camera or the camera rejected it (the failure is logged).

methods.name: ContinuousMoveAsync

methods.remarks: Continuous move starts the PTZ unit moving at the specified speeds and continues until: - StopMoveAsync is called - The specified timeout expires - Physical limits are reached Speed values: - Positive pan: move right, negative: move left - Positive tilt: move up, negative: move down - Positive zoom: zoom in, negative: zoom out - 0: no movement on that axis - Speed magnitude: 0.0 (stopped) to 1.0 (maximum speed) This is ideal for joystick-style control or following moving objects.

parameters.name: profileToken
parameters.summary: The token of the media profile that contains PTZ configuration.

parameters.name: speedPanTilt
parameters.summary: Pan and tilt speeds (-1.0 to 1.0 for each axis).

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.summary: Optional timeout after which movement automatically stops. If null, movement continues until StopMoveAsync is called.

methods.returns: A task whose result is true when the camera accepted the command, or false when the command did not reach the camera or the camera rejected it (the failure is logged).

parameters.name: pan
parameters.summary: Pan speed (-1.0 to 1.0). Positive = right, negative = left.

parameters.name: tilt
parameters.summary: Tilt speed (-1.0 to 1.0). Positive = up, negative = down.

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.summary: Zoom speed (-1.0 to 1.0). Positive = zoom in, negative = zoom out.

methods.returns: A task whose result is true when the camera accepted the command, or false when the command did not reach the camera or the camera rejected it (the failure is logged).

methods.name: ContinuousMoveAsync
methods.summary: Starts continuous PTZ movement at specified speeds using simple parameters.
methods.remarks: This is a simplified overload for continuous movement without timeout. Movement continues until StopMoveAsync is called or physical limits are reached. Use 0 for any axis to keep it stationary.

parameters.summary: Tilt speed (-1.0 to 1.0). Positive = up, negative = down.

classes.name: ONVIFClientXExtensions
classes.summary: Provides extension methods for the ONVIFClientX class to enhance usability.
classes.remarks: This class contains convenience extension methods that simplify common ONVIF operations by providing method overloads and helper functions. The extensions focus on: - Simplified parameter passing using objects instead of primitive values - Enhanced error handling with automatic fallback mechanisms - Improved API consistency across different ONVIF operations These extensions make the ONVIF client more intuitive to use while maintaining full compatibility with the underlying ONVIF services.

methods.name: GetStreamUriAsync

methods.remarks: This extension method provides a more convenient way to get stream URIs by accepting a Profile object directly instead of requiring the profile token string. The method internally extracts the token and calls the appropriate client method.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.summary: The media profile object containing the profile token.

methods.returns: A task that returns the MediaUri containing the streaming URI.

methods.name: PullPointPullMessagesAsync
methods.summary: Pulls event messages from a pull-point subscription.
methods.remarks: This extension simplifies pulling messages by accepting the subscription response object directly instead of requiring manual extraction of the subscription reference address.

parameters.name: subscribeResponse
parameters.summary: The subscription response containing the pull-point reference.

parameters.name: timeoutInSeconds
parameters.summary: Maximum time to wait for messages in seconds. Default is 60 seconds.

parameters.name: maxMessages
parameters.summary: Maximum number of messages to retrieve. Default is 100.

methods.returns: A task that returns the PullMessagesResponse containing event notifications and the current time on the device.

methods.name: PullPointPullMessagesWithFallbackAsync
methods.summary: Pulls event messages with automatic fallback for better device compatibility.
methods.remarks: This enhanced version provides better compatibility with various ONVIF devices by implementing automatic fallback mechanisms when the standard pull fails. It tries different parameter combinations and endpoints to maximize success rates. Fallback strategies include: - Adjusting timeout values - Trying different message count limits - Using alternative endpoint formats This method is recommended when dealing with devices from multiple manufacturers or when the standard pull method fails intermittently.

parameters.name: subscribeResponse
parameters.summary: Subscription response containing the pull-point reference.

parameters.name: timeoutInSeconds
parameters.summary: Maximum time to wait for messages in seconds. Default is 60.

parameters.name: maxMessages
parameters.summary: Maximum number of messages to retrieve. Default is 100.

methods.returns: A task that returns the PullMessagesResponse on success, or null if all fallback attempts fail.

methods.name: BasicSubscriptionRenewAsync
methods.summary: Renews a basic event subscription to extend its lifetime.
methods.remarks: Basic subscriptions have limited lifetimes and must be renewed before expiration to continue receiving events. This extension simplifies renewal by accepting the subscription response object directly. It's recommended to renew subscriptions well before expiration (e.g., at 80% of the timeout period) to account for network delays.

parameters.name: subscribeResponse
parameters.summary: The original subscription response containing the subscription reference.

parameters.name: timeoutInMinutes
parameters.summary: New subscription duration in minutes. Default is 5 minutes.

methods.returns: A task that returns the RenewResponse1 containing the new termination time and current device time.

methods.name: PullPointSubscribeWithFallbackAsync
methods.summary: Creates a pull-point subscription with automatic fallback for better device compatibility.
methods.remarks: This enhanced subscription method provides better compatibility across different ONVIF implementations by trying multiple approaches when the standard method fails. Fallback strategies include: - Trying different timeout formats - Using alternative subscription parameters - Adjusting message filtering options - Handling device-specific quirks This method is particularly useful when: - Working with devices from multiple manufacturers - The standard subscription method fails with timeout errors - Devices have non-standard ONVIF implementations

parameters.name: initialTerminationTimeInMinutes
parameters.summary: Initial subscription duration in minutes. Default is 5 minutes.

methods.returns: A task that returns the CreatePullPointSubscriptionResponse on success, or null if all fallback attempts fail.

classes.name: SimpleOnvifEventListener
classes.summary: Provides a simple HTTP listener for receiving ONVIF event notifications via basic subscriptions.
classes.remarks: This class implements a basic HTTP server that listens for ONVIF event notifications sent by devices using the WS-BaseNotification mechanism. It's designed for simple event subscriptions where the device pushes notifications to a client endpoint. Requirements: - Windows Firewall exception for the listening port - Administrator privileges (or URL reservation via netsh) - Network accessibility from the ONVIF device The listener extracts camera ID from the URL path (e.g., "/1/" for camera 1) and passes the raw event XML to the callback for processing. For production use, consider: - Using pull-point subscriptions instead for better reliability - Implementing proper security (HTTPS, authentication) - Adding error recovery and reconnection logic

classes.name: OnvifHelpers
classes.summary: Provides static helper methods for common ONVIF data format conversions and utilities.
classes.remarks: This utility class contains helper methods for converting between .NET types and ONVIF-specific formats, particularly for XML duration strings and date/time formats. ONVIF uses XML Schema duration format (ISO 8601) for timeouts and intervals: - PT5S = 5 seconds - PT5M = 5 minutes - PT0.5S = 500 milliseconds These helpers simplify working with ONVIF services by handling the format conversions automatically, reducing errors and improving code readability.

classes.name: OnvifProfileSelector
classes.summary: Picks the ONVIF media profile to stream from when the caller did not name one.
classes.remarks: ONVIF does not order profiles by quality, and several vendors list a MJPEG or low-resolution profile first, so the first profile is not a safe default. The codec decides first: H.264 and H.265 rank together above MPEG-4, which ranks above JPEG. Within a codec rank the larger frame wins, then the higher frame rate limit, and on a full tie H.264 is preferred to H.265 for decoder compatibility. A profile without a video encoder configuration ranks last; when no profile on that source has one, the first profile is used. When the caller reports that no H.265 decoder is available, H.265 ranks with the unknown codecs, below JPEG, because a stream that cannot be decoded shows nothing. Only the profiles on the first profile's video source are ranked, so a device with several inputs (an encoder, an NVR, a multi-sensor camera) stays on the input it streamed before rather than switching to another camera.

classes.name: DigestHelpers
classes.summary: Provides helper methods for creating cryptographic digests used in ONVIF authentication.
classes.remarks: This class implements digest algorithms required by: - WS-Security UsernameToken Profile (SOAP digest) - HTTP Digest Authentication RFC 2069 These methods are essential for secure authentication with ONVIF devices, preventing password transmission in plain text and protecting against replay attacks.

methods.name: CalculateNonce
methods.summary: Generates a cryptographically secure random nonce value.
methods.remarks: The nonce (number used once) is a random value included in authentication to ensure uniqueness of each request and prevent replay attacks. The value should be cryptographically random and sufficiently long to avoid collisions.

parameters.name: length
parameters.summary: The length in bytes of the random data to generate. Default is 32 bytes.

methods.returns: A Base64-encoded string containing the random nonce value.

methods.name: CreateSoapDigest
methods.summary: Creates a password digest for WS-Security UsernameToken authentication.
methods.remarks: The digest is calculated as: Base64(SHA-1(nonce + created + password)) where nonce is decoded from Base64 before concatenation. This follows the WS-Security UsernameToken Profile 1.0 specification for PasswordDigest authentication as required by ONVIF.

parameters.name: created
parameters.summary: The creation timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

methods.returns: A Base64-encoded SHA-1 digest of the concatenated values.

methods.name: CreateWebDigestRFC2069
methods.summary: Creates an HTTP digest authentication response according to RFC 2069.
methods.remarks: Implements the basic HTTP Digest authentication algorithm: - HA1 = MD5(username:realm:password) - HA2 = MD5(method:uri) - Response = MD5(HA1:nonce:HA2) This is used for HTTP-level authentication with ONVIF devices that require HTTP Digest authentication in addition to or instead of WS-Security.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.summary: The authentication realm from the server challenge.

parameters.name: nonce
parameters.summary: The nonce value from the server challenge.

methods.returns: The calculated digest response value.

methods.name: CreateWebDigestRFC7616
methods.summary: Creates an HTTP digest authentication response according to RFC 7616 / RFC 2617 with quality-of-protection (qop), client nonce (cnonce) and nonce-count (nc) support.
methods.remarks: Implements the qop-enabled HTTP Digest authentication algorithm: HA1 = MD5(username:realm:password)HA2 = MD5(method:uri)response = MD5(HA1:nonce:nc:cnonce:qop:HA2) Most modern ONVIF cameras advertise qop="auth" in their WWW-Authenticate challenge and require the qop variant. Use only when the server's challenge omits the qop directive (legacy RFC 2069 behaviour). This overload uses MD5 to remain interoperable with the broad installed base of ONVIF cameras. RFC 7616 also defines SHA-256 / SHA-512-256 algorithm variants, which are not covered here — extend with an explicit algorithm parameter if a deployment requires them.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.summary: The authentication realm from the server challenge.

parameters.name: qop
parameters.summary: The quality of protection token, typically "auth" (or "auth-int"; only "auth" is supported by this overload because no entity-body hash is supplied).

parameters.name: cnonce
parameters.summary: The client nonce — a fresh random value chosen per request, returned to the server unchanged.

parameters.name: nc
parameters.summary: The nonce-count, an 8-digit lowercase hex counter that increments per request reusing the same server nonce (e.g. "00000001").

methods.returns: The calculated digest response value (lowercase hex MD5).

classes.name: IHasUtcOffset
classes.summary: Defines a contract for objects that can compensate for time differences between client and device.
classes.remarks: This interface is crucial for ONVIF authentication success when the client and device clocks are not synchronized. WS-Security authentication includes timestamps that must fall within an acceptable window (typically 5 minutes) to be considered valid. Implementing this interface allows authentication components to adjust their timestamps to match the device's clock, preventing authentication failures due to time skew. Common scenarios requiring time offset: - Devices without NTP synchronization - Devices in different time zones incorrectly configured - Network latency causing apparent time differences - Devices with drifting internal clocks

properties.name: UtcNowOffset
properties.summary: Gets or sets the time offset to apply when generating UTC timestamps.
properties.value: The time difference between device time and client time. Positive values indicate the device is ahead of the client. Negative values indicate the device is behind the client.

classes.name: Nonce
classes.summary: Represents the Nonce element within a WS-Security UsernameToken.
classes.remarks: The nonce ("number used once") is a randomly generated value that ensures each UsernameToken is unique, preventing replay attacks where an attacker might capture and reuse authentication credentials. Key characteristics: - Must be cryptographically random - Should be sufficiently long (typically 16-32 bytes) - Base64-encoded for transmission - Combined with timestamp to limit token validity window - Used in password digest calculation The nonce ensures that even with the same username, password, and timestamp, each authentication token will be different.

properties.name: EncodingType
properties.summary: Gets or sets the encoding type of the nonce value.
properties.value: Typically "http://docs.oasis-open.org/wss/2004/01/oasis-200401-wss-soap-message-security-1.0#Base64Binary" to indicate Base64 encoding.

properties.name: Text
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Base64-encoded nonce value.
properties.value: A Base64-encoded string containing the random nonce bytes. Generated using cryptographically secure random number generators.

classes.name: Password
classes.summary: Represents the Password element within a WS-Security UsernameToken.
classes.remarks: This class represents the password component of WS-Security authentication. The password can be transmitted as either plain text or as a digest. For ONVIF compliance, PasswordDigest is strongly recommended over PasswordText to prevent password interception. The digest provides a one-way hash that includes the nonce and timestamp, making it unique for each request. Type attribute values: - PasswordText: Plain text password (not recommended) - PasswordDigest: SHA-1 digest of nonce + created + password (recommended)

properties.name: Type
properties.summary: Gets or sets the password type identifier.
properties.value: The URI identifying the password type: - "http://docs.oasis-open.org/wss/2004/01/oasis-200401-wss-username-token-profile-1.0#PasswordText" for plain text - "http://docs.oasis-open.org/wss/2004/01/oasis-200401-wss-username-token-profile-1.0#PasswordDigest" for digest

properties.name: Text
properties.summary: Gets or sets the password value.
properties.value: For PasswordText type: The plain text password. For PasswordDigest type: Base64-encoded SHA-1 digest.

classes.name: UsernameToken
classes.summary: Represents a WS-Security UsernameToken element for SOAP message authentication.
classes.remarks: This class represents the UsernameToken structure as defined in the WS-Security UsernameToken Profile 1.0 specification. It's used to serialize authentication credentials into SOAP headers for ONVIF communication. The UsernameToken contains: - Username: The user's login name - Password: Either plain text or digest (recommended) - Nonce: Random value to prevent replay attacks - Created: Timestamp to limit token validity This structure is automatically serialized to XML when added to SOAP headers.

properties.summary: Gets or sets the username for authentication.
properties.value: The plain text username.

properties.name: Password
properties.summary: Gets or sets the password information for authentication.
properties.value: A Password object containing the password digest or plain text.

properties.name: Nonce
properties.summary: Gets or sets the nonce (number used once) for preventing replay attacks.
properties.value: A Nonce object containing the Base64-encoded random value.

properties.name: Created
properties.summary: Gets or sets the creation timestamp of the token.
properties.value: The timestamp in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2023-01-01T12:00:00Z").

properties.name: Id
properties.summary: Gets or sets the optional identifier for the UsernameToken.
properties.value: A unique identifier for token reference purposes.

classes.name: WsUsernameTokenBehavior
classes.summary: Implements WS-Security UsernameToken authentication behavior for ONVIF WCF clients.
classes.remarks: This behavior adds WS-Security UsernameToken headers to outgoing SOAP messages as required by the ONVIF specification. It implements the UsernameToken profile with PasswordDigest authentication. The behavior is applied to WCF endpoints to automatically add authentication headers to all outgoing requests. This is the primary authentication mechanism for most ONVIF devices. Time synchronization is critical for this authentication method as the password digest includes a timestamp. Use the UtcNowOffset property to compensate for time differences between client and device.

classes.name: SceneManager
classes.summary: Top-level orchestrator for scene-based video composition. Manages a pool of registered sources, a collection of named scenes, and provides scene switching with animated transitions. Built on top of LiveVideoCompositor (LVC V2) using the bridge architecture.
classes.remarks: The SceneManager follows the "All Sources Always Connected" approach: all registered sources are connected to the mixer at all times with pre-allocated slots. Scene switching only modifies mixer stream properties (alpha, position, z-order) rather than changing the pipeline topology. This ensures zero-glitch, instantaneous scene switches. Key concepts: - Sources are independent and persist across scenes. - Scenes are configurations (named collections of source placements). - Transitions are animations on mixer stream properties. - Studio Mode supports Preview/Program workflow.

classes.summary: Provides a simplified, cross-platform media player implementation using GStreamer's PlayBin3 for easy media playback. This class offers a streamlined interface for basic media playback operations including play, pause, stop, seek, and volume control. Built on top of GStreamer's high-level PlayBin3 element, it automatically handles codec discovery, format negotiation, and pipeline construction. Supports multiple stream types (video, audio, subtitles), stream switching, and provides comprehensive error handling and logging capabilities. Implements the IDisposable. Implements the IAsyncDisposable.

methods.name: Bus_SyncMessage
methods.summary: Handles synchronous bus messages from the GStreamer pipeline, primarily for video overlay window setup.
methods.remarks: This handler is called synchronously during pipeline operation and must return quickly to avoid blocking. It specifically handles the prepare-window-handle message that video sink elements send when they need a window handle for video rendering. Operations performed: - Checks if the message is a video overlay prepare-window-handle message - Sets force-aspect-ratio on the video sink element from the view's RendererSettings.Letterbox - Creates a VideoOverlayAdapter and sets the window handle from the video view - Enables event handling on the video overlay - Properly disposes the message after processing This is critical for integrating video output with platform-specific UI controls.

methods.name: Bus_Message
methods.summary: Handles asynchronous bus messages from the GStreamer pipeline, routing them to specific handlers based on message type.
methods.remarks: This is the main message dispatcher for the GStreamer bus. It receives messages asynchronously from the pipeline and routes them to appropriate handlers based on message type. Handled message types: - : Pipeline state transitions (Playing, Paused, etc.) - : End-of-stream notifications - : Pipeline errors requiring user notification - : Custom application messages - : Stream information discovery Messages are properly disposed after processing to prevent memory leaks. If the playbin is not initialized, messages are ignored.

methods.remarks: This method is called when the PlayBin3 element discovers available streams in the media file. It processes the stream collection and populates the internal stream lists that back the public stream properties. Processing steps: - Parses the stream collection message - Iterates through all streams in the collection - Categorizes streams by type (video, audio, text/subtitles) - Converts GStreamer stream objects to typed StreamInfo objects - Publishes complete snapshots atomically (readers never see a mid-update list) - Logs each discovered stream for debugging - Raises event when parsing is complete After this method completes, the , , and properties are populated with available streams.

Application messages provide a mechanism for elements to communicate application-specific information that doesn't fit standard GStreamer message types.

methods.remarks: This handler is called when any element in the pipeline posts an error message. Errors typically indicate unrecoverable failures that prevent continued playback. Error handling steps: - Parses error message and debug information from the message - Raises event with formatted error details including source element name - Transitions the pipeline to Ready state to stop playback gracefully Common error sources: - Missing codecs or plugins - Network connectivity issues (for streaming media) - Corrupted or invalid media files - Hardware decoder failures - I/O errors reading media files After an error, the player should be stopped and can be restarted with new media.

parameters.name: bus

methods.name: StartAsync
methods.summary: Starts media playback asynchronously with the specified settings.
methods.remarks: This method creates a GStreamer PlayBin3 pipeline, configures it with the specified settings, and starts playback on a background thread. The PlayBin3 element automatically handles format detection, codec selection, and stream management. Use this method when you need to start playback without blocking the calling thread. Subscribe to OnError event to handle playback errors.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The universal source settings containing media URI and playback configuration.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if playback started successfully; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Start
methods.summary: Starts media playback synchronously with the specified settings.
methods.remarks: This method performs the following operations: - Creates a new PlayBin3 element instance - Configures the media URI from settings - Optionally configures audio stream mixing if is enabled - Attaches bus message handlers for error and state change notifications - Invokes video view initialization - Transitions the pipeline to Playing state This is a synchronous operation that blocks until the pipeline state change completes. For non-blocking operation, use instead.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The universal source settings containing media URI and playback configuration.

methods.returns: true if the GStreamer pipeline was created and started successfully; false if pipeline initialization or state change failed.

methods.name: StopAsync
methods.summary: Stops media playback asynchronously and releases GStreamer resources.
methods.remarks: This method transitions the GStreamer pipeline to Null state, disposes the PlayBin3 element, and sets the player state to Free. If the player is already stopped (State is Free), the method returns immediately. Use this method when you need to stop playback without blocking the calling thread.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if playback was stopped successfully; false if the player was already in Free state.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops media playback synchronously and releases GStreamer resources.
methods.remarks: This method performs the following operations: - Sets the async flag to false - Transitions the GStreamer pipeline to Null state (if active) - Disposes the PlayBin3 element and releases resources - Sets the player state to Free This is a synchronous operation that blocks until cleanup completes. For non-blocking operation, use StopAsync instead.
methods.returns: Always returns true. This method does not fail if resources are already released.

methods.name: DurationAsync
methods.summary: Gets the total duration of the currently playing media asynchronously.
methods.remarks: Duration may not be available for live streams or certain streaming protocols. The duration is queried from the GStreamer pipeline and may not be accurate for files with variable bitrate or incomplete index.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains the media duration, or Zero if duration cannot be determined.

methods.name: Position_GetAsync
methods.summary: Gets the current playback position asynchronously.
methods.remarks: The position represents the elapsed time from the start of the media. Position updates continuously during playback and can be used for displaying time information or progress bars. For live streams, the returned position may represent buffered data position rather than actual broadcast time.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains the current playback position, or Zero if position cannot be determined.

methods.name: Position_Get
methods.summary: Gets the current playback position synchronously.
methods.remarks: This method queries the GStreamer pipeline for the current time position. The position is converted from nanoseconds (GStreamer's internal time unit) to milliseconds. Position accuracy depends on the media format and seeking capabilities of the source.
methods.returns: The current playback position as a TimeSpan, or Zero if no media is loaded or position query fails.

methods.name: Position_SetAsync
methods.summary: Seeks to a specific position in the media asynchronously.
methods.remarks: Seeking to a keyframe is faster but may result in a position slightly different from the requested position. Frame-accurate seeking is slower but positions more precisely at the requested time. Not all media formats support accurate seeking. Errors during seeking are reported via the OnError event.

parameters.name: position
parameters.summary: The target playback position to seek to.

parameters.name: seekToKeyframe
parameters.summary: True to seek to the nearest keyframe (faster but less accurate); false for frame-accurate seeking.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous seek operation.

methods.name: Position_Set
methods.summary: Seeks to a specific position in the media synchronously.
methods.remarks: This method performs a seek operation with flush semantics, clearing buffered data before seeking. When seekToKeyframe is true, the flag is added to snap to the nearest keyframe. Keyframe seeking is recommended for: - Quick navigation in large files - Live stream rewind operations - Preview thumbnails generation Frame-accurate seeking is recommended for: - Precise editing operations - Subtitle synchronization - Frame-by-frame analysis If the seek operation fails, an error is raised via event.

parameters.name: position
parameters.summary: The target playback position to seek to.

parameters.name: seekToKeyframe
parameters.summary: True to seek to the nearest keyframe (faster but less accurate); false for frame-accurate seeking.

methods.name: PauseAsync
methods.summary: Pauses media playback asynchronously.
methods.remarks: When paused, the player maintains its current position and can be resumed with ResumeAsync or Resume. Audio and video output are suspended, but buffered data is retained. The player state transitions to Pause.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous pause operation.

methods.name: Pause
methods.summary: Pauses media playback synchronously.
methods.remarks: This method transitions the GStreamer pipeline to Paused state, suspending audio and video output while maintaining current position. The player state is updated to Pause before the pipeline state change. If the state change fails, an error is raised via OnError event and the method returns false.
methods.returns: true if the pipeline was successfully paused; false if no media is loaded or the state change failed.

methods.name: ResumeAsync
methods.summary: Resumes paused media playback asynchronously.
methods.remarks: This method resumes playback from the position where it was paused. It should only be called when the player is in Pause state. After resuming, the player state transitions to Play.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous resume operation.

methods.name: Resume
methods.summary: Resumes paused media playback synchronously.
methods.remarks: This method transitions the GStreamer pipeline from Paused state back to Playing state. The player state is updated to Play before the pipeline state change. If the state change fails, an error is raised via OnError event and the method returns false. Playback continues from the position where it was paused.
methods.returns: true if the pipeline was successfully resumed; false if no media is loaded or the state change failed.

methods.name: Duration
methods.summary: Gets the total duration of the currently playing media synchronously.
methods.remarks: This method queries the GStreamer pipeline for the media duration in nanoseconds and converts it to milliseconds. Duration may be unavailable or inaccurate for: - Live streams (returns zero or maximum value) - Files with incomplete or missing index information - Certain streaming protocols that don't provide duration metadata If the duration query fails, an error is raised via OnError event.
methods.returns: The total media duration as a TimeSpan, or Zero if no media is loaded or duration query fails.

methods.summary: Gets the index of the currently playing audio stream.
