methods.summary: Starts the video capture process.
methods.returns: true if the capture started successfully, false otherwise.

methods.name: StartAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously starts the video capture process.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if the capture started successfully, false otherwise.

methods.name: Pause
methods.summary: Pauses the video capture. The capture session remains active and can be resumed.
methods.returns: true if the capture was paused successfully, false otherwise.

methods.name: PauseAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously pauses the video capture.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if the capture was paused successfully, false otherwise.

methods.name: Resume
methods.summary: Resumes a paused video capture.
methods.returns: true if the capture was resumed successfully, false otherwise.

methods.name: ResumeAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously resumes a paused video capture.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if the capture was resumed successfully, false otherwise.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops the video capture and finalizes any output files.

methods.name: StopAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously stops the video capture.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous stop operation.

methods.name: Duration
methods.summary: Gets the duration of the current capture session.
methods.returns: A TimeSpan representing the elapsed time since the capture started.

methods.name: DurationAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously gets the duration of the current capture session.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains a TimeSpan representing the elapsed time.

methods.name: State
methods.summary: Gets the current state of the capture component (e.g., Capturing, Paused, Stopped).
methods.returns: The current PlaybackState.

methods.name: Volume_Set
methods.summary: Sets the audio volume for the capture source.

parameters.name: volume
parameters.summary: The volume level, typically from 0.0 (silent) to 1.0 (full volume). Values can sometimes exceed 1.0 for amplification.

methods.name: Volume_Get
methods.summary: Gets the current audio volume for the capture source.
methods.returns: The current volume level.

classes.name: IVideoEffectsControls
classes.summary: Defines a standard set of controls for applying basic real-time video effects. This interface provides methods to adjust common image properties such as brightness, contrast, and saturation, as well as apply simple transformations like grayscale, flip, and invert.
classes.remarks: This interface is intended to be implemented by components that handle video rendering or processing, such as media players or video capture controls. It provides a unified way to manipulate the visual appearance of the video stream in real-time. Effects are typically applied using GPU shaders or image processing filters for optimal performance. All effect values are multiplicative or boolean - brightness/contrast/saturation typically use 1.0 as the neutral value. Effects can be stacked and are generally applied in the order they are set. The VideoEffects_Clear method resets all effects to their default neutral state. These effects are applied before rendering and do not modify the source video data when recording.

methods.name: VideoEffects_SetBrightness
methods.summary: Sets the brightness level of the video.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: The brightness value. Typically, 1.0 is the default; values greater than 1.0 increase brightness, and values less than 1.0 decrease it.

methods.name: VideoEffects_SetContrast
methods.summary: Sets the contrast level of the video.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: The contrast value. Typically, 1.0 is the default; values greater than 1.0 increase contrast, and values less than 1.0 decrease it.

methods.name: VideoEffects_SetSaturation
methods.summary: Sets the color saturation level of the video.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: The saturation value. Typically, 1.0 is the default; 0.0 results in a grayscale image, and values greater than 1.0 intensify colors.

methods.name: VideoEffects_SetGrayscale
methods.summary: Toggles the grayscale effect on the video.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: If set to true, the video is rendered in grayscale; otherwise, it is rendered in color.

methods.name: VideoEffects_SetFlipX
methods.summary: Toggles a horizontal flip (mirror) effect on the video.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: If set to true, the video is flipped horizontally.

methods.name: VideoEffects_SetFlipY
methods.summary: Toggles a vertical flip effect on the video.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: If set to true, the video is flipped vertically.

methods.name: VideoEffects_SetInvert
methods.summary: Toggles the color inversion effect on the video.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: If set to true, the video colors are inverted (like a photo negative).

methods.name: VideoEffects_Clear
methods.summary: Resets all video effects to their default values.

classes.name: IVideoView
classes.summary: Defines a platform-agnostic interface for a video rendering view. This interface abstracts the underlying UI control used for displaying video, allowing the core engine to remain independent of any specific UI framework (e.g., WinForms, WPF, Android, iOS).
classes.remarks: Implementations of this interface are responsible for managing a native UI element that can render video frames. It provides methods for lifecycle management, UI interaction, and event handling, including mouse input. The interface includes platform-specific sections to handle the unique requirements of different operating systems.

properties.name: RendererSettings
properties.summary: Gets or sets the settings of the renderer that draws into this view.

methods.name: Attach
methods.summary: Attaches this view to a parent core engine component.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.summary: The core engine component (e.g., MediaPlayerCore, VideoCaptureCore) to attach to.

methods.name: Detach
methods.summary: Detaches this view from a parent core engine component.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.summary: The core engine component to detach from.

methods.name: GetUIEngine
methods.summary: Gets the underlying UI engine being used by the view.
methods.returns: The VideoViewUIEngine used for rendering.

methods.name: GetBackgroundColor
methods.summary: Gets the background color of the video view.
methods.returns: The background color as an SKColor.

methods.name: InvokeVideoRendererUpdate
methods.summary: Triggers an update of the video renderer.

methods.name: InvokeStart
methods.summary: Signals the view that the engine has started.

methods.name: InvokeStartComplete
methods.summary: Signals the view that the engine has completed its start sequence.

methods.name: InvokeStop
methods.summary: Signals the view that the engine has stopped.

methods.name: GetHandle
methods.summary: Gets the native window handle of the underlying UI control.
methods.returns: An IntPtr representing the window handle.

methods.name: SetHandle
methods.summary: Sets the native window handle. Used for embedding the video in a specific control.

methods.name: GetSize
methods.summary: Gets the current size of the video view.
methods.returns: The size as a Size structure.

methods.name: ClearUI
methods.summary: Clears the user interface, removing any overlays or graphics.

methods.name: LogDialogError
methods.summary: Displays an error message in a dialog box.
methods.remarks: An SDK engine calls this from inside its own error handler, which the logger raises. An implementation that logs from here - including from a catch - therefore feeds the error back into the channel that is currently reporting it, and without something to stop it the process dies of a stack overflow (issue #1173). The SDK breaks that loop centrally, with a re-entrancy guard in the log observer, but the guard is per thread and covers only the call it is inside: a write made synchronously, on the thread this method was called on, is safe. A view that marshals to its UI thread first - DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue, Dispatcher.BeginInvoke, Control.BeginInvoke, Task.Run - runs its catch on a fresh stack where the guard is already clear, and must not log from there. Report that failure on a channel the SDK does not observe, such as Trace.TraceError. Keep this method cheap and make it return even when it cannot show anything.

methods.name: LogDialogClose
methods.summary: Closes the log dialog if it is open.

methods.name: LogDialogClear
methods.summary: Clears all messages from the log dialog.

methods.name: ShowMessage
methods.summary: Shows a message box to the user.
methods.remarks: Reached from an engine's error handler as well - see the remarks on String).
methods.returns: A MessageBoxResult indicating which button the user clicked.

methods.name: ResizeRoundTo
methods.summary: Resizes the video view, rounding the dimensions to a specified value.

parameters.name: round
parameters.summary: The value to round the dimensions to (e.g., 16).

methods.name: CallRefresh
methods.summary: Forces the view to redraw or refresh its content.

methods.name: CallInvoke
methods.summary: Executes a delegate on the UI thread of the control.

parameters.name: args
parameters.summary: The arguments to pass to the delegate.

methods.name: GetIsHandleCreated
methods.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the underlying UI control's handle has been created.
methods.returns: true if the handle is created; otherwise, false.

methods.name: GetInvokeRequired
methods.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the caller must use an invoke method when making calls to the control.
methods.returns: true if the call must be invoked; otherwise, false.

methods.name: PictureBoxCreate
methods.summary: Creates a PictureBox control for video rendering.

methods.name: PictureBoxDestroy
methods.summary: Destroys the PictureBox control.

methods.name: PictureBoxSetImage
methods.summary: Sets the image to be displayed in the PictureBox. The view takes ownership of image and disposes it: the WinForms view when the image is replaced or the picture box goes away, the WPF view at once (it shows a copy), and any view at once when it cannot show it. Do not dispose or reuse a bitmap after passing it here.

methods.name: PictureBoxGetImage
methods.summary: Gets a copy of the image the PictureBox shows. The copy belongs to the caller, who disposes it; the image the view shows stays the view's.
methods.returns: A new bitmap, or null when the view shows none.

methods.name: PictureBoxExists
methods.summary: Checks if the PictureBox control currently exists.
methods.returns: true if the PictureBox exists; otherwise, false.

methods.name: PushMouseMove
methods.summary: Pushes a mouse move event to the control for processing.

methods.name: PushMouseButtonDown
methods.summary: Pushes a mouse button down event to the control.

parameters.name: button
parameters.summary: The mouse button that was pressed.

methods.name: PushMouseButtonUp
methods.summary: Pushes a mouse button up event to the control.

parameters.name: button
parameters.summary: The mouse button that was released.

events.name: OnMouseButtonDown
events.summary: Occurs when a mouse button is pressed down over the control.

events.name: OnMouseButtonUp
events.summary: Occurs when a mouse button is released over the control.

events.name: OnMouseMoved
events.summary: Occurs when the mouse pointer is moved over the control.

classes.name: IVideoViewNativeRendering
classes.summary: Defines an interface for video view components that support switching to a native rendering backend. This is typically used to improve performance in demanding scenarios, such as playing high-resolution (4K/8K) video or using hardware-accelerated GPU decoding.
classes.remarks: When native rendering is enabled, the video is rendered directly by the underlying system's graphics API (e.g., DirectX, OpenGL) instead of through a higher-level UI framework like WPF. This can significantly reduce CPU usage and improve rendering smoothness, especially for high-bitrate or high-resolution content. However, native rendering may have implications for UI integration, such as difficulty in layering UI elements on top of the video, as the video surface may be rendered in a separate composition layer. Native rendering is particularly beneficial when combined with hardware decoding (DXVA, NVDEC, Quick Sync) as it allows for a direct GPU-to-GPU pipeline without CPU involvement. In WPF applications, enabling native rendering typically creates an HWND-based video surface rather than using WPF's composition engine. This mode should be preferred for performance-critical applications or when frame drops are observed with standard WPF rendering.

methods.name: SetNativeRendering
methods.summary: Enables or disables native rendering for the video view.
methods.remarks: It is recommended to enable this for performance-critical applications, such as those involving GPU-accelerated decoding or ultra-high-definition video.

parameters.name: native
parameters.summary: Set to true to enable native rendering; false to use the default framework rendering (e.g., WPF).

classes.name: IVideoViewPushFrame
classes.summary: Defines an interface for video views that support direct pushing of video frames for rendering. This interface is crucial for scenarios where raw video data needs to be displayed without relying on a traditional media pipeline (e.g., for custom video processing or real-time frame injection).
classes.remarks: Implementations of this interface are responsible for taking raw video frame data and rendering it efficiently to the display. This allows for fine-grained control over the video rendering process and is essential for custom video processing pipelines. The interface supports two frame types: legacy VideoFrame for backwards compatibility, and VideoFrameX for the newer MediaBlocks framework. Push frame rendering bypasses normal playback synchronization, making it suitable for real-time applications where the caller controls frame timing. Common use cases include computer vision applications that need to display processed frames, custom video generators, screen sharing implementations, or bridging between different media frameworks. When using this interface, the caller is responsible for frame timing and synchronization. The caller keeps ownership of a pushed frame. A view reads the frame's memory only during the call and copies whatever it needs later, and it never frees the frame. The caller can free or reuse the memory as soon as the call returns, and must free a frame it allocated: frames have no finalizer. This also holds for a frame the view drops, for example because it is stopped or its queue is full.

methods.name: PushFrame
methods.summary: Pushes a VideoFrame to the view for rendering. This method is typically used for raw video frames that conform to the legacy VideoFrame structure.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: The VideoFrame containing the video data to be rendered. The caller keeps ownership and can free it when this method returns.

methods.name: PushFrame
methods.summary: Pushes a VideoFrameX to the view for rendering. This method is used for video frames generated by the MediaBlocks engine, offering more advanced frame metadata.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: The VideoFrameX containing the video data and extended metadata to be rendered. The caller keeps ownership and can free it when this method returns.

classes.name: IVRVideoControl
classes.summary: Defines an interface for controlling Virtual Reality (VR) video playback parameters. This interface allows manipulation of camera orientation (yaw, pitch, roll), field of view, and the VR projection mode.
classes.remarks: Implementations of this interface are typically found in video renderers or effects that support 360-degree or VR video content. It enables interactive viewing of immersive video by adjusting the viewer's perspective within the virtual environment. Yaw controls horizontal rotation (looking left/right), pitch controls vertical rotation (looking up/down), and roll controls tilting. Field of view determines how zoomed in or out the view appears - smaller values create a telephoto effect, larger values create a wide-angle effect. The Mode property determines how the 2D video source is projected into 3D space (equirectangular for 360° videos, cubemap for better quality at poles, or normal for standard video). Different VR modes may be supported by different components - use IsModeSupported to check compatibility before setting the mode. The SettingsChanged event notifies listeners when any VR parameters change, useful for synchronizing UI controls.

properties.name: Yaw
properties.summary: Gets or sets the yaw (left/right rotation) of the VR camera in degrees.
properties.value: The yaw angle.

properties.name: Pitch
properties.summary: Gets or sets the pitch (up/down rotation) of the VR camera in degrees.
properties.value: The pitch angle.

properties.name: Roll
properties.summary: Gets or sets the roll (tilt) of the VR camera in degrees.
properties.value: The roll angle.

properties.name: FieldOfView
properties.summary: Gets or sets the field of view (FOV) of the VR camera in degrees. This controls the zoom level or how much of the scene is visible.
properties.value: The field of view angle.

properties.name: Mode
properties.summary: Gets or sets the current VR projection mode.
properties.value: The VRMode.

methods.name: IsModeSupported
methods.summary: Checks if a specific VR mode is supported by the implementing component (e.g., video block, effect, or renderer).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.summary: The VRMode to check for support.

methods.returns: true if the mode is supported; otherwise, false.

events.name: SettingsChanged
events.summary: Occurs when any of the VR control settings (Yaw, Pitch, Roll, FieldOfView, Mode) have changed.

classes.name: AudioStreamInfo
classes.summary: Represents detailed information about an audio stream within a media file. This class provides properties such as bitrate, channels, sample rate, codec, and duration.
classes.remarks: This information is typically retrieved by a media information parser and is useful for displaying stream properties to the user, or for making decisions about audio processing and playback. The class provides both basic audio characteristics (channels, sample rate) and advanced metadata (codec info, language, tags). Bitrate is provided in bits per second and helps determine file size and quality. The Channels property indicates audio configuration: 1=mono, 2=stereo, 6=5.1 surround, 8=7.1 surround, etc. ChannelMask provides detailed speaker position information for multi-channel audio. SampleRate is measured in Hz with common values being 44100 (CD quality), 48000 (DVD/professional), or 96000 (high-resolution audio). The Tags collection contains stream-specific metadata that may differ from file-level tags. This information is essential for audio format validation, stream selection in multi-audio files, and transcoding decisions.

constructors.name: AudioStreamInfo
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the AudioStreamInfo class. All string properties are initialized to Empty, Duration to Zero, and Tags as an empty list.

properties.name: Bitrate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the average bitrate of the audio stream in bits per second (bps).

properties.name: Channels
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of audio channels (e.g., 1 for mono, 2 for stereo, 6 for 5.1 surround).

properties.name: ChannelMask
properties.summary: Gets or sets the channel mask, indicating the speaker positions for multi-channel audio.

properties.name: SampleRate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the sample rate of the audio stream in Hertz (Hz). Common values include 44100 Hz (CD quality) or 48000 Hz.

properties.name: BPS
properties.summary: Gets or sets the bits per sample (bit depth) of the audio data.

properties.name: Codec
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the audio codec (e.g., "AAC", "MP3", "AC3").

properties.name: CodecInfo
properties.summary: Gets or sets additional information about the audio codec, such as profile or specific encoder details.

properties.name: Duration
properties.summary: Gets or sets the duration of the audio stream.

properties.name: Language
properties.summary: Gets or sets the language of the audio stream, typically represented by a two-letter ISO 639-1 code (e.g., "en", "fr").

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the audio track, if available (e.g., "Director's Commentary").

properties.name: ID
properties.summary: Gets or sets a unique identifier for the audio stream within the media file.

properties.name: Tags
properties.summary: Gets a list of MediaInfoTag objects associated with this audio stream. These tags can include metadata like title, artist, album, etc.

methods.name: ToString
methods.summary: Returns a string that represents the current AudioStreamInfo instance. The string includes the codec, number of channels, sample rate, and duration.
methods.returns: A String that represents this instance.

methods.name: Clone
methods.summary: Returns a copy with its own Tags list, so a published stream list does not alias the source media info.

classes.name: MediaContainerInfo
classes.summary: Represents detailed information about the media container format of a file. This includes the overall duration of the media and any associated tags.
classes.remarks: This class is typically populated by a media information parser and provides high-level details about the media file itself, rather than individual streams within it. Container formats (MP4, MKV, AVI, MOV, WebM, FLV) encapsulate multiple elementary streams (video, audio, subtitles) with synchronization information. Duration property indicates the total playback time of the longest stream in the container. Format property identifies the container type, which determines supported features and codec compatibility. Tags collection contains file-level metadata like title, artist, album, creation date, encoder, and copyright information. Container-level tags differ from stream-specific tags and apply to the entire file. Some containers support chapters, attachments (fonts, cover art), and complex metadata structures. Understanding container format is essential for compatibility checking, transcoding decisions, and metadata management. The ToString method provides a summary of container information for logging and debugging. Container information is fundamental for media library management, file inspection tools, and transcoding workflows.

constructors.name: MediaContainerInfo
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MediaContainerInfo class. The Tags list is initialized as an empty list.

properties.name: Duration
properties.summary: Gets or sets the total duration of the media contained within this container.

properties.name: Tags
properties.summary: Gets a list of MediaInfoTag objects associated with the media container. These tags can include general metadata about the file, such as title, artist, or genre.

properties.name: Format
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the media container format (e.g., "AVI", "MP4", "MKV").

methods.name: ToString
methods.summary: Returns a string that represents the current MediaContainerInfo instance. The string includes the container format and its duration.
methods.returns: A String that represents this instance.

classes.name: MediaFileInfo
classes.summary: Provides comprehensive information about a media file, including details about its container, video streams, audio streams, subtitle streams, and RTP streams.
classes.remarks: This class serves as a central repository for all parsed metadata from a media file. It is typically populated by a media information parser and is essential for applications that need to display detailed file properties, select specific streams for playback or processing, or analyze media content. The Container property provides format-level information such as duration and container type (MP4, AVI, MKV, etc.). Stream collections (VideoStreams, AudioStreams, SubtitleStreams, RTPStreams) contain detailed properties for each elementary stream. Media files can contain multiple streams of each type (e.g., multiple audio tracks for different languages). The IsLive property indicates real-time sources like cameras or network streams, which affects buffering and seeking behavior. GetAudioInfo and GetVideoInfo methods provide quick access to the primary stream information in platform-native formats. The ToString method generates a human-readable summary of all detected streams. This class is thread-safe for reading after initialization, but modifications should be synchronized. Used extensively for stream selection, transcoding planning, and media player initialization.

constructors.name: MediaFileInfo
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MediaFileInfo class. All stream lists and the container info are initialized to empty instances.

properties.name: Container
properties.summary: Gets the MediaContainerInfo for the media file. This contains overall information about the file's container format and duration.

properties.name: VideoStreams
properties.summary: Gets a list of VideoStreamInfo objects, each representing a video stream found in the media file.

properties.name: AudioStreams
properties.summary: Gets a list of AudioStreamInfo objects, each representing an audio stream found in the media file.

properties.name: SubtitleStreams
properties.summary: Gets a list of SubtitleStreamInfo objects, each representing a subtitle stream found in the media file.

properties.name: RTPStreams
properties.summary: Gets a list of RTPStreamInfo objects, each representing an RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol) stream found in the media file.

properties.name: IsLive
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the media source is live (e.g., a live stream from a camera or network).

methods.name: ToString
methods.summary: Returns a string that represents the current MediaFileInfo instance. The string includes summary information about the container and all detected video and audio streams.
methods.returns: A String that represents this instance.

methods.name: GetAudioInfo
methods.summary: Retrieves audio information in the AudioInfoX format from the first available audio stream.
methods.returns: An AudioInfoX object if an audio stream is present; otherwise, null.

methods.name: GetVideoInfo
methods.summary: Retrieves video information in the VideoFrameInfoX format from the first available video stream.
methods.returns: A VideoFrameInfoX object if a video stream is present; otherwise, null.

methods.name: Clear
methods.summary: Clears all stream information and resets the container information to its default empty state.

classes.name: MediaInfoTag
classes.summary: Represents a single metadata tag associated with a media file or stream. This class stores a key-value pair for a specific piece of information.
classes.remarks: Media tags can include various details such as title, artist, album, genre, creation date, and more. They are typically retrieved from media containers by a media information parser. Tag names are usually standardized strings like "title", "artist", "album", "genre", "date", "comment", "encoder". Values are stored as strings but may represent different data types (text, numbers, dates) requiring parsing. Tags can exist at container level (applying to entire file) or stream level (specific to video/audio/subtitle tracks). Common tag standards include ID3 (MP3), Vorbis Comments (OGG/FLAC), iTunes tags (MP4), and APE tags. Tag availability and format depends on the container type and encoder that created the file. Applications use tags for media library organization, search, display, and metadata editing. The ToString method formats tags as "Name: Value" for easy logging and display. Tags are read-only after parsing but can be modified and written back using appropriate media editing APIs.

constructors.name: MediaInfoTag
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MediaInfoTag class with a specified name and value.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name or key of the metadata tag (e.g., "Title", "Artist", "Genre").

properties.name: Value
properties.summary: Gets or sets the value associated with the metadata tag.

methods.name: ToString
methods.summary: Returns a string that represents the current MediaInfoTag instance in the format "Name: Value".
methods.returns: A String that represents this instance.

classes.name: RTPStreamInfo
classes.summary: Represents detailed information about an RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol) stream. This class provides properties such as encoding name, payload type, and stream type.
classes.remarks: RTP streams are commonly used for real-time media transmission over IP networks. This information is typically retrieved by a media information parser and is useful for configuring RTP receivers or analyzing network streams. RTP is the standard protocol for delivering audio and video over IP networks in real-time applications. EncodingName identifies the codec or format (H264, H265, VP8, VP9, PCMU, PCMA, Opus, AAC, etc.). Payload type is a 7-bit identifier (0-127) mapping to the encoding format in RTP packets. Standard payload types (0-95) are defined in RFC 3551, while dynamic types (96-127) require SDP negotiation. Type property (from CapsType) indicates whether the stream carries video, audio, or other data. RTP stream info is essential for RTSP clients, SIP applications, WebRTC implementations, and IP camera integration. Understanding RTP parameters enables proper decoder selection, jitter buffer configuration, and quality monitoring. RTP streams typically require companion RTCP (RTP Control Protocol) for quality feedback and synchronization. Applications use this information for stream selection, codec negotiation, and dynamic RTP handling.

properties.name: EncodingName
properties.summary: Gets or sets the encoding name of the RTP stream (e.g., "H264", "PCMU", "MPEG4-GENERIC").

properties.name: Payload
properties.summary: Gets or sets the payload type ID of the RTP stream. This identifies the type of data carried by the RTP packets (e.g., 96 for custom video, 0 for PCMU audio).

properties.name: Type
properties.summary: Gets or sets the type of the RTP stream, typically indicating if it's video, audio, or other data.

classes.name: SubtitleStreamInfo
classes.summary: Represents detailed information about a subtitle stream within a media file. This class provides properties such as offset, track name, codec, and language.
classes.remarks: This information is typically retrieved by a media information parser and is useful for displaying subtitle properties to the user, or for selecting specific subtitle tracks for rendering. Subtitle streams provide text overlays synchronized with video content for translation, accessibility, or additional information. Name property provides a human-readable track title (e.g., "English", "Director's Commentary", "SDH"). Codec identifies the subtitle format: text-based (SRT, SSA, ASS, WebVTT) or image-based (VobSub, PGS, DVB). Language typically uses ISO 639-1 two-letter codes (en, es, fr) or ISO 639-2 three-letter codes for less common languages. Offset property may indicate timing offset or stream position, with interpretation depending on container format. ID provides unique stream identification within the file for precise track selection. Tags collection contains stream-specific metadata like title, language name, or forced/default flags. Text-based subtitles support styling, positioning, and effects (SSA/ASS), while image-based subtitles provide pixel-perfect rendering. Applications use this information for subtitle track selection, language filtering, and subtitle rendering configuration. Accessibility considerations include supporting SDH (Subtitles for Deaf and Hard of hearing) and closed captions.

constructors.name: SubtitleStreamInfo
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the SubtitleStreamInfo class. All string properties are initialized to Empty, and Tags as an empty list.

properties.name: Offset
properties.summary: Gets or sets the offset of the subtitle stream within the media file. The meaning of this offset can vary depending on the subtitle format.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the subtitle track, if available (e.g., "English Subtitles", "For the hearing impaired").

properties.name: ID
properties.summary: Gets or sets a unique identifier for the subtitle stream within the media file.

properties.name: Codec
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the subtitle codec or format (e.g., "SRT", "ASS", "VobSub").

properties.name: RawCapsName
properties.summary: The caps structure name the media info reader saw this stream under (e.g. subpicture/x-dvb), or when it could not tell. Internal on purpose: it is a GStreamer detail. The demuxer source and the demuxer source block use it to agree on which subtitle streams can actually be decoded, so a subtitle output pad is never published that nothing feeds (issue #1414). A missing value reads as "not decodable".

properties.name: Language
properties.summary: Gets or sets the language of the subtitle stream, typically represented by a two-letter ISO 639-1 code (e.g., "en", "fr").

properties.name: Tags
properties.summary: Gets a list of MediaInfoTag objects associated with this subtitle stream. These tags can include metadata specific to the subtitle track.

methods.name: Clone
methods.summary: Returns a copy with its own Tags list, so a published stream list does not alias the source media info.

classes.name: VideoStreamInfo
classes.summary: Represents detailed information about a video stream within a media file. This class provides properties such as bitrate, frame rate, codec, dimensions, and duration.
classes.remarks: This information is typically retrieved by a media information parser and is useful for displaying stream properties to the user, or for making decisions about video processing, playback, and transcoding. The class provides comprehensive video characteristics including resolution (Width/Height), codec information, frame rate, and interlacing status. Bitrate is provided in bits per second and helps estimate quality and bandwidth requirements. FrameRate is expressed using the VideoFrameRate type and may include fractional values for NTSC formats (e.g., 29.97, 23.976). The IsInterlaced property indicates whether the video uses interlaced scanning (common in broadcast formats) versus progressive scanning. Rotation property indicates if the video requires display rotation (common in mobile recordings): 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees. AspectRatio provides the display aspect ratio which may differ from the pixel aspect ratio (Width/Height). BitsPerPixel indicates color depth and can affect quality and file size. The Tags collection contains stream-specific metadata useful for stream identification in multi-track files. This information is essential for compatibility checks, playback optimization, and determining appropriate transcoding parameters.

constructors.name: VideoStreamInfo
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VideoStreamInfo class. All string properties are initialized to Empty, Duration to Zero, Tags as an empty list, and FrameRate to an empty VideoFrameRate.

properties.name: Bitrate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the average bitrate of the video stream in bits per second (bps).

properties.name: FrameRate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the frame rate of the video stream.

properties.name: Codec
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the video codec (e.g., "H264", "MPEG2", "MPEG4", "VP9").

properties.name: Duration
properties.summary: Gets or sets the duration of the video stream.

properties.name: FourCC
properties.summary: Gets or sets the FourCC code of the video format (e.g., "H264", "XVID").

properties.name: MPEGAudioTag
properties.summary: Gets or sets the MPEG audio tag, if applicable (e.g., for MPEG program streams).

properties.name: Width
properties.summary: Gets or sets the width of the video frame in pixels.

properties.name: Height
properties.summary: Gets or sets the height of the video frame in pixels.

properties.name: FramesCount
properties.summary: Gets or sets the total number of frames in the video stream. This property may not always be available or accurate for all formats.

properties.name: Rotation
properties.summary: Gets or sets the rotation of the video stream in degrees (e.g., 0, 90, 180, 270). Represents only the rotation component of an image-orientation tag; check IsHorizontallyFlipped to distinguish a plain rotation from a flip-then-rotate orientation (e.g. "flip-rotate-90").

properties.name: IsHorizontallyFlipped
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the video stream's image-orientation tag includes the horizontal-flip component of GStreamer's flip-rotate form (e.g. "flip-horizontal", "flip-rotate-90", "flip-rotate-180", "flip-vertical").

properties.name: IsInterlaced
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the video stream is interlaced. true if interlaced, false if progressive, and null if the information is not available.

properties.name: AspectRatio
properties.summary: Gets or sets the aspect ratio of the video, represented as a tuple of width-to-height ratio. For example, (16, 9) for widescreen video.

properties.name: ParNumerator
properties.summary: Gets or sets the pixel aspect ratio numerator. Defaults to 1 (square pixels); anamorphic sources report the ratio their pixels must be stretched by for correct display.

properties.name: ParDenominator
properties.summary: Gets or sets the pixel aspect ratio denominator. Defaults to 1 (square pixels); anamorphic sources report the ratio their pixels must be stretched by for correct display.

properties.name: Tags
properties.summary: Gets a list of MediaInfoTag objects associated with this video stream. These tags can include metadata specific to the video track.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the video track, if available (e.g., "Main Video", "Chapter 1").

properties.name: ID
properties.summary: Gets or sets a unique identifier for the video stream within the media file.

methods.name: ToString
methods.summary: Returns a string that represents the current VideoStreamInfo instance. The string includes the codec, resolution (widthxheight), and frame rate.
methods.returns: A String that represents this instance.

methods.name: Clone
methods.summary: Returns a copy with its own Tags list, so a published stream list does not alias the source media info.

classes.name: DVDAudioAttributes
classes.summary: Represents the complete set of attributes for a DVD audio stream, including format, language, and technical specifications.
classes.remarks: This structure encapsulates all the metadata associated with a DVD audio track as defined in the DVD-Video specification. It provides comprehensive information about the audio stream's encoding, language settings, and technical parameters. This information is typically extracted from the DVD's IFO (Information) files and is used by media players to properly decode and present audio options to users.

properties.name: AppMode
properties.summary: Gets or sets the application mode that indicates the special purpose or features of this audio track.
properties.value: The application mode such as karaoke, surround, or standard playback.

properties.name: AppModeData
properties.summary: Gets or sets additional data specific to the application mode.
properties.value: Application-specific data byte that provides extra configuration for the AppMode.

properties.name: AudioFormat
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio encoding format used for this track.
properties.value: The audio format such as AC3, DTS, LPCM, or MPEG audio.

properties.name: Language
properties.summary: Gets or sets the language of the audio track as a human-readable string.
properties.value: The language name, typically in English (e.g., "English", "Spanish", "Japanese").

properties.name: LanguageID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Windows Language Code Identifier (LCID) for the audio track.
properties.value: The LCID value representing the language and regional variant.

properties.name: LanguageExtension
properties.summary: Gets or sets the language extension that indicates special audio track types.
properties.value: The language extension type such as captions, visually impaired, or director's commentary.

properties.name: HasMultichannelInfo
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this audio stream contains explicit multichannel information.
properties.value: true if the stream has dedicated multichannel encoding; otherwise, false.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Gets or sets the sampling frequency of the audio stream in Hz.
properties.value: The sampling frequency, typically 48000 Hz or 96000 Hz for DVD audio.

properties.name: Quantization
properties.summary: Gets or sets the bit depth (quantization) of the audio samples.
properties.value: The number of bits per sample, typically 16, 20, or 24 bits.

properties.name: NumberOfChannels
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of audio channels in the stream.
properties.value: The channel count, ranging from 1 (mono) to 8 (7.1 surround).

classes.name: DVDAudioStream
classes.summary: Represents information about a single audio stream within a DVD title.
classes.remarks: DVDs support multiple audio streams per title, allowing viewers to choose between different languages, audio formats (Dolby Digital, DTS, PCM), or specialized tracks like director's commentary. Each audio stream can have different characteristics such as sample rate, bit depth, and channel configuration. This class encapsulates all the metadata associated with a DVD audio stream, including: - Audio format and encoding attributes - Language information - Karaoke capabilities (for music/singing DVDs) - Stream enable/disable state DVD audio streams are indexed starting from 0, and viewers can switch between available streams during playback using the DVD menu or player controls.

properties.name: Attributes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio format and encoding attributes for this stream.
properties.value: The DVDAudioAttributes containing details about the audio format, sample rate, bit depth, channel configuration, and compression type.

properties.name: IsAudioStreamEnabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this audio stream is currently enabled and available for playback.
properties.value: true if this audio stream can be selected and played; false if the stream is present but disabled (possibly due to region restrictions or disc authoring choices).

properties.name: KaraokeAttributes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the karaoke-specific attributes for this audio stream, if applicable.
properties.value: The DVDKaraokeAttributes containing karaoke channel assignments and mixing options, or null if this is not a karaoke-enabled audio stream.

properties.name: Language
properties.summary: Gets or sets the language code for this audio stream.
properties.value: An integer representing the ISO 639 language code, where common values include: - 0x656E (25966): English - 0x6672 (26226): French - 0x6573 (25971): Spanish - 0x6465 (25701): German - 0x6A61 (27489): Japanese

classes.name: DVDDecoderCaps
classes.summary: Represents the capabilities of a DVD decoder, including supported playback rates and audio format capabilities.
classes.remarks: DVD decoders have varying capabilities depending on their implementation (hardware vs. software) and design. This class provides information about what a particular DVD decoder can handle, including maximum data rates for different stream types and special playback features. The capability information is crucial for: - Determining if smooth fast-forward and reverse playback are supported - Understanding the decoder's performance limits - Checking audio format support (AC3, DTS, PCM, etc.) - Validating if a DVD can be played properly on the current system Data rates are typically expressed as multipliers of normal playback speed (1x). For example, a FwdMaxRateVideo of 16.0 means the decoder can handle video playback at up to 16 times normal speed while maintaining smooth motion.

properties.name: Size
properties.summary: Gets or sets the size of the decoder capabilities structure in bytes.
properties.value: The size of the structure, used for version compatibility and validation.

properties.name: AudioCaps
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio decoding capabilities of the DVD decoder.
properties.value: A DVDAudioCaps object containing detailed information about supported audio formats, channels, and features.

properties.name: FwdMaxRateVideo
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum video data rate supported in the forward direction.
properties.value: The maximum playback rate multiplier for video streams (e.g., 2.0 for 2x speed, 16.0 for 16x speed). A value of 1.0 indicates normal playback speed only.

properties.name: FwdMaxRateAudio
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum audio data rate supported in the forward direction.
properties.value: The maximum playback rate multiplier for audio streams during fast-forward. Often lower than video rates due to audio processing limitations.

properties.name: FwdMaxRateSP
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum subpicture (subtitle) data rate supported in the forward direction.
properties.value: The maximum playback rate multiplier for subpicture streams during fast-forward.

properties.name: BwdMaxRateVideo
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum video data rate supported in the reverse direction.
properties.value: The maximum reverse playback rate multiplier for video streams. Returns 0 if the decoder does not support smooth reverse playback.

properties.name: BwdMaxRateAudio
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum audio data rate supported in the reverse direction.
properties.value: The maximum reverse playback rate multiplier for audio streams. Returns 0 if smooth reverse audio playback is not supported.

properties.name: BwdMaxRateSP
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum subpicture data rate supported in the reverse direction.
properties.value: The maximum reverse playback rate multiplier for subpicture streams. Returns 0 if smooth reverse subpicture display is not supported.

classes.name: DVDGPRMArray
classes.summary: Represents an array of DVD General Purpose Register Memory (GPRM) values used for DVD navigation and playback control.
classes.remarks: DVD General Purpose Registers (GPRMs) are 16 storage locations (registers 0-15) that can be used by DVD authors to store values and control navigation logic during playback. These registers act as variables in the DVD's programming language (DVD-Video Virtual Machine commands). GPRMs are used for: - Storing user selections and preferences during playback - Implementing complex navigation logic and branching - Tracking viewing history or progress through content - Controlling conditional playback based on user choices - Creating interactive games or quizzes on DVD - Implementing parental control features Each GPRM is a 16-bit register that can store values from -32768 to 32767 (signed) or 0 to 65535 (unsigned). The DVD Virtual Machine can perform operations like load, store, add, subtract, and compare on these registers. GPRMs persist only during the current playback session and are reset when the disc is ejected. Common GPRM usage patterns: - GPRM 0-3: Often used for menu navigation state - GPRM 4-7: Frequently used for angle and audio stream selection - GPRM 8-11: Commonly used for subtitle selection and display options - GPRM 12-15: Typically used for custom interactive features

properties.name: Registers
properties.summary: Gets or sets the array containing all 16 General Purpose Register Memory (GPRM) values.
properties.value: An array of 16 signed 16-bit integers representing the current values stored in GPRMs 0-15. Each value can range from -32768 to 32767 when interpreted as signed, or 0 to 65535 when interpreted as unsigned.

classes.name: DVDInfo
classes.summary: Provides comprehensive information about a DVD disc, including its structure, content, capabilities, and current playback state.
classes.remarks: The DVDInfo class serves as a central repository for all DVD-related metadata and state information. It encompasses disc-level properties, title information, audio/video streams, navigation state, and decoder capabilities. This information is essential for DVD player applications to properly handle disc navigation, stream selection, and user interface presentation. DVD Structure Overview: - A DVD contains one or more titles (movies, episodes, etc.) - Each title can have multiple chapters (scenes) - Each title can contain multiple audio streams (languages, commentary) - Each title can contain multiple subpicture streams (subtitles) - Menus provide navigation between titles and configuration options - Navigation is controlled by a Virtual Machine using registers (GPRMs/SPRMs) Key concepts represented in this class: - Title structure and navigation - Multi-language support for audio, subtitles, and menus - Parental control ratings - Region coding and copy protection - Hardware decoder capabilities - Current playback state and user selections

constructors.name: DVDInfo
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the DVDInfo class with default values.
constructors.remarks: Initializes all collections and sets appropriate default values for string properties. The country code array is initialized to the standard 2-byte size required for ISO 3166 codes.

properties.name: Audio_CurrentStream
properties.summary: Gets or sets the currently selected audio stream index.
properties.value: Zero-based index of the active audio stream. Range is 0 to (Audio_StreamsCount - 1). A value of -1 typically indicates no audio stream is selected.

properties.name: Audio_DefaultAudioLanguage
properties.summary: Gets or sets the default audio language code as specified by the DVD author.
properties.value: An integer representing the ISO 639 language code for the preferred audio language. Common values include 0x656E (English), 0x6672 (French), 0x6573 (Spanish).

properties.name: Audio_DefaultAudioLanguageS
properties.summary: Gets or sets the default audio language as a human-readable string.
properties.value: The language name (e.g., "English", "French", "Spanish") corresponding to the Audio_DefaultAudioLanguage code.

properties.name: Audio_DefaultAudioLanguageExt
properties.summary: Gets or sets the extension type for the default audio language.
properties.value: A DVDAudioLangExt value indicating special audio track types such as director's commentary, visually impaired audio description, or standard audio.

properties.name: Audio_StreamsCount
properties.summary: Gets or sets the total number of audio streams available on the current DVD title.
properties.value: The count of available audio streams. DVDs can have up to 8 audio streams per title.

properties.name: DecoderCaps
properties.summary: Gets or sets the capabilities of the DVD decoder being used for playback.
properties.value: A DVDDecoderCaps object containing information about supported playback rates, audio formats, and special features.

properties.name: Disc_CountryCode
properties.summary: Gets or sets the country code associated with this DVD disc.
properties.value: A 2-byte array representing the ISO 3166 country code. This is used for region-specific content and parental rating systems.

properties.name: Disc_CurrentUOPS
properties.summary: Gets or sets the current User Operation Prohibitions (UOPs) flags.
properties.value: A DVDValidUOPFlag indicating which user operations are currently prohibited by the DVD author at this point in playback.

properties.name: Disc_DVD_Side
properties.summary: Gets or sets which side of a double-sided DVD is currently active.
properties.value: A DVDDiscSide value indicating Side A or Side B. For single-sided discs, this will typically be SideA.

properties.name: Disc_GPRMs
properties.summary: Gets or sets the current General Purpose Register Memory (GPRM) values.
properties.value: A DVDGPRMArray containing 16 general-purpose registers used by the DVD Virtual Machine for navigation logic and state tracking.

properties.name: Disc_ID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the unique identifier for this DVD disc.
properties.value: A 64-bit integer that uniquely identifies this DVD. This ID is typically derived from disc metadata and can be used for disc recognition.

properties.name: Disc_NumOfTitles
properties.summary: Gets or sets the total number of titles available on this DVD.
properties.value: The count of titles (main features, episodes, extras) on the disc. Most movie DVDs have 1-5 titles, while TV series DVDs may have many more.

properties.name: Disc_NumOfVolumes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the total number of volumes in this DVD set.
properties.value: The total volume count for multi-disc sets. Single discs will have a value of 1.

properties.name: Disc_SPRMs
properties.summary: Gets or sets the current System Parameter Register Memory (SPRM) values.
properties.value: A DVDSPRMArray containing system registers that track player state, user preferences, and hardware capabilities.

properties.name: Disc_Volume
properties.summary: Gets or sets the current volume number within a multi-volume DVD set.
properties.value: The volume number of the currently loaded disc, starting from 1. For single-disc releases, this will be 1.

properties.name: Menu_DefaultLanguage
properties.summary: Gets or sets the default menu language code.
properties.value: An integer representing the ISO 639 language code for the default menu language. This determines which language version of the DVD menus will be displayed initially.

properties.name: Menu_DefaultLanguageS
properties.summary: Gets or sets the default menu language as a human-readable string.
properties.value: The language name (e.g., "English", "French", "Japanese") for the default menu language.

properties.name: Menu_Languages
properties.summary: Gets or sets the list of all available menu languages on this DVD.
properties.value: A list of language names representing all menu languages available on the disc. Users can switch between these languages for menu navigation.

properties.name: Menu_VMG_Attributes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Video Manager (VMG) menu attributes.
properties.value: A DVDMenuAttributes object containing properties of the main disc menu, including video format, aspect ratio, and display capabilities.

properties.name: ParentalLevel
properties.summary: Gets or sets the current parental control level setting.
properties.value: An integer from 1 to 8 representing the parental control level: - 1: G (General Audiences) - Suitable for all ages - 2-3: PG (Parental Guidance) - Some material may not be suitable for children - 4: PG-13 - Parents strongly cautioned, some material inappropriate for children under 13 - 5-6: R (Restricted) - Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian - 7-8: NC-17 - No one 17 and under admitted

properties.name: Subpicture_CurrentStream
properties.summary: Gets or sets the currently selected subpicture (subtitle) stream index.
properties.value: Zero-based index of the active subpicture stream. Range is 0 to (Subpicture_StreamsCount - 1). A value of -1 typically indicates no subpicture stream is selected.

properties.name: Subpicture_DefaultLanguage
properties.summary: Gets or sets the default subpicture language code.
properties.value: An integer representing the ISO 639 language code for the preferred subtitle language. Common values include 0x656E (English), 0x6672 (French), 0x6573 (Spanish).

properties.name: Subpicture_DefaultLanguageS
properties.summary: Gets or sets the default subpicture language as a human-readable string.
properties.value: The language name (e.g., "English", "French", "Spanish") corresponding to the Subpicture_DefaultLanguage code.

properties.name: Subpicture_DefaultLanguageExt
properties.summary: Gets or sets the extension type for the default subpicture language.
properties.value: A DVDSubPictureLangExt value indicating special subtitle types such as normal subtitles, large captions for hearing impaired, or director's commentary.

properties.name: Subpicture_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether subpicture display is currently enabled.
properties.value: true if subtitles/subpictures are being displayed; false if they are hidden.

properties.name: Subpicture_StreamsCount
properties.summary: Gets or sets the total number of subpicture streams available on the current DVD title.
properties.value: The count of available subpicture streams. DVDs can have up to 32 subpicture streams per title.

properties.name: Titles
properties.summary: Gets or sets the collection of all titles available on this DVD.
properties.value: A list of DVDTitleInfo objects, each containing detailed information about a title including duration, chapters, angles, and available streams.

classes.name: DVDKaraokeAttributes
classes.summary: Represents the attributes and configuration of DVD karaoke audio tracks.
classes.remarks: DVD karaoke is a specialized format that extends standard DVD audio capabilities to support interactive singing experiences. This class encapsulates the metadata that describes how karaoke content is structured on the disc, including channel assignments, duet support, and guide vocal configurations. Key concepts in DVD karaoke: - Multiple audio channels carry different elements (instrumental, guide vocals, effects) - Channels can be dynamically mixed based on user preferences - Support for solo and duet performances - Master of Ceremonies (MC) tracks for instruction or entertainment The karaoke player uses these attributes to: - Configure the audio mixer for proper channel routing - Enable/disable guide vocals based on user skill level - Support duet mode with separate guide tracks for each singer - Display appropriate on-screen information about available features

properties.name: Version
properties.summary: Gets or sets the karaoke format version number.
properties.value: The version number of the DVD karaoke specification used.

properties.name: MasterOfCeremoniesInGuideVocal1
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether a Master of Ceremonies (MC) track is present in guide vocal channel 1.
properties.value: true if guide vocal channel 1 contains MC announcements or instructions; false if it contains only singing guide vocals.

properties.name: Duet
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this karaoke track supports duet mode.
properties.value: true if the track contains separate guide vocals for two singers; false for solo performance tracks.

properties.name: ChannelAssignment
properties.summary: Gets or sets the channel assignment mode for this karaoke track.
properties.value: The DVDKaraokeAssignment value indicating how audio channels are configured.

properties.name: ChannelContents
properties.summary: Gets or sets an array describing the content type of each audio channel.
properties.value: An array of DVDKaraokeContents flags for each channel, indicating what type of audio content each channel contains.

classes.name: DVDMenuAttributes
classes.summary: Represents the attributes of a DVD menu, providing comprehensive information about the menu's multimedia components.
classes.remarks: DVD menus are interactive screens that allow users to navigate and select various options on a DVD disc. They typically include a background video or still image, optional audio (such as background music), and subpicture overlays for buttons and navigation elements. The menu system in DVD-Video consists of several types: - Title Menu: The main menu accessed when a disc is first played - Root Menu: Top-level menu for disc navigation - Subpicture Menu: For selecting subtitle tracks - Audio Menu: For choosing audio streams - Angle Menu: For multi-angle content selection - Chapter Menu: For direct chapter access Menu attributes define the technical characteristics of these interactive elements, including video format, audio properties, and subpicture specifications for button highlights and text overlays.

properties.name: CompatibleRegion
properties.summary: Gets or sets an array indicating which DVD regions are compatible with this menu.

properties.name: VideoAttributes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the video attributes of the menu, including resolution, aspect ratio, and encoding format.

properties.name: AudioPresent
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio is present in the menu.
properties.value: true if the menu includes an audio stream; otherwise, false.

properties.name: AudioAttributes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio attributes when audio is present in the menu.

properties.name: SubpicturePresent
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether subpicture streams are present in the menu.
properties.value: true if the menu includes subpicture overlays; otherwise, false.

properties.name: SubpictureAttributes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the subpicture attributes when subpictures are present in the menu.

classes.name: DVDMUACoeff
classes.summary: Represents the mixing coefficients for DVD Multi-channel User Audio (MUA) downmixing.
classes.remarks: DVD MUA (Multi-channel User Audio) allows for dynamic downmixing of multichannel audio to stereo output. This class defines the logarithmic mixing coefficients that control how each source channel contributes to the final left (channel 0) and right (channel 1) stereo output channels. The coefficients are stored as logarithmic values (base 2) for several reasons: - Efficient computation in digital signal processors - Better precision across a wide dynamic range - Natural representation of audio levels in decibels In the context of DVD karaoke: - These coefficients allow proper stereo imaging of multichannel karaoke content - Guide vocals can be centered or panned as needed - Instrumental tracks maintain proper stereo separation - Effects can be positioned in the stereo field for optimal impact The actual mixing gain is calculated as: gain = 2^(Log2Coefficient) For example: - Log2Alpha = 0.0 results in unity gain (1.0) - Log2Alpha = -1.0 results in -6dB attenuation (0.5) - Log2Alpha = 1.0 results in +6dB amplification (2.0)

properties.name: Log2Alpha
properties.summary: Gets or sets the logarithmic mixing coefficient for contributing this channel to the left stereo output (channel 0).
properties.value: The base-2 logarithm of the mixing gain. A value of 0.0 represents unity gain, negative values represent attenuation, and positive values represent amplification.

properties.name: Log2Beta
properties.summary: Gets or sets the logarithmic mixing coefficient for contributing this channel to the right stereo output (channel 1).
properties.value: The base-2 logarithm of the mixing gain. A value of 0.0 represents unity gain, negative values represent attenuation, and positive values represent amplification.

classes.name: DVDMUAMixingInfo
classes.summary: Represents the mixing configuration for a DVD Multi-channel User Audio (MUA) channel.
classes.remarks: DVD MUA mixing information controls how multichannel audio is downmixed to stereo or other channel configurations. This is particularly important for DVD karaoke where multiple audio elements (vocals, instruments, effects) need to be properly positioned and mixed for optimal playback on various audio systems. Key concepts in MUA mixing: - Channel routing: Which source channels contribute to which output channels - Phase relationships: Whether signals are mixed in-phase or out-of-phase - Speaker targeting: The intended playback position in a surround sound system Phase relationships are crucial for: - Creating stereo width and spaciousness - Implementing vocal removal techniques (out-of-phase mixing) - Ensuring mono compatibility when channels are summed - Creating special effects like pseudo-surround from stereo In karaoke applications, this allows sophisticated control over how different elements are presented, enabling features like vocal isolation, dynamic panning, and adaptive mixing based on the playback system's capabilities.

properties.name: MixTo0
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this channel is mixed to the left output (channel 0).
properties.value: true if this channel contributes to the left stereo output; false if it does not contribute to the left channel.

properties.name: MixTo1
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this channel is mixed to the right output (channel 1).
properties.value: true if this channel contributes to the right stereo output; false if it does not contribute to the right channel.

properties.name: Mix0InPhase
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this channel is mixed in-phase to the left output (channel 0).
properties.value: true if the signal is mixed in-phase (normal polarity); false if the signal is mixed out-of-phase (inverted polarity).

properties.name: Mix1InPhase
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this channel is mixed in-phase to the right output (channel 1).
properties.value: true if the signal is mixed in-phase (normal polarity); false if the signal is mixed out-of-phase (inverted polarity).

properties.name: SpeakerPosition
properties.summary: Gets or sets the intended speaker position for this channel in a surround sound system.
properties.value: A speaker position identifier indicating the intended playback location. Common values include: - 0: Front left - 1: Front right - 2: Front center - 3: Low frequency effects (subwoofer) - 4: Back left (surround left) - 5: Back right (surround right) - Additional values for extended surround formats (7.1, etc.)

classes.name: DVDMultichannelAudioAttributes
classes.summary: Represents the attributes for DVD multichannel audio streams, providing detailed information about channel mixing and downmixing coefficients for surround sound playback.
classes.remarks: DVD-Video supports sophisticated multichannel audio formats, primarily 5.1 and 7.1 surround sound configurations. This class contains the metadata necessary for proper audio channel management, including downmixing coefficients for playback on systems with fewer speakers than the source material. The multichannel audio system in DVD uses the following standard channel configurations: - 5.1: Front Left, Front Right, Center, LFE (Low Frequency Effects), Surround Left, Surround Right - 6.1: Adds a Rear Center channel - 7.1: Adds Surround Back Left and Surround Back Right instead of single Rear Center Downmixing is the process of converting multichannel audio to fewer channels (e.g., 5.1 to stereo). The coefficients define how each source channel contributes to the output channels, ensuring proper balance and preventing clipping while maintaining the artistic intent of the mix. DVD players use these attributes to: - Properly route audio to available speakers - Calculate downmix matrices for stereo or Pro Logic output - Apply dynamic range compression when requested - Maintain proper phase relationships between channels

properties.name: Info
properties.summary: Gets or sets an array of DVDMUAMixingInfo objects containing mixing information for each audio channel.
properties.value: An array of up to 8 DVDMUAMixingInfo objects, with the actual count depending on the audio format (5.1, 6.1, or 7.1).

properties.name: Coeff
properties.summary: Gets or sets an array of DVDMUACoeff objects containing the mixing coefficients for channel downmixing.
properties.value: An array of up to 8 DVDMUACoeff objects corresponding to each audio channel's contribution to the downmixed output.

classes.name: DVDSPRMArray
classes.summary: Represents an array of DVD System Parameter Register (SPRM) values that control DVD player state and behavior.
classes.remarks: System Parameter Registers (SPRMs) are a set of 24 read-only registers (SPRM0-SPRM23) that maintain the current state of the DVD player. These registers store critical information about player configuration, user preferences, and current playback state. Unlike General Parameter Registers (GPRMs) which can be modified by DVD content, SPRMs are controlled by the player and reflect its current operational state. The SPRM registers serve as the interface between DVD content and player capabilities, allowing disc authors to create content that adapts to different player configurations and user preferences. DVD navigation commands can read these values to make decisions about playback flow, menu presentation, and feature availability. Key SPRM registers include: RegisterPurpose and ContentsSPRM0Preferred menu language code (ISO 639-1, e.g., "en" for English)SPRM1Current audio stream number and attributesSPRM2Current subpicture stream number and display flagSPRM3Current angle number (for multi-angle features)SPRM4Current title number in Title setSPRM5Current Video Title Set (VTS) numberSPRM6Current Title PGC (Program Chain) numberSPRM7Current Part of Title (chapter) numberSPRM8Highlighted button number (0-36, 0 means no button selected)SPRM9Navigation timer for auto-actionsSPRM10Current PGC playback time (in BCD format)SPRM11Player audio mixing mode for karaoke (bit flags)SPRM12Country code for parental management (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2)SPRM13Parental management level (1-8, lower = more restrictive)SPRM14Player video configuration (bit 0-1: aspect ratio, bit 2: display mode)SPRM15Player audio capabilities (decoder format support flags)SPRM16Preferred audio language code (ISO 639-1)SPRM17Preferred audio language extension (normal, commentary, etc.)SPRM18Preferred subpicture language code (ISO 639-1)SPRM19Preferred subpicture language extension (normal, large, children, etc.)SPRM20Player region code (bit mask, bit 0-7 for regions 1-8)SPRM21Reserved for future useSPRM22Reserved for future useSPRM23Player state and capabilities extension These registers enable sophisticated DVD behavior such as: - Automatic language selection based on player preferences - Seamless branching for different versions of content - Parental control enforcement - Multi-angle scene synchronization - Region-specific content protection

properties.name: Registers
properties.summary: Gets or sets the array containing all 24 DVD System Parameter Register values.
properties.value: An array of 24 short (16-bit signed integer) values representing the current state of all System Parameter Registers.

classes.name: DVDSubpictureAttributes
classes.summary: Represents the attributes and characteristics of a DVD subpicture stream.
classes.remarks: DVD subpicture streams contain overlay graphics that can be displayed on top of the main video. Each subpicture stream has specific attributes that define its content type, encoding format, language information, and special characteristics. These attributes help DVD players determine how to process and present the subpicture content to users. Subpictures on DVDs are typically used for: - Subtitles in multiple languages - Closed captions for accessibility - Menu button highlights - Karaoke lyrics with timing information - Director's commentary indicators - Special graphical overlays A DVD can contain up to 32 subpicture streams, allowing for extensive multilingual support and various overlay features. The player selects which stream to display based on user preferences, disc programming, and these attribute values.

properties.name: Type
properties.summary: Gets or sets the type of content contained in the subpicture stream.
properties.value: A DVDSubPictureType value indicating whether the stream contains language-specific content (subtitles/captions) or other graphical overlays.

properties.name: CodingMode
properties.summary: Gets or sets the encoding format used for the subpicture graphics data.
properties.value: A DVDSubPictureCoding value indicating the compression and encoding method used for the subpicture bitmap data.

properties.name: LanguageID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Windows Language Code Identifier (LCID) for language-type subpictures.
properties.value: An integer representing the LCID of the subpicture's language. This value is only meaningful when Type equals Language. Common values include 1033 for English (US), 1034 for Spanish, 1036 for French, etc.

properties.name: Language
properties.summary: Gets or sets the human-readable language name or description of the subpicture stream.
properties.value: A string containing the language name (e.g., "English", "Spanish", "French") or a description of the subpicture content (e.g., "Director's Commentary", "Trivia Track").

properties.name: LanguageExtension
properties.summary: Gets or sets additional language classification information for the subpicture stream.
properties.value: A DVDSubPictureLangExt value providing extended language information such as whether the subtitles are normal, for children, or contain adult content.

classes.name: DVDSubpictureStream
classes.summary: Represents a complete DVD subpicture stream with its attributes and playback state.
classes.remarks: This class encapsulates all information about a single subpicture stream on a DVD, including its attributes (type, encoding, language) and current playback state. DVD subpicture streams are used to overlay graphics on top of the main video, most commonly for subtitles but also for other visual elements. DVDs can contain up to 32 subpicture streams per title, allowing viewers to choose from multiple subtitle languages or special overlay features. Each stream can be independently enabled or disabled, and only one stream is typically active at a time (though some players support displaying multiple streams simultaneously). The subpicture system is designed to be bandwidth-efficient, using only about 2-10% of the total disc bandwidth, while providing high-quality text and graphics overlays that can be perfectly synchronized with the video content.

properties.name: Attributes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the detailed attributes of this subpicture stream.
properties.value: A DVDSubpictureAttributes object containing information about the stream's content type, encoding format, language, and other characteristics.

properties.name: IsSubpictureStreamEnabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this subpicture stream is currently enabled for display.
properties.value: true if the subpicture stream is active and its content will be rendered on top of the video; false if the stream is available but not currently displayed.

properties.name: Language
properties.summary: Gets or sets the language code associated with this subpicture stream.
properties.value: An integer representing the language code. This may be an LCID (Windows Language Code Identifier) or another form of language identification used by the DVD authoring system.

classes.name: DVDTitleAttributes
classes.summary: Represents the complete set of attributes and stream information for a DVD title.
classes.remarks: A DVD title is a complete program unit on a DVD, such as a movie, TV episode, or special feature. Each title contains its own set of video, audio, and subpicture streams, along with metadata that describes how these streams should be presented and what special features are available. DVD structure hierarchy: - Disc → Titles → Chapters → Cells - Each title can have up to 99 chapters - Each title can contain up to 8 audio streams - Each title can contain up to 32 subpicture streams - Titles can have different aspect ratios, encoding formats, and features Title attributes are crucial for: - Determining playback capabilities and requirements - Building stream selection menus - Enabling special features like karaoke or multi-angle viewing - Applying appropriate audio/video processing - Enforcing parental controls and region restrictions

properties.name: AppMode
properties.summary: Gets or sets the application mode that indicates special features or processing requirements for this title.
properties.value: A DVDTitleAppMode value indicating whether the title has special features like karaoke mode enabled, or is a standard video title.

properties.name: VideoAttributes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the video stream attributes for this title.
properties.value: A DVDVideoAttributes object containing detailed information about the video encoding, resolution, aspect ratio, and other video characteristics.

properties.name: NumberOfAudioStreams
properties.summary: Gets or sets the total number of audio streams available in this title.
properties.value: An integer between 0 and 8 indicating how many audio streams are present. Most commercial DVDs include 1-6 audio streams for different languages and formats.

properties.name: AudioAttributes
properties.summary: Gets or sets an array containing detailed attributes for each audio stream in the title.
properties.value: An array of DVDAudioAttributes objects, with one entry for each available audio stream. The array size should match NumberOfAudioStreams.

properties.name: MultichannelAudioAttributes
properties.summary: Gets or sets extended information about multichannel audio capabilities for each stream.
properties.value: An array of DVDMultichannelAudioAttributes objects providing additional details about surround sound configurations and special audio features.

properties.name: NumberOfSubpictureStreams
properties.summary: Gets or sets the total number of subpicture streams available in this title.
properties.value: An integer between 0 and 32 indicating how many subpicture streams are present. Commercial DVDs typically include 2-10 subtitle streams for different languages.

properties.name: SubpictureAttributes
properties.summary: Gets or sets an array containing detailed attributes for each subpicture stream in the title.
properties.value: An array of DVDSubpictureAttributes objects, with one entry for each available subpicture stream. The array size should match NumberOfSubpictureStreams.

classes.name: DVDTitleInfo
classes.summary: Represents comprehensive information about a DVD title, including its attributes, menu structure, chapters, and parental controls.
classes.remarks: A DVD title is a major content unit on a DVD disc, typically representing a movie, episode, or other complete program. Each title contains its own set of chapters, audio tracks, subtitle tracks, and menu systems. DVDs can contain multiple titles - for example, a disc might have the main feature as Title 1, deleted scenes as Title 2, and behind-the-scenes content as Title 3.
