DVD Title Structure:Title: Complete program unit (movie, episode, etc.)Chapter: Subdivision of a title for navigation (scenes)Cell: Smallest playback unit containing video/audio dataVOBU: Video Object Unit - group of GOPs (Group of Pictures)Title Attributes: Each title has specific attributes defining its video format, audio options, subtitle availability, and playback restrictions. These attributes help players determine compatibility and available features. Menu System: DVD titles often include interactive menus for navigation, language selection, and special features. The menu attributes define the video format and capabilities of these interactive elements.

properties.name: MainAttributes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the main attributes of the DVD title, including video, audio, and subtitle stream information.
properties.value: A DVDTitleAttributes object containing comprehensive information about all available streams and their properties within this title.

properties.name: MenuAttributes
properties.summary: Gets or sets the attributes of the DVD menu system associated with this title.
properties.value: A DVDMenuAttributes object describing the menu's video format and available language options, or null if the title has no associated menu.

properties.name: NumberOfChapters
properties.summary: Gets or sets the total number of chapters (scenes) in this DVD title.
properties.value: The chapter count, typically ranging from 1 to 99. Most feature films have 10-30 chapters.

properties.name: ParentalLevel
properties.summary: Gets or sets the parental control levels supported by this DVD title.
properties.value: A flags enumeration indicating which parental levels can access this title. Multiple levels can be set, allowing flexible parental control configurations.

properties.name: TimeCodeFlags
properties.summary: Gets or sets the time code flags that indicate special timing or playback characteristics of the title.
properties.value: A 64-bit value containing various timing-related flags. The specific bit meanings are defined by the DVD specification and may include drop-frame indicators, film/video source flags, and synchronization markers.

classes.name: DVDVideoAttributes
classes.summary: Represents the comprehensive video format attributes of DVD content, including resolution, aspect ratio, frame rate, and encoding details.
classes.remarks: DVD video attributes define the technical characteristics of the video stream stored on a DVD. These attributes are crucial for proper playback and display, as they inform the player how to decode and present the video content. The DVD specification supports specific combinations of resolutions, frame rates, and aspect ratios to ensure compatibility across all DVD players. DVD Video Standards:NTSC (525/60): Used in North America, Japan - Resolutions: 720×480, 704×480, 352×480, 352×240 - Frame rates: 29.97 fps (interlaced), 23.976 fps (progressive)PAL (625/50): Used in Europe, Australia - Resolutions: 720×576, 704×576, 352×576, 352×288 - Frame rates: 25 fps (interlaced or progressive)Aspect Ratio and Display: DVDs store video in specific resolutions but include metadata about how it should be displayed. The actual pixel aspect ratio (PAR) differs from the display aspect ratio (DAR): 4:3 content: Standard TV format, displayed as-is16:9 content: Widescreen, can be displayed as: - Anamorphic: Full resolution stretched horizontally - Letterbox: Black bars added within 4:3 frame - Pan & Scan: Cropped to 4:3, following actionCompression and Quality: DVDs primarily use MPEG-2 compression, though MPEG-1 is supported for lower quality content. The video bitrate typically ranges from 3-9.8 Mbps, with an average around 5-7 Mbps for movies. Higher motion content requires higher bitrates to maintain quality. Special Features: - Line 21 data: Closed caption information for hearing impaired - Film mode flags: Indicate 24fps film content with 3:2 pulldown - Source letterboxing: Pre-letterboxed content information

properties.name: PanscanPermitted
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the picture can be shown as pan-scan if the display aspect ratio is 4 x 3.
properties.value: true if pan-scan display is permitted; otherwise, false.

properties.name: LetterboxPermitted
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the picture can be shown as letterbox if the display aspect ratio is 4 x 3.
properties.value: true if letterbox display is permitted; otherwise, false.

properties.name: AspectRatio
properties.summary: Gets or sets the display aspect ratio (W:H) of the video content.
properties.value: A tuple where Item1 is the width component and Item2 is the height component of the ratio. Common values are (4,3) for standard content and (16,9) for widescreen.

properties.name: FrameRate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the frame rate in frames per second.
properties.value: The frame rate as an integer. Common values include 23 (film), 25 (PAL), and 29 (NTSC). Note that actual rates may be fractional (e.g., 23.976, 29.97).

properties.name: FrameHeight
properties.summary: Gets or sets the frame height in lines (rows of pixels).
properties.value: The number of horizontal lines in the video frame. Standard values are 480 for NTSC and 576 for PAL, though this includes non-visible overscan areas.

properties.name: Compression
properties.summary: Gets or sets the video compression format used for encoding the video stream.
properties.value: The compression type, typically MPEG-2 for standard DVDs or MPEG-1 for Video CDs and low-quality content.

properties.name: Line21Field1InGOP
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether there is user data in line 21, field 1 of the video signal.
properties.value: true if Line 21 Field 1 contains data; otherwise, false.

properties.name: Line21Field2InGOP
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether there is user data in line 21, field 2 of the video signal.
properties.value: true if Line 21 Field 2 contains data; otherwise, false.

properties.name: SourceResolutionX
properties.summary: Gets or sets the horizontal source resolution in pixels.
properties.value: The width in pixels. DVD supports specific values: 352, 704, or 720 pixels.

properties.name: SourceResolutionY
properties.summary: Gets or sets the vertical source resolution in pixels (lines).
properties.value: The height in pixels. Values depend on the video system: NTSC supports 240 or 480 lines, PAL supports 288 or 576 lines.

properties.name: IsSourceLetterboxed
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the source video is pre-letterboxed within the encoded frame.
properties.value: true if the video contains letterbox bars as part of the encoded image; otherwise, false.

properties.name: IsFilmMode
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the content originated from film (24/25 fps) or video cameras.
properties.value: true for film-originated content; false for video camera content. For 625/50 Hz (PAL) systems specifically, this indicates film mode vs. camera mode.

classes.name: DVDVideoStream
classes.summary: Represents a DVD video stream with multi-angle support, extending basic video attributes with angle-specific information.
classes.remarks: DVDVideoStream extends DVDVideoAttributes to include support for multi-angle scenes, a unique feature of the DVD format. Multi-angle functionality allows viewers to switch between different camera angles during playback of the same scene, commonly used in: Concert videos - Multiple camera positions (stage, audience, close-ups)Sports content - Different viewing angles of the actionAdult content - Different perspectives of scenesSpecial features - Behind-the-scenes angles during movie scenesInteractive content - Choose-your-own-adventure style narrativesHow Multi-Angle Works:Multiple video streams are interleaved on the disc for the same time periodEach angle is divided into small cells that can be seamlessly switchedThe player reads ahead to buffer all angles for smooth switchingAudio typically remains constant across all anglesAngle changes are instantaneous without interrupting playbackTechnical Limitations:Maximum 9 angles per scene (limited by DVD specification)All angles must have identical duration and frame countIncreased disc space usage (each angle requires separate encoding)Reduced maximum bitrate per angle due to interleaving requirementsNot all DVD players support seamless angle switching Multi-angle scenes are relatively rare on commercial DVDs due to the additional production cost and disc space requirements. When present, an angle icon typically appears on screen to indicate availability.

properties.name: AnglesAvailable
properties.summary: Gets or sets the total number of camera angles available in the current multi-angle scene.
properties.value: The number of available angles, ranging from 1 (single angle) to 9 (maximum allowed by DVD specification). A value of 1 indicates standard single-angle content.

properties.name: CurrentAngle
properties.summary: Gets or sets the currently selected camera angle being displayed.
properties.value: The current angle number, ranging from 1 to AnglesAvailable. Angle 1 is typically the default or primary camera angle.

classes.name: RAWAudioFrame
classes.summary: Represents a raw audio frame, designed for direct memory manipulation and interop scenarios. This struct holds a pointer to the raw audio data, its size, and basic audio format information, along with timing details.
classes.remarks: This struct is marked with [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] to ensure its memory layout is compatible with unmanaged code. It is primarily used for high-performance audio processing where direct access to audio buffers is required. The Data field is an IntPtr, meaning memory management (allocation and deallocation) for the audio data buffer must be handled externally or by converting to AudioFrame which manages its own data. This struct is commonly used in callbacks from native audio components or in high-throughput audio processing pipelines. The timing fields (Timestamp and Duration) are in milliseconds for compatibility with native code, unlike the managed AudioFrame which uses TimeSpan. When receiving a RAWAudioFrame from native code, ensure that the memory pointed to by Data remains valid for the duration of processing.

methods.name: ToAudioFrame
methods.summary: Converts the current RAWAudioFrame instance into an AudioFrame object. This conversion facilitates working with the audio frame in a more managed and object-oriented way.
methods.returns: A new AudioFrame instance populated with data from the raw frame.

classes.name: RAWAudioFrameEventArgs
classes.summary: Provides data for events that deliver raw audio frames. This class encapsulates a RAWAudioFrame, allowing it to be passed as an argument in event handlers.
classes.remarks: This event argument is typically used in scenarios where an application needs to process raw audio data directly, such as for custom audio analysis, visualization, real-time effects, or machine learning applications. The Frame property provides access to the raw audio buffer and its associated metadata. When handling events of this type, be aware that the audio data pointer may only be valid for the duration of the event handler. If you need to retain the audio data, copy it to a managed buffer or convert it to an AudioFrame before the handler returns. Common use cases include audio metering, spectrum analysis, voice activity detection, or feeding audio to custom processing pipelines.

constructors.name: RAWAudioFrameEventArgs
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the RAWAudioFrameEventArgs class.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: The RAWAudioFrame to be encapsulated by these event arguments.

properties.name: Frame
properties.summary: Gets the RAWAudioFrame associated with this event. This frame contains the raw audio data and its metadata.
properties.value: The RAWAudioFrame.

classes.name: RAWBaseAudioInfo
classes.summary: Represents fundamental information about a raw audio stream. This struct provides details such as the sample container width, number of channels, sample rate, and audio format.
classes.remarks: This struct is critical for interoperation with unmanaged code and is marked with [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] to ensure its memory layout matches native structures. Do not modify its structure without careful consideration of compatibility. The BPS field indicates the width of one sample's container in bits, which is not always its bit depth - see the field's own documentation. Channels typically range from 1 (mono) to 2 (stereo) for common audio, but can be higher for surround sound (5.1 = 6 channels, 7.1 = 8 channels). SampleRate is measured in Hz and determines the audio quality and frequency range - 44100 Hz is CD quality, 48000 Hz is DVD/professional quality. The Format field disambiguates between different representations of the same bit depth (e.g., PCM16 vs IEEE32). This struct is used throughout the framework to describe audio streams in a consistent, platform-independent manner.

methods.name: ToString
methods.summary: Returns a string that represents the current RAWBaseAudioInfo instance. The string includes the bits per sample, channels, sample rate, and audio format.
methods.returns: A String that represents this instance.

classes.name: RAWImage
classes.summary: Represents a raw image frame, providing direct access to image data in unmanaged memory. This struct is designed for high-performance image processing and interoperation with native code.
classes.remarks: The RAWImage struct holds a pointer to the raw pixel data, along with its dimensions, stride, and color space. It is crucial to manage the memory pointed to by Data using the Alloc and Free methods, or ensure that the memory is managed externally if the RAWImage is merely a view into an existing buffer. This struct is marked with [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] to ensure its memory layout is compatible with native structures. The Stride field is critical for correct memory access - it represents the byte width of each row including any padding for alignment. Always use Stride * Height to calculate the total buffer size, never Width * BytesPerPixel * Height. This type is commonly used when interfacing with native image processing libraries, video decoders, or when optimizing critical image operations. Memory allocated with Alloc() must be freed with Free() to prevent leaks - consider using try/finally blocks. The constructor allows wrapping existing memory without allocation, useful for zero-copy scenarios.

constructors.name: RAWImage
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the RAWImage struct with specified parameters.

parameters.name: data
parameters.summary: A pointer to the raw image data.

parameters.name: dataSize
parameters.summary: The size of the data in bytes.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: The width of the image in pixels.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: The height of the image in pixels.

parameters.name: stride
parameters.summary: The stride of the image in bytes.

parameters.name: colorspace
parameters.summary: The color space of the image.

methods.name: Alloc
methods.summary: Allocates unmanaged memory for the image data buffer based on the Stride and Height. The DataSize field is updated accordingly.
methods.remarks: This method should be called before writing pixel data to the Data pointer. It is crucial to call Free when the allocated memory is no longer needed.

methods.name: Free
methods.summary: Frees the unmanaged memory previously allocated for the image data buffer.
methods.remarks: This method should always be called to prevent memory leaks when the RAWImage instance is no longer needed, especially if Alloc was used.

classes.name: RAWVideoColorSpaceHelper
classes.summary: Provides helper methods for working with RAWVideoColorSpace. This static class facilitates conversions between different color space representations and calculates image stride.
classes.remarks: This helper is essential for managing raw video and image data, ensuring correct interpretation and memory allocation when dealing with various pixel formats and platform-specific image structures. The conversion methods bridge between the framework's internal color space representation and platform-specific types. On Windows, conversions to/from System.Drawing.Imaging.PixelFormat enable integration with GDI+ and Windows Forms. On other platforms, conversions use PixelFormatX for cross-platform compatibility. The ToVideoFormat method maps to MediaBlocks VideoFormatX for use with the modern pipeline. These conversions are essential when interfacing with platform-specific UI frameworks or external image libraries. Not all color spaces have direct mappings to all target types - some conversions may throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException.

methods.name: ToVideoFormat
methods.summary: Converts a RAWVideoColorSpace enumeration value to its corresponding VideoFormatX value. This is useful for mapping raw video formats to the MediaBlocks video format definitions.
methods.returns: The equivalent VideoFormatX.

classes.name: RAWVideoFrame
classes.summary: Represents a raw video frame, designed for direct memory manipulation and interop scenarios. This struct holds a pointer to the raw video data, its size, and basic video format information, along with timing details.
classes.remarks: This struct is marked with [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] to ensure its memory layout is compatible with unmanaged code. It is primarily used for high-performance video processing where direct access to video buffers is required. The Data field is an IntPtr, meaning memory management (allocation and deallocation) for the video data buffer must be handled externally or by converting to VideoFrame which manages its own data. This struct is commonly used in callbacks from native video components, video processing pipelines, or when interfacing with hardware encoders/decoders. The timing fields (Timestamp and Duration) are in milliseconds for compatibility with native code, unlike the managed VideoFrame which uses TimeSpan. The Alloc and Free methods provide manual memory management for scenarios where you need to create and populate frames from scratch. When receiving a RAWVideoFrame from native code, ensure that the memory pointed to by Data remains valid for the duration of processing. The ToVideoFrame method provides conversion to the managed VideoFrame type for easier manipulation in C# code.

methods.name: Alloc
methods.summary: Allocates unmanaged memory for the video data buffer based on the Info.Stride and Info.Height. The DataSize field is updated accordingly.
methods.remarks: This method should be called before writing pixel data to the Data pointer. It is crucial to call Free when the allocated memory is no longer needed.

methods.name: Free
methods.summary: Frees the unmanaged memory previously allocated for the video data buffer.
methods.remarks: This method should always be called to prevent memory leaks when the RAWVideoFrame instance is no longer needed, especially if Alloc was used.

methods.name: ToVideoFrame
methods.summary: Converts the current RAWVideoFrame instance into a VideoFrame object. This conversion facilitates working with the video frame in a more managed and object-oriented way.
methods.returns: A new VideoFrame instance populated with data from the raw frame.

classes.name: RAWVideoFrameEventArgs
classes.summary: Provides data for events that deliver raw video frames. This class encapsulates a RAWVideoFrame, allowing it to be passed as an argument in event handlers.
classes.remarks: This event argument is typically used in scenarios where an application needs to process raw video data directly, such as for custom video analysis, computer vision algorithms, rendering to custom surfaces, or real-time effects. The Frame property provides access to the raw video buffer and its associated metadata including dimensions, color space, and timing. When handling events of this type, be aware that the video data pointer may only be valid for the duration of the event handler. If you need to retain the video data, copy it to a managed buffer or convert it to a VideoFrame before the handler returns. Common use cases include motion detection, QR code scanning, face detection, augmented reality overlays, or feeding frames to machine learning models. Frame event handlers should execute quickly to avoid blocking the video pipeline and causing frame drops.

classes.name: Rect

classes.remarks: This class is commonly used to define regions of interest, video frame dimensions, cropping areas, or UI element bounds. It includes constructors for various initialization scenarios and utility properties for width and height. The rectangle is defined by edges (Left, Top, Right, Bottom) rather than position and size, which is common in graphics APIs. Width is calculated as Right - Left, and Height as Bottom - Top. classes.name: MediaFileTags

classes.remarks: This class is designed to provide a unified access point to media file metadata, regardless of the underlying tag format. It includes standard fields like title, artist, album, and genre, as well as more specific fields like MusicBrainz IDs, ReplayGain information, and lyrics. The class supports both simple text metadata (Title, Album, Comment) and array-based metadata (Performers, Genres, Composers) to handle multi-valued tags. The ToString method provides a formatted representation of all non-empty tags for display or debugging purposes. classes.name: VideoFrame
classes.summary: Represents a single frame of video data, including its raw data, format information, and timing. This struct provides a managed way to work with video frames, abstracting some of the complexities of unmanaged memory.
classes.remarks: The VideoFrame struct holds a pointer to the raw pixel data, along with its dimensions, stride, color space, and timing information. It includes methods for memory management (Alloc, Free) and conversions to other frame types like RAWVideoFrame and RAWImage. Unlike RAWVideoFrame which uses millisecond timestamps, VideoFrame uses TimeSpan for timing, making it more convenient for C# code. The Info field contains all format metadata including dimensions, color space, stride, and frame rate. Memory management is manual - Alloc() allocates unmanaged memory which must be freed with Free() to prevent leaks. The struct provides multiple conversion methods: ToRAWVideoFrame for interop, ToArray for byte array access, ToRAWImage for image processing. IsEmpty() checks if the Data pointer is null, useful for validating frame availability. CreateAndAlloc is a static factory method that combines construction and allocation in one call. This type is central to video processing workflows in the framework, bridging managed and unmanaged code.

classes.name: VideoFrameRate
classes.summary: Represents a video frame rate, typically expressed as a fraction (numerator/denominator) or a floating-point value. This struct provides methods for comparison, conversion, and common frame rate constants.
classes.remarks: Frame rates are crucial for accurate video playback, synchronization, and encoding. This struct handles the precision required for various video standards by storing frame rates as rational numbers (fractions). The numerator (Num) and denominator (Den) representation is essential for exact representation of rates like 29.97 (30000/1001) or 23.976 (24000/1001). The Value property provides a computed floating-point representation for convenience. Static properties provide standard frame rates: FPS_10, FPS_25 (PAL), FPS_30 (NTSC), FPS_60, FPS_29_97 (NTSC drop-frame), FPS_23_976 (film), etc. The struct implements IComparable, IEquatable, and IConvertible for comprehensive integration with .NET types. Comparison operators allow intuitive frame rate comparisons. IsEmpty property checks if the frame rate is uninitialized (0/0). This type is used throughout the framework wherever frame rate needs to be specified or queried.

classes.name: CVFace
classes.summary: Represents a detected face in a video frame, including its bounding box and the positions of key facial features like eyes, nose, and mouth.
classes.remarks: This class is used in conjunction with face detection and tracking functionalities to provide detailed information about each identified face. It can be used for various applications such as facial recognition, emotion analysis, or augmented reality overlays. Position property defines the overall face bounding box in the video frame. Eyes list typically contains two Rect objects for left and right eye positions, enabling gaze tracking and eye-based features. Nose and Mouth properties provide additional facial landmarks for expression analysis and face alignment. Timestamp indicates when the face was detected, enabling temporal tracking and synchronization. Facial landmarks enable advanced features: eye tracking, emotion detection, face mesh generation, AR filters, and liveness detection. Detection accuracy depends on face angle, lighting, occlusion, resolution, and the detection algorithm used. Feature positions are relative to the frame coordinates and can be used for overlay rendering or geometric analysis. This information is fundamental for face recognition systems, requiring alignment and normalization for comparison. Applications include access control, attendance systems, emotion analytics, AR effects, and user interface control. Privacy considerations are important when storing or processing facial feature data.

properties.value: A list of Rect objects for the eyes.

properties.name: Nose
properties.summary: Gets or sets the bounding rectangle of the detected nose.
properties.value: The Rect representing the nose's position.

properties.name: Mouth
properties.summary: Gets or sets the bounding rectangle of the detected mouth.
properties.value: The Rect representing the mouth's position.

properties.name: Timestamp
properties.summary: Gets or sets the timestamp of the video frame in which the face was detected.
properties.value: The timestamp.

methods.returns: A String that represents this instance.

classes.name: CVHand
classes.summary: Represents a detected hand in a video frame, including its bounding box and recognized gesture.
classes.remarks: This class is used in conjunction with hand detection and gesture recognition functionalities to provide detailed information about each identified hand. It can be used for various applications such as human-computer interaction, sign language recognition, or activity monitoring. Position property defines the hand bounding box coordinates in the video frame. Gesture property identifies the recognized hand pose (Fist, Palm, or other gestures). Hand detection enables touchless interaction for applications where physical contact is impractical or undesirable. Gesture recognition transforms hand poses into commands, enabling natural user interfaces. Applications include virtual reality controllers, smart home control, presentation control, gaming, and accessibility features. Detection accuracy depends on hand orientation, lighting, skin tone contrast, background complexity, and camera resolution. Advanced implementations may track individual fingers, hand orientation, and complex gesture sequences. Hand tracking across frames enables smooth interaction and trajectory-based commands (swiping, pinching, rotating). This is a fundamental component for contactless interfaces in medical, industrial, and automotive applications. Consider implementing gesture state machines to recognize multi-step gestures and prevent false triggers.

properties.name: Position
properties.summary: Gets or sets the bounding rectangle of the detected hand.
properties.value: The Rect representing the hand's position, in the coordinates of the 320x240 frame that CVHandDetectBlock outputs.

properties.name: Gesture

properties.value: The CVHandGesture representing the gesture.

methods.name: ToString

methods.returns: A String that represents this instance.

classes.name: FaceTrackingSettings
classes.summary: Represents the settings for configuring face tracking operations within the video processing components. This class allows control over parameters such as minimum face size, color mode, search mode, and scaling factors.
classes.remarks: Proper configuration of these settings is crucial for optimizing face detection and tracking performance and accuracy for various scenarios, such as different camera distances, lighting conditions, or target face sizes. MinimumWindowSize filters out small false positives and defines the minimum detectable face size in pixels. ColorMode determines the color space used by the tracking algorithm (RGB, HSL, or Mixed), affecting robustness to lighting changes. SearchMode controls whether to detect a single face or multiple faces in each frame. ScaleFactor determines step size when resizing the search window: smaller values provide finer search but slower performance. ScalingMode defines search direction (larger-to-smaller or smaller-to-larger), optimized based on expected face sizes. Highlight enables visual overlay rendering of detected faces for debugging and user feedback. Optimal settings depend on use case: security cameras benefit from multiple face detection, selfie apps may use single mode. Smaller MinimumWindowSize detects distant faces but increases false positives and processing time. ScaleFactor of 1.05-1.1 provides thorough search, 1.3-1.5 prioritizes speed over accuracy. These settings directly impact CPU/GPU usage and detection latency, requiring balance for real-time applications.

properties.name: ScalingMode

properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether visual highlighting of detected faces is enabled.

classes.name: IFaceDetector
classes.summary: Defines the contract for a face detection component. This interface extends IVideoProcessor, indicating that face detection is a form of video processing.
classes.remarks: Implementations of this interface are responsible for analyzing video frames to identify human faces. The results of the detection are communicated through the FacesDetected event. Face detection algorithms process video frames to locate faces and extract facial features (eyes, nose, mouth). FacesDetected event is raised for each frame where faces are detected, providing CVFace objects with position and landmark data. Implementations may use various detection algorithms: Haar cascades, HOG+SVM, or deep learning models (MTCNN, RetinaFace, YOLOv8). The interface extends IVideoProcessor to enable integration into video processing pipelines with format negotiation and frame processing. Settings configuration (not part of this interface) typically controls detection parameters like minimum face size, confidence threshold, and search mode. Detection performance depends on algorithm choice, hardware capabilities, frame resolution, and configuration settings. Applications should handle FacesDetected events asynchronously to avoid blocking the video processing pipeline. Face detection is the foundation for face recognition, emotion analysis, attention tracking, and AR applications. Implementations must be thread-safe as video frames may be processed concurrently on multiple threads.

events.name: FacesDetected
events.summary: Occurs when one or more faces are detected in a video frame. The event provides a CVFaceDetectedEventArgs object containing details about the detected faces.

classes.name: IVideoProcessor
classes.summary: Defines the contract for a video processing component. This interface provides methods for processing individual video frames and querying supported formats.
classes.remarks: Implementations of this interface can perform various video manipulations, such as applying effects, analyzing content, or transforming frames. It supports processing both legacy VideoFrame and modern VideoFrameX types. ProcessFrame methods accept video frames and perform operations like filtering, effects, analysis, or content detection. GetSupportedFrameFormats enables format negotiation, informing the pipeline which pixel formats the processor can handle. SetContext provides dependency injection for resources, configurations, or shared components needed by the processor. VideoFrameX is the modern format used by MediaBlocks engine with enhanced metadata and performance optimizations. VideoFrame is the legacy format maintained for backward compatibility with older components. Implementations must handle frame processing efficiently as they operate in real-time video pipelines. Video processors can be chained in pipelines, with each processor transforming or analyzing frames sequentially. Common processor types include color correction, denoising, sharpening, overlay rendering, motion detection, and object recognition. Thread safety is crucial as processors may handle frames from multiple sources or parallel pipelines. Performance optimization considerations include SIMD operations, GPU acceleration, frame skipping, and multi-threading.

classes.name: MotionDetectionExSettings
classes.summary: Provides comprehensive configuration settings for advanced motion detection in video processing pipelines.
classes.remarks: The class offers extensive control over motion detection algorithms and visualization options. It supports multiple detection methods and processing techniques suitable for various applications including: - Security and surveillance systems - Traffic monitoring - Industrial automation - Sports analysis - Wildlife observation The class provides two main configuration aspects: 1. Detection configuration: Controls how motion is detected (detector type, sensitivity, noise suppression) 2. Visualization configuration: Controls how detected motion is displayed (highlighting, grids, colors) Performance considerations: - Different detector types have varying computational requirements - Enabling visualization features adds processing overhead - Grid-based processing is more efficient for large areas - Object counting requires more CPU than simple motion detection

constructors.remarks: Default configuration provides a balanced setup suitable for general motion detection: - Processor: MotionAreaHighlighting (visualizes all motion) - Detector: TwoFramesDifference (fast, simple detection) - Threshold: 15 (moderate sensitivity) - Noise suppression: Enabled - Color: Red highlighting The default settings are optimized for: - Indoor surveillance with moderate lighting - Detection of human-sized objects - Real-time processing with visual feedback - Balance between sensitivity and false positives For specific applications, adjust the settings after initialization: - Security: Increase sensitivity, enable object tracking - Analytics: Use grid processing, disable visualization - Outdoor: Increase threshold, enable edge preservation

classes.name: BarcodeReaderSettings
classes.summary: Provides configuration settings for barcode detection in video frames during video processing operations.
classes.remarks: The class is used to configure barcode detection functionality within the video processing pipeline. It allows enabling or disabling barcode detection and specifying the type of barcodes to detect. When barcode detection is enabled, the video processor analyzes each frame to identify and decode barcodes of the specified type. This is useful for applications such as: - Inventory management systems with video surveillance - QR code-based authentication systems - Automated product scanning in manufacturing - Document processing with embedded barcodes Performance considerations: - Barcode detection adds computational overhead to video processing - Specifying a specific barcode type (rather than Auto) improves performance - Detection accuracy depends on video quality, barcode size, and lighting conditions

classes.name: MotionDetectionSettings
classes.summary: Provides configuration settings for motion detection in video streams with color channel analysis and frame processing options.
classes.remarks: The class enables motion detection by analyzing pixel differences between video frames. It offers flexible configuration for color channel analysis, motion visualization, and adaptive frame dropping based on motion levels. Key features: - Selective color channel comparison (RGB or grayscale) - Motion highlighting with configurable colors - Frame dropping optimization for low-motion scenes - Grid-based motion matrix analysis - Adjustable sensitivity thresholds This class provides a simpler interface compared to , focusing on basic motion detection with color-based analysis.

constructors.name: MotionDetectionSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MotionDetectionSettings class with optimized default values.
constructors.remarks: Default configuration provides a balanced setup for general motion detection: - Motion detection: Disabled (must be explicitly enabled) - Comparison mode: Grayscale (efficient and effective) - Highlight color: Green (moderate visibility) - Thresholds: Moderate sensitivity (25 for highlighting, 5 for dropping) - Matrix: 8×8 grid (adequate for most applications) - Frame interval: 0 (compare consecutive frames) This configuration is optimized for: - Indoor surveillance with moderate lighting - Real-time processing requirements - Balance between sensitivity and false positives - General-purpose motion detection scenarios Adjust settings after initialization based on your specific requirements: - Outdoor scenes: Increase thresholds to handle lighting changes - High-resolution video: Increase matrix dimensions for better detail - Performance-critical: Increase frame interval or enable frame dropping - Color-specific detection: Disable grayscale and enable specific RGB channels

properties.name: Compare_Blue
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the blue color channel is analyzed for motion detection.
properties.value: true to include the blue channel in motion comparison; otherwise, false. Default is false.

properties.name: Compare_Green
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the green color channel is analyzed for motion detection.
properties.value: true to include the green channel in motion comparison; otherwise, false. Default is false.

properties.name: Compare_Greyscale
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether grayscale (luminance) comparison is used instead of RGB channels.
properties.value: true to use grayscale comparison; false to use RGB channel comparison. Default is true.

properties.name: Compare_Red
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the red color channel is analyzed for motion detection.
properties.value: true to include the red channel in motion comparison; otherwise, false. Default is false.

properties.name: DropFrames_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether frames with motion below the threshold should be dropped from processing.
properties.value: true to enable frame dropping for low-motion scenes; otherwise, false. Default is false.

properties.name: DropFrames_Threshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the motion level threshold for frame dropping decisions.
properties.value: The threshold value for motion detection. Valid range is typically [0-100]. Default is 5.

properties.name: Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether motion detection is enabled for video processing.
properties.value: true to enable motion detection; otherwise, false. Default is false.

properties.name: FrameInterval
properties.summary: Gets or sets the interval between reference frames used for motion comparison.
properties.value: The number of frames to skip between motion comparisons. A value of 0 compares every consecutive frame. Default is 0.

properties.name: Highlight_Color
properties.summary: Gets or sets the color channel used for highlighting detected motion in video frames.
properties.value: The color channel for motion visualization. Default is Green.

properties.name: Highlight_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether motion areas are visually highlighted in the output video.
properties.value: true to enable motion highlighting; otherwise, false. Default is false.

properties.name: Highlight_Threshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the pixel difference threshold for motion highlighting.
properties.value: The threshold value ranging from 0 to 255, where higher values require more significant changes to trigger highlighting. Default is 25.

properties.name: Matrix_Height
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of rows in the motion analysis matrix grid.
properties.value: The number of vertical divisions in the motion grid. Default is 8. Valid range is typically [2-32].

properties.name: Matrix_Width
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of columns in the motion analysis matrix grid.
properties.value: The number of horizontal divisions in the motion grid. Default is 8. Valid range is typically [2-32].

classes.name: AudioEventDetectorSettings
classes.summary: Settings for the audio-event-detection block (YAMNet / AudioSet, 521 classes).
classes.remarks: Unlike the vision AI settings, this type does NOT derive from OnnxInferenceSettings: YAMNet consumes a 16 kHz mono audio waveform rather than an image, so the image-size / letterbox / NCHW knobs do not apply. The YAMNet ONNX model is not shipped in the SDK NuGet packages: the application supplies it and points ModelPath at it. The block never downloads anything itself. The block accumulates tapped PCM into an unbounded queue (audio is never discarded — a source that outruns the worker only grows the backlog), runs inference on a background worker over WindowSeconds windows, smooths the per-class scores over SmoothingWindows windows, and raises one event per continuous sound with hysteresis (Threshold to enter, Threshold * ReleaseRatio to leave). Every property here is read once, when the block is built. Set them before starting the pipeline: changing one on a running pipeline has no effect until the block is rebuilt (the next start).

constructors.name: AudioEventDetectorSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the AudioEventDetectorSettings class.

constructors.name: AudioEventDetectorSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the AudioEventDetectorSettings class with a model path.

parameters.name: modelPath
parameters.summary: The absolute path to the YAMNet ONNX model file (yamnet.onnx).

properties.name: ModelPath
properties.summary: Gets or sets the absolute path to the YAMNet ONNX model file. Required. The model takes a 1-D 16 kHz mono float waveform and returns a per-frame [frames, 521] AudioSet score vector.

properties.name: Provider
properties.summary: Gets or sets the execution provider for the ONNX session. Defaults to Auto, which uses the fastest hardware provider present in the loaded ONNX Runtime native build and falls back to the CPU. YAMNet is tiny — on the CPU, roughly 0.6 ms for the default 0.975 s window and 1.8 ms for the 5 s maximum, over 1000× real time either way — so the CPU is usually sufficient.

properties.name: DeviceId
properties.summary: Gets or sets the hardware device id used when a GPU provider is selected. Defaults to 0.

properties.name: Threshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the confidence threshold a class must reach for an event to start. Defaults to 0.5. The model's scores live in 0..1, and a value outside 0.01..1 is clamped into it with a warning: the ceiling keeps the threshold reachable, and the floor keeps an active event releasable (it ends below Threshold * ReleaseRatio, which at a threshold of 0 no score could ever fall below, latching every class until end-of-stream). Clamping does not rescue a mis-scaled value — a 0..100 slider bound straight through still detects nothing — so the warning names the value it replaced.

properties.name: ReleaseRatio
properties.summary: Gets or sets the hysteresis release ratio. An active event ends when its smoothed score falls below Threshold * ReleaseRatio. A value below 1 keeps a single continuous sound from flickering into many events. Defaults to 0.7. A value outside 0.01..1 (or NaN) is clamped into that range with a warning naming the value it replaced: the floor keeps an active event releasable (a ratio of 0 yields a release threshold of 0, which no score could ever fall below, latching every started event until end-of-stream), and the ceiling keeps the release threshold from exceeding the enter threshold.

properties.name: SmoothingWindows
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of consecutive windows the per-class scores are averaged over (a moving average) to suppress one-window blips before thresholding. 1 disables smoothing. Defaults to 3. The average covers the windows seen so far rather than the configured count, so it ramps in at the start of a stream: a sound that is present from the very first window is reported immediately, with no start-of-stream latency. The trade-off is that smoothing only takes effect once enough windows have accumulated — a one-window blip in the very first window is thresholded unsmoothed and can raise an event. Raising this trades detection latency (for sounds that start later in the stream) for fewer false positives.

properties.name: WindowSeconds
properties.summary: Gets or sets the inference window length, in seconds. Each window is classified independently and its per-frame scores are averaged. Defaults to 0.975 s — one 0.96 s YAMNet patch plus a small margin. Clamped to the range 0.96–5 s: YAMNet frames its input into 0.96 s patches and zero-pads anything shorter, so a sub-patch window is still scored — but against synthetic silence more than against the audio, which is why the floor exists.

properties.name: ClassFilter
properties.summary: Gets or sets an optional allowlist of AudioSet class display names (case-insensitive, e.g. "Siren", "Dog", "Glass"). When non-empty, only these classes can raise events; all other classes are ignored. null or empty (the default) detects every class. Names must match an AudioSet class exactly: a name that does not is ignored with a warning, and a non-empty filter in which NO name matches fails the block's build with an error rather than quietly detecting everything.

properties.name: EnableScoresEvent
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the block raises a lightweight top-K scores event for every processed window (useful for a live meter). Off by default to avoid per-window event traffic.

properties.name: TopK
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of highest-scoring classes reported in the scores event when EnableScoresEvent is true. Defaults to 5 and is clamped to 1..521 (the class count).

classes.name: AudioEventScore
classes.summary: A single AudioSet class score for one processed window, reported by the audio-event block's scores event.

constructors.name: AudioEventScore
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the AudioEventScore class.

parameters.name: confidence
parameters.summary: The class score for the window, in the range 0..1.

properties.name: ClassId
properties.summary: Gets the AudioSet class id (0..520).

properties.name: Label
properties.summary: Gets the AudioSet class display name.

properties.name: Confidence
properties.summary: Gets the class score for the window, in the range 0..1.

classes.name: AutoReframeSettings
classes.summary: Settings for the AI auto-reframe block, which converts landscape footage into a fixed (typically vertical 9:16) output by dynamically cropping around the detected subject.
classes.remarks: The block runs object detection on a sampled stream (every DetectionInterval frames), selects a subject per TargetSelection / ClassLabelFilter, centers a crop window of the output aspect ratio on that subject, smooths the crop position over time (Smoothing + DeadZoneFraction), and scales the result to OutputWidth x OutputHeight with square pixels. Anamorphic (non-square-pixel) sources are handled by PAR-aware cropping: the crop is sized using the negotiated source pixel aspect ratio so the output keeps true display proportions. When no subject is present for longer than LostTargetTimeout, the crop eases back to the frame center.

constructors.name: AutoReframeSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the AutoReframeSettings class.

parameters.name: detector
parameters.summary: The YOLO detector settings. Must not be null.

properties.name: Detector
properties.summary: Gets the YOLO detector settings used to locate subjects. Must not be null.

properties.name: OutputWidth
properties.summary: Gets or sets the output frame width in pixels. Defaults to 1080. Must be a positive even number.

properties.name: OutputHeight
properties.summary: Gets or sets the output frame height in pixels. Defaults to 1920. Must be a positive even number.

properties.name: DetectionInterval
properties.summary: Gets or sets how many frames to advance between detections. A value of 5 runs detection on every 5th frame and reuses the smoothed crop (which keeps gliding) on the frames in between. Defaults to 5. Must be >= 1.

properties.name: Smoothing
properties.summary: Gets or sets the exponential-moving-average retention factor for the crop position, in [0, 1). Higher values glide more slowly (0.85 moves 15% toward the target each frame). Defaults to 0.85.

properties.name: DeadZoneFraction
properties.summary: Gets or sets the dead-zone half-width as a fraction of the frame dimension, in [0, 1). When the subject center stays within this fraction of the current crop center the target is not updated, suppressing micro-jitter. Defaults to 0.05 (5%).

properties.name: TargetSelection
properties.summary: Gets or sets the subject-selection policy. Defaults to Largest.

properties.name: ClassLabelFilter
properties.summary: Gets or sets the class label the block prefers to follow (for example "person"). When set, only detections with this label are considered candidates. Set to null or empty to follow any class. Defaults to "person".

properties.name: LostTargetTimeout
properties.summary: Gets or sets how long the subject may be absent before the crop eases back to the frame center. Measured from the last detection that found the subject and evaluated only when detection runs, so frames skipped by DetectionInterval never drop a subject that is still detected. Defaults to one second. Must be >= Zero.

properties.name: TargetAspect
properties.summary: Gets the target output aspect ratio (width / height).

methods.name: Validate
methods.summary: Validates the settings, throwing when a value is out of range.

classes.name: BackgroundRemovalSettings
classes.summary: Settings for the background-removal (matting) block/engine.
classes.remarks: Extends OnnxInferenceSettings with the matting Model family and the background-replacement options. The block runs the ONNX model to estimate a per-pixel foreground alpha mask and then composites the chosen replacement background where the foreground alpha is low. The inherited InputWidth/InputHeight apply only to a model with dynamic input dimensions: a model that bakes in a fixed size reports that size and the configured values are ignored for it. The default input size is 512x512, which is tuned for MODNet and is NOT applied per-model automatically. For any other dynamic-input model you must set InputWidth/InputHeight to that model's expected size yourself: 320 for U2Net, 1024 for BiRefNet. The pixel normalization (mean/std) is chosen automatically from Model; Custom uses the inherited NormalizeTo01 flag with no mean/std.

constructors.name: BackgroundRemovalSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the BackgroundRemovalSettings class.

constructors.name: BackgroundRemovalSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the BackgroundRemovalSettings class with the specified model path.

parameters.name: modelPath
parameters.summary: The absolute path to the matting ONNX model file.

properties.name: Model
properties.summary: Gets or sets the matting model family the supplied ONNX model belongs to. This selects the input normalization convention. Defaults to MODNet.

properties.name: ReplacementMode
properties.summary: Gets or sets how the background is replaced where the foreground alpha is low. Defaults to Blur.

properties.name: ReplacementColor
properties.summary: Gets or sets the solid background color used when ReplacementMode is SolidColor. Defaults to Green (a virtual green-screen).

properties.name: BackgroundImagePath
properties.summary: Gets or sets the absolute path to the static background image used when ReplacementMode is Image. The image is scaled to the frame size. Defaults to null.

properties.name: BlurRadius
properties.summary: Gets or sets the blur radius, in pixels, used when ReplacementMode is Blur. Larger values blur the background more. Defaults to 15.

properties.name: MaskThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets an optional foreground alpha threshold. The effective range is 0..0.5; values above 0.5 are clamped to 0.5 (the symmetric hardening band only makes sense for thresholds up to the midpoint). Mask values at or below this threshold are forced to full background and values at or above (1 - threshold) to full foreground, hardening the matte edge; the band in between is kept as a soft transition. A value of 0 (the default) keeps the model's raw soft matte unchanged.

properties.name: MaskFeatherAmount
properties.summary: Gets or sets an optional edge-feather radius, in matte (model-resolution) pixels. When greater than 0, the alpha matte is blurred by this radius before compositing, softening the foreground/background transition (useful for hair and motion-blurred edges). A value of 0 (the default) leaves the matte edges as the model produced them. MaskThreshold hardens the edge and feathering softens it; they are opposite controls.

classes.name: ByteTrackerSettings
classes.summary: Settings for the ByteTrack multi-object tracker.
classes.remarks: Confidence thresholds operate on OnnxDetection.Confidence. Association thresholds are maximum accepted costs. IoU cost is 1 - IoU. Score-fused cost is 1 - (IoU * detection confidence). LostTrackBuffer is measured in tracker Update calls, not wall-clock time.

properties.name: LowConfidenceThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum confidence for a detection to be considered. Detections below this threshold are ignored entirely. Defaults to 0.1.

properties.name: HighConfidenceThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the confidence threshold above which a detection participates in the first (high-confidence) association stage. Defaults to 0.25.

properties.name: NewTrackThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum confidence a high-confidence detection must reach to create a new track. Defaults to 0.35.

properties.name: FirstAssociationThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum accepted cost for the first (high-confidence) association stage. Defaults to 0.8.

properties.name: SecondAssociationThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum accepted cost for the second (low-confidence) association stage. Defaults to 0.5.

properties.name: UnconfirmedAssociationThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum accepted cost for matching unconfirmed tracks against remaining high-confidence detections. Defaults to 0.7.

properties.name: LostTrackBuffer
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of tracker Update calls a track may remain lost before it is expired and removed. Defaults to 30.

properties.name: FuseDetectionScore
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether detection confidence is fused into the association cost (1 - IoU * confidence). Defaults to true.

properties.name: ClassAwareMatching
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether class-aware matching is enabled. When enabled, a track and detection with different class IDs receive an unmatchable cost. Defaults to true.

methods.name: Validate
methods.summary: Validates the settings and throws ArgumentException if any value is invalid.

classes.name: DetectionFilterSettings
classes.summary: Settings for filtering detections before they are passed to the tracker.
classes.remarks: Filtering order: 1. Reject null detections and boxes. 2. Reject boxes with width or height less than or equal to zero. 3. If IncludedClassIds is non-empty, retain only included classes. 4. Apply ExcludedClassIds; exclusion wins if an ID is present in both lists. 5. Reject boxes whose integer pixel area is less than MinimumBoxArea. Confidence filtering is NOT performed here; it belongs to the tracker.

properties.name: IncludedClassIds
properties.summary: Gets or sets the class IDs to include. When non-empty, only detections whose class ID is in this list are retained. Null or empty means no inclusion filter is applied.

properties.name: ExcludedClassIds
properties.summary: Gets or sets the class IDs to exclude. Detections whose class ID is in this list are rejected. Exclusion wins over inclusion when an ID appears in both lists. Null or empty means no exclusion filter is applied.

properties.name: MinimumBoxArea
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum bounding box area in pixels. Detections whose area (width * height) is less than this value are rejected. Defaults to 0.

methods.name: Validate
methods.summary: Validates the settings and throws ArgumentException if any value is invalid.

classes.name: DiarizedTranscriptBuilder
classes.summary: Merges a speech-to-text transcript with a speaker-diarization timeline, labeling each transcript segment with the speaker who talks over most of it.
classes.remarks: This is pure data processing with no model or media dependency: it pairs the timed text a SpeechToTextBlock produces with the SpeakerSegment timeline a SpeakerDiarizationBlock produces, so the two on-device AI blocks combine into a "who said what" transcript. Attribution is by maximum temporal overlap; ties go to the lower speaker id.

methods.name: Build
methods.summary: Labels each transcript segment with the speaker id that overlaps it the most.

parameters.name: transcript
parameters.summary: The transcript segments as (start, end, text) tuples. Order is preserved in the output.

methods.returns: The transcript segments, each labeled with the best-overlapping speaker id, or -1 when no turn overlaps.

methods.name: BestSpeaker
methods.summary: Finds the speaker id whose turns overlap the interval [start, end) the most.
methods.returns: The best-overlapping speaker id, or -1 when no turn overlaps and the interval is empty of speech.

methods.name: OverlapTicks
methods.summary: Computes the overlap, in TimeSpan ticks, between two time intervals.
methods.returns: The overlap in ticks, or 0 when the intervals are disjoint.

classes.name: DiarizedTranscriptSegment
classes.summary: A transcript segment labeled with the speaker who most overlaps it — the output of DiarizedTranscriptBuilder merging a speech-to-text transcript with a diarization timeline.

constructors.name: DiarizedTranscriptSegment
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the DiarizedTranscriptSegment class.

parameters.name: start
parameters.summary: The start time of the transcript segment.

parameters.name: end
parameters.summary: The end time of the transcript segment.

parameters.name: speakerId
parameters.summary: The attributed speaker id, or -1 when no diarization turn overlaps the segment.

properties.name: Start
properties.summary: Gets the start time of the transcript segment.

properties.name: End
properties.summary: Gets the end time of the transcript segment.

properties.name: Text
properties.summary: Gets the recognized text.

properties.name: SpeakerId
properties.summary: Gets the attributed speaker id, or -1 when no diarization turn overlaps this segment.

methods.name: ToString
methods.summary: Returns a readable representation of the labeled segment.
methods.returns: A string with the speaker label, time span, and text.

classes.name: FaceGallery
classes.summary: An in-memory gallery of enrolled face identities used for 1:N face recognition. Each identity holds one or more L2-normalized face embeddings; a query embedding is matched by cosine similarity (the maximum over all stored embeddings of all identities). The gallery is thread-safe and can be persisted to and loaded from disk.
classes.remarks: Embeddings are produced by a face recognizer; use a recognition block's enrollment API (for example FaceRecognitionBlock.Enroll), which computes and stores the embedding for you. All embeddings in one gallery must share the same dimension (the same embedding model); enrolling a vector of a different length throws. Switching the embedding model requires a separate gallery.

properties.name: Count
properties.summary: Gets the number of enrolled identities.

methods.name: GetNames
methods.summary: Gets the names of the enrolled identities.
methods.returns: A snapshot array of the enrolled identity names.

methods.name: Add
methods.summary: Adds an embedding for the given identity. Multiple embeddings can be enrolled per identity (for example from several photos) to improve robustness. The embedding is L2-normalized before storage.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The identity name. Must not be null or empty.

parameters.name: embedding
parameters.summary: The face embedding vector. Must not be null or empty and must have a non-zero magnitude.

methods.name: Remove
methods.summary: Removes all embeddings of the given identity.
methods.returns: true if the identity existed and was removed; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Clear
methods.summary: Removes all enrolled identities.

methods.name: Identify
methods.summary: Finds the best-matching identity for a query embedding by cosine similarity.

parameters.name: embedding
parameters.summary: The query embedding (any magnitude; it is normalized internally).

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.summary: The minimum cosine similarity to report a match.

parameters.name: score
parameters.summary: Receives the best cosine similarity found (even if below the threshold), or 0 when the gallery is empty.

methods.returns: The best-matching identity name when its score meets threshold; otherwise null.

methods.name: Save
methods.summary: Saves the gallery to a binary file. Overwrites an existing file.

methods.name: Load
methods.summary: Loads the gallery from a binary file, replacing the current contents.

classes.name: FaceRecognitionSettings
classes.summary: Settings for the face recognition (face identity) block. The block runs a two-stage pipeline: a face detector (YuNet) locates faces and their five landmarks, each face is aligned to a canonical 112x112 crop and turned into an embedding (SFace / ArcFace), and the embedding is matched 1:N against an enrolled FaceGallery by cosine similarity.
classes.remarks: The default models are the OpenCV Zoo YuNet detector (MIT) and SFace recognizer (Apache-2.0), which are designed to work together (SFace aligns with YuNet's five landmarks). Model weights are not shipped with the SDK; point DetectorModelPath and EmbeddingModelPath at the ONNX files.

constructors.name: FaceRecognitionSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the FaceRecognitionSettings class.

constructors.name: FaceRecognitionSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the FaceRecognitionSettings class with model paths.

properties.name: DetectorModelPath
properties.summary: Gets or sets the path to the face-detection ONNX model (YuNet). Required.

properties.name: EmbeddingModelPath
properties.summary: Gets or sets the path to the face-embedding ONNX model (SFace / ArcFace). Required.

properties.name: EmbeddingModel
properties.summary: Gets or sets the embedding model family, which selects the aligned-crop preprocessing. Defaults to SFace.

properties.name: Gallery
properties.summary: Gets or sets the enrolled face gallery the detected faces are matched against. When null or empty, faces are detected and embedded but reported as unknown (no identity).

properties.name: Provider
properties.summary: Gets or sets the execution provider. Defaults to Auto.

properties.name: DeviceId
properties.summary: Gets or sets the hardware device id for CUDA / DirectML. Defaults to 0.

properties.name: FramesToSkip
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of frames to skip between recognitions on live video. 0 processes every frame.

properties.name: DetectionInputSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the square input size, in pixels, the frame is letterboxed into for the detector. Must be a multiple of 32 (YuNet requirement); non-multiples are rounded up internally. Defaults to 320.

properties.name: DetectionConfidenceThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum detection score (0..1) a face must reach to be kept. Defaults to 0.6.

properties.name: NmsThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the IoU threshold (0..1) used to suppress overlapping face boxes. Defaults to 0.3.

properties.name: MaxFaces
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of faces to detect per frame. Defaults to 20.

properties.name: RecognitionThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum cosine similarity (typically 0..1) an embedding must reach against a gallery entry to be reported as that identity. Defaults to 0.36 (the SFace same-identity threshold).

properties.name: DrawResults
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether recognized faces are drawn into the video frame. Defaults to true.

properties.name: DrawLandmarks
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the five facial landmarks are drawn for each face. Defaults to false.

properties.name: BoxColor
properties.summary: Gets or sets the color used for face boxes and labels when DrawResults is enabled. Defaults to lime green.

properties.name: BoxThickness
properties.summary: Gets or sets the stroke thickness, in pixels, of the face boxes. Defaults to 2.

properties.name: LabelFontSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the label font size, in pixels. A value of 0 auto-scales the font to the frame height. Defaults to 0.

classes.name: FrameEmbeddingIndex
classes.summary: An in-memory index of per-frame CLIP embeddings used for semantic video search. Each entry stores a frame's presentation timestamp, the source tag it came from, and the embedding vector produced by a VideoEmbeddingBlock. A query embedding (for example the CLIP text embedding of a natural-language phrase) is matched by cosine similarity and the closest frames are returned. The index is thread-safe and can be persisted to and loaded from disk.
classes.remarks: All embeddings in one index must share the same dimension (the same CLIP model); adding a vector of a different length throws. Cosine similarity is computed by normalizing both the stored vector and the query, so raw (unnormalized) vectors are matched correctly as well; embeddings produced by the block are already L2-normalized. The on-disk format is a compact binary layout with a 'VFEI' magic header and a version number so a future format change is detectable.

properties.name: Count
properties.summary: Gets the number of indexed frame embeddings.

properties.name: Dimension
properties.summary: Gets the embedding dimension shared by every vector in the index, or 0 when the index is empty.

methods.name: Add
methods.summary: Adds a frame embedding to the index. The first embedding added fixes the index dimension; every later embedding must match it.

parameters.name: timestamp
parameters.summary: The presentation timestamp of the frame within its source.

parameters.name: sourceTag
parameters.summary: The source tag to associate with the frame (for example a file name). May be null.

parameters.name: embedding
parameters.summary: The frame embedding vector. Must not be null or empty. A copy is stored.

methods.name: Search
methods.summary: Finds the frames whose embeddings are most similar to a query embedding by cosine similarity, highest first.

parameters.name: query
parameters.summary: The query embedding (any magnitude; it is normalized internally).

parameters.name: topK
parameters.summary: The maximum number of results to return. Values > the entry count return every entry.

methods.returns: The top matches sorted by descending cosine similarity; an empty array when the index is empty, the query is null/empty or its length differs from the index dimension, or topK is not positive.

methods.name: Clear
methods.summary: Removes all indexed embeddings and resets the index dimension.

methods.name: Save
methods.summary: Saves the index to a binary file. Overwrites an existing file.

methods.name: Load
methods.summary: Loads the index from a binary file, replacing the current contents.

classes.name: FrameEmbeddingSearchResult
classes.summary: A single hit returned by Int32): the video timestamp of an indexed frame, the source tag it was indexed under, and the cosine similarity score against the query embedding.

constructors.name: FrameEmbeddingSearchResult
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the FrameEmbeddingSearchResult class.

parameters.name: timestamp
parameters.summary: The presentation timestamp of the indexed frame.

parameters.name: sourceTag
parameters.summary: The source tag the frame was indexed under (may be null or empty).

parameters.name: score
parameters.summary: The cosine similarity (typically -1..1) of the frame embedding against the query.

properties.name: Timestamp
properties.summary: Gets the presentation timestamp of the indexed frame within its source.

properties.name: SourceTag
properties.summary: Gets the source tag the frame was indexed under (for example a file name or camera id). May be null or empty.

properties.name: Score
properties.summary: Gets the cosine similarity of this frame's embedding against the query embedding. Higher means more similar.

classes.name: LicensePlateRecognizerSettings
classes.summary: Settings for the license plate recognizer (ANPR/LPR) block. The block runs a specialized two-stage pipeline: a dedicated license-plate detector (YOLO) locates plates in the frame, then a plate-specific OCR model reads the characters of each cropped plate.
classes.remarks: Both models come from the FastALPR family (MIT): a YOLOv9-T plate detector and a fast-plate-ocr recognition head. A global head covers the USA and 90+ countries; a European head is tuned for EU plates. The recognition model's geometry (RGB/grayscale, input size) and alphabet are read from the model itself, so selecting a region is simply a matter of pointing RecognitionModelPath at that head.

classes.name: LineZoneSettings
classes.summary: Settings for a directed line (tripwire) zone.
classes.remarks: Coordinates are in source-frame pixels. The directed line is Start -> End. Signed side is (End - Start) x (Point - Start). Stable negative-to-positive movement is In. Stable positive-to-negative movement is Out. Crossing the infinite extension outside the finite segment is not a crossing.

properties.name: Id
properties.summary: Gets or sets the unique identifier for this line zone. Required.

properties.name: Start
properties.summary: Gets or sets the start point of the directed line, in source-frame pixels.

properties.name: End
properties.summary: Gets or sets the end point of the directed line, in source-frame pixels.

properties.name: Anchor
properties.summary: Gets or sets which point of the detection bounding box is used as the reference anchor for crossing evaluation. Defaults to BottomCenter.

properties.name: DeadbandPixels
properties.summary: Gets or sets the deadband distance in pixels. Anchor movement within this perpendicular distance from the line does not change the stable side and does not produce crossings. Defaults to 2.

properties.name: Color
properties.summary: Gets or sets the color used to draw this line and its counters. Defaults to Yellow.

properties.name: UseNormalizedCoordinates
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether Start and End are expressed in normalized 0..1 coordinates (fraction of frame width/height). When true, coordinates are multiplied by the frame dimensions at runtime. Defaults to false (source-frame pixels).

classes.name: ObjectAnalyticsSettings
classes.summary: Aggregate settings for the object analytics block, combining detector, tracker, filter, overlay, line-zone, and polygon-zone configuration.
classes.remarks: The detector's ConfidenceThreshold is overridden at runtime by LowConfidenceThreshold (default 0.1f). ByteTrack requires low-confidence detections for its second association pass — high-confidence-only detection would miss recovering temporarily occluded tracks. Set Tracker's LowConfidenceThreshold to a higher value if you want fewer low-confidence candidates fed to the tracker.

constructors.name: ObjectAnalyticsSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the ObjectAnalyticsSettings class from a pipeline document.
constructors.remarks: Non-public and not parameterless-by-accident: "[JsonConstructor]" is what lets System.Text.Json build this type at all, because two public constructors and no parameterless one is refused outright, and the two public ones cannot be told apart by name - both take a parameter called "detector", of different types. The parameters are optional so neither detector becomes a required member of a payload, and the type's contract - exactly one detector - is enforced here instead, as a JsonException the materializer reports with the block's id. This is the only door a document comes through, so it is also what keeps the block from being handed settings whose detector is null.

classes.name: OcrSettings
classes.summary: Settings for the OCR block, which runs a multi-stage PaddleOCR (PP-OCR) pipeline on video frames: text detection (DBNet) → optional angle classification → text-line recognition (CRNN/SVTR + CTC).
classes.remarks: Unlike a single-model detector, OCR needs three ONNX models plus a recognizer character dictionary. Provide them via DetectionModelPath, RecognitionModelPath, CharacterDictionaryPath, and optionally ClassificationModelPath. The Apache-2.0 licensed PP-OCRv5 mobile models are a good default; the dictionary must match the recognition model's language.

constructors.name: OcrSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the OcrSettings class.

constructors.name: OcrSettings
