properties.summary: Gets the loudness range in LU. Present when LoudnessRange is enabled.
properties.value: The loudness range, or .

classes.name: EchoAudioEffect
classes.summary: Echo audio effect creates echo/delay effects by repeating the audio signal with configurable delay, intensity, and feedback. Uses the GStreamer 'audioecho' element to produce single or multiple echo repetitions.
classes.remarks: GStreamer element: audioecho Properties: - delay: Time delay between original and echo (in nanoseconds internally) - max-delay: Maximum delay buffer size (must be ≥ delay) - intensity: Volume level of the echo (0.0 to 1.0) - feedback: Amount of echo fed back into the effect (0.0 to 1.0) - creates multiple repeating echoes Higher feedback values create longer echo tails with multiple repetitions.

constructors.name: EchoAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the EchoAudioEffect class.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.summary: The echo delay time. Typical values range from 50ms to 500ms.

properties.name: Delay
properties.summary: Gets or sets the delay time between the original signal and the echo. Typical values: 50ms (short slap-back) to 500ms (long echo). Can be changed during playback.
properties.value: The echo delay time.

properties.name: MaxDelay
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum delay buffer size. Must be equal to or greater than the Delay value. This allocates buffer space for the delay line. Can only be changed when the pipeline is in Pause or Stop state.
properties.value: The maximum delay time allowed.

properties.name: Feedback
properties.summary: Gets or sets the feedback amount that controls how much of the echo is fed back into the effect. Range: 0.0 (single echo) to 1.0 (infinite repetitions). Higher values create longer echo tails. Typical values: 0.0-0.3 for short tails, 0.4-0.6 for medium, 0.7+ for long tails.
properties.value: The feedback amount (0.0 to 1.0).

properties.name: Intensity
properties.summary: Gets or sets the intensity (volume level) of the echo relative to the original signal. Range: 0.0 (no echo) to 1.0 (echo at same volume as original). Typical values: 0.3-0.7 for natural-sounding echoes.
properties.value: The echo intensity (0.0 to 1.0).

methods.name: GenerateDescription
methods.summary: Generates the description.
methods.returns: A string representation of the audio effect parameters.

classes.name: Equalizer10AudioEffect
classes.summary: 10-band graphic equalizer for precise frequency control across the audio spectrum. Uses the GStreamer 'equalizer-10bands' element with fixed center frequencies. Each band can be adjusted independently to shape the tonal balance of audio.
classes.remarks: GStreamer element: equalizer-10bands Each band has a fixed center frequency and adjustable gain. Band frequencies (approximate): - Band 0: 29 Hz (Sub-bass) - Band 1: 59 Hz (Bass) - Band 2: 119 Hz (Upper bass) - Band 3: 237 Hz (Low midrange) - Band 4: 474 Hz (Midrange) - Band 5: 947 Hz (Upper midrange) - Band 6: 1889 Hz (Presence) - Band 7: 3770 Hz (Upper presence) - Band 8: 7523 Hz (Brilliance) - Band 9: 15011 Hz (Air/sparkle) Gain range per band: -24 dB (cut) to +12 dB (boost) Common EQ curves: - Vocal clarity: Boost bands 4-6, cut bands 1-2 - Bass boost: Boost bands 0-2 - Presence: Boost bands 6-7 - De-essing: Cut band 8-9 - Phone/radio: Cut bands 0-1 and 8-9

constructors.name: Equalizer10AudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the Equalizer10AudioEffect class.

parameters.name: levels
parameters.summary: Array of 10 gain levels in dB for each band. Range: -24 dB (cut) to +12 dB (boost) per band. Band order: 29Hz, 59Hz, 119Hz, 237Hz, 474Hz, 947Hz, 1889Hz, 3770Hz, 7523Hz, 15011Hz.

properties.name: Levels
properties.summary: Gets or sets the gain levels for all 10 equalizer bands. Array must contain exactly 10 values corresponding to the 10 frequency bands. Range: -24 dB (maximum cut) to +12 dB (maximum boost) per band. 0 dB means no change for that frequency band.
properties.value: Array of 10 gain values in dB.

methods.name: GenerateDescription
methods.summary: Generates the description.
methods.returns: A string representation of the audio effect parameters.

classes.name: Equalizer10Settings
classes.summary: Settings for Equalizer10Block. The block keeps its band gains in a private array reachable only through SetBand; this type is the serializable form of that state, so a pipeline document can carry a configured equalizer curve.

properties.name: Bands
properties.summary: Gets or sets the gain of every band, in decibels, from -24 dB to +12 dB; a value outside that range is clamped, because the underlying GStreamer property rejects it with a log line and keeps its old value. The array is always BandCount entries long; a shorter array is padded with 0 dB and a longer one is truncated. Band centers: 29, 59, 119, 237, 474, 947, 1889, 3770, 7523 and 15011 Hz. Default is a flat response. The getter returns a copy: writing through it - settings.Bands[3] = 6 - changes nothing. Assign a whole array to change the curve.

methods.name: CreateBlock
methods.summary: Creates an Equalizer10Block configured from these settings.
methods.returns: The configured block.

classes.name: EqualizerParametricAudioEffect
classes.summary: Parametric n-band audio equalizer with adjustable frequency, Q (bandwidth), and gain for each band. Provides more precise and flexible frequency control compared to graphic equalizers. Ideal for surgical EQ adjustments, feedback elimination, and professional audio work.
classes.remarks: Unlike graphic equalizers with fixed frequencies, parametric EQ allows you to: 1. Choose the exact center frequency for each band 2. Adjust the bandwidth (Q factor) to target narrow or wide frequency ranges 3. Boost or cut by any amount within limits Q Factor (bandwidth) guidelines: - Low Q (0.5-1.0): Wide bandwidth, affects broad frequency range (musical, gentle) - Medium Q (1.0-3.0): Moderate bandwidth (typical for general EQ) - High Q (5.0-10.0+): Narrow bandwidth (surgical cuts, feedback elimination) Common uses: - Feedback elimination: High Q, narrow cuts at problem frequencies - Vocal de-essing: Narrow cut at 5-8 kHz - Bass tightening: Narrow cut at 100-200 Hz - Presence boost: Wide boost at 2-5 kHz - Air enhancement: Wide boost at 10-15 kHz Each band is independently configurable via ParametricEqualizerBand objects. Call Update after modifying bands to apply changes during playback.

constructors.name: EqualizerParametricAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the EqualizerParametricAudioEffect class.

parameters.name: numBands
parameters.summary: Number of equalizer bands to create. Range: 1 to 64. More bands provide finer control but use more CPU. Typical values: 3-5 bands for general use, 8-12 for professional mixing.

properties.name: Bands
properties.summary: Gets the array of equalizer bands. Each band can be configured with frequency, Q (bandwidth), and gain. Access individual bands by index to set their parameters. After modifying band parameters, call Update to apply changes.
properties.value: Array of ParametricEqualizerBand objects.

methods.name: Update
methods.summary: Updates the equalizer with the current band settings. Must be called after modifying any band parameters in the Bands array to apply the changes to the audio processing pipeline. Can be called during playback to adjust EQ in real-time.

classes.name: FadeAudioEffect
classes.summary: Creates smooth volume transitions (fade-in/fade-out) over specified time periods. Gradually changes volume between two levels across a defined time range for professional audio transitions. Essential for smooth intro/outro effects and preventing audio pops or clicks. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.
classes.remarks: Fade-in: Low start volume to higher stop volume.Fade-out: High start volume to lower stop volume.Can create custom fade curves by adjusting start/stop values.Time range defines when the fade begins and ends in the audio stream.

constructors.name: FadeAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the FadeAudioEffect class.

parameters.name: startVolume
parameters.summary: Volume level at the fade start time.

parameters.name: stopVolume
parameters.summary: Volume level at the fade end time.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: Time position when the fade begins.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: Time position when the fade completes.

properties.name: StartVolume
properties.summary: Gets or sets the volume level at the fade start time.
properties.value: The starting volume. For fade-in, use low value; for fade-out, use high value.

properties.name: StopVolume
properties.summary: Gets or sets the volume level at the fade end time.
properties.value: The ending volume. For fade-in, use high value; for fade-out, use low value (often 0 for silence).

properties.name: StartTime
properties.summary: Gets or sets the time position when the fade effect begins.
properties.value: The start time. Audio before this time plays at the start volume.

properties.name: StopTime
properties.summary: Gets or sets the time position when the fade effect completes.
properties.value: The stop time. Audio after this time maintains the stop volume.

classes.name: FlangerAudioEffect
classes.summary: Flanger audio effect creates a sweeping, "jet plane" sound by mixing the audio signal with a delayed copy of itself. The delay time is modulated by a low-frequency oscillator (LFO), creating the characteristic swooshing effect. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.
classes.remarks: GStreamer element: audioflanger (custom implementation) The flanger effect is created by: 1. Delaying the audio signal by a time-varying amount 2. The delay time oscillates at the specified frequency 3. The delayed signal can be phase-inverted before mixing for different tonal characteristics Typical delay times: 1-10ms, Typical frequency: 0.1-2 Hz

constructors.name: FlangerAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the FlangerAudioEffect class.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.summary: The base delay time. Typical range: 1-10 milliseconds. This determines the depth of the flanger effect.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.summary: The LFO (Low Frequency Oscillator) rate that modulates the delay. Typical range: 0.1-2 Hz. Higher values create faster sweeps.

parameters.name: phaseInvert
parameters.summary: If true, inverts the phase of the delayed signal before mixing, creating a different tonal character (often more hollow/resonant).

properties.name: Delay
properties.summary: Gets or sets the base delay time that is modulated to create the flanger effect. Typical range: 1-10 milliseconds. Shorter delays create sharper, more metallic sounds. Longer delays create deeper, more pronounced sweeps. In the X engines it is kept between one sample and 5 seconds.
properties.value: The delay time.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Gets or sets the frequency of the Low Frequency Oscillator (LFO) that modulates the delay time. Typical range: 0.1-2 Hz. Lower values (0.1-0.5 Hz) create slow, sweeping effects. Higher values (1-2 Hz) create faster, more vibrato-like modulation.
properties.value: The LFO frequency in Hz.

properties.name: PhaseInvert
properties.summary: Gets or sets whether the delayed signal should have its phase inverted before mixing with the original. When true, creates a more hollow, resonant character with notch filtering effects. When false, creates a more subtle, chorus-like effect with peak filtering.
properties.value: true to invert phase; otherwise, false.

classes.name: HighPassAudioEffect
classes.summary: High-pass audio filter that attenuates frequencies below a specified cutoff frequency. Allows high frequencies to pass through while progressively removing low frequencies. Also known as a low-cut filter. Essential for removing rumble, reducing muddiness, and improving clarity. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.
classes.remarks: High-pass filters are fundamental audio processing tools used to: - Remove unwanted low-frequency content (rumble, handling noise, wind) - Reduce muddiness in mixes by cleaning up low-mid frequencies - Improve clarity by preventing low-frequency buildup - Prepare audio for speakers that can't reproduce very low frequencies - Create "thin" or "tinny" effects at higher cutoff frequencies Common cutoff frequencies: - 20-40 Hz: Remove sub-sonic rumble only (most transparent) - 60-80 Hz: Remove low-end rumble and hum (typical for vocals) - 100-150 Hz: Reduce bass for clarity in dense mixes - 150-250 Hz: Thin out sound, reduce warmth (electric guitars, vocals) - 300-500 Hz: Aggressive thinning, "telephone" effect - 1000+ Hz: Extreme filtering, removes most frequency content Applications by source: - Vocals: 80-150 Hz (remove proximity effect, muddiness) - Acoustic guitar: 80-120 Hz (clarity without losing body) - Electric guitar: 100-200 Hz (definition in mix) - Snare drum: 80-120 Hz (remove rumble, improve crack) - Overhead mics: 200-400 Hz (reduce cymbal bleed from kit) Note: In the X engines this runs on ChebyshevLimitAudioEffect with its default settings, and the cut-off has to be below half the sample rate. Use that effect to control the slope.

constructors.name: HighPassAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the HighPassAudioEffect class.

parameters.name: cutOff
parameters.summary: The cutoff frequency in Hz. Frequencies below this are progressively attenuated. Typical range: 20 Hz (minimal filtering) to 500 Hz (aggressive filtering). For most uses, 60-150 Hz is appropriate.

properties.name: CutOff
properties.summary: Gets or sets the cutoff frequency below which frequencies are attenuated. The filter starts to reduce the amplitude of frequencies below this point. The rate of attenuation increases further below the cutoff (typically 12-24 dB/octave). Guidelines by application: - Sub-sonic filtering: 20-30 Hz (removes inaudible content only) - General cleanup: 40-80 Hz (typical for most sources) - Vocal clarity: 80-120 Hz (removes muddiness, proximity effect) - Instrument definition: 100-200 Hz (improve clarity in mix) - Thinning effect: 200-400 Hz (reduce body, create space) - Special effects: 500+ Hz (radio/telephone effect, dramatic thinning) Start with lower values and increase gradually while monitoring the sound. Excessive high-pass filtering can make audio sound thin, hollow, or unnatural.
properties.value: The cutoff frequency in Hz.

classes.name: HRTFRenderAudioEffect
classes.summary: Head-Related Transfer Function (HRTF) spatial audio rendering effect from the rsaudiofx GStreamer plugin. Renders spatial audio using HRTF data for 3D positional audio. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.

constructors.name: HRTFRenderAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the HRTFRenderAudioEffect class.

parameters.name: hrirFile
parameters.summary: The path to the HRIR (Head-Related Impulse Response) file.

constructors.name: HRTFRenderAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the HRTFRenderAudioEffect class with default values.

parameters.name: hrirFile
parameters.summary: The path to the HRIR (Head-Related Impulse Response) file.

constructors.name: HRTFRenderAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the HRTFRenderAudioEffect class with empty HRIR file.

properties.name: HrirFile
properties.summary: Gets or sets the path to the HRIR (Head-Related Impulse Response) file. This file contains the spatial audio data for HRTF rendering.
properties.value: The HRIR file path.

properties.name: InterpolationSteps
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of interpolation steps. Higher values provide smoother transitions but use more CPU. Default: 8.
properties.value: The interpolation steps.

properties.name: BlockLength
properties.summary: Gets or sets the block length for processing. Determines the size of audio blocks processed at once. Default: 512.
properties.value: The block length.

classes.name: ISharedAudioEffectX
classes.summary: Common interface for audio effects, providing identification and naming.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets or sets the display name of the audio effect.
properties.value: The effect name used for identification in the pipeline.

properties.name: ID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio effect type identifier.
properties.value: The AudioEffectID value identifying the effect type.

classes.name: IVideoEditXAudioEffect
classes.summary: Interface for audio effects that can generate a GStreamer pipeline description string. Used by video editing pipelines to serialize effect parameters.

methods.name: GenerateDescription
methods.summary: Generates a GStreamer pipeline description string representing this audio effect and its current parameters.
methods.returns: A GStreamer element description string (e.g., "audioecho delay=500000000 intensity=0.50").

classes.name: KaraokeAudioEffect
classes.summary: Karaoke effect removes or reduces center-panned vocals from stereo audio by filtering the center channel. Uses the GStreamer 'audiokaraoke' element to analyze and suppress mono (center) content. Useful for vocal removal, karaoke track creation, or isolating background music.
classes.remarks: GStreamer element: audiokaraoke Properties: - level: Overall effect strength (0.0 to 1.0, where 1.0 = maximum vocal removal) - mono-level: Suppression level for mono/center content (0.0 to 1.0) - filter-band: Center frequency of the filter band in Hz (typically 100-400 Hz) - filter-width: Width of the frequency band to process in Hz The effect works by: 1. Identifying content that's identical in left and right channels (center-panned) 2. Applying frequency-selective filtering to target vocal ranges 3. Reducing or removing the identified center content Works best on: - Studio recordings with center-panned vocals - Professional mixes with clear stereo separation Less effective on: - Live recordings - Mono or pseudo-stereo sources - Vocals with heavy stereo processing

constructors.name: KaraokeAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the KaraokeAudioEffect class.

properties.name: FilterBand
properties.summary: Gets or sets the center frequency of the filter band. This defines the frequency range where vocal removal is most effective. Range: Typically 100-400 Hz. Default: 220 Hz (middle of typical vocal fundamental range). Lower values target deeper voices, higher values target higher voices.
properties.value: The filter band center frequency in Hz.

properties.name: FilterWidth
properties.summary: Gets or sets the width of the frequency band to filter. This determines how wide a frequency range around FilterBand will be affected. Range: Typically 50-200 Hz. Default: 100 Hz. Wider bands remove more frequency content but may affect instruments. Narrower bands are more selective but may miss some vocal content.
properties.value: The filter width in Hz.

properties.name: Level
properties.summary: Gets or sets the overall level of the karaoke effect. Controls how strongly center-panned content is suppressed. Range: 0.0 (no effect) to 1.0 (maximum suppression). Default: 1.0. Lower values (0.3-0.6) reduce vocals subtly. Higher values (0.8-1.0) attempt complete vocal removal.
properties.value: The effect level (0.0 to 1.0).

properties.name: MonoLevel
properties.summary: Gets or sets the suppression level for mono/center channel content. Specifically targets audio that appears identically in both stereo channels. Range: 0.0 (no suppression) to 1.0 (complete suppression). Default: 1.0. This is the primary control for vocal removal strength.
properties.value: The mono channel suppression level (0.0 to 1.0).

methods.name: GenerateDescription
methods.summary: Generates the description.
methods.returns: A string representation of the audio effect parameters.

classes.name: LowPassAudioEffect
classes.summary: Low-pass audio filter that attenuates frequencies above a specified cutoff frequency. Allows low frequencies to pass through while progressively removing high frequencies. Also known as a high-cut filter. Used for removing harshness, controlling brightness, creating warmth, or special effects. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.
classes.remarks: Low-pass filters are fundamental audio processing tools used to: - Remove unwanted high-frequency content (hiss, digital artifacts, sibilance) - Reduce harshness and brightness in audio - Create warmth and smoothness - Simulate analog tape or vintage equipment - Create "muffled" or "underwater" effects - Control resonance and feedback in live sound Common cutoff frequencies: - 15000-20000 Hz: Remove only ultra-high frequencies (subtle, transparent) - 10000-15000 Hz: Reduce air/sparkle, gentle de-essing - 8000-10000 Hz: Noticeably warmer, reduced sibilance - 5000-8000 Hz: Clear warmth, "vintage" character - 3000-5000 Hz: "Telephone" or "radio" effect, significant dulling - 1000-3000 Hz: Very muffled, underwater effect - Below 1000 Hz: Extreme filtering, removes most harmonic content Applications by source: - Harsh vocals: 8000-12000 Hz (de-essing, smoothness) - Cymbals: 10000-15000 Hz (reduce excessive brightness) - Bass synth: 2000-5000 Hz (focus on fundamentals) - Mix bus: 18000-20000 Hz (subtle "analog" warmth) - String section: 8000-10000 Hz (reduce scratchiness) Creative effects: - Lo-fi/vintage: 5000-8000 Hz - Telephone: 3000-3500 Hz - AM radio: 4000-5000 Hz - Underwater: 1000-2000 Hz - Old record: 6000-8000 Hz with gentle slope Note: In the X engines this runs on ChebyshevLimitAudioEffect with its default settings, and the cut-off has to be below half the sample rate. Use that effect to control the slope.

constructors.name: LowPassAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the LowPassAudioEffect class.

parameters.name: cutOff
parameters.summary: The cutoff frequency in Hz. Frequencies above this are progressively attenuated. Typical range: 1000 Hz (extreme muffling) to 15000 Hz (subtle filtering). For most uses, 5000-10000 Hz is appropriate.

properties.name: CutOff
properties.summary: Gets or sets the cutoff frequency above which frequencies are attenuated. The filter starts to reduce the amplitude of frequencies above this point. The rate of attenuation increases further above the cutoff (typically 12-24 dB/octave). Guidelines by application: - Gentle air reduction: 15000-18000 Hz (barely noticeable) - De-essing: 10000-12000 Hz (reduces sibilance) - Warmth: 8000-10000 Hz (vintage, analog character) - Obvious darkening: 5000-8000 Hz (reduced presence) - Special effects: 3000-5000 Hz (telephone, radio) - Extreme muffling: 1000-3000 Hz (underwater, distant) Mixing considerations: - Vocals: 10000-15000 Hz (smooth harsh recordings) - Guitars: 8000-12000 Hz (reduce pick noise, harshness) - Drums (overheads): 12000-15000 Hz (control cymbal brightness) - Bass: 3000-5000 Hz (remove clank/fret noise) - Synth pads: 8000-10000 Hz (smooth, warm pads) Start with higher cutoff values and lower gradually while listening. Excessive filtering can make audio sound dull, muffled, or lifeless. Use in combination with high-pass filtering for complete frequency shaping.
properties.value: The cutoff frequency in Hz.

classes.name: NotchAudioEffect
classes.summary: Notch filter (band-stop filter) that attenuates a narrow frequency band. Ideal for removing specific frequency interference like 50/60 Hz hum or feedback. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.
classes.remarks: Creates a dip in the frequency response at the specified frequency. In the X engines the dip reaches 10% of that frequency to either side.Frequencies above and below the notch frequency pass through relatively unchanged.Common applications: removing AC hum (50/60 Hz), eliminating feedback frequencies, removing tonal noise.

constructors.name: NotchAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the NotchAudioEffect class.

parameters.name: cutOff
parameters.summary: Center frequency in Hz where maximum attenuation occurs. This is the frequency to be removed.

properties.name: CutOff
properties.summary: Gets or sets the center frequency of the notch filter in Hz.
properties.value: The notch center frequency. This frequency and a narrow band around it are attenuated. Typical values: 50/60 Hz for hum removal.

classes.name: ParametricEqualizerBand
classes.summary: Defines a single band for a parametric equalizer, with center frequency, bandwidth, and gain.

constructors.name: ParametricEqualizerBand
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the ParametricEqualizerBand class with default values.

constructors.name: ParametricEqualizerBand
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the ParametricEqualizerBand class.

parameters.name: gain
parameters.summary: The gain in dB. Positive boosts, negative cuts.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Gets or sets the center frequency of this band.
properties.value: The center frequency in Hz.

properties.name: Width
properties.summary: Gets or sets the bandwidth of this band.
properties.value: The bandwidth in Hz. Wider values affect a broader frequency range.

properties.name: Gain
properties.summary: Gets or sets the gain for this band.
properties.value: The gain in dB. Positive values boost, negative values cut.

classes.name: PhaseInvertAudioEffect
classes.summary: Inverts the phase (polarity) of audio signal by 180 degrees. Multiplies the audio waveform by -1, effectively flipping it vertically. Used for phase correction, cancelling audio signals, or creative stereo effects. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.
classes.remarks: Simple phase inversion (multiply by -1).Commonly used to fix out-of-phase recordings or microphone setups.When combined with original signal, creates complete cancellation (silence).Essential tool for stereo field manipulation and phase-related problem solving.

constructors.name: PhaseInvertAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the PhaseInvertAudioEffect class.

classes.name: PhaserAudioEffect
classes.summary: Classic phaser effect that creates sweeping, swirling tones through phase shifting. Modulates the phase of audio frequencies using an LFO (Low Frequency Oscillator). Popular in rock and electronic music for its distinctive "swooshing" sound. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.
classes.remarks: LFO (Low Frequency Oscillator) controls the speed of the phasing sweep.More stages create a more pronounced, dramatic phasing effect.Feedback parameter determines how much processed signal is fed back into the input.DryWetRatio controls the balance between original and processed audio.

constructors.name: PhaserAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the PhaserAudioEffect class.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.summary: Phaser sweep depth. Valid range: 0-255. Higher values create more dramatic phase shifts.

parameters.name: dryWetRatio
parameters.summary: Dry/wet mix ratio. Valid range: 0-255. 0 = completely dry (original), 255 = completely wet (effected).

parameters.name: feedback
parameters.summary: Feedback amount. Valid range: 0 to 100. 0 = no feedback, higher values create stronger resonant peaks.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.summary: LFO frequency in Hz. Controls the speed of the phasing sweep. Typical values: 0.1 to 5 Hz.

parameters.name: stages
parameters.summary: Number of phaser stages. Recommended range: 2-24. More stages = more pronounced effect.

parameters.name: startPhase
parameters.summary: LFO start phase in radians. Used for stereo phasing effects to create width.

properties.name: Depth
properties.summary: Gets or sets the phaser sweep depth.
properties.value: The depth. Valid range: 0-255. Higher values produce more dramatic sweeping effects.

properties.name: DryWetRatio
properties.summary: Gets or sets the dry/wet mix ratio.
properties.value: The dry/wet ratio. Valid range: 0 (completely dry, original) to 255 (completely wet, effected). Typical value: 128 for equal mix.

properties.name: Feedback
properties.summary: Gets or sets the feedback amount for resonance.
properties.value: The feedback. Valid range: 0 to 100. 0 = no feedback, higher values create stronger resonant peaks.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Gets or sets the LFO (Low Frequency Oscillator) frequency that controls sweep speed.
properties.value: The LFO frequency in Hz. Typical range: 0.1 to 5 Hz. Lower = slower sweep, higher = faster sweep.

properties.name: Stages
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of phaser stages (all-pass filter stages).
properties.value: The stages count. Recommended range: 2 to 24. More stages create a more pronounced, dramatic phasing effect.

properties.name: StartPhase
properties.summary: Gets or sets the LFO start phase in radians for stereo width.
properties.value: The start phase in radians. Used to create stereo phasing effects by offsetting the phase between left and right channels.

classes.name: PitchAudioEffect
classes.summary: Pitch audio effect changes the pitch of audio without affecting playback speed. Uses the GStreamer 'pitch' element from the soundtouch library. Supports pitch shifting, tempo adjustment, and rate control independently.
classes.remarks: GStreamer element: pitch (from soundtouch plugin) Properties: - pitch: Pitch multiplier (0.5 = one octave down, 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = one octave up) - tempo: Tempo multiplier (1.0 = no change) - rate: Rate multiplier (1.0 = no change)

constructors.name: PitchAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the PitchAudioEffect class.

properties.name: Pitch
properties.summary: Gets or sets the pitch multiplier. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = one octave up, 0.5 = one octave down.
properties.value: The pitch multiplier. Default: 1.0.

properties.name: Tempo
properties.summary: Gets or sets the tempo multiplier. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = double speed, 0.5 = half speed.
properties.value: The tempo multiplier. Default: 1.0.

properties.name: Rate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the rate multiplier. 1.0 = no change.
properties.value: The rate multiplier. Default: 1.0.

properties.name: PitchSemitones
properties.summary: Gets or sets the pitch shift in semitones. Range: -12 to +12 (one octave down to one octave up). 0 = no change, +1 = one semitone up, -1 = one semitone down. This is a convenience property that converts to/from the Pitch multiplier. Values outside the -12 to +12 range will be clamped.
properties.value: The pitch shift in semitones. Default: 0.

methods.name: GenerateDescription
methods.summary: Generates the GStreamer launch string description.
methods.returns: A string representation of the audio effect parameters.

classes.name: PitchShiftAudioEffect
classes.summary: Pitch shift audio effect changes the pitch of audio without affecting its tempo/speed. Uses the SoundTouch library via GStreamer to perform high-quality pitch shifting. Useful for key transposition, vocal correction, or special effects. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.
classes.remarks: Uses soundtouch-based pitch shifting algorithm. The effect maintains audio duration while changing frequency content. Pitch multiplier examples: - 0.5 = one octave down - 0.75 = minor third down - 1.0 = no change (original pitch) - 1.122 = approximately one semitone up - 1.5 = perfect fifth up - 2.0 = one octave up Quality considerations: - Small pitch changes (0.9-1.1) sound very natural - Moderate changes (0.7-1.4) are noticeable but acceptable - Large changes (<0.5 or >2.0) can introduce artifacts

constructors.name: PitchShiftAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the PitchShiftAudioEffect class.

parameters.name: pitch
parameters.summary: The pitch multiplier. 1.0 = no change, 0.5 = one octave down, 2.0 = one octave up. Typical range: 0.5 to 2.0. Values outside this range may produce artifacts.

properties.name: Pitch
properties.summary: Gets or sets the pitch multiplier that determines how much the pitch is shifted. - Values < 1.0 shift pitch down (0.5 = one octave down) - Value = 1.0 means no pitch change (original pitch) - Values > 1.0 shift pitch up (2.0 = one octave up) Musical intervals (approximate): - 0.5 = -12 semitones (one octave down) - 0.841 = -3 semitones (minor third down) - 0.943 = -1 semitone - 1.059 = +1 semitone - 1.122 = +2 semitones (whole tone up) - 1.5 = +7 semitones (perfect fifth up) - 2.0 = +12 semitones (one octave up) The duration of the audio remains unchanged.
properties.value: The pitch multiplier. Typical range: 0.5 to 2.0.

classes.name: RemoveSilenceAudioEffect
classes.summary: Audio effect for automatic silence detection and removal. This effect analyzes audio streams to identify sections where the signal level falls below a specified threshold and drops them from the stream. Useful for cleaning up recordings, podcasts, and voice content by eliminating unwanted silent gaps. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.

constructors.name: RemoveSilenceAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the RemoveSilenceAudioEffect class.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name for this audio effect instance.

constructors.name: RemoveSilenceAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the RemoveSilenceAudioEffect class with custom threshold and squash settings.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name for this audio effect instance.

parameters.name: squash
parameters.summary: Whether to pull the surviving buffers back to close the gap (true) or keep their original timestamps (false). Silence is dropped either way.

properties.name: Threshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets the silence detection threshold. Audio levels below this threshold will be considered as silence. Values range from 0.0 (clamped to the element's -70 dB floor - only near-digital silence is removed) to 1.0 (full scale - every sample counts as silence). Lower values are more permissive; higher values remove more audio.
properties.value: The silence threshold as a linear value from 0.0 to 1.0. Default: 0.001 (-60 dB).

properties.name: Squash
properties.summary: Gets or sets the squash mode. Silent sections are always dropped; squash controls what happens to the timeline afterwards. When enabled (true), the timestamps of the surviving buffers are pulled back by the dropped duration, so the output is shorter and gapless - which also means the audio no longer lines up with the video of the same recording. When disabled (false), the gap is left in place and the surviving buffers keep their original timestamps, which keeps A/V sync.
properties.value: true to close the gap left by removed silence; false to keep the original timeline. Default: false, matching the element.

classes.name: ReverberationAudioEffect
classes.summary: Reverberation audio effect adds simulated room acoustics and spatial depth to audio. Uses the GStreamer 'freeverb' element, implementing the Freeverb algorithm for realistic room simulation. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.
classes.remarks: GStreamer element: freeverb Properties: - room-size: Size of the simulated room (0.0 = small, 1.0 = large hall) - damping: High frequency damping (0.0 = bright, 1.0 = dark/muffled) - width: Stereo width/panorama (0.0 = mono, 1.0 = full stereo) - level: Wet/dry mix (0.0 = dry only, 1.0 = wet only, 0.5 = 50/50 mix) The Freeverb algorithm uses Schroeder reverberators with all-pass filters for natural-sounding reverb.

constructors.name: ReverberationAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the ReverberationAudioEffect class with default settings. Default values create a medium-sized room with balanced characteristics.

properties.name: Damping
properties.summary: Gets or sets the damping of high frequencies in the reverb tail. Controls how quickly high frequencies decay compared to low frequencies. Range: 0.0 (bright, minimal damping) to 1.0 (dark, heavy damping). Lower values (0.1-0.3) simulate hard, reflective surfaces. Higher values (0.6-0.9) simulate soft, absorptive surfaces like carpets and curtains.
properties.value: The high frequency damping amount. Default: 0.2.

properties.name: Level
properties.summary: Gets or sets the wet/dry mix level of the reverberation effect. Controls the balance between the original (dry) signal and the reverb (wet) signal. Range: 0.0 (completely dry, no reverb) to 1.0 (completely wet, reverb only). Typical values: 0.3-0.5 for subtle ambience, 0.6-0.8 for pronounced reverb.
properties.value: The dry/wet mix level. Default: 0.5 (50% wet, 50% dry).

properties.name: RoomSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the size of the simulated room or space. Affects the length and character of the reverb tail. Range: 0.0 (small room, short reverb) to 1.0 (large hall, long reverb). Small values (0.2-0.4) simulate rooms and studios. Medium values (0.5-0.7) simulate halls and auditoriums. Large values (0.8-1.0) simulate cathedrals and large spaces.
properties.value: The room size parameter. Default: 0.5 (medium room).

properties.name: Width
properties.summary: Gets or sets the stereo width of the reverb effect. Controls the spatial spread of the reverberation in the stereo field. Range: 0.0 (mono, centered reverb) to 1.0 (full stereo width). Higher values create more spacious, enveloping reverb. Lower values create more focused, centered reverb.
properties.value: The stereo width parameter. Default: 1.0 (full stereo).

methods.name: GenerateDescription
methods.summary: Generates the description.
methods.returns: A string representation of the audio effect parameters.

classes.name: ScaleTempoAudioEffect
classes.summary: Scale tempo audio effect changes the playback speed (tempo) of audio without significantly affecting pitch. Uses the GStreamer 'scaletempo' element with WSOLA (Waveform Similarity Overlap-Add) algorithm. Ideal for time-stretching audio, creating slow-motion or fast-forward effects while preserving pitch.
classes.remarks: GStreamer element: scaletempo Properties: - rate: Playback speed multiplier (0.5 = half speed, 2.0 = double speed) - stride: Length of audio segments processed (in milliseconds) - overlap: Percentage of segment overlap for smooth transitions - search: Time window for finding best overlap position (in milliseconds) WSOLA Algorithm: 1. Divides audio into overlapping segments (stride length) 2. Searches for best position to overlap segments (search window) 3. Cross-fades overlapping portions (overlap percentage) 4. Reconstructs audio at new tempo Quality vs Efficiency trade-offs: - Larger stride = faster processing, but more artifacts - Larger search = better quality, but slower processing - More overlap = smoother, but more CPU intensive Best for: - Speech (podcasts, audiobooks): stride=30-50ms, search=14ms - Music: stride=15-30ms, search=20-30ms for better quality - Real-time: smaller stride and search for lower latency

constructors.name: ScaleTempoAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the ScaleTempoAudioEffect class.

parameters.name: rate
parameters.summary: The tempo scale rate. 1.0 = original speed, 0.5 = half speed, 2.0 = double speed. Typical range: 0.5 to 2.0. Values outside this range may have reduced quality.

properties.name: Rate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the playback rate (tempo multiplier). Controls the speed of audio playback while attempting to preserve pitch. - Values < 1.0: Slower playback (0.5 = half speed) - Value = 1.0: Normal speed (no change) - Values > 1.0: Faster playback (2.0 = double speed) Typical ranges: - 0.5-0.8: Slowed down (better comprehension, detail analysis) - 1.2-1.5: Sped up (faster listening, time-saving) - 1.5-2.0: Very fast (may reduce comprehension) Quality decreases at extreme values (<0.4 or >3.0). For music, smaller changes (0.8-1.25) work best.
properties.value: The playback rate multiplier. Default: 1.0.

properties.name: Overlap
properties.summary: Gets or sets the percentage of stride length to overlap between adjacent segments. Higher overlap creates smoother transitions but requires more processing. Range: 0.0 (no overlap) to 0.9 (90% overlap). Default: 0.2 (20%). Typical values: - 0.1-0.15: Minimal overlap, efficient but may have artifacts - 0.2-0.3: Balanced quality and performance (default: 0.2) - 0.4-0.6: High overlap, smoother but more CPU intensive Increase for: - More complex material (music with harmonics) - Higher quality requirements Decrease for: - Real-time processing - Simple material (speech, single instruments)
properties.value: The overlap percentage (0.0 to 0.9). Default: 0.2.

properties.name: Search
properties.summary: Gets or sets the length of the search window for finding the best overlap position. Larger search windows find better matches but require more processing time. Default: 14 milliseconds. Typical values: - 5-10 ms: Fast, lower quality (real-time applications) - 14-20 ms: Balanced (default: 14ms for speech) - 20-40 ms: High quality (music, offline processing) Increase for: - Music or harmonic content - When quality is priority over speed Decrease for: - Real-time or low-latency requirements - Simple material like speech
properties.value: The search window length. Default: 14 milliseconds.

properties.name: Stride
properties.summary: Gets or sets the length of each audio segment (stride) to be processed. Determines the granularity of the time-stretching operation. Default: 30 milliseconds. Typical values: - 15-25 ms: Fine-grained, better for music - 30-40 ms: Balanced (default: 30ms for speech) - 50-100 ms: Coarse, efficient but may have noticeable artifacts Shorter strides: - Better quality for complex material - More CPU intensive - Better for music Longer strides: - More efficient processing - Adequate for speech - May produce audible artifacts in music Note: Stride length affects perceived quality more than search or overlap.
properties.value: The stride segment length. Default: 30 milliseconds.

classes.name: Sound3DAudioEffect
classes.summary: Creates spatial 3D audio effects by enhancing stereo width and channel separation. Simulates three-dimensional sound positioning for increased immersion and spatial perception. Can enhance stereo width from natural to extreme depending on amplification value. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.
classes.remarks: Custom 3D spatialization effect.Value of 1000 = disabled (no effect, neutral).Values less than 1000: Reduces stereo width (moves toward mono).Values greater than 1000: Increases stereo width (expands sound field).Values above 10000: May cause distortion and phase issues.Best used with headphones for immersive 3D audio experience.In the X engines the value is the stereo width, 2000 being 2x. The width stops at half, reached at 500.In the X engines the effect processes stereo only; any other stream passes through unprocessed and raises OnError.

constructors.name: Sound3DAudioEffect

parameters.name: value

properties.name: Value
properties.summary: Gets or sets the 3D spatial amplification intensity.
properties.value: The amplification value. 1000 = neutral (no effect). Less than 1000 = narrower stereo (toward mono). Greater than 1000 = wider stereo field. Above 10000 may distort.

classes.name: TrebleEnhancerAudioEffect
classes.summary: Boosts high-frequency content (treble) above a specified frequency threshold. Enhances clarity, presence, and "air" in audio by amplifying treble frequencies. Opposite of TrueBass effect - targets high frequencies instead of low. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.
classes.remarks: Amplifies frequencies from specified frequency up to Nyquist frequency (sample rate / 2).Common uses: Adding sparkle to dull recordings, enhancing cymbals and hi-hats, improving vocal clarity.Volume parameter controls amplification strength (0 = no effect, higher = more boost).Frequency parameter sets where enhancement begins (typical: 4000-8000 Hz).In the X engines the frequency goes up to a sixth of the sample rate (8000 Hz at 48 kHz). A higher value works at that limit and raises OnError.

constructors.name: TrebleEnhancerAudioEffect

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.summary: Starting frequency for treble enhancement in Hz. Frequencies from this point to sample_rate/2 are amplified. Typical values: 4000-8000 Hz.

parameters.name: volume
parameters.summary: Amplification strength. 0 = no effect, higher values = more boost. 8000 boosts the band 20x or more, so loud material clips well below that.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Gets or sets the starting frequency for treble enhancement in Hz.
properties.value: The frequency threshold. Frequencies above this are amplified. Typical values: 4000-8000 Hz for general enhancement.

properties.name: Volume
properties.summary: Gets or sets the amplification strength.
properties.value: The volume boost amount. 0 = no effect, higher = more treble boost. 8000 boosts the band 20x or more, so loud material clips well below that.

classes.name: TrueBassAudioEffect
classes.summary: TrueBass audio effect enhances low frequencies to provide richer bass response. Boosts bass frequencies within a specified range to add depth and punch to audio. Useful for improving bass on small speakers or enhancing low-end in music. Implements the BaseAudioEffect.
classes.remarks: This effect amplifies bass frequencies from 0 Hz up to the specified frequency. Unlike a simple low-pass boost, TrueBass can enhance perceived bass even on systems with limited low-frequency response by using psychoacoustic techniques. Frequency selection guidelines: - 60-80 Hz: Sub-bass region (rumble, kick drum fundamentals) - 80-120 Hz: Bass fundamentals (bass guitar, lower male vocals) - 120-250 Hz: Upper bass (warmth, body) Volume settings: - 1000: about 3.5x in the band - 5000: about 13.5x - 10000: about 26x. Loud material clips well below this. In the X engines the frequency goes up to a sixth of the sample rate (8000 Hz at 48 kHz). A higher value works at that limit and raises OnError. Caution: Excessive bass boost can cause: - Speaker damage (especially on small speakers) - Audio clipping and distortion - Muddy, undefined low end

constructors.name: TrueBassAudioEffect
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the TrueBassAudioEffect class.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.summary: The upper frequency limit for bass enhancement in Hz. Range: 0 to 250 Hz typically. Common values: 60 Hz (deep bass), 100 Hz (balanced), 150 Hz (warm).

parameters.name: volume
parameters.summary: The amplification amount for the bass frequencies. Range: 0 to 10000. 0 = no effect. Output in the band is about 1 + volume / 400 times the input, so loud material clips at low values already.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Gets or sets the frequency range that will be enhanced. All frequencies from 0 Hz up to this frequency will be amplified. Typical values: - 40-60 Hz: Deep sub-bass (felt more than heard, requires good subwoofer) - 60-80 Hz: Standard bass range (kick drums, bass fundamentals) - 80-120 Hz: Upper bass (warmth, body, male vocal fundamentals) - 120-200 Hz: Lower midrange (can add muddiness if over-boosted) Lower frequencies require capable speakers/headphones to reproduce effectively.
properties.value: The upper frequency limit in Hz (typically 0-250 Hz range).

properties.name: Volume
properties.summary: Gets or sets the amplification amount applied to frequencies below the specified frequency limit. Controls the strength of the bass enhancement effect. Range: 0 (no enhancement) to 10000. Output in the band is about 1 + Volume / 400 times the input: 1000 is about 3.5x, 5000 about 13.5x and 10000 about 26x. Start with lower values and increase gradually while monitoring for distortion.
properties.value: The bass amplification volume (0 to 10000).

classes.name: WeightedChannelMixAudioEffect
classes.summary: Weighted channel mixing audio effect for dual-mono audio sources like CD+G karaoke files. This effect mixes stereo channels with adjustable weights and outputs the merged signal on both channels, or as mono. Perfect for karaoke applications where left channel contains music only and right channel contains music + vocals.
classes.remarks: This effect is particularly useful for CD+G karaoke files that use dual-mono multiplexing: Left channel: Instrumental backing track (music only)Right channel: Full mix with lead vocals The effect allows users to control the vocal level by adjusting the mix ratio between channels. The weighted mix is output to both left and right channels, or as a single channel when is false. GStreamer Pipeline: The effect creates an internal bin containing: deinterleave → volume (left) → audiomixer → audioconvert → stereo or mono output → volume (right) ↗ Runtime Adjustable: Channel weights can be modified during playback without pipeline reconstruction.

methods.name: GenerateDescription
methods.summary: Generates the GStreamer pipeline description string for this audio effect. This method is called internally by the audio effects processor to build the GStreamer bin.
methods.remarks: The generated pipeline: deinterleave name=d ! queue ! volume volume={LeftChannelWeight} ! mix.sink_0 d. ! queue ! volume volume={RightChannelWeight} ! mix.sink_1 audiomixer name=mix ! audioconvert ! audio/x-raw,channels=1 ! audioconvert ! audio/x-raw,channels={1 or 2} First audioconvert forces mono, second upmixes to stereo (duplicates mono to both L and R).
methods.returns: A string representation of the GStreamer pipeline elements and their configuration.

classes.name: WideStereoAudioEffect

classes.name: DSReverbAudioEffect
classes.summary: DirectSound I3DL2 (Interactive 3D Audio Level 2) Reverb effect simulates environmental reverberation with comprehensive room acoustics modeling, including early reflections, diffusion, and decay characteristics.
classes.remarks: Platform: Windows only (DirectX/DirectSound DSP)Available in: Classic SDKs (VideoCaptureCore, MediaPlayerCore, VideoEditCore)Effect Type: Spatial/Reverb The I3DL2 reverb is a professional-quality environmental reverb algorithm that models realistic room acoustics with separate control over early reflections and late reverberation. Supports preset-based configuration for common acoustic environments or detailed manual parameter adjustment. Typical Applications:Simulating room acoustics (small room to large hall)Adding depth and space to vocals and instrumentsCreating environmental audio for games and multimediaProfessional music production and mixingParameters:Room: -10000 to 0 mB - Master room gain (attenuation)RoomHF: -10000 to 0 mB - High-frequency room gainDecayTime: 0.1-20.0 seconds - Reverberation decay timeDecayHFRatio: 0.1-2.0 - Ratio of high-frequency to full-spectrum decay timeReflections: -10000 to 1000 mB - Early reflections levelReflectionsDelay: 0.0-0.3 seconds - Delay before early reflectionsReverbValue: -10000 to 2000 mB - Late reverberation levelReverbDelay: 0.0-0.1 seconds - Delay before late reverberationDiffusion: 0-100% - Echo density in late reverberationDensity: 0-100% - Modal density in late reverberationHFReference: 20-20000 Hz - Reference high-frequency cutoffQuality: 0-3 - Processing quality (0=low, 3=high)RoomRollOffFactor: 0.0-10.0 - Distance-based attenuation factorPreset: Predefined acoustic environments (Room, Hall, Cathedral, etc.)Cross-Platform Alternative: Use ReverberationAudioEffect for cross-platform Freeverb-based reverb.

classes.name: DSWavesReverbAudioEffect
classes.summary: DirectSound Waves Reverb effect provides a simplified reverberation algorithm with basic controls for reverb time, frequency damping, and wet/dry mix. Ideal for quick reverb effects with minimal configuration.
classes.remarks: Platform: Windows only (DirectX/DirectSound DSP)Available in: Classic SDKs (VideoCaptureCore, MediaPlayerCore, VideoEditCore)Effect Type: Spatial/Reverb Waves Reverb is a streamlined reverb algorithm with fewer parameters than I3DL2 Reverb, making it easier to configure while still providing natural-sounding reverberation effects. Ideal for applications where simplicity and performance are priorities over detailed acoustic modeling. Typical Applications:Quick reverb effects for multimedia and gamesSimple room ambience simulationAdding depth to vocals and instrumentsLow-CPU reverb for real-time processingParameters:InGain: -96 to 0 dB - Input gain (dry signal level)ReverbMix: -96 to 0 dB - Reverb output level (wet signal level)ReverbTime: 0.001-3000 ms - Reverb decay time (RT60)HighFreqRTRatio: 0.001-0.999 - High-frequency decay time ratio (relative to ReverbTime)Usage Tips:ReverbTime 100-500 ms: Small room ambienceReverbTime 500-1500 ms: Medium halls and studiosReverbTime 1500-3000 ms: Large halls and cathedralsHighFreqRTRatio < 0.5: Warm, damped reverb (simulates sound absorption)HighFreqRTRatio > 0.8: Bright, lively reverb (reflective surfaces)Cross-Platform Alternative: Use ReverberationAudioEffect for cross-platform Freeverb-based reverb.

classes.name: MFAACEncoderSettings
classes.summary: Media Foundation AAC encoder settings.
classes.remarks: This encoder was deprecated because building a pipeline with it used to break every later nvh264enc/nvh265enc/nvav1enc session in the process with NV_ENC_ERR_INVALID_VERSION. The AAC encoder was never the cause: requesting it loads the mediafoundation plugin, which activated NVIDIA's Media Foundation video encoder MFTs while registering its elements, and that activation is what invalidated NVENC. The Windows redistributables ship a patched plugin that excludes those MFTs, so Media Foundation AAC and GStreamer NVENC coexist in one process; the deprecation has been lifted. This holds while the SDK loads its own runtime - the `VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Windows.*` package for the process architecture. An application that instead resolves GStreamer from a stock installation on PATH / GST_PLUGIN_PATH gets the unpatched plugin and the original failure, silently. _SETUP/NuGet/verify-patched-plugins.ps1 is what proves a deployment carries the fix. remains the Windows default for and is interchangeable for the typical capture/streaming use case. Prefer MFAACEncoderSettings for VideoEditCoreX with EncodingProfile/ges_pipeline_set_render_settings, where libav AAC does not roundtrip the GstPreset in this build.

methods.name: TryParseUrl
methods.summary: Parses a udp://host:port URL into Host and Port, and hands the parsed pair back to the caller.
methods.remarks: A caller that retargets a running sink must push the pair this returns, not read Host and Port back off these settings afterwards: two threads retargeting at once both write here, so the two reads can straddle the other's write and produce a host and a port from different URLs. GitHub issue #948. That is all this buys, and the limit is worth stating. and remain two independent stores on a settings object with no lock, so concurrent callers can still leave *these properties* holding a host from one URL and a port from another - which will then report, and which a later rebuild through ApplySettings will push. Nor is parse order push order. What is guaranteed is only that the pair handed to one caller came from one URL.

parameters.name: host
parameters.summary: The parsed host. Undefined when the method returns false.

parameters.name: port
parameters.summary: The parsed port. Undefined when the method returns false.

methods.returns: true when the URL parsed.

classes.name: DebugMediaBlockSettings
classes.summary: Provides a set of debugging and control settings for media blocks within the VisioForge X engine. These settings allow for fine-grained control over buffer handling, timing, and error simulation for testing and diagnostic purposes.
classes.remarks: This class is primarily intended for developers and advanced users to debug and analyze the behavior of media pipelines. Modifying these settings can significantly alter the performance and stability of media processing.

properties.name: CheckImperfectOffset
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to send element messages if buffer offsets and offset_ends do not match up. This helps in debugging issues related to buffer segmentation and continuity.

properties.name: CheckImperfectTimestamp
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to send element messages if buffer timestamps and durations do not match up. This helps in debugging issues related to timing and synchronization.

properties.name: DataRate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the data rate in bytes per second for (re)timestamping buffers. If set to 0, this feature is inactive. Useful for simulating specific data flow rates.

properties.name: DropAllocation
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to drop allocation queries. If set to true, the element will not forward allocation queries, which can be used for testing memory management scenarios.

properties.name: DropProbability
properties.summary: Gets or sets the probability (0.0 to 1.0) that a buffer will be dropped. This can be used to simulate network packet loss or other data corruption scenarios.

properties.name: EOSAfter
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of buffers after which an End-Of-Stream (EOS) signal will be sent. A value of -1 means no EOS will be sent based on buffer count. Useful for testing stream termination.

properties.name: ErrorAfter
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of buffers after which an error will be simulated. A value of -1 means no error will be simulated based on buffer count. Useful for testing error handling.

properties.name: SignalHandoffs
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the identity element should emit a handoff signal when processing a buffer. This signal can be used for external monitoring or debugging of buffer flow.

properties.name: Silent
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the media block should operate in silent mode. In silent mode, less debug information might be printed to the console.

properties.name: SingleSegment
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to timestamp buffers and eat segments so as to appear as one continuous segment. This is useful for ensuring continuous playback even with fragmented input.

properties.name: SleepTime
properties.summary: Gets or sets the time in microseconds to sleep between processing each buffer. This can be used to simulate processing delays or to throttle the pipeline for debugging purposes.

properties.name: Sync
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the media block should synchronize to the pipeline clock. Enabling synchronization ensures smooth playback and proper timing with other elements in the pipeline.

properties.name: TimestampOffset
properties.summary: Gets or sets the timestamp offset in nanoseconds for synchronization. A negative value indicates an earlier synchronization point, while a positive value indicates a later one.

classes.name: UVCModeSelector
classes.summary: Pure, platform-independent mode-picking logic for USB (UVC) cameras. Kept out of the platform-gated source file so it can be unit-tested on any target.

methods.name: SelectMode
methods.summary: Picks the advertised mode closest to what was asked for, preferring MJPEG because uncompressed modes are limited to very low frame rates over USB 2.0 (a camera offering 1080p30 in MJPEG typically manages only 1080p5 uncompressed).

parameters.name: fps
parameters.summary: Requested frame rate. Compared against each mode's exact rate rather than its rounded-down whole-frame field, so a camera offering both 30 and 29.97 fps can be asked for either.

parameters.name: preferredFormat
parameters.summary: Format to favour at the chosen resolution, or Unknown for the default. The default favours MJPEG, because an uncompressed mode runs at a fraction of the frame rate over USB - but that also means a caller who read an uncompressed mode out of the mode list could not otherwise ask for it.

methods.returns: The chosen mode, or a default UVCMode (Width zero) when the camera advertises nothing this bridge can stream.

methods.name: GetFrameRate
methods.summary: Gets the frame rate of a mode. UVC reports a frame interval in 100 ns units, and the raw rate is 10000000/interval - but a nominal 30 fps camera reports 333333, whose reduced fraction is 10000000/333333 rather than 30/1. GStreamer compares framerates by cross-multiplication, so that fraction does not intersect a downstream caps filter pinned to 30/1 and negotiation fails on a camera that really is running at 30 fps. Rates within RateTolerance of a whole number, or of one of the n*1000/1001 broadcast rates, are therefore reported in that canonical form. Anything else - 7.5 fps, say - keeps its exact reduced fraction.
methods.returns: The frame rate. Cameras that report no interval fall back to the rounded Fps, or to 30 fps when that is absent too.

methods.name: RateMatches
methods.summary: Determines whether a mode runs at the requested rate, ignoring the rounding the reported interval introduces.
methods.returns: true when the mode's rate is the requested one.

methods.name: ToCameraMode
methods.summary: Converts a mode read from the native bridge into the public description handed to applications.
methods.returns: The public mode description.

methods.name: ToPublicFormat
methods.summary: Maps a native frame format onto the public one. Written out rather than cast so a format added to the bridge cannot silently arrive as the wrong public value.

parameters.name: format
parameters.summary: Format reported by the native bridge.

methods.returns: The public format, or Unknown when the SDK cannot stream it.

methods.name: MatchDevice
methods.summary: Finds the device that carries a camera's identity in a Pylon device list.
methods.remarks: Kept free of P/Invoke so the selection can be tested without the Pylon SDK. The strongest identity the camera actually carries decides and the search stops there: falling through to a weaker field after a stronger one found nothing would answer a serial number with a model name. SerialNumber is unique by definition, FullName carries the transport-layer address, and Name is Pylon's FriendlyName - the same string on two identical bodies, which is why several matches are reported rather than silently narrowed.

parameters.name: devices
parameters.summary: The device list, in Pylon enumeration order - the array position is the index PylonCreateDeviceByIndex takes.

parameters.name: ambiguity
parameters.summary: The serial numbers of every device answering to the identity when more than one does; null otherwise.

methods.returns: The index of the device, or -1 when the identity matches none.

methods.name: ResolveIdentity
methods.summary: Points this instance at the device that actually carries its identity, and fills in the fields the identity did not come with.
methods.remarks: DeviceIndex is a position in one Pylon enumeration, taken once by DeviceEnumerator and cached for the life of the process, while pylonsrc builds its own device list - so the index alone is not an identity even for an enumerated camera. Resolving is also what gives a camera constructed from a name alone the serial number the element is addressed by.
methods.returns: true when the device was found, or when there is no identity to look for and DeviceIndex is all this instance ever knew; false when the identity names a device that is not present.

methods.name: StrongestIdentity
methods.summary: Gets the strongest identity field this instance carries, with the accessor reading the matching field out of a Pylon device record.

parameters.name: read
parameters.summary: The accessor for the field that was chosen.

methods.returns: The value to match on, or null when the instance carries no identity.

methods.name: IsPylonLoadFailure
methods.summary: Gets whether an exception from a Pylon P/Invoke means the Pylon natives could not be loaded or initialized. A missing DLL arrives as DllNotFoundException, a wrong-architecture image as BadImageFormatException, a missing export as EntryPointNotFoundException, and PylonInitialize returning an error as InvalidOperationException. TypeInitializationException is still accepted: it is what a failed static constructor used to produce, and the warning carries the inner fault. ReadInfo reports it and returns false rather than throwing into a constructor or a build.
methods.returns: true for a load failure.

methods.name: WarnPylonNotLoaded
methods.summary: Reports a Pylon load failure.

methods.name: Warn
methods.summary: Reports a diagnostic through the logging context when there is one, and through Trace otherwise - the shape the rest of this class uses.

methods.name: ReadInfo
methods.summary: Reads the information.
methods.returns: true when the size was read, false otherwise; false leaves the size from an earlier read in place. Always false outside a Windows x64 process: it reads through the Basler pylon SDK for Windows x64.

methods.name: DestroyDevice
methods.summary: Releases the device object PylonCreateDeviceByIndex produced. Closing a device does not release it, so every ReadInfo used to leak one.
methods.remarks: PylonDestroyDevice could not be checked against the binary - PylonC_v7_4.dll ships with the Basler SDK and is on neither dev machine nor in this repository. A wrong guess would turn a leak into an EntryPointNotFoundException on a cleanup path, which is worse than the leak, so it is caught: the call fixes the leak wherever the export is there and leaves today's behaviour where it is not.

classes.name: NDISourcesChangedEventArgs

classes.remarks: Threading: the event fires from the background watcher thread that drives NDIlib_find_wait_for_sources. Subscribers that touch UI must marshal to their UI thread (e.g. RunOnUiThread, Dispatcher.Invoke, BeginInvokeOnMainThread) — the SDK does not do that for them. Identity: "added" / "removed" / "current" are computed by NDI source name (the canonical NDI identifier — two senders with the same Name on the network is the user-visible misconfiguration the NDI spec forbids). A sender that comes back online after a brief disconnect surfaces as a entry followed by an entry on the next event, not as a continuous presence — there's no way for libndi (and therefore for us) to correlate that it's the same physical sender.

properties.name: MaxPullFps
properties.summary: Optional cap on the rate at which the Android framesync loop pulls frames from libndi. Platform note: This property only affects Android NDI receivers. On non-Android platforms (Windows, Linux, macOS) it has no effect because those platforms use a push-based receiver model where the source controls the frame delivery rate. 0 means uncapped — pull at the source frame rate. A non-zero value clamps the polling period to 1 / MaxPullFps seconds: the framesync still receives every source frame, but our consumer only pulls the latest one MaxPullFps times per second, halving the CPU cost of the poll loop on high-fps sources where the device cannot display every frame anyway. Default is 30 — appropriate for a 4K@60 NDI source feeding a typical 30 Hz display; raise to 0 (uncapped) for full source-rate playback when the device can keep up.
properties.value: Frames per second cap; 30 (default), 0 for uncapped.

properties.value: True to apply timestamps; otherwise, false. Default is true for live sources.

properties.value: The maximum queue length. Default is 10.

properties.name: TimestampMode
properties.summary: Gets or sets the timestamp mode for synchronization.
properties.value: The timestamp mode. Default is 0 (Auto).

properties.name: ProbeTimeoutMs
properties.summary: Gets or sets how long a probe waits for the sender, in milliseconds. It bounds NDISourceBlock.BuildAndroid waiting for the first frame, the ndisrc probe pipeline behind ContextX) on macOS and Linux, and NDISourceXBlock.Build waiting for its first video frame on Windows. It does not reach ContextX) on Windows or Android: there the NDI SDK reader is bounded by ReadInfoTimeoutMs. It does not bound ndisrc's own state-change timeline once the block is built and running either.
properties.value: The probe timeout in milliseconds. Default is 10 000 (10 seconds). Accepts [100, 60000].

properties.name: ReadInfoTimeoutMs
properties.summary: Gets or sets how long ContextX) waits for the sender's video and audio on Windows and Android, in milliseconds. The NDI SDK reader waits for both streams, so a sender with only one of them always waits the full window; raise it for a sender whose video or audio starts late. When the sender's address is known (it is looked up by name) and one stream has arrived without the other two seconds later, with at least a second of the window left, the reader reconnects to the sender, up to three times; the last connection keeps the rest of the window. On macOS and Linux the probe is bounded by ProbeTimeoutMs instead.
properties.value: The timeout in milliseconds. Default is 10 000 (10 seconds). Accepts [100, 60000].

properties.name: VideoCodecHint
properties.summary: Gets or sets the video codec hint sent to the NDI sender after connection.
properties.value: Hardware (default) sends <ndi_video_codec type="hardware"/> requesting HX2/HX3 encoding. Software sends <ndi_video_codec type="software"/> requesting full-bandwidth NDI (SpeedHQ). None skips the hint entirely.

methods.name: ReadInfoAsync
methods.summary: Reads the stream information asynchronously, with cancellation support and a default 30-second timeout.
methods.remarks: The synchronous ReadInfo performs blocking network I/O via the MediaInfoReaderCore probe and currently has no inner cancellation hook. To keep the public contract responsive we wrap it in a Task.Run that observes cancellationToken for the dispatch latency, and race the completion against a 30s Task.Delay so the call never hangs longer than the timeout if the RTMP server is unreachable. When the timeout wins the underlying thread continues running (we cannot abort it safely) but the caller receives a null result and a warning log instead of an indefinite hang.

This is the JSON persistence path: Uri, Login, Password and AudioEnabled are set from the document payload afterwards. Unlike CancellationToken) it never contacts the camera, so CompatibilityMode starts enabled and the stream information is read when the block opens. Use CancellationToken) when the camera is reachable and its media information should be probed up front. One consequence: an ONVIF device-service URL is not resolved to a media URL here, as does. methods.remarks: onvifProfile applies when uri is an ONVIF device-service URL (http://<camera>/onvif/device_service; any http or https URL is taken as one); an RTSP URL is used as given. It is matched against the profile tokens first and the profile names second, over the camera's ONVIF Media 2.0 service when it offers one and over Media 1.0 when it does not, when Media 2.0 does not list the profile, or when a Media 2.0 request fails. The tokens and names GetProfilesAsync reports (Profile.token, Profile.Name) work either way. When the camera has no such profile, a warning lists the profiles it does have and the URL stays unresolved. null, an empty string or white space picks the profile by its video stream, as the overload without this parameter does.

methods.name: GetVideoURLByONVIFAsync
methods.summary: Resolves the ONVIF device-service URL in Uri to the RTSP URL of one of the camera's media profiles.
methods.remarks: The profile is the one named by the onvifProfile argument of , otherwise it is chosen by its video stream, because ONVIF does not order profiles by quality and several vendors list a MJPEG or low-resolution profile first. The codec decides first: H.264 and H.265 rank together above MPEG-4, which ranks above JPEG. Within a codec rank the larger frame wins, then the higher frame rate limit, and on a full tie H.264 is preferred to H.265. Only the profiles on the same video source (input) as the camera's first profile are considered, so an encoder, NVR or multi-sensor camera stays on its first input; when none of them describes a video encoder, the first profile is used. The profiles are read from the ONVIF Media 2.0 service when the camera offers it, which is the only one that reports H.265, and from Media 1.0 otherwise or when Media 2.0 fails. Media 1.0 knows JPEG, MPEG-4 and H.264 only, so on a camera without Media 2.0 an H.265-only profile is not recognized as such. H.265 ranks with H.264 only when this process has an H.265 decoder (the VisioForge Libav redist, or a GPU decoder the hardware provides); otherwise it ranks below every other codec, since an undecodable stream shows nothing. The profile used is logged at Info and the others at Debug.
methods.returns: true when Uri now holds the profile's RTSP URL; false when it is unchanged.

properties.summary: When true, the SDK pre-resolves any DNS hostname in Uri to a literal IPv4 address on the managed side (via System.Net.Dns) before handing the URI to the native srtsrc. properties.value: true (default) to render audio; false to suppress the audio pad.

properties.value: false (default) because most callers don't render subtitles; set to true to opt in.

properties.value: false (default) to use decodebin3.

methods.name: ReadInfoAsync
methods.summary: Reads the information asynchronous.
methods.remarks: Previously returned null, which silently broke MediaPlayerCoreX's audio path: AddAudioBlocks gates on _info?.AudioStreams.Count > 0, so a null or zero-stream disables the audio renderer entirely — no audio ever played from a stream source even when the stream contained audio.Stream-based probing is not currently available via (which needs a URI or file path), so this method returns a placeholder whose stream counts reflect the user's Render* intent rather than measured stream presence. Adding a stub / / per enabled flag is enough to keep the downstream > 0 gates passing; the actual codec/sample-rate details are discovered by decodebin during pipeline construction and surface through the pad caps.TODO: add a stream-based probing overload to so we can return genuine stream metadata here without consuming bytes the pipeline later needs.
methods.returns: Task<MediaFileInfo>.

methods.name: CreateBlock
methods.summary: Creates the block.
methods.remarks: Previously returned a bare StreamSourceBlock, which produced an encoded-elementary-stream output pad rather than the decoded video/audio pads the rest of the media-player wiring expects. The pipeline factory was patched to route StreamSourceSettings through StreamSourceBlockWithDecoder; this factory method is updated to match so callers that build blocks directly (outside MediaPlayerX) get the same shape.

classes.name: UDPRAWMPEGTSSourceSettings
classes.summary: Settings for UDPRAWMPEGTSSourceBlock — a raw MPEG-TS-over-UDP receiver that delivers the untouched transport-stream byte stream (188- or 192-byte packets, per PacketSize) to downstream blocks without demuxing. Suitable for feeding the TS analyzer from a live UDP unicast or multicast broadcast.

constructors.name: UDPRAWMPEGTSSourceSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the UDPRAWMPEGTSSourceSettings class.
constructors.remarks: [JsonConstructor] because the type has two public constructors and neither is parameterless, which System.Text.Json refuses outright. This is the one a document binds - Uri is a settable property, so the string overload stays for code.

constructors.name: UDPRAWMPEGTSSourceSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the UDPRAWMPEGTSSourceSettings class.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.summary: The UDP source URI string, e.g. "udp://239.0.0.1:1234".

properties.name: Uri
properties.summary: Gets or sets the source URI, e.g. udp://239.0.0.1:1234 for multicast or udp://0.0.0.0:1234 to listen for unicast on all interfaces.

properties.name: AutoJoinMulticast
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to automatically join/leave the multicast group when the URI is a multicast address. Default is true.

properties.name: MulticastInterface
properties.summary: Gets or sets the network interface(s) on which to join the multicast group (for example "eth0" or "eth0,eth1"). Optional.

properties.name: BufferSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the kernel receive buffer size in bytes. 0 uses the OS default. Default is 524288 (512 KB).

properties.name: PacketSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the MPEG-TS packet size advertised in the source caps, in bytes. Use 188 for standard transport streams (default) or 192 for M2TS-style streams with a 4-byte timecode prefix. Any other value is ignored and treated as 188.

classes.name: UDPRAWSourceSettings
classes.summary: Settings for UDPRAWSourceBlock. Receives a live UDP stream and exposes parsed but still-encoded H264/H265 video (and optional audio) without decoding, suitable for passthrough recording (for example, splitting into MP4 files without re-encoding).
classes.remarks: The source is addressed by a single udp://host:port URI, where the port is the local port the receiver listens on (a udpsrc binds a local socket — it does not connect to a remote sender): udp://0.0.0.0:1234 (or an empty host) — listen for unicast on the given port on all local interfaces.udp://239.1.1.1:1234 — join the multicast group 239.1.1.1 on the given port (any address in 224.0.0.0–239.255.255.255 is treated as multicast and joined automatically).udp://192.168.1.10:1234 — bind to that specific local interface.

constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the UDPRAWSourceSettings class.
constructors.remarks: [JsonConstructor] because the type has two public constructors and neither is parameterless, which System.Text.Json refuses outright. This is the one a document binds - Uri is a settable property, so the string overload stays for code.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.summary: The source URI, for example udp://0.0.0.0:1234 or udp://239.1.1.1:1234.
