methods.returns: The String.

classes.name: SubtitlesSettings
classes.summary: Configures the settings for displaying subtitles during video playback.
classes.remarks: This class allows you to specify the subtitle file to be used. Supported formats include SRT, SUB, ASS, and SSA. Additional subtitle rendering options might be available through the OnSubtitleSettings event.

constructors.name: SubtitlesSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the SubtitlesSettings class with the specified subtitle file.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The full path to the subtitle file. Supported formats include SRT, SUB, ASS, and SSA.

properties.name: Filename
properties.summary: Gets or sets the full path to the subtitle file.
properties.value: The filename of the subtitle file. Supported formats are SRT, SUB, ASS, and SSA.

classes.name: TextStatusOverlay
classes.summary: Represents a status overlay that displays text on top of the video stream.
classes.remarks: This class allows you to display dynamic text messages, such as "Connecting..." or "Buffering...", directly on the video output. You can customize the text, font, color, and alignment.

constructors.name: TextStatusOverlay
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the TextStatusOverlay class with default settings.
constructors.remarks: By default, the text is "Connecting...", centered both horizontally and vertically, with a white, bold, 24pt monospace font.

properties.name: TextConnecting
properties.summary: Gets or sets the text to be displayed when the component is in a "connecting" state.
properties.value: The string message to show during connection or loading. The default value is "Connecting...".

properties.name: Font
properties.summary: Gets or sets the font used for rendering the text overlay.
properties.value: A Font object specifying the typeface, size, and style of the text.

properties.name: Brush
properties.summary: Gets or sets the brush used for painting the text overlay.
properties.value: A Brush object, typically a SolidBrush, defining the color of the text.

properties.name: StringFormat
properties.summary: Gets or sets the StringFormat object that encapsulates text layout information.
properties.value: A StringFormat object that controls text alignment, line spacing, and other layout options.

properties.name: VerticalAlignment
properties.summary: Gets or sets the vertical alignment of the text overlay on the video frame.
properties.value: A VerticalAlignment value (e.g., Top, Center, Bottom).

properties.name: HorizontalAlignment
properties.summary: Gets or sets the horizontal alignment of the text overlay on the video frame.
properties.value: A HorizontalAlignment value (e.g., Left, Center, Right).

classes.name: AudioCaptureDeviceInfo
classes.summary: Represents comprehensive information about an audio capture device including its capabilities, supported formats, input lines, and available configuration dialogs.
classes.remarks: This class uses lazy initialization for device properties to improve performance. Device information is only retrieved when accessed for the first time through the OnInitiateRequired event mechanism.

constructors.name: AudioCaptureDeviceInfo
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the AudioCaptureDeviceInfo class with the specified device name.
constructors.remarks: This constructor only sets the device name. Other properties must be populated later using the String) and Boolean) methods.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The display name of the audio capture device.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets the display name of the audio capture device.
properties.value: The friendly name of the device as reported by the system.

properties.name: DevicePath
properties.summary: Gets the unique device path that identifies this audio capture device in the system.
properties.value: The system-specific path (e.g., DirectShow moniker string on Windows) that uniquely identifies this device. This path can be used to distinguish between multiple devices with the same name.

properties.name: Formats
properties.summary: Gets a list of all audio formats supported by this capture device.
properties.value: A list of format strings describing the supported audio formats. Format strings typically include sample rate, bit depth, and channel configuration (e.g., "44100 Hz, 16-bit, Stereo").

properties.name: Lines
properties.summary: Gets a list of available audio input lines for this capture device.
properties.value: A list of input line names (e.g., "Line In", "Microphone", "CD Audio"). The list may be empty if the device doesn't support multiple input lines or if line enumeration is not supported.

properties.name: DialogDefault
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the device supports a default configuration dialog.
properties.value: true if the device provides a default configuration dialog; otherwise, false.

properties.name: DialogCaptureDisplay
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the device supports a capture display dialog.
properties.value: true if the device provides a capture display dialog; otherwise, false.

properties.name: DialogCaptureFormat
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the device supports a capture format dialog.
properties.value: true if the device provides a capture format dialog; otherwise, false.

properties.name: DialogCaptureSource
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the device supports a capture source dialog.
properties.value: true if the device provides a capture source dialog; otherwise, false.

properties.name: DialogCompressorConfig
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the device supports a compressor configuration dialog.
properties.value: true if the device provides a compressor configuration dialog; otherwise, false.

properties.name: DialogCompressorAbout
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the device supports a compressor about dialog.
properties.value: true if the device provides a compressor about dialog; otherwise, false.

properties.name: Initiated
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the device information has been initialized.
properties.value: true if device information has been loaded; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Fill
methods.summary: Populates the device information with input lines, supported formats, and device path.
methods.remarks: This method is typically called in response to the OnInitiateRequired event to populate the device information when first accessed.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.summary: A list of available input lines for the audio device.

parameters.name: formats
parameters.summary: A list of supported audio formats.

parameters.name: devicePath
parameters.summary: The unique system path identifying this device.

methods.name: CheckInitiate
methods.summary: Checks if device initialization is required and triggers the initialization process if needed.
methods.remarks: This method implements the lazy initialization pattern. It's called by property getters to ensure device information is loaded before returning values. The OnInitiateRequired event is raised only once, the first time initialization is needed.

methods.name: FillDialogs
methods.summary: Populates the device dialog availability information.
methods.remarks: This method is typically called along with String) to complete the device information initialization process.

parameters.name: default_
parameters.summary: Indicates whether the device supports a default configuration dialog.

parameters.name: captureDisplay
parameters.summary: Indicates whether the device supports a capture display dialog.

parameters.name: captureFormat
parameters.summary: Indicates whether the device supports a capture format dialog.

parameters.name: captureSource
parameters.summary: Indicates whether the device supports a capture source selection dialog.

parameters.name: compressorConfig
parameters.summary: Indicates whether the device supports a compressor configuration dialog.

parameters.name: compressorAbout
parameters.summary: Indicates whether the device supports a compressor about/information dialog.

methods.name: ToString
methods.summary: Returns a string representation of the audio capture device.
methods.remarks: This method returns the device name without triggering initialization, making it safe to use in UI lists and debug output.
methods.returns: The name of the audio capture device.

events.name: OnInitiateRequired
events.summary: Occurs when device initialization is required due to accessing a property for the first time.

classes.name: AudioCaptureSource
classes.summary: Represents an audio capture source configuration for audio recording and preview operations.
classes.remarks: This class encapsulates all settings required to configure an audio capture device, including device selection, format configuration, input line selection, and custom source filters. It supports both physical audio devices and custom audio source implementations through the ICustomAudioSourceFilter interface.

constructors.name: AudioCaptureSource
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the AudioCaptureSource class with default settings.
constructors.remarks: The instance is initialized with the following defaults: is set to true, , and are set to empty stringsAll other properties are set to their default values

constructors.name: AudioCaptureSource
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the AudioCaptureSource class with the specified device name.
constructors.remarks: This constructor automatically attempts to detect the preferred audio format for the specified device. If a format with 44100 Hz, 16-bit, 2 channels is available, it will be selected. Otherwise, is set to true. The constructor temporarily creates a instance to query device capabilities, which is disposed after use.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The name of the audio capture device to use.

constructors.name: AudioCaptureSource
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the AudioCaptureSource class using device information.
constructors.remarks: This constructor uses the device information to set the device name and automatically detect the preferred format. The format detection logic is the same as in the String) constructor.

parameters.name: info
parameters.summary: An AudioCaptureDeviceInfo instance containing device information.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the audio capture device to use.
properties.value: The friendly name of the audio capture device as reported by the system. An empty string indicates no device is selected.

properties.name: SourceFilter
properties.summary: Gets or sets a custom audio source filter implementation.
properties.value: An instance of a class implementing ICustomAudioSourceFilter, or null to use a physical audio device instead.

properties.name: MasterDevice
properties.summary: Gets or sets the master device name for audio synchronization.
properties.value: The name of the master device used for synchronization, or null if not used.

properties.name: MasterDevice_Format
properties.summary: Gets or sets the format of the master device used for synchronization.
properties.value: The format string of the master device, or null if not applicable.

properties.name: Format
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio format to use for recording and preview.
properties.value: A format string describing the audio format (e.g., "44100 Hz, 16-bit, Stereo"). An empty string indicates that the format should be automatically selected.

properties.name: Format_UseBest
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the best available audio format should be automatically selected.
properties.value: true to automatically select the best format; false to use the format specified in the Format property.

properties.name: Line
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio input line to use for recording and preview.
properties.value: The name of the input line (e.g., "Microphone", "Line In", "CD Audio"). An empty string indicates the default line should be used.

properties.name: CustomLatency
properties.summary: Gets or sets the custom audio latency in milliseconds.
properties.value: The desired audio latency in milliseconds. For a DirectShow audio capture device, a value of 0 uses 100 ms; a negative value uses the device default, whose larger buffers can lose the last part of a recording on stop. Other sources (ASIO, "What You Hear", a video capture device's audio pin) keep their default at 0, and a custom SourceFilter ignores this property.

properties.name: Path
properties.summary: Gets or sets the unique device path for the audio capture device.
properties.value: The system-specific device path (e.g., DirectShow moniker string on Windows), or null to select by name only.

methods.name: DetectPreferredFormat
methods.summary: Automatically detects and sets the preferred audio format based on device capabilities.
methods.remarks: This method searches for a format that matches 44100 Hz sample rate, 16-bit depth, and 2 channels (stereo), which is considered the standard CD-quality audio format. If no such format is found, Format_UseBest is set to true to let the system choose the best available format.

parameters.name: info
parameters.summary: The device information containing the list of supported formats.

methods.name: ToString
methods.summary: Returns a string representation of the audio capture source.
methods.remarks: This method is useful for displaying the audio source in user interfaces or for debugging purposes.
methods.returns: The name of the audio capture device, or an empty string if no device is selected.

classes.name: BDAChannel
classes.summary: Represents a Broadcast Driver Architecture (BDA) channel configuration for digital TV reception.
classes.remarks: This class encapsulates all the parameters required to tune to a specific digital TV channel using BDA-compatible tuner devices. BDA is the Microsoft standard for digital TV reception on Windows, supporting various broadcast standards including DVB-T, DVB-S, DVB-C, and ATSC. The properties in this class correspond to the MPEG-2 transport stream parameters and tuning information required by the BDA subsystem.

constructors.name: BDAChannel
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the BDAChannel class with default values.
constructors.remarks: Creates an empty channel configuration. All properties must be set manually before the channel can be used for tuning.

constructors.name: BDAChannel
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the BDAChannel class with specified parameters.
constructors.remarks: This constructor initializes the basic channel parameters but does not set tuning parameters (Frequency, Polarisation, SymbolRate). These must be set separately after construction. This constructor is typically used when parsing channel information from service information tables or channel scan results.

parameters.name: aSID
parameters.summary: The service ID (SID) that uniquely identifies the service in the transport stream.

parameters.name: aName
parameters.summary: The display name of the channel.

parameters.name: aServType
parameters.summary: The service type value indicating the type of service (TV, radio, etc.).

parameters.name: aFreeCAmode
parameters.summary: true if the channel is encrypted; false if free-to-air.

parameters.name: aVideoPid
parameters.summary: The PID of the video elementary stream, or -1 if no video.

parameters.name: aAudioPid
parameters.summary: The PID of the primary audio elementary stream, or -1 if no audio.

properties.name: ServId
properties.summary: Gets or sets the service ID (SID) of the channel.
properties.value: The MPEG-2 service identifier that uniquely identifies this service within a transport stream.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets or sets the display name of the channel.
properties.value: The human-readable name of the channel as broadcast in the service information.

properties.name: ServType
properties.summary: Gets or sets the service type of the channel.
properties.value: A byte value indicating the type of service as defined in the DVB/ATSC standards.

properties.name: FreeCAmode
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the channel is encrypted (Free CA mode).
properties.value: true if the channel is encrypted and requires a Conditional Access (CA) system to decrypt; false if the channel is free-to-air (unencrypted).

properties.name: VideoPid
properties.summary: Gets or sets the video stream Packet Identifier (PID).
properties.value: The 13-bit PID value identifying the video elementary stream in the transport stream. A value of -1 or 0x1FFF indicates no video stream.

properties.name: AudioPid
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio stream Packet Identifier (PID).
properties.value: The 13-bit PID value identifying the primary audio elementary stream in the transport stream. A value of -1 or 0x1FFF indicates no audio stream.

properties.name: Modulation
properties.summary: Gets or sets the modulation type used for this channel.
properties.value: A value representing the modulation scheme. The interpretation depends on the broadcast standard (DVB-T/T2, DVB-S/S2, DVB-C, ATSC).

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Gets or sets the tuning frequency for this channel.
properties.value: The frequency in kHz (kilohertz) for terrestrial and cable systems, or in MHz (megahertz) for satellite systems.

properties.name: Polarisation
properties.summary: Gets or sets the signal polarization for satellite reception.
properties.value: The polarization type from the BDAPolarisation enumeration.

properties.name: SymbolRate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the symbol rate for this channel.
properties.value: The symbol rate in symbols per second (baud rate).

classes.name: BDASourceSettings
classes.summary: Provides configuration settings for Broadcast Driver Architecture (BDA) digital TV sources.
classes.remarks: BDA sources represent digital TV tuner devices that receive broadcast signals via terrestrial (DVB-T, ATSC), satellite (DVB-S), or cable (DVB-C) delivery systems. This class encapsulates the tuner and receiver components that make up a complete BDA capture path. A BDA capture path consists of two DirectShow filters, and both names are required: Source filter - Tunes to the frequency and delivers the transport streamReceiver filter - Demultiplexes and processes the transport stream

properties.name: SourceName
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the BDA source (tuner) filter.
properties.value: The DirectShow filter name of the digital TV tuner device (e.g., "Hauppauge WinTV DVB-T Tuner").

properties.name: ReceiverName
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the BDA receiver (demultiplexer) filter.
properties.value: The DirectShow filter name of the receiver/demux filter. Required: the BDA graph connects the tuner through it.

properties.name: SourceType
properties.summary: Gets or sets the broadcast standard type for the BDA source.
properties.value: A BDAType enumeration value specifying the digital TV standard (DVB-T, DVB-S, DVB-C, or ATSC).

classes.name: BDATuningParameters
classes.summary: Encapsulates comprehensive tuning parameters for Broadcast Driver Architecture (BDA) digital TV reception.
classes.remarks: This class contains all the parameters necessary to tune a BDA-compatible digital TV tuner device to a specific channel and service. The required parameters vary depending on the broadcast standard (DVB-T, DVB-S, DVB-C, ATSC) and the transmission characteristics of the target channel. BDA tuning is a multi-step process: Tune to the correct frequency using Lock onto the transport stream using modulation and symbol rate parametersSelect the specific service using and stream PIDsDemultiplex audio and video streams using the PID values

constructors.name: BDATuningParameters
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the BDATuningParameters class.

properties.name: Channel
properties.summary: Gets or sets the logical channel number for the service.
properties.value: The user-friendly channel number (e.g., 7, 13, 102). Default is -1 for unspecified.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Gets or sets the tuning frequency for the channel.
properties.value: Frequency in kHz for terrestrial/cable or MHz for satellite systems. Default is -1 for unspecified.

properties.name: SymbolRate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the symbol rate for the digital signal.
properties.value: Symbol rate in symbols per second (baud). Default is -1 for unspecified.

properties.name: FEC
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Forward Error Correction (FEC) rate.
properties.value: FEC rate value indicating the error correction coding scheme. Default is 0.

properties.name: LnbSwitchFrequency
properties.summary: Gets or sets the LNB (Low Noise Block) switch frequency for dual-band satellite reception.
properties.value: Switch frequency in MHz that determines when the LNB switches between low and high bands. Default is 0.

properties.name: Diseq
properties.summary: Gets or sets the DiSEqC (Digital Satellite Equipment Control) switch position.
properties.value: DiSEqC switch port number (0-3 for DiSEqC 1.0, extended for DiSEqC 1.1/1.2). Default is 0.

properties.name: ProgramNumber
properties.summary: Gets or sets the MPEG program number within the transport stream.
properties.value: Program number identifying the service. Default is 0.

properties.name: ServiceType
properties.summary: Gets or sets the service type identifier.
properties.value: Numeric value indicating the service type (1=TV, 2=Radio, etc.). Default is 0.

properties.name: ProviderName
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the service provider.
properties.value: Provider name as broadcast in the Service Description Table (e.g., "BBC", "ARD", "NHK").

properties.name: ChannelName
properties.summary: Gets or sets the human-readable channel or service name.
properties.value: Service name as broadcast (e.g., "BBC One", "CNN International").

properties.name: AudioPid
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Packet Identifier (PID) for the primary audio elementary stream.
properties.value: 13-bit PID value (0x0010-0x1FFE) identifying the audio stream packets. Default is 0.

properties.name: VideoPid
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Packet Identifier (PID) for the video elementary stream.
properties.value: 13-bit PID value (0x0010-0x1FFE) identifying the video stream packets. Default is 0.

properties.name: AC3Pid
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Packet Identifier (PID) for Dolby Digital (AC-3) audio stream.
properties.value: PID for AC-3 audio if available separately from main audio. Default is 0.

properties.name: Audio1Pid
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Packet Identifier (PID) for the first alternative audio stream.
properties.value: PID for alternative audio track 1 (different language, audio description, etc.). Default is 0.

properties.name: Audio2Pid
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Packet Identifier (PID) for the second alternative audio stream.
properties.value: PID for alternative audio track 2. Default is 0.

properties.name: Audio3Pid
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Packet Identifier (PID) for the third alternative audio stream.
properties.value: PID for alternative audio track 3. Default is 0.

properties.name: TeletextPid
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Packet Identifier (PID) for teletext data.
properties.value: PID for teletext/subtitles if broadcast separately. Default is 0.

properties.name: Scrambled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the service is scrambled (encrypted).
properties.value: Non-zero if the service requires conditional access (subscription), 0 if free-to-air. Default is 0.

properties.name: Polarisation
properties.summary: Gets or sets the signal polarization for satellite reception.
properties.value: Polarization type from BDAPolarisation enumeration. Default is NotDefined.

properties.name: LNBFrequency
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Local Oscillator frequency of the LNB for satellite reception.
properties.value: LNB local oscillator frequency in MHz (e.g., 9750, 10600). Default is 0.

properties.name: TSID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Transport Stream Identifier (TSID).
properties.value: 16-bit identifier uniquely identifying the transport stream. Default is -1 for unspecified.

properties.name: SID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Service Identifier (SID).
properties.value: 16-bit identifier uniquely identifying the service within a transport stream. Default is -1.

properties.name: ONID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Original Network Identifier (ONID).
properties.value: 16-bit identifier identifying the originating delivery network. Default is -1.

properties.name: PCRPid
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Packet Identifier (PID) for the Program Clock Reference (PCR).
properties.value: PID containing timing information for stream synchronization. Default is 0.

properties.name: LanguageCodeAudio
properties.summary: Gets or sets the ISO 639 language code for the primary audio stream.
properties.value: Three-letter language code (e.g., "eng", "fra", "deu", "spa"). Default is null.

properties.name: LanguageCodeAudio1
properties.summary: Gets or sets the ISO 639 language code for the first alternative audio stream.
properties.value: Three-letter language code for audio stream 1. Default is null.

properties.name: LanguageCodeAudio2
properties.summary: Gets or sets the ISO 639 language code for the second alternative audio stream.
properties.value: Three-letter language code for audio stream 2. Default is null.

properties.name: LanguageCodeAudio3
properties.summary: Gets or sets the ISO 639 language code for the third alternative audio stream.
properties.value: Three-letter language code for audio stream 3. Default is null.

properties.name: ECMPID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Packet Identifier (PID) for Entitlement Control Messages (ECM).
properties.value: PID carrying ECM data for conditional access systems. Default is 0.

properties.name: PMTPID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Packet Identifier (PID) for the Program Map Table (PMT).
properties.value: PID where the PMT for this service is transmitted. Default is 0.

properties.name: Modulation
properties.summary: Gets or sets the modulation scheme used for signal transmission.
properties.value: Modulation type from BDAModulationType enumeration. Default is NotDefined.

properties.name: Bandwidth
properties.summary: Gets or sets the channel bandwidth for terrestrial broadcasts.
properties.value: Bandwidth in Hz or MHz depending on implementation. Default is 0.

properties.name: PhysicalChannel
properties.summary: Gets or sets the physical (RF) channel number.
properties.value: Physical channel identifier (e.g., UHF channel 21-69). Default is 0.

properties.name: MinorChannel
properties.summary: Gets or sets the ATSC minor channel number.
properties.value: Minor channel number in ATSC systems (e.g., the ".1" in "7.1"). Default is 0.

properties.name: MajorChannel
properties.summary: Gets or sets the ATSC major channel number.
properties.value: Major channel number in ATSC systems (e.g., the "7" in "7.1"). Default is 0.

properties.name: SubtitlePID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the Packet Identifier (PID) for DVB subtitles.
properties.value: PID carrying DVB subtitle data. Default is -1 for unspecified.

classes.name: CrossBarConnections
classes.summary: Represents a connection between input and output pins on a video crossbar device.
classes.remarks: The CrossBarConnections class defines a routing connection within a crossbar device, mapping a specific input pin to an output pin. Crossbar devices are used in video capture hardware to route multiple input sources (such as composite, S-Video, or component inputs) to different outputs or processing paths.

properties.name: InPin
properties.summary: Gets or sets the input pin identifier for the connection.
properties.value: The zero-based index of the input pin to connect. This corresponds to a physical input on the crossbar device (e.g., 0 for composite input, 1 for S-Video input).

properties.name: OutPin
properties.summary: Gets or sets the output pin identifier for the connection.
properties.value: The zero-based index of the output pin to connect to. This typically represents the capture or processing path within the device.

classes.name: CrossBarInputPin
classes.summary: Represents an input pin on a video crossbar device used for routing video signals.
classes.remarks: The CrossBarInputPin class represents an input connection point on a crossbar device. Crossbars are hardware components that allow routing of multiple video and audio inputs to different outputs. This class contains information about a specific input pin, including its routing capabilities and relationships to other pins.

properties.name: CanRoute
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this input pin can be routed to output pins.
properties.value: if the pin supports routing to output pins; otherwise, . Some input pins may be fixed or disabled and cannot be dynamically routed.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets or sets the display name of the input pin.
properties.value: A descriptive name for the pin (e.g., "Composite In", "S-Video In", "Component In"). This name is typically provided by the hardware driver and helps identify the physical input connector.

properties.name: PinIndex
properties.summary: Gets or sets the logical index of the pin within the crossbar.
properties.value: The zero-based index used to identify this input pin in the crossbar's routing operations. This may differ from the physical pin index.

properties.name: RealPinIndex
properties.summary: Gets or sets the actual physical pin index on the hardware.
properties.value: The real hardware pin index, which may differ from the logical PinIndex. This represents the actual physical connector on the device.

properties.name: RelatedPinIndex
properties.summary: Gets or sets the index of a related pin (typically an audio pin associated with this video pin).
properties.value: The index of a related pin, or -1 if no related pin exists. For video input pins, this often references the corresponding audio input pin that should be used together.

classes.name: CrossBarOutputPin
classes.summary: Represents an output pin on a video crossbar device used for routing video signals.
classes.remarks: The CrossBarOutputPin class represents an output connection point on a crossbar device. Each output pin can be connected to one of several input pins, allowing flexible routing of video signals. This class maintains a list of all possible input pins that can be routed to this output.

constructors.name: CrossBarOutputPin
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the CrossBarOutputPin class.
constructors.remarks: Creates a new output pin with an empty collection of input pins. Input pins should be added to the InputPins collection after instantiation.

properties.name: InputPins
properties.summary: Gets the list of input pins that can be connected to this output pin.
properties.value: A read-only collection of CrossBarInputPin objects representing all possible input sources that can be routed to this output.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets or sets the display name of the output pin.
properties.value: A descriptive name for the pin (e.g., "Video Decoder Out", "Video Preview Out"). This name is typically provided by the hardware driver.

properties.name: PinIndex
properties.summary: Gets or sets the logical index of the pin within the crossbar.
properties.value: The zero-based index used to identify this output pin in crossbar routing operations.

properties.name: RelatedPinIndex
properties.summary: Gets or sets the index of a related pin (typically an audio pin associated with this video pin).
properties.value: The index of a related pin, or -1 if no related pin exists. For video output pins, this often references the corresponding audio output pin.

properties.name: RoutedTo
properties.summary: Gets or sets the index of the input pin currently routed to this output.
properties.value: The index of the input pin that is currently connected to this output pin, or -1 if no input is connected.

classes.name: CustomSourceSettings
classes.summary: Provides configuration settings for custom DirectShow video and audio source filters.
classes.remarks: The CustomSourceSettings class allows integration of custom DirectShow filters as video or audio sources. This enables support for proprietary hardware devices, specialized codecs, or custom media sources that aren't natively supported by the framework. You can specify filters by name, CLSID, or category, and configure their media types and formats.

constructors.name: CustomSourceSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the CustomSourceSettings class.
constructors.remarks: The constructor sets default values: VideoFilterCategory is set to VideoCaptureSourceAudioFilterCategory is set to AudioCaptureSourceBoth CLSIDs are initialized to Guid.Empty

properties.name: VideoFilterName
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the custom video source filter.
properties.value: The friendly name of the DirectShow filter to use as a video source. This name must match exactly as registered in the system.

properties.name: VideoFilterFormat
properties.summary: Gets or sets the video format string for the custom source filter.
properties.value: A format string that specifies the desired video format. The exact format of this string depends on the specific filter being used.

properties.name: VideoFilterFrameRate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the frame rate for the custom video source filter.
properties.value: The desired frame rate for video capture. The filter must support the specified frame rate.

properties.name: VideoFilenameOrURL
properties.summary: Gets or sets the file name or URL for filters that support the IFileSourceFilter interface.
properties.value: A file path or URL that will be passed to the filter if it implements IFileSourceFilter. This is commonly used for file-based source filters.

properties.name: VideoFilterCLSID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the CLSID (Class Identifier) of the video filter.
properties.value: The GUID that uniquely identifies the DirectShow filter. Use this when you know the exact CLSID of the filter you want to instantiate.

properties.name: VideoFilterCategory
properties.summary: Gets or sets the category of the custom video source filter.
properties.value: The DirectShow filter category. Default is VideoCaptureSource.

properties.name: VideoFilterAMMediaType
properties.summary: Gets or sets the custom AM_MEDIA_TYPE structure for the video source.
properties.value: An AM_MEDIA_TYPE object that specifies the exact media type for the video stream. This provides fine-grained control over the media format when needed.

properties.name: AudioFilterName
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the custom audio source filter.
properties.value: The friendly name of the DirectShow filter to use as an audio source. This name must match exactly as registered in the system.

properties.name: AudioFilterFormat
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio format string for the custom source filter.
properties.value: A format string that specifies the desired audio format. Common formats include sample rate and bit depth information (e.g., "48000Hz 16bit Stereo").

properties.name: AudioFilterCategory
properties.summary: Gets or sets the category of the custom audio source filter.
properties.value: The DirectShow filter category. Default is AudioCaptureSource.

properties.name: AudioFilterCLSID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the CLSID (Class Identifier) of the audio filter.
properties.value: The GUID that uniquely identifies the DirectShow audio filter.

properties.name: AudioFilterAMMediaType
properties.summary: Gets or sets the custom AM_MEDIA_TYPE structure for the audio source.
properties.value: An AM_MEDIA_TYPE object that specifies the exact media type for the audio stream.

properties.name: AudioFilterPCMConverterAMMediaType
properties.summary: Gets or sets the AM_MEDIA_TYPE for an optional PCM converter connected to the audio source.
properties.value: An AM_MEDIA_TYPE object for configuring a PCM converter filter that may be inserted after the audio source to convert to standard PCM format.

properties.name: AudioFilenameOrURL
properties.summary: Gets or sets the file name or URL for audio filters that support the IFileSourceFilter interface.
properties.value: A file path or URL that will be passed to the audio filter if it implements IFileSourceFilter.

properties.name: SourceInterface
properties.summary: Gets or sets a custom video source interface implementation.
properties.value: An implementation of ICustomVideoSource that will be used instead of DirectShow filters for video capture.

classes.name: DecklinkSourceSettings
classes.summary: Provides configuration settings for Blackmagic DeckLink video capture devices.
classes.remarks: The DecklinkSourceSettings class is used to configure professional Blackmagic DeckLink capture cards for video input. DeckLink devices are commonly used in broadcast and professional video production environments.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of the DeckLink device.
properties.value: The display name of the DeckLink device (e.g., "DeckLink Studio 4K", "DeckLink Mini Recorder"). This value is used to identify and select the specific DeckLink hardware device from the system.

properties.name: VideoFormat
properties.summary: Gets or sets the video format for the DeckLink input.
properties.value: The video format string that specifies the input video standard (e.g., "1080p50", "1080p59.94", "720p60", "NTSC", "PAL"). The available formats depend on the specific DeckLink device model and the connected video source.

classes.name: ICustomAudioSourceFilter
classes.summary: Defines the interface for custom audio source filters that can be integrated into the DirectShow filter graph.
classes.remarks: This interface allows developers to create custom audio sources that can be used as input devices in the video capture pipeline. Implementations can provide audio from various sources such as multiple microphones, network streams, or synthesized audio. See the TwoMicsAudioSource class for a sample implementation that demonstrates mixing audio from two microphones.

methods.name: GetOutputPin
methods.summary: Gets the output pin of the audio source filter.
methods.remarks: The output pin is used by the DirectShow graph builder to connect this audio source to downstream filters such as audio encoders, effects, or renderers. The pin should provide audio data in a format compatible with DirectShow audio filters.
methods.returns: The DirectShow output pin object that other filters can connect to. This is typically an IPin COM interface wrapped as an object.

methods.name: Init
methods.summary: Initializes the audio source filter and adds it to the DirectShow filter graph.
methods.remarks: This method should perform all necessary initialization including: - Creating the DirectShow filter - Configuring audio format and parameters - Adding the filter to the provided graph - Preparing the filter to start providing audio data Any resources allocated during initialization should be properly released in the Dispose method.

parameters.name: filterGraph
parameters.summary: The DirectShow filter graph object (IGraphBuilder) that this source will be added to.

parameters.name: error
parameters.summary: When the method returns false, contains an error message describing what went wrong. When successful, this parameter is set to null or an empty string.

methods.returns: true if the initialization was successful; otherwise, false.

classes.name: ICustomVideoSource
classes.summary: Defines the interface for custom video sources that can provide video frames to the capture pipeline.
classes.remarks: This interface enables developers to create custom video sources from various inputs such as IP cameras, screen capture, generated graphics, or any other video data source. Implementations must handle frame generation, format specification, and event notification. The video source can be used as an input device in video capture and processing scenarios.

properties.name: VideoWidth
properties.summary: Gets or sets the width of the video frames in pixels.
properties.value: The horizontal resolution of the video stream.

properties.name: VideoHeight
properties.summary: Gets or sets the height of the video frames in pixels.
properties.value: The vertical resolution of the video stream.

properties.name: VideoFrameRate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the frame rate of the video stream in frames per second.
properties.value: The number of frames per second the source will attempt to provide.

methods.name: VideoFillBuffer
methods.summary: Fills the provided frame buffer with video data.
methods.remarks: This method is called by the framework to retrieve video frames from the custom source. The implementation should copy the current video frame data into the provided buffer, respecting the frame's format and dimensions. This method should be thread-safe and performant as it may be called frequently based on the frame rate.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: The RAWVideoFrame object to be filled with video data.

methods.name: GetCameraInfo
methods.summary: Retrieves information about a camera or video source from the specified URL.
methods.remarks: This method is typically used to validate connection parameters and retrieve source capabilities before starting the video stream. It's particularly useful for IP cameras and network video sources that require authentication.

parameters.name: url
parameters.summary: The URL or connection string for the video source (e.g., RTSP URL, HTTP stream URL).

parameters.name: username
parameters.summary: The username for authentication, if required by the video source. Pass null or empty string if authentication is not needed.

parameters.name: password
parameters.summary: The password for authentication, if required by the video source. Pass null or empty string if authentication is not needed.

parameters.name: error
parameters.summary: When the method returns false, contains an error message describing the connection or authentication failure. When successful, this is set to null or empty string.

parameters.name: videoSize
parameters.summary: When successful, contains the native video size reported by the source. This helps in configuring the VideoWidth and VideoHeight properties appropriately.

methods.returns: true if the camera information was successfully retrieved; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Start
methods.summary: Starts the video source and begins generating or capturing video frames.
methods.remarks: This method should initialize any necessary resources, establish connections, and begin the frame generation process. After calling this method, the source should either respond to VideoFillBuffer calls or raise OnVideoBuffer events with video frame data. The VideoWidth, VideoHeight, and VideoFrameRate properties should be properly configured before calling this method.

events.name: OnVideoBuffer
events.summary: Occurs when a new video frame is available from the source.

classes.name: IPCameraSourceSettings
classes.summary: Provides comprehensive configuration settings for IP camera and network video stream sources.
classes.remarks: This class encapsulates all parameters required to connect to and configure IP cameras, RTSP streams, HTTP video streams, and other network-based video sources. It supports multiple streaming engines (FFMPEG, VLC, LAV, low-latency RTSP) and provides extensive control over connection parameters, authentication, latency optimization, and codec settings. The class supports various network streaming protocols including: RTSP (Real-Time Streaming Protocol) - most common for IP camerasHTTP/HTTPS - for MJPEG streams and web-based camerasONVIF - standardized protocol for network camera configurationMMS/WMV - Windows Media streamingNDI - NewTek Network Device Interface for professional video

properties.name: Type
properties.summary: Gets or sets the streaming engine type for processing the IP camera stream.
properties.value: An IPSourceEngine value specifying which backend to use. Default is Auto_LAV.

properties.name: URL
properties.summary: Gets or sets the URL for IP camera.

properties.name: Login
properties.summary: Gets or sets IP camera login, if required.

properties.name: Password
properties.summary: Gets or sets IP camera password, if required.

properties.name: ForcedFramerate
properties.summary: Gets or sets IP camera framerate, if required. Some HTTP cams do not send time stamp and frame rate is required.

properties.name: ForcedFramerate_InstanceID
properties.summary: Gets or sets IP camera forced framerate mode instance id. Must be unique for each process/application.

properties.name: AudioCapture
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio capture from IP camera enabled.

properties.name: VideoCapture
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether video capture from IP camera enabled. True by default. Currently used only for LAV engine.

properties.name: Debug_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether IP camera debugging enabled.

properties.name: Debug_Filename
properties.summary: Gets or sets IP camera debug file name.

properties.name: VLC_CustomLatency
properties.summary: Gets or sets custom cache size (milliseconds). This option can decrease latency.

properties.name: VLC_ZeroClockJitterEnabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether clock jitter option will be set to 0. This option can decrease latency.

properties.name: VLC_CustomDefaultFrameRate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the custom default frame rate for network sources that do not provide the frame rate correctly.
properties.value: The custom default frame rate.

properties.name: DisconnectEventInterval
properties.summary: Gets or sets interval. If this interval > 0, OnNetworkSourceDisconnect will be fired if no frames arrive in "interval" time. This property must be set before the Start method call. 10 seconds by default.

properties.name: ONVIF_Source
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether camera connected using ONVIF protocol.

properties.name: ONVIF_SourceProfile
properties.summary: Gets or sets the ONVIF camera profile, by token or by name (the token is matched first).

properties.name: VLC_CustomParameters
properties.summary: Gets or sets custom command-line parameters.

properties.name: RTSP_LowLatency_UseUDP
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether UDP will be used instead TCP.

properties.name: LAV_GPU_Use
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether GPU decoding will be used for LAV engine.

properties.name: LAV_GPU_Mode
properties.summary: Gets or sets source GPU mode, if Source_Mode property set to GPU.

properties.name: FFMPEG_CustomOptions
properties.summary: Gets or sets the FFMPEG custom options.
properties.value: The ffmpeg custom options.

properties.name: FFMPEG_MaxLoadTimeout
properties.summary: Gets or sets the FFMPEG maximum load timeout. For an rtsp:// source it also bounds the stream: the connection and each network read wait at most half of it, so a camera that sends nothing for about this long ends the stream, which does not resume by itself. FFMPEG_CustomOptions["timeout"] overrides the per-read wait (microseconds); "0" waits for the camera forever. A DirectCapture recording from an rtsp:// camera uses the same read timeout, whatever the source engine: when it fires, the recording ends with its file finalized; it resumes only with the next separate capture segment, if there is one. Of FFMPEG_CustomOptions, that recording also takes "rtsp_transport".
properties.value: The FFMPEG maximum load timeout.

properties.name: VideoInfo
properties.summary: Gets or sets the video info.

methods.name: Clone
methods.summary: Returns a copy for one start to resolve the ONVIF stream into, leaving the customer's object as it was set.

classes.name: MediaFoundationCaptureDevice
classes.summary: A camera that Media Foundation can open, and the video sizes it actually provides.
classes.remarks: Obtain instances from VideoCaptureCore.Video_MediaFoundationCaptureDevices. This is not a : there is no crossbar, audio pin, tuner, or DirectShow format list. Pass the instance to . Each format is a size the camera's own Media Foundation source reports, with the frame rates reported for that size. The capture graph receives RGB24 at the chosen size. A size that appears only in the DirectShow device list is not included.

constructors.name: MediaFoundationCaptureDevice
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MediaFoundationCaptureDevice class.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The camera name reported by Media Foundation.

parameters.name: devicePath
parameters.summary: The camera's Media Foundation symbolic link.

parameters.name: formats
parameters.summary: The sizes the camera provides. Copied.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets the camera name reported by Media Foundation.

properties.name: DevicePath
properties.summary: Gets the Media Foundation symbolic link for this camera.

properties.name: Formats
properties.summary: Gets the sizes this camera provides, in the order Media Foundation reported them.

methods.name: ToString
methods.summary: Returns the camera name.
methods.returns: The value of Name.

classes.name: MediaFoundationCaptureFormat
classes.summary: One video size a Media Foundation camera provides, and the frame rates for that size.
classes.remarks: Name is the string to assign to Format (for example 1280x960). Set Format_UseBest to and FrameRate to one of FrameRates. The capture graph receives RGB24 at this size.

constructors.name: MediaFoundationCaptureFormat
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MediaFoundationCaptureFormat class.

parameters.name: frameRates
parameters.summary: The frame rates for this size. Copied. A rate with a zero numerator is omitted.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Gets the size string, widthxheight, for Format.

properties.name: Width
properties.summary: Gets the frame width in pixels.

properties.name: Height
properties.summary: Gets the frame height in pixels.

properties.name: FrameRates
properties.summary: Gets the frame rates Media Foundation reported for this size.

methods.name: ToString
methods.summary: Returns the size string.
methods.returns: The value of Name.

classes.name: PIPChromaKeySettings
classes.summary: Provides configuration settings for chroma key (green/blue screen) effects in video mixing operations.
classes.remarks: Chroma keying, also known as color keying or green/blue screen, is a technique that removes a specific color from a video stream and makes it transparent, allowing another video source to show through. This is widely used in video production for placing subjects against virtual backgrounds. The quality of chroma key results depends on: Even lighting on the chroma key backgroundSelecting the exact color of your backgroundProperly configured tolerance valuesSubject separation from the background

constructors.name: PIPChromaKeySettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the PIPChromaKeySettings class with default chroma green settings.
constructors.remarks: Creates a chroma key configuration with standard values for typical green screen setups: Color: Chroma green (RGB: 57, 162, 37)Tolerance1: 10 - tight inner keying rangeTolerance2: 30 - moderate edge softness These defaults work well for evenly-lit green screens with good color saturation. You may need to adjust the color to match your specific background and fine-tune tolerances based on lighting conditions.

properties.name: Color
properties.summary: Gets or sets the chroma key color to be made transparent.
properties.value: The target color for keying. Default is a typical chroma green (RGB: 57, 162, 37).

properties.name: Tolerance1
properties.summary: Gets or sets the first tolerance value for color matching precision.
properties.value: Tolerance value ranging from 0 (exact match only) to 255 (very loose matching). Default is 10.

properties.name: Tolerance2
properties.summary: Gets or sets the second tolerance value for edge softness and color transition.
properties.value: Tolerance value ranging from 0 to 255. Default is 30.

classes.name: PushSourceSettings
classes.summary: Push source settings.
classes.remarks: This class defines the video format settings for push-based video sources, where frames are actively pushed into the capture pipeline rather than being pulled from a device or file. This is commonly used for custom video sources or when integrating with external video generation systems.

constructors.name: PushSourceSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the PushSourceSettings class.
constructors.remarks: Creates a new push source configuration with default settings: 640x480 resolution at 25 fps.

properties.name: VideoWidth
properties.summary: Gets or sets video width.
properties.value: The width of the video frame in pixels. Default is 640.

properties.name: VideoHeight
properties.summary: Gets or sets video height.
properties.value: The height of the video frame in pixels. Default is 480.

properties.name: VideoFrameRate
properties.summary: Gets or sets video frame rate.
properties.value: The frame rate for the video stream. Default is 25 fps.

classes.name: ScreenCaptureSourceSettings
classes.summary: Provides configuration settings for screen capture operations, including capture area, frame rate, and visual enhancements.
classes.remarks: This class encapsulates all the settings required to configure screen capture functionality, supporting both full-screen and region-based capture modes. It provides fine-grained control over the capture process, including performance optimizations and visual enhancements. The settings support various capture scenarios: - Full screen capture across multiple displays - Specific window capture using window handles - Custom region capture with coordinate specification - Mouse cursor capture with optional highlighting effects On Windows 8 and later, the Desktop Duplication API can be enabled for improved performance and lower CPU usage compared to traditional GDI-based capture methods.

constructors.name: ScreenCaptureSourceSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the ScreenCaptureSourceSettings class with default values.
constructors.remarks: The default configuration captures the full primary screen at 10 frames per second without the mouse cursor. The capture area is initially set to 640x480 pixels for non-fullscreen mode, though this is overridden when FullScreen is true.

properties.name: Bottom
properties.summary: Gets or sets the bottom boundary coordinate for the screen capture area.
properties.value: The Y-coordinate of the bottom edge of the capture rectangle in screen pixels.

properties.name: FrameRate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the frame rate at which the screen will be captured.
properties.value: A VideoFrameRate object specifying the capture frame rate.

properties.name: FullScreen
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to capture the entire screen or a specific region.
properties.value: true to capture the full screen; false to capture only the region defined by Left, Top, Right, and Bottom.

properties.name: GrabMouseCursor
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the mouse cursor should be included in the capture.
properties.value: true to include the mouse cursor in the captured video; otherwise, false.

properties.name: AllowDesktopDuplicationEngine
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the Desktop Duplication API should be used for screen capture.
properties.value: true to enable Desktop Duplication API; false to use traditional GDI capture.

properties.name: DisplayIndex
properties.summary: Gets or sets the zero-based index of the display monitor to capture.
properties.value: The display index where 0 represents the primary monitor.

properties.name: Left
properties.summary: Gets or sets the left boundary coordinate for the screen capture area.
properties.value: The X-coordinate of the left edge of the capture rectangle in screen pixels.

properties.name: Right
properties.summary: Gets or sets the right boundary coordinate for the screen capture area.
properties.value: The X-coordinate of the right edge of the capture rectangle in screen pixels.

properties.name: Top
properties.summary: Gets or sets the top boundary coordinate for the screen capture area.
properties.value: The Y-coordinate of the top edge of the capture rectangle in screen pixels.

properties.name: Mode
properties.summary: Gets or sets the screen capture mode that determines what content is captured.
properties.value: A ScreenCaptureMode enumeration value specifying the capture mode.

properties.name: WindowHandle
properties.summary: Gets or sets the handle of the window to capture when using window-specific capture mode.
properties.value: An IntPtr representing the window handle (HWND on Windows).

properties.name: MouseHighlight
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to display a visual highlight effect around the mouse cursor.
properties.value: true to enable mouse highlighting; otherwise, false.

properties.name: MouseHighlightColor
properties.summary: Gets or sets the color of the mouse highlight circle.
properties.value: A Color value representing the highlight color. The default value is Green.

properties.name: MouseHighlightSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the thickness of the mouse highlight circle border in pixels.
properties.value: The border thickness in pixels. The default value is 5.

properties.name: MouseHighlightDuration
properties.summary: Gets or sets the duration for which the mouse highlight remains visible after a click.
properties.value: A TimeSpan representing the highlight duration. The default value is 0.7 seconds.

properties.name: MouseHighlightOpacity
properties.summary: Gets or sets the opacity level of the mouse highlight effect.
properties.value: A value between 0.0 (fully transparent) and 1.0 (fully opaque). The default value is 0.5.

properties.name: MouseHighlightRadius
properties.summary: Gets or sets the radius of the mouse highlight circle in pixels.
properties.value: The radius of the highlight circle. The default value is 50 pixels.

properties.name: ColorModeColor
properties.summary: Gets or sets the fill color used in Color capture mode.
properties.value: A Color value representing the solid fill color. The default value is violet (R=128, G=0, B=255).

properties.name: PictureData
properties.summary: Gets or sets the BGRA32 image data to use as the video source in Picture capture mode.
properties.value: A byte array containing BGRA32 pixel data. The dimensions are determined by the Left, Top, Right, and Bottom properties.

methods.name: ToString
methods.summary: Returns a string representation of the current screen capture settings.
methods.remarks: This method provides a concise summary of the capture configuration, useful for logging or displaying the current settings to users.
methods.returns: A string describing the capture mode and frame rate. For fullscreen mode, returns "Fullscreen@{fps}fps". For region capture, returns "{left}x{top}x{right}x{bottom}@{fps}fps".

classes.name: TimeshiftSettings
classes.summary: Provides configuration settings for timeshift functionality in video capture operations.
classes.remarks: Timeshift enables viewers to pause, rewind, and fast-forward live video streams by continuously recording the stream to temporary storage while simultaneously allowing playback from that storage. This creates a buffer that allows time-shifted viewing of live content. The implementation uses Stream Buffer Engine (SBE) technology to manage the recording and playback processes. Multiple backing files are used to store the content, with automatic file rotation to manage storage space efficiently. Common use cases include: - Pausing live TV to resume watching later - Rewinding to replay interesting moments - Fast-forwarding through previously recorded content - Creating a delay buffer for censorship or editing purposes

constructors.name: TimeshiftSettings
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the TimeshiftSettings class with default values.
constructors.remarks: The default configuration creates a 1-hour timeshift buffer in the system's temporary folder. A new unique recording ID is automatically generated for each instance. Default values: - Temporary folder: System temp path + "SBE\" - Backing file count: 4-6 files - Buffer duration: 1 hour (3600 seconds) - Recording ID: New GUID

properties.name: TempFolder
properties.summary: Gets or sets the folder path where temporary timeshift files will be stored.
properties.value: The full path to the temporary storage folder. Default is the system temp path with "SBE\" subdirectory.

properties.name: RecordingID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the unique identifier for this timeshift recording session.
properties.value: A Guid that uniquely identifies the recording session.

properties.name: OutputFormat
properties.summary: Gets or sets the output format used by the Stream Buffer Engine encoder.
properties.value: An SBEOutputFormat value specifying the encoding format.

properties.name: CaptureMode
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the Stream Buffer Engine should operate in capture mode.
properties.value: true to enable direct capture mode; false to use temporary file mode.

properties.name: Player_Screen
properties.summary: Gets or sets the video view control where the time-shifted content will be displayed.
properties.value: An IVideoView implementation that provides the rendering surface.

properties.name: Player_AudioOutput_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio playback is enabled during timeshift playback.
properties.value: true to enable audio output; false to mute audio during playback.

properties.name: Player_AudioOutput_Device
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio output device to use for timeshift playback.
properties.value: The name or identifier of the audio output device. Use null or empty string for the default device.

properties.name: BackingFileCountMinimum
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum number of backing files to maintain in the timeshift buffer.
properties.value: The minimum number of files. Valid range is 4 to 100. Default is 4.

properties.name: BackingFileCountMaximum
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of backing files allowed in the timeshift buffer.
properties.value: The maximum number of files. Valid range is 6 to 102. Must be at least 2 greater than BackingFileCountMinimum. Default is 6.

properties.name: BackingFileDuration
properties.summary: Gets or sets the total duration of content that can be stored in all backing files.
properties.value: The duration in seconds. Minimum value is 15. Default is 3600 (1 hour).

properties.name: EncodingSettings
properties.summary: Gets or sets the encoding settings used for the timeshift buffer.
properties.value: An MP4Output object containing video and audio encoding parameters.

classes.name: VideoCaptureDeviceAdjustRanges
classes.summary: Represents the adjustment ranges and capabilities for video capture device properties.
classes.remarks: This class defines the valid range of values for adjustable properties on video capture devices, such as brightness, contrast, saturation, and other video processing parameters. It provides information about the minimum and maximum allowed values, the default value, the step size for adjustments, and whether automatic control is available for the property.

properties.name: Min
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum allowed value for the property.
properties.value: The minimum value that can be set for this property.

properties.name: Max
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum allowed value for the property.
properties.value: The maximum value that can be set for this property.

properties.name: Default
properties.summary: Gets or sets the default value for the property.
properties.value: The manufacturer's recommended default value for this property.

properties.name: Step
properties.summary: Gets or sets the step size for property adjustments.
properties.value: The minimum increment or decrement when changing the property value. For example, a step of 10 means the value can only be changed in increments of 10.

properties.name: Auto
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether automatic control is available for this property.
properties.value: true if the device supports automatic adjustment of this property; false if only manual control is available.

classes.name: VideoCaptureDeviceAdjustValue
classes.summary: Represents the current value and control mode for a video capture device adjustment property.
classes.remarks: This class is used to get or set the current state of adjustable properties on video capture devices, such as brightness, contrast, saturation, and other video processing parameters. It combines the actual value with information about whether automatic control is enabled.

constructors.name: VideoCaptureDeviceAdjustValue
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VideoCaptureDeviceAdjustValue class with default values.
constructors.remarks: Creates an instance with Value set to 0 and Auto set to false.

constructors.name: VideoCaptureDeviceAdjustValue
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VideoCaptureDeviceAdjustValue class with specified values.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: The initial value for the adjustment property.

parameters.name: auto
parameters.summary: true to enable automatic control; false for manual control.

properties.name: Value
properties.summary: Gets or sets the current value of the adjustment property.
properties.value: The current value of the property. This value should be within the range defined by the corresponding VideoCaptureDeviceAdjustRanges for this property.

properties.name: Auto
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether automatic control is enabled for this property.
properties.value: true if automatic control is enabled; false if manual control is being used.

classes.name: VideoCaptureDeviceCameraControlRanges
classes.summary: Represents the control ranges and capabilities for camera-specific properties on video capture devices.
classes.remarks: This class defines the valid range of values for camera control properties such as pan, tilt, zoom, focus, exposure, and other mechanical or optical adjustments available on the camera hardware. It extends the basic range information with camera-specific control flags that indicate supported control modes (manual, automatic, absolute, relative).

properties.name: Min
properties.summary: Gets or sets the minimum allowed value for the camera control property.
properties.value: The minimum value that can be set for this property. For absolute controls, this is typically a physical unit (e.g., degrees for pan/tilt).

properties.name: Max
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum allowed value for the camera control property.
properties.value: The maximum value that can be set for this property. For absolute controls, this is typically a physical unit (e.g., degrees for pan/tilt).

properties.name: Default
properties.summary: Gets or sets the default value for the camera control property.
properties.value: The manufacturer's recommended default value for this property. This is typically the neutral or home position for mechanical controls.

properties.name: Step
properties.summary: Gets or sets the step size for property adjustments.
properties.value: The minimum increment or decrement when changing the property value. For mechanical controls, this often represents the smallest controllable movement.

properties.name: Flags
properties.summary: Gets or sets the control flags that indicate supported control modes for this property.
properties.value: A combination of CameraControlFlags values indicating whether the property supports manual control, automatic control, absolute positioning, or relative positioning.

classes.name: VideoCaptureDeviceCameraControlValue
classes.summary: Represents the current value and control mode for a camera-specific control property.
classes.remarks: This class is used to get or set the current state of camera control properties such as pan, tilt, zoom, focus, exposure, and other mechanical or optical adjustments. It combines the actual value with control flags that specify how the value should be interpreted (absolute vs. relative) and what control mode is active (manual vs. automatic).

constructors.name: VideoCaptureDeviceCameraControlValue
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VideoCaptureDeviceCameraControlValue class with default values.
constructors.remarks: Creates an instance with Value set to 0 and Flags set to None.

constructors.name: VideoCaptureDeviceCameraControlValue
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VideoCaptureDeviceCameraControlValue class with specified values.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: The initial value for the camera control property.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.summary: The control flags that specify how the value should be interpreted and controlled.

properties.name: Value
properties.summary: Gets or sets the current value of the camera control property.

classes.name: VideoCaptureModeHelper

classes.remarks: This static class contains helper methods to determine the characteristics of different capture modes, such as whether they are preview-only or capture modes, and whether they handle audio-only scenarios.

methods.name: IsPreview
methods.summary: Determines whether the specified capture mode is a preview mode.
methods.returns: true if the mode is a preview mode (displays without saving); otherwise, false.

methods.name: IsCapture
methods.summary: Determines whether the specified capture mode is a capture (recording) mode.
methods.remarks: This method simply returns the inverse of VideoCaptureMode).
methods.returns: true if the mode saves data to file or stream; otherwise, false.

classes.name: VideoCaptureOutputFormatHelper
classes.summary: Provides extension methods for determining the capture mode characteristics of video capture output formats.
classes.remarks: This helper class contains extension methods that analyze VideoCaptureOutputFormat values to determine their capture characteristics, such as whether they use direct capture or Media Foundation multiplexing. These methods help in routing video capture streams through the appropriate processing pipelines.

methods.name: IsDirectCapture
methods.summary: Determines whether the specified format uses direct capture mode.
methods.remarks: Direct capture formats bypass intermediate processing and write directly to the output file using the capture device's native format or a hardware-accelerated encoder. This typically results in lower CPU usage and minimal latency. The following formats are considered direct capture: DirectCaptureDV - Digital Video formatDirectCaptureMPEG - MPEG formatDirectCaptureAVI - AVI containerDirectCaptureMKV - Matroska containerDirectCaptureASF - Advanced Systems FormatDirectCaptureMP4_GDCL - MP4 using GDCL encoderDirectCaptureMP4_Monogram - MP4 using Monogram encoderDirectCaptureCustom - Custom direct capture implementation

parameters.name: format

methods.returns: if the format uses direct capture mode; otherwise, .

methods.name: IsMFMux
methods.summary: Determines whether the specified format uses Media Foundation multiplexing.
methods.remarks: Media Foundation (MF) multiplexing formats use Windows Media Foundation technology to combine audio and video streams into a single container file. This provides better compatibility with modern Windows applications and hardware acceleration support. The following formats use MF multiplexing: MP4_HW - Hardware-accelerated MP4 encodingMPEGTS - MPEG Transport StreamMOV - QuickTime Movie formatMKVv2 - Matroska version 2 using MF multiplexer

parameters.name: format
parameters.summary: The video capture output format to evaluate.

methods.returns: if the format uses Media Foundation multiplexing; otherwise, .

classes.name: VideoCaptureSource
classes.summary: Represents a video capture source device configuration for DirectShow-based video capture operations.
classes.remarks: This class encapsulates the configuration settings for a video capture device, including format selection, frame rate control, and special features like closed captions and raw sample grabbing. It automatically detects and selects optimal capture formats based on device capabilities. The class supports various capture scenarios including: Standard video capture devices (webcams, capture cards)TV tuners with internal MPEG encodersDevices that can also serve as audio sourcesProfessional capture devices with multiple output pins
