classes.name: VUMeterEventArgs
classes.summary: Provides data for events that report VU (Volume Unit) meter levels for audio visualization and monitoring.
classes.remarks: This event argument is used in audio processing pipelines to report real-time volume levels for each audio channel. The VU meter data is typically used to create visual representations of audio intensity, such as level meters, peak indicators, or other audio visualization components in media players and audio processing applications. Each value in the array represents the current volume level for a specific audio channel. For stereo audio, index 0 typically represents the left channel and index 1 represents the right channel. Multi-channel audio (e.g., 5.1, 7.1) will have corresponding indices for each channel. The values are typically normalized to a specific range (e.g., 0-100 or 0-255) depending on the implementation, where 0 represents silence and the maximum value represents the loudest possible signal before clipping.

constructors.name: VUMeterEventArgs
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VUMeterEventArgs class with the specified VU meter data.

parameters.name: meterData
parameters.summary: An array of integer values representing the VU meter levels for each audio channel. Must not be null. The array should contain one value per audio channel.

properties.name: MeterData
properties.summary: Gets an array of integer values representing the current VU meter levels for each audio channel.
properties.value: An array of Int32 values where each element corresponds to the volume level of an audio channel. The array length corresponds to the number of audio channels in the source material. Values typically range from 0 (silence) to a maximum value (e.g., 100 or 255) representing peak volume.

classes.name: VUMeterFFTEventArgs
classes.summary: Provides data for events that report Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) results for audio frequency analysis.
classes.remarks: This event argument contains FFT data that represents the frequency spectrum of audio signals. The FFT transforms time-domain audio samples into frequency-domain data, allowing analysis of which frequencies are present in the audio and their relative amplitudes. Common uses include: - Spectrum analyzers and frequency visualizers - Audio equalization and filtering analysis - Beat detection and rhythm analysis - Pitch detection and harmonic analysis - Real-time audio effects based on frequency content The FFT result is an array of complex numbers where: - The magnitude represents the amplitude of each frequency component - The phase represents the phase shift of each frequency component - Each index corresponds to a specific frequency bin The frequency represented by each bin can be calculated as: frequency = (binIndex * sampleRate) / fftSize

constructors.name: VUMeterFFTEventArgs
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VUMeterFFTEventArgs class with the specified FFT results.
constructors.remarks: The FFT size determines the frequency resolution: - Larger FFT sizes provide better frequency resolution but poorer time resolution - Smaller FFT sizes provide better time resolution but poorer frequency resolution Common FFT sizes: - 512: Fast response, suitable for real-time visualization - 1024: Good balance between frequency and time resolution - 2048: Better frequency resolution for detailed analysis - 4096 or higher: High frequency resolution for precision applications

parameters.name: result
parameters.summary: An array of Complex numbers representing the FFT output. Must not be null. The array length should typically be a power of 2 (e.g., 512, 1024, 2048, 4096) for optimal FFT performance.

properties.name: Result
properties.summary: Gets the array of complex numbers representing the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) result.
properties.value: An array of Complex objects where each element represents a frequency bin. The first half of the array contains the positive frequencies from 0 Hz to Nyquist frequency (sampleRate/2). The second half contains the negative frequencies (mirror image) which are typically ignored for real signals.

classes.name: VUMeterMaxSampleEventArgs
classes.summary: Provides data for events that report the minimum and maximum audio sample values for peak level monitoring.
classes.remarks: This event argument is essential for implementing peak meters, clipping indicators, and dynamic range monitoring in audio applications. It reports the extreme sample values detected within a specific time window, allowing applications to monitor signal peaks and detect potential audio issues. Common uses include: - Peak level meters with hold functionality - Clipping detection and warning systems - Dynamic range measurement - Automatic gain control (AGC) systems - Audio normalization and leveling Audio samples are typically normalized to the range [-1.0, 1.0], where: - 0.0 represents silence - 1.0 represents maximum positive amplitude (0 dBFS) - -1.0 represents maximum negative amplitude (0 dBFS) - Values exceeding ±1.0 indicate clipping (distortion)

constructors.name: VUMeterMaxSampleEventArgs
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VUMeterMaxSampleEventArgs class with the specified minimum and maximum sample values.
constructors.remarks: Sample values outside the range [-1.0, 1.0] indicate clipping or improper gain staging. Applications should monitor for values approaching or exceeding these limits to prevent audio distortion. The time window for detecting these extremes depends on the implementation but is typically synchronized with the audio buffer processing rate (e.g., every 10-50ms).

parameters.name: minValue
parameters.summary: The minimum sample value detected in the audio stream. Expected range is typically [-1.0, 0.0] for normalized audio, where -1.0 represents maximum negative amplitude.

parameters.name: maxValue
parameters.summary: The maximum sample value detected in the audio stream. Expected range is typically [0.0, 1.0] for normalized audio, where 1.0 represents maximum positive amplitude.

properties.name: MaxSample
properties.summary: Gets the maximum sample value detected by the VU meter within the measurement window.
properties.value: A Single representing the highest audio sample value. For normalized audio, values typically range from 0.0 to 1.0. Values exceeding 1.0 indicate clipping (audio distortion).

properties.name: MinSample
properties.summary: Gets the minimum sample value detected by the VU meter within the measurement window.
properties.value: A Single representing the lowest audio sample value. For normalized audio, values typically range from -1.0 to 0.0. Values below -1.0 indicate clipping (audio distortion).

This class implements and must be properly disposed to release native resources.

It creates the native processor instance, configures error logging, and initializes the video processing pipeline with the specified parameters. If initialization fails, the processor automatically cleans up any allocated resources.

The frame data is expected to be in RGB format and is modified in-place. Returns false once the processor is disposed: it runs on the streaming thread, where an exception would tear the application down.

If the filter rejects the value, the previous configuration stays in place and false is returned. After a failed Boolean), a corrected value (a valid file, for example) brings the processor up.

methods.remarks: This destructor is called by the garbage collector during finalization. It ensures that native resources are released even if Dispose is not called explicitly. For better performance, always call Dispose explicitly when done with the processor.

methods.name: Dispose

methods.remarks: This method destroys the native video processor instance and releases all associated resources. After calling Dispose, the processor instance cannot be reused. This method implements the pattern and should be called when the processor is no longer needed. Consider using a 'using' statement to ensure proper disposal.

properties.name: Video_Renderer_IsSync
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the video renderer synchronizes to the pipeline clock. When false (default), frames are rendered immediately for minimal latency — ideal for live camera preview. When true, the renderer waits for the pipeline clock, which adds latency but ensures precise A/V sync.

properties.name: Video_Output_IsSync
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the bridge feeding each output pipeline synchronizes to the pipeline clock. When true (default), it waits for the clock like any other sink. When false, buffers are handed over as they arrive, which is what a live capture branch wants: the sink then never waits out a render delay it was given, never has its queue fill, and cannot stall the tee - and everything sharing that tee, the preview included - with it. Set this to false for live capture; leave it alone when output timing must follow the clock. Read when an output's pipeline is built, so set it before the output is added - changing it afterwards, or after StartAsync, has no effect on an output that already exists.

properties.name: Audio_Output_IsSync
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the audio bridge feeding each output pipeline synchronizes to the pipeline clock. The audio counterpart of Video_Output_IsSync: set both the same way for a live capture, so the two branches of one output are handed over on the same terms rather than one waiting on the clock while the other does not. Unlike the video side, this is a consistency and latency control and not a fix for a known defect - a desktop capture measured over three runs recorded the same ~9-10 ms audio-ahead offset whichever way this was set, so do not expect it to change A/V alignment on its own. Like Video_Output_IsSync it is read when an output's pipeline is built, so set it before the output is added.

properties.name: Audio_Renderer_IsSync
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the audio renderer synchronizes to the pipeline clock. When false (default), audio buffers are rendered immediately for minimal latency. When true, the renderer waits for the pipeline clock for precise synchronization.

properties.summary: Gets or sets the URI of an external subtitle file to load. Supports common subtitle formats like SRT, SSA, and WebVTT.

properties.name: Video_Source
properties.summary: Gets or sets the video source configuration for capture. This can be a camera device, screen capture, IP camera, or other video source types.

properties.name: Audio_Source
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio source configuration for capture. This can be a microphone, system audio, or other audio input device.

properties.name: Video_Views
properties.summary: Gets the list of video view controls where captured video will be displayed. Add IVideoView implementations (UI controls) to enable video preview during capture.
properties.value: A list of video view instances.

properties.name: FallbackSwitchWrapper.OriginalSource
properties.summary: Gets the original video source settings before fallback switch wrapping. Contains the primary source configuration that will be used when available.

properties.name: FallbackSwitchWrapper.FallbackSettings
properties.summary: Gets the fallback switch settings that define the backup behavior. Includes fallback source configuration and failover parameters.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_AddOrUpdate
methods.summary: Adds a new audio effect or updates an existing one in the audio processing chain by name. Effects are applied in real-time to the audio stream during capture. If an effect with the same name exists, it will be updated with the new settings. Otherwise, a new effect is added to the chain.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.summary: The audio effect to add or update in the processing pipeline.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Remove
methods.summary: Removes a specific audio effect from the audio processing chain by instance reference. The capture is temporarily paused during removal to ensure smooth operation and prevent audio glitches. After removal, capture automatically resumes.
methods.remarks: An effect that changes the channel count of the running stream - a mono weighted channel mix on a stereo source - is not removed until the capture stops: the encoder and the muxer cannot take a channel-count change mid-recording. The refusal is reported as an error.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.summary: The audio effect instance to remove from the processing chain.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Remove
methods.summary: Removes an audio effect by its name identifier from the audio processing chain. The capture is temporarily paused during removal to ensure smooth operation and prevent audio glitches. After removal, capture automatically resumes. If no effect with the specified name exists, no action is taken.
methods.remarks: An effect that changes the channel count of the running stream - a mono weighted channel mix on a stereo source - is not removed until the capture stops: the encoder and the muxer cannot take a channel-count change mid-recording. The refusal is reported as an error.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The name of the audio effect to remove from the processing chain.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Clear
methods.summary: Removes all audio effects from the audio processing chain, restoring unprocessed audio. Use this to reset audio processing to default state without individual effect removal.
methods.remarks: An effect that changes the channel count of the running stream - a mono weighted channel mix on a stereo source - stays until the capture stops: the encoder and the muxer cannot take a channel-count change mid-recording. The refusal is reported as an error.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Get
methods.summary: Gets an audio effect by its name identifier from the audio effects chain. Use this to retrieve effect instances for inspection or modification of effect parameters.

parameters.name: effectName
parameters.summary: The name of the effect to retrieve from the processing chain.

methods.returns: The audio effect instance if found by name; otherwise, null if no effect with that name exists.

methods.name: VideoSampleGrabber_OnVideoFrameBuffer
methods.summary: Handles the OnVideoFrameBuffer event from the VideoSampleGrabber, processing each captured video frame. This method performs motion detection, face tracking, custom video processing, and raises frame events.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The source of the event, typically the VideoSampleGrabber instance.

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: The VideoFrameXBufferEventArgs instance containing the captured video frame data.

methods.name: StopCallbackHandler
methods.summary: Handles the stop callback event from the pipeline, forwarding it to the OnStop event.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.summary: The position in the media stream where playback stopped.

methods.name: ErrorCallbackHandler
methods.summary: Handles error callbacks from the pipeline, logging messages according to their severity level.

parameters.name: level
parameters.summary: The debug level indicating the severity of the error (Info, Warning, or Error).

parameters.name: text
parameters.summary: The error message text to be logged.

methods.name: InitCore
methods.summary: Initializes the cross-platform media framework and creates the video capture context. Sets up framework debug logging, logging context, and initializes the video composition manager.

methods.name: UnsubscribePipelineEvents
methods.summary: Detaches the forwarders StartAsync attached to the pipeline and releases them.

methods.name: ClearPipeline
methods.summary: Clears and disposes the current MediaBlocks pipeline. Stops the pipeline if running, removes event handlers, and releases all pipeline resources. Calls this method before creating a new pipeline or during cleanup.

methods.name: ClearPipelineAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously clears and disposes the current MediaBlocks pipeline. Stops the pipeline if running, removes event handlers, and releases all pipeline resources asynchronously.
methods.returns: A task representing the asynchronous clear operation.

methods.name: SafeDispose
methods.summary: Disposes one object of the capture context, logging rather than propagating a failure. Every release in ClearData reaches native code, and one that throws must not stop the rest of the teardown - the context is replaced either way, so whatever is skipped is left with no owner.

parameters.name: disposable
parameters.summary: The object to dispose. Ignored when null.

parameters.name: what
parameters.summary: Name used in the log message when the disposal throws.

methods.name: ReleaseOutputContexts
methods.summary: Disposes the output contexts of a finished session (#3458). Each output runs its own pipeline, and a stop only readies it for a restart: its blocks are cleaned up but not disposed, and nothing else owns the contexts once the capture context is replaced.
methods.remarks: The blocks the application assigned to an output's settings go with the pipeline, so the properties that still point at them are cleared - the next start then runs without them rather than wiring a disposed block. A block that was never wired, or that the application has already replaced, is left assigned.

methods.name: ClearData
methods.summary: Clears all capture context data and releases associated video/audio resources. Disposes renderers, sources, sample grabbers, motion detectors, and reinitializes the context.
methods.returns: true if data was successfully cleared; otherwise, false.

methods.name: AudioOutputMuteSet
methods.summary: Sets the mute state of the audio output renderer without changing the volume level. When muted, audio playback is silenced while preserving the current volume setting for when unmuted.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: true to mute audio playback; false to unmute and restore audio at the current volume level.

methods.name: AudioOutputMuteGet
methods.summary: Gets the current mute state of the audio output renderer. Returns whether audio playback is currently muted regardless of the volume level setting.
methods.returns: true if audio is currently muted; false if unmuted. Returns false if no audio renderer exists.

methods.name: SetCustomErrorHandler
methods.summary: Sets a custom error handler for the MediaBlocks pipeline to provide specialized error handling logic. The custom handler will be called for specific pipeline errors that require specialized handling beyond the default error processing. Pass null to remove custom error handling and revert to default behavior.

parameters.name: errorHandler
parameters.summary: The custom error handler implementation, or null to remove custom handling and use default error processing.

methods.name: Video_Source_GetResolutionAndFrameRate
methods.summary: Gets the current video resolution and frame rate from the active video source. Queries the video source output pad for current video format capabilities.

parameters.name: frameRate
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains the video frame rate in fps, or Empty if unavailable.

methods.returns: The video resolution as a Size structure, or Empty if unavailable or no video source is active.

methods.name: Audio_Source_GetInfo
methods.summary: Gets detailed audio format information from the current audio source. Queries the audio source output pad for current audio capabilities including sample rate, channels, and format.

parameters.name: sampleRate
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains the audio sample rate in Hz, or 0 if unavailable.

parameters.name: channels
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains the number of audio channels, or 0 if unavailable.

parameters.name: format
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains the audio sample format, or Unknown if unavailable.

methods.returns: true if audio information was successfully retrieved; false if no audio source is active or information is unavailable.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases unmanaged and optionally managed resources. Stops capture if active, closes pipeline resources, and disposes core components.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources.

methods.name: TryClaimClose
methods.summary: Claims the close for the calling dispose path; false when another one has claimed it.

methods.name: WaitOutRunningStop
methods.summary: Waits out a Stop running on another thread; one arriving after the close was claimed returns. Not on a thread with a synchronization context: a UI thread that Stop's video views may need. There a Stop already running when the close begins is not waited for - DisposeAsync waits for it.

methods.name: CloseAfterDeferredDispose
methods.summary: The close a Boolean) that could not wait for a start left to it, run by that start when it finishes. The Dispose has claimed the close.

methods.name: DisposeAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously releases resources used by the video capture engine. Implements the IAsyncDisposable pattern for async cleanup operations. Stops capture if active and properly releases all async resources.
methods.returns: A ValueTask representing the asynchronous dispose operation.

methods.name: FlushAndRearmLogger
methods.summary: Flushes the buffered debug-log sink and immediately builds a fresh one. Used on the faulted teardown path, where the object stays usable and a retry still needs somewhere to log.

methods.name: DisposeCore
methods.summary: Disposes core components including the video composition manager. Called during both synchronous and asynchronous disposal.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: Always true: Boolean) returns on the finalizer path before it can reach this method, so the only callers are the disposing branch of Boolean) and DisposeAsync.

methods.name: Finalize
methods.summary: Finalizer for the VideoCaptureCoreX class. Ensures resources are released if Dispose was not called explicitly.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Performs application-defined tasks associated with freeing, releasing, or resetting unmanaged resources. Call this method when done using the VideoCaptureCoreX instance to ensure proper cleanup.
methods.remarks: A start still building is cancelled and waited for. On a thread with a synchronization context, such as the UI thread its video views may need, and inside a handler raised during a stop, this method returns at once instead and the cancelled start closes the capture when it finishes. Call DisposeAsync instead of this method to wait for that. A Stop running on another thread is waited for too, except on a thread with a synchronization context; DisposeAsync waits for it there. Once the close has begun, a Stop does nothing and a Start returns false with an error. A call made while another Dispose or DisposeAsync is closing the capture returns without waiting.

methods.name: GetDiagramAsImage
methods.summary: Renders the current capture pipeline diagram as a raster image. When output pipelines are active, they are included below the main pipeline in a single vertically-stacked image with section headers. In mode, only the logical media block nodes and their connections are shown. This works at any time after blocks have been added (even before StartAsync). In mode, every pad is labelled with its media type and, when available, the underlying GStreamer pad name.

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary: Rendering options controlling mode, scale, spacing, colors, and orientation. Pass null to use defaults (HighLevel, scale 1.0, left-to-right).

methods.returns: An SKImage containing the rendered diagram, or null if no pipeline is active. The caller owns the image and must dispose it.

methods.name: GetDiagramAsSvg
methods.summary: Renders the current capture pipeline diagram as an SVG string. When output pipelines are active, they are included below the main pipeline in a single vertically-stacked SVG with section headers. In mode, only the logical media block nodes and their connections are shown. In mode, every pad is labelled with its media type and GStreamer pad name when available.

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary: Rendering options controlling mode, scale, spacing, colors, and orientation. Pass null to use defaults.

methods.returns: A complete SVG document as a string, or null if no pipeline is active.

methods.name: SetLicenseCertificateAsync
methods.summary: Loads a license certificate into this instance and activates it if the certificate requires activation.
methods.remarks: This is the only public licensing API. The file-path and stream overloads and every license-key method were removed in 2026.5.2, so an application reads the .vflicense file itself and passes the bytes here. The certificate belongs to this instance: call it on every instance you create, before starting it -- licensing one instance does not license another. Without a certificate the instance runs in the 30-day trial.

parameters.name: certificateData
parameters.summary: The bytes of a .vflicense certificate file issued by VisioForge.

methods.returns: A task that completes once the certificate has been loaded and any required activation has run.

methods.name: CheckLicenseOnStart
methods.summary: Validates the license on start. Sets dsVMREventID and propagates license to pipeline. Returns false if startup should be aborted.

methods.name: CheckRequiredLicense

methods.name: GetLicenseRequirement
methods.summary: Calculates the required edition and explanatory message for the current capture configuration.

methods.name: RequiresProfessionalNetworkStream

methods.name: ToLicenseLevel
methods.summary: Converts the numeric requirement level to the public enum.

methods.name: OnErrorCall
methods.summary: Handles error events from the logging system and forwards them to the public OnError event. Processes errors in a thread-safe manner and ensures proper event invocation.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The sender object. Can be null.

parameters.name: errorsEventArgs
parameters.summary: The error event arguments containing error details.

methods.name: GetLogger
methods.summary: Gets the current Serilog logger instance for this capture context.
methods.returns: The ILogger instance used for logging.

methods.name: GetContext
methods.summary: Gets the current logging and media context.
methods.returns: The ContextX instance containing logger and media configuration.

methods.name: _loggerSink_OnErrorX
methods.summary: Handles Serilog log events and converts them to error events for the public API. Also sends telemetry data to Sentry when enabled during debugging.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The source of the log event.

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: The Serilog log event containing error information.

methods.name: LoggerClose
methods.summary: Closes and disposes the current logger, replacing it with a silent logger. Ensures proper cleanup of logging resources.

methods.name: LoggerConfigure
methods.summary: Configures the logging system based on debug settings and error event requirements. Sets up file logging in debug mode and configures Sentry telemetry when enabled.

parameters.name: errorEvent
parameters.summary: Indicates whether to enable error event forwarding.

methods.name: LoggerSentryOnStartConfigure
methods.summary: Configures Sentry telemetry settings when capture starts. Collects environment information and system paths for debugging support. Only active when Debug_Telemetry is enabled and debugger is attached.

methods.name: InvokeErrorHandler
methods.summary: Invokes the error handler event or displays an error dialog if no handler is registered. On Windows, shows a message dialog if Debug_DisableMessageDialogs is false and no event handler exists.

parameters.name: args
parameters.summary: The error event arguments containing error details.

methods.name: Init
methods.summary: Initializes core video capture components and default settings. Configures callbacks, audio/video playback flags, initial state, and debug output directory.

methods.name: Subtitles_Settings_Update
methods.summary: Updates subtitle overlay settings for the video renderer. Call this method after modifying the Subtitles_Settings property to apply changes to the active renderer.

methods.name: StartAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously starts video capture with configured sources and outputs. Builds the media processing pipeline, initializes hardware devices, validates license, and begins capturing video/audio.
methods.returns: A task that returns true if capture started successfully; otherwise, false.

methods.name: AddVideoTee
methods.summary: Creates and configures a video tee element for splitting the video stream to multiple outputs. The tee allows parallel processing of video to multiple destinations such as preview, recording, and streaming.

parameters.name: pins
parameters.summary: The number of output pads (pins) to create for the tee. Each pad connects to a separate output or renderer.

methods.name: AddVideoRenderers
methods.summary: Creates and connects video renderer blocks for all configured video views. Each renderer is connected to a free output pad of the video tee and initialized with synchronization enabled. Notifies each video view to prepare for video rendering.

methods.name: AddNullVideoRenderer
methods.summary: Creates and connects a null video renderer that discards video frames without displaying them. Used when capture is active but no video preview is needed, allowing video processing and recording without display overhead.

methods.name: AddAudioRenderer
methods.summary: Creates and connects an audio renderer block for audio playback to the configured output device. Connects the renderer to a free output pad of the audio tee to enable live audio monitoring during capture.

methods.name: WaitForStartAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously waits for the capture pipeline to reach the playing state, for at most 30 seconds.
methods.remarks: Use CancellationToken) to choose the deadline or to cancel the wait, and to learn whether the pipeline actually reached PLAYING.
methods.returns: A task that completes when the pipeline is playing, when the start has settled somewhere it will not leave on its own, or when the 30-second deadline expires.

methods.name: WaitForStartAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously waits for the capture pipeline to reach the playing state.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.summary: How long to wait. InfiniteTimeSpan waits without a deadline (the wait still ends when the start settles somewhere it will not leave).

methods.returns: true if the pipeline reached PLAYING; false if the start settled without getting there or the deadline expired.

methods.name: OutputContainsType
methods.summary: Checks if any configured output matches the specified type. Used internally for license validation and feature availability checks.

parameters.name: type
parameters.summary: The output type to search for in the configured outputs collection.

methods.returns: true if at least one output of the specified type exists; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Start
methods.summary: Starts video capture with configured sources and outputs. Builds the media processing pipeline, initializes hardware devices, validates license, and begins capturing video/audio. This is a blocking call that waits for pipeline initialization. Use StartAsync for non-blocking operation.
methods.remarks: A stop still running on another thread is waited for before the start begins. That stop may need the UI thread - a video view's own teardown, or an OnStop handler that marshals to it synchronously - so call StartAsync rather than this method on the UI thread.
methods.returns: true if capture started successfully; false if startup failed.

methods.name: TryClaimStart
methods.summary: Claims the starting latch and numbers the start that claimed it.

parameters.name: method
parameters.summary: The public method, for the error reported when the latch is not free.

methods.returns: true if the latch was free and is now claimed.

methods.name: IsCloseClaimed
methods.summary: Whether a Dispose has claimed the close.

methods.name: CancelStart
methods.summary: Cancels the start in flight, if any. The start runs the stop itself once it is built.

parameters.name: finished
parameters.summary: Completes when the cancelled start has finished; null when none is in flight.

parameters.name: mayWait
parameters.summary: Whether the caller may block until then. Not on the start's own thread, and not on a thread with a synchronization context: a UI thread the start's video views marshal to. A caller inside a stop's handler must not wait either - it holds the stop lock the cancelled start needs.

methods.returns: The cancelled start's number; 0 when none is in flight.

methods.name: DeferCloseToStart
methods.summary: Leaves a Dispose that cannot wait for a start to the start in flight - cancelled here, in the same locked step, even if it began after the one the Dispose first cancelled - which closes the capture when it finishes.
methods.returns: true if the start will close the capture; false if no start is in flight.

methods.name: WaitForStartToFinish
methods.summary: Waits until the start numbered generation has released the starting latch.

methods.name: StartIntl
methods.summary: Performs the start with the starting latch already claimed by the caller (Start or StartAsync), and releases that claim on every exit.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.summary: The number Int32@) gave this start.

methods.returns: true if capture started successfully; false if startup failed.

methods.name: GetDefaultVideoView
methods.summary: Retrieves the first video view from the configured video views collection. The default view is used for error messages and primary preview operations.
methods.returns: The first IVideoView instance if available; otherwise, null.

methods.name: AudioSampleGrabber_OnAudioFrameBuffer
methods.summary: Forwards audio frame buffer events from the internal sample grabber to the public OnAudioFrameBuffer event. This handler provides a bridge between the internal audio grabber and external event subscribers.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The AudioSampleGrabber instance that captured the audio frame.

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: The AudioFrameBufferEventArgs containing the raw audio frame data and metadata.

methods.name: StopAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously stops video capture, finalizes recordings, and releases all resources. Stops all active outputs, closes video/audio devices, and clears the pipeline.
methods.returns: A task representing the asynchronous stop operation.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops video capture, finalizes recordings, and releases all resources. Stops all active outputs, closes video/audio devices, and clears the pipeline. This is a blocking call. Use StopAsync for non-blocking operation.
methods.remarks: A start still building its pipeline is cancelled: it stops once it is built and returns false. This method returns once that start has finished - except on a thread with a synchronization context, such as the UI thread, which the start's video views may need, and inside a handler raised during a stop. There it returns at once, and a start made before the cancelled one has finished is refused; call StopAsync instead to wait for it.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops the capture, or cancels the start in flight, for a Stop issued when startGeneration starts had been claimed.

parameters.name: startGeneration
parameters.summary: The starts issued before this Stop; one issued after it is not this Stop's to end (issue #4156).

methods.name: StopFromStart
methods.summary: The Stop a start makes of its own: the opening one before it builds, and the one a Stop that cancelled it left to it. Never cancels or waits for a start.

methods.name: StopLocked
methods.summary: Stops the views and the pipeline, with _stopLock held by the caller.
methods.returns: true if the capture was stopped and OnStop is to be raised.

methods.name: StopIntl
methods.summary: Performs the internal stop operation to halt all capture activities. Stops all configured outputs, stops the main pipeline, clears resources, and updates the playback state. This method is called by the public Stop and StopAsync methods.
methods.returns: true if a pipeline was stopped and OnStop is to be raised by the caller.

methods.name: CloseX
methods.summary: Closes the capture session and releases all associated resources synchronously. Clears the pipeline, clears data structures, and sets the state to Free. Called internally during Stop and Dispose operations.

methods.name: CloseAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously closes the capture session and releases all associated resources. Clears the pipeline asynchronously, clears data structures, and sets the state to Free. Provides a non-blocking cleanup operation during asynchronous disposal.
methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous close operation.

methods.name: PauseAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously pauses video capture while maintaining the pipeline state. Video/audio playback and recording are suspended but the pipeline remains ready to resume.
methods.returns: A task that returns true if capture was paused successfully; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Pause
methods.summary: Pauses video capture while maintaining the pipeline state. Video/audio playback and recording are suspended but the pipeline remains ready to resume.
methods.returns: true if capture was paused successfully; false if pause failed or pipeline is not active.

methods.name: ResumeAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously resumes video capture after being paused. Restarts video/audio playback and recording from the paused state.
methods.returns: A task that returns true if capture was resumed successfully; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Resume
methods.summary: Resumes video capture after being paused. Restarts video/audio playback and recording from the paused state.
methods.returns: true if capture was resumed successfully; false if resume failed or pipeline is not paused.

methods.name: WaitForEffectSpliceOffPlaying
methods.summary: Insurance against the graph being back on Playing when the effect edit runs: verifies, bounded, that the pipeline is verifiably off Playing. Pause settles its own transition synchronously (#1002), so this normally answers on its first poll.
methods.remarks: Success is a state that is actually not Playing (Paused, Null, Ready) with no transition in flight - not merely "no longer moving". A foreign resume completing inside the window answers Playing and must yield false, or the edit would run over a live graph in silence. Every iteration re-checks the wrapper's handle and the engine's stop/dispose flags before the native call: a teardown landing mid-wait zeroes the handle, and the gap between check and call stays open no matter what guards it - the same window every raw-state read in this SDK acknowledges.

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.summary: The raw GStreamer pipeline, or null when there is none.

methods.returns: true when the graph is verifiably not Playing, is gone, or the engine is stopping; false when it was still Playing when the cap ran out - in which case the caller logs before editing a live graph.

methods.name: WaitForEffectRemovalResume
methods.summary: Waits, bounded, for the resume issued by an effect edit to bring the pipeline back to Playing. This is the only place that transition is waited out: Resume answers whether SetState was accepted, not whether it completed (#1152).

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.summary: The raw GStreamer pipeline, or null when there is none.

methods.returns: true when the pipeline reached Playing, is gone, or the engine is stopping; false when the transition failed or never completed.

methods.name: Duration
methods.summary: Gets the current capture duration since start. Returns the elapsed time of the current capture session.
methods.returns: The current capture duration, or Zero if not capturing.

methods.name: DurationAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously gets the current capture duration since start. Returns the elapsed time of the current capture session.
methods.returns: A task containing the current capture duration, or Zero if not capturing.

methods.name: AudioOutputVolumeSet

methods.name: AudioOutputVolumeGet
methods.summary: Gets the current audio output playback volume.
methods.returns: The volume level from 0.0 (silent) to 1.0 (maximum), or 0 if no audio renderer exists.

methods.name: Outputs_Add
methods.summary: Adds a new output configuration to the capture engine for recording or streaming to a destination. Multiple outputs can be added to simultaneously record or stream to different destinations with independent settings. Each output operates in a separate pipeline branch with its own encoding and processing configuration. An output the engine refuses at start keeps its index: the outputs added after it are still addressed by theirs. String), Int32), Int32) and Int32) on the refused one return false and raise OnError; Int32), Int32) and Int32) return false or zero without an error.

parameters.name: output
parameters.summary: The output configuration defining the destination and encoding (file format, streaming destination, etc.).

parameters.name: autostart
parameters.summary: If set to true, the output will start automatically when capture begins; if false, use StartCapture to manually start the output later.

methods.name: Outputs_RemoveAt
methods.summary: Removes an output configuration at the specified index from the outputs collection. During a capture a running output is stopped as well, which finalizes its file; the call blocks until then and raises no OnOutputStopped, since the index no longer names the output. The outputs after it move down one index, for String), Int32) and Int32) as for Int32). Other running outputs are not affected.

parameters.name: index

methods.name: EffectsProduceUnpinnedFrameSize
methods.summary: True when the effects chain holds an effect whose output size cannot be pinned on the bridge up front.
methods.remarks: A resize is expressible: its output size is a constant, so the bridge is pinned to it. Crop, aspect-ratio crop and box are not - the size they produce is a function of the size that reached them, so the bridge cannot know it before the first frame. Pinning the source resolution instead makes the tee branch unsatisfiable: videoconvert cannot rescale, so the capsfilter would never negotiate and the capture would not start. Those effects leave the bridge unpinned and the inter pipe carries whatever the chain emits.
methods.returns: true when the bridge must follow the effect output instead of a fixed size.

methods.name: GetOutputBridgeFrameInfo
methods.summary: Returns the frame info an output bridge is pinned to, or null when the bridge must follow the frames.
methods.remarks: A mobile camera's size is known only once it negotiates: iOS swaps Format to portrait in SystemVideoSource.Init, after the outputs are added; a UVC camera settles on a mode of its own; Android rotation can change mid-session. A mobile screen source does not use Rectangle at all and delivers the full screen. Pinning the bridge to the size read from the settings would letterbox the recording or refuse a 0x0 size, so for those sources the bridge carries whatever arrives (#2574). When the source's frame info is known, a resize effect pins the bridge to its output size (even for those sources), and a crop or box effect unpins it.

parameters.name: frameInfo
parameters.summary: The frame info read from the video source settings.

methods.returns: The frame info for the bridge.

methods.name: GetUniversalSourceFrameInfo

methods.name: Video_Processing_AddBlock
methods.summary: Registers a video processing block (e.g. an AI object detector, OCR, face recognition or background removal block) to be inserted into the video chain on the next Start.
methods.remarks: Blocks must be registered before capture starts; calling this while the engine is running is a no-op (logged as a warning). The block is inserted after the video effects and before the sample grabber, so its overlays reach both the renderer and every output. Once capture starts the block is owned by the capture pipeline and is disposed when capture stops; register a fresh block instance before each session. Subscribe to the block's own event to receive detections.

parameters.summary: The video processing block to add. Ignored when null or already added.

methods.name: Audio_Processing_AddBlock

methods.remarks: The audio chain is only built when audio playback or recording is active, so an audio source must be configured for the block to run. Same lifecycle as IVideoProcessingBlock): register before Start; the block is owned and disposed by the capture pipeline once started.

parameters.name: block
parameters.summary: The audio processing block to add. Ignored when null or already added.

methods.name: Audio_Processing_RemoveBlock

methods.returns: true if the block was registered and removed; otherwise false.

methods.name: Audio_Processing_Clear

methods.name: DisposeRegisteredProcessingBlocksOnFailure
methods.summary: Disposes every registered processing block and clears the lists. Called on a failed Start (every failure exit, not just the exception path). Blocks already wired into the pipeline are disposed by ClearPipeline; re-disposing them here is a safe no-op because Dispose is idempotent. Blocks registered but never wired (the build failed before reaching them) are NOT owned by the pipeline, so disposing them here is what prevents their heavy native AI resources (ONNX / Whisper models) from leaking. The caller re-adds fresh blocks for the next session.

methods.name: DisposeUnwiredProcessingBlocks
methods.summary: Disposes and drops registered processing blocks whose host chain was NOT built on a SUCCESSFUL Start. A block registered for an inactive chain — a video block with no Video_Source, or an audio block with no audio source / neither Audio_Play nor Audio_Record — is never wired into the pipeline (the Start warning already surfaced the misconfiguration), so the pipeline never owns or disposes it and ClearData only clears the list reference. The engine owns registered blocks, so it disposes the un-wired ones here to keep their native AI models from leaking. Blocks for a chain that WAS built are owned by the pipeline and left untouched for the running session. Disposes outside the lock.

parameters.name: videoChainBuilt
parameters.summary: True if the video chain (and its block-wiring loop) ran.

parameters.name: audioChainBuilt
parameters.summary: True if the audio chain (and its block-wiring loop) ran.

methods.summary: Asynchronously captures a snapshot from the current video frame. Requires Snapshot_Grabber_Enabled to be true before starting capture.
methods.returns: A task containing the captured frame as VideoFrameX, or null if snapshot grabber is not enabled.

methods.name: Snapshot_Get
methods.summary: Captures a snapshot from the current video frame. Requires Snapshot_Grabber_Enabled to be true before starting capture. The caller is responsible for calling Free() on the returned VideoFrameX to release resources.
methods.returns: The captured frame as VideoFrameX, or null if snapshot grabber is not enabled.

methods.name: Snapshot_GetSKAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously captures a snapshot from the current video frame as a SkiaSharp bitmap. Requires Snapshot_Grabber_Enabled to be true before starting capture.
methods.returns: A task containing the captured frame as SKBitmap, or null if snapshot grabber is not enabled. Caller must dispose the bitmap.

methods.name: Snapshot_GetSK
methods.summary: Captures a snapshot from the current video frame as a SkiaSharp bitmap. Requires Snapshot_Grabber_Enabled to be true before starting capture.
methods.returns: The captured frame as SKBitmap, or null if snapshot grabber is not enabled or format is unsupported. Caller must dispose the bitmap.

methods.name: GetSourceMixerControl
methods.summary: Gets the video mixer control interface when using a VideoMixerSourceSettings as the video source. Allows dynamic control of video mixing parameters during capture.
methods.returns: The IVideoMixerControl interface if the source is a video mixer; otherwise, null.

methods.name: WrapWithFallbackSwitchIfEnabled
methods.summary: Checks if the video source has fallback switch capability enabled and wraps it with fallback functionality if configured. Fallback switch allows automatic failover to a backup source when the primary source fails or becomes unavailable. Validates fallback configuration and returns the original settings if fallback is not properly configured.

parameters.name: sourceSettings
parameters.summary: The source settings to check for fallback switch configuration.

methods.returns: The source settings wrapped with fallback switch if enabled and valid, otherwise the original settings unchanged.

methods.name: ValidateFallbackConfiguration
methods.summary: Validates the fallback configuration to ensure it contains all required information for the specified fallback type. Checks that text fallbacks have non-empty text, image fallbacks have valid file paths, and media fallbacks have valid URIs.
methods.returns: true if the configuration is valid and complete for the fallback type; false if validation fails.

methods.name: CreateBlock
methods.summary: Creates and returns a FallbackSwitchSourceBlock media block instance for the pipeline. The block handles automatic switching between the original source and fallback source.
methods.returns: A new FallbackSwitchSourceBlock configured with the wrapped source and fallback settings.

methods.name: AddVideoSource
methods.summary: Adds the configured video source to the capture pipeline and returns its output pad. Determines the source type from Video_Source property and creates the appropriate source block. Supports fallback switch wrapping for sources with failover capability enabled. An http or https ONVIF device-service address in RTSPSourceSettings is resolved to the camera's RTSP URL first, with or without the fallback switch.
methods.returns: The output pad of the video source if successful; otherwise, null if source creation or configuration fails.

methods.name: AddVideoSourceUniversal
methods.summary: Adds a universal source that can handle various media formats and protocols with automatic detection. Supports files, HTTP/RTSP streams, and network sources. Automatically enables audio rendering if configured and no explicit audio source is set.

parameters.name: universal
parameters.summary: The universal source settings including URI and rendering options.

methods.returns: The video output pad of the universal source for connecting to the pipeline.

methods.name: AddVNCVideoSource
methods.summary: Adds a VNC (Virtual Network Computing) source for remote desktop capture over VNC protocol. Allows capturing video from VNC servers with configurable resolution and connection parameters.

parameters.name: vnc
parameters.summary: The VNC source settings including server address, port, credentials, and capture resolution.

methods.returns: The output pad of the VNC source for connecting to the video pipeline.

methods.name: AddVideoSourceByBlock
methods.summary: Adds a custom video source using a pre-created MediaBlock instance from plugins or custom implementations. Used for extensibility when source types are not directly supported by the SDK but implement the MediaBlock interface. Commonly used with Spinnaker, GenICam, and other third-party source plugins.

parameters.name: block
parameters.summary: The pre-created media block instance to use as video source.

methods.returns: The output pad of the provided media block for connecting to the pipeline.

methods.name: AddNDIVideoSource
methods.summary: Adds an NDI (Network Device Interface) source for IP-based professional video capture over local networks. Supports capturing from NDI-enabled devices and applications. Automatically configures audio source if NDI stream contains audio. Attempts to read stream information to determine available audio/video streams.

parameters.name: ndi
parameters.summary: The NDI source settings including device name, network parameters, and stream selection.

methods.returns: The output pad of the NDI source for connecting to the video pipeline.

methods.name: AddBaslerVideoSource
methods.summary: Adds a Basler industrial camera source using the Pylon SDK. Supports high-performance machine vision cameras.

parameters.name: basler
parameters.summary: The Basler camera settings including device selection and capture parameters.

methods.returns: The output pad of the Basler camera source.

methods.name: AddAlliedVisionVideoSource
methods.summary: Adds an Allied Vision industrial camera source using the Vimba SDK. Supports professional machine vision and scientific cameras.

parameters.name: basler
parameters.summary: The Allied Vision camera settings including device and capture configuration.

methods.returns: The output pad of the Allied Vision camera source.

methods.name: AddVideoSourceWithFallbackSwitch
methods.summary: Adds a video source with fallback switch capability for automatic failover to a backup source. Creates a fallback switch source block that monitors the main source and automatically switches to the configured fallback (static image, text, or media) when the main source fails or becomes unavailable. Configures audio failover if enabled and the main source supports audio.

parameters.name: fallbackWrapper

methods.returns: The video output pad of the fallback switch source if successful; otherwise, null if creation fails.

methods.name: AddVideoSourceVirtual
methods.summary: Adds a virtual video source that generates synthetic test patterns or solid colors without requiring physical devices. Useful for testing, development, and creating placeholder content. Supports various test patterns including SMPTE color bars, black, white, and custom colors.

parameters.name: virtualVideo
parameters.summary: The virtual video source settings including pattern type, resolution, frame rate, and color parameters.

methods.returns: The output pad of the virtual video source for connecting to the pipeline.

methods.name: AddImageVideoSource
methods.summary: Adds an image-based video source that displays static images or animated image sequences as video. Can create video from single images (displayed continuously) or animated sequences from multiple images. Supports various image formats including JPEG, PNG, BMP, and animated formats.

parameters.name: imageVideo
parameters.summary: The image video source settings including image path(s), display duration, resolution, and frame rate.

methods.returns: The output pad of the image video source for connecting to the pipeline.

methods.name: AddInternalVideoSource
methods.summary: Adds a bridge video source for inter-pipeline video data sharing using shared memory. Allows receiving video from another pipeline or process through named shared memory buffers. Used for advanced scenarios requiring video data exchange between separate SDK instances or applications.

parameters.name: internalVideo

methods.returns: The output pad of the bridge video source for connecting to the pipeline.

methods.name: AddVideoSourceRTSP
methods.summary: Adds an RTSP (Real Time Streaming Protocol) source for IP camera capture and network video streaming. An ONVIF device-service address has already been resolved to the RTSP URL by AddVideoSource. Configures audio source automatically if the RTSP stream contains audio tracks.

parameters.name: rtsp
parameters.summary: The RTSP source settings including URL, authentication credentials, and connection parameters.

methods.returns: The video output pad of the RTSP source for connecting to the pipeline.

methods.name: AddVideoSourceHTTPMJPEG
methods.summary: Adds an HTTP MJPEG source for capturing motion JPEG streams from IP cameras over HTTP protocol. Supports cameras that provide MJPEG (Motion JPEG) streams, which are sequences of JPEG images. Commonly used with security cameras and webcams that support MJPEG streaming.

parameters.name: mjpeg
parameters.summary: The HTTP MJPEG source settings including URL, authentication credentials, and connection parameters.

methods.returns: The output pad of the MJPEG source for connecting to the video pipeline.

methods.name: AddVideoSourceSRT
methods.summary: Adds an SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) source for low-latency video streaming with error correction. Supports receiving SRT streams with built-in error recovery and optional encryption. SRT is ideal for live streaming over unreliable networks, providing better quality than TCP-based protocols. Automatically configures audio source if the SRT stream contains audio tracks.

parameters.name: srt
parameters.summary: The SRT source settings including connection mode (caller/listener), address, port, latency, and encryption.

methods.returns: The video output pad of the SRT source for connecting to the pipeline.

methods.name: AddVideoSourceScreen
methods.summary: Adds a screen capture source for recording desktop, window, or region content with optional cursor rendering. Supports full screen capture, specific window capture, or custom rectangular region capture. Platform-specific implementations provide optimal performance for each operating system. Frame rate and cursor visibility can be configured.

parameters.name: screen
parameters.summary: The screen capture settings including capture mode (fullscreen/window/region), area, frame rate, and cursor options.

methods.returns: The output pad of the screen capture source for connecting to the pipeline.

methods.name: MouseHighlight_Subscribe
methods.summary: Subscribes to global mouse events for the mouse click highlight overlay. On Windows, this installs a global mouse hook that captures all mouse clicks. On other platforms, use Int32) to feed click events manually. Requires MouseHighlight to be set in the video source settings before starting.

methods.summary: Unsubscribes from global mouse events and disposes the mouse hook.

Use this method on platforms where global mouse hooks are not available, or to simulate click highlights programmatically. Requires MouseHighlight to be set in the video source settings before starting.

parameters.name: screenX
parameters.summary: The screen X coordinate of the click.

parameters.name: screenY
parameters.summary: The screen Y coordinate of the click.

methods.name: MouseHighlight_UpdateSettings
methods.summary: Updates the mouse highlight settings on the underlying filter in real-time. Call this after modifying MouseHighlight on the video source settings while the pipeline is running.

methods.name: AddVideoSourceCaptureDevice
methods.summary: Adds a system video capture device source such as webcams, USB capture cards, or built-in cameras. Uses platform-specific APIs (DirectShow on Windows, AVFoundation on macOS/iOS, V4L2 on Linux, Camera2 on Android) to access video capture hardware. Supports device selection, format configuration, and camera controls.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The capture device settings including device selection, video format (resolution/frame rate), and camera controls.

methods.returns: The output pad of the video capture device for connecting to the pipeline.

methods.name: AddDecklinkVideoSource
methods.summary: Adds a Blackmagic DeckLink professional video capture device source for high-quality SDI and HDMI input. Supports professional video equipment including broadcast cameras, switchers, and playback devices. Provides access to uncompressed video capture with precise timing and genlock support.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The DeckLink device settings including device selection, input connection type (SDI/HDMI), and video mode.

methods.returns: The output pad of the DeckLink video source for connecting to the pipeline.

methods.name: AddVideoMixerSource
methods.summary: Adds a video mixer source that combines multiple video inputs into a single composited output stream. Supports various layouts including picture-in-picture, side-by-side, grid, and custom positioning. Each input can have independent position, size, and z-order for flexible video composition.

parameters.name: pipeline

parameters.name: settings
