methods.summary: Serializes the current VideoEditCoreX instance settings to a JSON string.
methods.returns: A JSON representation of the current settings, or empty string if serialization fails.

methods.name: Settings_Load
methods.summary: Loads SDK configuration settings from a JSON file, restoring all properties to their saved values.
methods.remarks: This method deserializes the JSON file and copies all property values to the current instance. The settings file should have been previously created using String). This is useful for persisting user configurations or restoring complex editing setups. Verify the file exists before calling to avoid errors.

parameters.name: jsonFilename
parameters.summary: The full path to the JSON settings file to load.

methods.returns: true if settings were successfully loaded; false if the file doesn't exist or loading failed.

methods.name: Settings_Save
methods.summary: Saves the current SDK configuration settings to JSON files for later restoration.
methods.remarks: This method serializes the current VideoEditCoreX configuration to JSON format, including all properties, effects, and transitions. Video effects are saved to a separate "_video_effects.json" file in the same directory. Use String) to restore these settings later. The directory is created if it doesn't exist. Settings can be used to persist user preferences or save complex editing projects for later resumption.

parameters.name: jsonFilename
parameters.summary: The full path where the main settings JSON file will be saved.

parameters.name: infoFilename
parameters.summary: Optional path for saving SDK version information. Can be null or empty to skip.

methods.returns: true if settings were successfully saved; false if an error occurred during saving.

methods.name: LoggerSentryOnStartConfigure
methods.summary: Configures Sentry telemetry on start, attaching relevant debug information including environment paths and runtime details.

methods.name: InvokeErrorHandler
methods.summary: Invokes the error handler.

parameters.name: args
parameters.summary: The ErrorsEventArgs instance containing the event data.

methods.name: ReportMissingNativeLibrary
methods.summary: Tells the developer that a native library the SDK needs is missing, without going back through the logger that is currently reporting the error (see ErrorsEventArgs)).
methods.remarks: The hint is not a copy of the error already in the log - it is the actionable half - so it goes to Trace as well as to the video view. An instance built for rendering to a file, which is most of them, has no view to show it on.

parameters.name: library
parameters.summary: File name of the missing native library.

methods.name: Build
methods.summary: Builds the video editing pipeline, configures license checks, and sets up bus event handlers.
methods.returns: true if the pipeline was successfully built; otherwise, false.

methods.name: UsePipeline
methods.summary: Starts a use of the current pipeline: until it is disposed, TakePipeline does not hand the pipeline over for release. Nothing inside a use should log or reach user code.
methods.returns: The use; its pipeline is null if there is none.

methods.name: TakePipeline
methods.summary: Clears the pipeline field and hands the pipeline back for the caller to dispose. Once this returns, no query holding _pipelineReleaseLock and no UsePipeline use is still using it. The wait is short - the caller has set the pipeline to NULL first - and bounded: a use that outlives it, or one this thread holds, leaves the pipeline undisposed, to the garbage collector.
methods.returns: The pipeline, or null if there was none or it must not be disposed now.

methods.name: TryClaimTeardown
methods.summary: Claims the current pipeline's teardown.

parameters.name: drains
parameters.summary: Whether the caller may drain a render before the teardown (Stop, Dispose): the claim then reads TeardownClaimedDraining until Pipeline) is done, so a path that loses it waits for the drain too.

methods.returns: true if the caller now owns the teardown; false if another path already does.

methods.name: VerifyGesThread
methods.summary: Throws instead of letting a GES call from another thread than _gesThread abort the process (#3438). Called at the end of CheckPipeline, which may build the pipeline on the calling thread. A timeline waiting to be rebuilt is not checked: the next session's thread builds its own, and the callers do not touch the old one.

methods.name: SDKInit
methods.summary: Initializes GStreamer and the GES timeline editing services. Optional: every VideoEditCoreX constructor already performs this initialization.
methods.remarks: The initialization entry point for an application is Boolean): it loads the GStreamer bindings, configures the local GStreamer redistributable on Windows and wires the logging context, but it does not touch GES. This method adds the GES half and is kept for callers that want to pay that cost up front rather than inside the first constructor. Calling it is never required, and calling it twice is harmless.
methods.returns: true if both GStreamer and GES initialized successfully; otherwise, false.

methods.name: CreateGESPipeline
methods.summary: Creates the GES pipeline with every rank-none encoder visible to its encodebin.
methods.remarks: encodebin lists its encoder candidates once, when the GES pipeline is built, and leaves out rank-none factories - so a profile pinned to avenc_aac, wavpackenc or a rank-none hardware encoder never found it (#2189). They are lifted to MARGINAL for this construction only; the lock keeps a concurrent construction from restoring them under it. wavpackparse is dropped below MARGINAL for the same construction, so encodebin plugs no parser after wavpackenc: the parser appends the first block wavpackenc rewrites at EOS to the end of the file, a WavPack output then ends on a block timestamped 0 (#4107).

methods.name: CreatePipeline
methods.summary: Creates a new pipeline with timeline, layers, and tracks for video editing operations.

methods.name: InitIntl
methods.summary: Initializes the internal core components including media framework, pipeline creation, and progress timer.

methods.name: Start
methods.summary: Starts the video editing operation, either beginning timeline playback for preview or initiating rendering to the output file. Validates license, builds the pipeline with all configured clips, effects, and transitions, and begins processing.
methods.remarks: This method performs license validation, constructs the complete editing pipeline including all input clips, effects, transitions, and output settings, then starts either preview playback or file rendering depending on the configuration. Progress can be monitored through the OnProgress event.
methods.returns: true if the operation started successfully; otherwise, false - including a call on a disposed instance, and a call made while the previous session cannot finish stopping in time, such as from an SDK event handler or while an OnStop handler holds up this thread, which is reported through OnError unless another thread's Stop is under way. Call it again once the handler has returned, adding again any input added before that: it went to the session that ended.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops the current video editing operation, whether it's timeline preview playback or rendering to file. Gracefully shuts down the pipeline and releases associated resources.
methods.remarks: This method sends an end-of-stream event to the pipeline, waits for proper shutdown, and cleans up all pipeline resources. After stopping, the pipeline can be reconfigured and started again.
methods.returns: true if the stop operation completed successfully; otherwise, false - including a render to a file whose output could not be finished (an error or a timeout while the encoders drained), where the pipeline is stopped all the same and OnStop is raised.

methods.name: WaitForTeardown
methods.summary: Waits for a teardown another path owns. While that owner drains, the drain is waited for first - it can take DrainTimeout, and Pipeline) signals its end however it ends - and the teardown after it with normal only, which stays short because the owner's OnStop handler may be marshalling to this thread.

parameters.name: normal
parameters.summary: The wait for the teardown itself.

methods.name: DrainFileRender
methods.summary: Lets a render to a file finish its output before the teardown forces the pipeline to NULL (#2041): sends EOS below the timeline and waits until it reaches the bus, an error ends the drain, or DrainTimeout runs out. A preview has nothing to finish. The caller holds the teardown claim, so Bus_EOS only signals the wait.
methods.returns: false if the output was not finished: an error ended the drain, it timed out, or it could not run; otherwise true, including when there was nothing to drain.

methods.name: DrainFileRenderCore
methods.summary: The body of Pipeline).
methods.returns: Whether the output was finished.

methods.name: SendEosBelowTimeline
methods.summary: Sends EOS into each track's branch below the timeline, so the encoders drain and the muxer writes its trailer (#2041). An EOS sent to the pipeline goes to the sources inside the timeline's nlecompositions, whose src pad probe drops every EOS but the composition's own end-of-timeline one.

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.summary: The pipeline being drained; a late send skips any other one.

methods.name: DestroyPipeline
methods.summary: Destroys the pipeline and releases all associated resources including timeline, layers, assets, and clips. The caller must hold the teardown claim (Boolean)); _teardownDone is set on the way out, whatever happens inside, and what the teardown logged reaches OnError only after it.

parameters.name: raiseAsLogged
parameters.summary: Set by the teardown Dispose() runs itself: no next session waits for it, and raised as logged, what it reports reaches OnError before Dispose() returns rather than racing it from a pool thread.

methods.name: RaiseTeardownErrors
methods.summary: Raises the errors through the log observer and its re-entrancy guard (#1173). This can run after Dispose(): the customer may have released what the handler uses, so those not yet raised are dropped once it has started. One already being raised can overlap Dispose(), which cannot wait for it: the handler may wait for that thread.

parameters.name: errors
parameters.summary: The errors, in the order they were logged.

methods.name: DestroyPipelineIntl
methods.summary: The body of Boolean).

methods.name: ClearData
methods.summary: Resets the playback state and marks the pipeline for recreation.
methods.returns: Always true.

methods.name: DeleteTempFiles
methods.summary: Deletes the temporary copies of the inputs added from a stream and the text overlay images. A file that cannot be deleted - a pipeline left to the garbage collector still holds it open - stays in the list for the next teardown, Dispose()'s included; _startFiles is reset, as every file in it is in that list.

methods.name: TryDeleteTempFile
methods.summary: Deletes a temporary file; one that cannot be deleted is reported.
methods.returns: true when the file is gone.

methods.name: WaitForStoppingSession
methods.summary: Waits for a stopping session's teardown, so that a caller reacting to OnStop while the handler is still returning gets the next session (#3685). Bounded, because the handler may be marshalling to this thread, and not extended for another path's drain as TimeSpan) does: a sink marshalling to this thread would hold up that drain and cut off its output. Skipped on the thread running the teardown and on the main loop, which the teardown may need. In each of those cases the session can still be stopping on return.

methods.name: CheckPipeline
methods.summary: Checks if pipeline needs to be recreated and performs recreation if necessary.

methods.name: StopCallbackHandler
methods.summary: Stop callback handler.

methods.name: ErrorCallbackHandler
methods.summary: Error callback handler.

methods.name: EOS_Callback
methods.summary: EOS callback. Invoked by the bus when the pipeline reaches end-of-stream naturally (e.g. timeline finished playing). Bus_EOS has already stopped the progress timer and transitioned the pipeline to Ready, and it will invoke OnStopCallback (TimeSpan)) immediately after this method returns to perform the actual teardown (ClearData + DestroyPipeline). This callback is responsible for flipping the local lifecycle flags so subsequent Stop / Start calls see a consistent state, and for emitting a log breadcrumb so a natural EOS is distinguishable from a user-initiated stop in the trace. Bus_EOS has claimed the teardown before calling this, so the teardown is left to the OnStopCallback chain.

methods.name: _progressTimer_Elapsed
methods.summary: Handles the Elapsed event of the _progressTimer control.

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: The ElapsedEventArgs instance containing the event data.

methods.name: Duration
methods.summary: Gets the total duration of the timeline based on all clips, effects, and transitions currently in the project.
methods.remarks: The duration reflects the combined length of all media on the timeline, including any transitions. Returns TimeSpan.Zero if the pipeline is not initialized or no clips have been added.
methods.returns: A TimeSpan representing the total timeline duration.

methods.name: Position_Get
methods.summary: Gets the current playback or rendering position within the timeline.
methods.remarks: During preview playback, this indicates the current viewing position. During rendering, this reflects the progress of the rendering operation. Returns TimeSpan.Zero if the pipeline is not initialized.
methods.returns: A TimeSpan representing the current position in the timeline.

methods.name: Position_Set
methods.summary: Sets the current playback position within the timeline, allowing you to jump to a specific time during preview.
methods.remarks: Seeking to keyframes is faster but less precise. For frame-accurate positioning during editing, set seekToKeyframe to false. This method only works during preview playback, not during rendering.

parameters.name: position
parameters.summary: The target position in the timeline to seek to.

parameters.name: seekToKeyframe
parameters.summary: If true, seeks to the nearest keyframe for faster seeking; if false, seeks to the exact frame (slower but more accurate).

methods.name: GetSnapshot
methods.summary: Gets the snapshot (in Preview mode).
methods.returns: Bitmap.

methods.name: IsUsableSize
methods.summary: Whether a video size is usable: both dimensions set. A size with one zero dimension is not a size - the track caps fall back to 1920x1080 for it - so it must neither count as the caller's own setting nor stop an input from replacing it (#3557).
methods.returns: true when both dimensions are non-zero.

methods.name: UpdateVideoTrack
methods.summary: Updates the video track restriction caps with the configured video size and frame rate settings.

parameters.name: gesDefaultWhenNothingSet
parameters.summary: True for a timeline that asked for no output format at all and has nothing left to derive one from - a cleared input list. Its caps go back to what GES gives such a timeline, 1280x720 at 30 fps (ges-internal.h:68-71), rather than the 1920x1080 fallback, which is for a half-set output (#3557).

methods.name: GetClipVideoInfo
methods.summary: Reads the first video stream's properties from a clip asset's discovered info.
methods.returns: The first video stream's properties, or null when the asset exposes none.

methods.name: UpdateAudioTrack
methods.summary: Updates the audio track restriction caps with the configured sample rate and channel settings.

methods.name: AddOutputOPUS
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for Opus audio-only output in Ogg container format. Configures high-quality audio encoding profile suitable for voice, music, and streaming applications with excellent compression efficiency and low latency support.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The Opus output configuration specifying bitrate, sample rate, and encoding quality parameters.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for Opus audio output in Ogg container, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputFLAC
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for FLAC lossless audio-only output without container wrapping. Configures lossless audio compression profile that preserves perfect audio quality while reducing file size, ideal for archival and audiophile applications.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The FLAC output configuration specifying compression level and audio parameters.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for FLAC lossless audio output, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputWavPack
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for WavPack audio-only output, written without a container like FLAC.
methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile, or null when there is no audio to encode.

methods.name: AddOutputSpeex
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for Speex audio-only output in Ogg container format. Configures voice-optimized audio encoding profile specifically designed for speech compression with low bitrate requirements, commonly used in VoIP and voice recording applications.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The Speex output configuration specifying quality, bitrate mode, and voice enhancement parameters.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for Speex audio output in Ogg container, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputWAV
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for WAV uncompressed audio output in RIFF WAV container format. Configures lossless, uncompressed PCM audio profile providing maximum quality and compatibility, commonly used in professional audio production and as an intermediate format.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The WAV output configuration specifying sample format, bit depth, and channel layout.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for WAV uncompressed audio output, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputOGGVorbis
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for Ogg Vorbis audio-only output in Ogg container format. Configures high-quality lossy audio compression profile that provides excellent audio quality at reasonable bitrates, widely used as an open-source alternative to proprietary audio codecs.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The Ogg Vorbis output configuration specifying quality level, bitrate management, and encoding parameters.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for Ogg Vorbis audio output, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputMP3
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for MP3 audio-only output with ID3 tagging support. Configures the widely compatible MPEG-1 Layer 3 audio codec profile, the de facto standard for music distribution and portable audio with universal device and software support.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The MP3 output configuration specifying bitrate mode (CBR/VBR), quality, and ID3 metadata parameters.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for MP3 audio output with ID3 container, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputMKV
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for Matroska (MKV) container format with flexible video and audio codec support. Configures a versatile open-source container profile supporting H.264, HEVC, MJPEG video codecs and MP3, AAC, Vorbis, Opus audio codecs, providing excellent codec compatibility and modern features.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The MKV output configuration specifying video encoder (H.264/HEVC/MJPEG) and audio encoder (MP3/AAC/Vorbis/Opus/AptX) settings.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for MKV container output with selected codecs, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputFLV
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for Flash Video (FLV) container format with H.264 video and AAC/MP3 audio. Configures a profile suitable for web streaming and legacy Flash-based video platforms, though modern web standards favor WebM or MP4 for new applications.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The FLV output configuration specifying H.264 video encoder and AAC/MP3/AptX audio encoder settings.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for FLV container output, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputAVI
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for Audio Video Interleave (AVI) container format with various video and audio codec support. Configures a classic multimedia container profile supporting H.264, HEVC, MJPEG video codecs and AAC, MP3, AptX audio codecs, maintaining compatibility with legacy systems while supporting modern codecs.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The AVI output configuration specifying video encoder (H.264/HEVC/MJPEG) and audio encoder (AAC/MP3/AptX) settings.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for AVI container output with selected codecs, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputDV
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for Digital Video (DV) format in AVI container, used for professional video editing. Configures a profile for DV codec, the standard format for digital camcorders and professional video production, maintaining broadcast-quality video with fixed bitrate and frame-accurate editing support.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The DV output configuration specifying DV video encoder format and parameters.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for DV format output in AVI container, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputMPEGTS
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for MPEG Transport Stream (MPEG-TS) container format with H.264/HEVC video and AAC/MP3 audio. Configures a broadcast-standard container profile supporting streaming and broadcast applications, with robust error resilience and multiplexing capabilities for professional video distribution.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The MPEG-TS output configuration specifying video encoder (H.264/HEVC) and audio encoder (AAC/MP3/AptX) settings.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for MPEG-TS container output with 192-byte packet size, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputMXF
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for the MXF container with H.264 video and MP3 audio. A stream whose MXF stream type is None is left out, as the capture engine does.
methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile, or null when an encoder the MXF muxer cannot take is set.

methods.name: AddOutput
methods.summary: Configures and applies the output format, encoders, and rendering settings to the editing pipeline based on the Output_Format property. Creates encoding profiles for container and codec configuration, detects available audio and video streams, and initializes the rendering pipeline mode (smart render or full re-encode).
methods.remarks: This method performs several critical operations: validates the output filename and creates the output directory, detects whether audio and video streams are present in the timeline, constructs the appropriate encoding profile based on the output format type (MP4, WebM, MKV, etc.), configures the encoding mode (smart render or full render), and applies the profile to the pipeline. If Output_Format is null or has an empty filename, the method returns true to allow preview-only mode without file output.
methods.returns: true if the output configuration was successfully applied to the pipeline; false if profile creation failed or rendering settings could not be applied.

methods.name: AttachWmvPtsRebaser
methods.summary: Attaches a WmvOutputPtsRebaser to the src pad of an avenc_wmv1 element encodebin has just created, so the gst-libav min-pts offset is stripped before asfmux. Called on a GStreamer thread by _wmvEncoderWatcher.

methods.name: ClearWmvPtsRebasers
methods.summary: Detaches every WMV output PTS rebaser (removes its native buffer probe and releases the pinned encoder src pad) and clears the list. Must be called while the encoder pads are still live, i.e. before the render pipeline is disposed. Detach is idempotent, so calling this after a previous teardown is safe. Serialized against the deep-element-added handler via _wmvPtsRebasersLock.

methods.name: TeardownWmvOutput
methods.summary: Tears down the WMV output rebaser hook on the render teardown path: disconnects the deep-element-added watcher from the pipeline and detaches/clears every rebaser while the encoder pads are still live. Call BEFORE the pipeline (and its encoder elements) is disposed. Safe to call when no WMV render is active — it is a no-op if the watcher was never created and the list is empty.

methods.name: ResolveOutputVideoSettings
methods.summary: Returns the video encoder settings carried by the current Output_Format, or null when the format has none (audio-only formats, DV, WMV).

methods.name: DisposeLibAVDirectRenderingWatcher
methods.summary: Disconnects the libav direct-rendering watcher. Same rule as DisposeEncoderConfigWatcher: the watched pipeline must still be alive.

methods.name: DisposeEncoderConfigWatcher
methods.summary: Disconnects the encoder-configuration watcher. Must be called while the watched pipeline is still alive - before the pipeline wrapper is disposed on the teardown path, and at the start of every AddOutput before re-subscribing.

methods.name: GetPresentTrackTypes
methods.summary: The track types the source clips of every layer of the timeline support, combined. Used during output configuration to decide which encoder profiles the output gets: a timeline whose clips all sit on an added layer still needs them, or the render never ends (#3599). The effect and transition clips Start puts on the timeline are left out: a video transition on an audio-only timeline must not add a black video stream.
methods.returns: The union of every source clip's supported formats; 0 for an empty timeline.

methods.name: AddOutputGIF
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for animated GIF output. GIF has no container — gifenc emits the final file directly.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The GIF output configuration specifying loop count and encoding speed.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingVideoProfile ready for GIF output, or null if the timeline has no video stream or profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputM4A
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for MPEG-4 Audio (M4A) container format with AAC audio encoding. Configures an audio-only profile using the MP4 container with AAC codec, providing excellent audio quality and compatibility across Apple devices and modern media players.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The M4A output configuration specifying AAC audio encoder bitrate, quality, and profile settings.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for M4A audio-only output in MP4 container, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputMP4
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for MPEG-4 (MP4) container format with H.264/HEVC video and AAC/MP3 audio. Configures the industry-standard MP4 container profile with modern video codecs (H.264 or HEVC) and audio codecs (AAC, MP3, AptX), providing universal compatibility and excellent compression efficiency.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The MP4 output configuration specifying video encoder (H.264/HEVC) and audio encoder (AAC/MP3/AptX) settings.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for MP4 container output with selected codecs, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputMOV
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for QuickTime (MOV) container format with H.264/HEVC video and AAC/MP3 audio. Configures Apple's multimedia container profile supporting modern video codecs (H.264 or HEVC) and audio codecs (AAC, MP3, AptX), providing excellent compatibility with Apple ecosystem and professional tools.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The MOV output configuration specifying video encoder (H.264/HEVC) and audio encoder (AAC/MP3/AptX) settings.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for MOV container output with selected codecs, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputWebM
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for WebM container format with VP8/VP9 video encoding and Vorbis/Opus audio encoding. Configures video and audio encoder profiles based on the provided settings, supporting modern web-friendly output with efficient compression and broad browser compatibility.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The WebM output configuration specifying video encoder (VP8/VP9) and audio encoder (Vorbis/Opus) settings.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for WebM container output, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputOGGTheora
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for Ogg Theora container format with Theora video encoding and Vorbis audio encoding. Configures a standards-compliant profile for open-source Ogg multimedia container with widely supported codecs.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The Ogg Theora output configuration specifying Theora video and Vorbis audio encoder settings.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for Ogg Theora/Vorbis output, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputWMA
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for Windows Media Audio (WMA) output in ASF container format. Configures Microsoft's proprietary audio codec profile providing efficient compression with good quality, commonly used on Windows platforms and in Windows Media ecosystem.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The WMA output configuration specifying bitrate, quality, and encoding mode parameters.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for WMA audio output in ASF container, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: AddOutputWMV
methods.summary: Creates an encoding profile for Windows Media Video (WMV) format in ASF container with WMV video and WMA audio. Configures Microsoft's proprietary multimedia container and codecs profile, providing efficient compression with good quality, commonly used on Windows platforms and Windows Media ecosystem.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.summary: The WMV output configuration specifying WMV video encoder and WMA audio encoder quality and bitrate settings.

methods.returns: A configured EncodingProfile ready for WMV/WMA output in ASF container, or null if profile creation fails.

methods.name: Input_AddAudioFile
methods.summary: Adds an audio file's audio stream to the timeline, including the entire duration of the audio.
methods.remarks: Only the audio stream is added to the audio track. Supports all commonly used audio formats (MP3, AAC, WAV, FLAC, Vorbis, Opus, etc.). The audio will be mixed with any other audio on the timeline.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The path to the audio file to add.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position where the audio should be inserted. If null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the audio was successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddAudioFile
methods.summary: Adds an audio file's audio stream to the timeline using advanced source configuration options.
methods.remarks: This overload provides access to advanced features like multi-segment editing and per-clip audio effects through the AudioFileSource object.

parameters.name: source
parameters.summary: An AudioFileSource object containing the audio file path, optional segments, and effects configuration.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position where the audio should be inserted. If null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the audio was successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddAudioFile
methods.summary: Adds a specific segment of an audio file's audio stream to the timeline, from startTime to stopTime.
methods.remarks: This method enables precise trimming of source audio files. Only the portion between startTime and stopTime is added to the timeline and mixed with other audio tracks.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The path to the audio file to add.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: The start time within the source audio from which to begin the clip.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: The end time within the source audio at which to end the clip.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position where the audio segment should be inserted. If null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the audio segment was successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddAudioFromStream
methods.summary: Adds a specific segment of audio data from a seekable stream to the timeline, from startTime to stopTime.
methods.remarks: The stream must support seeking. The audio data is copied to a temporary file for processing. The copy starts at the stream's current position. If the copy fails, OnError is raised and false is returned. This enables precise trimming when loading audio from streams rather than files.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.summary: A seekable stream containing the audio data.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: Optional start time within the source audio. If null, starts from the beginning.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: Optional end time within the source audio. If null, includes until the end.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position where the audio segment should be inserted. If null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the audio segment was successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddAudioFileMain
methods.summary: Internal implementation for adding audio files to the timeline, validating file existence, detecting format properties, and processing either single clips or multi-segment clips based on the source configuration. Handles audio-only timeline editing for music, voiceovers, and sound effects.

parameters.name: source
parameters.summary: The audio file source specification containing filename, optional segments, and per-clip audio effects.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position for clip insertion; if null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if all audio segments were successfully added to the audio track; false if the file doesn't exist or any segment fails to add.

methods.name: Input_AddAudioVideoFile
methods.summary: Adds both audio and video streams from a media file to the timeline.
methods.remarks: This method adds both audio and video tracks from the source file. If the file contains only audio or only video, only the available stream will be added. Supports all commonly used media formats.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The path to the media file to add.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: Optional start time within the source file. If null, starts from the beginning of the file.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: Optional end time within the source file. If null, includes until the end of the file.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position where the media should be inserted. If null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the audio and video streams were successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddAudioVideoFromStream
methods.summary: Adds both audio and video streams from a seekable stream containing media data to the timeline.
methods.remarks: The stream must support seeking. The media data is copied to a temporary file for processing. The copy starts at the stream's current position. If the copy fails, OnError is raised and false is returned. Both audio and video tracks are added if present in the stream.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.summary: A seekable stream containing the media data.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: Optional start time within the source media. If null, starts from the beginning.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: Optional end time within the source media. If null, includes until the end.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position where the media should be inserted. If null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the audio and video streams were successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddAudioVideoFileMain
methods.summary: Internal implementation for adding media files with both audio and video streams to the timeline, validating file existence, detecting format properties, and creating clips that include all available streams.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The media file path to add to the timeline.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: Optional start time within the source media for clip trimming; null uses the beginning of the file.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: Optional end time within the source media for clip trimming; null uses the end of the file.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position for clip insertion; null appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the media file was successfully added with both audio and video streams; false if the file doesn't exist or clip creation fails.

methods.name: CopyStreamToTempFile
methods.summary: Copies a stream input to a temporary file and registers it in _tempFileCache once it is written: a teardown that runs during the copy has no business with the file. Runs CheckPipeline first, so after a stop it waits for the teardown and builds the next pipeline.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.summary: The seekable input stream, copied from its current position.

methods.returns: The temporary file name, or null if the copy failed (reported through OnError) or the instance was disposed during it.

methods.name: CheckOutputAVInfo
methods.summary: Analyzes media file properties to extract and configure output video and audio settings if not already specified. Reads video resolution, frame rate, audio channels, and sample rate from the first video/audio streams, automatically configuring output settings to match the source media for seamless editing without format conversion.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The media file path to analyze for format detection and property extraction.

parameters.name: adoptAudio
parameters.summary: True when this add puts an audio clip on the timeline. A video-only add still carries the file's audio streams, and those must not become the output format.

methods.returns: true if media information was successfully read and settings updated; false if the file cannot be read or media info extraction fails.

methods.name: CheckOutputImageInfo
methods.summary: Analyzes image file dimensions to configure output video settings if not already specified. Reads image width and height, automatically setting output resolution to match, and enables image-to-video conversion in the timeline at 25 fps when no clip has provided a frame rate.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The image file path to analyze for dimension extraction.

methods.returns: true if image properties were successfully read and settings updated; false if the file cannot be decoded or property extraction fails.

methods.name: ClearAdoptedOutputSettings
methods.summary: Drops the output settings an input provided, keeping the ones the caller set. An adopted value describes the job that adopted it: the next job on the instance adopts from its own inputs instead of inheriting a format nobody asked for (#3594).

methods.name: Input_AddVideoLayer
methods.summary: Creates a new video layer in the timeline for advanced multi-layer composition.
methods.remarks: Video layers enable picture-in-picture effects, watermarks, and complex compositions. Each new layer is composited under the layers added before it, and the main layer (index 0) is on top: a picture-in-picture clip goes on the main layer, over a full-frame clip on an added layer. Use the layer ID when adding clips with VideoFileSource or ImageFileSource to specify which layer the clip should be added to.
methods.returns: The zero-based index of the newly created layer.

methods.name: Input_Clear_List
methods.summary: Removes all clips from the main layer of the timeline, clearing its audio and video content.
methods.remarks: This method removes all media clips that have been added to the main layer. The Video_Effects, Audio_Effects, Video_Transitions and Audio_Transitions collections are kept, and the next Start() applies them once, to the clips on the timeline then. After clearing, you can add new clips to build a different timeline composition. When this leaves the timeline without clips, the output size, frame rate, channel count and sample rate an input provided are dropped with them and the timeline renders at the defaults again; a clip on another layer is left alone, and the values set through the Output_* properties keep theirs.

methods.name: HasClips
methods.summary: Whether any layer of the timeline still holds a clip.
methods.returns: true when at least one clip is left on any layer.

methods.name: GetBaseVideoLayer
methods.summary: The layer the global video settings - crop, rotation, Video_Effects, non-fade transitions - act on: the main layer, or, when it holds no video clip, the first added layer that does (#3599). The clips of the other layers are overlays and keep their own look.
methods.returns: The base video layer; the main layer when no layer holds a video clip.

methods.name: TimelineClips
methods.summary: Every clip of the timeline with the layer it sits on, main layer first (#3599).
methods.remarks: Walks a copy of the layer list and skips a null entry: DestroyPipeline, which can run on the bus thread, nulls the entries and then clears the list. That keeps the walk itself from throwing; it does not make a layer being disposed safe to read.
methods.returns: The clips of every layer, in layer order.

methods.name: Input_AddTestClip
methods.summary: Adds a test clip to the timeline for debugging and testing purposes, generating synthetic video content.
methods.remarks: Test clips are useful for debugging pipelines, testing effects, and creating placeholder content. Available patterns include solid colors, SMPTE color bars, snow, and various test patterns.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: The start time in the timeline where the test clip begins.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: The end time in the timeline where the test clip ends.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: The in-point time within the test pattern itself.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The test pattern identifier (e.g., "blue", "smpte", "snow", "black"). Default is "blue".

methods.returns: true if the test clip was successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddImageFile
methods.summary: Adds a static image to the timeline with the specified duration, creating a video clip from the image file.
methods.remarks: Supported image formats include JPEG, PNG, BMP, GIF, and other formats supported by SkiaSharp. The image will be scaled to match the output video resolution while maintaining aspect ratio.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The path to the image file to add.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.summary: The duration for which the image should be displayed in the timeline.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position where the image should be inserted. If null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the image was successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddImageFromStream
methods.summary: Adds a static image to the timeline from a seekable stream with the specified duration.
methods.remarks: The stream must support seeking. The image data is copied to a temporary file for processing. The copy starts at the stream's current position. If the copy fails, OnError is raised and false is returned. Supported formats are the same as TimeSpan}).

parameters.name: stream
parameters.summary: A seekable stream containing the image data.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.summary: The duration for which the image should be displayed in the timeline.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position where the image should be inserted. If null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the image was successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddImageFile
methods.summary: Adds a static image to the timeline using advanced source configuration options.
methods.remarks: This overload allows specifying additional properties through the ImageFileSource object, such as layer assignment and per-clip video effects.

parameters.name: source
parameters.summary: An ImageFileSource object containing the image file path, duration, and optional effects.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position where the image should be inserted. If null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the image was successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddImageFileMain
methods.summary: Internal implementation for adding image files to the timeline as static video clips, validating file existence, detecting image dimensions, and creating a clip with the specified duration. Automatically configures output resolution based on image size if not already set.

parameters.name: source
parameters.summary: The image file source specification containing filename, display duration, layer assignment, and per-clip effects.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position for clip insertion; if null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the image was successfully added as a timeline clip; false if the file doesn't exist or clip creation fails.

methods.name: AddClip
methods.summary: Core internal method for adding any media clip (audio, video, image, or combined) to the timeline with comprehensive configuration including timing, track type selection, layer assignment, and effect attachment. Handles asset loading, clip creation, time range configuration, and effect application in a single unified operation.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The media file URI or path to add as a clip source.

parameters.name: start
parameters.summary: The start time within the source media for clip trimming; null starts from the beginning.

parameters.name: stop
parameters.summary: The end time within the source media for clip trimming; null extends to the end.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: The timeline position where the clip should be inserted; null appends to the timeline end.

parameters.name: trackType
parameters.summary: The track type (audio, video, or both) to include from the source; null includes all available tracks.

parameters.name: layerID
parameters.summary: The zero-based layer index for clip placement, enabling multi-layer composition; must be less than the layer count.

parameters.name: videoEffects
parameters.summary: Optional list of video effects to apply specifically to this clip.

parameters.name: audioEffects
parameters.summary: Optional list of audio effects to apply specifically to this clip.

methods.returns: true if the clip was successfully created, configured, and added to the timeline; false if asset loading fails, time ranges are invalid, or layer ID is out of bounds.

methods.name: DescribeAddClipRefusal
methods.summary: The text reported when the timeline refuses a clip. Names the asset's formats and duration and the track and times that were requested, so a later run can tell those cases apart.

methods.name: Input_AddVideoFile
methods.summary: Adds a video file's video stream to the timeline, including the entire duration of the video.
methods.remarks: Only the video stream is added; audio is not included. Use TimeSpan}) to add both. Supports all commonly used video formats (MP4, AVI, MKV, WebM, MOV, etc.).

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The path to the video file to add.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position where the video should be inserted. If null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the video was successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddVideoFile
methods.summary: Adds a video file's video stream to the timeline using advanced source configuration options.
methods.remarks: This overload provides access to advanced features like multi-segment editing, layer assignment, and per-clip video effects through the VideoFileSource object.

parameters.name: source
parameters.summary: A VideoFileSource object containing the video file path, optional segments, and effects configuration.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position where the video should be inserted. If null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the video was successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddVideoFile
methods.summary: Adds a specific segment of a video file's video stream to the timeline, from startTime to stopTime.
methods.remarks: This method enables precise trimming of source video files. Only the portion between startTime and stopTime is added to the timeline. Only the video stream is included; use TimeSpan}) for both audio and video.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The path to the video file to add.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: The start time within the source video from which to begin the clip.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: The end time within the source video at which to end the clip.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position where the video segment should be inserted. If null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the video segment was successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddVideoFromStream
methods.summary: Adds a specific segment of video data from a seekable stream to the timeline, from startTime to stopTime.
methods.remarks: The stream must support seeking. The video data is copied to a temporary file for processing. The copy starts at the stream's current position. If the copy fails, OnError is raised and false is returned. This enables precise trimming when loading video from streams rather than files.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.summary: A seekable stream containing the video data.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: The start time within the source video from which to begin the clip.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: The end time within the source video at which to end the clip.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position where the video segment should be inserted. If null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if the video segment was successfully added; otherwise, false.

methods.name: Input_AddVideoFileMain
methods.summary: Internal implementation for adding video files to the timeline, validating file existence, detecting format properties, and processing either single clips or multi-segment clips based on the source configuration. Handles segment-based editing for trimming and concatenating portions of video files.

parameters.name: source
parameters.summary: The video file source specification containing filename, optional segments, layer assignment, and per-clip effects.

parameters.name: insertTime
parameters.summary: Optional timeline position for clip insertion; if null, appends to the end of the timeline.

methods.returns: true if all video segments were successfully added to the timeline; false if the file doesn't exist or any segment fails to add.

methods.name: OnPropertyChanged
methods.summary: Raises the PropertyChanged event for the specified property.

parameters.name: propertyName
parameters.summary: The name of the property that changed.

methods.name: RaiseNativeCritical
methods.summary: Raises OnError for a native critical; see Debug_NativeCriticals. Static, so the watcher's subscription list does not keep this engine alive.

methods.name: Video_Transition_Add_FadeIn
methods.summary: Adds a fade-in transition effect to the video timeline, creating a smooth transition from black to full opacity. This is a convenience method that creates a FadeIn VideoTransition and adds it to the Video_Transitions collection.
methods.remarks: The duration of the fade is determined by the difference between stopTime and startTime. Typical fade durations range from 0.5 to 2 seconds for professional video production. The fade acts only between startTime and stopTime: outside them the picture is at full opacity, and fades that overlap multiply.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: The timeline position where the fade-in effect begins.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: The timeline position where the fade-in effect completes, reaching full opacity.

methods.name: Video_Transition_Add_FadeOut
methods.summary: Adds a fade-out transition effect to the video timeline, creating a smooth transition from full opacity to black. This is a convenience method that creates a FadeOut VideoTransition and adds it to the Video_Transitions collection.
methods.remarks: The duration of the fade is determined by the difference between stopTime and startTime. Fade-out transitions are commonly used at the end of videos or scenes for professional finishing. The fade acts only between startTime and stopTime: after stopTime the picture is back at full opacity, so a fade-out followed by a fade-in that starts at its stopTime dips to black between two scenes.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: The timeline position where the fade-out effect begins at full opacity.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: The timeline position where the fade-out effect completes, reaching complete black.

methods.name: Video_Transition_Clear
methods.summary: Removes all video transitions from the timeline.
methods.remarks: Clears the Video_Transitions collection, removing all fade-in, fade-out, and other transition effects. This results in hard cuts between all clips. Call this before reconfiguring transitions to start fresh.

methods.name: Video_Transitions_Names
methods.summary: Gets a list of all available video transition type names that can be used in the timeline.
methods.remarks: This method returns the names from the VideoTransitionType enumeration, excluding the "None" value. Use these names to discover available transition effects. Common transitions include crossfade, wipe variations, clock wipes, and iris effects.
methods.returns: An observable collection of strings containing the names of all supported transition types.

methods.name: AddVideoCrop
methods.summary: Applies the global video crop effect (if configured via Output_VideoCrop) to the video clips of the base video layer (see GetBaseVideoLayer). This internal method creates effect clips that crop all video content uniformly, removing unwanted edges or adjusting aspect ratios across the entire timeline during rendering.
methods.remarks: The crop effect is applied as separate effect clips that match the duration of each video clip, ensuring consistent cropping throughout the timeline. If Output_VideoCrop is null, no action is taken.

methods.name: AddVideoRotateFlip
methods.summary: Applies the global video rotation and flip effect (if configured via Output_VideoRotateFlip) to the video clips of the base video layer (see GetBaseVideoLayer). This internal method creates effect clips that rotate or mirror all video content uniformly, correcting orientation issues or creating mirror effects across the entire timeline during rendering.
methods.remarks: The rotate/flip effect is applied as separate effect clips that match the duration of each video clip, ensuring consistent transformation throughout the timeline. If Output_VideoRotateFlip is null, no action is taken. Common uses include correcting mobile phone video orientation or creating artistic mirror effects.

methods.name: AddVideoEffects
methods.summary: Applies all video effects from the Video_Effects collection to the video clips of the base video layer (see GetBaseVideoLayer). This internal method creates effect clips for each configured effect, respecting their individual start and stop times to apply effects to specific portions of the timeline, enabling frame-accurate effect control and multi-effect stacking.
methods.remarks: Each effect generates one EffectClip per video clip, over the part of the effect's StartTime-StopTime range that clip covers; a clip outside the range gets none. If an effect has zero duration (StartTime equals StopTime), it covers each whole clip; a zero StopTime alone means until the end. Effects are applied in the order they appear in the Video_Effects collection, with later effects processing the output of earlier effects for proper effect chaining. The Video_TextOverlays follow them, each pre-rendered to an image overlay for this Start() only: written into Video_Effects, they were applied once more by every later Start() (#3649).

methods.remarks: Fade-in and fade-out transitions are implemented by a black clip on a layer above every other, whose alpha a GStreamer interpolation control source animates. A fade acts only inside its own interval and overlapping fades multiply. Non-fade transitions use GES TransitionClip.

classes.name: GesAssetLoader
classes.summary: Loads clip assets on a main context of its own, in place of ges_uri_clip_asset_request_sync. That call needs the default main context, which an SDK event handler holds while it runs on the main loop thread: a handler waiting for the thread that is adding a file would hang both (#3781).
classes.remarks: One context for the process, not one per call or per thread: GES caches a discoverer per thread and the discoverer keeps the context it started on, so a later load on another context would wait for one nobody iterates. For the same reason the context is kept on the native GStreamer registry, which outlives a domain reload in the Unity Editor, not only in a static, which does not. Nobody iterates it between loads, so the next load runs what came due. ponytail: a discoverer in READY, with no file open, lives until the next load instead of for 1 s; a thread iterating the context all the time would fix that. One context has one owner, so loads run one at a time, across instances too.

classes.name: VideoDecryptor
classes.summary: Provides cross-platform video decryption functionality using AES-128 encryption in CBC mode. This static class offers both synchronous and asynchronous methods for decrypting video files and streams that were previously encrypted using the corresponding VideoEncryptor class.
classes.remarks: This class implements AES-128 decryption in Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode. The decryption key and initialization vector (IV) are derived from the password and salt using PBKDF2 with 10,000 iterations. For .NET 6.0 and later, PBKDF2 uses SHA-256 as the hash algorithm. For earlier versions, the default hash algorithm of Rfc2898DeriveBytes is used. The password and salt used for decryption must exactly match those used during encryption. If no salt is provided, the same automatic salt generation logic from the password's MD5 hash is used, which must match the encryption process. For stream-based decryption with random access support, consider using the class instead. Data encrypted by the current version records its original length in a 16-byte header, so a partial final block is returned without the zero padding that was added before encryption. Data encrypted by an earlier version has no header and is returned padded to a whole number of AES blocks, as before.

classes.summary: Provides cross-platform video encryption functionality using AES-128 encryption in CBC mode. This static class offers both synchronous and asynchronous methods for encrypting video files and streams using password-based encryption with optional salt values for key derivation.
classes.remarks: This class implements AES-128 encryption in Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode. The output starts with a 16-byte header holding the format signature and the original data length, followed by the ciphertext. A final block shorter than 16 bytes is zero-padded before encryption; the header lets remove that padding and return the exact original length. The encryption key and initialization vector (IV) are derived from the password and salt using PBKDF2 with 10,000 iterations. For .NET 6.0 and later, PBKDF2 uses SHA-256 as the hash algorithm. For earlier versions, the default hash algorithm of Rfc2898DeriveBytes is used. If no salt is provided, a salt is automatically generated from the MD5 hash of the password. For maximum security, it is recommended to provide a unique, randomly generated 16-byte salt for each encryption operation. The encrypted data can be decrypted using the class with the same password and salt values.

methods.name: DrainDisposeAsync
methods.summary: Releases the session when a Dispose landed while this call held the gate.
methods.remarks: A synchronous Dispose that cannot take the gate leaves the teardown to whoever holds it. The in-flight call checks disposedValue at every await, but the last of those checks is not the last instruction it runs: a Dispose landing between that check and the release would otherwise be owned by nobody, and the session would outlive the disposed instance - the very leak the gate exists to close. Whoever releases the gate therefore looks once more, from outside it.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous drain.

methods.name: AbandonPlayAsync
methods.summary: Releases the session this call built after a Dispose landed mid-start. A disposal is not a failure, so it is logged as such and nothing is reported to OnError.

methods.name: StopAsync
methods.summary: Stops the current session and releases its pipeline and blocks.
methods.remarks: Safe to call when nothing is playing - the call is a no-op in that case. The FrameSource can be reused afterwards by calling UniversalSourceSettings) again.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous stop operation.

methods.name: ReleaseSessionAsync
methods.summary: Detaches the current session's event handlers, stops and disposes its pipeline and blocks, and clears the session fields. Safe to call when no session is active.
methods.remarks: Must be called with _sessionLock held: it reads and nulls the session fields around an await, so two unsynchronized callers would both see the same pipeline and dispose it twice.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Performs application-defined tasks associated with freeing, releasing, or resetting unmanaged resources.
methods.remarks: A synchronous Dispose cannot wait for a UniversalSourceSettings) that is already running - waiting on it from a UI or pipeline-callback thread is exactly the deadlock this class must not have. It therefore marks the instance disposed and, when a session transition is in flight, leaves the teardown to that call, so Dispose can return before the session is fully gone. Use DisposeAsync when the caller needs the teardown to have completed on return.

methods.name: DisposeAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously releases the current session and marks the instance disposed.
methods.remarks: The deterministic teardown: it waits for any UniversalSourceSettings) or StopAsync already in flight, so on return nothing of the session is left running. Do not call it - nor UniversalSourceSettings) or StopAsync - and then block on the returned task from an OnError or OnStop handler of the same instance: the session gate is not re-entrant.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous dispose operation.

classes.name: VFPProgressCallback
classes.summary: Represents a callback method that reports progress during video fingerprinting operations.
classes.remarks: This callback is invoked periodically during lengthy fingerprinting operations to provide feedback on the operation's progress. The percent value increases monotonically from 0 (operation started) to 100 (operation complete). Implementations should return quickly to avoid blocking the fingerprinting process.

classes.name: VFPErrorCallback
classes.summary: Represents a callback method that reports errors during video fingerprinting operations.
classes.remarks: This callback is invoked when an error occurs during fingerprinting operations such as file access failures, codec issues, insufficient memory, or invalid parameters. The error message provides details to help diagnose and resolve the issue. After this callback is invoked, the fingerprinting operation typically terminates.

classes.name: VFPComparisonResult
classes.summary: Represents the result of a fingerprint comparison or search operation.
classes.remarks: This class encapsulates all information returned from a fingerprint comparison or search operation, including the similarity score, any detected video transformations, temporal alignment information, and the overall operation status. It is used by both whole-video comparison and fragment search operations.

properties.name: Difference
properties.summary: Gets or sets the difference score indicating how similar the fingerprints are.
properties.value: A non-negative value where 0 indicates identical content, and higher values indicate greater differences. Lower scores represent better matches. Typical matching thresholds are application-specific but usually range from 10-30 for similar content.

properties.name: MirrorMode
properties.summary: Gets or sets the detected mirror mode for the best match.
properties.value: A VFPMirrorMode value indicating any video transformations (flips or rotations) detected between the compared fingerprints. None indicates no transformation was detected.

properties.name: TimeOffset
properties.summary: Gets or sets the time offset in seconds where the best match was found.
properties.value: An integer representing the offset in seconds from the beginning of the larger video where the searched fragment was found. This value is only meaningful for search operations and may be 0 for direct comparisons.

properties.name: Success
properties.summary: Gets or sets whether the comparison operation completed successfully.
properties.value: true if the comparison operation completed without errors; otherwise, false. A failed comparison may occur due to invalid fingerprints, insufficient data, or internal errors.

classes.name: VFPAnalyzer
classes.summary: Provides high-level methods for video fingerprinting analysis, comparison, and search operations.
classes.remarks: The VFPAnalyzer class is the main entry point for video fingerprinting operations. It provides methods to generate fingerprints from video files, compare videos for similarity, and search for video fragments within larger videos. The class handles the complexity of video decoding, frame processing, and fingerprint generation, providing a simple API for common video fingerprinting tasks. All methods are static and support asynchronous operations.
