methods.name: Compare
methods.summary: Compares two video fingerprints and returns a similarity score with automatic mirror detection.
methods.remarks: Enhanced with automatic mirror detection (v15.8.4+):This method now automatically detects and matches videos that have been mirrored or rotated:Horizontal flip (left-right mirror)Vertical flip (top-bottom mirror)180-degree rotation (both horizontal and vertical flip)The method returns the best match across all orientations, ensuring accurate comparison even when videos have been transformed. This enhancement requires no code changes - existing implementations will automatically benefit from improved matching accuracy.Backward compatibility: Existing code continues to work without modification. The performance impact is minimal (up to 4x comparison time in worst case when checking all orientations).Note: If you need to know which specific mirror transformation was detected, use the method instead, which returns both the similarity score and the detected mirror mode.

parameters.name: maxDifference
parameters.summary: Maximum time shift in seconds searched for the best alignment. Despite its name, this is not a difference limit.

methods.returns: The difference score: 0 for identical content, higher values for greater differences (lower means more similar).

methods.name: CompareMirror
methods.summary: Compares two fingerprints with explicit mirror detection information.
methods.remarks: This method provides the same mirror detection capabilities as the standard method, but additionally returns information about which mirror transformation was detected.Use cases:When you need to know if videos are mirrored versions of each otherFor forensic analysis requiring transformation detailsWhen implementing UI that shows how videos matchThe returned includes:Difference: Similarity score (lower is better match)MirrorMode: The specific transformation detected (None, Horizontal, Vertical, or Both)Success: Whether the comparison completed successfullyNote: The standard method uses this functionality internally but only returns the similarity score for backward compatibility.

parameters.name: maxShift
parameters.summary: Maximum time shift allowed in seconds.

methods.returns: Comparison result including similarity score and the specific mirror mode detected.

classes.name: VFPFingerPrint
classes.summary: Represents a video fingerprint containing unique characteristics of video content for identification and comparison. Supports serialization and deserialization of fingerprint data with metadata.

constructors.name: VFPFingerPrint
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VFPFingerPrint class.

properties.name: Data
properties.summary: Gets or sets the binary fingerprint data representing the video content signature.
properties.value: A byte array containing the encoded fingerprint data. This is the core signature used for comparison and search operations. The size varies based on the video duration and fingerprinting parameters.

properties.name: Duration
properties.summary: Gets or sets the duration of the fingerprinted video segment.
properties.value: The length of time covered by this fingerprint. This may be shorter than the original file duration if only a portion of the video was fingerprinted.

properties.name: ID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the unique identifier for this fingerprint.
properties.value: A Guid that uniquely identifies this fingerprint instance. Useful for tracking and managing fingerprints in databases or collections.

properties.name: OriginalFilename
properties.summary: Gets or sets the path to the source file from which this fingerprint was generated.
properties.value: The full path or filename of the original video file. This is stored as metadata to help identify the source of the fingerprint.

properties.name: OriginalDuration
properties.summary: Gets or sets the total duration of the original source file.
properties.value: The complete duration of the source video file. This may differ from Duration if only a portion of the file was fingerprinted (e.g., excluding intros or credits).

properties.name: Tag
properties.summary: Gets or sets an optional user-defined tag for categorizing or identifying this fingerprint.
properties.value: A custom string that can be used to store additional metadata such as content type, category, or any other application-specific identifier.

properties.name: Width
properties.summary: Gets or sets the width of the source video frames used for fingerprinting.
properties.value: The width in pixels of the video frames that were analyzed to generate this fingerprint. This reflects the frame dimensions after any cropping or resizing operations.

properties.name: Height
properties.summary: Gets or sets the height of the source video frames used for fingerprinting.
properties.value: The height in pixels of the video frames that were analyzed to generate this fingerprint. This reflects the frame dimensions after any cropping or resizing operations.

properties.name: FrameRate
properties.summary: Gets or sets the frame rate of the source video.
properties.value: The frame rate in frames per second (fps) of the source video. Common values include 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 50, and 60 fps.

properties.name: IgnoredAreas
properties.summary: Gets the collection of rectangular regions that were ignored during fingerprint generation.
properties.value: A list of Rect objects defining areas excluded from analysis. These typically represent logos, timestamps, or other overlays that should not affect content matching.

properties.name: SupportsMirrorDetection
properties.summary: Gets or sets whether this fingerprint supports mirror-aware comparison.
properties.value: true if the fingerprint can detect mirrored or flipped video content; false if only exact orientation matching is supported. Default is true.

properties.name: Version
properties.summary: Gets or sets the fingerprint format version.
properties.value: An integer indicating the fingerprint algorithm version: Version 1 - Original implementation without mirror detection support. Version 2 - Enhanced implementation with mirror-aware comparison capabilities (default).

methods.name: Finalize
methods.summary: Finalizes an instance of the VFPFingerPrint class.

methods.name: GetSerializerOptions
methods.summary: Gets the JSON serializer options configured for handling binary data and fingerprint serialization.
methods.returns: JsonSerializerOptions configured with ByteArrayConverter for binary data handling.

methods.name: Load
methods.summary: Loads a video fingerprint from a file on disk.
methods.remarks: This method deserializes fingerprint data saved in JSON format with custom binary encoding for the fingerprint data array. The file format supports both current and legacy versions.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The path to the fingerprint file to load. Recommended extension is .vsigx.

methods.returns: A deserialized VFPFingerPrint object containing the fingerprint data and metadata.

methods.name: Load
methods.summary: Loads a video fingerprint from a byte array in memory.
methods.remarks: This method is useful for loading fingerprints that have been transmitted over a network, retrieved from a database, or stored in memory. The data must be in the same JSON format used by the Save method.

parameters.name: data
parameters.summary: A byte array containing the serialized fingerprint data.

methods.returns: A deserialized VFPFingerPrint object containing the fingerprint data and metadata.

methods.name: Save
methods.summary: Saves the fingerprint to a file on disk.
methods.remarks: If the file already exists, it will be deleted before writing the new fingerprint data. The fingerprint is serialized to JSON format with custom binary encoding for efficient storage. Legacy extension .sig is supported for backward compatibility, but .vsigx is recommended.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The destination file path. Recommended extension is .vsigx (.sig for legacy compatibility).

methods.name: Save
methods.summary: Serializes the fingerprint to a byte array for in-memory storage or transmission.
methods.remarks: The returned byte array can be stored in a database, transmitted over a network, or kept in memory. It can later be deserialized using the Byte[]) method. The data is compact and includes all fingerprint metadata and settings.
methods.returns: A byte array containing the serialized fingerprint data in JSON format with binary encoding.

methods.name: SaveBSON
methods.summary: Saves binary data to file.

methods.name: SaveBSON
methods.summary: Saves binary data to memory.
methods.returns: A byte array.

classes.name: VFPFingerPrintDB
classes.summary: Represents a database of video fingerprints for managing and searching video content signatures.
classes.remarks: The VFPFingerPrintDB class provides functionality to store, retrieve, and manage video fingerprints. It supports serialization to persist fingerprint databases to disk and provides methods to check for duplicate content based on fingerprint signatures.

constructors.name: VFPFingerPrintDB
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VFPFingerPrintDB class.

properties.name: Items
properties.summary: Gets or sets the collection of video fingerprints stored in the database.
properties.value: A list of VFPFingerPrint objects representing individual video fingerprints.

methods.name: GetSerializerOptions
methods.summary: Get serializer options with binary data handling
methods.returns: JsonSerializerOptions configured for binary data

methods.name: Save
methods.summary: Saves the fingerprint database to a file on disk.
methods.remarks: The entire database, including all fingerprints and their metadata, is serialized to JSON format with custom binary encoding. This allows efficient storage and retrieval of large fingerprint collections.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The destination file path for the database. Recommended extension is .vsigx.

methods.name: Load
methods.summary: Loads a fingerprint database from a file on disk.
methods.remarks: This method gracefully handles errors by returning an empty database if the file is corrupted, inaccessible, or contains invalid data. Error details are logged to the console and debug output. This ensures the application can continue running even if the database file is damaged.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The path to the database file to load. Recommended extension is .vsigx.

methods.returns: A deserialized VFPFingerPrintDB object containing all stored fingerprints. If the file cannot be loaded or contains invalid data, returns an empty database instance.

methods.name: ContainsFile
methods.summary: Checks whether the database contains a fingerprint matching the specified source configuration.
methods.remarks: This method performs an exact match on both the filename and the ignored areas configuration. Two sources are considered matching only if they have the same filename and identical ignored area rectangles (order-independent). This helps avoid duplicate fingerprints and enables fingerprint caching to skip re-processing of previously analyzed videos.

parameters.name: source
parameters.summary: A VFPFingerprintSource specifying the filename and ignored areas to search for.

methods.returns: true if the database contains a fingerprint with matching filename and ignored areas; otherwise, false.

methods.name: GetFingerprint
methods.summary: Retrieves a fingerprint from the database that matches the specified source.
methods.remarks: This method searches for an exact match based on both the filename and the ignored areas configuration. If multiple fingerprints exist for the same file with different ignored areas, only the one with matching ignored areas will be returned.

parameters.name: source
parameters.summary: The fingerprint source containing the filename and ignored areas to match against.

methods.returns: The matching VFPFingerPrint if found; otherwise, null.

methods.name: CompareIgnoreAreas
methods.summary: Compares two lists of ignored areas for equality.
methods.remarks: This method performs a content-based comparison of the two lists. Empty lists are considered equal. The comparison checks if all rectangles in the first list exist in the second list, regardless of order.

parameters.name: areas1
parameters.summary: The first list of rectangles representing ignored areas.

parameters.name: areas2
parameters.summary: The second list of rectangles representing ignored areas.

methods.returns: true if both lists contain the same rectangles (order-independent); otherwise, false.

classes.name: VFPFingerprintFromFrames
classes.summary: Creates video fingerprints from individual image frames.
classes.remarks: The VFPFingerprintFromFrames class allows creation of video fingerprints from a sequence of image frames rather than from a video file. This is useful when processing video streams, generated content, or when frames are already available in memory. The class accepts frames in RGB24 format, SKBitmap objects (cross-platform), or Bitmap objects (Windows only) and builds a fingerprint that can be used for content matching.

constructors.name: VFPFingerprintFromFrames
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VFPFingerprintFromFrames class.
constructors.remarks: All frames pushed to this instance must match the specified width and height. The frame rate is used to calculate proper timestamps for each frame. The total duration should be an estimate of the complete video length to properly initialize the fingerprinting algorithm.

parameters.name: frameRate
parameters.summary: The frame rate of the video in frames per second.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: The width of the video frames in pixels.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: The height of the video frames in pixels.

parameters.name: totalDuration
parameters.summary: The total expected duration of the video content.

methods.name: Push
methods.summary: Adds an RGB24 frame to the fingerprint generation process.
methods.remarks: The frame data must be in RGB24 format with pixels stored in row-major order. Each pixel consists of 3 bytes representing red, green, and blue channels. Frames should be pushed in chronological order for accurate fingerprint generation.

parameters.name: rgb24frame
parameters.summary: A byte array containing the frame data in RGB24 format (3 bytes per pixel).

methods.name: Push
methods.summary: Adds a bitmap frame to the fingerprint generation process.
methods.remarks: The method accepts bitmaps in any pixel format and automatically converts them to RGB24 format if necessary. For best performance, provide frames already in 24bppRgb format. The bitmap is not modified and can be reused after this call. Frames should be pushed in chronological order. This method is only available on Windows platforms.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: A Bitmap containing the video frame.

methods.name: Push
methods.summary: Adds a SkiaSharp bitmap frame to the fingerprint generation process.
methods.remarks: The method accepts SKBitmap in any pixel format and automatically converts it to RGB24 format. The bitmap is not modified and can be reused after this call. Frames should be pushed in chronological order. This method is available on all platforms.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: A SKBitmap containing the video frame.

methods.name: Push
methods.summary: Adds an RGB24 frame from unmanaged memory to the fingerprint generation process.
methods.remarks: This method is useful when working with frames from native libraries or when frames are already available in unmanaged memory. The timestamp for each frame is automatically calculated based on the frame rate and the order in which frames are pushed.

parameters.name: rgb24frame
parameters.summary: Pointer to the frame data in RGB24 format in unmanaged memory.

parameters.name: rgb24frameSize
parameters.summary: Size of the frame data in bytes. Must equal width * height * 3.

methods.name: Build
methods.summary: Builds the final video fingerprint from all processed frames.
methods.remarks: This method should be called after all frames have been pushed using the Push methods. It finalizes the fingerprint generation process and returns a fingerprint object that can be saved to disk or used for comparison operations. After calling Build, the internal resources are freed and this instance should not be used further.
methods.returns: A VFPFingerPrint object containing the generated fingerprint data and metadata about the video.

methods.name: Finalize
methods.summary: Finalizes an instance of the VFPFingerprintFromFrames class.
methods.remarks: The finalizer ensures that any unmanaged memory allocated for temporary frame buffers is properly released even if Dispose is not called explicitly.

classes.name: VFPFingerprintSource
classes.summary: Represents a source file configuration for video fingerprinting operations.
classes.remarks: The VFPFingerprintSource class encapsulates all the settings and parameters needed to generate a video fingerprint from a media file. It supports temporal trimming, spatial cropping, resolution adjustment, and the ability to ignore specific regions of the video frame during fingerprint generation.

constructors.name: VFPFingerprintSource
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VFPFingerprintSource class.
constructors.remarks: The constructor automatically reads the video duration from the file metadata and initializes the StopTime to match the full duration. The CustomResolution is set to Empty and CustomCropSize is initialized to an empty rectangle.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The path to the video file to be used as a fingerprint source.

properties.name: Filename
properties.summary: Gets or sets the path to the source media file for fingerprinting.
properties.value: The full path to the video file that will be analyzed.

properties.name: StartTime
properties.summary: Gets or sets the start time for fingerprint generation within the video.
properties.value: The time offset from the beginning of the video where fingerprinting should start. Default is Zero.

properties.name: StopTime
properties.summary: Gets or sets the stop time for fingerprint generation within the video.
properties.value: The time offset from the beginning of the video where fingerprinting should stop. Default is the video's total duration.

properties.name: CustomCropSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the custom crop rectangle to apply to video frames before fingerprinting.
properties.value: A Rect specifying the distances from each edge to crop. Left, Top, Right, and Bottom values represent the distance from each respective edge.

properties.name: CustomResolution
properties.summary: Gets or sets the custom resolution to which video frames should be resized before fingerprinting.
properties.value: A Size specifying the target width and height. Empty indicates that no resizing should be performed.

properties.name: IgnoredAreas
properties.summary: Gets the collection of rectangular areas to be ignored during fingerprint generation.
properties.value: A list of Rect objects defining regions to exclude from fingerprinting.

properties.name: OriginalDuration
properties.summary: Gets or sets the original duration of the source media file.
properties.value: The total duration of the video file as read from its metadata.

methods.name: ReadDuration
methods.summary: Reads the duration and other metadata from the source video file.
methods.remarks: This method uses MediaInfoReaderX to extract video metadata. If the file cannot be opened or contains no video streams, the method returns without setting the duration properties. When successful, both StopTime and OriginalDuration are set to the container's total duration.

classes.name: VFPSearchData
classes.summary: Manages native memory allocation for video fingerprint search operations.
classes.remarks: The VFPSearchData class encapsulates unmanaged memory used by the native video fingerprinting library during search operations. It implements IDisposable to ensure proper cleanup of native resources. The memory allocation size varies between x86 (48 bytes) and x64 (80 bytes) platforms.

constructors.name: VFPSearchData
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VFPSearchData class.
constructors.remarks: The constructor allocates platform-specific amounts of unmanaged memory (48 bytes for x86, 80 bytes for x64) and initializes the native search structure with the specified duration.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.summary: The expected duration of the video content to be processed.

properties.name: Data
properties.summary: Gets or sets the pointer to the native search data structure.
properties.value: An IntPtr pointing to the unmanaged memory containing search data.

properties.name: Context
properties.summary: Gets or sets the optional logging context. When set, diagnostic messages from VFPSearch operations involving this instance are routed through the SDK's centralized Serilog-backed logger. When null, the logger falls back to Context (if set) and finally to Trace.

methods.name: Free
methods.summary: Releases the unmanaged memory allocated for search data.
methods.remarks: This method clears the native search structure and sets the data pointer to Zero. It is automatically called during disposal but can be called manually if immediate cleanup is required.

methods.name: Finalize
methods.summary: Finalizes an instance of the VFPSearchData class.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases all resources used by the VFPSearchData instance.
methods.remarks: This method implements the IDisposable pattern and ensures that unmanaged memory is properly freed. It also suppresses finalization to improve performance.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases the unmanaged resources and optionally releases the managed resources.
methods.remarks: This method follows the standard dispose pattern. When called from the finalizer (disposing = false), only unmanaged resources are freed. When called from Dispose() (disposing = true), both managed and unmanaged resources are freed.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources.

methods.summary: Determines whether the current process is running as a 32-bit (x86) application.
methods.remarks: This method is used internally to determine the correct memory allocation size for platform-specific structures.
methods.returns: true if the process is 32-bit; false if it is 64-bit.

classes.name: VFPSearch
classes.summary: Provides static methods for building and analyzing video fingerprints for content matching.
classes.remarks: The VFPSearch class is the main entry point for video fingerprint search operations. It provides methods to process video frames, build fingerprints from the processed data, and search for matching content between different fingerprints. All methods are static and interact with the native video fingerprinting library through P/Invoke calls.

properties.name: Context
properties.summary: Gets or sets the optional SDK logging context shared by all VFPSearch operations. When set, diagnostic messages are routed through the SDK's centralized logger. When null, falls back to Trace.

methods.remarks: A valid license key is required to use the video fingerprinting functionality without limitations. Call this method once during application initialization before using any other fingerprinting features.

methods.name: Process
methods.summary: Processes a single video frame for fingerprint generation.
methods.remarks: This method should be called for each frame of the video in chronological order. The frame data must be in RGB24 format. Invalid dimensions or stride values will result in the method returning 0 without processing the frame.

parameters.name: video

methods.returns: Returns 1 if processing was successful, 0 if invalid parameters were provided.

methods.name: Build
methods.summary: Builds a fingerprint from the accumulated frame data.
methods.remarks: This method should be called after all frames have been processed using the VFPSearchData@) method. The returned fingerprint can be saved to disk or used for searching operations. The method allocates new memory for the fingerprint data which must be freed by the caller.

parameters.name: length
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains the length of the fingerprint data in bytes.

parameters.name: video
parameters.summary: The VFPSearchData instance containing the processed frame data.

methods.returns: A pointer to the newly allocated memory containing the fingerprint data. The caller is responsible for freeing this memory using IntPtr).

methods.name: Search
methods.summary: Searches for a video fragment within another video using fingerprint matching with automatic mirror detection.
methods.remarks: This method performs a sliding window search to find the best match location. The search is optimized for finding video fragments that may have undergone slight modifications such as compression, scaling, or minor edits.Enhanced with automatic mirror detection (v15.8.4+):The search now automatically detects and matches video fragments that have been transformed:Horizontally flipped (mirrored left-right)Vertically flipped (mirrored top-bottom)Rotated 180 degrees (both flips combined)This enhancement dramatically improves the ability to find matching content in videos that have been intentionally modified to avoid detection, such as:Copyright infringement attempts using mirrored uploadsSocial media videos flipped to bypass content matchingSurveillance footage from different camera orientationsBackward compatibility: Existing code works without modification. The method automatically checks all orientations and returns the best match. Performance impact is proportional to the search space but optimized to minimize overhead.Note: If you need to know which specific mirror transformation was detected, use the method instead.

parameters.name: fp1
parameters.summary: The fingerprint of the video fragment to search for (needle).

parameters.name: skip1
parameters.summary: Number of seconds to skip from the beginning of the first fingerprint.

parameters.name: fp2
parameters.summary: The fingerprint of the video to search within (haystack).

parameters.name: skip2
parameters.summary: Number of seconds to skip from the beginning of the second fingerprint.

parameters.name: difference
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains the calculated difference score between the best match found. Lower values indicate better matches.

parameters.name: maxDiff
parameters.summary: The maximum allowed difference threshold. Matches with differences exceeding this value will not be considered valid.

methods.returns: The position (in seconds) within fp2 where fp1 was found, or MaxValue if no match was found within the difference threshold.

methods.name: SearchMirror
methods.summary: Searches for a video fragment within another video with explicit mirror detection information.
methods.remarks: This method provides the same mirror detection capabilities as the standard method, but additionally returns detailed information about which mirror transformation was detected.Use cases:Content moderation systems that need to log how videos were modifiedForensic analysis requiring transformation documentationAnalytics dashboards showing common transformation patternsAutomated correction systems that can un-mirror detected contentThe returned includes:TimeOffset: Position in seconds where the match was foundDifference: Match quality score (lower is better)MirrorMode: The specific transformation (None, Horizontal, Vertical, or Both)Success: Whether the search completed successfullyNote: The standard method uses this functionality internally for mirror detection but only returns the position and difference for backward compatibility.

parameters.name: fp1
parameters.summary: The fingerprint of the video fragment to search for (needle).

parameters.name: fp2
parameters.summary: The fingerprint of the video to search within (haystack).

methods.returns: Search result including position, difference score, and the specific mirror mode detected.

methods.name: SearchMirror
methods.summary: Searches for a video fragment within another video with explicit mirror detection and duration hints.
methods.remarks: Mirror detection modes returned:None: Videos match in original orientationHorizontal: Match found with horizontal flipVertical: Match found with vertical flipBoth: Match found with 180-degree rotation

parameters.name: fp1
parameters.summary: The fingerprint of the video fragment to search for (needle).

parameters.name: fp2
parameters.summary: The fingerprint of the video to search within (haystack).

parameters.name: duration1
parameters.summary: Duration of the first video in seconds. Reserved search hint, currently not used.

parameters.name: duration2
parameters.summary: Duration of the second video in seconds. Reserved search hint, currently not used.

methods.returns: Search result including position, difference score, and the specific mirror mode detected. The search result is identical to the two-argument VFPFingerPrint) overload.

classes.name: VisioForgeX
classes.summary: Provides static methods for initializing, managing, and destroying the VisioForge SDK. This class serves as the main entry point for setting up the SDK environment and controlling its lifecycle.
classes.remarks: Proper initialization and destruction of the SDK are crucial for resource management and application stability. The SDK relies on GStreamer, and this class handles the underlying GStreamer initialization and cleanup. Use Boolean) to avoid blocking the calling thread; it offloads Boolean) to the thread pool, so if initialization must run on a specific thread call Boolean) directly. Only the cross-platform X-engines (VideoCaptureCoreX, VideoEditCoreX, MediaPlayerCoreX, MediaBlocksPipeline) require this initialization; the Windows-only DirectShow cores (VideoCaptureCore, VideoEditCore, MediaPlayerCore) do not.

properties.name: DebugLevel
properties.summary: Gets or sets the debug level for GStreamer messages. This controls the verbosity of logging from the underlying GStreamer framework.

properties.name: Debug_Telemetry
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the SDK sends any telemetry to VisioForge while a debugger is attached to the process.
properties.value: true (the default) to allow it; false to send nothing at all, from any engine.

properties.summary: Gets or sets the folder the SDK loads its GStreamer natives from on Windows.

properties.value: true if the SDK is initialized; otherwise, false.

methods.name: #cctor
methods.summary: Initializes static members of the VisioForgeX class. This static constructor is responsible for setting up the default cache folder on Windows platforms.

methods.name: NativeSetStamp
methods.summary: A short stamp identifying the native set the application deployed, appended to the SDK version in the cache path.
methods.remarks: The managed SDK version on its own is only a proxy for which natives are present: the VisioForge.CrossPlatform.* packages version independently of it, so two applications on the same managed version can deploy different redistributables. Sharing one cache folder between them would make each start overwrite the other's files and invalidate the registry both of them rely on - the exact churn the shared cache exists to prevent, and a cache that cannot be written would serve one application the other's plugins. The stamp is therefore taken over the name, size and timestamp of every library and data file the mirror copies (), so one cache folder holds exactly one set of them (#3376). The price is that applications deploying different packages - or a DLL a customer copied next to the natives - get folders of their own, each with its own registry. Returns an empty string when the folder holds no such file, leaving the plain version as the key.

methods.name: NativeSetStampOf
methods.summary: String) of a native folder.

methods.name: InitSDKAsync
methods.summary: Initializes the VisioForge SDK asynchronously. This method performs the necessary setup for the SDK, including GStreamer initialization.
methods.remarks: Threading semantics: This method offloads Boolean) to the thread pool via Task.Run. InitSDK performs synchronous, potentially blocking work (GStreamer registry scan, plugin loading, native dependency resolution, optional SSL setup on macOS) that can take hundreds of milliseconds on cold starts, so running it on the calling thread would freeze UIs. Side-effect to be aware of: GStreamer / GLib unhandled-exception handlers registered during InitSDK are bound to whichever thread first triggered initialization. Because that thread is now a thread-pool worker rather than the caller's thread, application code that relies on init being run on a specific thread (e.g., for thread-static GLib state) should call directly on that thread instead of using .

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: Optional. The ContextX to use for initialization. If null, a default context is created.

parameters.name: editing
parameters.summary: Optional. A boolean value indicating whether the SDK is initialized for editing purposes. Defaults to false.

methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous initialization operation.

methods.name: InitSDK
methods.summary: Initializes the VisioForge SDK synchronously. This method performs the necessary setup for the SDK, including GStreamer initialization.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: Optional. The ContextX to use for initialization. If null, a default context is created.

parameters.name: editing
parameters.summary: Optional. A boolean value indicating whether the SDK is initialized for editing purposes. Defaults to false.

methods.name: DestroySDK
methods.summary: Destroys the VisioForge SDK, releasing all allocated resources. This method should be called when the application no longer needs the SDK to prevent resource leaks. It waits for a clip that another thread is loading through VideoEditCoreX, without a time limit of its own, so stop adding inputs on other threads first.
methods.returns: true if the SDK was successfully destroyed; otherwise, false.

methods.name: StopMainLoop
methods.summary: Stops the GStreamer GLib main-loop background thread WITHOUT deinitializing GStreamer. Intended for hosts that reload the managed AppDomain in-process — most notably the Unity Editor on script recompile / assembly reload or on entering/leaving Play mode with Domain Reload enabled — where the un-abortable native main-loop thread would otherwise hang the reload. Unlike DestroySDK this does NOT call gst_deinit or reset the init state. Because the init state is left untouched, the main loop is recreated only after the initialization bookkeeping is reset from clean statics — i.e. when the AppDomain is reloaded in-process (the Unity Editor reload guard's intended use), so the next runs a full init and rebuilds the loop. A plain in-domain call after this method returns via its fast path (_initState stays initialized and GstInitializer.IsInitialized stays true) and will NOT recreate the loop. To tear down and rebuild GStreamer without a domain reload, call instead. Waits for a clip that another thread is loading through VideoEditCoreX, without a time limit of its own. Stop adding inputs on other threads before calling this method.

methods.summary: Loads the VC++ runtime Redist.Shared deploys to <app>\<arch> (#3337) by full path, once per process. System32 comes before PATH in the DLL search order; once a module is loaded, every later import of its name resolves to it, so the shipped copy wins as it did from the executable's folder. The rest of the set binds to whichever vcruntime140 is loaded, so it is loaded only on top of the folder's own vcruntime140: when another one is already in the process, or this one fails to load, the set is left to the DLL search order. The folder is <app>\<arch>, else one of GetPaths or its <arch> subfolder; while none of them holds the runtime, or a failure had no context to report it, a later call looks again. Never throws.

parameters.name: context

classes.name: D3D11ComposablePanel
classes.summary: Direct3D 11 composable WPF video panel. Acts as both the visible WPF control and the IVideoSurfaceProvider hook for consumer custom shaders / overlays. Frame pushes are thread-safe; the upload happens on the caller's thread, the WPF invalidation is dispatched.

constructors.name: D3D11ComposablePanel
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the D3D11ComposablePanel class with a black background. The panel is ready to receive frames via VideoFrameX) immediately after construction; no separate init call is required.

methods.name: PushFrame
methods.summary: Pushes a single video frame into the GPU shared texture and schedules a WPF compose-tick invalidation. Safe to call from any thread.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases the D3D11 shared texture, D3DImage bridge, and all associated GPU resources. Safe to call from any thread. Idempotent — subsequent calls are no-ops.

events.name: RenderError
events.summary: Raised when an internal frame-upload, texture-allocation, or dispatcher-marshalling step fails. Subscribers receive the underlying exception so integrators can log or surface the failure without attaching a debugger (the panel also writes the message via String), which is invisible in release builds without a debugger). The panel itself continues to retry on the next frame — this event is purely diagnostic. Handler exceptions are swallowed so a misbehaving consumer cannot break the pipeline.

events.name: RendererUnavailable
events.summary: Raised when the composable path cannot be established on this machine at all — the D3D9Ex bridge onto the shared D3D11 texture could not be created, so nothing this panel draws will ever reach the screen. The usual cause is a session whose D3D9Ex device lives on a different adapter than the D3D11 device that owns the texture — a remote-desktop session is the common case: IDirect3DDevice9Ex::CreateTexture rejects the cross-adapter shared handle with E_INVALIDARG and WPF reports render tier 0. Retrying frame after frame cannot fix that, so the owner (VideoView) uses this to fall back to its software path instead of showing a black rectangle. Handler exceptions are swallowed, as with RenderError. Raised at most once per panel, and the panel stops presenting for good afterwards — every later returns immediately instead of rebuilding a device that cannot present. A consumer using this panel directly (rather than through VideoView, which swaps in its software path) should react by replacing the panel, not by waiting for it to recover: build a new if the desktop's capabilities change later.

classes.name: D3D11SharedTexture
classes.summary: Owns a single BGRA-typed shared D3D11 texture together with its creator device/context. Thread-safe for concurrent Int32) calls from a streaming thread vs. SharedHandle reads from the UI thread: the handle is computed once at construction and remains stable for the texture's lifetime; Dispose zeroes it (under _lock) for diagnostic clarity, and post-Dispose reads return Zero by contract — see the SharedHandle property remarks.

constructors.name: D3D11SharedTexture
constructors.summary: Creates an 8-bit BGRA shared texture sized to width by height.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: Texture width in pixels. Must be strictly positive.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: Texture height in pixels. Must be strictly positive.

properties.name: IsDeviceRemoved
properties.summary: Set to true when an upload observed ID3D11Device::GetDeviceRemovedReason returning a failure HRESULT (TDR, driver crash, RDP transition, hybrid-GPU hot-switch). Consumers should tear down the pipeline and rebuild from scratch.

properties.name: Width
properties.summary: Width in pixels.

properties.name: Height
properties.summary: Height in pixels.

properties.name: RowBytes
properties.summary: BGRA row stride in bytes.

properties.name: SharedHandle
properties.summary: DXGI shared handle (HANDLE) safe to pass to D3D9Ex's CreateTexture as the pSharedHandle argument. Valid until Dispose; reads after Dispose are intentionally non-throwing and return Zero (the Dispose path zeroes _sharedHandle under _lock; this getter reads the field directly without re-acquiring it because the post-Dispose contract is "return Zero", not "throw ObjectDisposedException" — the latter would force every consumer of IVideoSurfaceProvider to wrap reads in a try/catch).

methods.name: UploadBgra
methods.summary: Uploads a tightly-packed BGRA8 frame into the shared texture. Safe to call from any thread; serialised internally. The caller's source pixels must remain valid for the duration of the call but not after.

methods.name: UploadBgrOrRgb
methods.summary: Uploads a BGR24 / RGB24 frame, expanding to BGRA8 on the fly into a temporary buffer. Used by callers that receive 24-bit DirectShow frames; for high frame rates prefer to negotiate BGRA upstream.

methods.name: Finalize
methods.summary: Backstop finalizer for instances that were abandoned without an explicit Dispose — e.g. a constructor that threw downstream of IntPtr@) succeeding but before the caller obtained the reference, or a consumer that drops the object on an exception path. Releases only the native resources this class owns directly (the raw texture IntPtr and the BGR/RGB conversion buffer). The ComObject wrappers for _device and _context have their own finalizers and will release themselves; we do not touch them here because reaching into them on the finalizer thread risks ordering issues. Dispose calls Object), so on the normal path this finalizer never runs and the GC pressure is zero.

classes.name: D3DImageBridge
classes.summary: Owns a headless IDirect3DDevice9Ex plus a single D3D9 texture opened from a DXGI shared handle. The texture's level-0 surface is fed to IntPtr) once; subsequent frames just call Invalidate which issues Lock / AddDirtyRect / Unlock on the UI thread.

constructors.name: D3DImageBridge
constructors.summary: Creates the bridge for a texture of the given dimensions, opening it from the D3D11 shared handle. focusHwnd may be any valid window handle (typically GetDesktopWindow()); the D3D9Ex device only uses it for cooperative-level bookkeeping.

properties.name: D3DImage
properties.summary: The WPF image source clients should bind to.

methods.name: Invalidate
methods.summary: Marks the whole image dirty so WPF re-reads the back buffer this compose cycle. Must be called on the UI thread (the dispatcher that owns D3DImage). Callers from a producer/streaming thread must marshal via Dispatcher.BeginInvoke first — VideoFrameX) already does this.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Disposes the bridge. Splits cleanup into two phases: (1) UI-thread phase (best-effort): unhook the D3DImage event and clear its back-buffer pointer. The D3DImage is a DispatcherObject and Lock / IntPtr) throw InvalidOperationException off its owning dispatcher. If this Dispose is called from a non-UI thread the phase is marshalled synchronously via Dispatcher.Invoke. The marshal is best-effort: if the dispatcher has already shut down (process exit, window already closed), the failure is caught and logged but Phase 2 still runs — otherwise the D3D9Ex surface / texture / device / factory would leak for the remainder of the process lifetime. Leaving the D3DImage's back-buffer pointing at the released surface is harmless in that case because the dispatcher is already gone and WPF will not compose against it again. (2) Native phase (always runs): release the COM surface pointer and dispose the D3D9Ex device / texture / factory. These are not dispatcher-affine and can run on any thread. When Phase 1 succeeds, the surface IUnknown is released only after the D3DImage back-buffer has been pointed away from it, so the D3DImage never holds a freed pointer it can actually access.

methods.name: Finalize
methods.summary: Backstop finalizer for instances that were abandoned without an explicit Dispose — e.g. a ctor that threw between acquiring _surface and the caller obtaining the reference. Releases only the raw _surface COM pointer that this class owns directly. The _device / _texture / _factory ComObject wrappers have their own finalizers. The D3DImage has UI- thread affinity; from the finalizer thread we cannot reach the dispatcher, so we deliberately do not touch it — WPF will treat the stale back-buffer pointer as detached once the dispatcher is gone. Dispose calls Object), so on the normal path this finalizer never runs.

events.name: FrontBufferLost
events.summary: Raised on the UI thread when the D3DImage front buffer becomes unavailable (driver TDR, RDP session change, hybrid-GPU hot-switch). Consumers should dispose this bridge and rebuild from scratch.

methods.name: RemoveAndRelease
methods.summary: Takes filter out of the graph, disconnecting its pins, and releases it now, on this thread, rather than leaving it to the GC's finalizer after the graph is gone (#3446). Only for a filter nobody else holds: an OnFilterAdded subscriber may share its RCW.

methods.name: ConnectRGBInput
methods.summary: Connects rgbOnly to pin, through VisioForge Video Converter when the pin is a YUV format the graph builder cannot convert. The resizer takes RGB only, and the graph builder never inserts the converter: its merit is MERIT_DO_NOT_USE (#2015, #3433, #3445). The connects are quiet, so a source the graph builder can convert keeps its chain and the caller reports a failure once. The converter is connected directly, so nothing else lands on the source pin, and removed again when rgbOnly still does not connect. On failure the hr returned is that of the last connect of rgbOnly.

parameters.name: rgbOnly
parameters.summary: The filter that takes RGB only.

parameters.name: pin
parameters.summary: The output pin to connect from.

parameters.name: converter
parameters.summary: The converter left in the graph, for the caller to dispose; null when none was needed.

methods.returns: Returns 0 or a positive value if the operation was successful.

methods.name: ConnectThroughVideoConverter
methods.summary: Puts VisioForge Video Converter behind pin, for a pin the graph builder cannot convert: it never inserts the converter, whose merit is MERIT_DO_NOT_USE (#3751, #3805). The converter is connected directly, so nothing else lands on pin, and removed again when connectOut fails.

parameters.name: name

parameters.summary: Connects the converter's output pin onwards and returns the hr.

parameters.summary: The converter left in the graph, for the caller to dispose; null on failure.

properties.name: RtspTimeout
properties.summary: Gets or sets the RTSP socket read timeout in microseconds for an rtsp:// or rtsps:// URL, passed as -timeout, or -stimeout to a build before FFmpeg 5, and not at all to a binary whose help lists neither. Without it a camera that goes silent with its session open is waited for forever. Empty passes nothing; "0" waits forever. Read by TryParseMicroseconds: decimals, exponents and the k/K, M, G, T, P, E suffixes are taken; anything else, and a value other than 0 that rounds to 0, is dropped with a warning.

methods.name: Restart

methods.remarks: The whole stop-rebuild-start sequence runs under one lock. Doing it step by step from the caller was not enough: separate capture reaches it from two thread-pool paths at once - SeparateCapture_StartAsync and the split's SeparateCaptureDelegateMethod - and their steps could interleave so that one thread started the task the other had just built, leaving the first FFmpeg unreferenced and still writing its file.

methods.name: ResolveRtspTransport
methods.summary: Resolves rtspTransportArgs. The value is the caller's own, but it lands in a command line: only names in FFmpeg's flags syntax ("tcp", "+tcp", "udp+tcp", "-udp") or one short number are taken, so it cannot close the quotes around it. Whether a name is one FFmpeg knows is left to FFmpeg.

methods.name: TryParseMicroseconds
methods.summary: Parses a timeout in the forms of FFmpeg's option parser that make sense for it: a non-negative number of microseconds, decimal or with an exponent ("1e7"), optionally with one of the multipliers k/K, M, G, T, P, E ("5M" = 5000000), rounded to a whole number. Lower-case m and the other prefixes FFmpeg reads as fractions are refused, and so is a positive value that rounds to 0, which FFmpeg would read as "wait forever".

methods.name: DisposeStep
methods.summary: Runs one teardown step, logging and swallowing whatever it throws so the steps after it still run. Disposal is single-pass, so a step that takes the whole method down with it never gets a second chance.

methods.name: CloseFFMpegOnDispose
methods.summary: Drops the FFMpeg.exe handle, and closes the child process first when Stop never finished. Stop owns the orderly shutdown, but it is reached from one place per engine inside a catch that logs and moves on, and Clear is reachable with no stop ahead of it - so a Stop that threw, or never ran, arrives here with the recorder still live and this object about to drop the only reference to it (issue #1549).

methods.name: CloseSessionInBackground
methods.summary: Gives a still-running recorder the shutdown grace and then ends it, on a worker rather than on the caller's thread: both callers run on whatever thread the application used - usually the UI thread - and a multi-second wait there is the construction that produced the freeze in issue #1535.

classes.summary: One FFMpeg.exe recording session. Stop and Boolean) take it with an Object), so exactly one of them ever owns closing the recorder however they interleave, and neither has to guess from flags what the other did. Its state is per session, so a previous capture's launch thread finishing late cannot speak for the capture after it.

properties.name: CanDrain
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether joining the pipe workers can still make progress. False once the launch has returned and false once the child has exited: nothing will connect to the pipes in either case, and a worker parked in WaitForConnection would then cost the caller - usually the UI thread - the whole shutdown timeout for nothing. A launch whose process is not visible yet reads as "on its way", which is what it is.

methods.name: TryArmWatchdog
methods.summary: Claims the right to close this session in the background, once. Two claimants can legitimately reach for it - a stop that found no process to write to and the start it overlapped - and two watchdogs racing to kill the same child is one more than needed.
methods.returns: True for the first caller only.

methods.summary: Keeps the frame just written for padding and hands the one it replaces back to the grabber.

methods.name: Write
methods.summary: Writes one video frame to the muxer pipe, padding with duplicate frames so the rawvideo CFR frame-count timeline stays locked to the frame's real SampleTime. Runs only on the single video worker thread (no locking needed).

methods.name: AnchorCfrOrigin
methods.summary: Anchors the rawvideo CFR origin so the running _videoExpectedIndex maps to the supplied frame's real SampleTime, keeping base and index mutually consistent. When the index has not advanced far enough for the origin to stay non-negative (frames clustered at/before t=0, or a restart very early in the stream), it falls back to treating this frame as a fresh origin (index 0). Runs only on the single video worker thread (no locking needed).

methods.name: SelectBestFormatIndex
methods.summary: Selects the index of the best capture format for automatic selection. The same pick fills Format and FrameRate and is applied with Format_UseBest. Within the 1920x1080 cap, in order: a format with a listed rate; H.264/H.265 only when nothing else is left (DirectShow); a format under 15 fps loses when a 1280x720 or larger format reaches 15 fps; highest resolution; MJPG, then any other subtype the sample grabber recognizes; the fastest frame rate. Ties keep the entry the driver enumerated first, also in the name-sorted device list.

parameters.summary: Whether H.264 and H.265 entries are taken only when no other format is left. The DirectShow graph decodes them only when the LAV decoder is installed; the Media Foundation reader decodes them.

methods.name: InvalidateBorder
methods.summary: Marks the whole video window as needing a repaint, so it erases with its own background what the picture no longer covers.
methods.remarks: The EVR presents inside its destination rect and never touches the rest of the video window - unlike VMR-9, whose SetBorderColor fills the clipping window around it. A rect that shrank therefore leaves the previous, larger picture on screen around the new one, and only the application can erase it (issue #1654). SetBorderColor, RepaintVideo and re-attaching the video window were each measured against it and leave the leftover exactly where it was. The whole window goes, not a rectangle around the picture: this runs on whatever thread called Update, whose DPI awareness is not the window's, so every coordinate handed to user32 from here is virtualized to a different scale - measured, a 640x360 window reads back as 426x240. A rectangle-less call carries no coordinates and no such error. The picture therefore goes with the border; a running graph brings it back with the next frame, and for a paused one IFilterGraph2) asks the renderer for it.

methods.name: EraseBorderAndRepaintAsync
methods.summary: Erases the border once more after the renderer has settled, then puts the picture back.

parameters.name: version
parameters.summary: The value of _borderEraseVersion this pass was armed with. A rect applied since means this pass has nothing left to do: every rect that moves arms a pass of its own, and that one erases for the rect it applied and repaints after it.

methods.returns: A task representing the pass.

methods.name: Repaint
methods.summary: Asks the renderer to present the frame it is holding, into whatever rect it holds now.
methods.returns: true when a picture went back on the window; false as well when the display control is being released or is gone, which costs this attempt and not the ones after it.

methods.name: Stale
methods.summary: Whether a pass armed at version has been overtaken, or the renderer is being torn down under it.

parameters.name: version
parameters.summary: The value of _borderEraseVersion the pass holds.

methods.returns: true when the pass should stop.

methods.name: RebindBorderState
methods.summary: Forgets what was known about the window this renderer was drawing on, because it is about to draw on another one.
methods.remarks: A pass armed for the old window would erase what has just been bound, and the rect that window ended on says nothing about the new one - compared against it, the first rect of the new window reads as a shrink or a grow that never happened.

properties.summary: Gets or sets video thread count.

properties.summary: Gets or sets video encoder.

properties.name: VideoErrorResilient
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether error resilient enabled. Error resilient mode indicates to the encoder that it should take measures appropriate for streaming over lossy or noisy links, if possible. Disabled by default.

properties.name: VideoDropframeThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets dropframe threshold. Temporal resampling allows the codec to "drop" frames as a strategy to meet its target data rate. This can cause temporal discontinuities in the encoded video, which may appear as stuttering during playback. This trade-off is often acceptable, but for many applications is not. It can be disabled in these cases. This threshold is described as a percentage of the target data buffer. When the data buffer falls below this percentage of fullness, a dropped frame is indicated. Set the threshold to zero (0) to disable this feature. 0 by default.

properties.name: VideoSpatialResamplingAllowed
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether spatial resampling enabled. Spatial resampling allows the codec to compress a lower resolution version of the frame, which is then upscaled by the encoder to the correct presentation resolution. This increases visual quality at low data rates, at the expense of CPU time on the encoder/decoder.

properties.name: VideoSpatialResamplingUpThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets spatial resampling up watermark. This threshold is described as a percentage of the target data buffer. When the data buffer rises above this percentage of fullness, the encoder will step up to a higher resolution version of the frame.

properties.name: VideoSpatialResamplingDownThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets spatial resampling down watermark. This threshold is described as a percentage of the target data buffer. When the data buffer falls below this percentage of fullness, the encoder will step down to a lower resolution version of the frame.

properties.name: VideoLagInFrames
properties.summary: Gets or sets lag in frame. If set, this value allows the encoder to consume a number of input frames before producing output frames. This allows the encoder to base decisions for the current frame on future frames. This does increase the latency of the encoding pipeline, so it is not appropriate in all situations (ex: realtime encoding). This is a maximum value - the encoder may produce frames sooner than the given limit. Set this value to 0 to disable this feature.

properties.name: VideoTokenPartition
properties.summary: Gets or sets VP8 token partition mode. This defines VP8 partitioning mode for compressed data, i.e., the number of sub-streams in the bitstream. Used for parallelized decoding. Value 0 = one token partition. Value 1 = two token partitions. Value 2 = four token partitions. Value 3 = eight token partitions.

properties.name: VideoMinQuantizer
properties.summary: Gets or sets minimum (best quality) quantizer. The quantizer is the most direct control over the quality of the encoded image. The quantizer range is [0, 63].

properties.name: VideoMaxQuantizer
properties.summary: Gets or sets maximum (worst quality) quantizer. The quantizer is the most direct control over the quality of the encoded image. The quantizer range is [0, 63].

properties.name: VideoUndershootPct
properties.summary: Gets or sets rate control undershoot tolerance. This value, expressed as a percentage of the target bitrate, describes the target bitrate for easier frames, allowing bits to be saved for harder frames. Set to zero to use the codec default.

properties.name: VideoOvershootPct
properties.summary: Gets or sets rate control overshoot tolerance. This value, expressed as a percentage of the target bitrate, describes the maximum allowed bitrate for a given frame. Set to zero to use the codec default.

properties.name: VideoDecoderBufferSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets decoder buffer size. This value indicates the amount of data that may be buffered by the decoding application. This value is expressed in units of time (milliseconds). For example, a value of 5000 indicates that the client will buffer (at least) 5000 ms worth of encoded data.

properties.name: VideoDecoderBufferInitialSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets decoder buffer initial size. This value indicates the amount of data that will be buffered by the decoding application prior to beginning playback. This value is expressed in units of time (milliseconds).

properties.name: VideoDecoderBufferOptimalSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets decoder buffer optimal size. This value indicates the amount of data that the encoder should try to maintain in the decoder's buffer. This value is expressed in units of time (milliseconds).

properties.name: VideoKeyframeMinInterval
properties.summary: Gets or sets keyframe minimum interval. This value, expressed as a number of frames, prevents the encoder from placing a keyframe nearer than MinInterval to the previous keyframe. At least MinInterval frames non-keyframes will be coded before the next keyframe. Set MinInterval equal to MaxInterval for a fixed interval.

properties.name: VideoKeyframeMode
properties.summary: Gets or sets keyframe placement mode. This value indicates whether the encoder should place keyframes at a fixed interval, or determine the optimal placement automatically (as governed by the KeyframeMinInterval and KeyframeMaxInterval).

properties.name: VideoKeyframeMaxInterval
properties.summary: Gets or sets keyframe maximum interval. This value, expressed as a number of frames, forces the encoder to code a keyframe if one has not been coded in the last MaxInterval frames. A value of 0 implies all frames will be keyframes. Set MinInterval equal to MaxInterval for a fixed interval.

properties.name: VideoAutoAltRef
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether alternate reference frame will be added.

properties.name: VideoARNRMaxFrames
properties.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of frames to run the temporal filter over. The number of frames has to be less than or equal to lag in frames. The range is [0, 15]. Zero is the default.

properties.name: VideoARNRStrength
properties.summary: Gets or sets the relative strength of the blur for the temporal filter. The range is [0, 6]. Zero is the weakest and six is the strongest. Three is the default.

properties.name: VideoARNRType
properties.summary: Gets or sets the type of blur for the temporal filter. The range is [1, 3]. Value 1 = a backward blur. Value 2 = a forward blur. Value 3 = a center blur (default).

properties.name: VideoFixedKeyframeInterval
properties.summary: Gets or sets fixed keyframe interval. If keyframe generation at a fixed interval is desired, set keyframe mode to kKeyframeModeDisabled, and set the interval using this method. This is most useful when dealing with a variable frame rate video source when a consistent keyframe interval is desired for streaming purposes.

properties.name: VideoCPUUsed
properties.summary: Gets or sets encoder complexity control. Changes in this value influences, among others, the encoder's selection of motion estimation methods. Values greater than 0 will increase encoder speed at the expense of quality. See libvpx documentation of the VP8E_SET_CPUUSED option for further information. Value range is [-16,16]. Values outside the range are ignored. The default value for configuration of libvpx used within webmdshow is 0.

properties.name: VideoStaticThreshold
properties.summary: Gets or sets static macroblock threshold. Sets the threshold for macroblocks to be treated as static by libvpx. When active it allows the encoder to skip blocks that it deems static based on the provided threshold. Values > 1000 not advisable, and any value greater than 0 can cause encoding artifacts due to skipped blocks. Values less than 0 are ignored.

properties.name: VideoDecimate
properties.summary: Gets or sets decimate value. Reduces frame rate of input video by discarding video frames based on Decimate value. For Decimate value N, and N >= 2, the VP8 encoder filter encodes only every Nth frame. Decimate values less or equal 1 disable decimation.

classes.name: KLVReorderBuffer
classes.summary: Sliding-window sorter that emits KLV packets in monotonically non-decreasing PTS order.
classes.remarks: The native FFMPEG source filter can briefly produce out-of-order KLV PTS during the startup window because its live-source rebase logic recomputes startPosition from the graph clock for the first few packets. The result is rebased PTS that can step backward by tens of milliseconds. Without reordering, downstream consumers — notably the external ffmpeg.exe MPEG-TS muxer used by UDP_FFMPEG_EXE and FFMPEGEXEOutput — abort the whole pipeline with "Application provided invalid, non monotonically increasing dts". The buffer holds up to windowSize pending packets sorted by PTS. When a new packet arrives and the buffer is full, the smallest-PTS packet is released to the caller. A packet that lands later than the last released PTS (i.e. arrived after the window already moved past it) is dropped — this is rare and only happens when the real out-of-order distance exceeds the window. The default window of 3 covers the largest backward jump observed in practice (3 sequential packets within ~40ms). Not thread-safe. Calls are expected to come from a single DirectShow callback thread.

constructors.name: KLVReorderBuffer
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the KLVReorderBuffer class.

parameters.name: windowSize
parameters.summary: Maximum number of packets to hold pending. Must be >= 1.

properties.name: DroppedLateCount
properties.summary: Number of out-of-order packets that were dropped because they landed after the sliding window had already advanced past their PTS. Useful for diagnostics.

properties.name: LastVideoPts100ns
properties.summary: Gets or sets the last time a packet of this destination was given after being moved onto a forced-frame-rate video's clock, which keeps those times in order (#1983).

methods.name: Push
methods.summary: Pushes a KLV packet into the buffer. Returns zero or one item ready for emission.

parameters.name: data
parameters.summary: Pointer to the raw KLV payload (may be reused after this call returns).

parameters.name: size
parameters.summary: Size of the payload in bytes.

methods.name: Flush
methods.summary: Drains all currently-buffered packets in PTS-ascending order. Call on stream stop to release the final window. Any packet whose PTS is not strictly greater than the last emitted PTS is dropped (and increments DroppedLateCount) to keep output strictly monotonic, matching the rule used by Int64).

methods.name: Reset
methods.summary: Clears all buffered packets without emitting them and resets DroppedLateCount to zero. Call when restarting capture to discard the previous stream's window.

methods.name: ConfigureVideoDecoder
methods.summary: Prepares a LAV Video Decoder the SDK has just added to a graph. Its settings are kept in the graph instead of the user's registry, and RGB24 output is turned off: LAV writes RGB24 rows unpadded (width * 3 bytes) where a DIB needs them 4-byte aligned, so at a width that is not a multiple of 4 the frames come out sheared or the next filter refuses the connection. LAV then offers RGB32, which is converted to RGB24 by the Color Space Converter when a filter needs it. Call it before any other setting and before the decoder is connected: runtime mode reloads the defaults.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: SDK logging context. Pass the engine's Context.

methods.name: ConfigureAudioDecoder
methods.summary: Prepares a LAV Audio Decoder the SDK has just added to a graph: its settings are kept in the graph instead of the user's registry, and it outputs 16-bit PCM only, which every capture audio chain takes; LAV converts its float or 24/32-bit decoder output to it. Call it before any other setting and before the decoder is connected: runtime mode reloads the defaults.

classes.name: GMFBridge
classes.summary: The GMF bridge controller and the two filters it inserts, callable from any thread.
classes.remarks: A bridge loaded from file is never registered, so COM has no proxy for its interfaces, and an ordinary RCW works only in the apartment that created it: from any other one the CLR asks COM for a proxy and gets E_NOINTERFACE (GitHub issue #1690). The native bridge is thread-safe, so this keeps the raw pointers and calls through wrappers made in the calling thread's context. The filters are held too, because the bridge accepts only its own filters, not proxies to them.

classes.summary: Enumerates DXGI graphics adapters on Windows and maps LUIDs to CUDA device ordinals. Returns an empty list and null translations on non-Windows platforms.

methods.name: Enumerate
methods.summary: Enumerates hardware and software graphics adapters visible to DXGI. Results are cached for the lifetime of the process; call Invalidate to refresh after a device hotplug.

methods.name: Invalidate
methods.summary: Drops the cached adapter list so the next Enumerate call re-queries DXGI. Use sparingly; DXGI enumeration allocates native handles.

methods.name: LuidToCudaDeviceId
methods.summary: Translates a DXGI adapter LUID to a CUDA device ordinal suitable for the cuda-device-id property on nvh264enc / nvh265enc. Returns null if the LUID does not map to an NVIDIA adapter or CUDA is not available on this host.
methods.remarks: Best-effort heuristic. This method does NOT query CUDA or NVML — it simply walks the DXGI adapter list and returns the enumeration index of the matching NVIDIA adapter. On single-NVIDIA-GPU systems this typically matches the CUDA device ordinal, but on multi-NVIDIA-GPU rigs the DXGI enumeration order is not guaranteed to match CUDA's ordinal order (CUDA can reorder devices based on compute capability, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, driver version, and other factors). When precise GPU pinning is required, pass an explicit CudaDeviceId on the settings class instead of relying on this heuristic.

classes.name: NDIUtils
classes.summary: Provides utility methods for NDI (Network Device Interface) initialization and availability checking. This static class handles platform-specific NDI library initialization and validation.

methods.name: IsAvailable
methods.summary: Determines whether the NDI library is available and properly initialized. Configures the NDI runtime environment, then hands the library lifetime to NDIRuntime so the process gets exactly one initialize and one destroy.
methods.remarks: Initializing the runtime here and never destroying it is what left the process hanging in libndi's DllMain(DLL_PROCESS_DETACH): the detach handler waits on a worker thread the loader has already terminated, inside LdrShutdownProcess with the loader lock held, so even TerminateProcess cannot finish it (issue #1490).
methods.returns: true if the NDI library is available and initialized; otherwise, false.

methods.name: CheckAvailable
methods.summary: Checks whether the NDI library is available and logs an error message if it is not. This method provides user-friendly error reporting with installation instructions.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: The base context used for logging error messages.

methods.returns: true if the NDI library is available; otherwise, false.

classes.name: FastImageProcessing
classes.summary: Fast Image Processing - High-performance image processing operations using native C++ library (VisioForge_MFP.dll/VisioForge_MFP64.dll).
classes.remarks: This class provides .NET P/Invoke wrappers around a native C++ library that implements various image processing operations using Intel IPP (Integrated Performance Primitives) for optimal performance. Supported Image Formats:RGB24: 24-bit color, 3 bytes per pixel (Blue, Green, Red order in memory)RGB32/ARGB: 32-bit color with alpha, 4 bytes per pixel (Blue, Green, Red, Alpha order in memory)Memory Layout Concepts:IntPtr pixels: Pointer to raw pixel data in memory, representing continuous buffer of color valuesint width, height: Image dimensions in pixelsint stride: Number of bytes per image row (scan line), may include padding for alignment. For RGB24: typically width*3 rounded up. For RGB32: typically width*4Pixel addressing: Pixel at (x,y) is at offset: y * stride + x * bytesPerPixelPlatform Support:x86 (32-bit): Uses VisioForge_MFP.dll via MFPCoreX86 classx64 (64-bit): Uses VisioForge_MFP64.dll via MFPCoreX64 classPerformance Features:Smart multithreading: Automatically parallelizes operations for images larger than 200x200 pixelsIntel IPP acceleration: Uses optimized SIMD instructions for fast processingDirect memory manipulation: Operates on raw pixel buffers without managed allocationsC++ Library Location: _SOURCE\MFP\VisioForge_MFP\

methods.name: Init
methods.summary: Initializes the Fast Image Processing library by loading the appropriate native DLL (x86 or x64).
methods.remarks: This method must be called before using any other methods in this class. It attempts to load and initialize the platform-specific native library: - On 32-bit processes: VisioForge_MFP.dll - On 64-bit processes: VisioForge_MFP64.dll If initialization fails, all subsequent operations will fail. Use IsFound to check if initialization was successful.

methods.name: IsFound
methods.summary: Checks if the Fast Image Processing library was successfully initialized.
methods.remarks: Always check this before using any image processing methods. If this returns false, the native DLL could not be loaded (missing file, wrong architecture, or missing dependencies).
methods.returns: true if the native library is loaded and ready to use; otherwise, false.

methods.summary: Extracts a sub-region from an RGB24 source image starting at specified coordinates and copies it to output buffer.
methods.remarks: Operation: Copies the portion of source image from (cutX, cutY) to (srcWidth-1, srcHeight-1) into output buffer.Extracted Size: Width = srcWidth - cutX, Height = srcHeight - cutYOutput Buffer Size: Must be at least (srcWidth - cutX) * (srcHeight - cutY) * 3 bytes.Use Cases: Removing top-left border/margin, extracting bottom-right portion, simple cropping from fixed position.Difference from Crop: ImageCut extracts from (cutX, cutY) to image end. Crop extracts arbitrary rectangle.Example: ImageCutRGB24(img, 640, 480, out, 10, 20) extracts 630×460 region starting at (10, 20).Bounds: cutX must be < srcWidth, cutY must be < srcHeight, otherwise results are undefined.Related: See for extracting arbitrary rectangles, for RGB32 format.Native Implementation: Calls ImageCutRGB24 in VisioForge_MFP.dll

methods.remarks: CAST Algorithm: Advanced temporal denoising using Intel IPP that analyzes both spatial (within frame) and temporal (between frames) information.How It Works:Detects edges in current frame using edge detectionCompares current frame with previous frame to identify static vs moving areasApplies stronger denoising to static areas (temporal filtering)Preserves edges and moving areas to avoid motion blurAnisotropic: Applies different filtering strengths in different directions to preserve edges while removing noise.Coupled: Combines spatial filtering (within frame) with temporal filtering (across frames) for superior results.Use Cases: Video denoising for surveillance footage, low-light video enhancement, cleaning up compressed video artifacts.Requirements: Requires storing previous frame for temporal comparison. Best results with static camera or minimal motion.Performance: More computationally expensive than single-frame denoisers due to temporal analysis.Native Implementation: Calls EffectDenoiseCAST in VisioForge_MFP.dll (uses Intel IPP ippiFilterDenoiseCAST functions)

methods.name: FadeInOut
methods.summary: Applies a fade-in or fade-out effect to an RGB24 image based on time position within a time range.
methods.remarks: Fade Effect: Gradually adjusts image brightness over time to create smooth transitions.Algorithm:Calculates progress: progress = (currentTime - startTime) / (stopTime - startTime), range 0.0 to 1.0For fade-in: multiplier = progress (0.0 = black, 1.0 = full)For fade-out: multiplier = (1.0 - progress) (1.0 = full, 0.0 = black)Multiplies each RGB channel by multiplier: newValue = oldValue * multiplierFade-In Behavior:At startTime: Image is completely black (all pixels = 0)Between times: Image gradually brightens proportionallyAt stopTime: Image is at full original brightnessFade-Out Behavior:At startTime: Image is at full original brightnessBetween times: Image gradually darkens proportionallyAt stopTime: Image is completely black (all pixels = 0)Time Units: Time values should use consistent units (all milliseconds or all ticks). Only relative differences matter.Clamping: If currentTime is outside [startTime, stopTime] range, effect will clamp to nearest endpoint (fully bright or fully dark).Use Cases: Video transitions, scene changes, title sequences, end credits, crossfades (combined with compositing).Performance: Simple per-pixel multiplication, suitable for real-time video processing.Native Implementation: Calls EffectFadeInOut in VisioForge_MFP.dll

methods.remarks: Purpose: Creating a zoom context allows pre-calculating interpolation data for efficient repeated zoom operations.Interpolation Modes:Nearest Neighbor: Fastest, blocky appearance when zooming in, good for pixel artLinear/Bilinear: Fast, smooth zoom, good for real-time videoCubic/Bicubic: Slower, highest quality, best for still images and detailed contentUsage Pattern:Call ZoomCreate once with image specificationsCall multiple times with different zoom levels and shiftsCall to free resources when donePerformance: Reusing context is much faster than creating new context for each zoom operation.Related: See for pan-only operations, for pure resizing.Native Implementation: Calls ZoomCreate in VisioForge_MFP.dll

parameters.name: image
parameters.summary: RAWImage structure describing the image format, dimensions, and stride

parameters.name: interpolationMode
parameters.summary: Interpolation algorithm to use for zooming quality (nearest, linear, cubic)

methods.returns: IntPtr handle to zoom context. Must be destroyed with IntPtr) when done.

methods.name: ZoomDestroy
methods.summary: Destroys a zoom context created by VideoInterpolationMode) and frees all associated resources.
methods.remarks: Resource Management: Always call this when done using a zoom context to prevent memory leaks.Safe to Call: Can safely be called with IntPtr.Zero (will be ignored).After Calling: The zoom handle becomes invalid and must not be used in subsequent operations.Native Implementation: Calls ZoomDestroy in VisioForge_MFP.dll

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.summary: IntPtr handle to zoom context returned by ZoomCreate

methods.name: ZoomImage
methods.summary: Applies zoom and pan transformations to an image using a pre-created zoom context.
methods.remarks: Zoom + Pan Operation: Applies both zooming and panning in a single optimized operation.Zoom Factors:1.0: Original size (100%, no zoom)2.0: 2x magnification (zoom in, image appears 2x larger)0.5: 0.5x reduction (zoom out, image appears 2x smaller)Different X and Y values: Non-uniform scaling (aspect ratio change)Pan Offsets:Applied after zoom transformationAllow viewing different portions of zoomed imageUseful for digital pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) camera simulationUse Cases:Digital zoom for cameras without optical zoomPTZ simulation (pan-tilt-zoom without mechanical movement)Focus on specific image regionsKen Burns effect (slow zoom/pan over still images)Video stabilization previewPerformance: Efficient when using pre-created zoom context with same image size. Uses interpolation mode specified in ZoomCreate.Clipping: Areas outside the source image after zoom/pan will show black or undefined data.Native Implementation: Calls ZoomImage in VisioForge_MFP.dll
