methods.name: SafeSendInputOnCancel
methods.summary: Send input to a possibly-already-exited FFmpeg instance from a cancel handler. The cancel hook can fire after the process has exited (e.g. CancelEvent posted just before the process flushed and quit on its own), in which case Instance.SendInput → _process.StandardInput.Write raises ObjectDisposedException / IOException / InvalidOperationException and the exception propagates out of the cancellation handler. Wrap the call so the cancellation path is robust to that race.

parameters.name: input
parameters.summary: Input string to send (typically "q" to quit).

methods.name: LogCancelSetterError

methods.name: WaitExited
methods.summary: Waits for an FFMpeg process that has ended on its own: for the process object to signal, since the exit status is set while the child still holds its output file (issue #1580), and then for its stderr to be read out, so LastErrorLine is its last word. classes.name: DVDInfoReader
classes.summary: Provides functionality to read and extract detailed information from DVD video volumes. This class uses DirectShow's DVD interfaces to analyze DVD structure, including titles, chapters, audio tracks, subtitles, and menu information.

constructors.name: DVDInfoReader
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the DVDInfoReader class. Creates an empty DVDInfo structure ready to be populated with DVD metadata.

properties.name: Info
properties.summary: Gets the comprehensive DVD information extracted from the video volume. This includes disc metadata, title information, audio/subtitle streams, menu attributes, and playback capabilities.

properties.name: Filename
properties.summary: Gets or sets the path to the DVD video volume. This can be a physical DVD drive path (e.g., "D:\") or a path to a DVD folder structure containing VIDEO_TS directory.

methods.name: ReadDVDInfo
methods.summary: Reads comprehensive information from the specified DVD video volume. This method creates a DirectShow DVD graph to extract metadata including disc structure, titles, chapters, audio/subtitle streams, menu languages, parental levels, and decoder capabilities.
methods.returns: true if the DVD information was successfully read; false if an error occurred during graph creation or information extraction.

methods.name: DVD_Menu_Languages
methods.summary: Retrieves the list of available menu languages from the DVD. These are the languages available for DVD menus, not content audio or subtitles.
methods.returns: A list of menu language names (e.g., "English", "Spanish", "French") available on the DVD. Returns null if no menu languages are available or if an error occurred during retrieval.

classes.name: MediaInfoFilesCache
classes.summary: Provides an in-memory cache for media file information to optimize repeated access to file metadata. This cache stores MediaInfoReader instances to avoid redundant file analysis operations, significantly improving performance when accessing the same media files multiple times.

constructors.name: MediaInfoFilesCache
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MediaInfoFilesCache class. Creates an empty cache ready to store media file information.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: The DirectShow context for media operations and logging.

methods.name: Clear
methods.summary: Clears all cached media information from memory. This method should be called when the cache is no longer needed or when memory usage needs to be reduced.

methods.name: GetInfo
methods.summary: Retrieves media information for the specified file, using cache if available. If the file information is not cached, it analyzes the file and stores the result for future access. This method significantly improves performance for repeated access to the same media files.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The full path to the media file to analyze.

parameters.name: useLibMediaInfo
parameters.summary: When true, uses the LibMediaInfo library for analysis (more comprehensive but slower). When false, uses DirectShow filters (faster but may not support all formats).

methods.returns: A MediaInfoReader instance containing comprehensive media file information including video streams, audio streams, subtitles, and format details.

methods.name: GetInfo
methods.summary: Retrieves basic video properties for the specified media file using the cache. This is a convenience method for quickly obtaining common video attributes without needing to process the full MediaInfoReader object.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The full path to the media file to analyze.

parameters.name: useLibMediaInfo
parameters.summary: When true, uses the LibMediaInfo library for analysis. When false, uses DirectShow filters.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: Output parameter that receives the video width in pixels. Set to 0 if no video stream is found.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: Output parameter that receives the video height in pixels. Set to 0 if no video stream is found.

parameters.name: frameRate
parameters.summary: Output parameter that receives the video frame rate (frames per second). Set to 0 if no video stream is found.

classes.name: MediaInfoReader
classes.summary: Provides comprehensive media file analysis capabilities using DirectShow and LibMediaInfo. This class can extract detailed information about video files including codec information, stream properties, duration, bitrates, and format-specific metadata. Supports a wide range of media formats including AVI, MP4, MKV, MPEG, WMV, and many others.

constructors.name: MediaInfoReader
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MediaInfoReader class with a specific DirectShow context. Use this constructor when you need to share a context across multiple operations or when you need custom logging/error handling.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The full path to the media file to analyze.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: The DirectShow context for filter operations and logging.

constructors.name: MediaInfoReader
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MediaInfoReader class with a default context. This is the simplest constructor for basic media file analysis.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The full path to the media file to analyze.

constructors.name: MediaInfoReader
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MediaInfoReader class without a filename. Use this constructor when you need to set the filename later or when analyzing streams rather than files.

properties.name: Audio_Streams_AllInOne
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether all audio streams should be treated as a single combined stream. When true, multiple audio tracks are presented as one unified stream. When false, each audio track is analyzed and reported separately.
properties.value: true if audio streams should be combined; otherwise, false.

properties.name: FileFormat
properties.summary: Gets the detected media container format of the analyzed file. Examples include "AVI", "MP4", "MKV", "MPEG-PS", "MPEG-TS", "WMV", etc. This represents the container format, not the codec used within.
properties.value: The file container format as a string.

properties.name: Filename
properties.summary: Gets or sets the full path to the media file to be analyzed. Supports local file paths, UNC paths, and in some cases HTTP/RTSP URLs.
properties.value: The complete file path or URL.

properties.name: Subtitles
properties.summary: Gets the list of subtitle/caption streams found in the media file. Each stream contains information about language, format (SRT, ASS, VobSub), and other subtitle-specific properties.
properties.value: A list of SubtitleStreamInfo objects, one for each subtitle track.

properties.name: VideoStreams
properties.summary: Gets the list of video streams found in the media file. Each stream contains detailed information including codec, resolution, frame rate, bitrate, aspect ratio, and duration.
properties.value: A list of VideoStreamInfo objects, one for each video track.

properties.name: AudioStreams
properties.summary: Gets the list of audio streams found in the media file. Each stream contains information about codec, sample rate, channels, bitrate, language, and duration.
properties.value: A list of AudioStreamInfo objects, one for each audio track.

properties.name: DefaultVideoDuration
properties.summary: Gets the overall duration of the video content in the file. This represents the primary video stream duration and is used when individual stream durations are not available.
properties.value: The video duration as a TimeSpan, or TimeSpan.Zero if no video is present.

properties.name: DefaultAudioDuration
properties.summary: Gets the overall duration of the audio content in the file. This represents the primary audio stream duration and is used when individual stream durations are not available.
properties.value: The audio duration as a TimeSpan, or TimeSpan.Zero if no audio is present.

properties.name: Debug_Mode
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether debug mode is enabled. When true, additional diagnostic information is logged and debug files (such as filter graphs) may be saved to Debug_Dir.
properties.value: true if debug mode is enabled; otherwise, false.

properties.name: Debug_Dir
properties.summary: Gets or sets the directory path where debug files should be saved. This includes filter graph files (.grf) and text representations of the graph. Only used when Debug_Mode is true.
properties.value: The full path to the debug output directory.

methods.name: Attach
methods.summary: Attaches a DirectShow context to this MediaInfoReader instance. This allows changing the context after construction, useful for reusing the reader with different logging or filter configurations.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: The DirectShow context to attach for subsequent operations.

methods.name: Init
methods.summary: Initializes internal data structures and sets default values. Called by all constructors to ensure consistent initialization.

methods.name: ConfigureLocalRedist
methods.summary: Configures the application to use local redistributable DirectShow filters. Call this method once at application startup to ensure all required codecs and filters are available from the local installation directory rather than relying on system-installed components.

methods.name: AddMediaType
methods.summary: Processes and adds media type information to the appropriate stream collection. This method analyzes DirectShow media type structures and extracts relevant information for video, audio, or subtitle streams.

parameters.name: mt
parameters.summary: The DirectShow AMMediaType structure containing stream format information.

parameters.name: mediaDet
parameters.summary: The IMediaDet interface for retrieving additional stream properties like duration and frame rate.

methods.name: FixBitrates
methods.summary: Calculates and updates the video bitrate based on file size and duration if the initial bitrate detection failed. This is a fallback mechanism to ensure a non-zero bitrate is reported when the codec header information is insufficient.

methods.name: IsFilePlayable
methods.summary: Determines whether a media file can be successfully played back on the current system. This method checks file validity, extension, and attempts to build a DirectShow render graph to verify if the necessary codecs and filters are installed.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The full path to the media file to test.

parameters.name: errorCode
parameters.summary: Output parameter returning a specific error code if playback fails.

parameters.name: errorText
parameters.summary: Output parameter returning a descriptive error message if playback fails.

methods.returns: True if the file can be played; otherwise, false.

methods.name: GetAspectFromResolution
methods.summary: Calculates the simplified aspect ratio (e.g., "16:9", "4:3") from the given video resolution. Iterates through common rational approximations to find the closest matching standard aspect ratio.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: The width of the video in pixels.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: The height of the video in pixels.

parameters.name: w
parameters.summary: Output parameter receiving the numerator of the aspect ratio (e.g., 16).

parameters.name: h
parameters.summary: Output parameter receiving the denominator of the aspect ratio (e.g., 9).

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: Optional context for error logging and diagnostics.

methods.returns: A string representation of the aspect ratio (e.g., "16:9").

methods.name: ReadFullFileInfoEx
methods.summary: Performs a comprehensive analysis of the media file using DirectShow filter graph rendering. This method attempts to render the file to allow downstream filters to report detailed stream information, handling various DirectShow return codes and fallback scenarios for different file types.

methods.name: ReadBluRayInfo
methods.summary: Analyzes Blu-Ray media files by building a DirectShow filter graph with LAV filters. This method is specifically designed to handle Blu-Ray structures, extracting video and audio stream details by explicitly loading and connecting LAV Splitter and Decoder filters.

methods.name: ReadFileInfoUsingMediaLib
methods.summary: Extracts detailed media information using the LibMediaInfo library. This provides comprehensive metadata support for a wide range of formats, often providing details that DirectShow filters might miss, such as specific codec profiles or container tags.

methods.name: ReadFileInfoUsingMediaLib
methods.summary: Reads file info using LibMediaInfo.

methods.name: ReadFileInfoUsingMediaLib
methods.summary: Reads file info using LibMediaInfo.

methods.name: ReadFileInfo
methods.summary: Reads file info.

methods.name: ReadFileInfo
methods.summary: Reads file info from stream using LibMediaInfo.

methods.name: ReadFileInfo
methods.summary: Reads file info.

methods.name: ApplyCryptoConfig
methods.summary: Applies crypto config.

methods.name: ReadInfoMainEncrypted
methods.summary: Reads media info.
methods.returns: Returns true if the operation was successful.

methods.name: ReadInfoDeep
methods.summary: Performs a deep fallback analysis of the media file by rendering it in a filter graph. This method is used when standard analysis fails, attempting to extract basic properties like duration and resolution by directly querying DirectShow interfaces (IMediaSeeking, IBasicVideo).

methods.name: ReadInfoMain
methods.summary: Orchestrates the primary media information retrieval process. This method determines the file format, executes various analysis strategies (including deep analysis and fallback mechanisms), and compiles the results. It handles both local files and network streams (HTTP/RTSP).
methods.returns: True if the media information was successfully read; otherwise, false.

methods.name: GetStreamAvailabilityFromMemoryStream
methods.summary: Gets the stream availability from memory stream.
methods.returns: true if successful, false otherwise.

methods.name: SecondsToString
methods.summary: Converts time to string.
methods.returns: Returns time as a string.

methods.name: Video_ResolutionWithAspect
methods.summary: Returns video width.
methods.returns: Returns video width, 0 if error happen.

methods.name: EvalAudioCodec
methods.summary: Gets codec name.
methods.returns: Returns codec name.

methods.name: EvalFourCC
methods.summary: Resolves the human-readable codec name from the provided FourCC string. Matches the code against a comprehensive list of known video and audio codecs.

parameters.name: srcFourCC
parameters.summary: The FourCC (Four Character Code) string to evaluate.

methods.returns: The human-readable codec name (e.g., "MPEG-4", "DivX"), or "Unknown Codec" if not found.

methods.name: FillFileFormat
methods.summary: Determines and sets the human-readable file format description based on the file extension. Populates the FileFormat property with a friendly name (e.g., "MPEG 4" for .mp4, "Matroska" for .mkv).

classes.name: TSProgramEnumerator
classes.summary: Provides functionality to enumerate programs within MPEG Transport Stream (TS) files. MPEG-TS files can contain multiple programs (channels), each with its own set of video, audio, and subtitle streams. This class helps identify all unique programs within a TS file using the MediaInfo library for analysis.

methods.name: EnumeratePrograms
methods.summary: Enumerates all unique program IDs found in an MPEG-TS file. Each program in a transport stream represents a separate channel or service, which may contain multiple elementary streams (video, audio, subtitles). This method scans all video streams and collects their associated program IDs.

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.summary: The full path to the MPEG-TS file to analyze.

methods.returns: An array of unique program IDs found in the transport stream. Returns an empty array if no programs are found or if the file is not a valid TS file.

classes.name: MediaPlayerCore
classes.summary: Provides comprehensive Windows-based media playback functionality using DirectShow technology. This is the core class of the VisioForge Media Player SDK for Windows platforms.
classes.remarks: MediaPlayerCore is a Windows-specific implementation that uses DirectShow (and optionally Media Foundation or FFMPEG) for media playback. It supports a wide range of media formats, codecs, and playback scenarios including:Local file playback (video and audio files)DVD playback with full menu and chapter navigationNetwork streaming (RTSP, RTMP, HTTP, UDP, TCP)Playlist management for sequential playbackReal-time video and audio effects processingHardware-accelerated decoding (GPU decode support)Multiple audio/video stream selectionOn-screen display (OSD) and text overlayPicture-in-picture (PIP) supportMotion detection and video analysisAudio VU meters and spectrum analysisThe class is implemented as a partial class split across multiple files for better organization. It provides both synchronous and asynchronous APIs for most operations.Platform Requirements: Windows 7 or later, DirectShow filters installed, appropriate codecs for target media formats.

constructors.name: MediaPlayerCore
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MediaPlayerCore class with a video view and optional automatic initialization.
constructors.remarks: Deferred initialization (initialize=false) is useful when you need to configure properties before the player infrastructure is created.

parameters.name: videoView
parameters.summary: The IVideoView implementation for video display. Pass null for audio-only playback.

parameters.name: initialize
parameters.summary: If true (default), immediately initializes all components. If false, you must call Init() or InitAsync() manually before use.

constructors.name: MediaPlayerCore
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MediaPlayerCore class with default settings.
constructors.remarks: Creates a player without a video view and immediately initializes all components. For video playback, attach a video view using appropriate methods before playing. This constructor is suitable for simple audio playback scenarios.

constructors.name: MediaPlayerCore
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MediaPlayerCore class with control over automatic initialization.
constructors.remarks: Use deferred initialization when you need to set properties that affect initialization behavior, such as custom redistributable paths or specific renderer modes.

parameters.name: initialize
parameters.summary: If true, immediately initializes all components. If false, initialization is deferred until Init() or InitAsync() is called.

properties.name: HasCustomWindow
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the application gave a custom window that still exists. The handle is kept across stops, so the window may have been destroyed since (#3059).

properties.name: MultiScreen_Count
properties.summary: How many extra screens the caller has described.

properties.name: VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#State
properties.summary: Gets the current playback state of the media player.
properties.value: The current state: Stopped, Playing, Paused, or Finished. Use this property to update UI controls or determine valid operations.

properties.name: Debug_IsStopping
properties.summary: True while a stop is between publishing _stopping and clearing it. A test throws from a frame handler only in that window (#3449).

properties.name: Debug_Dir
properties.summary: Gets or sets debug directory. An empty value or null means the working directory.

properties.name: Debug_Mode
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether debug mode enabled.

properties.name: Debug_DisableMessageDialogs
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether message dialog will be shown in case of error if OnError event is not implemented.

properties.name: Debug_Telemetry
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether anonymous error and feature-usage telemetry is sent to VisioForge while a debugger is attached to the process.
properties.value: true to send anonymous error and feature-usage telemetry while a debugger is attached; false to send nothing.

properties.name: GraphCall.StopRequests
properties.summary: Gets how many stops had been requested when the call was counted in; see Int32).

properties.name: GraphCall.Entered
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the call was counted in and may use the graph.

properties.name: NeedsGraphPump
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the graph has to live on _graphPump.

properties.name: CallerWillNotPump
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the calling thread will not be pumping messages for as long as the graph lives, so the graph has to be built on _graphPump instead (GitHub issue #1659).

properties.name: Loop
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether media playback should automatically restart when reaching the end.
properties.value: true to enable continuous looping; false for single playback. Default is false.

properties.name: Loop_DoNotSeekToBeginning
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value kept for compatibility; it no longer changes how loop mode restarts playback.
properties.value: Default is false.

properties.name: Info_UseLibMediaInfo
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to use the MediaInfo library for detailed file analysis.
properties.value: true to use MediaInfo for comprehensive metadata; false to use basic DirectShow info. Default is true.

properties.name: Audio_OutputDevice
properties.summary: Gets or sets the audio output device name for playback.
properties.value: The friendly name of the audio device as returned by Audio_OutputDevice_GetList(). Empty string or null uses the system default audio device.

properties.name: Audio_PlayAudio
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio output is enabled during playback.
properties.value: true to play audio through speakers/headphones; false to mute audio output. Default is true.

properties.name: Audio_Channel_Mapper
properties.summary: Gets or sets audio channel mapping configuration for custom channel routing.
properties.value: AudioChannelMapperSettings object defining how input channels map to output channels. null disables channel mapping.

properties.name: Audio_Effects_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio effect processing is enabled.
properties.value: true to enable audio effects pipeline; false to bypass all audio effects. Default is false.

properties.name: Audio_Effects_Tempo_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether tempo/pitch control effect is enabled.
properties.value: true to enable tempo adjustment without pitch change; false to disable. Default is false.

properties.name: Audio_Effects_Tempo_Value
properties.summary: Gets or sets the tempo adjustment value for time-stretching audio.
properties.value: Tempo multiplier in permille (1000 = normal speed). Range: 500 (half speed) to 4000 (four times the speed). Default is 1000.

properties.name: Audio_Enhancer_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the audio enhancement processor is enabled.
properties.value: true to enable multi-band audio enhancement; false to disable. Default is false.

properties.name: Audio_Sample_Grabber_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether raw audio sample capture is enabled.
properties.value: true to enable audio frame capture events; false to disable. Default is false.

properties.name: Audio_VUMeter_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether basic audio level metering is enabled.
properties.value: true to enable VU meter events; false to disable. Default is false.

properties.name: Audio_VUMeter_Pro_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether professional audio metering and analysis is enabled.
properties.value: true to enable advanced audio analysis; false to disable. Default is false.

properties.name: Audio_VUMeter_Pro_Volume
properties.summary: Gets or sets the reference volume level for VU Meter Pro calculations.
properties.value: Volume level as a percentage (0-100). Default is 100.

properties.name: VideoView
properties.summary: Gets or sets the video display surface for rendering video output.
properties.value: An IVideoView implementation (WinForms, WPF, MAUI, etc.) or null for audio-only.

properties.name: Video_Renderer
properties.summary: Gets or sets video renderer configuration including renderer type and display options.
properties.value: VideoRendererSettings object containing renderer mode, aspect ratio, and other display settings.

properties.name: Source_MemoryStream
properties.summary: Gets or sets the memory stream source for playing media from memory buffers.
properties.value: MemoryStreamSource object providing media data, or null if not using memory mode.

properties.name: Source_Mode
properties.summary: Gets or sets the media source type determining which playback engine to use.
properties.value: The source mode: LAV (recommended), MediaFoundation, FFMPEG, etc. Default is LAV.

properties.name: Source_GPU_Mode
properties.summary: Gets or sets the GPU decoder type when using hardware acceleration.
properties.value: LAVGPUDecoder enumeration value specifying which GPU decoder to use. Default depends on system capabilities.

properties.name: Source_Custom_CLSID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the CLSID of a custom DirectShow source filter.
properties.value: GUID string in format "{XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX}" or empty for default.

properties.name: Play_PauseAtFirstFrame
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to automatically pause after displaying the first frame.
properties.value: true to pause at first frame; false to play normally. Default is false.

properties.name: Play_DelayEnabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether delayed start mode is enabled for synchronized playback.
properties.value: true to enable two-phase startup; false for normal immediate playback. Default is false.

properties.name: Selection_Active
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether playback range selection is active.
properties.value: true to limit playback to the selected range; false for full file playback. Default is false.

properties.name: Selection_Start
properties.summary: Gets or sets the start position for range-based playback.
properties.value: TimeSpan indicating where selected playback should begin. Must be less than a positive Selection_Stop and within media duration.

properties.name: Selection_Stop
properties.summary: Gets or sets the end position for range-based playback.
properties.value: TimeSpan indicating where selected playback should end. Must be greater than Selection_Start, or zero to play to the end.

properties.name: Custom_Video_Decoder
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of a custom video decoder filter to use instead of the default.
properties.value: DirectShow filter name for video decoding, or empty string/null for automatic selection.

properties.name: Custom_Splitter
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of a custom splitter/demuxer filter for parsing media containers.
properties.value: DirectShow filter name for splitting, or empty string/null for automatic selection.

properties.name: Custom_Audio_Decoder
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of a custom audio decoder filter to use instead of the default.
properties.value: DirectShow filter name for audio decoding, or empty string/null for automatic selection.

properties.name: Virtual_Camera_Output_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether video output is redirected to Virtual Camera SDK.
properties.value: true to output video as a virtual webcam; false for normal display. Default is false.

properties.name: NDI_Output
properties.summary: Gets or sets NDI (Network Device Interface) output configuration for network video streaming.
properties.value: NDIOutput object with streaming settings, or null to disable NDI output.

properties.name: Virtual_Camera_Output_LicenseKey
properties.summary: Gets or sets the license key for Virtual Camera SDK output functionality.
properties.value: Valid Virtual Camera SDK license key string, or null/empty for trial mode.

properties.name: Virtual_Camera_Output_AlternativeAudioFilterName
properties.summary: Gets or sets the name of an alternative audio filter to use with Virtual Camera output.
properties.value: DirectShow filter name for audio processing or rendering, or null for default.

properties.name: Video_Effects_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether CPU-based video effects processing is enabled.
properties.value: true to enable video effects pipeline; false to bypass all effects. Default is false.

properties.name: Video_Resize
properties.summary: Gets or sets video resizing and scaling configuration.
properties.value: IVideoResizeSettings implementation: VideoResizeSettings for basic scaling, MaxineUpscaleSettings for AI upscaling, or MaxineSuperResSettings for super-resolution. null disables resizing.

properties.name: Video_Crop
properties.summary: Gets or sets video cropping configuration to remove unwanted areas.
properties.value: VideoCropSettings defining crop margins, or null to disable cropping.

properties.name: Video_Effects_GPU_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether GPU-accelerated video effects are enabled. The effects added with Video_Effects_GPU_Add() are applied only while it is true; the chroma key is applied either way.
properties.value: true to enable GPU effects processing; false to disable. Default is false.

properties.name: Video_Sample_Grabber_UseForVideoEffects
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to use sample grabber for video effects processing.
properties.value: true to process effects via sample grabber; false for in-place processing. Default is true.

properties.name: Motion_Detection
properties.summary: Gets or sets motion detection configuration for detecting movement in video.
properties.value: MotionDetectionSettings object with detection parameters, or null to disable.

properties.name: MIDI_Renderer
properties.summary: Gets or sets the MIDI synthesizer device for playing MIDI files.
properties.value: MIDI device name as returned by MIDI_Renderer_GetList(), or empty for default.

properties.name: MultiScreen_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether multi-monitor video display is enabled.
properties.value: true to enable output to multiple displays; false for single display. Default is false.

properties.name: Motion_DetectionEx
properties.summary: Gets or sets advanced motion and object detection configuration.
properties.value: MotionDetectionExSettings with AI-based detection parameters, or null to disable.

properties.name: ChromaKey
properties.summary: Gets or sets chroma key (green/blue screen) removal configuration.
properties.value: ChromaKeySettings object with color and tolerance values, or null to disable.

properties.name: Barcode_Reader_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether barcode and QR code detection is enabled.
properties.value: true to scan video frames for barcodes; false to disable scanning. Default is false.

properties.name: Barcode_Reader_Type
properties.summary: Gets or sets which types of barcodes to detect in video frames.
properties.value: BarcodeType flags indicating which barcode formats to scan for. Can combine multiple types using bitwise OR.

properties.name: Face_Tracking
properties.summary: Gets or sets face detection and tracking configuration.
properties.value: FaceTrackingSettings with detection parameters, or null to disable face tracking.

properties.name: MaximalSpeedPlayback
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to play media as fast as possible without timing constraints.
properties.value: true to disable frame timing and play at maximum speed; false for normal playback. Default is false.

properties.name: Encryption_Key
properties.summary: Sets the encryption key for playing protected media files.
properties.value: Can be: string (text key), byte[] (binary key), or string (path to key file). Type is determined by Encryption_KeyType property.

properties.name: Encryption_KeyType
properties.summary: Gets or sets how to interpret the Encryption_Key value.
properties.value: EncryptionKeyType: String, Binary, or File. Must match the key format provided in Encryption_Key.

properties.name: ReversePlayback_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether reverse (backwards) playback mode is enabled.
properties.value: true to play video in reverse; false for normal forward playback. Default is false.

properties.name: ReversePlayback_CacheSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the number of frames to cache for reverse playback performance.
properties.value: Number of frames to keep in memory. Larger values improve reverse playback smoothness but use more RAM. Default varies by video resolution.

properties.name: ConsoleUsage
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the SDK is being used in a console application.
properties.value: true for console/service applications; false for GUI applications. Default is false.

properties.name: CustomRedist_Path
properties.summary: Gets or sets the custom path for redistributable DirectShow filters and codecs.
properties.value: Full path to the folder containing .ax and .dll files, or null for default locations.

properties.name: CustomRedist_DisableDialog
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to suppress the missing codec warning dialog.
properties.value: true to disable the warning dialog; false to show it when codecs are missing. Default is false.

properties.name: CustomRedist_Auto
properties.summary: Gets or sets whether to automatically detect and use redistributable filters in the application folder.
properties.value: true to auto-detect filters in app folder and subfolders; false for manual configuration only. Default is true.

properties.name: CustomParameters
properties.summary: Gets or sets custom key-value parameters for advanced SDK configuration.
properties.value: Dictionary of parameter names and values for SDK customization.

properties.name: OSD_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets whether On-Screen Display (OSD) overlay system is enabled.
properties.value: true to enable OSD layer support; false to disable all overlays. Default is false.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_UseCustomAudioEffectsFilters
methods.summary: Registers custom audio effect filters for use in the media player by providing their CLSIDs (Class Identifiers). This method allows integration of third-party or custom DirectShow audio filters that are not built into the SDK.
methods.remarks: Use this method when you need to apply specialized audio processing that is not available through the built-in effects.Example usage: var customFilters = new List<Guid> { new Guid("12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012"), // Custom filter for stream 0 new Guid("87654321-4321-4321-4321-210987654321") // Custom filter for stream 1 }; player.Audio_Effects_UseCustomAudioEffectsFilters(customFilters);

parameters.name: clsidList
parameters.summary: List of CLSIDs (GUIDs) for custom audio filters. Each CLSID corresponds to a registered DirectShow filter. The number of CLSIDs should match the number of audio streams you want to apply custom effects to.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Add
methods.summary: Adds a new audio effect to the specified audio stream with timing control. Effects can be enabled/disabled and configured to activate only during specific time intervals of playback.
methods.remarks: Effects are processed in the order they are added to the stream.Example: Add a reverb effect that activates 10 seconds into playback: player.Audio_Effects_Add(0, AudioEffectType.Reverb, "myReverb", true, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10), TimeSpan.MaxValue);

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Index of the audio stream to apply the effect to (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams). Use -1 to apply the same effect to all available audio streams simultaneously.

parameters.name: effectType
parameters.summary: Type of audio effect to add (e.g., Amplify, Equalizer, Reverb, etc.). See AudioEffectType enumeration for all available effect types.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: Unique identifier name for this effect instance. Used to reference this specific effect when modifying parameters or removing it. Must be unique within the stream.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.summary: Initial enabled state of the effect. Set to true to immediately activate the effect, or false to add it in a disabled state (can be enabled later using Audio_Effects_Enable).

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: Time offset from the beginning of playback when the effect should automatically activate. Use TimeSpan.Zero to start immediately.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: Time offset from the beginning of playback when the effect should automatically deactivate. Use TimeSpan.MaxValue to keep the effect active until the end of playback.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Amplify
methods.summary: Configures the amplification (volume boost) effect for the specified audio stream. This effect allows precise control over audio volume levels with support for per-channel amplification.
methods.remarks: Be careful with high amplification values as they can cause audio clipping and distortion.Example: Boost volume by 50%: // First add the effect player.Audio_Effects_Add(0, AudioEffectType.Amplify, "volumeBoost", true, TimeSpan.Zero, TimeSpan.MaxValue); // Then configure it player.Audio_Effects_Amplify(0, "volumeBoost", 15000, false);

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Index of the audio stream to configure (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams).

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique identifier name of the amplify effect to configure. This must match the name used when adding the effect with Audio_Effects_Add.

parameters.name: volume
parameters.summary: Amplification level where 10000 = 1.0x (no change), 20000 = 2.0x (double volume), 5000 = 0.5x (half volume). Valid range: 0 to 100000 (0x to 10x amplification)Common values:10000 - Original volume (1.0x)15000 - 50% louder (1.5x)20000 - Double volume (2.0x)5000 - Half volume (0.5x)

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: When true, each audio channel can have its own amplification value. When false, all channels use the same amplification value (from channel 0). Use separate=true for stereo effects or multi-channel audio processing.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_BandPass
methods.summary: Configures a band-pass filter effect that allows only frequencies within a specified range to pass through while attenuating frequencies outside this range. Useful for isolating specific frequency bands in audio.
methods.remarks: Band-pass filters are commonly used for:Voice isolation (300 Hz - 3000 Hz)Instrument isolation in mixingRemoving unwanted noise outside a frequency rangeCreating "telephone" or "radio" voice effectsExample: Create a "telephone voice" effect: // Add band-pass effect player.Audio_Effects_Add(0, AudioEffectType.BandPass, "phoneVoice", true, TimeSpan.Zero, TimeSpan.MaxValue); // Configure for typical telephone frequency range player.Audio_Effects_BandPass(0, "phoneVoice", 3400, 300, false);

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Index of the audio stream to configure (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams).

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique identifier name of the band-pass effect to configure. This must match the name used when adding the effect with Audio_Effects_Add.

parameters.name: cutOffHigh
parameters.summary: Upper frequency limit in Hz. Frequencies above this value will be attenuated. Typical range: 100 Hz to 20000 HzCommon values: 8000 Hz (voice), 15000 Hz (most instruments)

parameters.name: cutOffLow
parameters.summary: Lower frequency limit in Hz. Frequencies below this value will be attenuated. Typical range: 20 Hz to 10000 HzCommon values: 80 Hz (remove rumble), 300 Hz (voice fundamentals)

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: When true, each audio channel can have different cutoff frequencies. When false, all channels use the same frequency range. Use separate=true for creative stereo effects.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_ChannelOrderEx
methods.summary: Configures channel routing/remapping for multi-channel audio. This effect allows you to rearrange, duplicate, or swap audio channels, useful for fixing incorrect channel mappings or creating special effects.
methods.remarks: Common use cases:Swap left/right stereo channelsConvert mono to stereo by duplicatingExtract single channel from multi-channel audioFix 5.1/7.1 surround sound channel mappingsExample: Swap left and right stereo channels: // Add channel order effect player.Audio_Effects_Add(0, AudioEffectType.ChannelOrder, "stereoSwap", true, TimeSpan.Zero, TimeSpan.MaxValue); // Configure to swap channels byte[,] swapOrder = new byte[,] { {0, 1}, {1, 0} }; // L→R, R→L player.Audio_Effects_ChannelOrderEx(0, "stereoSwap", swapOrder);

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Index of the audio stream to configure (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams).

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique identifier name of the channel order effect to configure. This must match the name used when adding the effect with Audio_Effects_Add.

parameters.name: orders
parameters.summary: A 2-dimensional byte array defining the channel mapping. Each row contains a pair: [target_channel, source_channel]. Array structure: orders[n,2] where n is the number of mappingsExample mappings:[0,1] - Route source channel 1 to target channel 0[1,0] - Route source channel 0 to target channel 1 (swap stereo)[0,0] and [1,0] - Duplicate channel 0 to both outputs (mono to stereo)

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Clear
methods.summary: Removes all audio effects from the specified audio stream. This completely clears the effects chain and restores the original unprocessed audio signal.
methods.remarks: This method immediately removes all effects including:All DSP effects (reverb, echo, chorus, etc.)All filters (equalizer, band-pass, etc.)All dynamic processors (compressor, limiter, etc.)Any custom effects added via CLSIDsNote: This action cannot be undone. To temporarily disable effects, use Audio_Effects_Enable instead.Example: // Clear all effects from stream 0 player.Audio_Effects_Clear(0); // Clear all effects from all streams player.Audio_Effects_Clear(-1);

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Index of the audio stream to clear (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams). Use -1 to remove all effects from all audio streams simultaneously.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Count
methods.summary: Returns the total number of audio effects currently applied to the specified audio stream. Useful for monitoring the effects chain or implementing effect limits.
methods.remarks: The count includes all effect types: built-in effects, DirectSound effects, and custom effects.Example: Check if effects are applied before clearing: int effectCount = player.Audio_Effects_Count(0); if (effectCount > 0) { Console.WriteLine($"Stream 0 has {effectCount} effects applied"); player.Audio_Effects_Clear(0); }

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Index of the audio stream to query (0-3). Note: This method does not support -1 for all streams; you must query each stream individually.

methods.returns: The number of effects currently in the effects chain for the specified stream. Returns 0 if no effects are applied or if the stream index is invalid.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_Chorus
methods.summary: Configures a DirectSound Chorus effect that creates a richer, fuller sound by simulating multiple voices or instruments playing in unison. The effect works by mixing the original signal with slightly delayed and pitch-modulated copies.
methods.remarks: Common chorus settings:Subtle thickening: delay=15, depth=10, feedback=0, frequency=1.1, wetDryMix=30Classic chorus: delay=30, depth=25, feedback=25, frequency=1.5, wetDryMix=50Extreme effect: delay=40, depth=100, feedback=50, frequency=5.0, wetDryMix=70 // Add and configure a classic chorus effect player.Audio_Effects_Add(0, AudioEffectType.DSChorus, "chorus", true, TimeSpan.Zero, TimeSpan.MaxValue); player.Audio_Effects_DS_Chorus(0, "chorus", 30.0f, 25.0f, 25.0f, 1.5f, DSChorusPhase.Phase_90, DSChorusWaveForm.Triangle, 50.0f);

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Index of the audio stream to configure (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams).

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique identifier name of the chorus effect to configure.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.summary: Base delay time in milliseconds (0.0 - 20.0). Controls the time offset of the chorus voices. Typical values: 10-25 ms for subtle chorus, 40-60 ms for pronounced effect

parameters.name: depth
parameters.summary: Modulation depth as percentage (0.0 - 100.0). Controls how much the delay time varies. Higher values create more dramatic pitch variations and "warbling"

parameters.name: feedback
parameters.summary: Feedback percentage (-99.0 to 99.0). Controls how much of the output is fed back to the input. Positive values create resonant effects, negative values create hollow effects

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.summary: LFO (Low Frequency Oscillator) rate in Hz (0.0 - 10.0). Controls the speed of delay modulation. Lower values (0.1-2.0) create slow, sweeping effects; higher values create vibrato

parameters.name: phase
parameters.summary: Phase relationship between channels (DSChorusPhase enum). Controls stereo width: Phase_Neg180 - Wide stereo imagePhase_Neg90 - Moderate stereo spreadPhase_Zero - Mono chorusPhase_90 - Moderate stereo spreadPhase_180 - Wide stereo image (inverted)

parameters.name: waveformTriangle
parameters.summary: LFO waveform shape (DSChorusWaveForm enum). Triangle waves sound smoother, sine waves sound more natural.

parameters.name: wetDryMix
parameters.summary: Balance between processed (wet) and original (dry) signal (0.0 - 100.0). 0 = dry only, 50 = equal mix, 100 = wet only

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_Compressor
methods.summary: Configures a DirectSound Compressor effect that reduces the dynamic range of audio by automatically lowering the volume of loud sounds while keeping quiet sounds unchanged. Essential for professional audio processing, broadcast limiting, and preventing clipping.
methods.remarks: Common compressor presets:Vocal: attack=5, gain=3, preDelay=0, ratio=3, release=100, threshold=-15Master bus: attack=10, gain=2, preDelay=0.5, ratio=2, release=200, threshold=-12Limiting: attack=0.1, gain=0, preDelay=1, ratio=20, release=50, threshold=-3Bass: attack=10, gain=4, preDelay=0, ratio=4, release=200, threshold=-20 // Add and configure compressor for vocals player.Audio_Effects_Add(0, AudioEffectType.DSCompressor, "vocalComp", true, TimeSpan.Zero, TimeSpan.MaxValue); player.Audio_Effects_DS_Compressor(0, "vocalComp", 5.0f, 3.0f, 0.0f, 3.0f, 100.0f, -15.0f);

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Index of the audio stream to configure (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams).

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique identifier name of the compressor effect to configure.

parameters.name: attack
parameters.summary: Attack time in milliseconds (0.01 - 500.0). How quickly the compressor responds to signals exceeding the threshold. Fast attack (0.1-10 ms): Catches transients but may sound unnaturalSlow attack (10-100 ms): Preserves transients but may miss peaks

parameters.name: gain
parameters.summary: Output gain in dB (-60.0 to 60.0). Compensates for volume reduction caused by compression. Typically set to restore perceived loudness after compression

parameters.name: preDelay
parameters.summary: Look-ahead time in milliseconds (0.0 - 4.0). Allows the compressor to "see" incoming peaks. Helps prevent transients from passing through uncompressed

parameters.name: ratio
parameters.summary: Compression ratio (1.0 - 100.0). Determines how much signals above threshold are reduced. 1:1 = No compression2:1 = Gentle compression (2 dB input = 1 dB output above threshold)4:1 = Moderate compression10:1 = Heavy compression20:1+ = Limiting

parameters.name: release
parameters.summary: Release time in milliseconds (50.0 - 3000.0). How quickly compression stops after signal drops below threshold. Fast release (50-100 ms): Responsive but may cause "pumping"Slow release (200-1000 ms): Smooth but may over-compress quiet passages

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.summary: Threshold level in dB (-60.0 to 0.0). Signal level at which compression begins. 0 dB = Compress everything-10 dB = Compress only loud peaks-20 to -30 dB = Typical for general compression

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_Distortion
methods.summary: Configures a DirectSound Distortion effect that adds harmonic content and "grit" to audio by clipping and shaping the waveform. Commonly used for electric guitar, bass, and creative sound design to add aggression, warmth, or lo-fi character to audio.
methods.remarks: The signal flow is: Input → Low-pass filter → Gain → Distortion → EQ → OutputCommon distortion presets:Warm overdrive: edge=15, gain=-15, postEQBandwidth=1000, postEQCenterFrequency=800, preLowpassCutOff=3000Rock distortion: edge=50, gain=-10, postEQBandwidth=2000, postEQCenterFrequency=2000, preLowpassCutOff=5000Fuzz bass: edge=80, gain=-5, postEQBandwidth=500, postEQCenterFrequency=250, preLowpassCutOff=1000Lo-fi effect: edge=30, gain=-20, postEQBandwidth=3000, postEQCenterFrequency=1500, preLowpassCutOff=2000 // Add and configure rock guitar distortion player.Audio_Effects_Add(0, AudioEffectType.DSDistortion, "rockDist", true, TimeSpan.Zero, TimeSpan.MaxValue); player.Audio_Effects_DS_Distortion(0, "rockDist", 50.0f, -10.0f, 2000.0f, 2000.0f, 5000.0f);

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Index of the audio stream to configure (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams).

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique identifier name of the distortion effect to configure.

parameters.name: edge
parameters.summary: Distortion intensity/hardness (0.0 - 100.0). Controls the sharpness of clipping. 0-20: Soft clipping, warm overdrive20-50: Moderate distortion, tube-like50-80: Hard distortion, aggressive80-100: Extreme clipping, fuzz effect

parameters.name: gain
parameters.summary: Pre-distortion gain in dB (-60.0 to 0.0). Input level before distortion. Higher values drive the distortion harder, creating more harmonicsTypical: -20 to -10 dB for moderate distortion

parameters.name: postEQBandwidth
parameters.summary: Post-distortion EQ bandwidth in Hz (100.0 - 8000.0). Width of frequency boost/cut. Narrow (100-500): Focused tone shapingWide (1000-8000): Broad tonal changes

parameters.name: postEQCenterFrequency
parameters.summary: Post-distortion EQ center frequency in Hz (100.0 - 8000.0). Frequency to boost/cut after distortion. 200-500 Hz: Adds body and warmth1000-2000 Hz: Adds presence and bite3000-5000 Hz: Adds brightness and edge

parameters.name: preLowpassCutOff
parameters.summary: Pre-distortion low-pass filter cutoff in Hz (100.0 - 8000.0). Removes high frequencies before distortion. Lower values (500-2000) create smoother, warmer distortionHigher values (4000-8000) preserve brightness and create harsher tones

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_Echo
methods.summary: Configures a DirectSound Echo effect that creates delayed repetitions of the audio signal. Unlike reverb, echo produces distinct, audible repetitions that can create spatial depth, rhythmic patterns, or psychedelic effects.
methods.remarks: Echo vs Reverb: Echo creates distinct repetitions, while reverb creates a wash of reflections.Common echo presets:Slapback: leftDelay=120, rightDelay=120, feedback=15, panDelay=0, wetDryMix=30Stereo spread: leftDelay=250, rightDelay=375, feedback=40, panDelay=0, wetDryMix=35Ping-pong: leftDelay=500, rightDelay=500, feedback=50, panDelay=1, wetDryMix=40Ambient: leftDelay=1000, rightDelay=1500, feedback=70, panDelay=0, wetDryMix=60 // Add and configure ping-pong echo player.Audio_Effects_Add(0, AudioEffectType.DSEcho, "pingPong", true, TimeSpan.Zero, TimeSpan.MaxValue); player.Audio_Effects_DS_Echo(0, "pingPong", 50.0f, 500.0f, 500.0f, 1, 40.0f);

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Index of the audio stream to configure (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams).

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique identifier name of the echo effect to configure.

parameters.name: feedback
parameters.summary: Feedback percentage (0.0 - 100.0). Controls how much of the echo output is fed back into the input. 0-30: Single or few echoes that fade quickly30-60: Multiple echoes with moderate decay60-90: Many echoes with slow decay90-100: Near-infinite echoes (use carefully to avoid feedback loops)

parameters.name: leftDelay
parameters.summary: Left channel delay in milliseconds (1.0 - 2000.0). Time between original sound and echo. Common values:50-150 ms: Slapback echo (rockabilly vocals)200-400 ms: Quarter/eighth note echoes at typical tempos500-1000 ms: Long echoes for ambient effects

parameters.name: rightDelay
parameters.summary: Right channel delay in milliseconds (1.0 - 2000.0). Can differ from left for stereo effects. Set equal to leftDelay for mono echo, or vary for ping-pong effects

parameters.name: panDelay
parameters.summary: Stereo ping-pong mode (0 or 1). When enabled, echoes alternate between left and right channels. 0 = Normal stereo echo, 1 = Ping-pong echo effect

parameters.name: wetDryMix
parameters.summary: Balance between processed (wet) and original (dry) signal (0.0 - 100.0). 0 = dry only, 50 = equal mix, 100 = wet onlyTypical: 20-40 for subtle echo, 50-70 for prominent effect

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_Flanger
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Flanger effect.
methods.remarks: Flange, also called flanger, is an echo effect in which the delay between the original signal and its echo is very short and varies over time. The result is sometimes referred to as a sweeping sound. The term flange originated with the practice of grabbing the flanges of a tape reel to change the speed.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.summary: Specifies the delay of the filter (0.0 - 4.0).

parameters.name: depth
parameters.summary: Specifies the depth of the filter (0.0 - 100.0).

parameters.name: feedback
parameters.summary: Specifies the feedback of the filter (-99.0 - 99.0).

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.summary: Specifies the frequency of the filter (0.0 - 10.0).

parameters.name: waveform
parameters.summary: Specifies the waveform type of the filter.

parameters.name: wetDryMix
parameters.summary: Specifies the wet and dry mix of the filter (0.0 - 100.0).

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_Gargle
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Gargle effect.
methods.remarks: The gargle effect modulates the amplitude of the signal.

parameters.name: rateHz
parameters.summary: Specifies the frequency of the gargle filter (1 - 1000).

parameters.name: waveForm
parameters.summary: Specifies the waveform type of the filter.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_ParamEQ
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS ParamEQ effect.
methods.remarks: A parametric equalizer amplifies or attenuates signals of a given frequency. Parametric equalizer effects for different pitches can be applied in parallel by setting multiple instances of the effect on the same buffer. In this way, the application can have tone control similar to that provided by a hardware equalizer.

parameters.name: bandwidth
parameters.summary: Specifies the bandwidth of the equalizer (1.0 - 36.0).

parameters.name: center
parameters.summary: Specifies the center frequency of the equalizer (80.0 - 16000.0).

parameters.name: gain
parameters.summary: Specifies the gain of the equalizer (-15.0 - 15.0).

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_Reverb
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Reverb effect.
methods.remarks: Environmental Reverberation filter.

parameters.name: decayHFRatio
parameters.summary: Specifies the decay HF ratio for the filter (0.1 - 2.0, 0.83 by default).

parameters.name: decayTime
parameters.summary: Specifies the decay time for the filter (0.1 - 20.0, 1.49 by default).

parameters.name: density
parameters.summary: Specifies the density value for the filter (0 - 100.0, 100.0 by default).

parameters.name: diffusion
parameters.summary: Specifies the diffusion value for the filter (0 - 100.0, 100.0 by default).

parameters.name: HFReference
parameters.summary: Specifies the HF reference for the filter (20.0 - 20000.0, 5000.0 by default).

parameters.name: quality
parameters.summary: Specifies the quality of the filter (0 - 3, 2 by default).

parameters.name: reflections
parameters.summary: Specifies the reflections value for the filter (-10000 - -1000, -2602 by default).

parameters.name: reflectionsDelay
parameters.summary: Specifies the reflections delay for the filter (0.0 - 0.3, 0.007 by default).

parameters.name: reverbValue
parameters.summary: Specifies the reverb value for the filter (-10000 - 2000, 200 by default).

parameters.name: reverbDelay
parameters.summary: Specifies the reverb delay for the filter (0.0 - 0.1, 0.011 by default).

parameters.name: room
parameters.summary: Specifies the room value for the filter (-10000 - 0, -1000 by default).

parameters.name: roomHF
parameters.summary: Specifies the room HF value of the filter (-10000 - 0, -100 by default).

parameters.name: roomRollOffFactor
parameters.summary: Specifies the room roll off factor for the filter (0.0 - 10.0, 0.0 by default).

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_WavesReverb
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Waves Reverb effect.
methods.remarks: The waves reverberation effect is intended for use with music. The waves reverberation DirectX Media Object (DMO) is based on the Waves MaxxVerb technology, which is licensed to Microsoft.

parameters.name: highFreqRTRatio
parameters.summary: Specifies the high frequency ratio (0.001 - 0.999, 0.001 by default).

parameters.name: inGain
parameters.summary: Specifies in-gain of the filter (-96.0 - 0.0, 0.0 by default).

parameters.name: reverbMix
parameters.summary: Specifies the reverb mix of the filter (-96.0 - 0.0, 0.0 by default).

parameters.name: reverbTime
parameters.summary: Specifies the reverb time of the filter (0.001 - 3000.0, 1000.0 by default).

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DynamicAmplify
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the Dynamic Amplify effect.
methods.remarks: DSP Filter to automatically keep the volume eat a specific maximum value.

parameters.name: attackTime
parameters.summary: Specifies the amplification value than will be used when amplifying.

parameters.name: maxAmplification
parameters.summary: Sets the amplification for a channel. Default value is 10000, which means that no amplification occurs. A value of 20000 raises the amplification by 2.

parameters.name: releaseTime
parameters.summary: Specifies the time in milliseconds that the DSP will wait to continue amplification, after the maximum has been reached.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DynamicAmplify_GetCurrentAmp
methods.summary: Gets the value for the current amplification level.
methods.returns: System.Double.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Enable
methods.summary: Enables or disables a specific audio effect without removing it from the effects chain. This allows you to temporarily bypass effects while preserving their configuration.
methods.remarks: This method is useful for:A/B testing effects by toggling them on/offCreating effect presets that can be enabled on demandTemporarily bypassing CPU-intensive effectsBuilding effect automation systemsExample: Toggle reverb on/off during playback: // Add reverb but start disabled player.Audio_Effects_Add(0, AudioEffectType.Reverb, "reverb", false, TimeSpan.Zero, TimeSpan.MaxValue); // Configure reverb parameters... // Later, enable reverb player.Audio_Effects_Enable(0, "reverb", true); // Disable reverb again player.Audio_Effects_Enable(0, "reverb", false);

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Index of the audio stream containing the effect (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams).

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique identifier name of the effect to enable/disable. Must match the name used when the effect was added with Audio_Effects_Add.

parameters.name: enable

parameters.name: separate

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Equalizer_Preset_Set

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Equalizer
methods.summary: Configures a multi-band graphic equalizer effect for precise frequency control. This professional-grade equalizer supports up to 4096 frequency bands, allowing detailed spectral shaping of audio.
methods.remarks: The equalizer uses FFT-based processing with these band options:10 bands: Basic tone control (typical graphic EQ)31 bands: Professional 1/3 octave equalizer128+ bands: Surgical precision for masteringUp to 4096 bands: Ultra-precise spectral controlAfter adding the equalizer, use Audio_Effects_Equalizer_Band_Set to adjust individual bands, or Audio_Effects_Equalizer_Preset_Set to apply standard presets. // Add and configure 10-band equalizer player.Audio_Effects_Add(0, AudioEffectType.Equalizer, "eq10", true, TimeSpan.Zero, TimeSpan.MaxValue); player.Audio_Effects_Equalizer(0, "eq10", false, 12.0f); // Boost bass and treble (smile curve) player.Audio_Effects_Equalizer_Band_Set(0, "eq10", 0, 60); // +6dB at low freq player.Audio_Effects_Equalizer_Band_Set(0, "eq10", 9, 40); // +4dB at high freq

parameters.name: name

parameters.name: separate

parameters.name: maxGainDB
parameters.summary: Maximum gain/attenuation range in decibels (default: 20.0 dB). Common ranges:6 dB: Subtle adjustments, mastering12 dB: Moderate control, mixing20 dB: Full control, corrective EQ30 dB: Extreme adjustments, special effects
