methods.name: DVD_Chapter_GetCurrent
methods.summary: Gets the current chapter number being played in the active DVD title.
methods.remarks: DVD chapters are segments within a title (movie). Most DVDs organize content into titles and chapters for easy navigation, similar to chapters in a book.Use DVD_Chapter_GetCurrent in combination with chapter navigation methods like DVD_Chapter_Next or DVD_Chapter_Select to implement custom DVD navigation controls.
methods.returns: Zero-based index of the current chapter. Returns -1 if no chapter is playing or DVD is not loaded. For example, if playing chapter 3, this returns 2.

methods.name: DVD_Chapter_NextAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously navigates to and plays the next chapter in the current DVD title.
methods.remarks: This method is for use with async/await patterns. For synchronous operation, use DVD_Chapter_Next.If currently playing the last chapter of a title, this method will return false and playback continues.Example usage: bool success = await player.DVD_Chapter_NextAsync(); if (!success) { Console.WriteLine("Cannot skip to next chapter - possibly at end of title"); }
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if navigation was successful, false if failed (e.g., already at last chapter or DVD error).

methods.name: DVD_Chapter_Next
methods.summary: Navigates to and plays the next chapter in the current DVD title.
methods.remarks: This is the synchronous version. For async operations, use DVD_Chapter_NextAsync.Common usage scenario for implementing "Next Chapter" button: private void btnNextChapter_Click(object sender, EventArgs e) { if (!player.DVD_Chapter_Next()) { MessageBox.Show("Cannot skip to next chapter"); } }
methods.returns: True if navigation was successful, false if failed (e.g., already at last chapter, DVD not playing, or navigation error).

methods.name: DVD_Chapter_NextIntl
methods.summary: Play next chapter (intl).
methods.returns: true if successful, false otherwise.

methods.name: DVD_Chapter_PrevAsync
methods.summary: Play previous chapter (async).
methods.returns: Task<System.Boolean>.

methods.name: DVD_Chapter_Prev
methods.summary: Navigates to and plays the previous chapter in the current DVD title.
methods.remarks: This is the synchronous version. For async operations, use DVD_Chapter_PrevAsync.If currently at the beginning of a chapter, this will jump to the start of the previous chapter. If at the first chapter, the method returns false and playback continues.Example implementation of chapter navigation controls: private void btnPrevChapter_Click(object sender, EventArgs e) { if (!player.DVD_Chapter_Prev()) { MessageBox.Show("Already at first chapter"); } }
methods.returns: True if navigation was successful, false if failed (e.g., already at first chapter, DVD not playing, or navigation error).

methods.name: DVD_Chapter_PrevIntl
methods.summary: Play previous chapter (intl).
methods.returns: Returns Boolean.

methods.name: DVD_Chapter_ReplayAsync
methods.summary: Replay current chapter (async).
methods.returns: Task<System.Boolean>.

methods.name: DVD_Chapter_Replay
methods.summary: Restarts playback from the beginning of the current chapter.
methods.remarks: This is useful for implementing a "replay chapter" feature or returning to the start of a chapter after seeking within it.The playback position will jump to the beginning of the current chapter and continue playing.Example usage: // Replay current chapter when user presses a hotkey private void OnReplayHotkey() { if (player.DVD_Chapter_Replay()) { statusLabel.Text = "Chapter restarted"; } }
methods.returns: True if the chapter was successfully restarted, false if the operation failed (e.g., DVD not playing or navigation error).

methods.name: DVD_Chapter_ReplayIntl
methods.summary: Replay current chapter (intl).
methods.returns: Returns Boolean.

methods.name: DVD_Chapter_SelectAsync
methods.summary: Starts playback from the specified chapter in the current title (async).
methods.returns: Returns Task.

methods.name: DVD_Chapter_Select
methods.summary: Jumps to and starts playback from a specific chapter within the current DVD title.
methods.remarks: This method allows direct chapter access, useful for implementing chapter selection menus or bookmarking functionality.If the specified chapter index is invalid (out of range), the DVD navigator may ignore the request or generate an error event.Example: Create a chapter selection menu: // Populate chapter list (assuming you know the chapter count) for (int i = 0; i < chapterCount; i++) { listBoxChapters.Items.Add($"Chapter {i + 1}"); } // Handle chapter selection private void listBoxChapters_SelectedIndexChanged(object sender, EventArgs e) { player.DVD_Chapter_Select(listBoxChapters.SelectedIndex); }

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: Zero-based chapter index to play. For example, 0 for first chapter, 1 for second chapter, etc. Must be a valid chapter index within the current title.

methods.name: DVD_Chapter_SelectIntl
methods.summary: Starts playback from the specified chapter in the current title (intl).

methods.name: DVD_Menu_ResumePlaybackAsync
methods.summary: Replay current chapter (async).
methods.returns: Task<System.Boolean>.

methods.name: DVD_Menu_ResumePlayback
methods.summary: Replay current chapter.
methods.returns: Returns Boolean.

methods.name: DVD_Menu_ResumePlaybackIntl
methods.summary: Replay current chapter (intl).
methods.returns: Returns Boolean.

methods.name: DVD_Menu_ShowAsync
methods.summary: Displays the specified menu, if available (async).
methods.returns: Task<System.Boolean>.

methods.name: DVD_Menu_Show
methods.summary: Displays the specified DVD menu (main menu, chapter selection, audio options, etc.) if available on the disc.
methods.remarks: Not all DVDs contain all menu types. Calling this method for an unavailable menu will return false.When a menu is displayed, use mouse clicks or DVD navigation commands to interact with it.Example: Implement DVD menu buttons: private void btnMainMenu_Click(object sender, EventArgs e) { if (!player.DVD_Menu_Show(DVDMenu.Title)) { MessageBox.Show("Main menu not available on this DVD"); } } private void btnChapterMenu_Click(object sender, EventArgs e) { player.DVD_Menu_Show(DVDMenu.Chapter); }

parameters.name: menuType
parameters.summary: The type of DVD menu to display (DVDMenu enumeration). Common types include: Title - Main/Top menu of the DVDRoot - Root menu (often same as Title)Chapter - Chapter selection menuAudio - Audio track selection menuSubpicture - Subtitle selection menuAngle - Camera angle selection (for multi-angle DVDs)

methods.returns: True if the menu was successfully displayed, false if the menu is not available on this DVD or if navigation failed.

methods.name: DVD_Menu_ShowIntl
methods.summary: Displays the specified menu, if available.
methods.returns: Returns Boolean.

methods.name: DVD_Select_AudioStreamAsync
methods.summary: Selects the audio stream to play (async).
methods.returns: Returns Task.

methods.name: DVD_Select_AudioStream
methods.summary: Selects which audio stream (language track) to play from the available audio streams on the DVD.
methods.remarks: DVDs often contain multiple audio tracks for different languages, commentary tracks, or different audio formats (stereo, 5.1 surround, etc.).Use the DVD info methods to query available audio streams before selection.The change takes effect immediately during playback.Example: Create an audio track selector: // Get available audio streams (pseudo-code - use actual DVD info methods) var audioStreams = GetDVDAudioStreams(); // Populate audio menu for (int i = 0; i < audioStreams.Count; i++) { comboAudio.Items.Add($"{audioStreams[i].Language} - {audioStreams[i].Format}"); } // Handle selection private void comboAudio_SelectedIndexChanged(object sender, EventArgs e) { player.DVD_Select_AudioStream(comboAudio.SelectedIndex); }

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the audio stream to activate. The number and type of available streams depends on the DVD content. Common examples: 0 - Primary language (often English)1 - Secondary language (e.g., Spanish, French)2+ - Additional languages or commentary tracks

methods.name: DVD_Select_AudioStreamIntl
methods.summary: Selects the audio stream to play.

methods.name: DVD_Select_SubpictureStreamAsync
methods.summary: Method sets the subpicture stream to display (async).
methods.returns: Returns Task.

methods.name: DVD_Select_SubpictureStream
methods.summary: Selects which subpicture (subtitle) stream to display, or disables subtitles entirely.
methods.remarks: DVD subpictures include subtitles, captions, and sometimes karaoke lyrics or director's notes.Not all DVDs include subtitle streams. The availability and languages depend on the disc.Subtitles are overlaid on the video during playback and can be turned on/off at any time.Example: Implement subtitle controls: // Turn off subtitles player.DVD_Select_SubpictureStream(-1); // Enable first subtitle stream (usually primary language) player.DVD_Select_SubpictureStream(0); // Create subtitle menu private void PopulateSubtitleMenu() { comboSubtitles.Items.Add("Off"); comboSubtitles.Items.Add("English"); comboSubtitles.Items.Add("Spanish"); comboSubtitles.Items.Add("French"); } private void comboSubtitles_SelectedIndexChanged(object sender, EventArgs e) { player.DVD_Select_SubpictureStream(comboSubtitles.SelectedIndex - 1); }

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the subtitle stream to display, or -1 to disable all subtitles. Common subtitle streams include: 0 - Primary subtitle language1+ - Additional subtitle languages-1 - Turn off all subtitles

methods.name: DVD_Select_SubpictureStreamIntl
methods.summary: Method sets the subpicture stream to display (intl).

methods.name: DVD_SetDisplayModeAsync
methods.summary: Sets the specified video mode display (wide screen, letterbox, or pan-scan) for playback (async).
methods.returns: Returns Task.

methods.name: DVD_SetDisplayMode
methods.summary: Sets the video display mode for DVD playback, controlling how widescreen content is displayed on different aspect ratio screens.
methods.remarks: This setting affects how anamorphic (widescreen) DVDs are displayed. The actual result depends on both this setting and the DVD's encoding.Modern displays are typically 16:9, but older content may be 4:3. This method helps adapt content to different display aspect ratios.Example: Let users choose their preferred display mode: private void RadioButtonDisplayMode_CheckedChanged(object sender, EventArgs e) { if (radioLetterbox.Checked) player.DVD_SetDisplayMode(DVDDisplayMode.LetterBox); else if (radioPanScan.Checked) player.DVD_SetDisplayMode(DVDDisplayMode.PanScan); else if (radioFullScreen.Checked) player.DVD_SetDisplayMode(DVDDisplayMode.FullScreen); }

parameters.name: mode
parameters.summary: The display mode to use (DVDDisplayMode enumeration): FullScreen - Stretches video to fill the entire display (may distort aspect ratio)LetterBox - Preserves aspect ratio with black bars on top/bottom for widescreen content on 4:3 displaysPanScan - Crops sides of widescreen content to fill 4:3 display (may lose picture information)Original - Uses the DVD's default display mode

methods.name: DVD_SetDisplayModeIntl
methods.summary: Sets the specified video mode display (wide screen, letterbox, or pan-scan) for playback.

methods.name: DVD_SetSpeedAsync
methods.summary: Plays forward / backward at the specified speed from the current location (async).

parameters.name: backward
parameters.summary: false for forward playback, true for backward playback.

methods.returns: Task<System.Boolean>.

methods.name: DVD_SetSpeed
methods.summary: Controls DVD playback speed and direction, allowing fast forward, slow motion, and reverse playback.
methods.remarks: DVD players typically support specific speed increments (1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x, 32x). Requesting unsupported speeds may result in the nearest supported speed being used.Audio is typically muted during fast forward/rewind operations.Example: Implement transport controls: // Fast forward private void btnFastForward_Click(object sender, EventArgs e) { currentSpeed *= 2; if (currentSpeed > 32) currentSpeed = 32; player.DVD_SetSpeed(currentSpeed, false); } // Rewind private void btnRewind_Click(object sender, EventArgs e) { player.DVD_SetSpeed(4.0, true); } // Resume normal playback private void btnPlay_Click(object sender, EventArgs e) { player.DVD_SetSpeed(1.0, false); currentSpeed = 1.0; }

parameters.name: speed
parameters.summary: Playback speed multiplier. Common values: 0.5 - Half speed (slow motion)1.0 - Normal speed2.0 - Double speed (2x fast forward)4.0 - 4x fast forward8.0 - 8x fast forward Actual supported speeds depend on the DVD and decoder capabilities.

parameters.name: backward
parameters.summary: False for forward playback, true for reverse/backward playback. Note: Not all DVDs or decoders support reverse playback.

methods.returns: True if the speed change was successful, false if the requested speed/direction is not supported or if an error occurred.

methods.name: DVD_SetSpeedIntl
methods.summary: Plays forward / backward at the specified speed from the current location.

parameters.name: backward
parameters.summary: false for forward playback, true for backward playback.

methods.returns: Returns Boolean.

methods.name: DVD_Title_GetCurrent
methods.summary: Gets the current DVD title number being played.
methods.remarks: DVD titles are major sections of content on a disc. Typically:Title 1 (index 0) - Main feature filmTitle 2+ - Special features, trailers, deleted scenes, etc.Each title can contain multiple chapters for navigation within that content.Use this with DVD_Title_Play to implement title selection features.
methods.returns: Zero-based index of the current title. Returns -1 if no title is playing or DVD is not loaded. For example, if playing title 1 (the main movie), this returns 0.

methods.name: DVD_Title_GetDurationAsync
methods.summary: Returns current title duration (async).
methods.returns: Task<TimeSpan>.

methods.name: DVD_Title_GetDuration
methods.summary: Gets the total duration/length of the current DVD title.
methods.remarks: This returns the full duration of the entire title, not just the current chapter.Duration information may not be available immediately after starting playback. Wait for the DVD to fully initialize before querying duration.Example: Display title duration in UI: private void UpdateDurationDisplay() { TimeSpan duration = player.DVD_Title_GetDuration(); if (duration != TimeSpan.Zero) { labelDuration.Text = $"Duration: {duration:hh\\:mm\\:ss}"; } else { labelDuration.Text = "Duration: Unknown"; } }
methods.returns: A TimeSpan representing the total duration of the current title. Returns TimeSpan.Zero if no title is playing, duration cannot be determined, or an error occurs.

methods.name: DVD_Title_GetDurationIntl
methods.summary: Returns current title duration (intl).
methods.returns: The TimeSpan.

methods.name: DVD_Title_PlayAsync
methods.summary: Starts playback from the first chapter in the specified title (async).
methods.returns: Returns Task.

methods.name: DVD_Title_Play
methods.summary: Starts DVD playback from the beginning of the specified title (e.g., main movie, special features).
methods.remarks: This method jumps directly to a title, bypassing any menus. Playback begins at chapter 1 of the selected title.To get available titles, use DVD info methods to enumerate title count and information.If the specified title doesn't exist, the DVD navigator may play the default title or generate an error.Example: Create a title selection menu: // Populate title list private void PopulateTitleList() { int titleCount = GetDVDTitleCount(); // Use actual DVD info method listBoxTitles.Items.Clear(); listBoxTitles.Items.Add("Main Movie"); for (int i = 1; i < titleCount; i++) { listBoxTitles.Items.Add($"Special Feature {i}"); } } // Play selected title private void btnPlayTitle_Click(object sender, EventArgs e) { if (listBoxTitles.SelectedIndex >= 0) { player.DVD_Title_Play(listBoxTitles.SelectedIndex); } }

parameters.name: titleIndex
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the title to play. Common titles: 0 - Usually the main feature film1+ - Special features, deleted scenes, trailers, etc. The actual content of each title varies by DVD.

methods.name: DVD_Title_PlayIntl
methods.summary: Starts playback from the first chapter in the specified title.

methods.name: DVDAdd
methods.summary: Initializes and configures the DVD source filter for playback. This method sets up the complete DVD playback pipeline including the DVD Navigator, video/audio decoders, renderers, and effects.
methods.remarks: This method performs the following operations:Creates and configures the DVD Navigator filterSets up IDvdInfo2 and IDvdControl2 interfaces for DVD controlConfigures custom video/audio decoders if specifiedSets up video effects and rendering pipelineConfigures audio processing and effectsInitializes DVD-specific options like HMSF timecode eventsCalled internally during DVD playback initialization.

methods.name: DVDSubpictureConfigure
methods.summary: Configures the DVD subpicture (subtitle) stream connections in the filter graph. Handles the routing of subpicture data from the DVD source through decoders to the video renderer.
methods.remarks: DVD subpictures include:Subtitles in various languagesClosed captions (Line21 data)Menu highlights and overlaysKaraoke lyrics or other overlay graphicsThis method ensures proper connection of subpicture streams through the decoder to the video renderer for overlay display.

methods.name: DVDAudioConfigure
methods.summary: Configures the complete DVD audio pipeline including custom decoders, audio renderers, effects processors, and audio analysis components.
methods.remarks: This method handles:Custom audio decoder setup (if specified)Audio format detection (AC3, MPEG, etc.)Audio renderer configuration based on playback modeAudio effects chain initializationVU meter and audio analysis setupChannel mapping and audio enhancementDVD audio can include multiple formats like Dolby AC3, DTS, MPEG audio, or LPCM. The method automatically detects and configures the appropriate decoder.

methods.name: IsSourceConnected
methods.summary: Always returns true: a media player has no capture source to wait on, so consumers (such as VideoView) must not draw a "no signal" overlay over it. Implements IsSourceConnected.

methods.name: AddFilterGraph
methods.summary: Initializes and configures the DirectShow filter graph infrastructure. This is the foundation of all media playback, creating the graph builder, capture graph builder, and querying essential interfaces.
methods.remarks: This method sets up:IFilterGraph2 - Main filter graph managerICaptureGraphBuilder2 - Helper for building filter graphsIMediaControl - Start/stop/pause controlIMediaSeeking - Seeking and duration queriesIMediaEventEx - Event notificationsIVideoFrameStep - Frame stepping supportAlso configures blacklisted filters if specified to avoid problematic codecs.

methods.name: PlaylistPlayDelegateDelegateMethod
methods.summary: Plays the playlist file the end of the previous one stepped to.

methods.name: OnDSEventCodeDVDProcess
methods.summary: Processes DVD-specific DirectShow events including navigation, errors, warnings, and playback state changes. This method handles all DVD event notifications from the DirectShow event queue.
methods.remarks: Handles events such as:Time updates (current playback position)Chapter changesTitle changesDomain changes (menu vs. content)Parental level restrictionsCopy protection and region errorsFormat compatibility warningsThis method updates internal state and raises corresponding events for the application to handle.

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: Event arguments containing the DirectShow event code and parameters. Different DVD events carry information about chapters, titles, menus, errors, and navigation state.

methods.name: SeekToSelection
methods.summary: Seeks the graph to the selection start (the start of the file with no selection), and sets the selection's stop where one is wanted. A stop of zero or below ("to the end of the file", #2116) or no selection leaves the graph's stop alone or, when an earlier selection's stop was sent, lifts it by sending long.MaxValue; a VLC source that took the stop on its command line keeps its --stop-time. A selection whose stop is at or before its start is not sent (#2276).

parameters.name: invertedSelection
parameters.summary: The error for an inverted selection, or null when the seek was sent.

methods.returns: The HRESULT of the seek; E_INVALIDARG when nothing was sent.

methods.name: InvertedSelectionError
methods.summary: The error for an active selection whose stop is at or before its start (#2276): a source refuses such a stop or ends at once, and the error would otherwise name the source.
methods.returns: The message, or null when the selection is valid or not active.

methods.name: VlcSourceTakesStop
methods.summary: Whether the VLC source filter is 2026.10.7 or later, the first to act on the graph's stop position (#2248).
methods.returns: true for 2026.10.7 or later; false for an older filter, one without IVlcSrc4 included.

methods.name: FinishEndOfFile
methods.summary: The end of a file once its stop has run: refreshes the view and steps the playlist (#2076).

parameters.name: playlistMoves
parameters.summary: The playlist moves when that start was published.

parameters.name: drewIntoView
parameters.summary: Whether the file drew into the view's window.

methods.name: OnDSEventCode
methods.summary: OnDSEventCode event.

methods.name: Video_Stream_SelectAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously selects and activates a specific video stream from a multi-stream source.
methods.remarks: This method is useful for:Multi-angle DVD playbackFiles with multiple video tracks (e.g., different camera angles)Switching between main video and commentary tracksUse MediaInfo methods to enumerate available video streams before selection.See for how the index is stored and checked at Play.Example: // Switch to second video stream if available bool success = await player.Video_Stream_SelectAsync(1); if (!success) { Console.WriteLine("Failed to switch video stream"); }

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the video stream to activate. Use -1 to select the default/primary stream. For files with multiple video tracks (e.g., multi-angle DVDs, MKV files with multiple video streams), this allows switching between available video streams.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result is true if the stream was selected, or the index was stored while the player is stopped (it is checked at Play); false if the index is invalid, no video stream exists at that index, or selection failed.

methods.name: Video_Stream_Select
methods.summary: Selects and activates a specific video stream from a multi-stream source.
methods.remarks: This is the synchronous version. For async operations, use Video_Stream_SelectAsync.Common use cases include multi-angle DVDs, security camera recordings with multiple views, or educational content with different presentation tracks.The stream change takes effect immediately if playing (see the File_DS exception below), or will be applied when playback starts.While the player is stopped the index is stored without a check and kept across Stop and file changes; Play fails with an error if the file has no video stream at that index (Encrypted_File_DS without Multiple_Video_Streams_Mappings_Add does not use the index and skips the check); a file with no video stream plays its audio and ignores the index (in LAV and GPU modes a video output the splitter exposes, such as embedded cover art, counts as a video stream). A call made while Play is still starting can be rejected (call it again once Play has returned), and a call that returns false leaves the stored index unchanged.LAV, GPU and FFMPEG modes play the selected stream, and stream 0 when none was selected. File_DS does the same when its source filter or splitter can select streams (LAV Splitter Source, or LAV Splitter installed on the system). Other File_DS sources, File_VLC and CustomSource without Multiple_Video_Streams_Mappings_Add cannot switch the stream at Play: they show stream 0 and log a warning. During playback File_DS rejects a switch to a stream whose frame size differs from the one the video is connected with, or cannot be read, and, when the system MJPEG Decompressor decodes the video, a stream of another subtype or another bit count (another chroma subsampling, such as 4:4:4 against 4:2:0), or whose bit count cannot be read; select it before Play. Only these are checked: subsamplings of the same bit count (4:1:1 and 4:2:0, 4:2:2 and 4:4:0) are not told apart.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the video stream to activate. Use -1 to select the default/primary stream. For files with multiple video tracks, this allows switching between available video streams.

methods.returns: True if the stream was selected, or the index was stored while the player is stopped (it is checked at Play); false if the index is invalid, no video stream exists at that index, or selection failed.

methods.name: ReversePlayback_GoToFrame
methods.summary: Navigates to a specific frame number during reverse playback mode. This method provides frame-accurate positioning when playing media in reverse.
methods.remarks: Reverse playback requires special handling because most video codecs only support forward decoding. This method works with a frame cache built during reverse playback.Prerequisites:Media must be loaded and reverse playback mode activeFrame must be within the cached rangeSufficient memory for frame cachingNote: Reverse playback is resource-intensive and may not work smoothly with all video formats, especially those with long GOP structures.

parameters.name: number
parameters.summary: Zero-based frame number to navigate to, 0 being the oldest cached frame. A negative number is reported through OnError and changes nothing; for a number past the frames cached so far playback is paused, as by any call of this method, but nothing is drawn and no error is reported.

methods.name: ReversePlayback_PreviousFrame
methods.summary: Moves to the previous frame during reverse playback or frame-stepping mode. Provides frame-by-frame backward navigation through video content.
methods.remarks: This method is useful for:Frame-accurate video editing and analysisSlow-motion reverse playback implementationFinding exact cut points when editingSports or scientific video analysisPerformance depends on the video codec and GOP structure. Formats with frequent keyframes (like Motion JPEG) perform better than long-GOP formats (like H.264).Example usage: // Implement frame-by-frame reverse navigation private void btnPreviousFrame_Click(object sender, EventArgs e) { player.Pause(); player.ReversePlayback_PreviousFrame(); UpdateFrameDisplay(); }

methods.name: ReversePlayback_NextFrame
methods.summary: Advances to the next frame during reverse playback mode or returns to forward direction. Provides frame-by-frame forward navigation even when in reverse playback mode.
methods.remarks: When in reverse playback mode, this method moves forward one frame, which can be used to fine-tune position after reverse seeking.Common usage scenarios:Fine-tuning position after reverse navigationImplementing jog/shuttle controlsFrame-accurate editing workflowsCreating smooth variable-speed playbackFor standard forward frame-stepping when not in reverse mode, use NextFrame() instead.

parameters.name: hexString
parameters.summary: Hexadecimal string to convert. Can include spaces between hex pairs. Supports formats like "FF00FF", "FF 00 FF", or "0xFF0xFF". Must contain an even number of hex digits.

methods.returns: Byte array containing the converted values. Returns null if the input string is invalid or contains non-hexadecimal characters.

methods.name: VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Position_Set
methods.summary: Seeks to a specific position within the media file.
methods.remarks: Seeking performance varies by media format. Formats with keyframes (H.264, MPEG) may have seek delays. Some formats or network streams may not support seeking. The actual position after seeking may differ slightly from the requested position.

parameters.name: position

methods.name: VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Position_SetAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously seeks to a specific position within the media file.
methods.remarks: Use this async version for smoother UI responsiveness, especially when seeking in large files or network streams where seek operations can take several seconds.

parameters.name: position
parameters.summary: The target position as a TimeSpan. Must be between zero and the media duration.

parameters.name: seekToKeyframe
parameters.summary: Currently not used in this implementation. In other contexts, would determine whether to seek to the nearest keyframe (faster but less accurate) or exact position.

methods.returns: A task that completes when all resources have been released and the player is fully stopped.

methods.name: VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Volume_Get

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Dispose.
methods.remarks: Called on two threads at once, one of them stops and releases the player and the other returns at once, possibly while that release is still running. The same applies to DisposeAsync. Called while a stop is running - Stop on another thread, or an OnStop handler that stop raises - it returns at once and that stop releases the player when it is done. The same applies to DisposeAsync, whose task completes once the player is released. A Stop() called after Dispose() does nothing. The finalizer never releases a player this method or DisposeAsync has been called on: when the release fails or is declined, call Dispose again. A playing player is stopped first, so OnStop is raised. Called while Play() or PlayAsync() is still opening the source, it returns at once and that start stops and releases the player when it is done; the start then reports false. The same applies to DisposeAsync, whose task completes once that start has released the player. Once Dispose() or DisposeAsync() has been called, deferred or not, Play() and PlayAsync() return false - unless that release failed or was declined, which leaves the player to a second Dispose.

methods.name: DeferOrClaimDispose
methods.summary: Hands a dispose issued while Boolean) or Boolean) is in flight to that start, which carries it out once it returns (GitHub issue #1977) - and likewise one issued while a stop is running, to that stop (#2064), or while a call is using the graph, to that call (#2076).
methods.remarks: It cannot run now: the build is still using what it would release, and waiting for the build deadlocks when the dispose runs on the build's own thread or on the UI thread the build marshals onto. Decided under the lock the start leaves under, so exactly one of the two runs the teardown - and the claim is taken under the lock String) checks it under, so no start can count itself in between the two. A running stop is the same case: waiting for it parks a UI thread its view or an OnStop handler marshals onto, and releasing under it is the #841 access violation; Boolean}) counts it in.

parameters.name: claimed
parameters.summary: When no start or stop is in flight: true when the caller took the dispose claim and must run the teardown, false when another dispose holds it.

methods.returns: The task that completes once the start or stop has carried the dispose out, when it was deferred and the caller must return at once; null when none is in flight.

methods.returns: true when this caller now owns the teardown.

methods.summary: Stops a playing player the way Stop() does, so OnStop is raised and the view is cleared before the graph is released (GitHub issue #1977).

methods.name: PlayAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously starts media playback or prepares the media for delayed playback.
methods.remarks: A Playlist_PlayNext() or Playlist_PlayPrevious() while it is still opening the source - with , during the whole playback, which then covers the whole playlist - is played by this call too: the task completes with the result of the file played last.This method performs the following operations:Builds the DirectShow filter graph based on media typeInitializes video and audio renderersApplies configured effects and filtersStarts playback (unless onlyPreload is true)Use Cases:Normal playback: await player.PlayAsync()Synchronized start: await player.PlayAsync(true), then player.PlayDelayed()Playlist transitions: Preload next item while current is playingExample: // Simple playback player.Source_FileName = "video.mp4"; if (await player.PlayAsync()) { Console.WriteLine("Playback started"); } // Delayed start for synchronization await player.PlayAsync(true); // Prepare only // ... wait for sync signal ... player.PlayDelayed(); // Start playback

parameters.name: onlyPreload
parameters.summary: If true, only builds and prepares the playback graph without starting actual playback. Use this with PlayDelayed() to start playback at a precise moment. Default is false.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result is true if playback started successfully or the graph was prepared successfully, false if an error occurred.

methods.name: Play
methods.summary: Starts media playback or prepares the media for delayed playback.
methods.remarks: This is the synchronous version. For async operations, use PlayAsync().With , a Play() that opens the source returns only once the playback is over and stopped, after ; it returns false when Stop() or Dispose() ended it. Resuming a paused playback returns at once, as without it. With more than one file in the playlist it plays them all - raising on its own thread after the last one - and returns once the last file is over, or once Stop() has ended the playback.Before calling Play(), set the media source using one of:Source_FileName - For file playbackSource_URL - For network streamsSource_Stream - For memory streamsDVD folder path - For DVD playbackThe method will automatically:Detect media format and required codecsBuild appropriate filter graphConfigure audio/video renderersApply any configured effectsStart playback from the beginningWith - the legacy DirectShow Video Renderer - or , the renderer owns a window of its own, and the thread that builds the graph owns it. Called from a thread that runs no message loop (the thread pool, a worker thread, a console Main), this method builds and runs the graph on a dedicated message-pumping thread of its own so the playback can still be stopped; called from a UI thread it builds the graph there, as it always has. always uses that thread with these two renderers.Example: player.Source_FileName = @"C:\Videos\sample.mp4"; player.Video_Renderer = VideoRendererMode.EVR; if (player.Play()) { Console.WriteLine("Playing: " + player.Source_FileName); } else { Console.WriteLine("Failed to start playback"); }

methods.name: StopAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously stops media playback and releases all resources associated with the current media.
methods.remarks: This method performs a complete cleanup:Stops all media streamsReleases DirectShow filters and graphFrees video and audio resourcesClears effects and processing chainsResets playback position to beginningAfter Stop completes, you can:Load and play a different media fileChange configuration and replay the same fileDispose of the player instanceThe OnStop event is raised when stopping is complete.Called while PlayAsync() is still opening the source, the stop is carried out by that start once it is done - PlayAsync() then returns false - and the task completes when it has. When another thread is inside a call on the playback by then, that stop runs once the call returns, and the task - and that of a StopAsync() issued after PlayAsync() has returned - completes once it has run; do not block on it from a handler that call raised, or from a thread it may be waiting on.One exception: if that start fails and a handler of yours begins another PlayAsync() before it returns, the stop belongs to a start that no longer exists. The returned task completes - it never hangs - but the newer playback keeps running, and the engine logs an error saying so. Await this task before starting playback again to avoid it.Example: await player.StopAsync(); // Player is now ready for new media player.Source_FileName = "next_video.mp4"; await player.PlayAsync();
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous stop operation.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops media playback and releases all resources associated with the current media.
methods.remarks: This is the synchronous version. For async operations, use StopAsync().Stopping playback:Immediately halts audio/video outputReleases all DirectShow filtersClears the filter graphResets position to 00:00:00Preserves configuration settingsThis method is safe to call multiple times or when already stopped.Called while Play() is still opening the source, it returns at once and that start stops the playback itself once it is done; Play() then returns false. When another thread is inside a call on the playback by then, Play() returns false at once and the playback is stopped once that call returns, as described below - except with or when Play() builds the graph on a message-pumping thread of its own, where the start still stops it at once. With that is the whole playback: Stop() returns at once, and the running Play() stops the playback and returns false - wait for it before the next Play().Called while another thread is inside a call on the playback (Pause, a seek, a position query), it also returns at once: the playback is stopped on a thread-pool thread once that call returns, and OnStop is raised there. Until then such calls are refused, and a Play() returns true at once and starts once that stop has run - unless another Stop() or a Dispose() comes first; a failure to open is then reported through OnError. With the async API, StopAsync() completes once the stop has run.Common usage patterns: // Stop current playback player.Stop(); // Change media file player.Source_FileName = "new_file.mp4"; player.Play(); // Or dispose of player player.Stop(); player.Dispose();

methods.name: Frame_GetCurrentFromRenderer
methods.summary: Captures the currently displayed video frame directly from the video renderer with timestamp information.
methods.remarks: This method captures frames directly from the video renderer, which means:Works with EVR (Enhanced Video Renderer) and VMR-9 renderersCaptures the frame as displayed (including any renderer-level effects)More efficient than sample grabber for single frame captureTimestamp accuracy depends on renderer (EVR provides best accuracy)For continuous frame capture or when using effects, use Frame_GetCurrent() instead.Example: TimeSpan frameTime; using (var frame = player.Frame_GetCurrentFromRenderer(out frameTime)) { if (frame != null) { frame.Save($"frame_at_{frameTime.TotalSeconds}s.jpg", ImageFormat.Jpeg); } }

methods.name: Frame_GetCurrent
methods.summary: Captures the current video frame from the sample grabber, including any applied video effects.
methods.remarks: Prerequisites:Video_Sample_Grabber_Enabled must be true (set before Play)Video must be currently playing or pausedValid video stream must be presentThis method captures frames after video effects processing, so the returned frame includes any applied effects like:Color adjustments (brightness, contrast, etc.)Geometric transforms (rotation, flip)Filters and overlaysText/image overlaysAfter a reverse playback step it returns the frame stepped to, as it was cached: before video effects and overlays.Performance note: Enabling sample grabber may impact playback performance, especially for high-resolution video.Example usage: // Enable sample grabber before playback player.Video_Sample_Grabber_Enabled = true; player.Source_FileName = "video.mp4"; player.Play(); // Capture frame during playback using (var frame = player.Frame_GetCurrent()) { if (frame != null) { pictureBox1.Image = new Bitmap(frame); } }
methods.returns: A Bitmap containing the current processed video frame, or null if capture failed, no video is playing, or sample grabbing is not enabled. The caller is responsible for disposing the returned Bitmap.

methods.name: GetCurrentFrameSnapshot
methods.summary: Copies the current frame into a 24-bit bitmap of its own, or returns null when no frame has been received.
methods.returns: The bitmap, owned by the caller, or null.

methods.name: Frame_GetCurrentAsBuffer
methods.summary: Gets the current video frame.
methods.remarks: Allocates a new array on every call; to reuse one buffer, call the overload taking ref byte[] buffer.
methods.returns: A copy of the current frame (RGB24), or null when no frame has been received, reported through OnError.

methods.name: Frame_GetCurrentAsBuffer
methods.summary: Gets the current video frame (RGB24).
methods.remarks: With no frame, width and height are 0, buffer is left as it was and no error is raised; the overload with a length reports whether a frame was copied.

parameters.name: buffer
parameters.summary: RGB24 buffer. A new one is created when it is null or smaller than the frame.

methods.name: Frame_GetCurrentAsBuffer
methods.summary: Copies the current video frame (RGB24) into the provided buffer.

parameters.name: buffer
parameters.summary: RGB24 buffer. A new one is created when it is null or smaller than the frame; bytes past length are left as they were.

parameters.name: length
parameters.summary: Number of bytes copied into buffer; 0 when nothing was copied. Rows are padded to a multiple of 4 bytes, so it can exceed width × height × 3.

methods.returns: true if the frame was copied; otherwise, false, with the reason reported through OnError.

methods.name: CopyCurrentFrame
methods.summary: Copies the current frame into buffer, growing it when it is too small.

parameters.name: length
parameters.summary: Bytes copied; 0 when there is no frame.

methods.returns: false when the copy failed with an exception, reported through OnError; otherwise, true.

methods.name: Frame_Save
methods.summary: Saves the current frame in one of the available formats.
methods.returns: true when the frame was saved; otherwise, false, with the reason reported through OnError.

methods.name: Frame_SaveIntl
methods.summary: Saves the current frame in one of the available formats (intl).

methods.name: Multiple_Video_Streams_Mappings_Add
methods.summary: Adds mapping video stream index - screen handle, for video files with multiple video streams.
methods.remarks: The main window shows the index last accepted by Video_Stream_Select, which is kept across Stop and file changes, or stream 0 if it was never called (Play fails if the file has no video stream at that index); a map on that stream is skipped. The maps are cleared whenever a playback is torn down - Stop, a Play that replaces a running playback, a playlist advance or a failed start - so add them while the player is stopped, right before Play.

methods.name: Multiple_Video_Streams_Mappings_Clear
methods.summary: Clears mappings for multiple video streams.
