methods.name: OSDClearRenderer
methods.summary: Clears the renderer's OSD overlay. Counted as a graph call on its own: the layers belong to the player and are only counted against a dispose, but a stop releases the renderer (#2076).

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Move
methods.summary: Moves an existing OSD layer to a new position on the video surface.
methods.remarks: The position is relative to the video surface, not the window. After moving, the OSD is automatically re-rendered to reflect the new position.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the layer to move. Must be less than the total layer count.

parameters.name: x
parameters.summary: New horizontal position in pixels from the left edge of the video.

parameters.name: y
parameters.summary: New vertical position in pixels from the top edge of the video.

methods.returns: true if the layer was successfully moved and re-rendered; false if the operation failed or invalid parameters were provided.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Render
methods.summary: Renders all enabled OSD layers to the video surface by compositing them into a single overlay.
methods.remarks: This method creates a composite bitmap from all enabled layers in their z-order, then applies it to the video renderer. The overlay respects transparency settings and is scaled to match the current video dimensions. Call this after making changes to layers to update the display. Requirements: - Video must be playing or paused (not stopped) - Video dimensions must be valid (non-zero) - At least one layer must be enabled
methods.returns: true if layers were successfully rendered; false if rendering failed or no enabled layers exist.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Clear
methods.summary: Removes all OSD layers and clears the overlay from the video surface.
methods.remarks: This method deletes all layer objects and their associated resources, then updates the video renderer to remove any visible overlay. Use this for complete OSD cleanup or when switching between different OSD configurations.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Clear
methods.summary: Clears the content of a specific OSD layer while preserving the layer itself.
methods.remarks: This method resets the layer's bitmap to transparent, removing all drawn content while maintaining the layer's size, position, and other properties. The graphics context is recreated with high-quality rendering settings. After clearing, the video overlay is updated to reflect the change.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the layer to clear. Must be less than the total layer count.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Enable
methods.summary: Enables or disables a specific OSD layer without removing it.
methods.remarks: Disabled layers are skipped during rendering but retain their content and properties. This allows temporary hiding of overlays without losing their configuration. Call OSD_Layers_Render() after changing enable state to update the display.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the layer to modify. Must be less than the total layer count.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.summary: true to make the layer visible during rendering; false to hide it.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Create
methods.summary: Creates a new OSD layer with specified dimensions and position.
methods.remarks: The new layer is added to the end of the layer list, giving it the highest z-order (rendered on top). The layer is initialized with a transparent background and high-quality graphics settings. Use the returned layer index (count-1) for subsequent operations on this layer.

parameters.name: left
parameters.summary: Horizontal position in pixels from the left edge of the video surface.

parameters.name: top
parameters.summary: Vertical position in pixels from the top edge of the video surface.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: Width of the layer in pixels. Should not exceed video width.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: Height of the layer in pixels. Should not exceed video height.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.summary: true to immediately enable the layer for rendering; false to create it disabled.

methods.returns: true if the layer was successfully created; false if creation failed.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Delete
methods.summary: Deletes a specific OSD layer and removes it from the display.
methods.remarks: Deleting a layer removes it from the layer list and updates the video overlay. Layer indices above the deleted layer are shifted down by one. The layer's resources are automatically disposed. Consider using OSD_Layers_Enable(false) if you need to temporarily hide a layer without losing its content.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the layer to delete. Must be less than the total layer count.

methods.returns: true if the layer was successfully deleted; false if deletion failed or invalid ID.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Draw_Image
methods.summary: Draws an image from a file onto the specified OSD layer at the given position.
methods.remarks: The image is drawn at its original size. For scaling or cropping, use the overload that accepts source and destination rectangles. Color key transparency is useful for logos and graphics with solid backgrounds that should appear transparent.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the target layer. Must be less than the total layer count.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: Full path to the image file. Supports common formats: BMP, PNG, JPG, GIF, etc.

parameters.name: left
parameters.summary: Horizontal position within the layer to draw the image, in pixels.

parameters.name: top
parameters.summary: Vertical position within the layer to draw the image, in pixels.

parameters.name: useColorKey
parameters.summary: true to treat the specified color as transparent; false to draw the image as-is.

parameters.name: colorKey
parameters.summary: Color to treat as transparent when useColorKey is true. Typically used for logos with solid color backgrounds.

methods.returns: true if the image was successfully drawn; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Draw_Image
methods.summary: Draws an image from a file onto the specified OSD layer with source cropping and destination scaling.
methods.remarks: This overload provides full control over image positioning and scaling. Use srcRect to crop the source image and destRect to scale/position the result. This is useful for sprite sheets, image atlases, or precise positioning needs.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the target layer. Must be less than the total layer count.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: Full path to the image file. Supports common formats: BMP, PNG, JPG, GIF, etc.

parameters.name: srcRect
parameters.summary: Rectangle defining the portion of the source image to draw. Pass Rectangle.Empty to use the entire image.

parameters.name: destRect
parameters.summary: Rectangle defining where and how large to draw the image on the layer. Set Width/Height to 0 to use the source image's dimensions.

parameters.name: useColorKey
parameters.summary: true to treat the specified color as transparent; false to draw the image as-is.

parameters.name: colorKey
parameters.summary: Color to treat as transparent when useColorKey is true.

methods.returns: true if the image was successfully drawn; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Draw_Image
methods.summary: Draws a Bitmap object onto the specified OSD layer with full control over source and destination.
methods.remarks: This is the core image drawing method used by other overloads. It provides maximum flexibility for dynamic image content. The bitmap is not disposed by this method, allowing reuse. Color key transparency uses GDI+ ImageAttributes for hardware acceleration.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the target layer. Must be less than the total layer count.

parameters.name: image
parameters.summary: Bitmap object to draw. The caller retains ownership and must dispose of it.

parameters.name: srcRect
parameters.summary: Rectangle defining the portion of the source bitmap to draw. Pass Rectangle.Empty to use the entire bitmap starting at (0,0).

parameters.name: destRect
parameters.summary: Rectangle defining where and how large to draw the image on the layer. Set Width/Height to 0 to use the source bitmap's dimensions.

parameters.name: useColorKey
parameters.summary: true to treat the specified color as transparent; false to draw normally.

parameters.name: colorKey
parameters.summary: Color to treat as transparent when useColorKey is true. Exact color matching is used.

methods.returns: true if the image was successfully drawn; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Draw_Text
methods.summary: Draws text onto the specified OSD layer with the given font and color.
methods.remarks: Text is rendered with anti-aliasing for smooth edges. For dynamic text updates (e.g., timecodes), clear the layer or specific area before redrawing to avoid overlapping. Consider using a dedicated layer for frequently changing text. The layer's graphics context uses high-quality text rendering.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the target layer. Must be less than the total layer count.

parameters.name: left
parameters.summary: Horizontal position within the layer to start drawing text, in pixels.

parameters.name: top
parameters.summary: Vertical position within the layer for the text baseline, in pixels.

parameters.name: text
parameters.summary: The text string to draw. Supports multi-line text with newline characters.

parameters.name: font
parameters.summary: Font to use for rendering. The caller retains ownership of the Font object.

parameters.name: color
parameters.summary: Color for the text. Use colors with alpha for semi-transparent text.

methods.returns: true if the text was successfully drawn; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_GetBitmap
methods.summary: Retrieves the bitmap content of a specific OSD layer.
methods.remarks: This method provides direct access to a layer's bitmap for advanced manipulation or analysis. The returned bitmap is the actual layer content - modifications will affect the OSD display. Do not dispose the bitmap as it's owned by the layer. Call OSD_Layers_Render() after modifications to update the display. The bitmap lives only as long as its layer: OSD_Layers_Clear() and OSD_Layers_Delete() dispose it, and OSD_Layers_Clear(int) disposes it and gives the layer a fresh one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the layer. Must be less than the total layer count.

parameters.name: bitmap
parameters.summary: Output parameter that receives a reference to the layer's bitmap. This is a direct reference, not a copy - do not dispose it.

methods.returns: true if the bitmap was successfully retrieved; false if the operation failed or invalid ID.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_SetTransparency
methods.summary: Sets the transparency level for a specific OSD layer.
methods.remarks: Layer transparency affects the entire layer uniformly, making it useful for fading effects or semi-transparent overlays. This is different from per-pixel alpha in PNG images or color-keyed transparency. The transparency value is applied during the next OSD_Layers_Render() call.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the layer. Must be less than the total layer count.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: Transparency level from 0 (fully transparent/invisible) to 255 (fully opaque). Common values: 255 = no transparency, 128 = 50% transparent, 0 = invisible.

methods.returns: true if the transparency was successfully set; false if the operation failed or invalid ID.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Add
methods.summary: Adds a video file as a Picture-in-Picture source to be displayed alongside the main video.
methods.remarks: The PiP video will be overlaid on the main video at the specified position and size. Multiple PiP sources can be added and will be layered in the order they were added. PiP requires VMR9 video renderer to be active. The call is declined and logged while a playback is running: adding out of step with the clear and the delete, which also decline, would leave a reconfigure half-applied. The list survives a stop, so an add after one reaches the next playback. Reconfigure after StopAsync() returns, not from the OnStop handler - for a stop carried out by a Play() still in progress, the player still counts as running while that event is raised, and a stop the player performs itself at the end of a file raises the same event with no call for the customer to await. From OnStop, post the reconfiguration to the UI thread instead of running it inline.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: Full path to the video file to display as PiP. Supports common video formats.

parameters.name: outLeft
parameters.summary: Horizontal position in pixels from the left edge of the main video surface.

parameters.name: outTop
parameters.summary: Vertical position in pixels from the top edge of the main video surface.

parameters.name: outWidth
parameters.summary: Display width in pixels for the PiP video. Can differ from source video dimensions.

parameters.name: outHeight
parameters.summary: Display height in pixels for the PiP video. Can differ from source video dimensions.

methods.returns: true if the PiP source was successfully added; false if addition failed.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Clear
methods.summary: Removes all Picture-in-Picture sources from the display list.
methods.remarks: This method clears all configured PiP sources but does not affect the main video. Call this before reconfiguring PiP sources or when switching to single-video mode. The call is declined and logged while a playback is running: those filters are connected in the graph.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Delete
methods.summary: Removes a specific Picture-in-Picture source from the display list.
methods.remarks: Removing a PiP source shifts the indices of all subsequent sources down by one. The main video (index 0) cannot be removed using this method. The call is declined and logged while a playback is running: those filters are connected in the graph.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the PiP source to remove.

methods.returns: true if the source was successfully removed; false if the index was invalid.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Change
methods.summary: Runs a change to the PiP source list, declined while a playback is running or starting.

parameters.name: method
parameters.summary: The public method name, for the log line.

parameters.name: change
parameters.summary: The change; returns its own result.

methods.returns: The result of change, or false when declined.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourceOrderAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously sets the z-order (layering priority) of a Picture-in-Picture source.
methods.remarks: This method only works during playback. Use this to dynamically change which PiP sources appear in front of or behind others. The main video typically has order 0. Only available when using async API mode.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the PiP source to modify. Index 0 is the main video.

parameters.name: order
parameters.summary: Z-order value from 0 (bottom) to stream count - 1 (top). Higher values appear above lower values.

methods.returns: A task that returns true if the z-order was successfully changed; false otherwise.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourceOrder
methods.summary: Sets the z-order (layering priority) of a Picture-in-Picture source.
methods.remarks: This method only works during playback. Use this to dynamically change which PiP sources appear in front of or behind others. The main video typically has order 0. Only available when using synchronous API mode.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the PiP source to modify. Index 0 is the main video.

parameters.name: order
parameters.summary: Z-order value from 0 (bottom) to stream count - 1 (top). Higher values appear above lower values.

methods.returns: true if the z-order was successfully changed; false otherwise.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourceOrderIntl
methods.summary: Internal implementation for setting Picture-in-Picture source z-order.
methods.remarks: When playback is stopped, this updates the OrderID property for later use. During playback, it directly calls the video renderer's SetStreamZOrder method.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: One-based index of the PiP source when not playing, zero-based during playback.

methods.returns: true if successful; false otherwise.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourcePositionAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously sets the position, size, and transparency of a Picture-in-Picture source.
methods.remarks: This method allows dynamic repositioning and resizing of PiP sources during playback. The rectangle coordinates are relative to the main video surface, not the window. Alpha blending provides smooth transparency effects for professional-looking overlays. Only available when using async API mode.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the PiP source to modify. Index 0 is the main video.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.summary: Rectangle defining the position (X, Y) and size (Width, Height) in pixels on the video surface.

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.summary: Transparency level from 0.0 (fully transparent/invisible) to 1.0 (fully opaque). Use values like 0.5 for semi-transparent overlays.

methods.returns: A task that returns true if the position was successfully updated; false otherwise.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourcePosition
methods.summary: Sets the position, size, and transparency of a Picture-in-Picture source.
methods.remarks: This method allows dynamic repositioning and resizing of PiP sources during playback. The rectangle coordinates are relative to the main video surface, not the window. Alpha blending provides smooth transparency effects for professional-looking overlays. Only available when using synchronous API mode.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the PiP source to modify. Index 0 is the main video.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.summary: Rectangle defining the position (X, Y) and size (Width, Height) in pixels on the video surface.

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.summary: Transparency level from 0.0 (fully transparent/invisible) to 1.0 (fully opaque). Use values like 0.5 for semi-transparent overlays.

methods.returns: true if the position was successfully updated; false otherwise.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourcePositionIntl
methods.summary: Internal implementation for setting Picture-in-Picture source position and transparency.
methods.remarks: When playback is stopped, this updates the PiP object properties for later use. During playback, it directly calls the video renderer's SetStreamPosition and SetStreamAlpha methods to apply changes immediately.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: One-based index of the PiP source when not playing, zero-based during playback.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.summary: Rectangle defining position and size on the video surface.

methods.returns: true if successful; false otherwise.

methods.name: AddPIPDevices
methods.summary: Initializes and connects all configured Picture-in-Picture sources to the DirectShow graph.
methods.remarks: This internal method is called during playback initialization to set up PiP sources. It performs the following for each PiP source: - Creates appropriate source filters (LAV or standard DirectShow) - Connects sources to the video renderer's input pins - Configures stream sizes and positions - Sets up any required color space converters Currently only supports file-based PiP sources with LAV or standard DirectShow filters. Requires VMR9 video renderer for PiP functionality.

methods.name: Playlist_GetPosition
methods.summary: Gets the current position (index) within the playlist.
methods.remarks: The position indicates which file is currently playing or will play next. This value persists between playback sessions until changed or the playlist is cleared.
methods.returns: Zero-based index of the currently playing or selected item. Returns 0 if playlist is empty.

methods.name: Playlist_SetPosition
methods.summary: Sets the current position within the playlist without starting playback.
methods.remarks: This method only changes the playlist position; it doesn't start playback. Use Play() after setting position to begin playing from the new position. If currently playing, stop and play again to switch to the new item.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the item to make current. Must be within valid range.

methods.returns: true if the position was successfully set; false if the index is out of range.

methods.name: Playlist_Reset
methods.summary: Resets the playlist position to the beginning (first item).
methods.remarks: This method sets the current index to 0 but doesn't affect playback state. Useful for restarting playlist playback from the beginning after reaching the end.

methods.name: Playlist_PlayNext
methods.summary: Stops current playback and starts playing the next item in the playlist.
methods.remarks: This method automatically stops the current file, advances the playlist position, and starts playing the next file. At the last item it returns false and does not wrap to the first one, whatever Loop is set to. The OnNewFilePlaybackStarted event will fire when the new file begins playing. Called while Play() or PlayAsync() is still opening the source - with ConsoleUsage, during the whole playback - it returns true at once, and that Play() or PlayAsync() stops the current file and plays the next one itself; a Stop() before it has started that file - also one from OnStop - cancels it.
methods.returns: true if successfully moved to and started playing the next item; false if already at the end of the playlist.

methods.name: Playlist_PlayNextAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously stops current playback and starts playing the next item in the playlist.
methods.remarks: This async version prevents UI blocking during the stop/start transition. Particularly useful for network streams or large files where stopping might take time. The method awaits both stop and play operations to complete - except when called while Play() or PlayAsync() is still opening the source (with ConsoleUsage, during the whole playback): it then hands the next file to that call and completes at once, as Playlist_PlayNext does.
methods.returns: A task that returns true if successfully moved to and started playing the next item, or handed it to a Play() or PlayAsync() still opening the source; false if already at the end.

methods.name: Playlist_PlayPrevious
methods.summary: Stops current playback and starts playing the previous item in the playlist.
methods.remarks: This method automatically stops the current file, moves back one position, and starts playing the previous file. Returns false if currently at index 0. The OnNewFilePlaybackStarted event will fire when the new file begins playing. Called while Play() or PlayAsync() is still opening the source - with ConsoleUsage, during the whole playback - it returns true at once, and that Play() or PlayAsync() stops the current file and plays the previous one itself; a Stop() before it has started that file - also one from OnStop - cancels it.
methods.returns: true if successfully moved to and started playing the previous item; false if already at the beginning.

methods.name: Playlist_PlayPreviousAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously stops current playback and starts playing the previous item in the playlist.
methods.remarks: This async version prevents UI blocking during the stop/start transition. Useful for maintaining responsive UI when dealing with network streams or large files. Called while Play() or PlayAsync() is still opening the source - with ConsoleUsage, during the whole playback - it hands the previous file to that call and completes at once, as Playlist_PlayPrevious does.
methods.returns: A task that returns true if successfully moved to and started playing the previous item, or handed it to a Play() or PlayAsync() still opening the source; false if at the beginning.

methods.name: Playlist_Clear
methods.summary: Removes all items from the playlist and resets the position to zero.
methods.remarks: This method clears all playlist entries but doesn't stop current playback. After clearing, you'll need to add new items before playing again. The playlist position is reset to 0 for consistency.
methods.returns: Always returns true.

methods.name: Playlist_Add
methods.summary: Adds a media file or stream URL to the end of the playlist.
methods.remarks: This method validates local file existence but doesn't verify URL accessibility. Items are added to the end of the playlist. Use Playlist_Insert to add at specific positions. The playlist can contain a mix of local files and network streams.

parameters.name: path
parameters.summary: Full path to a local file or a valid stream URL. Supported URL protocols: http://, https://, rtsp://, rtmp://, udp://, tcp://

methods.returns: true if the item was successfully added; false if the path is invalid or file doesn't exist.

methods.name: Playlist_Remove
methods.summary: Removes the first occurrence of a specific file or URL from the playlist.
methods.remarks: This method uses exact string matching. If multiple identical entries exist, only the first is removed. The current position may be adjusted if the removed item was before the current position.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The exact file path or URL to remove. Must match exactly.

methods.returns: true if the item was found and removed; false if not found in the playlist.

methods.name: Playlist_RemoveAt
methods.summary: Removes the playlist item at the specified index.
methods.remarks: Removing an item shifts all subsequent items down by one position. If the removed item is currently playing, playback continues but the current index may need adjustment. Consider stopping playback before removing the currently playing item.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the item to remove.

methods.returns: true if an item was removed; false if the index is out of range.

methods.name: Playlist_Insert
methods.summary: Inserts a media file at a specific position in the playlist.
methods.remarks: Unlike Playlist_Add, this method only accepts local files, not URLs. The file existence is verified before insertion. If the index is beyond the current count, the item is added at the end.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: Full path to the file to insert. Must exist on disk.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: Zero-based position where the item should be inserted. Items at and after this position are shifted up.

methods.returns: true if the file was inserted; false if the file doesn't exist.

methods.name: Playlist_GetFilename
methods.summary: Retrieves the file path or URL of the item at the specified playlist position.
methods.remarks: Use this to display playlist contents, check what will play next, or verify playlist entries. The returned path is exactly as it was added to the playlist.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the item to retrieve.

methods.returns: The full file path or URL at the specified index; empty string if index is out of range.

methods.name: Playlist_GetCount
methods.summary: Gets the total number of items currently in the playlist.
methods.remarks: Use this to validate indices before calling other playlist methods, display playlist information, or determine if the playlist is empty. The count includes all items regardless of their playback status.
methods.returns: The count of playlist items. Returns 0 for an empty playlist.

methods.name: OnPropertyChanged
methods.summary: Raises the PropertyChanged event for the specified property.

parameters.name: propertyName
parameters.summary: Name of the property that changed. Automatically populated by CallerMemberName attribute.

methods.name: State
methods.summary: Gets the current playback state of the media player.
methods.remarks: Use this to determine valid operations. For example, Pause() only works when Playing, Resume() only works when Paused. The state is updated automatically and corresponding events fire on state changes.
methods.returns: Current PlaybackState: Free (stopped), Playing, Paused, or Finished.

methods.name: SDK_BuildDate
methods.summary: Gets the build date of the currently loaded SDK assembly.
methods.remarks: Useful for version verification and troubleshooting. The build date helps identify specific SDK releases when the version number alone isn't sufficient.
methods.returns: DateTime when this SDK version was compiled.

methods.name: SDK_Version
methods.summary: Gets the version number of the currently loaded SDK assembly.
methods.remarks: Use this to verify SDK compatibility and features. Version numbers follow semantic versioning where Major changes indicate breaking changes, Minor changes add features, and Build/Revision are for bug fixes.
methods.returns: Version object with Major.Minor.Build.Revision components.

methods.name: CustomRedist_Enable
methods.summary: Enables or disables the use of custom redistributable filters.
methods.remarks: Call this before initializing playback. When enabled, filters from the custom path take precedence over system filters. Useful for ensuring consistent behavior across different systems or using specific filter versions.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.summary: true to load filters from CustomRedist_Path; false to use only system-registered filters.

methods.name: CustomRedist_IsEnabled
methods.summary: Gets whether custom redistributable filter loading is currently enabled.
methods.remarks: Use this to verify the current filter loading configuration, especially when troubleshooting codec issues or verifying deployment settings.
methods.returns: true if loading filters from custom path; false if using system filters only.

methods.name: Tags_Read
methods.summary: Reads metadata tags from a media file without loading it for playback.
methods.remarks: Supported metadata includes: - Basic tags: Title, Artist, Album, Year, Genre, Comment - Advanced tags: AlbumArtist, Composer, Publisher, Conductor - Technical info: Bitrate, Duration, Codec information - Embedded artwork: Cover images and thumbnails Supported formats include: - Audio: MP3 (ID3v1/v2), MP4/M4A, WMA, OGG Vorbis, FLAC - Video: MP4, MKV, AVI (limited), WMV All text values are returned as strings. Artwork is returned as byte arrays. This method is lightweight and doesn't require initializing playback.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: Full path to the media file to read tags from.

methods.returns: MediaFileTags object containing all available metadata, or null if reading fails.

methods.name: Video_Effects_Add
methods.summary: Adds a video effect to the processing pipeline.
methods.remarks: Effects are processed in the order they are added. Common effect types include: - Color adjustments: brightness, contrast, saturation, hue - Transforms: rotate, flip, crop, resize - Overlays: text logos, image watermarks, scrolling text - Filters: blur, sharpen, denoise, edge detection - Special effects: fade, chroma key, picture-in-picture Effects can be added before or during playback. Remember to set Video_Effects_Enabled = true for effects to be processed. The effect's Name property should be unique for later retrieval.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.summary: Video effect implementation to add. Must implement IVideoEffect interface.

methods.name: Video_Effects_Get
methods.summary: Retrieves a video effect by its name for runtime modification.
methods.remarks: Use this to modify effect parameters during playback. For example: - Adjust brightness/contrast in response to user input - Update text overlay content - Enable/disable effects dynamically - Animate effect parameters Cast the returned interface to the specific effect type to access its properties. The search is case-insensitive for convenience.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The name assigned to the effect when created. Case-insensitive.

methods.returns: The IVideoEffect instance if found; null if no effect with that name exists.

methods.name: Video_Effects_Clear
methods.summary: Removes all video effects from the processing pipeline.
methods.remarks: This method: - Removes all effects immediately - Properly disposes of effects that hold resources (logos, images) - Restores original video appearance - Is thread-safe and can be called during playback Effects that implement IDisposable (ImageLogo, TextLogo, ScrollingTextLogo) are disposed to free resources like loaded images or fonts. After clearing, you can add new effects without stopping playback.

methods.name: Video_Effects_Remove
methods.summary: Removes a specific video effect from the processing pipeline.
methods.remarks: Removes the first effect found with the specified name. If multiple effects have the same name, only the first is removed. The method: - Safely removes the effect during playback - Disposes of effects that hold resources - Maintains the order of remaining effects - Silently succeeds if the effect is not found Use this for dynamic effect management, such as removing temporary overlays or disabling specific processing based on conditions.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The exact name of the effect to remove (case-sensitive).

methods.name: Video_Effects_GPU_Add
methods.summary: Adds a GPU-accelerated video effect to the processing pipeline.
methods.remarks: GPU effects leverage DirectX 11 compute shaders for high-performance processing: - Color grading and correction - Advanced denoising and sharpening - Real-time video stabilization - Complex transitions and blending - AI-powered effects (super-resolution, style transfer) Requirements: - DirectX 11 compatible GPU - Video_Effects_GPU_Enabled must be true - Compatible video renderer (EVR preferred) GPU effects can be combined with CPU effects. Processing order is maintained. Effects are identified by their Name property for later modification.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.summary: GPU video effect implementation. Must implement IGPUVideoEffect interface.

methods.name: Video_Effects_GPU_Get
methods.summary: Retrieves a GPU video effect by its name for runtime modification.
methods.remarks: Use this to modify GPU effect parameters during playback: - Adjust shader parameters in real-time - Enable/disable effects based on performance - Animate effect properties - Update textures or lookup tables Cast the returned interface to the specific GPU effect type to access its specialized properties and shader parameters.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name assigned to the effect when created.

methods.returns: The IGPUVideoEffect instance if found; null if no effect with that name exists.

methods.name: Video_Effects_GPU_Clear
methods.summary: Removes all GPU video effects from the processing pipeline.
methods.remarks: Immediately removes all GPU effects and releases associated GPU resources: - Shader resources and textures - Compute buffers - DirectX 11 device contexts This operation is thread-safe and can be performed during playback. The video returns to its original appearance. GPU resources are properly released to prevent memory leaks.

methods.name: Video_Effects_GPU_Remove
methods.summary: Removes a specific GPU video effect from the processing pipeline.
methods.remarks: Removes the named effect and releases its GPU resources: - Unloads compute shaders - Releases texture resources - Frees GPU memory allocations The removal is immediate and thread-safe. Other effects continue processing in their original order. If the effect is not found, the method completes silently without error.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The exact name of the GPU effect to remove.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_UpdateAsync
methods.summary: Asynchronously updates video renderer display settings to handle window size changes.
methods.remarks: Call this method when the video display window is resized to ensure proper video scaling and aspect ratio. The method recalculates display parameters and notifies the renderer of the new dimensions. Safe to call during playback. Only available when using async API mode.

parameters.name: newWidth
parameters.summary: New display width in pixels. Pass 0 to use current window width.

parameters.name: newHeight
parameters.summary: New display height in pixels. Pass 0 to use current window height.

methods.returns: A task that completes when the renderer has been updated.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_Update
methods.summary: Updates video renderer display settings to handle window size changes.
methods.remarks: Call this method when the video display window is resized to ensure proper video scaling and aspect ratio. The method recalculates display parameters and notifies the renderer of the new dimensions. Safe to call during playback. Only available when using synchronous API mode.

parameters.name: newWidth
parameters.summary: New display width in pixels. Pass 0 to use current window width.

parameters.name: newHeight
parameters.summary: New display height in pixels. Pass 0 to use current window height.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_UpdateIntl
methods.summary: Internal implementation for updating video renderer display settings.
methods.remarks: This method performs the actual renderer update including: - Invoking UI thread updates via the video view - Recalculating display parameters - Updating window handle if requested - Refreshing the DirectShow filter graph

parameters.name: updateHandle
parameters.summary: If true, also updates the window handle binding.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_SetAuto
methods.summary: Automatically selects the best available video renderer for the current system.
methods.remarks: Selection priority: 1. EVR (Enhanced Video Renderer) - Windows 7+ with best features 2. VMR-9 (Video Mixing Renderer 9) - Windows XP+ with good features 3. Legacy Video Renderer - Fallback for older systems EVR is preferred for modern systems as it provides: - Better performance and quality - DXVA hardware acceleration - Advanced deinterlacing - Improved color space handling

methods.name: Video_Renderer_SetCustomWindowHandle
methods.summary: Sets a custom window handle for video rendering output.
methods.remarks: Use this to render video to a specific window handle instead of the default video view. Useful for: - Rendering to external windows - Custom UI frameworks - Multi-window applications The handle must remain valid throughout playback. It is used when no video view is set, and kept across stops until it is changed: every later playback with no view renders into it while the window exists.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.summary: Native window handle (HWND) where video should be rendered, or Zero to stop using one.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_Deinterlace_Modes_Fill
methods.summary: Populates the list of available deinterlacing modes from the video renderer.
methods.remarks: Queries the video renderer (typically VMR9) for supported deinterlacing algorithms. Different modes offer various quality/performance tradeoffs: - Bob: Fast but lower quality - Weave: Simple, may show combing - Motion Adaptive: Better quality, more CPU - Motion Compensated: Best quality, highest CPU The available modes depend on graphics hardware capabilities.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_Deinterlace_Modes
methods.summary: Gets the list of available deinterlacing modes supported by the current video renderer.
methods.remarks: Deinterlacing removes interlacing artifacts from video sources like: - Analog TV captures - DV camcorder footage - Some broadcast content The list is populated on first access and cached. Available modes depend on the video renderer and graphics hardware. Returns empty collection if deinterlacing is not supported.
methods.returns: Observable collection of deinterlacing mode names.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_GetRanges
methods.summary: Gets the valid range of values for a specific video adjustment parameter.
methods.remarks: Hardware video adjustments provide real-time control without CPU overhead. Ranges and units depend on the video renderer, the graphics hardware and the driver, so read them with this method instead of assuming fixed values. The EVR renderer reports DXVA2 fixed-point units, where 1.0 is 65536. Pass values in the same units to Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_SetValue(). Only available during playback with synchronous API.

parameters.name: adjustment
parameters.summary: The video property to query: Brightness, Contrast, Hue, or Saturation.

methods.returns: VideoRendererVideoAdjustRanges containing min, max, default, and step values; null if the adjustment is not supported.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_GetRangesIntl
methods.summary: Gets video adjustment ranges.
methods.returns: The VideoRendererVideoAdjustRanges.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_GetRangesAsync
methods.summary: Gets video adjustment ranges (async).
methods.returns: Task<VideoRendererVideoAdjustRanges>.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_GetValuesAsync
methods.summary: Gets video adjustment value (async).
methods.returns: Task<System.Nullable<System.Single>>.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_GetValues
methods.summary: Gets the current value of a specific video adjustment parameter.
methods.remarks: Retrieves the current hardware video adjustment setting. Values are within the ranges returned by Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_GetRanges(). These adjustments are applied by the graphics hardware without affecting the source video data. Only available during playback with synchronous API.

parameters.name: adjustment
parameters.summary: The video property to query: Brightness, Contrast, Hue, or Saturation.

methods.returns: Current adjustment value as a float; null if the adjustment is not supported or cannot be read.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_GetValuesIntl
methods.summary: Gets video adjustment value (intl).
methods.returns: System.Nullable<System.Single>.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_SetValueAsync
methods.summary: Sets video adjustment value (async).
methods.returns: Task<System.Boolean>.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_SetValue
methods.summary: Sets the value of a specific video adjustment parameter.
methods.remarks: Applies hardware video adjustments in real-time without reprocessing frames. Values must be within the ranges returned by Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_GetRanges(). Changes take effect immediately and persist until changed or playback stops. These adjustments are preferable to software effects for performance. Only available during playback with synchronous API.

parameters.name: adjustment
parameters.summary: The video property to modify: Brightness, Contrast, Hue, or Saturation.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: New value within the valid range for this adjustment.

methods.returns: true if the value was successfully set; false if not supported or out of range.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_SetValueIntl
methods.summary: Sets video adjustment value.
methods.returns: true if successful, false otherwise.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_GetSupportedAsync
methods.summary: Gets video adjustment supported values (async).
methods.returns: Task<VideoRendererAdjustmentSupported>.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_GetSupported
methods.summary: Determines which video adjustment parameters are supported by the current renderer.
methods.remarks: Tests hardware support for each video adjustment type. Support depends on: - Video renderer type (EVR and VMR-9 report what the video card's video processor offers; a card without hardware adjustment returns an object with every flag false) - Graphics hardware capabilities - Video driver features Use this before attempting to get/set adjustment values to avoid errors. Hardware adjustments are preferred over software effects for performance. Only available during playback with synchronous API.
methods.returns: VideoRendererAdjustmentSupported object indicating which adjustments are available; null if support cannot be determined or playback is not active.

methods.name: Video_Renderer_VideoAdjust_GetSupportedIntl
methods.summary: Gets video adjustment supported values.
methods.returns: The VideoRendererAdjustmentSupported.

events.name: OnDVDDomainChanged

events.name: OnAudioFrameBuffer

events.name: OnDataFrameBuffer

events.name: OnAudioVUMeter

events.name: OnNetworkSourceStop

events.name: OnMIDIFileInfo

events.name: OnMotionDetectionEx

events.name: OnBarcodeDetected

events.name: PropertyChanged

classes.name: ScreenUpdateDelegate
classes.summary: Screen update delegate.

classes.name: MultiScreenScreen
classes.summary: What an extra screen is, between playbacks. The renderer objects in FScreens belong to one graph and are disposed with it on every Stop (see Clear in Main.cs, issue #1545), so what MultiScreen_AddScreen was given has to be kept somewhere that survives that - otherwise the second Play has no screens to build and the extra windows keep whatever the previous graph left on them (issue #1599).

methods.name: Copy
methods.summary: Copies the values, so a rebuild reading them off the lock cannot pick up half of a resize.
methods.returns: A copy.

classes.name: CachedFrame
classes.summary: A cached RGB24 frame: Size bytes at Data, rows Stride bytes apart.

classes.name: GraphCall
classes.summary: Counts a graph call in for as long as it is not disposed; see String).

properties.name: StopRequests
properties.summary: Gets how many stops had been requested when the call was counted in; see Int32).

properties.name: Entered
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the call was counted in and may use the graph.

classes.name: MultipleVideoStreamsMap
classes.summary: Defines the mapping between video stream indices and their corresponding display screens for multi-stream video playback scenarios.
classes.remarks: This internal class is used when playing media files containing multiple video streams, allowing each stream to be rendered to a different display surface. Common use cases include multi-angle DVDs, security camera systems, or educational content with multiple views.

constructors.name: MultipleVideoStreamsMap
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MultipleVideoStreamsMap class with the specified stream index and display parameters.
constructors.remarks: The Screen property will be initialized later when the DirectShow graph is built. Ensure the window handle remains valid for the lifetime of this mapping.

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: Zero-based index of the video stream to map (0 for first stream, 1 for second, etc.).

parameters.name: screenHandle
parameters.summary: The window handle (HWND) where the video stream will be rendered. Must not be IntPtr.Zero.

parameters.name: screenWidth
parameters.summary: Initial width of the rendering surface in pixels. Should match the window's client area width.

parameters.name: screenHeight
parameters.summary: Initial height of the rendering surface in pixels. Should match the window's client area height.

properties.name: StreamIndex
properties.summary: Gets or sets the zero-based index of the video stream within the media file.
properties.value: The stream index, where 0 represents the first video stream, 1 the second, and so on. Valid range depends on the number of video streams in the media file.

properties.name: ScreenHandle
properties.summary: Gets or sets the window handle (HWND) where this video stream should be rendered.
properties.value: A platform-specific window handle. On Windows, this is an HWND obtained from Control.Handle or similar. Must be a valid window handle that supports video rendering.

properties.name: Screen
properties.summary: Gets or sets the DirectShow video renderer instance associated with this stream.
properties.value: The video renderer object that handles the actual rendering of the video stream. This is typically an EVR, VMR9, or VMR7 renderer depending on system capabilities.

properties.name: ScreenWidth
properties.summary: Gets or sets the width of the rendering surface in pixels.
properties.value: The width in pixels. Should match the actual window width for proper aspect ratio. Typical values range from 320 to 3840 pixels depending on the display resolution.

properties.name: ScreenHeight
properties.summary: Gets or sets the height of the rendering surface in pixels.
properties.value: The height in pixels. Should match the actual window height for proper aspect ratio. Typical values range from 240 to 2160 pixels depending on the display resolution.

classes.name: IMediaPlayerCore
classes.summary: Defines the core interface for Media Player SDK implementations, providing access to underlying player functionality, DVD controls, and source mode information.
classes.remarks: This interface extends IMPVCVECore and serves as the foundation for all media player implementations. It provides access to the concrete MediaPlayerCore instance, DVD navigation controls (when playing DVDs), and information about the current media source type and playback engine.

methods.name: GetCore
methods.summary: Gets the underlying MediaPlayerCore instance that implements this interface.
methods.remarks: Use this method when you need access to functionality not exposed through the interface abstraction, such as platform-specific features or advanced configuration.
methods.returns: The concrete MediaPlayerCore implementation providing full access to all player functionality, properties, and events.

methods.name: GetDVDControl
methods.summary: Gets the DirectShow DVD navigation control interface for DVD playback control.
methods.remarks: This interface provides DVD-specific controls such as menu navigation, chapter selection, angle changes, and audio/subtitle stream selection. Only available when using the DirectShow engine (LAV mode) with DVD content.
methods.returns: An IDvdControl2 interface for controlling DVD navigation, or null if not playing a DVD or if the DirectShow engine is not in use.

methods.name: GetDVDInfo
methods.summary: Gets the DirectShow DVD information interface for querying DVD properties and state.
methods.remarks: This interface provides read-only access to DVD information such as current domain, title/chapter count, available audio/subtitle streams, parental level settings, and disc region information. Only available when using the DirectShow engine with DVD content.
methods.returns: An IDvdInfo2 interface for retrieving DVD information, or null if not playing a DVD or if the DirectShow engine is not in use.

methods.name: GetSourceMode
methods.summary: Gets the current media source mode indicating which playback engine is in use.
methods.remarks: The source mode determines which underlying technology is used for media playback. Different modes offer different capabilities: - LAV: Best compatibility and codec support via DirectShow - MediaFoundation: Native Windows API, good for DRM content - FFMPEG: Cross-platform support, best for streaming protocols The mode is typically set in Player.SourceMode before playback.
methods.returns: The active MediaPlayerSourceMode: LAV (DirectShow with LAV Filters), File (DirectShow), MediaFoundation, FFMPEG, or other specialized modes.

classes.name: BaseEffectNet
classes.summary: Base class for Media Framework Primitives (MFP) video effects. Provides common properties for effect timing, identification, and configuration.

properties.name: StartTime
properties.summary: Gets or sets the start time when the effect begins to be applied.
properties.value: The start time of the effect. Use Zero to apply from the beginning.

properties.name: StopTime
properties.summary: Gets or sets the stop time when the effect stops being applied.
properties.value: The stop time of the effect. Use MaxValue to apply until the end.

properties.name: ID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the unique identifier for this effect instance.
properties.value: The effect identifier used to reference and manage this effect.

properties.name: Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this BaseEffectNet is enabled and should be processed.
properties.value: true if the effect is enabled and will be applied; otherwise, false.

classes.name: MFPCoreX64
classes.summary: Provides P/Invoke declarations for Media Framework Primitives Core native library (x64 architecture).
classes.remarks: This class contains all P/Invoke signatures for the VisioForge_MFP64.dll and VisioForge_MFPX64.dll native libraries. These libraries provide high-performance video and image processing operations optimized for x64 systems. Supported operation categories include: Drawing operations: RGB24/RGB32 compositing with transparency supportColor space conversion: YUY2, YV12, RGB24, RGB32, UYVY, RGBA formatsVideo effects: Blur, sharpen, contrast, saturation, and many moreDenoising: CAST, Adaptive, Mosquito noise reduction algorithmsDeinterlacing: Blend, Triangle, and CAVT methodsTransformations: Rotate, flip, mirror, zoom, pan, crop, resizeMotion detection: Frame comparison and motion matrix generationDirectShow integration: Filter management and LAV decoder configuration This class is decorated with for performance optimization in trusted scenarios.

classes.name: MFPCoreX86
classes.summary: Provides P/Invoke declarations for Media Framework Primitives Core native library (x86 architecture).
classes.remarks: This class contains all P/Invoke signatures for the VisioForge_MFP.dll and VisioForge_MFPX.dll native libraries. These libraries provide high-performance video and image processing operations optimized for x86 systems. Supported operation categories include: Drawing operations: RGB24/RGB32 compositing with transparency supportColor space conversion: YUY2, YV12, RGB24, RGB32, UYVY, RGBA formatsVideo effects: Blur, sharpen, contrast, saturation, and many moreDenoising: CAST, Adaptive, Mosquito noise reduction algorithmsDeinterlacing: Blend, Triangle, and CAVT methodsTransformations: Rotate, flip, mirror, zoom, pan, crop, resizeMotion detection: Frame comparison and motion matrix generationDirectShow integration: Filter management and LAV decoder configuration This class is decorated with for performance optimization in trusted scenarios.

classes.name: DirectShowMFP
classes.summary: Provides DirectShow helper methods for Media Framework Primitives (MFP) operations. This class automatically selects the appropriate x86 or x64 implementation based on the current process architecture.
classes.remarks: All methods in this class delegate to platform-specific implementations in MFPCoreX86 or MFPCoreX64.

methods.name: DSRemoveAllFilters
methods.summary: Removes all filters from the specified DirectShow filter graph.
methods.remarks: This method will safely catch and suppress any exceptions that occur during filter removal. It automatically selects the x86 or x64 implementation based on the current process architecture.

parameters.name: pGraph
parameters.summary: The DirectShow filter graph from which to remove all filters.

methods.name: DSIsFilePlayable
methods.summary: Determines whether the specified media file can be played using DirectShow.
methods.remarks: This method attempts to build a filter graph for the specified file to determine playability. It automatically selects the x86 or x64 implementation based on the current process architecture.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The path to the media file to check for playability.

parameters.name: errorCode
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains the error code if the file is not playable; otherwise, indicates success.

methods.returns: true if the file can be played; otherwise, false.

methods.name: DSRemoveFilter
methods.summary: Removes a specific filter from the DirectShow filter graph.
methods.remarks: This method automatically selects the x86 or x64 implementation based on the current process architecture.

parameters.name: pGraph
parameters.summary: The DirectShow filter graph from which to remove the filter.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.summary: The filter to remove from the graph.

classes.name: IPPAPI
classes.summary: Provides platform-agnostic wrappers for Intel Integrated Performance Primitives (IPP) library functions. This class automatically selects the appropriate x86 or x64 implementation based on the current process architecture.

classes.name: LAVHelperMFP
classes.summary: Provides helper methods for LAV Filters integration with Media Framework Primitives (MFP). This class automatically selects the appropriate x86 or x64 implementation based on the current process architecture.
classes.remarks: LAV Filters (ffmpeg based DirectShow splitter and decoders) provide advanced media playback capabilities. All methods in this class delegate to platform-specific implementations in MFPCoreX86 or MFPCoreX64.

methods.name: LAV_EnableAllFormats
methods.summary: Enables all supported media formats in the LAV Filters splitter or decoder.
methods.remarks: This method configures the LAV Filter to accept and process all supported media format types. It automatically selects the x86 or x64 implementation based on the current process architecture.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.summary: The LAV Filter instance to configure.

methods.returns: Zero on success; otherwise, an error code.

methods.name: LAV_AudioSet16BitOnly
methods.summary: Configures the LAV Audio decoder to output only 16-bit audio samples.
methods.remarks: This method restricts the LAV Audio decoder output to 16-bit PCM format, which can improve compatibility with certain audio pipelines. It automatically selects the x86 or x64 implementation based on the current process architecture.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.summary: The LAV Audio decoder instance to configure.

methods.returns: Zero on success; otherwise, an error code.

methods.name: LAV_IsAvailable
methods.summary: Determines whether LAV Filters are available and can be used on the current system.
methods.remarks: This method checks if the LAV Filters library is installed and accessible for the current platform architecture. It automatically selects the x86 or x64 implementation based on the current process architecture.
methods.returns: true if LAV Filters are available; otherwise, false.

classes.name: MFPArm64Resolver
classes.summary: Loads the ARM64 builds of VisioForge_MFP, VisioForge_MFPX, VisioForge_DXP and MediaInfo in an ARM64 process, where every P/Invoke into them, declared against the x64 file names, would otherwise find no loadable file.
classes.remarks: .NET Framework has no DllImport resolver: there an ARM64 process still fails to load them.

classes.name: MFPVideoEffectsProcessor
classes.summary: Provides video effects processing functionality for Media Framework Primitives (MFP). Implements IDisposable to properly manage native resources.
classes.remarks: This class is the central processor for applying video effects to individual video frames. It supports a wide variety of effects including color adjustments, filters, logos, deinterlacing, denoising, and transformations. The processor maintains internal buffers for frame history (used by temporal effects like denoising), temporary processing buffers, and state for zoom/pan effects. Implements the disposable pattern to properly clean up all native memory allocations.

constructors.name: MFPVideoEffectsProcessor
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MFPVideoEffectsProcessor class.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: The context instance for logging and error reporting.

methods.name: Finalize
methods.summary: Finalizes an instance of the MFPVideoEffectsProcessor class.
methods.remarks: Calls Dispose(false) to clean up unmanaged resources if the object wasn't explicitly disposed.

methods.name: Process
methods.summary: Processes the specified video frame by applying the given video effect.
methods.remarks: This overload extracts frame data from a VideoFrame object.

methods.name: Process
methods.summary: Processes the specified video frame by applying the given video effects in order.
methods.remarks: Most effects walk the frame at the DIB stride, so a frame at any other stride is processed as a copy at it, once for all the effects (#3084).

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: The RGB24 video frame to process, at any row stride.

methods.name: Process
methods.summary: Processes video frame data by applying the specified video effect.
methods.remarks: This is the core processing method that handles all effect types.Supported effects include:Color effects: Grayscale, Invert, FilterRed/Green/Blue, Red/Green/Blue, Saturation, Contrast, Lightness, DarknessFilters: Blur, Sharpen, Mosaic, Posterize, Solarize, Spray, ColorNoise, MonoNoiseTransforms: FlipHorizontal, FlipVertical, MirrorHorizontal, MirrorVertical, RotateOverlays: TextLogo, ScrollingTextLogo, ImageLogoDenoising: DenoiseMosquito, DenoiseAdaptive, DenoiseCASTDeinterlacing: DeinterlaceBlend, DeinterlaceCAVT, DeinterlaceTriangleAnimation: FadeIn, FadeOut, Zoom, Pan, ShakeDownColor grading: LUTEffects are only applied when the current timestamp falls within the effect's StartTime and StopTime range.

parameters.name: data
parameters.summary: Pointer to the frame data (RGB24 format).

parameters.name: dataSize
parameters.summary: Size of the frame data in bytes. A frame shorter than its rows at stride is left alone, with a warning.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: Width of the frame in pixels. A frame with no pixels is left alone.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: Height of the frame in pixels. A frame with no rows is left alone; a negative (top-down) height is not supported and is left alone, with a warning.

parameters.name: stride
parameters.summary: Row stride of the frame in bytes, at least one row of pixels. Most effects walk the frame at the DIB stride (Int32)), so a frame at another stride is processed as a copy at it, once per call; the VideoFrameX overload copies once for the whole chain.

parameters.name: videoEffect
parameters.summary: The video effect instance to apply.

parameters.name: timeStamp
parameters.summary: The timestamp of the current frame.

parameters.name: bgr
parameters.summary: Whether the pixels are stored B,G,R, as in a DirectShow RGB24 frame. Only the LUT effect reads it.

methods.name: ResetHistory
methods.summary: Frees a temporal effect's frames, so it starts over the next time it runs. Called for an effect skipped on a frame, disabled or out of its time window, by the engines too: they skip such an effect without calling the processor.

parameters.name: videoEffect
parameters.summary: The effect; one without a history is ignored.

methods.name: ResetHistories
methods.summary: Frees every temporal effect's frames, so effects switched off as a whole start over when switched on again. Called by the engines on their streaming thread for every frame the effects are off.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Performs application-defined tasks associated with freeing, releasing, or resetting unmanaged resources.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases unmanaged and optionally managed resources.
methods.remarks: Frees all native memory buffers including temporary frames, logo buffers, frame history, and destroys zoom/pan native objects.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources - none at .NET Framework process exit, where a graph left running may still use them and the OS reclaims them.

methods.name: IsMerged
methods.summary: Whether the effect is on one of the merged canvases, so the per-frame path does not draw it again.

methods.name: ReleaseMergedImageLogos
methods.summary: Frees the merged image-logo canvas and its temp buffer and forgets which logos were on it.

methods.name: ReleaseMergedLogosOnSizeChange
methods.summary: Frees both merged canvases when the frame size differs from the one they were drawn for (#3390).

methods.name: ReleaseMergedTextLogos
methods.summary: Frees the merged text-logo canvas and its temp buffer and forgets which logos were on it.

classes.name: Processors
classes.summary: Provides extension methods for processing various video effect types on raw video frame data.
classes.remarks: This static class contains Process extension methods that apply specific video effects to RGB24 frame data. Each method processes the pixel data in-place, modifying the original buffer. Supported effect categories include: Color adjustments: LUT, Grayscale, Red/Green/Blue channels, Contrast, Saturation, Lightness, DarknessFilters: Blur, Sharpen, Mosaic, Posterize, Solarize, Spray, NoiseTransforms: Flip, Mirror, Rotate, Zoom, PanDenoising: DenoiseCAST, DenoiseAdaptive, DenoiseMosquitoDeinterlacing: DeinterlaceBlend, DeinterlaceCAVT, DeinterlaceTriangleOverlays: TextLogo, ScrollingTextLogo, ImageLogoTransitions: FadeIn, FadeOut Many effects support animated values through StartTime/StopTime and Value/ValueStop parameters, allowing the effect intensity to change smoothly over time.

classes.summary: Provides high-performance image resizing functionality using Media Framework Primitives (MFP). Implements the IDisposable pattern to properly manage native resources.

parameters.summary: If set to true, performs an initial resize operation to warm up the processor (useful for benchmarking or initialization).

parameters.name: videoResizeMode
parameters.summary: The video resize mode (e.g., Nearest, Bilinear, Bicubic). Default is Bilinear.

parameters.name: antialiasing

methods.name: Process
methods.summary: Processes and resizes the specified source image to the destination image.
methods.remarks: The source and destination image parameters must match the dimensions and format specified during construction. This method is thread-safe and can be called multiple times on different image data with the same resize configuration.

parameters.name: destImage
parameters.summary: The destination image that will receive the resized output.

methods.returns: true if the resize operation was successful; false if the object was disposed or an error occurred.

methods.name: NvCVImage_Transfer
methods.summary: Transfer one image to another, with a limited set of conversions.
methods.remarks: If any of the images resides on the GPU, it may run asynchronously, so cudaStreamSynchronize() should be called if it is necessary to run synchronously. The following table indicates (with X) the currently-implemented conversions: +-------------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+ | | u8 --> u8 | u8 --> f32 | f32 --> u8 | f32 --> f32 | +-------------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+ | Y --> Y | X | | X | X | | Y --> A | X | | X | X | | Y --> RGB | X | X | X | X | | Y --> RGBA | X | X | X | X | | A --> Y | X | | X | X | | A --> A | X | | X | X | | A --> RGB | X | X | X | X | | A --> RGBA | X | | | | | RGB --> Y | X | X | | | | RGB --> A | X | X | | | | RGB --> RGB | X | X | X | X | | RGB --> RGBA | X | X | X | X | | RGBA --> Y | X | X | | | | RGBA --> A | X | | | | | RGBA --> RGB | X | X | X | X | | RGBA --> RGBA | X | X | X | X | | RGB --> YUV420 | X | | X | | | RGBA --> YUV420 | X | | X | | | RGB --> YUV422 | X | | X | | | RGBA --> YUV422 | X | | X | | | RGB --> YUV444 | X | | X | | | RGBA --> YUV444 | X | | X | | | YUV420 --> RGB | X | X | | | | YUV420 --> RGBA | X | X | | | | YUV422 --> RGB | X | X | | | | YUV422 --> RGBA | X | X | | | | YUV444 --> RGB | X | X | | | | YUV444 --> RGBA | X | X | | | +-------------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+ where * Either source or destination can be CHUNKY or PLANAR. * Either source or destination can reside on the CPU or the GPU. * The RGB components are in any order (i.e. RGB or BGR; RGBA or BGRA). * For RGBA (or BGRA) destinations, most implementations do not change the alpha channel, so it is recommended to set it at initialization time with [cuda]memset(im.pixels, -1, im.pitch * im.height) or [cuda]memset(im.pixels, -1, im.pitch * im.height * im.numComponents) for chunky and planar images respectively. * YUV requires that the colorspace field be set manually prior to Transfer, e.g. typical for layout=NVCV_NV12: image.colorspace = NVCV_709 | NVCV_VIDEO_RANGE | NVCV_CHROMA_INTSTITIAL; * There are also RGBf16-->RGBf32 and RGBf32-->RGBf16 transfers. * Additionally, when the src and dst formats are the same, all formats are accommodated on CPU and GPU, and this can be used as a replacement for cudaMemcpy2DAsync() (which it utilizes). This is also true for YUV, whose src and dst must share the same format, layout and colorspace. When there is some kind of conversion AND the src and dst reside on different processors (CPU, GPU), it is necessary to have a temporary GPU buffer, which is reshaped as needed to match the characteristics of the CPU image. The same temporary image can be used in subsequent calls to NvCVImage_Transfer(), regardless of the shape, format or component type, as it will grow as needed to accommodate the largest memory requirement. The recommended usage for most cases is to supply an empty image as the temporary; if it is not needed, no buffer is allocated. NULL can be supplied as the tmp image, in which case an ephemeral buffer is allocated if needed, with resultant performance degradation for image sequences.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.summary: The scale factor that can be applied when one (but not both) of the images is based on floating-point components; this parameter is ignored when all image components are represented with integer data types, or all image components are represented with floating-point data types.

parameters.name: tmp
parameters.summary: The temporary buffer that is sometimes needed when transferring images between the CPU and GPU in either direction (can be empty or NULL). It has the same characteristics as the CPU image, but it resides on the GPU.

methods.returns: NvCVStatus. NVCV_SUCCESS - if successful. NVCV_ERR_PIXELFORMAT - if one of the pixel formats is not accommodated. NVCV_ERR_CUDA - if a CUDA error has occurred. NVCV_ERR_GENERAL - if an otherwise unspecified error has occurred.

methods.name: NvCVImage_MapResource
methods.summary: Between rendering by a graphics system and Transfer by CUDA, it is necessary to map the texture resource. There is a fair amount of overhead, so its use should be minimized. Every call to NvCVImage_MapResource() should be matched by a subsequent call to NvCVImage_UnmapResource().

parameters.name: stream
parameters.summary: The CUDA stream on which the mapping is to be performed.

methods.returns: NvCVStatus. NVCV_SUCCESS is the operation was completed successfully.

methods.name: NvCVImage_Composite
methods.summary: Composite one source image over another using the given matte. This accommodates all RGB and RGBA formats, with u8 and f32 components.
methods.remarks: Though RGBA destinations are accommodated, the A channel is not updated at all.

parameters.name: mat
parameters.summary: The matte Yu8 (or Au8) image, indicating where the src should come through.

parameters.name: dst
parameters.summary: The destination image. This can be the same as fg or bg.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.summary: The CUDA stream on which the composition is to be performed.

methods.returns: NvCVStatus. NVCV_SUCCESS if the operation was successful. NVCV_ERR_PIXELFORMAT if the pixel format is not accommodated. NVCV_ERR_MISMATCH if either the fg & bg & dst formats do not match, or if fg & bg & dst & mat are not in the same address space (CPU or GPU).

methods.name: NvCVImage_CompositeRect
methods.summary: Composite one source image over another using the given matte. This accommodates all RGB and RGBA formats, with u8 and f32 components.
methods.remarks: If a smaller region of a matte is desired, a window can be created using NvCVImage_InitView() for chunky or NvCVImage_Init() for planar pixels. in the same address space (CPU or GPU). BUG: Though RGBA destinations are accommodated, the A channel is not updated at all.

parameters.name: fgOrg
parameters.summary: The upper-left corner of the fg image to be composited (NULL implies (0,0)).

parameters.name: bgOrg
parameters.summary: The upper-left corner of the bg image to be composited (NULL implies (0,0)).

parameters.name: mat
parameters.summary: The matte image, indicating where the src should come through. This determines the size of the rectangle to be composited. If this is multi-channel, the alpha channel is used as the matte.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.summary: The composition mode: 0 (straight alpha over) or 1 (premultiplied alpha over).

parameters.name: dst
parameters.summary: The destination image. This can be the same as fg or bg.

parameters.name: dstOrg
parameters.summary: The upper-left corner of the dst image to be updated (NULL implies (0,0)).

parameters.name: stream
parameters.summary: The CUDA stream on which the composition is to be performed.

methods.returns: NvCVStatus. NVCV_SUCCESS if the operation was successful. NVCV_ERR_PIXELFORMAT if the pixel format is not accommodated. NVCV_ERR_MISMATCH if either the fg & bg & dst formats do not match, or if fg & bg & dst & mat are not

methods.name: NvCVImage_CompositeOverConstant
methods.summary: Composite a source image over a constant color field using the given matte.
methods.remarks: The bgColor must remain valid until complete; this is an important consideration especially if the buffers are on the GPU and NvCVImage_CompositeOverConstant() runs asynchronously. Though RGBA destinations are accommodated, the A channel is not updated at all.

parameters.name: mat
parameters.summary: The matte image, indicating where the src should come through.

parameters.name: bgColor

parameters.name: dst
parameters.summary: The destination image. May be the same as src.

methods.returns: NvCVStatus. NVCV_SUCCESS if the operation was successful. NVCV_ERR_PIXELFORMAT if the pixel format is not accommodated. NVCV_ERR_MISMATCH if fg & mat & dst & bgColor are not in the same address space (CPU or GPU).

methods.name: NvCVImage_FlipY
methods.summary: Flip the image vertically. No actual pixels are moved: it is just an accounting procedure. This is extremely low overhead, but requires appropriate interpretation of the pitch. Flipping twice yields the original orientation.

classes.name: MJPEGSource
classes.summary: Provides functionality to connect to and receive video frames from an MJPEG (Motion JPEG) stream over HTTP.
classes.remarks: This class downloads JPEG images from a specified URL representing an MJPEG stream. Each received frame is parsed from the multipart HTTP response and raised through the event.The class handles various MJPEG stream formats including multipart/x-mixed-replace and application/octet-stream.Note: Some cameras produce HTTP headers that do not conform strictly to standards, which may lead to .NET exceptions. To avoid this, set the useUnsafeHeaderParsing configuration option in your application configuration file.

methods.summary: Starts receiving video frames from the MJPEG stream.
methods.remarks: Starts the video source and returns execution to the caller. The video source creates a background thread and notifies about new frames through the NewFrame event.

methods.name: SignalToStop
methods.summary: Signals the video source to stop receiving frames.
methods.remarks: Signals the video source to stop its background thread, stop providing new frames, and free resources. This method returns immediately; use WaitForStop to wait for the thread to actually stop.

methods.name: WaitForStop
methods.summary: Waits for the video source to stop after SignalToStop has been called.
methods.remarks: This method blocks until the background thread has completely stopped. Call SignalToStop before calling this method.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops the video source immediately.
methods.remarks: This method signals the video source to stop and waits for the background thread to terminate.Note: The preferred way to stop the video source is to call and then to allow graceful shutdown.
