properties.name: FSeparateCaptureStarted
properties.summary: Separate capture status. A segment that ends is no longer paused (#1738): clearing this clears FSeparateCapturePaused, so no teardown path can leave a stale pause behind.

properties.name: FSeparateCapturePaused
properties.summary: Separate capture pause status. Only a started segment can be paused (#1739): a pause flag with nothing recording would let a resume run the stopped graph over the finished file. A segment that stops being paused is no longer paused by the application either.

properties.name: HasCustomWindow
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the application gave a custom window that still exists. The handle is kept across stops, so the window may have been destroyed since (#3059).

properties.name: TeardownDeferredOnThisThread
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether a Stop() or Dispose() pumped on this thread was deferred until the serialized operation it arrived in has left the lock.

properties.name: SeparateCaptureTeardownPending
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this separate-capture call must not start a file a deferred Stop or Dispose would only finish empty (#1932). A Dispose on another thread sets _disposing before it waits for the lock; a Stop or Dispose pumped on this thread is recorded in TeardownDeferredOnThisThread.

properties.name: Debug_IsStopping
properties.summary: True while a stop is between publishing _stopping and clearing it. A test throws from OnVideoFrameBitmap only in that window (#1733).

properties.name: NeedsGraphPump
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the graph has to live on _graphPump.

properties.name: BuildsMadVR
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether a start builds a madVR renderer: a main one only with a view or a custom window, and extra screens as built - each took the setting MultiScreen_AddScreen was called under (#3059). madVR owns its window on the thread that builds the graph and sends to it from its final release (#3038), so StartAsync refuses it.

properties.name: CallerWillNotPump
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the calling thread will not be pumping messages for as long as the graph lives, so the graph has to be built on _graphPump instead.

properties.name: CallerRunsMessageLoop
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the calling thread runs a message loop that dispatches window messages, as the low-level input hooks need: a WinForms or WPF UI thread.

properties.name: StartInFlight
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether a start is published and has not returned yet. Wider than _starting, which CommitStart clears while the start is still finishing. Read under _pipDeviceLock for a decision.

properties.name: SeparateAdditionalAudioInputCount
properties.summary: Additional audio devices recorded as tracks of their own. With Additional_Audio_CaptureDevice_MixChannels the one device in the list already feeds the audio mixer, whose output is the main audio, so it adds no track. The devices add no track either when they are out of the writer's reach: built in the main graph while a separate capture writes from its own graph, or already connected to the WMV network streaming encoder.

properties.name: AdditionalAudioOutOfWriterReach
properties.summary: True when the additional audio devices cannot reach the AVI/MKVv1/WMV writer; see SeparateAdditionalAudioInputCount.

properties.name: Video_Still_Frames_Grabber_Enabled
properties.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether video still frames grabber enabled. The grabber connects to the device's still pin (the hardware snapshot button) and raises OnStillVideoFrameBitmap and OnStillVideoFrameBuffer. A device without a still pin raises neither event and reports an error at start; use Frame_GetCurrent or OnVideoFrameBuffer to take frames from the stream.

properties.name: SeparateCaptureStopRunning
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether a capture stop is between setting _stopping and releasing the graphs. Any thread is refused in that window - a re-entrant call pumped inside the stop's own STA IMediaControl.Stop() too - and admitted after it, so an OnStop handler can still stop separate capture from whatever thread it marshals to (#1724).

properties.name: WindowsFileWriterName
properties.summary: Gets the Windows writer behind the current format - the File Writer or the WM ASF Writer - which opens at most MaxWindowsWriterPath characters; null for a format written by any other writer. A custom output is known only once this session has built its encoder, so not during the start, where the field may still hold the previous session's.

properties.name: SeparateCaptureCanSwitch
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the output can switch files on the fly now. The same decision as IVFAVEncoder@) without building its reason: the split check reads it for every frame.

properties.name: IsDeviceDirectCapture
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the output is the device flavour of DirectCapture, which writes Output_Filename from inside the graph from the moment the capture starts. The IP-camera flavour records through the ffmpeg side-car, which is built only in IPCapture mode. Latched by StartGraph, so a Mode change during the capture does not reclassify it.

properties.name: SeparateCaptureDefersFile
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the recording is named by SeparateCapture_Start rather than by Output_Filename: separate capture with autostart off. Device DirectCapture writes from the moment the graph runs, so it does not defer.

properties.name: TagsSupportedForMode
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether tags are set and the mode the graph was built in writes them to its output files.

properties.name: AudioCaptureLatency
properties.summary: Audio capture buffer length for every capture device: CustomLatency, or 100 ms when it is 0.

methods.name: CreateAsync
methods.summary: Creates a new instance of VideoCaptureCore asynchronously with a video view.
methods.remarks: This factory method creates and initializes a VideoCaptureCore instance asynchronously. Use this method when you need to avoid blocking the UI thread during initialization. The video view is attached during creation and will be used for video rendering.

parameters.name: videoView
parameters.summary: The video view control where captured video will be displayed.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous creation operation. The task result contains the initialized VideoCaptureCore instance.

methods.name: CreateAsync
methods.summary: Creates a new instance of VideoCaptureCore asynchronously without a video view.
methods.remarks: This factory method creates and initializes a VideoCaptureCore instance asynchronously. Use this overload when you don't need video preview or will attach a video view later. This is useful for scenarios like audio-only capture or background processing.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous creation operation. The task result contains the initialized VideoCaptureCore instance.

methods.name: InitAsync
methods.summary: Initializes the video capture control asynchronously.
methods.remarks: This internal method wraps the synchronous Init method in a Task for asynchronous execution. It's used by the CreateAsync factory methods to avoid blocking the calling thread.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous initialization operation.

methods.name: Init
methods.summary: Initializes the video capture control with default settings and configurations.
methods.remarks: This method performs comprehensive initialization including: - Setting up logging and telemetry - Configuring local redistributables (codecs, filters) - Initializing DirectShow components and filter caches - Setting default video renderer based on OS version - Configuring default audio/video settings - Loading system codecs and profiles - Setting up device notifiers for plug-and-play support - Initializing effects processors and DSP components This method should only be called once during the lifetime of the instance.

methods.name: DisposeAsync
methods.summary: Performs application-defined tasks associated with freeing, releasing, or resetting unmanaged resources asynchronously.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous dispose operation.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Dispose method.
methods.remarks: This method implements the IDisposable pattern and ensures proper cleanup: - Stops any active capture or preview - Releases all DirectShow filters and COM objects - Clears event handlers and callbacks - Frees unmanaged resources This method can be called multiple times safely. For async operations, use DisposeAsync instead. Called while Start() or StartAsync() is still building the graph, it returns straight away and the release is carried out by that start when it returns; the start then reports false. The same applies to DisposeAsync. Called on the thread of a Pause, Resume, StartDelayed, String) or SeparateCapture_* call still in progress - a window close pumped inside it - it returns at once as well, and that call carries the release out before it returns and then returns false. Called on two threads at once, one of them stops and releases the engine and the other returns at once, possibly while that release is still running. The finalizer never releases an engine this method or DisposeAsync has been called on: when the release fails or is declined, call Dispose again. Until then the engine is good only for that call: OnError is no longer raised and the output methods return false, because the graph is still being torn down by another thread.

methods.name: DeferDisposeToStart
methods.summary: Hands a dispose issued while Start or StartAsync is in flight to that start, before it changes anything.
methods.remarks: See String) for why it cannot run now. Decided under the lock the start leaves under, so exactly one of the two runs the teardown (#1663).
methods.returns: true when the dispose was deferred and the caller must return at once.

methods.name: TryClaimDispose
methods.summary: Claims the teardown for this dispose and marks the engine as disposing.
methods.remarks: One step under the lock String) counts under, so a start either got in first and the dispose is deferred to it, or sees _disposing and is refused. The check at the dispose's entry alone leaves a start slipping in between it and the claim, building a graph that DisposeCore then releases (#1917). _disposing stays set when the teardown fails, so a start stays refused then as well.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: false on the finalizer path, which neither defers nor locks.

methods.returns: true when this call owns the teardown; false when it was deferred to a start or another dispose already owns it, and the caller must return.

methods.name: WaitForStopToFinish
methods.summary: Waits for a stop running on another thread to finish before the graph is released.
methods.remarks: StopIntl no-ops when a stop is already in progress, so without this wait DisposeCore's Clear() would call Marshal.ReleaseComObject on the filter graph while the stopping thread is still inside IMediaControl.Stop() - an uncatchable 0xC0000005 (issue #841). The wait is bounded: a filter that never returns from Stop must not make Dispose hang forever.

methods.name: ReleaseOnPumpFromFinalizer
methods.summary: The finalizer's stop and release, run on the pump thread that owns the graph (#1939).

parameters.name: wasActive
parameters.summary: Whether there was a graph or a start to stop.

methods.returns: false only when it declined to release, so the pump keeps the graph.

methods.name: TryEnterStopGate
methods.summary: Claims the graph for a stop, before that stop is queued. Two callers must not both see no stop running and both queue a full teardown - that is a second OnStop to customer code, a second WriteTags over the finished file, a second Clear(). StopIntl's own _stopping check cannot catch that pair either: it is read outside _stopLock, and both would pass it before either reached StopMain.
methods.returns: true when the caller now owns the stop and must release it.

methods.name: LeaveStopGate
methods.summary: Drops that mark once the stop has fully unwound, from StopIntl's finally - after the UI marshalling in its tail, not before it. That tail tears the video view down, so a Start admitted there would bring the preview up only for this stop to kill it again.

methods.name: DeferDisposeToSerializedOperation
methods.summary: Records a Dispose() pumped on this thread inside a serialized operation, for that operation to carry out once it has left the lock: disposing here would release the graph under the operation's COM call (#1896).
methods.returns: true when the dispose was deferred and the caller must return at once.

methods.name: Debug_CountGraphChangeWhileStopping
methods.summary: Counts a main-graph state change the stop serialization let through (#1727).

methods.name: Debug_WaitBeforeCommitStart
methods.summary: Blocks a test that has to call separate capture in the window before the engine is marked started (#2018).

methods.name: Debug_WaitBeforePumpBuild
methods.summary: Blocks a test that has to start again while the first start's pump has not begun the build (#2918).

methods.name: EnterStart
methods.summary: Counts a start in, so a dispose arriving before it has returned is deferred to it.
methods.remarks: A dispose issued while a start is still running - from a handler the build raised on its own thread, from the UI thread the build is marshalling onto, or from anywhere else - cannot run then: the build is still using what it would release, _starting is not a stop the dispose may run beside, and waiting for the build from the UI thread deadlocks against the build's own calls onto it (#1663).

parameters.name: tag
parameters.summary: The public method, for the refusal line.

methods.returns: false when a Dispose has claimed the engine or is deferred to a start still in flight: the start is refused and not counted, because the graph it would build is released by that dispose (#1917). Decided under the lock Boolean) claims under.

methods.name: LeaveStart
methods.summary: Counts a start out, and carries out a dispose deferred to it when it is the last one.
methods.returns: true when the engine is being disposed, so the start must report false. The dispose ran here, unless another one already holds the engine and runs it instead.

methods.name: HasExtraScreen``1
methods.summary: Gets a value indicating whether an extra screen is built with the given renderer. Each screen takes the renderer the setting named when MultiScreen_AddScreen was called, not the one it names now (#3059).

methods.name: StartOnPumpThread
methods.summary: Builds and runs the graph on a dedicated message-pumping thread that lives until the graph is torn down.
methods.returns: See Start.

methods.name: ReleasePreviousPump
methods.summary: Joins and releases a pump left by an earlier start, before a new graph is built. Called under a start's claim, so no other start can publish a pump meanwhile.
methods.remarks: A pump left over from a run that ended normally is reclaimed by the stop that ended it, unless that stop ran on the pump itself: the thread is then still exiting.
methods.returns: false when the start is refused and reported: that pump's thread is still running after the bounded join - its teardown is wedged, and a graph must not be built over the COM state it is still using - or the caller is that very thread, a handler it raised.

methods.name: TryRunOnPumpThread
methods.summary: Marshals action onto the graph pump thread when one is active.

parameters.name: pump
parameters.summary: The pump to marshal onto, as the caller captured it.

parameters.name: action
parameters.summary: Work to run on the graph pump thread.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.summary: When true, block until the action completes; otherwise post it.

parameters.name: queued
parameters.summary: true when the pump took the action, which means it WILL run - on the message loop or on the drain at thread exit - even when this method returns false because the bounded wait elapsed first. A caller that must not run the teardown twice has to read this rather than the return value alone.

methods.returns: true if the work ran to completion on that thread; false when there is no live pump thread, or the bounded wait elapsed while it was still queued.

methods.name: ReclaimGraphPump
methods.summary: Ends and reclaims the graph pump thread after its teardown has been marshalled onto it.
methods.remarks: A thread that is genuinely wedged keeps its reference: ownership is not dropped, an error is logged, and a later Stop or Start can retry. That is the bounded lesser evil against an unbounded hang.

parameters.name: pump
parameters.summary: The pump instance captured by the caller.

methods.returns: true if the thread exited and was disposed, or if the caller IS that thread and it is past the graph build - the loop has then been told to end and the caller may release the graph. false if the thread is still running - wedged, or the caller's own thread still inside the build - and was retained: callers must then NOT release the graph's COM objects, which that live thread is still using.

methods.name: ReportTeardownDiagnostic
methods.summary: Reports something that went wrong while tearing the graph down, WITHOUT routing it through Context.Error on the calling thread.
methods.remarks: Every line these paths write is written precisely when a thread is wedged, and Context.Error reaches OnErrorCall -> _videoView.CallInvoke, a synchronous marshal with no timeout, onto a UI thread that may itself be blocked inside the very Dispose writing the line. The engine log and OnError still get it, from a pool thread. (MediaPlayerCore reports the same class of line the same way.)

methods.name: StopThroughPump
methods.summary: Runs the teardown on the graph pump thread when the graph was built there, and reclaims that thread afterwards.
methods.remarks: The graph window belongs to the pump thread, so releasing the renderer from anywhere else blocks on a SendMessage that thread would have to answer. The pump is ended and reclaimed whether or not the marshalled teardown ran in time, so a timed-out Invoke can never orphan the thread. The caller is told to stand down in three cases, not one: the teardown ran there; it was taken and will still run there (the bounded wait elapsed first, reachable because StopMain's KLV drain is unbounded and InvokeStop marshals to the UI thread); or the thread is wedged. Repeating it inline in any of those would raise OnStop twice, write the tags twice and call Clear over released RCWs - the stop gate serializes stops, it does not make one idempotent.

parameters.name: pumpWedged
parameters.summary: true when the pump thread was still running after the bounded join. Its COM objects must then NOT be released by anyone else - that thread is still using them - so a caller about to tear the engine down has to stop there and leave them to it.

methods.returns: true when the caller has nothing left to do; false when the caller must run the teardown itself.

methods.name: StartAsync
methods.summary: Builds the DirectShow graph and starts capture or preview asynchronously.
methods.remarks: Screen capture's mouse highlight and OnScreenCaptureMouseClick / OnScreenCaptureKeyDown need this awaited on a UI thread that runs a message loop.
methods.returns: A task that resolves to true when the graph is running, or false on error. Also false when a Stop or StopAsync is still running, including when called from an OnStop handler: await the stop first. Also false when StopAsync was called while the graph was being built, or the engine was disposed then - it is disposed before the task completes. Also false while another Start or StartAsync has not returned yet, including from a handler that start raised. Also false when an OnStart handler, or a video view's start-complete notification, throws: the capture is stopped, raising OnStop - before the task completes, unless a stop already running carries it out. Also false once Dispose or DisposeAsync has begun releasing the engine, including from an OnStop handler that dispose raised, or while a dispose waits for another start still in flight; a release that failed does not lift this - call Dispose again. Not compatible with madVR renderer — use Start for that renderer.

methods.name: StartAsyncIntl
methods.summary: The body of StartAsync.
methods.returns: See StartAsync.

methods.name: InstallScreenHooks
methods.summary: Installs the screen-capture mouse and keyboard hooks on the calling thread, once a start has returned.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.summary: The public method, for the warning line.

methods.name: Start
methods.summary: Builds the DirectShow graph and starts capture or preview synchronously.
methods.remarks: Screen capture's mouse highlight and OnScreenCaptureMouseClick / OnScreenCaptureKeyDown need this called on a UI thread that runs a message loop. Called over a capture that is running, paused or waiting for , this stops that capture first and raises inside this call. From that handler: Start is refused.Dispose cancels this start: it returns false and builds nothing.Stop cancels it the same way, but only when the capture being replaced was started with Start. Over one started with , Stop is the wrong API and StopAsync is declined, because the stop raising the event is still running.
methods.returns: true when the graph is running, or false on configuration or graph-build error. Also false when a Stop or StopAsync is still running, including when called from an OnStop handler: that stop still owns the graph, so await it before starting again. Also false when a stop was requested while the graph was being built: it is torn down before this returns. Also false while another Start or StartAsync has not returned yet, including from a handler that start raised. Also false while a capture is running with the legacy Video Renderer or madVR selected when that capture or this call comes from a thread that is not STA (a thread-pool or other worker thread): call Stop first. Also false when an OnStart handler, or a video view's start-complete notification, throws: the capture is stopped, raising OnStop - before this returns, unless a stop already running carries it out. Also false when the engine was disposed while the graph was being built: it is disposed before this returns. Also false once Dispose or DisposeAsync has begun releasing the engine, including from an OnStop handler that dispose raised, or while a dispose waits for another start still in flight; a release that failed does not lift this - call Dispose again.

methods.name: BeginStart
methods.summary: Publishes a start: under the PiP lock, because a PiP mutator checks these flags and changes the list inside the same lock, so none can be half-way through a change once the build starts reading the list (#1569).
methods.returns: The task source that completes when this start has returned, or null when another start has not returned yet: it owns the graph (#2906).

methods.name: ClaimStart
methods.summary: Claims a start for Start, or reports why it is refused.
methods.remarks: A running capture is refused on the pump path - its pump would be quit with the graph still on it - and on the inline path when it runs on a pump: that pump would stay published, and the next Stop would go through it instead of reaching the graph built here (#2918).

parameters.name: onPumpPath
parameters.summary: true when the graph is to be built on the graph pump.

parameters.name: overStarted
parameters.summary: true when the claim replaces a started capture, which the start stops first (#2953).

methods.returns: The claim, or null when the start was refused and reported.

methods.name: EndStart
methods.summary: Ends a start published by BeginStart, on every way out of it.

parameters.name: startFinished
parameters.summary: The task source that start returned.

methods.name: RefuseStart
methods.summary: Reports a refused start on this thread: through OnError, and through Trace, since OnError drops it when the refused call comes from an error handler or once _disposing is set.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.summary: The public method, for the refusal line.

methods.returns: Always false.

methods.returns: false when the start is refused and reported.

methods.name: StartIntl
methods.summary: The body of Start().

parameters.name: claimedStart
parameters.summary: The start StartAsync() or StartOnPumpThread() already published, or null to publish one here.

parameters.name: onOwnPump
parameters.summary: true when StartOnPumpThread runs this on the pump it published for it.

methods.returns: See Start.

methods.name: StopAsync
methods.summary: Stops the running capture or preview graph asynchronously.
methods.returns: A task that completes when the graph has been torn down. Declined - and the task already completed - when nothing is running, when the synchronous API is in use, or when a stop is already running, which includes a call made from an OnStop handler. Awaiting a declined call therefore does not mean the graph is down. Called while StartAsync is still building, the stop is carried out by that start once the build is done, and the task completes when the start has returned.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops the running capture or preview graph synchronously.
methods.remarks: Does nothing when nothing is running (silently), when the asynchronous API is in use (reported - call StopAsync instead), or when a stop is already running, which includes a call made from an OnStop handler, where the stop in question is the one raising the event. Those checks run in that order, so on an engine started with StartAsync a Stop from the handler is reported as the wrong-API case. Called while Start is still building, it returns at once and that start tears the graph down itself once the build is done. That includes the OnStop a Start raises while stopping the capture it replaces: the call cancels that start, which returns false before it builds anything. Called from a handler pumped on the thread of a Pause, Resume, StartDelayed, String) or SeparateCapture_* call still in progress, it returns at once, and that call stops the capture before it returns and then returns false.

methods.name: RequestStopDuringStart
methods.summary: Records a stop that arrived while Start() is building, for Start() to carry out once the build is done. Stopping from here would tear the graph down under the build (GitHub issue #1646).
methods.returns: The task that completes when that Start() has returned, or null when no start is running.

methods.name: RequestStopOrEnterStopGate
methods.summary: Records the stop for a start in flight, or claims the stop gate - one step under the lock ClaimStart reads the gate under, so no start is admitted between the check and the claim (#2955).

parameters.name: claimed
parameters.summary: true when the caller now owns the stop and must release it.

methods.returns: The task that completes when the start in flight has returned, or null when no start is running.

methods.name: CommitStart
methods.summary: Publishes the engine as running, unless a stop was requested during the start. One step under the lock, so no stop can land between the check and the flags.
methods.returns: false when a stop was requested and the caller must tear the graph down.

parameters.name: gateHeld
parameters.summary: true when the caller already took the stop gate on this thread's behalf, which only Stop and StopAsync do - together with the start-in-flight check, so no start is admitted between the two (#2955); StopAsync also because the pool may not pick this method up for a while and a Start in that window would rebuild the graph under the stop about to run. Every other caller leaves it false and this method takes and releases the gate itself: the two must stay in one scope, or one of the internal StopIntl calls - a Start stopping the capture it replaces, Dispose, the separate-capture paths - would release a gate it never took, drive the count negative and refuse every later Start.

methods.name: StopViews
methods.summary: Calls InvokeStop on the video view and on every multi-screen view.

methods.name: StopMain
methods.summary: Tears the graphs down. Shared by the normal stop path and by the finalizer, so a graph added later cannot end up stopped on one path and released un-stopped on the other - which is how the MP4 bridge and the separate-capture graph were both missed.

parameters.name: raiseNotifications
parameters.summary: false on the finalizer path: OnStop runs customer code, and the process has a single finalizer thread to lose.

parameters.name: klvDrainTimeoutMs
parameters.summary: How long to wait for an in-flight native KLV write. OnDataFrameBufferKLV holds _klvWriteSync across WriteKLVData, so a stalled network peer can hold it indefinitely - the finalizer passes a bound rather than waiting forever.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: false only on the finalizer path. It skips the explicit-Dispose work and the view refresh, a synchronous IVideoView.CallRefresh to the UI thread (GitHub issue #1545).

methods.name: OutputFilename_ChangeOnTheFlyAsync
methods.summary: Changes the output filename on the fly during capture (async).
methods.remarks: The return value above describes an output without separate capture. For a capture whose output separate capture records (SeparateCapture_Enabled when it started, on an output and mode that support it), the call makes the switch SeparateCapture_ChangeFilenameOnTheFly makes, on the calling thread: the capture is not stopped, the return value and refusals are that method's, OnSeparateCaptureStopped is raised for the old file and OnSeparateCaptureStarted for the new one.
methods.returns: A task whose result is true if the capture records into the new file (a paused capture stays paused and records it once resumed); false if the output cannot change its file, the new file cannot be created, the writer refused the name, or the capture did not run or pause again afterwards. A file already at the new name is deleted before the capture stops, even when the call then returns false. A name refused before the capture stops leaves it recording to the current file; one the writer refuses after the stop leaves the capture stopped, the current file finished, until Stop or a later call that succeeds; Pause, Resume and StartDelayed are refused meanwhile, so nothing records over that file. Most refusals raise OnError; a call that overlaps a capture stop either completes before the stop takes the graph down or is refused with one. A call made while the capture is not started, once the stop has released the graph, or while the engine is being disposed returns false without one.

methods.returns: true if the capture records into the new file (a paused capture stays paused and records it once resumed); false if the output cannot change its file, the new file cannot be created, the writer refused the name, or the capture did not run or pause again afterwards. A file already at the new name is deleted before the capture stops, even when the call then returns false. A name refused before the capture stops leaves it recording to the current file; one the writer refuses after the stop leaves the capture stopped, the current file finished, until Stop or a later call that succeeds; Pause, Resume and StartDelayed are refused meanwhile, so nothing records over that file. methods.name: AddNetworkStreamingExternal
methods.summary: Configures external network streaming using third-party applications.
methods.remarks: This method sets up streaming through external applications like VLC or custom encoders. It creates a virtual camera output that can be captured by external streaming software. This approach provides flexibility to use any streaming software that supports camera input.

methods.name: AddNetworkStreamingFFMPEG
methods.summary: Adds network streaming (FFMPEG).
methods.remarks: This method configures network streaming using the FFMPEG executable in non-pipe mode. It supports custom FFMPEG arguments and various output muxers. Video and audio inputs are connected separately and pins are released after connection. For NuGet installations or custom redistribution, requires one-time admin registration.
methods.returns: true if FFMPEG network streaming was successfully configured; false if initialization failed.

methods.name: AddNetworkStreamingFFMPEGPipe
methods.summary: Adds network streaming (FFMPEG).
methods.remarks: This method configures network streaming using FFMPEG executable in pipe mode. Pipe mode provides better performance and lower latency than non-pipe mode. It uses named pipes to transfer data directly to FFMPEG without intermediate files. Supports the same customization options as non-pipe mode.
methods.returns: true if FFMPEG pipe network streaming was successfully configured; false if initialization failed.

methods.name: AddNetworkStreamingFFMPEG_InProc
methods.summary: Adds the in-process FFmpegSink-based network streaming output (parallel to AddNetworkStreamingFFMPEGPipe which spawns external vfffmpeg64.exe). Backs UDP_FFMPEG.
methods.remarks: libavformat (inside FFmpegSink) opens the destination via avio_open2, so Network_Streaming_URL may be a udp://<host>:<port>?pkt_size=<n> URL or any other protocol libavformat handles natively. Combined Output_Format = FFMPEGOutput + Network_Streaming_Output = FFMPEGOutput works because CaptureAddSplittersAndNetwork inserts a video/audio DSInfTee upstream of both consumers; by the time this method runs, dsVideoOutputPin / dsAudioOutputPin already point at the tee's second output pin (the first having been taken by Output_Format's AddOutputFFMPEGVideo). SMPTE KLV PTS preservation: when Network_Streaming_Output is FFMPEGOutput { OutputFormat: MPEG_TS_KLV }, the FFmpegSink writes KLV as synchronous (stream_id = METADATA_STREAM / 0xFC). KLV pump is wired by OnDataFrameBufferKLV in Sources.IPCamera.cs which writes to both dsFFMPEG (file) and dsFFMPEGNetworkStreamer (network) when present.
methods.returns: true on successful build; false if filter init or pin connection failed.

methods.name: AddNetworkStreamingHLS
methods.summary: Configures HTTP Live Streaming (HLS) for adaptive bitrate streaming.
methods.remarks: This method sets up HLS streaming, which creates segmented video files and a playlist. HLS is widely supported by mobile devices and web browsers. It provides adaptive bitrate streaming and supports live and on-demand content. The output consists of .m3u8 playlist files and .ts segment files.
methods.returns: true if HLS streaming was successfully configured; false if initialization failed.

methods.name: AddNetworkStreamingMJPEG
methods.summary: Configures Motion JPEG (MJPEG) network streaming.
methods.remarks: This method sets up MJPEG streaming over HTTP, suitable for web browsers and simple clients. MJPEG streams each frame as a separate JPEG image, providing good compatibility but higher bandwidth usage. The stream is accessible via HTTP on the specified port.
methods.returns: true if MJPEG streaming was successfully configured; false if initialization failed.

methods.name: AddNetworkStreamingMP4SW
methods.summary: Adds network streaming MP4 (software).
methods.remarks: This method configures software-based MP4 streaming using H.264 video and AAC audio codecs. It supports CPU and Intel Quick Sync Video (QSV) encoding modes. The video and audio pins are connected to the encoder and released after successful initialization.
methods.returns: true if the MP4 network streaming was successfully configured; false if initialization failed.

methods.name: AddNetworkStreamingNDI
methods.summary: Configures Network Device Interface (NDI) streaming.
methods.remarks: This method sets up NDI streaming for professional IP video production. NDI provides low-latency, high-quality video over IP networks. It automatically discovers NDI sources and receivers on the network. Requires the NDI runtime to be installed.
methods.returns: true if NDI streaming was successfully configured; false if initialization failed.

methods.name: AddNetworkStreamingWMV
methods.summary: Configures Windows Media Video (WMV) network streaming.
methods.remarks: This method sets up WMV streaming using Windows Media Format. WMV streaming is compatible with Windows Media Player and supports DRM. It provides good compression and quality for Windows-based clients. The encoder is configured with the specified profile and network settings.
methods.returns: true if WMV streaming was successfully configured; false if initialization failed.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Move
methods.summary: Moves an On-Screen Display (OSD) layer to a new position.
methods.remarks: This method updates the position of an existing OSD layer and re-renders all layers. The coordinates are relative to the top-left corner of the video frame. The video renderer must be initialized before calling this method.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the OSD layer to move.

parameters.name: x
parameters.summary: The new X coordinate (left position) for the layer.

parameters.name: y
parameters.summary: The new Y coordinate (top position) for the layer.

methods.returns: true if the layer was successfully moved; false if the operation failed or the ID is invalid.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Render
methods.summary: Renders all enabled On-Screen Display (OSD) layers to the video output.
methods.remarks: This method combines all enabled OSD layers into a single bitmap and applies it to the video renderer. It automatically clears the OSD if no layers are enabled. The method requires the video to be playing or in preview mode, and the video dimensions must be known. The rendered OSD will match the video dimensions for proper overlay alignment.
methods.returns: true if the layers were successfully rendered; false if rendering failed or no layers are enabled.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Clear
methods.summary: Clears all On-Screen Display (OSD) layers from the collection and removes any overlay from the video.
methods.remarks: This method removes all OSD layers and creates a transparent overlay to clear any existing OSD from the video. Use this method to completely reset the OSD system. After calling this method, you'll need to create new layers if you want to display OSD again.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Enable
methods.summary: Enables or disables a specific On-Screen Display (OSD) layer.
methods.remarks: Disabled layers remain in memory but are not rendered to the video output. Call OSD_Layers_Render after changing the enabled state to see the effect. If the ID is invalid, an error will be logged but no exception will be thrown.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the OSD layer to enable or disable.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.summary: If true, the layer will be rendered; if false, it will be hidden.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Clear
methods.summary: Clears the content of a specific On-Screen Display (OSD) layer.
methods.remarks: This method clears all drawings from the specified layer by creating a new transparent bitmap. The layer remains in the collection and retains its size and position settings. The graphics object is recreated with high-quality rendering settings. Call OSD_Layers_Render after clearing to update the video display.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the OSD layer to clear.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Create
methods.summary: Creates a new On-Screen Display (OSD) layer.
methods.remarks: Creates a new transparent layer that can be drawn on using other OSD methods. The layer is added to the internal collection and assigned an ID based on its index. Use the returned index (collection count - 1) to reference this layer in other methods.

parameters.name: left
parameters.summary: The left position of the layer relative to the video frame.

parameters.name: top
parameters.summary: The top position of the layer relative to the video frame.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: The width of the layer in pixels.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: The height of the layer in pixels.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.summary: If true, the layer will be visible immediately; if false, it will be hidden.

methods.returns: true if the layer was successfully created; false if an error occurred.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Delete
methods.summary: Deletes a specific On-Screen Display (OSD) layer from the collection.
methods.remarks: This method permanently removes the layer from the collection. All layers with higher indices will shift down by one position. After deletion, the OSD is automatically updated to reflect the change. The video renderer must be initialized before calling this method.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the OSD layer to delete.

methods.returns: true if the layer was successfully deleted; false if the operation failed or the ID is invalid.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Draw_Image
methods.summary: Draws an image from a file onto the specified OSD layer.
methods.remarks: The image is drawn at its original size at the specified position. Color keying allows you to make a specific color transparent, useful for logos with backgrounds. Call OSD_Layers_Render after drawing to update the video display. Supported image formats depend on the system's installed codecs (typically BMP, JPG, PNG, GIF).

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the OSD layer to draw on.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The full path to the image file to draw.

parameters.name: left
parameters.summary: The left position where the image will be drawn on the layer.

parameters.name: top
parameters.summary: The top position where the image will be drawn on the layer.

parameters.name: useColorKey
parameters.summary: If true, treats the specified color as transparent.

parameters.name: colorKey
parameters.summary: The color to treat as transparent when useColorKey is true.

methods.returns: true if the image was successfully drawn; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Draw_Image
methods.summary: Draws a portion of an image from a file onto the specified OSD layer with scaling support.
methods.remarks: This overload allows you to draw a specific portion of an image and scale it to fit a destination rectangle. Useful for sprite sheets, image atlases, or when you need to crop and scale images. The destination position is specified by destRect.X and destRect.Y.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the OSD layer to draw on.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The full path to the image file to draw.

parameters.name: srcRect
parameters.summary: The source rectangle defining which portion of the image to draw. Use Rectangle.Empty to draw the entire image.

parameters.name: destRect
parameters.summary: The destination rectangle on the layer. Width/height of 0 uses the source image dimensions.

parameters.name: useColorKey
parameters.summary: If true, treats the specified color as transparent.

parameters.name: colorKey
parameters.summary: The color to treat as transparent when useColorKey is true.

methods.returns: true if the image was successfully drawn; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Draw_Image
methods.summary: Draws a Bitmap object onto the specified OSD layer with advanced positioning and scaling options.
methods.remarks: This is the core image drawing method that other overloads call. It provides full control over source cropping and destination scaling. The image is drawn using high-quality interpolation settings. Color keying is implemented using GDI+ ImageAttributes.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the OSD layer to draw on.

parameters.name: image
parameters.summary: The Bitmap object to draw. Must not be null.

parameters.name: srcRect
parameters.summary: The source rectangle defining which portion of the image to draw. Use Rectangle.Empty to draw the entire image.

parameters.name: destRect
parameters.summary: The destination rectangle on the layer. Width/height of 0 uses the source image dimensions.

parameters.name: useColorKey
parameters.summary: If true, treats the specified color as transparent.

parameters.name: colorKey
parameters.summary: The color to treat as transparent when useColorKey is true.

methods.returns: true if the image was successfully drawn; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_Draw_Text
methods.summary: Draws text onto the specified OSD layer.
methods.remarks: The text is rendered with anti-aliasing for smooth appearance. The position specifies the top-left corner of the text bounding box. Call OSD_Layers_Render after drawing to update the video display. For dynamic text updates, consider clearing the layer first or using a dedicated layer for text.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the OSD layer to draw on.

parameters.name: left
parameters.summary: The left position where the text will be drawn.

parameters.name: top
parameters.summary: The top position where the text will be drawn.

parameters.name: font
parameters.summary: The font to use for rendering the text.

methods.returns: true if the text was successfully drawn; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_GetBitmap
methods.summary: Retrieves the Bitmap object for the specified OSD layer.
methods.remarks: This method provides direct access to the layer's bitmap for advanced manipulation. The returned bitmap is a reference to the actual layer bitmap, not a copy. Modifications to the returned bitmap will affect the OSD display after calling OSD_Layers_Render. Do not dispose of the returned bitmap as it's managed by the OSD system. The bitmap lives only as long as its layer: OSD_Layers_Clear() and OSD_Layers_Delete() dispose it, and OSD_Layers_Clear(int) disposes it and gives the layer a fresh one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the OSD layer.

parameters.name: bitmap
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains the Bitmap object of the layer, or null if the operation failed.

methods.returns: true if the bitmap was successfully retrieved; false if the operation failed or the ID is invalid.

methods.name: OSD_Layers_SetTransparency
methods.summary: Sets the transparency level for the specified OSD layer.
methods.remarks: This method sets the overall transparency for the entire layer, affecting all content drawn on it. The transparency is applied when the layer is rendered to the video. Call OSD_Layers_Render after changing transparency to see the effect. This is useful for creating semi-transparent overlays or fading effects.

parameters.name: id
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the OSD layer.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: The transparency level (0 = fully transparent, 255 = fully opaque).

methods.returns: true if the transparency was successfully set; false if the operation failed or the ID is invalid.
