methods.name: AddPIPDevices
methods.summary: Adds Picture-In-Picture (PIP) devices to the capture graph for rendering multiple video sources.
methods.remarks: This method initializes and configures PIP devices based on the current PIP mode settings. It supports multiple PIP modes including Custom, ChromaKey, Vertical, Horizontal, Mode2x2, and MultipleVideoStreams. The method handles device initialization, filter graph connections, and layout positioning.

methods.name: SkipPIPSource
methods.summary: Reports a PIP source that failed to open and takes it out of the graph, so the sources after it still connect.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: Its zero-based position in the PIP source list.

methods.name: ReleasePIPSource
methods.summary: Takes a PIP source that will not be connected out of the running graph and marks it skipped.

methods.name: DisposePIPSourceWrappers
methods.summary: Disposes the source wrappers a PIP source holds: its network sessions, its capture device and its file source.

methods.name: ReleasePIPOutputPin
methods.summary: Releases a PIP source's output pin. A capture device's own pin belongs to dsVidCapDevice; a sample grabber's behind it was taken here and is released.

methods.name: AddPIPConverter
methods.summary: Keeps a converter ConnectRGBInput put in front of the mixer or a PIP sample grabber, for Clear to dispose.

parameters.name: converter
parameters.summary: The converter; null when none was needed.

methods.name: DropPIPMixer
methods.summary: Takes the video mixer out of the graph when it refuses the main video or the output size, so the main video, still held in dsVideoOutputPin, is captured without PIP.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Clear
methods.summary: Clears all Picture-In-Picture (PIP) sources from the collection.
methods.remarks: This method removes all configured PIP devices from the internal collection. Call this method before reconfiguring PIP sources or when cleaning up resources. The call is declined and logged while a capture is running: the PiP sources are read when the graph is built, and their filters are connected in it.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Count
methods.summary: Gets the count of Picture-In-Picture (PIP) sources currently configured.
methods.remarks: Use this method to determine how many PIP sources have been added to the capture configuration. A stop removes and releases every PiP source, so the count is 0 after it.
methods.returns: The number of PIP sources in the collection.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Delete
methods.summary: Deletes a Picture-In-Picture (PIP) device from the collection at the specified index.
methods.remarks: This method safely removes a PIP source from the collection. If the index is out of range, the method returns false without throwing an exception. The call is declined and logged while a capture is running: the PiP sources are read when the graph is built, and their filters are connected in it.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the PIP source to remove.

methods.returns: true if the device was successfully removed; false if the index was invalid or an error occurred.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Change
methods.summary: Runs a change to the PiP source list, declined while a capture is running or starting.

parameters.name: method
parameters.summary: The public method name, for the log line.

parameters.name: change
parameters.summary: The change; returns its own result.

methods.returns: The result of change, or false when declined.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Device_GetCrossbar
methods.summary: Initializes and retrieves crossbar information from the specified video capture device.
methods.remarks: This method retrieves the crossbar configuration for a video capture device, which allows switching between different input sources (e.g., Composite, S-Video, etc.). The crossbar inputs are stored internally and can be retrieved using PIP_Sources_Device_GetCrossbarInputs.

parameters.name: deviceName
parameters.summary: The name of the video capture device to query for crossbar information.

methods.returns: true if the crossbar was successfully initialized and queried; false otherwise.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Device_GetCrossbarInputs
methods.summary: Gets the list of available crossbar inputs for the previously queried device.
methods.remarks: Call PIP_Sources_Device_GetCrossbar first to populate the crossbar input list. The returned collection typically contains input names like "Video Composite In", "Video SVideo In", etc.
methods.returns: An observable collection containing the names of available crossbar inputs.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourcePositionAsync
methods.summary: Sets the position of the video screen for the selected Picture-In-Picture device asynchronously.
methods.remarks: This method allows dynamic repositioning of PIP sources during playback. The rectangle coordinates are relative to the output video frame. This is the asynchronous version - use PIP_Sources_SetSourcePosition for synchronous operations.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The one-based index of the PIP source to reposition (1 for first PIP source, 2 for second, etc.).

parameters.name: rect
parameters.summary: The rectangle defining the new position and size of the PIP source (Left, Top, Width, Height).

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful; false otherwise.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourcePosition
methods.summary: Sets the position of the video screen for the selected Picture-In-Picture device synchronously.
methods.remarks: This method allows dynamic repositioning of PIP sources during playback. The rectangle coordinates are relative to the output video frame. This is the synchronous version - use PIP_Sources_SetSourcePositionAsync for asynchronous operations.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The one-based index of the PIP source to reposition (1 for first PIP source, 2 for second, etc.).

parameters.name: rect
parameters.summary: The rectangle defining the new position and size of the PIP source (Left, Top, Width, Height).

methods.returns: true if the position was successfully updated; false if the operation failed or capture is not started.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourcePositionIntl
methods.summary: Internal method that sets the position of a specific PIP source in the video frame.
methods.remarks: This method only works when PIP_Mode is set to Custom. The position is applied to the PIP filter layer corresponding to the source index + 1.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the PIP source to reposition.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.summary: The new position and size rectangle for the PIP source.

methods.returns: true if the position was successfully updated; false if the operation failed or the source is not in Custom mode.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourceOrderAsync
methods.summary: Sets the Z-order (layering order) of a Picture-In-Picture source asynchronously.
methods.remarks: Use this method to change which PIP sources appear in front of or behind others. Lower order values place the source behind higher values.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The one-based index of the PIP source to reorder.

parameters.name: order
parameters.summary: The new Z-order position (0 is bottom/back, higher values are on top/front). Valid range: 0 to (stream count - 1).

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful; false otherwise.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourceOrder
methods.summary: Sets the Z-order (layering order) of a Picture-In-Picture source synchronously.
methods.remarks: Use this method to change which PIP sources appear in front of or behind others. Lower order values place the source behind higher values. This is the synchronous version - use PIP_Sources_SetSourceOrderAsync for asynchronous operations.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The one-based index of the PIP source to reorder.

parameters.name: order
parameters.summary: The new Z-order position (0 is bottom/back, higher values are on top/front). Valid range: 0 to (stream count - 1).

methods.returns: true if the order was successfully updated; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourceOrderIntl
methods.summary: Internal method that changes the rendering order of a PIP source.
methods.remarks: This method updates the layer order in the PIP filter to control which sources appear above others. The main video source is always at order 0.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the PIP source to reorder.

parameters.name: order
parameters.summary: The new rendering order (Z-order) for the source. Higher values appear on top.

methods.returns: true if the order was successfully updated; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourceSettingsAsync
methods.summary: Sets visual settings for the selected Picture-In-Picture device asynchronously.
methods.remarks: This method allows you to adjust visual properties of PIP sources during playback. Changes are applied immediately if capture is running.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The one-based index of the PIP source to configure.

parameters.name: transparency
parameters.summary: The transparency level (0-255, where 0 is fully transparent and 255 is fully opaque).

parameters.name: flipX
parameters.summary: If true, flips the video horizontally (mirror effect).

parameters.name: flipY
parameters.summary: If true, flips the video vertically.

parameters.name: disabled
parameters.summary: If true, disables the PIP stream (hides it from view).

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful; false otherwise.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourceSettings
methods.summary: Sets visual settings for the selected Picture-In-Picture device synchronously.
methods.remarks: This method allows you to adjust visual properties of PIP sources. Changes are applied immediately if capture is running, or stored for later if not. This is the synchronous version - use PIP_Sources_SetSourceSettingsAsync for asynchronous operations.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The one-based index of the PIP source to configure.

parameters.name: transparency
parameters.summary: The transparency level (0-255, where 0 is fully transparent and 255 is fully opaque).

parameters.name: flipX
parameters.summary: If true, flips the video horizontally (mirror effect).

parameters.name: flipY
parameters.summary: If true, flips the video vertically.

parameters.name: disabled
parameters.summary: If true, disables the PIP stream (hides it from view).

methods.returns: true if the settings were successfully applied; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetSourceSettingsIntl
methods.summary: Internal method that updates various settings for a PIP source including transparency and flipping.
methods.remarks: This method applies multiple visual settings to a PIP source layer in a single operation.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the PIP source to configure.

parameters.name: transparency
parameters.summary: The transparency level (0-255, where 0 is opaque and 255 is fully transparent).

parameters.name: flipX
parameters.summary: If true, flips the source horizontally.

parameters.name: flipY
parameters.summary: If true, flips the source vertically.

parameters.name: disabled
parameters.summary: If true, disables rendering of this source.

methods.returns: true if the settings were successfully applied; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetFlipSettingsAsync
methods.summary: Sets flip settings for the selected Picture-In-Picture device asynchronously.
methods.remarks: This method provides a convenient way to adjust only the flip settings without affecting other visual properties. Changes are applied immediately if capture is running.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The one-based index of the PIP source to configure.

parameters.name: horizontal
parameters.summary: If true, flips the video horizontally (mirror effect).

parameters.name: vertical
parameters.summary: If true, flips the video vertically.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful; false otherwise.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetFlipSettings
methods.summary: Sets flip settings for the selected Picture-In-Picture device synchronously.
methods.remarks: This method provides a convenient way to adjust only the flip settings without affecting other visual properties. This is the synchronous version - use PIP_Sources_SetFlipSettingsAsync for asynchronous operations.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The one-based index of the PIP source to configure.

parameters.name: horizontal
parameters.summary: If true, flips the video horizontally (mirror effect).

parameters.name: vertical
parameters.summary: If true, flips the video vertically.

methods.returns: true if the flip settings were successfully applied; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetFlipSettingsIntl
methods.summary: Internal method that sets the flip settings for a PIP source.
methods.remarks: This method is a convenience wrapper that calls PIP_Sources_SetSourceSettingsIntl with existing transparency and disabled settings.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the PIP source to flip.

parameters.name: horizontal
parameters.summary: If true, flips the source horizontally (mirror image).

parameters.name: vertical
parameters.summary: If true, flips the source vertically (upside down).

methods.returns: true if the flip settings were successfully applied; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetTransparencySettingsAsync
methods.summary: Sets transparency settings for the selected Picture-In-Picture device asynchronously.
methods.remarks: This method provides finer control over transparency using normalized floating-point values. The value is internally converted to the 0-255 range used by the filter.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The one-based index of the PIP source to configure.

parameters.name: transparency
parameters.summary: The transparency level as a normalized value (0.0 = fully transparent, 1.0 = fully opaque).

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful; false otherwise.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetTransparencySettings
methods.summary: Sets transparency settings for the selected Picture-In-Picture device synchronously.
methods.remarks: This method provides finer control over transparency using normalized floating-point values. The value is internally converted to the 0-255 range used by the filter. This is the synchronous version - use PIP_Sources_SetTransparencySettingsAsync for asynchronous operations.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The one-based index of the PIP source to configure.

parameters.name: transparency
parameters.summary: The transparency level as a normalized value (0.0 = fully transparent, 1.0 = fully opaque).

methods.returns: true if the transparency was successfully set; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_SetTransparencySettingsIntl
methods.summary: Internal method that sets the transparency level for a PIP source.
methods.remarks: The transparency value is internally converted from the 0.0-1.0 range to the 0-255 range used by the filter.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the PIP source to modify.

parameters.name: transparency
parameters.summary: The transparency level (0.0-1.0, where 0.0 is opaque and 1.0 is fully transparent).

methods.returns: true if the transparency was successfully set; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: TryGetPIPLayer
methods.summary: Maps a one-based PIP source index to the video mixer layer it was connected to; 0 is the main video. The two differ once a source that failed to open was skipped (GitHub issue #2183).

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The one-based PIP source index, or 0 for the main video.

methods.returns: false for an index out of range or a skipped source.

methods.name: PIP_Background_Color_Set
methods.summary: Sets the background color for Picture-In-Picture composition.
methods.remarks: This color is visible in areas not covered by PIP sources or the main video. It's particularly useful in Custom and 2x2 PIP modes where gaps may exist between sources.

parameters.name: color
parameters.summary: The background color to use when PIP sources don't fill the entire output area.

methods.name: PIP_Background_Image_Set
methods.summary: Sets a background image for Picture-In-Picture composition.
methods.remarks: The background image is displayed behind all PIP sources. Supported image formats depend on the underlying DirectShow filters installed. Common formats include BMP, JPG, PNG, etc.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The full path to the image file to use as background.

methods.name: PIP_Background_Image_Clear
methods.summary: Clears the background image for Picture-In-Picture composition.
methods.remarks: After clearing, only the background color will be visible in areas not covered by PIP sources.

methods.name: PIP_CustomOutputSize_Set
methods.summary: Sets a custom output size for Picture-In-Picture composition when using Custom mode.
methods.remarks: This method only applies when PIP_Mode is set to PIPMode.Custom. It allows you to specify the exact dimensions of the composed output video. If not set, the output size defaults to the main video source dimensions.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: The desired output width in pixels.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: The desired output height in pixels.

methods.name: PIP_CustomOutputSize_Clear
methods.summary: Clears the custom output size for Picture-In-Picture composition.
methods.remarks: After clearing, the output size will default to the main video source dimensions. This method only affects Custom PIP mode.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Add_IPCamera
methods.summary: Adds an IP camera as a Picture-In-Picture source.
methods.remarks: Supports various IP camera protocols including RTSP, HTTP MJPEG, MMS, and NDI. The camera stream will be rendered at the specified position and size in the composed output. Default transparency is set to 255 (fully opaque). The call is declined and logged while a capture is running: the PiP sources are read when the graph is built, and their filters are connected in it. A stop removes and releases every PiP source: add them again before each start.

parameters.name: source
parameters.summary: The IP camera source settings including URL, credentials, and engine type.

parameters.name: outLeft
parameters.summary: The left position of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: outTop
parameters.summary: The top position of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: outWidth
parameters.summary: The width of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: outHeight
parameters.summary: The height of the PIP window in the output video.

methods.returns: true if the IP camera was successfully added; false if an error occurred.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Add_VideoFile
methods.summary: Adds a video file as a Picture-In-Picture source.
methods.remarks: The video file will be decoded and rendered at the specified position and size. Supported formats depend on installed DirectShow codecs. Default transparency is set to 255 (fully opaque). The call is declined and logged while a capture is running: the PiP sources are read when the graph is built, and their filters are connected in it. A stop removes and releases every PiP source: add them again before each start.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.summary: The full path to the video file to add.

parameters.name: outLeft
parameters.summary: The left position of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: outTop
parameters.summary: The top position of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: outWidth
parameters.summary: The width of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: outHeight
parameters.summary: The height of the PIP window in the output video.

methods.returns: true if the video file was successfully added; false if an error occurred.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Add_ScreenSource
methods.summary: Adds a screen capture source as a Picture-In-Picture source.
methods.remarks: Captures a portion or all of the screen/window and renders it as a PIP source. Supports desktop duplication engine for better performance on supported systems. Default transparency is set to 255 (fully opaque). The call is declined and logged while a capture is running: the PiP sources are read when the graph is built, and their filters are connected in it. A stop removes and releases every PiP source: add them again before each start.

parameters.name: screenSource
parameters.summary: The screen capture settings including capture area, display index, and mouse cursor options.

parameters.name: outLeft
parameters.summary: The left position of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: outTop
parameters.summary: The top position of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: outWidth
parameters.summary: The width of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: outHeight
parameters.summary: The height of the PIP window in the output video.

methods.returns: true if the screen source was successfully added; false if an error occurred.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Add_VideoCaptureDevice
methods.summary: Adds a video capture device as a Picture-In-Picture source.
methods.remarks: This method creates a new VideoCaptureSource internally with the specified parameters. Default transparency is set to 255 (fully opaque). Use PIP_Sources_Device_GetCrossbar to get available crossbar inputs. The call is declined and logged while a capture is running: the PiP sources are read when the graph is built, and their filters are connected in it. A stop removes and releases every PiP source: add them again before each start.

parameters.name: deviceName
parameters.summary: The name of the video capture device. You can use the device path for devices with duplicate names.

parameters.name: format
parameters.summary: The desired video format (e.g., "YUY2 640x480"). Pass null to use default.

parameters.name: useBestFormat
parameters.summary: If true, automatically selects the best available format, ignoring the format parameter.

parameters.name: frameRate
parameters.summary: The desired frame rate for capture.

parameters.name: input
parameters.summary: The crossbar input name (e.g., "Video Composite In"). Pass null if no crossbar.

parameters.name: left
parameters.summary: The left position of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: top
parameters.summary: The top position of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: The width of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: The height of the PIP window in the output video.

methods.returns: true if the device was successfully added; false if an error occurred.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_Add_VideoCaptureDevice
methods.summary: Adds a video capture device as a Picture-In-Picture source using an existing device configuration.
methods.remarks: This overload allows you to pass a pre-configured VideoCaptureSource object. This is useful when you need to set advanced properties on the device before adding it. Default transparency is set to 255 (fully opaque). The call is declined and logged while a capture is running: the PiP sources are read when the graph is built, and their filters are connected in it. A stop removes and releases every PiP source: add them again before each start.

parameters.name: device
parameters.summary: The pre-configured video capture device source object.

parameters.name: left
parameters.summary: The left position of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: top
parameters.summary: The top position of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: The width of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: The height of the PIP window in the output video.

parameters.name: crossbarInput
parameters.summary: The crossbar input name (e.g., "Video Composite In"). Pass null if no crossbar.

methods.returns: true if the device was successfully added; false if an error occurred.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_ScreenSource_UpdateAsync
methods.summary: Updates the capture area and settings for a screen capture PIP source asynchronously.
methods.remarks: This method only works with PIP sources that were added as screen capture sources. It allows dynamic updating of the capture area during playback.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The one-based index of the PIP source to update (must be a screen capture source).

parameters.name: left
parameters.summary: The new left coordinate of the capture area on the screen.

parameters.name: top
parameters.summary: The new top coordinate of the capture area on the screen.

parameters.name: grabMouseCursor
parameters.summary: If true, includes the mouse cursor in the capture.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful; false otherwise.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_ScreenSource_Update
methods.summary: Updates the capture area and settings for a screen capture PIP source synchronously.
methods.remarks: This method only works with PIP sources that were added as screen capture sources. It allows dynamic updating of the capture area during playback. This is the synchronous version - use PIP_Sources_ScreenSource_UpdateAsync for asynchronous operations.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The one-based index of the PIP source to update (must be a screen capture source).

parameters.name: left
parameters.summary: The new left coordinate of the capture area on the screen.

parameters.name: top
parameters.summary: The new top coordinate of the capture area on the screen.

parameters.name: grabMouseCursor
parameters.summary: If true, includes the mouse cursor in the capture.

methods.returns: true if the settings were successfully updated; false if the operation failed.

methods.name: PIP_Sources_ScreenSource_UpdateIntl
methods.summary: Internal method that updates the capture parameters for a screen capture PIP source.
methods.remarks: This method only works for PIP sources with SourceType set to Screen. The screen capture area is updated in real-time without restarting the capture.

parameters.name: index
parameters.summary: The zero-based index of the PIP source to update.

parameters.name: left
parameters.summary: The left coordinate of the screen area to capture.

parameters.name: top
parameters.summary: The top coordinate of the screen area to capture.

parameters.name: grabMouseCursor
parameters.summary: If true, includes the mouse cursor in the capture.

methods.returns: true if the screen source was successfully updated; false if the source is not a screen capture or update failed.

methods.name: AddAudioPCMConverter
methods.summary: Adds an audio PCM converter filter to the filter graph for audio format conversion.
methods.remarks: This method initializes a PCM converter to convert audio to the specified format including sample rate, bits per sample, and number of channels. The converter is inserted into the audio processing pipeline.

methods.name: AddAudioEnhancer
methods.summary: Adds an audio enhancer filter to improve audio quality and apply audio processing effects.
methods.remarks: The audio enhancer supports features like normalization, auto-gain control, input/output gain adjustments, and time shifting. It's inserted into the audio processing pipeline after initialization.

methods.name: AddAudioChannelMapper
methods.summary: Adds an audio channel mapper filter to remap audio channels.
methods.remarks: This filter allows remapping of audio channels, useful for converting between different channel configurations (e.g., stereo to mono, 5.1 to stereo, etc.). If output channel count is not specified, it uses the input channel count.

methods.name: AddAudioSampleGrabber
methods.summary: Adds an audio sample grabber to capture raw audio data for processing and analysis.
methods.remarks: The sample grabber intercepts PCM audio data and raises the AudioFrameCB1 callback. This is used for audio effects processing, VU meters, and providing audio data to applications. Only works with PCM audio format.

methods.name: AddAudioVUMeter
methods.summary: Adds an audio VU (Volume Unit) meter for visualizing audio levels.
methods.remarks: The VU meter processes audio data from the sample grabber to calculate volume levels. It uses the audio format parameters (sample rate, channels, bits per sample) from the grabber. The meter raises OnAudioVUMeter events with volume and frequency data. This is useful for creating audio level visualizations in the UI.

methods.name: AddNAVUMeter
methods.summary: Adds an advanced NAudio-based VU meter with additional audio analysis capabilities.
methods.remarks: This professional VU meter provides: - Volume level analysis with configurable sensitivity - FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) calculations for frequency analysis - Maximum level detection for peak monitoring Requires the audio sample grabber to be enabled. Raises multiple events for different audio analysis results.

methods.name: ProcessAudio
methods.summary: Processes audio frames through the DSP (Digital Signal Processing) effects chain.
methods.remarks: This method initializes the processor with audio format parameters if not already initialized. It then processes the audio buffer through the configured effects chain. Effects may include equalization, compression, reverb, and other audio transformations.

parameters.name: processor
parameters.summary: The DSP processor instance to use for processing audio effects.

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: Sample grabber event arguments containing audio buffer data and format information.

methods.name: AudioFrameCB1
methods.summary: Callback method that handles audio frames from the audio sample grabber.
methods.remarks: This callback is the main audio processing entry point that: - Applies audio effects if enabled - Processes VU meter data for volume visualization - Provides audio data to the application via OnAudioFrameBuffer event The method handles both standard and professional VU meter processing. All exceptions are caught to prevent interruption of the audio stream.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The source of the event (typically the audio sample grabber).

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: Event arguments containing the audio buffer data, format, and timing information.

methods.name: AddBarcodeReader
methods.summary: Adds and configures a barcode reader for detecting barcodes in video frames.
methods.remarks: This method initializes the barcode reader with the configured settings including barcode type and enabled state. The reader will process video frames to detect barcodes.

methods.name: ProcessFaceTracking
methods.summary: Processes video frames for face detection and tracking using Haar cascades.
methods.remarks: This method implements a two-phase face tracking system: 1. Detection phase: Uses Haar cascades to detect faces in downsampled frames 2. Tracking phase: Uses Camshift algorithm to track detected faces efficiently The detection runs periodically while tracking runs on every frame for performance. Detected faces can be highlighted with rectangles if Face_Tracking.Highlight is enabled. The OnFaceDetected event is raised with face locations and frame data.

parameters.name: buffer
parameters.summary: Pointer to the raw video frame data.

parameters.name: bufferLen
parameters.summary: Length of the buffer in bytes.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: Width of the video frame in pixels.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: Height of the video frame in pixels.

parameters.name: pixelFormat
parameters.summary: Pixel format of the video frame.

methods.name: AddAForgeMotionDetector
methods.summary: Initializes and configures the AForge.NET motion detection system.
methods.remarks: This method sets up motion detection using the AForge.NET framework. It cleans up any existing motion detector before creating a new one. The detector is configured with settings from Motion_DetectionEx property. Motion detection events are wired up to notify when motion is detected.

methods.name: OnAForgeData
methods.summary: Processes video frame data through the AForge.NET motion detection system.
methods.remarks: This method feeds video frames to the AForge motion detector for analysis. Motion detection algorithms are applied to identify movement in the video. Only processes frames when motion detection is enabled and configured.

parameters.name: data
parameters.summary: Pointer to the raw image data in memory.

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: Width of the image in pixels.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: Height of the image in pixels.

parameters.name: pixelFormat
parameters.summary: Pixel format of the image data (e.g., RGB24, RGB32).

methods.name: AddMotionDetection
methods.summary: Initializes and configures the motion detection system.
methods.remarks: This method creates a motion detector that analyzes video frames for movement. The detector is configured with settings from the Motion_Detection property. Motion events are wired up to notify when motion levels exceed thresholds. The detector provides both motion level values and a motion matrix showing areas of movement.

methods.name: dsMotionDetector_OnMotion
methods.summary: Handles motion detection events from the motion detector.
methods.remarks: This event handler forwards motion detection results to application code. The motion level indicates the amount of movement detected (0-100). The motion matrix provides detailed information about which areas contain motion.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The motion detector that detected movement.

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: Event arguments containing motion level and motion matrix data.

methods.name: ProcessMotion
methods.summary: Processes a video frame through the motion detection algorithm.
methods.remarks: This method feeds video frames to the motion detector for analysis. It uses the current frame dimensions to properly interpret the frame data. Motion detection algorithms compare the current frame with previous frames. All exceptions are suppressed to prevent interruption of video processing.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: Pointer to the raw video frame data to analyze for motion.

methods.name: AddVideoSampleGrabber
methods.summary: Adds a video sample grabber to capture raw video frames for processing and analysis.
methods.remarks: The sample grabber intercepts RGB24 video data and raises frame callbacks. Used for video effects processing, motion detection, and providing video frames to applications. Initializes the video effects processor.

methods.name: InsertYuv2RgbBeforeGrabber
methods.summary: Inserts VisioForge YUV2RGB in front of the RGB24 sample grabber when the upstream pin's current format is a YUV subtype that filter accepts. The WMV blacklist in CaptureMain does not stop this: it only covers the graph builder's choice.

methods.name: AddVideoSampleGrabberPreview
methods.summary: Adds a video sample grabber specifically for the preview stream.
methods.remarks: This sample grabber is separate from the main video grabber and processes preview frames independently. Used when different effects or processing is needed for preview vs capture streams.

parameters.name: videoPin
parameters.summary: Reference to the video output pin to connect the grabber to.

methods.name: AddVideoSampleGrabberOutput
methods.summary: Adds a video sample grabber specifically for the capture/output stream.
methods.remarks: This sample grabber processes frames being sent to the capture output. Allows different effects and processing for captured video compared to preview. Connected to the shared capture graph rather than the main graph.

parameters.name: videoPin
parameters.summary: Reference to the video output pin to connect the grabber to.

methods.name: AddVideoSampleGrabberStill
methods.summary: Adds a video sample grabber specifically for capturing still images from the video stream.
methods.remarks: This sample grabber delivers every still image the device sends (one per snapshot button press). It connects to the still pin of the video capture device if available. The grabber captures RGB24 format images and raises the FrameBufferCB24Still callback. A null renderer is attached to complete the graph without displaying the still images.

methods.name: GenerateSeparateCaptureFilename
methods.summary: Generates a unique filename for separate capture files based on the configured mask.
methods.remarks: This method creates filenames for the separate capture feature which splits recordings into multiple files. The filename mask can contain date/time placeholders like %yyyy, %MM, %dd, %hh, %mm, %ss. The %ext placeholder is replaced with the extension from the main output filename. Used when SeparateCapture_Mode is set to split by duration or file size.
methods.returns: A formatted filename string with date/time placeholders replaced with current values.

methods.name: SeparateCaptureSplit
methods.summary: Queues an automatic split to a newly generated file; the non-async API runs it on the UI thread when a view is attached. The switch itself updates FSeparateCaptureFilename, once the old segment has stopped.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.summary: _separateCaptureGeneration read before the split was decided.

methods.returns: true if the split was queued; false if it waits for the next check.

methods.name: ProcessVideoRGB
methods.summary: This is the core video processing method that: - Updates frame timing and position information - Handles separate capture file splitting - Applies video effects and GPU effects - Performs motion detection and face tracking - Processes barcode detection - Raises various frame events for application consumption - Manages frame buffers and format conversions The method includes extensive error handling and performance optimizations. All video processing passes through this central method.

methods.name: VideoFrameBufferCB24
methods.summary: Callback method that handles RGB24 video frames from the video effects filter.
methods.remarks: This callback is used when the graph has no video sample grabber. It processes video frames that have already passed through the effects filter. The frames are in RGB24 format and are forwarded to the main processing method.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The source of the event (typically the video effects filter).

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: Event arguments containing the video frame data and metadata.

methods.name: VideoFrameBufferCB24SG
methods.summary: Callback method that handles video frames from the main video sample grabber.
methods.remarks: This is the primary video frame callback for processing captured video. Frames are flipped horizontally to correct for DirectShow's coordinate system. The method forwards frames to ProcessVideoRGB for effects, motion detection, and other processing. This callback handles frames from the main video stream.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The source of the event (typically the main video sample grabber).

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: Event arguments containing the video frame buffer, dimensions, and timing information.

methods.name: VideoFrameBufferCB24SGPreview
methods.summary: Callback method that handles video frames from the preview sample grabber.
methods.remarks: This callback processes frames specifically for the preview stream. Preview frames may have different effects applied compared to the capture stream. Unlike the main stream, preview frames are not flipped horizontally. This allows separate processing pipelines for preview and capture.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The source of the event (typically the preview sample grabber).

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: Event arguments containing the preview frame buffer and metadata.

methods.name: FrameBufferCB24Still
methods.summary: Callback method that handles still image frames from the video capture device.
methods.remarks: This callback processes still images captured from the video stream. It provides the captured image data through two events: - OnStillVideoFrameBuffer: Provides raw buffer data - OnStillVideoFrameBitmap: Provides a Bitmap object The image is flipped vertically to correct for DirectShow's bottom-up format. Applications can modify the image data by setting UpdateData in the event args.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.summary: The source of the event (typically the still image sample grabber).

parameters.name: e
parameters.summary: Event arguments containing the image buffer data, dimensions, and format information.

methods.name: AddVideoEffects
methods.summary: Adds the main video effects processing filter to the filter graph.
methods.remarks: This method inserts the video effects processor into the video pipeline. The processor handles various effects including: - Image and text overlays - Color adjustments and filters - Transformations and distortions Frame callbacks are set up for applying effects to video frames.

methods.name: ProcessEffects
methods.summary: Processes and applies video effects to a video frame.
methods.remarks: This method is the central video effects processing pipeline that: - Merges still, always-on image logos by pre-rendering them once; animated, RGB24 and transparent ones are drawn per frame - Merges static, always-on text logos; dynamic and scrolling ones are drawn per frame - Applies NVIDIA Maxine AI effects (denoise, artifact reduction) - Processes other video effects through the effects processor Effects are filtered by stream type and time range. Performance optimizations include caching rendered logos and selective updates.

parameters.name: data
parameters.summary: Pointer to the raw video frame data to process.

parameters.name: dataSize
parameters.summary: Size of the frame data in bytes.

parameters.name: flip
parameters.summary: Whether the frame needs to be flipped (unused in this method).

parameters.name: width
parameters.summary: Width of the video frame in pixels.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: Height of the video frame in pixels.

parameters.name: stride
parameters.summary: Byte stride of the video frame.

parameters.name: timeStamp
parameters.summary: Timestamp of the current frame for time-based effects.

parameters.name: streamType
parameters.summary: Type of stream (Main, Preview, or Capture) to determine which effects to apply.

methods.name: AddVideoResize
methods.summary: Adds a video resize filter to crop and/or resize video frames.
methods.remarks: This method adds a video resize filter that can: - Crop video frames by removing pixels from edges - Resize video to different dimensions - Apply letterboxing for aspect ratio preservation The filter updates the internal video dimensions after processing. For VideoRenderer mode, an additional decoder filter may be added.

methods.name: AddMaxineResize
methods.summary: Adds an NVIDIA Maxine-powered resize filter for AI-enhanced video upscaling.
methods.remarks: This method adds an NVIDIA Maxine filter that uses AI models for: - Super-resolution upscaling - Artifact reduction during upscaling Requires NVIDIA GPU with appropriate drivers and Maxine SDK models. The models directory must be specified in the resize settings.

methods.name: AddVideoRotate
methods.summary: Adds a video rotation filter to rotate video frames by 90, 180, or 270 degrees.
methods.remarks: This filter rotates the video stream according to the Video_Rotation setting. For 90 and 270 degree rotations, the width and height are swapped. An additional decoder filter may be added for VideoRenderer mode.

methods.summary: Adds custom DirectShow video filters to the filter graph.

methods.name: SeparateCaptureSerialized
methods.summary: Runs a separate-capture operation under _separateCaptureLock, so start, stop, pause, resume and file switches never overlap (#1703). Nothing under the lock calls out: events and errors are queued (Action)) and delivered once it is released, so a thread waiting for the lock is never waited on by a handler run under it. The capture's own Pause, Resume and graph start run through here too: StopMain publishes _stopping under the same lock, so a stop cannot begin between the check and the main graph's Run() or Pause() (#1727).

parameters.name: method
parameters.summary: The call it serves, refused with an error while a capture stop is tearing the graphs down (#1724); null for an automatic split, which gives up on its own.

parameters.name: refusal
parameters.summary: The refusal message; null for the separate-capture one.

methods.name: SeparateCaptureCallout
methods.summary: Queues an event or error for delivery in order; delivers it now unless this thread holds _separateCaptureLock. The callout catches its own exceptions.

methods.name: SeparateCaptureDeliver
methods.summary: Delivers the queued callouts. One thread delivers at a time, which keeps the order; a thread that finds another delivering leaves its callouts to it and never waits for it.
methods.remarks: A deferred error is re-dispatched through the log observer, whose re-entrancy guard (#1173) is per thread: delivered by a thread that is itself inside an OnError dispatch - even an error another thread queued - it reaches Serilog but not OnError.

methods.name: SeparateCapturePauseChange
methods.summary: Runs a pause or resume. One that changes the pause state makes a queued automatic split stale: it would resume a paused MF mux, or cut the segment that has just resumed.

parameters.name: method
parameters.summary: The caller name used in the log.

parameters.name: quiet
parameters.summary: Set by the capture's own Pause/Resume, which follow a separate capture only when one records.

methods.name: SeparateCaptureStopGraph
methods.summary: Stops the separate capture graph with no KLV write in flight: the FFMPEG sink's Stop() frees the write session a concurrent WriteKLVData is still using (GitHub issue #1720). The writer is detached from KLV first, which waits out a file write in flight (_klvSeparateWriterSync is not held across the network streamer's write); the stop itself runs without the lock. String) reattaches it.

classes.name: MediaFoundationCameraSource
classes.summary: Reads one camera with a Media Foundation source reader and pushes RGB24 into the graph. The reader thread owns every Media Foundation object. Stop shuts the source down, stops the graph, then joins, so a push blocked inside the capture filter is released before the wait.

methods.name: FlushReader
methods.summary: Cancels the sample request the reader is waiting on. Shutdown alone does not: a camera that never answers leaves the read inside MFReadWrite for the life of the process. The reader is in synchronous mode, where Flush itself waits for that cancellation, so it runs beside the stop thread: a device that never completes it must not park the stop.

methods.name: Close
methods.summary: Stops the graph first when it is still running, so a push blocked in the capture filter returns, then waits for the reader, up to ReaderStopTimeoutMs. A frame posted to the UI thread is not waited for on that same thread: the callback sees the stop flag and does not touch the filter.
methods.returns: True when the reader was released. False when it was left behind, still inside a call - the caller has to leave the push filter to it instead of disposing it.

methods.name: SnapToNativeRate
methods.summary: The rate the camera itself reports for that size, when it is within RateMatchToleranceFps of the requested one. Otherwise the requested rate is kept, and the negotiation fails with the message that names it.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Add
methods.summary: Adds an audio effect to the specified audio stream.
methods.remarks: Effects can be added to individual audio streams or all streams simultaneously. The same effect type can be added multiple times with different names and parameters. Time-based effects allow for dynamic audio processing during playback.

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: The index of the audio stream (0-3), or -1 to apply to all streams.

parameters.name: effectType
parameters.summary: The type of audio effect to add (e.g., Amplify, Echo, Reverb).

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: A unique name identifier for this effect instance.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.summary: True to enable the effect immediately, false to add it in disabled state.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: The time position when the effect should start being applied.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: The time position when the effect should stop being applied.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Amplify
methods.summary: Configures parameters for an amplify audio effect.
methods.remarks: The amplify effect allows volume adjustment of audio streams. Values below 10000 reduce volume, values above 10000 increase it. Be careful with high values as they may cause audio clipping. Separate channel control is useful for stereo balance adjustments.

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: The index of the audio stream (0-3), or -1 to apply to all streams.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name of the amplify effect to configure.

parameters.name: volume
parameters.summary: The amplification level (10000 = no change, 20000 = 2x amplification, 5000 = 0.5x).

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: True to amplify each channel independently, false to use channel 0's value for all channels.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_BandPass
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the Band Pass effect.
methods.remarks: Filter to cutoff a certain Frequency Range. Each Channel can separate cutoff the Frequency range.

parameters.name: cutOffHigh
parameters.summary: Specifies the high cutoff frequency for a specific channel.

parameters.name: cutOffLow
parameters.summary: Specifies the low cutoff frequency for a specific channel.

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: Enables or Disables separate cutoff. If Enabled every channel will be processed by it's own cutoff value. If disabled every channel will be processed with the cutoff value of channel 0.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_ChannelOrderEx
methods.summary: Configures channel order remapping for audio streams.
methods.remarks: This effect allows flexible remapping of audio channels for various purposes: - Swapping left/right channels in stereo - Routing surround sound channels - Creating custom multi-channel configurations Channel numbers are zero-based (0 = first channel).

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: The audio stream index (0-3), or -1 to apply to all streams.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name of the channel order effect to configure.

parameters.name: orders
parameters.summary: A 2-dimensional array defining channel mappings. Each row contains [target_channel, source_channel] pairs. For example, [[0,1],[1,0]] swaps left and right channels in stereo audio.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Clear
methods.summary: Removes all audio effects from the specified audio stream.
methods.remarks: This method clears all effects that were added using Audio_Effects_Add. Use streamIndex=-1 to remove effects from all audio streams simultaneously. Any effect configuration will be lost and must be reapplied after clearing.

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: The audio stream index (0-3), or -1 to clear effects from all streams.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Count
methods.summary: Gets the count of audio effects applied to the specified audio stream.
methods.remarks: Use this method to determine how many effects are active on a specific audio stream. Each audio stream can have multiple effects applied simultaneously.

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: The audio stream index (0-3) to query.

methods.returns: The number of audio effects currently applied to the stream, or 0 if the stream index is invalid.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_Chorus
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Chorus effect.
methods.remarks: Chorus is a voice-doubling effect created by echoing the original sound with a slight delay and slightly modulating the delay of the echo.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.summary: Specifies the delay of the filter (0 - 20.0).

parameters.name: depth
parameters.summary: Specifies the depth of the filter (0 - 100.0).

parameters.name: feedback
parameters.summary: Specifies the feedback of the filter (-99.0 - 99.0).

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.summary: Specifies the frequency of the filter (0 - 10.0).

parameters.name: waveformTriangle
parameters.summary: Specifies the waveform type of the filter.

parameters.name: wetDryMix
parameters.summary: Specifies the wet and dry mix (0 - 100.0).

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_Compressor
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Compressor effect.
methods.remarks: Compression is a reduction in the fluctuation of a signal above a certain amplitude.

parameters.name: attack
parameters.summary: Specifies the attack time in ms (0.01 - 500).

parameters.name: gain
parameters.summary: Specifies the gain of the filter (-60.0 - 60.0).

parameters.name: preDelay
parameters.summary: Specifies the pre-delay of the filter (0.0 - 4.0).

parameters.name: ratio
parameters.summary: Specifies the ratio of the filter (1.0 - 100.0).

parameters.name: release

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.summary: Specifies the threshold of the filter (-60.0 - 0.0).

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_Distortion
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Distortion effect.
methods.remarks: Distortion is achieved by adding harmonics to the signal in such a way that, as the level increases, the top of the waveform becomes squared off or clipped.

parameters.name: edge
parameters.summary: Specifies the edge of the filter (0.0 - 100.0).

parameters.name: gain
parameters.summary: Specifies the gain of the filter (-60.0 - 0).

parameters.name: postEQBandwidth
parameters.summary: Specifies the bandwidth of the equalizer (100.0 - 8000.0).

parameters.name: postEQCenterFrequency
parameters.summary: Specifies the center frequency of the distortion equalizer (100.0 - 8000.0).

parameters.name: preLowpassCutOff
parameters.summary: Specifies the low pass cutoff of the filter (100.0 - 8000.0).

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_Echo
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Echo effect.
methods.remarks: An echo effect causes sounds to be repeated after a fixed delay, usually at a diminished volume. As the repeated sounds are fed back into the mix, they are repeated again.

parameters.name: feedback
parameters.summary: Specifies the feedback of the filter (0 - 100.0).

parameters.name: leftDelay
parameters.summary: Specifies the left delay of the filter (1.0 - 2000.0).

parameters.name: rightDelay
parameters.summary: Specifies the right delay of the filter (1.0 - 2000.0).

parameters.name: wetDryMix
parameters.summary: Specifies the wet and dry mix of the filter (0.0 - 100.0).

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_Flanger
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Flanger effect.
methods.remarks: Flange, also called flanger, is an echo effect in which the delay between the original signal and its echo is very short and varies over time. The result is sometimes referred to as a sweeping sound. The term flange originated with the practice of grabbing the flanges of a tape reel to change the speed.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.summary: Specifies the delay of the filter (0.0 - 4.0).

parameters.name: depth
parameters.summary: Specifies the depth of the filter (0.0 - 100.0).

parameters.name: feedback
parameters.summary: Specifies the feedback of the filter (-99.0 - 99.0).

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.summary: Specifies the frequency of the filter (0.0 - 10.0).

parameters.name: waveform

parameters.name: wetDryMix
parameters.summary: Specifies the wet and dry mix of the filter (0.0 - 100.0).

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_Gargle
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Gargle effect.
methods.remarks: The gargle effect modulates the amplitude of the signal.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DS_ParamEQ
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS ParamEQ effect.
methods.remarks: A parametric equalizer amplifies or attenuates signals of a given frequency. Parametric equalizer effects for different pitches can be applied in parallel by setting multiple instances of the effect on the same buffer. In this way, the application can have tone control similar to that provided by a hardware equalizer.

parameters.name: bandwidth
parameters.summary: Specifies the bandwidth of the equalizer (1.0 - 36.0).

parameters.name: center
parameters.summary: Specifies the center frequency of the equalizer (80.0 - 16000.0).

parameters.name: gain

methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Waves Reverb effect.
methods.remarks: The waves reverberation effect is intended for use with music. The waves reverberation DirectX Media Object (DMO) is based on the Waves MaxxVerb technology, which is licensed to Microsoft.

methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the Dynamic Amplify effect.
methods.remarks: DSP Filter to automatically keep the volume eat a specific maximum value.

parameters.name: attackTime
parameters.summary: Specifies the amplification value than will be used when amplifying.

parameters.name: maxAmplification
parameters.summary: Sets the amplification for a channel. Default value is 10000, which means that no amplification occurs. A value of 20000 raises the amplification by 2.

parameters.name: releaseTime
parameters.summary: Specifies the time in milliseconds that the DSP will wait to continue amplification, after the maximum has been reached.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_DynamicAmplify_GetCurrentAmp
methods.summary: Gets the value for the current amplification level.
methods.returns: System.Double.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Enable
methods.summary: Enables selected audio effect.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Equalizer_Band_Get
methods.summary: Gets the current level of audio volume for the selected equalizer band (slider).
methods.returns: System.Int32.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Equalizer_Band_Set
methods.summary: Sets the current level of audio volume for the selected equalizer band (slider).

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Flanger
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the Flanger effect.
methods.remarks: Filter to flange audio data. Every channel can be controlled separately.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.summary: Specifies the delay time in seconds.

parameters.name: phaseInvert
parameters.summary: Specifies whether the added signal should be inverted.

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: Enables or Disables separate amplification. If Enabled every channel will be amplified by it's own amplification value. If Disabled every channel will be amplified with the amplification value of channel 0.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_HighPass
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the High Pass effect.
methods.remarks: Filter that cuts Frequencies from a specified frequency to half of the sampling rate. Each channel can be separate processed with different cutoff values.

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: Enables or Disables separate cutoff. If Enabled every channel will be processed by it's own cutoff value. If Disabled every channel will be processed with the cutoff value of channel 0.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_LowPass
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the Low Pass effect.
methods.remarks: Filter that cuts frequencies from 0 to a specified frequency. Each channel can be separate processed with different cutoff values.

parameters.name: cutOff
parameters.summary: Specifies the cutoff frequency for a specific channel at which the cutoff will end.

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: Enables or Disables separate cutoff. If Enabled every channel will be processed by it's own cutoff value. If Disabled every channel will be processed with the cutoff value of channel 0.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Notch
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the Notch effect.
methods.remarks: Filter that cuts frequency's in a wide range of specified frequency. Each channel can be separate processed with different cutoff values.

parameters.name: cutOff
parameters.summary: Specifies the cutoff frequency for a specific channel at which the cutoff will have it's maximum amplification.

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: Enables or Disables separate cutoff. If Enabled every channel will be processed by it's own cutoff value. If Disabled every channel will be processed with the cutoff value of channel 0.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Equalizer_Presets
methods.summary: Gets the list of available equalizer preset names.
methods.remarks: Equalizer presets provide pre-configured frequency adjustments for common audio scenarios such as "Rock", "Jazz", "Classical", "Pop", etc. Use Audio_Effects_Equalizer_Preset_Set to apply a preset after adding an equalizer effect.
methods.returns: An observable collection containing all available equalizer preset names.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Equalizer_Preset_Set
methods.summary: Applies a predefined equalizer preset to the audio stream.
methods.remarks: Presets apply professionally-tuned frequency adjustments for various music genres and listening scenarios. Use Audio_Effects_Equalizer_Presets to get a list of available preset names. The equalizer effect must already be added to the stream before applying a preset.

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: The audio stream index (0-3), or -1 to apply to all streams.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name of the equalizer effect to configure.

parameters.name: preset
parameters.summary: The equalizer preset to apply (e.g., Rock, Jazz, Classical).

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Equalizer
methods.summary: Configures a multi-band equalizer effect with customizable frequency response.
methods.remarks: The equalizer supports 1 to 4096 frequency bands (using FFT sizes from 2 to 8192 points). Each channel can be equalized separately when the separate parameter is true. Use Audio_Effects_Equalizer_Preset_Set to apply pre-configured settings for common scenarios. Higher maxGainDB values allow more extreme frequency adjustments but may introduce distortion.

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: The audio stream index (0-3), or -1 to apply to all streams.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name of the equalizer effect to configure.

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: True to equalize each audio channel independently with its own amplification values, false to apply channel 0's values to all channels.

parameters.name: maxGainDB
parameters.summary: Maximum gain adjustment in decibels (default is 20 dB). Controls the dynamic range of frequency adjustments.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_ParametricEQ
methods.summary: Configures a parametric equalizer effect for precise frequency control.
methods.remarks: A parametric equalizer provides surgical frequency control, allowing precise adjustment of specific frequency ranges. Unlike graphic equalizers, parametric EQs let you choose both the center frequency and bandwidth. Use Q values around 1.0 for musical adjustments, higher values (5-10) for notching out specific frequencies. Each channel can be controlled separately for stereo or multi-channel fine-tuning.

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: The audio stream index (0-3), or -1 to apply to all streams.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name of the parametric EQ effect to configure.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.summary: The center frequency in Hz to boost or cut (typically 20 Hz to 20000 Hz).

parameters.name: gain
parameters.summary: The gain adjustment in decibels (-15 dB to +15 dB). Positive values boost, negative values cut.

parameters.name: q
parameters.summary: The Q factor (bandwidth) of the filter. Higher values create narrower frequency bands (typically 0.1 to 10).

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: True to apply independent settings to each channel using per-channel values, false to use channel 0's values for all channels.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_PhaseInvert
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the Phase Invert effect.
methods.remarks: Phase invert component that inverts specific channels.

parameters.name: invert
parameters.summary: Enables and Disables phase invert for a specific channel.

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: Enables or Disables separate invert. If Enabled every channel will be inverted by it's own invert value. If Disabled every channel will be inverted by the value of channel 0.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Phaser
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the Phaser effect.
methods.remarks: Class for phasing amplify audio data. Phasing can be done separate on each channel.

parameters.name: dryWetRatio
parameters.summary: Sets dry-wet mix ratio. 0 - dry, 255 - wet (0 - 255).

parameters.name: feedback
parameters.summary: Sets phaser feedback. 0 - no feedback, 100 = 100% feedback, -100 = -100% feedback (-100 - 100).

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: Enables or Disables separate phasing. If Enabled every channel will be phased by it's own phasing value. If Disabled every channel will be phased with the phasing value of channel 0.

parameters.name: stages
parameters.summary: Sets phaser stages. Recommended from 2 to 24.

parameters.name: startPhase
parameters.summary: Sets phaser's LFO start phase in radians. Needed for stereo phasers.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Fades
methods.summary: Configures fade-in and fade-out effects for audio volume control over time.
methods.remarks: Use this effect to create smooth volume transitions: - Fade-in: Set startVolume=0 and stopVolume=10000 - Fade-out: Set startVolume=10000 and stopVolume=0 - Cross-fade: Use overlapping fade effects on different streams The fade applies linearly between the start and stop times.

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: The audio stream index (0-3), or -1 to apply to all streams.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name of the fade effect to configure.

parameters.name: startVolume
parameters.summary: The initial volume level at the start time (0 to 10000, where 10000 = 100% volume).

parameters.name: stopVolume
parameters.summary: The final volume level at the stop time (0 to 10000, where 10000 = 100% volume).

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: The time position when the fade begins.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: The time position when the fade completes.

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: True to fade each channel independently with per-channel volume values, false to apply channel 0's settings to all channels.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_PitchShift
methods.summary: Configures pitch shifting effect to change audio pitch without affecting playback speed.
methods.remarks: This effect changes the frequency (pitch) of audio while maintaining the same duration and tempo. Common use cases: - Correcting slightly out-of-tune recordings - Creating vocal harmonies - Matching keys between different audio sources Extreme pitch changes (e.g., 0.1 or 10.0) may introduce audio artifacts.

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: The audio stream index (0-3), or -1 to apply to all streams.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name of the pitch shift effect to configure.

parameters.name: pitch
parameters.summary: The pitch multiplier. 1.0 = no change (original pitch). Values < 1.0 lower the pitch (e.g., 0.5 = one octave down). Values > 1.0 raise the pitch (e.g., 2.0 = one octave up). Typical range: 0.5 to 2.0 for musical adjustments.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_SetCurrentChannel
methods.summary: Sets the active audio channel for subsequent effect parameter changes.
methods.remarks: This method determines which audio channel is affected by effect parameter changes. It's useful when you want to apply different effect settings to different channels (e.g., different EQ settings for left and right in stereo). The channel setting persists until changed or the effect is removed.

parameters.name: streamIndex
parameters.summary: The audio stream index (0-3), or -1 to apply to all streams.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The unique name of the effect to configure.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.summary: The channel index to process (0 = first channel, 1 = second channel, etc.). Use -1 to process all channels simultaneously.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_Sound3D
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the Sound3D effect.
methods.remarks: 3D Sound amplification filter that works on 2 channels only. The difference between left and right channel is calculated and added to the main signal.

parameters.name: volume
parameters.summary: Sets the 3D amplification value. A value of 1000 is the same as disabling the filter. Values smaller then 1000 is the same as doing a downmix (mono) of the 2 channels. Values higher then 10000 will distort the sound.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_TrebleEnhancer
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the Treble Enhancer effect.
methods.remarks: Filter to amplify high frequency's of audio data. The frequency range can be adjusted.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.summary: Specifies the frequency range that will be used to amplify. Range is frequency to (sample rate div 2).

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: Enables or Disables separate amplification. If Enabled every channel will be amplified by it's own amplification value. If Disabled every channel will be amplified with the amplification value of channel 0.

parameters.name: volume
parameters.summary: Sets the amplification for a channel. Default value is 0, which means that no amplification occurs. The value shouldn't go over 10000. If separate is True, then every channel will be amplified by its own channel amplification value. If separate is False, then every channel is amplified with the value of channel 0.

methods.name: Audio_Effects_TrueBass
methods.summary: Sets the parameters for the True Bass effect.
methods.remarks: Filter to amplify low frequency's of audio data. The frequency range can be adjusted.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.summary: Specifies the frequency range that will be used to amplify. Range is 0 to frequency.

parameters.name: separate
parameters.summary: Enables or Disables separate amplification. If Enabled every channel will be amplified by it's own amplification value. If Disabled every channel will be amplified with the amplification value of channel 0.

parameters.name: volume
parameters.summary: Sets the amplification for a channel. Default value is 0, which means that no amplification occurs. The value shouldn't go over 10000. If separate is True, then every channel will be amplified by its own channel amplification value. If separate is False, then every channel is amplified with the value of channel 0.

methods.name: Decklink_Output_VideoRenderers
methods.summary: Gets a collection of available Decklink video output devices.
methods.remarks: Enumerates all Blackmagic Decklink cards installed on the system that support video output. These professional video cards are used for broadcast-quality video output.
methods.returns: An observable collection containing the names of all available Decklink video renderers.

methods.name: Decklink_Output_AudioRenderers
methods.summary: Gets a collection of available Decklink audio output devices.
methods.remarks: Enumerates all Blackmagic Decklink cards installed on the system that support audio output. Professional audio output supports multiple channels and embedded audio.
methods.returns: An observable collection containing the names of all available Decklink audio renderers.

methods.name: Decklink_Output_GetVideoProps
methods.summary: Gets real-time video rendering statistics from the active Decklink output.
methods.remarks: Provides performance metrics including: - Frame rate and dropped frames - Buffer utilization - Output timing information Useful for monitoring professional video output quality.
methods.returns: A DecklinkRendererProps object containing video rendering metrics, or null if no Decklink output is active.

methods.name: Decklink_Output_GetAudioProps
methods.summary: Gets real-time audio rendering statistics from the active Decklink output.
methods.remarks: Provides performance metrics including: - Sample rate accuracy - Buffer underruns/overruns - Audio synchronization timing Essential for monitoring professional audio output quality.
methods.returns: A DecklinkRendererProps object containing audio rendering metrics, or null if no Decklink output is active.

methods.name: AddDecklinkRenderer
methods.summary: Configures and adds a Blackmagic Decklink professional video/audio output to the processing pipeline.
methods.remarks: This method: - Initializes the Decklink output with configured settings - Connects video and optionally audio streams - Supports various professional features: - DV encoding for tape output - Analog output with SMPTE/NTSC standards - Dual-link SDI for high-resolution output - Down-conversion for HD to SD output - Uses tee filters to allow simultaneous file and Decklink output The source format must be compatible with Decklink-supported formats.
methods.returns: True if the Decklink renderer was successfully added, false otherwise.

methods.name: IsSourceConnected
methods.summary: Always returns true: a video editor has no capture source to wait on, so consumers (such as VideoView) must not draw a "no signal" overlay over it. Implements IsSourceConnected.

methods.name: Video_Transition_Names
methods.summary: Gets a collection of available video transition effect names.
methods.remarks: These transitions can be applied between video clips to create smooth visual effects. Use Video_Transition_GetIDFromName to convert a name to its corresponding ID.
methods.returns: An observable collection containing the names of all available video transitions.

methods.name: Video_Transition_GetIDFromName
methods.summary: Gets the numeric identifier for a video transition effect from its name.
methods.remarks: This method maps transition names to their internal numeric identifiers. The IDs are used when configuring transitions in the video editing timeline.

parameters.name: name

methods.returns: The numeric ID of the transition, or 0 if not found.

methods.summary: Starts delayed graph. Start_DelayEnabled must be true to use this method. A graph that has already run (a start without Start_DelayEnabled, or an earlier StartDelayed) is not started again; the call reports an error instead.

methods.name: Object_Detection_Update
methods.summary: Updates object detection settings.
