methods.summary: Processes AForge data.

methods.name: FireOnStop
methods.summary: Fires the OnStop event on the UI thread when a video view is available, or directly on the current thread otherwise. This ensures user event handlers always run on the UI thread and don't need to use Dispatcher.Invoke/BeginInvoke to access UI controls.

methods.name: FastEdit_ExtractAudioStreamAsync
methods.summary: Extracts the audio stream from a video file without re-encoding.
methods.remarks: This method performs fast audio extraction without re-encoding, preserving the original audio quality. The output format is determined by the file extension of outputFile. Requires FFMPEG executable files to be deployed with your application. Premium Edition license required for production use.

parameters.name: inputFile
parameters.summary: Path to the input video file containing audio.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: The time position to start extraction from.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: The time position to stop extraction at.

parameters.name: outputFile
parameters.summary: Path where the extracted audio file will be saved.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful.

methods.name: FastEdit_CutFileAsync
methods.summary: Cuts a segment from a video file without re-encoding.
methods.remarks: This method performs fast cutting without re-encoding, preserving original quality. The cut may not be frame-accurate for some codecs due to keyframe limitations. The default behavior uses output-side seeking. Use the overload accepting FastEditSeekMode to select input-side seeking. Requires FFMPEG executable files to be deployed with your application. Premium Edition license required for production use.

parameters.name: inputFile
parameters.summary: Path to the input video file to cut from.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: The time position to start the cut from.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: The time position to end the cut at.

parameters.name: outputFile
parameters.summary: Path where the cut video segment will be saved.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful.

methods.name: FastEdit_CutFileAsync
methods.summary: Cuts a segment from a video file without re-encoding using the selected seek mode.
methods.remarks: This method performs fast cutting without re-encoding, preserving original quality. The cut may not be frame-accurate for some codecs due to keyframe limitations. Use Input for large files when seeking speed is more important than output-side seeking. Input-side seeking is also keyframe-dependent. Requires FFMPEG executable files to be deployed with your application. Premium Edition license required for production use.

parameters.name: inputFile
parameters.summary: Path to the input video file to cut from.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.summary: The time position to start the cut from.

parameters.name: stopTime
parameters.summary: The time position to end the cut at.

parameters.name: outputFile
parameters.summary: Path where the cut video segment will be saved.

parameters.name: seekMode
parameters.summary: Specifies whether FFmpeg seeks before or after opening the input.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful.

methods.name: FastEdit_MuxStreamsAsync
methods.summary: Multiplexes (combines) audio and video streams from multiple files into a single output file.
methods.remarks: This method combines streams without re-encoding, making it very fast. Commonly used to add audio tracks to video files or combine separate audio/video streams. The streams must be compatible with the output container format. Premium Edition license required for production use.

parameters.name: sourceStreams
parameters.summary: List of source streams to multiplex, each specifying file path and stream type.

parameters.name: shortest
parameters.summary: If true, cuts all streams to match the duration of the shortest stream.

parameters.name: outputFile
parameters.summary: Path where the multiplexed output file will be saved.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful.

methods.name: FFMPEGWrapperOnStopDelegateMethod
methods.summary: Handles the completion of FFMPEG operations on the UI thread.
methods.remarks: This method is invoked on the UI thread to safely raise the OnStop event.

parameters.name: result
parameters.summary: True if the operation completed successfully, false otherwise.

methods.name: FFMPEGWrapperOnStop
methods.summary: Handles the FFMPEG wrapper stop event and performs cleanup operations.
methods.remarks: This method writes tags if in Convert mode and ensures the OnStop event is raised on the appropriate thread.

parameters.name: eventArgs
parameters.summary: Event arguments containing the operation result.

methods.name: FFMPEGWrapperOnProgressDelegateMethod
methods.summary: Handles progress updates from FFMPEG operations on the UI thread.
methods.remarks: This method is invoked on the UI thread to safely raise the OnProgress event.

parameters.name: args
parameters.summary: Progress event arguments containing completion percentage.

methods.name: FFMPEGWrapperOnProgress
methods.summary: Handles progress updates from the FFMPEG wrapper.
methods.remarks: Ensures progress events are raised on the appropriate thread for UI updates.

parameters.name: progressEventArgs
parameters.summary: Event arguments containing the current progress percentage.

methods.name: FastEdit_JoinFilesAsync
methods.summary: Joins multiple video files into a single output file without re-encoding.
methods.remarks: This method performs fast concatenation without re-encoding. IMPORTANT: All input files must have identical format parameters: - Same video codec - Same resolution - Same frame rate - Same audio codec and sample rate If files have different formats, use the standard editing mode with re-encoding. Requires FFMPEG executable files to be deployed with your application. Premium Edition license required for production use.

parameters.name: inputFiles
parameters.summary: Array of input file paths to join together.

parameters.name: outputFile
parameters.summary: Path where the joined output file will be saved.

methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful.

methods.name: FastEdit_StopAsync
methods.summary: Stops the currently running fast edit operation.
methods.remarks: Call this method to abort any running fast edit operation (cut, join, extract, or mux). The operation will be terminated and partial output files may be left incomplete.
methods.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if the operation was stopped successfully.

methods.name: CreateAsync
methods.summary: Creates a new instance of VideoEditCore asynchronously with a video view.
methods.remarks: Use this method to avoid blocking the UI thread during initialization. The returned instance is fully initialized and ready for use.

parameters.name: videoView
parameters.summary: The video view interface for rendering video output.

methods.returns: A Task<VideoEditCore> representing the asynchronous creation operation.

methods.name: CreateAsync
methods.summary: Creates a new instance of VideoEditCore asynchronously without a video view.
methods.remarks: Use this method for headless operation or when the video view will be set later. The initialization is performed on a background thread to avoid blocking.
methods.returns: A Task<VideoEditCore> representing the asynchronous creation operation.

methods.name: InitAsync
methods.summary: Initializes the video editing control asynchronously.
methods.remarks: Performs all initialization steps on a background thread. This includes loading codecs, filters, and setting up default properties.
methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous initialization operation.

methods.name: Init
methods.summary: Initializes the video editing control with all necessary components and default settings.
methods.remarks: This method performs the following initialization steps: - Configures logging and debugging - Sets up redistributable components - Initializes DirectShow filters and codecs - Creates audio processors and video effects - Loads system profiles and trusted filters - Sets default properties for video editing

methods.name: UnbanLAV
methods.summary: Removes LAV filters from the blacklist to enable their use.
methods.remarks: LAV filters are high-quality open-source DirectShow filters. This method enables their use and blacklists conflicting Microsoft filters when LAV is available. LAV filters typically provide better codec support and performance.

methods.name: BanLAV
methods.summary: Adds LAV filters to the blacklist to prevent their use.
methods.remarks: Disables LAV filters and re-enables Microsoft DTV filters. This may be necessary for compatibility with certain systems or when LAV filters cause issues. The system will fall back to default Windows codecs.

methods.name: CheckRequiredLicense
methods.summary: Checks the current configuration and determines which license edition is required based on enabled features.
methods.remarks: This method evaluates the current SDK configuration and determines the minimum license level needed. Standard features include basic video editing, AVI/WMV/MKV output, audio and animated GIF output, and common video effects. Professional features include DV output, custom output, WebM, FFMPEG, motion detection, WMV network streaming, virtual camera, Picture-in-Picture, video rotation, and custom DirectShow video filters. Premium features include encrypted output, MP4, FFmpeg.exe output, other network streaming, Decklink output, and GPU effects. Raises the OnLicenseRequired event with details about required features and the minimum license level.

parameters.name: std
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains true if standard edition license is required; otherwise, false.

parameters.name: pro
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains true if professional edition license is required; otherwise, false.

parameters.name: pre
parameters.summary: When this method returns, contains true if premium edition license is required; otherwise, false.

parameters.name: message

methods.summary: Builds the graph in the timeline's apartment. An MTA timeline uses the pump, which is the same apartment. An STA timeline is built on that thread. With no timeline yet, a UI thread builds inline and any other caller gets the pump so the graph window has a message loop (#1659).

methods.name: TryBeginStart
methods.summary: Checks that no start is in progress and publishes this one, in a single step.
methods.remarks: A graph that is already running belongs to the pump that built it. would join that thread as a leftover and end it under a live graph, and the in-place restart in - now a residual guard, reachable only where the state and the flags disagree - would tear the graph down from the caller's thread and leave the pump published with nothing to marshal but the next graph, which is not its (#1659). Stop the job first. Check and publish are one step because the flags the check reads are otherwise set much later, inside on the pump thread - a window a whole thread hand-off wide, through which two starts walked side by side and built two graphs over one set of engine fields (#1661). The API mode is claimed here for the same reason: set by the door that passed the check rather than by the one that goes on to build, it could leave a job started with on the async flag, which Stop() then declines to stop.

parameters.name: async
parameters.summary: Whether the caller is the async door, which fixes the API mode for the job this start builds.

parameters.name: claim
parameters.summary: The published claim, to be given back through Boolean) when the start builds no running graph.

methods.returns: false when a start is already in progress and the caller must not start.

methods.name: BeginTeardownClaim
methods.summary: Takes the engine for a teardown, so no start can begin while one is under way.
methods.remarks: clears _started in its finally, on the pump thread, while the caller is still blocked in the marshalled teardown and has its own left to do. Without this the engine reads as free for that whole stretch, and a start walking in reads the same _graphPump as its leftover and joins, nulls and disposes the pump the stop is reclaiming, in parallel with it. Never refused, unlike : a teardown has to go ahead. Whoever else is in flight is either the start whose job this is ending, or another teardown doing the same work, and neither is a reason to leave a running graph up or to return from Stop() before it is down. Both are counted, so the engine reopens when the last one leaves rather than when the last one arrived. Two teardowns overlapping still reclaim the same pump, as they always did - answers straight away for a thread that has exited and its Dispose is idempotent - and that is not what this claim is for. It also takes the start flags over: a start that this teardown is ending must not, on its own way out, wipe the state the teardown is now managing.
methods.returns: The claim, to be given back through Boolean).

methods.name: EndClaim
methods.summary: Gives a claim back, freeing the engine for the next start when the holder leaves nothing running behind it.
methods.remarks: The count always drops - exactly one release per claim, every one of them in a finally - but the flags are only cleared by the start that still owns them. A teardown takes that ownership away (BeginTeardownClaim), and the flags alone no longer say whether the engine is free (StartIntl clears them on its failure paths while their owner is still working), so clearing them here regardless would wipe state the teardown is managing - the race this whole mechanism exists to close. A dispose that arrived during the start is carried out here, outside the lock, once the build is over (#1663).

parameters.name: claim
parameters.summary: The claim Object@) or BeginTeardownClaim handed out.

parameters.name: freeEngine
parameters.summary: Clear the start flags with the claim. A start that built no graph needs that; a start that did, and a teardown, leave the flags to the job and to Boolean).

methods.returns: true when the engine was disposed on the way out, so the start must report false.

methods.name: StartAsyncOnPumpThread
methods.summary: Starts the async graph on a dedicated MTA message-pumping thread that lives for the graph's whole lifetime. See GraphPumpThread for why this is required.
methods.remarks: Gives the claim back on the pool thread when the start produced nothing, rather than in StartAsync after an await, so the returned task still completes without the caller's SynchronizationContext.
methods.returns: true when the graph was built and is running on the pump thread.

methods.name: StartOnPumpThread
methods.summary: The body of Object), run on the calling thread.
methods.remarks: Called directly by the synchronous Start when its own thread runs no message loop (GitHub issue #1659), and through a pool thread by StartAsync. Both doors hold the start claim across the whole call and give it back only after it has returned, so no second start can be in here - taking apart the pump this one is reclaiming - at the same time.
methods.returns: true when the graph was built and is running on the pump thread.

methods.name: TryRunOnPumpThread
methods.summary: Marshals action onto the graph pump thread when one is active. Returns true if the work was (or is being) run on that thread; false when there is no live pump thread and the caller should run the action inline.

parameters.name: action
parameters.summary: Work to run on the graph pump thread.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.summary: When true, block until the action completes; otherwise post it.

methods.name: ReclaimGraphPump
methods.summary: Ends and reclaims the graph pump thread after its teardown has been marshalled onto it. If the thread exits within the bounded join it is disposed and the _graphPump slot cleared. If it is genuinely wedged (join elapsed while still running) the reference is retained — ownership is NOT dropped — and an error is logged, so a later Stop/Start can retry instead of overlapping a live teardown. This is the bounded lesser-evil versus an unbounded hang.

parameters.name: pump
parameters.summary: The pump instance captured by the caller.

methods.returns: True if the pump thread exited and was disposed, or is the calling thread and was told to end its loop; false if it is still running (wedged) and was retained — callers must then NOT release the graph's COM objects, which the live thread is still using.

methods.name: Start
methods.summary: Starts the video editing process, building the DirectShow graph and beginning playback or conversion.
methods.remarks: This method performs the following operations: Validates configuration and timeline setupConfigures redistributable components and codecsBuilds the DirectShow Editing Services (DES) render graphCreates and connects all filters (sources, effects, encoders, renderers)Sets the graph to PLAYING stateStarts progress monitoring and event handling The behavior depends on the Mode property: - Preview: Displays video without saving - Convert: Processes and saves to Output_Filename - Edit: Full editing with timeline support This method is synchronous and may take several seconds to complete depending on the timeline complexity. For async operation, use StartAsync(). The DirectShow graph owns a window, and the thread that builds the graph owns it and must keep pumping messages for as long as the graph lives. The timeline's COM objects can be used only in the apartment that created them, so that is where the graph is built. A file added on a UI thread is edited on that thread. A file added on a worker thread is edited on a dedicated message-pumping thread, including when Start itself is called from the UI. Called while a job is already running or starting, it reports an error and returns false instead of restarting in place, as StartAsync() has always done. Call Stop() first.
methods.returns: true if the graph was successfully built and started; false if an error occurred.

methods.name: StartIntl
methods.summary: The body of Start, always executed on the thread that will own the graph.
methods.returns: true if the graph was successfully built and started; false if an error occurred.

methods.name: StopAsync
methods.summary: Stops the video editing process asynchronously, releasing all resources and closing the DirectShow graph.
methods.remarks: This method performs the following cleanup operations: Stops the DirectShow graph and sets filters to NULL stateReleases all COM objects and DirectShow filtersStops progress monitoring and event handlingFinalizes output file (if converting)Clears the timeline and temporary resources This is the async version of Stop(). Use this method when the video editor was started with StartAsync(). When the timeline was created on the calling thread, the stop runs there before the method returns. Otherwise the stop completes on a background thread.
methods.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous stop operation.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops the video editing process synchronously, releasing all resources and closing the DirectShow graph.
methods.remarks: This method performs the following cleanup operations: Stops the DirectShow graph and sets filters to NULL stateReleases all COM objects and DirectShow filtersStops progress monitoring and event handlingFinalizes output file (if converting)Clears the timeline and temporary resources This is the synchronous version of StopAsync(). The method blocks until the stop operation is complete. For async operation, use StopAsync().

methods.name: FinishStaStop
methods.summary: Stops a graph that lives on the timeline's STA and releases claim. StopEventArgs) stays outside the claim so a batch-convert handler can start the next job.

methods.name: StopIntl
methods.summary: Stops the capture or preview process. Thread-safe: acquires _stopLock and checks _stopping to prevent concurrent/re-entrant execution. Also checks _state to prevent redundant cleanup when a previous stop has already completed.
methods.remarks: Raises the errors other threads logged during the stop itself (#3449). A caller that raises OnStop once it has given its claim back uses the other overload and raises them there.

parameters.name: notifyView
parameters.summary: When true (default) the view stop notification (InvokeStop) is dispatched from inside this method. Pass false when the caller is the view's own UI thread and is blocked waiting on the pump thread to run this teardown — in that case a synchronous CallInvoke back to the blocked UI thread would deadlock, so the caller runs InvokeStop itself after this returns.

methods.returns: True if the stop was actually performed; false if it was skipped (already stopping or already stopped).

methods.name: StopIntl
methods.summary: Boolean) for a caller that raises OnStop after giving its claim back: the errors other threads logged during the stop are handed to it, to be raised there, just before OnStop - a Start() or Dispose() from the handler must not meet the claim (#3449).

parameters.name: errorsDuringStop
parameters.summary: Set to the errors when this call performed the stop and took any; left as it is otherwise.

methods.returns: See Boolean).

methods.name: NotifyViewStop
methods.summary: Dispatches the view stop notification (InvokeStop) on the view's UI thread. InvokeStop touches WPF/WinForms UI elements (ClearWPFImage, RecreateUI, etc.) so it must run on the UI thread; when called from a pool thread it is marshalled via CallInvoke. Call this from the thread that initiated the stop — never from the graph pump thread while a caller is blocked waiting on that pump, or the synchronous CallInvoke would deadlock.

methods.name: StopMain
methods.summary: Main internal method that performs the actual stop operation for video editing/playback.
methods.remarks: This method handles: - Stopping network streamers and FFMPEG processes - Stopping DirectShow media control (with timeout to prevent indefinite hangs) - Cleaning up graph callbacks - Resetting state to Free All operations are wrapped in try-catch to ensure cleanup continues even if errors occur. Must be called under _stopLock. The _stopping and _started flags are managed by StopIntl.

methods.name: StopMediaControl
methods.summary: Stops the DirectShow media control with a timeout to prevent indefinite hangs. IMediaControl.Stop() can block forever if a filter's streaming thread is deadlocked or waiting for resources. This method runs the stop on a background thread and waits up to MediaControlStopTimeoutMs milliseconds. If the timeout expires, cleanup proceeds anyway — the subsequent Clear() call will release COM references which should eventually unblock the filter graph.

methods.name: AddNetworkStreamingFFMPEG
methods.summary: Configures network streaming using FFMPEG executable for RTMP, RTSP, or UDP protocols.
methods.remarks: This method sets up FFMPEG-based network streaming by: - Creating an FFMPEG output filter configured for streaming - Connecting video and optionally audio streams - Supporting custom FFMPEG arguments for advanced streaming scenarios - Using a tee filter to split the stream for simultaneous file output and streaming Commonly used for streaming to services like YouTube, Twitch, or custom RTMP servers.

methods.name: AddNetworkStreamingNDI
methods.summary: Configures network streaming using NDI (Network Device Interface) protocol.
methods.remarks: NDI enables high-quality, low-latency video streaming over IP networks. This method: - Creates an NDI sender with a specified stream name - Connects video and optionally audio streams - Uses a tee filter to allow simultaneous file output and NDI streaming NDI is commonly used in professional broadcast and production environments for real-time video exchange between devices on the same network.

methods.name: AddNetworkStreamingHLS
methods.summary: Configures HLS (HTTP Live Streaming) output for adaptive bitrate streaming.
methods.remarks: HLS is Apple's adaptive streaming protocol that works over standard HTTP. This method: - Creates an HLS encoder using Media Foundation - Generates segmented video files and M3U8 playlists - Optionally starts a built-in HTTP server for testing - Supports both video and audio streams HLS is widely supported on mobile devices and modern browsers, making it ideal for web-based video delivery.

methods.name: AddNetworkStreamingSW
methods.summary: Configures software-based network streaming using built-in MP4 encoder.
methods.remarks: This method uses the software MP4 encoder with network streaming capabilities. Features: - Supports various streaming protocols through the MP4 encoder - Includes video resizing and cropping options - Can use NVENC hardware acceleration if available - Supports AAC or MP3 (LAME) audio encoding This is a fallback option when FFMPEG or specialized streaming methods are not available or suitable.

methods.name: AddOutputAVIAudio
methods.summary: Connects audio streams to the AVI encoder and builds the audio output pipeline.
methods.remarks: This method connects up to 4 audio output pins to the AVI encoder. Each audio stream is connected to a specific encoder input. After all connections are made, the encoder is built to finalize the audio pipeline.
methods.returns: true if all audio connections and build operations succeed, false otherwise.

methods.name: AddOutputAVIVideo
methods.summary: Configures and initializes the AVI video encoder with specified settings.
methods.remarks: This method: - Creates and configures the AVI encoder with video codec settings - Optionally configures audio compression (ACM or MP3/LAME) - Connects the video output pin to the encoder - Builds the encoder pipeline if no audio is present The AVI format supports various video codecs through VFW (Video for Windows).
methods.returns: true if the video encoder is successfully initialized, false otherwise.

methods.name: AddOutputWebMVideo

methods.remarks: This method: - Creates and configures the WebM encoder with VP8/VP9 settings - Adds a video effects filter for YUY2 color space conversion - Supports advanced VP8/VP9 encoding parameters - Handles both constant bitrate and quality-based encoding WebM is an open-source container format designed for web video.

methods.name: Video_Effects_Add
methods.summary: Adds a video effect to the processing pipeline.
methods.remarks: Effects are processed in the order they are added. Multiple effects of the same or different types can be added. Effects can include: - Color adjustments (brightness, contrast, saturation) - Image overlays and logos - Text overlays - Geometric transformations - Various filters and artistic effects Thread-safe operation.

methods.name: Video_Effects_Clear
methods.summary: Removes all video effects from the processing pipeline.
methods.remarks: This method: - Properly disposes of effects that hold resources (ImageLogo, TextLogo, ScrollingTextLogo) - Clears the entire effects collection - Is thread-safe Call this method when switching projects or cleaning up resources.

methods.name: Video_Effects_Remove
methods.summary: Removes a specific video effect from the processing pipeline.
methods.remarks: This method: - Finds the effect by exact name match - Properly disposes of effects that hold resources - Removes the effect from the collection - Is thread-safe If the effect is not found, no action is taken.

parameters.name: name

methods.name: Video_Effects_GPU_Add
methods.summary: Adds a GPU-accelerated video effect to the processing pipeline.
methods.remarks: GPU effects provide hardware-accelerated video processing using DirectX 11. Benefits include: - Significantly faster processing compared to CPU effects - Real-time performance for complex effects - Lower CPU usage Requires a DirectX 11 compatible graphics card. Effects are processed in the order they are added, and only while Video_Effects_GPU_Enabled is true.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.summary: The GPU video effect to add, implementing IGPUVideoEffect interface.

methods.name: Video_Effects_GPU_Get

methods.remarks: Use this method to access and modify GPU effect parameters during runtime. GPU effects can be adjusted in real-time without rebuilding the pipeline.

parameters.name: name

methods.returns: The GPU video effect with the specified name, or null if not found.

methods.name: Video_Effects_GPU_Clear
methods.summary: Removes all GPU video effects from the processing pipeline.
methods.remarks: This method clears all GPU-accelerated effects. GPU resources are properly released. Use this when switching projects or cleaning up GPU resources.

methods.name: Video_Effects_GPU_Remove

methods.remarks: Removes the specified GPU effect and releases its resources. If the effect is not found, no action is taken. The remaining effects continue processing in order.

classes.name: GraphPumpThread
classes.summary: A dedicated, long-lived MTA thread that runs a classic Win32 message loop for the lifetime of an async (StartAsync) DirectShow graph, in Preview and Convert alike.
classes.remarks: DirectShow graph teardown (quartz CFGControl::Shutdown) issues a blocking SendMessage to the filter graph's own (thread-affine) window. When the graph is built on a regular thread-pool thread (the old StartAsync → Task.Run(Start) behaviour), that thread returns to the pool and stops pumping messages, so a later teardown on a different pool thread deadlocks forever waiting for the graph window to answer. This helper builds, runs and tears the graph down on one thread that keeps pumping messages, so the teardown SendMessage is always serviced. The thread is MTA (the default for a new managed thread). AMTimeline is ThreadingModel=Both and IAMTimeline has no proxy/stub, so it can be called only in the apartment that created it. Input_Add*Async creates it on an MTA pool thread, and this pump is that same apartment. A timeline created on an STA is not used from here — the engine builds that graph on the STA (#1995).

properties.name: IsOnPumpThread
properties.summary: True when the calling code is executing on the pump thread.

properties.name: IsAlive
properties.summary: True while the underlying thread has not yet exited.

methods.name: RunStart
methods.summary: Starts the pump thread, runs startWork on it, and returns its result. On return (when the result is true) the thread is pumping messages until the loop is ended via Int32) or QuitFromPumpThread.

parameters.name: startWork
parameters.summary: The graph-build work (engine Start), executed on the pump thread.

methods.returns: The value returned by startWork.

methods.name: Start
methods.summary: Starts the pump thread on startWork and returns as soon as the thread owns a message queue - it does NOT wait for the work to finish.
methods.remarks: Split out of Boolean}) so a caller holding a lock can publish this pump and start it without also holding that lock across the whole graph build. The build calls into the UI thread synchronously, and a UI thread that then waits for the same lock deadlocks against it.

parameters.name: startWork
parameters.summary: The graph-build work, executed on the pump thread.

methods.name: WaitForStart
methods.summary: Waits for the work handed to Boolean}) to finish and returns its result.
methods.returns: The value returned by the start work.

methods.name: RunStartWork
methods.summary: Runs the start work and lets go of it. Every engine passes a delegate bound to itself, and this thread holding it - in the field or in a stack slot of the frame that pumps - keeps a dropped engine reachable, so its finalizer never runs (#1939). A frame of its own, not inlined, so no slot outlives the call.
methods.returns: What the start work returned.

methods.name: Invoke
methods.summary: Runs action on the pump thread. When wait is true the call blocks (bounded) until the action has run.

parameters.name: action
parameters.summary: Work to run on the pump thread.

methods.returns: True if the work was run on the pump thread; false if the thread is gone (caller should run inline) or a synchronous post could not be delivered.

methods.name: Invoke
methods.summary: Runs action on the pump thread, and reports whether that thread took it at all.

parameters.name: action
parameters.summary: Work to run on the pump thread.

parameters.name: queued
parameters.summary: True when the action went onto the queue, which means it WILL run - on the message loop, or on the drain at thread exit - even when this method returns false because the bounded wait elapsed. False means the pump never took it and the caller has to run it itself. The bounded wait and the entry guard below both return false, so a caller that must not run the work twice has to tell them apart by this flag.

methods.returns: True if the work completed on the pump thread.

methods.name: WaitProcessingPostedMessages
methods.summary: Waits for handle while dispatching the calling thread's posted and sent messages, where WPF Dispatcher.Invoke and WinForms Control.Invoke calls from other threads arrive. Input, paint and timer messages stay queued. Anything already queued on the WPF dispatcher runs too when its message is dispatched, so application code posted with BeginInvoke can run inside the wait: the usual price of a pumping STA wait, against both threads blocked until the timeout. A WM_QUIT already in the queue is held until this wait returns and then posted again. Putting it back at once and stopping made every later slice of WaitForStart a bare wait, so a window closed during Start never ran the pump's callback into the UI.
methods.returns: True if the handle was signalled within timeoutMs.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Ends the message loop and joins the thread (bounded wait).

parameters.name: joinTimeoutMs
parameters.summary: Maximum time to wait for the thread to exit.

methods.returns: True if the thread has exited (or was never alive); false if it was still running when the bounded join elapsed. Callers must not dispose / drop a pump that returned false — the thread may still touch the pump's resources.

methods.name: RunFinalWork
methods.summary: Runs the last work this pump will do and waits for it, bounded: work runs on the pump thread, and the loop ends after it when it reports it released the graph. For an engine's finalizer, which must not release the graph from its own thread (#1939). It waits rather than returning at once so the finalizer thread, the process's only one, finalizes nothing else of the engine while its graph is being released; it does not join.

parameters.name: work
parameters.summary: The release; false only when it declined and the graph stays with this thread. A release that ran - even one that threw partway - has done all it ever will, and returns true so the thread does not pump on for nothing.

methods.returns: true when the work was taken: it ran, or is still queued past the bounded wait and runs when this thread services its queue - the caller must not run it too.

methods.name: QuitFromPumpThread
methods.summary: Requests the message loop to end after the currently queued work, from the pump thread.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.remarks: The events are released only once the thread has actually exited. Disposing them under a thread that is still running makes its own Set calls throw, and makes WaitForStart return a default "the start failed" for work that is still in flight - see the bounded-wait contract on Int32).

classes.name: ViewErrorDispatch
classes.summary: Raises the DirectShow engines' OnError on the view's UI thread.
classes.remarks: From another thread the event is posted and waited for while the UI thread is raising it, as Invoke did - the graph thread keeps the UI's pace. The wait ends when the engine starts a stop, or when the UI thread has not picked the event up within PickUpTimeoutMs: it is then busy, or waiting in Stop(), a seek or a pause for this very graph thread, and a graph thread that waited on regardless deadlocked with it (#3449). The event is raised once the UI thread is back in its message loop, so an error the UI thread itself raises before then, inline, reaches OnError ahead of it. Not covered: once the UI thread has started the handler - the customer's, or the SDK's own error dialog when there is none - a seek or a pause made from inside it still waits for this graph thread, which waits for the handler (#3660).

methods.name: Raise
methods.summary: Raises raise on view's UI thread.
methods.remarks: A view that is neither a WinForms control nor a WPF element is invoked through Object[]), synchronously, as before.

parameters.summary: The engine's view, its handle created.

parameters.name: stopping
parameters.summary: True once the engine has started a stop; a graph thread then stops waiting.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.summary: The engine's name, for the trace of a posted handler that threw.

methods.name: RaiseCaught
methods.summary: Raises a posted error. A handler that throws is traced, as one called through Invoke was; on the UI thread it would otherwise reach the application's unhandled-exception handler.

classes.name: VirtualCameraCustomStreamer
classes.summary: Provides functionality to stream custom video frames to a VisioForge virtual camera device. This class creates a DirectShow filter graph that captures frames from a queue and outputs them to a virtual camera sink.
classes.remarks: The streamer uses a fake screen capture source combined with a sample grabber to intercept and replace frames with custom video data provided through VideoFrame). Frames are automatically resized and color space converted as needed.

constructors.name: VirtualCameraCustomStreamer
constructors.summary: Initializes a new instance of the VirtualCameraCustomStreamer class. Creates and configures a DirectShow filter graph for streaming custom video frames to a virtual camera.

parameters.name: context
parameters.summary: The DirectShow context for logging and error handling. If null, a new context is created.

parameters.summary: The width of the video frames in pixels.

parameters.name: height
parameters.summary: The height of the video frames in pixels.

parameters.summary: The frame rate for the video stream.

parameters.name: colorspace
parameters.summary: The color space of the input video frames. Default is RGB.

methods.name: WriteVideoFrame
methods.summary: Writes a video frame to the virtual camera stream. The frame is added to an internal queue and will be processed on the next sample grabber callback.
methods.remarks: The queue is limited to 5 frames. If the queue is full, the oldest frame is automatically discarded. Frames are automatically resized and color-converted to match the output format if needed.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.summary: The video frame to stream. The frame is cloned internally, so the caller retains ownership of the original.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases the unmanaged resources used by the VirtualCameraCustomStreamer and optionally releases the managed resources.

parameters.name: disposing
parameters.summary: Always true - this class has no finalizer. It never needed one: the frame buffers freed below are filled only by the sample grabber callback, and while that callback is registered the native filter's CCW roots this object, so a finalizer could only ever have run with nothing left to free - after freeing them without first clearing the callback (GitHub issue #1545). Kept so COM and managed objects stay out of a finalizer if one is ever added.

enums.name: ImageUpdateResult
enums.summary: The outcome of an image update.

values.name: Drawn
values.summary: The image was installed and has been painted into a frame.

values.name: NotDrawn
values.summary: The image was installed but had not been painted when the wait ran out - a pipeline that is not playing never draws.

values.name: Superseded
values.summary: A later update replaced this image before it was ever painted. The image on screen belongs to that call, not to this one.

values.name: NotBuilt
values.summary: The block was not built yet. The image will be loaded when it is, so nothing has been painted and nothing was waited for.

values.name: Failed
values.summary: The image was not installed at all.

enums.name: ScreenRecordingPermissionStatus
enums.summary: Result of a screen-recording permission request on macOS / Mac Catalyst.

values.name: Granted
values.summary: Permission is already granted; screen capture will succeed.

values.name: Denied
values.summary: Permission is not (yet) granted. Either the user has never been prompted, or they explicitly denied it — these are indistinguishable via the system API. Call BaseContext) to post the TCC dialog on first run; if it has already been shown, the user must enable access in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording and relaunch the app.

values.name: NotApplicable
values.summary: The current platform does not require screen-recording permission.

values.name: Unavailable
values.summary: The underlying TCC API could not be invoked — typically an EntryPointNotFoundException or DllNotFoundException from a stripped or sandbox-restricted CoreGraphics runtime. Distinct from Denied because the caller's UI should not tell the user "you denied access" when in fact the check never ran.

values.name: Angular

values.name: Raw
values.summary: The raw DPI. This is the DPI of the physical screen as measured on the screen itself. Use this when reading the pixel density from the monitor EDID.
