values.name: Height
values.summary: The height component of the size.

enums.name: BarcodeType
enums.summary: Specifies the types of barcodes that can be recognized or generated by the video processing components. This enumeration includes various 1D (linear) and 2D (matrix) barcode formats.

values.name: Code93

values.name: RSS14
values.summary: RSS-14 (GS1 DataBar), a compact linear symbology.

values.name: QR
values.summary: QR Code, a popular 2D matrix symbology.

values.name: PDF417

enums.name: CamshiftMode
enums.summary: Specifies the color space mode to be used by the Camshift (Continuously Adaptive Mean-Shift) tracking algorithm. The choice of color space can significantly impact the robustness and accuracy of object tracking.

values.name: RGB

values.name: HSL

values.name: Mixed

enums.name: CVHandGesture

values.name: Palm

enums.name: CVShapeType

values.name: SimpleBackgroundModeling

values.name: TwoFramesDifference

enums.name: MotionProcessorType
enums.summary: Specifies the algorithm used for processing and visualizing detected motion in video frames.

values.name: None
values.summary: No motion visualization or processing is performed; only raw motion detection occurs.

values.name: BlobCountingObjects
values.summary: Identifies, counts, and tracks individual moving objects with bounding rectangles.

values.name: GridMotionAreaProcessing
values.summary: Divides the frame into a grid and analyzes motion levels in each cell independently.

values.name: MotionAreaHighlighting
values.summary: Highlights all pixels where motion is detected, creating filled regions of color over moving areas.

values.name: MotionBorderHighlighting
values.summary: Highlights only the outer edges of motion regions, drawing colored outlines around moving areas.

enums.name: ObjectDetectorScalingMode
enums.summary: Specifies the scaling strategy for the search window used in object detection algorithms. This mode determines how the detector iterates through different sizes of objects to find matches.

values.name: GreaterToSmaller
values.summary: The object detector will start searching with larger windows and gradually scale down to smaller ones. This mode can be efficient if the target objects are expected to be large.

values.name: SmallerToGreater
values.summary: The object detector will start searching with smaller windows and gradually scale up to larger ones. This mode can be efficient if the target objects are expected to be small.

enums.name: ObjectDetectorSearchMode
enums.summary: Specifies the search mode for object detection algorithms. This enumeration defines how the detector scans an image or video frame for objects.

values.name: Default
values.summary: The entire image or video frame will be scanned for objects. This is the default and most comprehensive search mode.

values.name: Single
values.summary: Only a single object will be retrieved. The search stops after the first object is found. This mode is useful for performance optimization when only the presence of an object matters.

values.name: NoOverlap
values.summary: If an object has already been detected within an area, that area will not be scanned again for inner or overlapping objects. This can save computation time and prevent redundant detections.

values.name: Average
values.summary: If several objects are located within one another (overlapping detections), their bounding boxes will be averaged into a single result. This helps in consolidating multiple detections of the same object.

enums.name: HorizontalAlignment
enums.summary: Specifies the horizontal alignment of visual elements within video frames during video processing operations.

values.name: Left
values.summary: Aligns the element to the left edge of its container.

values.name: Right
values.summary: Aligns the element to the right edge of its container.

values.name: Center
values.summary: Centers the element horizontally within its container.

enums.name: MotionCHLColor
enums.summary: Specifies the color channel to use for highlighting motion areas in video frames during motion detection processing.

values.name: Red
values.summary: Highlights motion areas using the red color channel.

values.name: Green
values.summary: Highlights motion areas using the green color channel.

values.name: Blue
values.summary: Highlights motion areas using the blue color channel.

enums.name: ResizeFilterMode
enums.summary: Specifies the transformation mode for the video resize/rotate filter in video processing pipelines.

values.name: Resize
values.summary: Resize mode: Scales video dimensions to specified width and height.

values.name: Rotate
values.summary: Rotate mode: Rotates video frames by specified angles (90°, 180°, 270°, or custom).

enums.name: VerticalAlignment
enums.summary: Specifies the vertical alignment of visual elements within video frames during video processing operations.

values.name: Top
values.summary: Aligns the element to the top edge of its container.

values.name: Center
values.summary: Centers the element vertically within its container.

values.name: Bottom
values.summary: Aligns the element to the bottom edge of its container.

enums.name: VideoRendererEVRDeinterlaceMode
enums.summary: Specifies the deinterlacing modes available for the Enhanced Video Renderer (EVR). Deinterlacing converts interlaced video (where each frame consists of two fields captured at different times) into progressive video (where each frame contains all lines of a single moment in time).

values.name: Auto
values.summary: The EVR automatically selects the best deinterlacing method based on the video content and available hardware capabilities. This is generally the recommended setting for optimal quality and performance.

values.name: ForceHalfInterlace
values.summary: Forces the EVR to skip the second field (in temporal order) of every interlaced frame. This results in half-resolution video but can be useful for very low-latency scenarios or when higher-quality deinterlacing is not needed or causes performance issues.

values.name: ForceBob
values.summary: Forces the EVR to use bob deinterlacing. Bob deinterlacing creates a full frame from each field by interpolating missing lines, resulting in smoother motion but potentially visible artifacts.

values.name: AllowDropToHalfInterlace
values.summary: Allows the EVR to drop to half-interlace mode if it is falling behind in rendering. This provides a fallback for performance, sacrificing quality for smoothness.

values.name: AllowDropToBob
values.summary: Allows the EVR to drop to bob deinterlacing if it is falling behind in rendering. This provides a fallback for performance, sacrificing some quality for smoother playback.

enums.name: VideoRendererMode
enums.summary: Specifies the video rendering engine to be used for displaying video frames. The choice of renderer can impact performance, compatibility, and available features.

values.name: VideoRenderer
values.summary: The legacy Video Renderer, primarily available for WinForms applications. This renderer is deprecated and generally not recommended for new development.

values.name: VMR9
values.summary: Video Mixing Renderer 9, available for WinForms applications. Offers improved video mixing capabilities compared to the legacy Video Renderer.

values.name: EVR
values.summary: Enhanced Video Renderer (EVR), available on Windows Vista and later. This is a modern renderer offering better performance and quality, especially with hardware acceleration. Available for WinForms applications.

values.name: None
values.summary: No video renderer is used. This might be chosen when only audio processing or file saving is required, or when a custom rendering solution is implemented.

values.name: WPF_WinUI_Callback
values.summary: A rendering mode suitable for WPF, WinUI, or custom callback-based rendering scenarios. This mode typically involves receiving video frames as callbacks for manual rendering.

values.name: WPF_NativeHWND
values.summary: A rendering mode for WPF applications that uses a native HWND (window handle) for rendering. This can offer better performance and compatibility with certain video sources or effects.

values.name: Direct2D
values.summary: Direct2D renderer, offering high-performance 2D graphics rendering. Available for both WinForms and WPF applications.

values.name: Direct2DManaged
values.summary: A managed Direct2D renderer, specifically designed for WPF applications.

values.name: MadVR
values.summary: madVR renderer, a high-quality video renderer known for its advanced scaling and rendering algorithms. Primarily available for WinForms applications.

values.name: WinUI
values.summary: The WinUI 3 renderer, designed for applications built with the WinUI 3 framework.

values.name: FrameCallback
values.summary: An alias for WPF_WinUI_Callback, indicating a mode where video frames are delivered via callbacks for custom rendering.

values.name: D3D11Composable
values.summary: Direct3D 11 composable WPF renderer. The frame stays on the GPU end-to-end: pushed pixels are uploaded into a shared D3D11 texture which is opened on a hidden Direct3D 9Ex device and exposed to WPF as a D3DImage. Composes with the WPF visual tree (transforms, opacity, z-order, rounded clips) without the airspace limits of an HWND child. Windows-only, requires Vista+ (D3D9Ex) and a Direct3D 10/11-class GPU.

enums.name: VideoRendererStretchMode
enums.summary: Specifies how video frames are scaled or stretched to fit the display area of a video renderer. This enumeration controls the aspect ratio preservation and filling behavior.

values.name: Letterbox
values.summary: Preserves the video's original aspect ratio by adding black bars (letterboxing or pillarboxing) to fill any empty space in the display area.

values.name: Stretch
values.summary: Stretches the video to fill the entire display area, ignoring its original aspect ratio. This may result in a distorted image if the aspect ratios do not match.

values.name: LetterboxToFill
values.summary: Stretches the video to fill the entire display area while preserving its aspect ratio. This is achieved by cropping the video if its aspect ratio does not match the display area. This mode is typically available for WPF renderers.

enums.name: VideoStreamType
enums.summary: Defines the type of a video stream, typically used in frame grabber events or when managing multiple video sources. This enumeration helps distinguish between main video, preview, capture, and Picture-in-Picture (PIP) streams.

values.name: Unknown
values.summary: The video stream type is unknown or not specified.

values.name: Main
values.summary: Represents the primary video stream, typically used for both preview and capture.

values.name: Preview
values.summary: Represents a video stream specifically used for preview purposes.

values.name: Capture
values.summary: Represents a video stream specifically used for video capture or recording.

values.name: Still
values.summary: Represents still frames or snapshots captured from a video stream.

values.name: PIP1
values.summary: Represents the first Picture-In-Picture (PIP) video stream.

values.name: PIP2
values.summary: Represents the second Picture-In-Picture (PIP) video stream.

values.name: PIP3
values.summary: Represents the third Picture-In-Picture (PIP) video stream.

values.name: PIP4
values.summary: Represents the fourth Picture-In-Picture (PIP) video stream.

values.name: PIP5
values.summary: Represents the fifth Picture-In-Picture (PIP) video stream.

values.name: PIP6
values.summary: Represents the sixth Picture-In-Picture (PIP) video stream.

values.name: PIP7
values.summary: Represents the seventh Picture-In-Picture (PIP) video stream.

values.name: PIP8
values.summary: Represents the eighth Picture-In-Picture (PIP) video stream.

values.name: FFMPEGVideo
values.summary: Represents a video stream processed by FFmpeg.

values.name: FFMPEGAudio
values.summary: Represents an audio stream processed by FFmpeg.

values.name: MediaPlayerCache
values.summary: Represents a cached frame from the Media Player SDK.

values.name: StatusOverlay
values.summary: Represents a stream used for displaying status overlays.

enums.name: VideoViewUIEngine
enums.summary: Specifies the UI framework or rendering technology used by a video view component. This enumeration helps the framework adapt its rendering pipeline to different platforms and UI environments.

values.name: WinForms
values.summary: The video view is rendered using Windows Forms technology.

values.name: WPF
values.summary: The video view is rendered using Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF).

values.name: WPF_Native
values.summary: The video view is rendered using WPF with native interop (HWND).

values.name: Avalonia
values.summary: The video view is rendered using Avalonia UI framework.

values.name: Android
values.summary: The video view is rendered on Android using a standard Android View.

values.name: Android_TextureView
values.summary: The video view is rendered on Android using a TextureView, which offers more flexibility for transformations and animations.

values.name: WinUI
values.summary: The video view is rendered using WinUI (Windows UI Library).

values.name: MAUI
values.summary: The video view is rendered using .NET Multi-platform App UI (MAUI).

values.name: Apple_OpenGL
values.summary: The video view is rendered on Apple platforms using OpenGL.

values.name: Apple_Metal
values.summary: The video view is rendered on Apple platforms using Metal, Apple's low-overhead, high-performance 3D graphics API.

values.name: JPEGCallback
values.summary: The video frames are provided as JPEG images via a callback mechanism.

values.name: Android_SurfaceViewManaged
values.summary: The video view is rendered on Android using a managed SurfaceView.

values.name: BufferCallback
values.summary: The video frames are provided as raw buffers via a callback mechanism, allowing for custom rendering with specified format.

values.name: Avalonia_Software
values.summary: The video view is rendered using the Avalonia UI framework with a managed WriteableBitmap (software rendering). The video becomes part of the Avalonia visual tree: it is clipped and overlapped like any other control, unlike the native-window embedding used by Avalonia. Frame delivery goes through the IVideoViewPushFrame PushFrame(VideoFrameX) member with BGRA buffers.

enums.name: AutoReframeTargetSelection
enums.summary: Selects which detected object the auto-reframe block follows when several are present.

values.name: Largest
values.summary: Follow the largest (by bounding-box area) detection that passes the class filter. This is the default and the most stable choice for single-subject footage.

values.name: FirstDetected
values.summary: Follow the first detection (in detector output order) that passes the class filter.

values.name: ClassLabel
values.summary: Follow the highest-confidence detection whose label equals ClassLabelFilter. When no label filter is configured this follows the highest-confidence detection of any class.

enums.name: BackgroundRemovalModel
enums.summary: The segmentation/matting model family the background-removal block runs. Each family expects a distinct input size and pixel normalization, so the block must be told which one the supplied .onnx file belongs to. The model produces a single-channel foreground alpha mask that the block uses to composite the replacement background.

values.name: MODNet
values.summary: MODNet portrait matting (Apache-2.0). Real-time, designed for webcam/portrait use. Input is resized directly (no letterbox) to a square (default 512x512) and normalized to the -1..1 range (mean 0.5 / std 0.5). The model emits a single alpha matte [1, 1, H, W] in 0..1.

values.name: PPMattingV2
values.summary: PP-MattingV2 real-time human matting (PaddleSeg, Apache-2.0). Faster and more accurate than MODNet. Input is resized directly to the model's fixed size and normalized to the -1..1 range (mean 0.5 / std 0.5); the model bakes in the final sigmoid, so the single output [1, 1, H, W] is already a 0..1 alpha matte.

values.name: U2Net
values.summary: U2-Net salient-object / portrait segmentation (Apache-2.0). Input resized directly to 320x320 and normalized with ImageNet mean/std. The first output is a saliency map whose range varies per image, so the block rescales it to 0..1 by its own per-frame min/max.

values.name: BiRefNet
values.summary: BiRefNet high-accuracy dichotomous segmentation (MIT code). Heavier (typically run at 1024x1024 -- set InputWidth/InputHeight accordingly; the block's 512 default is not BiRefNet's native size), better edges, but not real-time on the CPU. Input resized directly and normalized with ImageNet mean/std. The common ONNX export emits a single raw logit map (unbounded), to which the block applies a sigmoid to obtain the 0..1 alpha matte.

values.name: Custom
values.summary: A custom segmentation model. The block uses the configured input size and normalization from the settings as-is and treats the first float output as the alpha mask. Use this for a model that does not match one of the built-in conventions.

enums.name: BackgroundReplacementMode
enums.summary: How the background-removal block replaces the pixels the matting model marks as background (low foreground alpha).

values.name: Blur
values.summary: Replace the background with a blurred copy of the original frame (the "virtual background blur" effect used by video-conferencing apps). The blur strength is controlled by BlurRadius.

values.name: SolidColor
values.summary: Fill the background with a solid color (ReplacementColor) — a virtual green-screen for downstream chroma keying or compositing.

values.name: Image
values.summary: Replace the background with a static image loaded from BackgroundImagePath, scaled to the frame size.

values.name: Transparent
values.summary: Keep the foreground and write the alpha mask into the frame's alpha channel, leaving the background transparent for compositing further down the pipeline. Requires an output that preserves the alpha channel (RGBA renderer or muxer).

enums.name: DetectionAnchor
enums.summary: Defines which point of a detection bounding box is used as its reference anchor for line-crossing and polygon-zone evaluation.

values.name: Center
values.summary: The center of the bounding box (x = Left + Width / 2, y = Top + Height / 2).

values.name: BottomCenter
values.summary: The bottom-center of the bounding box (x = Left + Width / 2, y = Bottom). Useful for tripwire scenarios where feet contact the ground plane.

enums.name: FaceEmbeddingModel
enums.summary: The face-embedding model family used by the face recognizer. The family only selects the input preprocessing of the aligned 112x112 crop (channel order and normalization); the embedding length is always read from the model itself, so any vector size works.

values.name: SFace
values.summary: OpenCV Zoo SFace (Apache-2.0). Aligned BGR crop fed as raw 0..255 values; produces a 128-D embedding. Designed to pair with the YuNet detector and its five landmarks. This is the default.

values.name: ArcFace
values.summary: ArcFace-style recognizer (for example AuraFace, Apache-2.0). Aligned RGB crop normalized with (pixel - 127.5) / 127.5; typically produces a 512-D embedding.

enums.name: LineCrossingDirection
enums.summary: The direction of a directed line crossing.

values.name: In
values.summary: The object crossed from the negative side to the positive side of the directed line.

values.name: Out
values.summary: The object crossed from the positive side to the negative side of the directed line.

enums.name: ObjectDetectorModel
enums.summary: The object-detection model family the detector decodes. Each family has a distinct ONNX output layout and a distinct frame-preprocessing convention (resize mode, pixel normalization, channel order), so the detector must be told which one the supplied .onnx file belongs to.

values.name: YOLOv8
values.summary: Ultralytics YOLOv8 / YOLO11 layout: a single transposed tensor [1, 4 + numClasses, numAnchors] (box values followed by per-class scores, no objectness term). Decoded with class-wise NMS. Frames are letterboxed (centered, gray 114 padding), pixels normalized to 0..1, channel order RGB.

values.name: YOLOX
values.summary: YOLOX (Megvii, Apache-2.0) layout: a single tensor [1, numAnchors, 5 + numClasses] (box values, objectness, per-class scores). Decoded with class-wise NMS. Frames are letterboxed (top-left, gray 114 padding), pixels NOT normalized, channel order BGR.

values.name: RTDETR
values.summary: RT-DETR / D-FINE (Apache-2.0) transformer layout as exported by Hugging Face Transformers / onnx-community: a single image input and two float outputs — class logits[1, numQueries, numClasses] (apply sigmoid) and pred_boxes[1, numQueries, 4] (cx, cy, w, h normalized to 0..1). End-to-end / NMS-free. Frames are resized directly to the model input size, pixels normalized to 0..1, channel order RGB.

enums.name: OnnxExecutionProvider
enums.summary: Execution provider used by the ONNX Runtime inference session.

values.name: CUDA
values.summary: NVIDIA CUDA execution provider (Windows/Linux with a compatible CUDA-capable GPU and runtime).

values.name: DirectML
values.summary: DirectML execution provider (Windows, DirectX 12 capable GPU).

values.name: Auto
values.summary: Automatically selects the fastest hardware provider that is actually present in the loaded ONNX Runtime native build (CUDA, then DirectML, then CoreML), and falls back to CPU when no hardware provider is available. This is the default.

enums.name: OpenVocabularyModel
enums.summary: The open-vocabulary detection model family a supplied ONNX model belongs to. This selects the text tokenizer, the frame-preprocessing convention, and the output decoder used by the open-vocabulary detector engine.

values.name: OWLv2
values.summary: OWLv2 (open-world localization). Uses the CLIP text tokenizer, pads the frame to a square (top-left anchored) and resizes it to 960x960, and decodes per-query sigmoid logits over a fixed 3600-patch grid.

values.name: GroundingDINO
values.summary: Grounding DINO. Uses the BERT WordPiece tokenizer over a "prompt1 . prompt2 ." caption, resizes the frame to the model's fixed input size, and decodes per-query token-span scores over 900 queries.

enums.name: PIICategory
enums.summary: The category of personally identifiable information a redacted region belongs to.

enums.name: PIIRedactionStyle
enums.summary: The visual style used to redact a detected PII region in the video frame.

values.name: GaussianBlur
values.summary: The region is replaced with a Gaussian-blurred copy of itself.

values.name: Pixelate
values.summary: The region is replaced with a coarse mosaic (downscale + nearest-neighbor upscale).

values.name: SolidFill
values.summary: The region is painted over with a solid color.

enums.name: PTZTargetSelection
enums.summary: Strategy used by the PTZ auto-tracking controller to pick which detected object to follow when more than one object is present in a frame.

values.name: Largest
values.summary: Follow the object whose bounding box has the largest area. This is the default.

values.name: FirstDetected
values.summary: Follow the first object in the detection array (as produced by the detector/tracker).

values.name: ByTrackerId
values.summary: Follow only the object whose tracker identifier equals ManualTrackerId.

values.name: ByClassLabel
values.summary: Follow the largest object whose label matches ClassLabelFilter (case-insensitive).

enums.name: SpeakerEmbeddingModel
enums.summary: Selects which speaker-embedding ("voiceprint") model the diarization block is configured for. The value is a declarative hint: the ONNX file actually loaded is EmbeddingModelPath, and the feature front-end auto-configures itself from that file's ONNX metadata. The enum picks the default download URL and documents the recommended clustering threshold for each model; both models are Apache-2.0.

values.name: WeSpeakerEnglish
values.summary: WeSpeaker English voxceleb_resnet34_LM (Apache-2.0). Trained on VoxCeleb (English), 256-dim embedding. The default; best on English speech. Recommended ClusterThreshold ≈ 0.5 (the shipped default).

values.name: ERes2NetV2Multilingual
values.summary: 3D-Speaker ERes2NetV2 sv_zh-cn_16k-common (Apache-2.0). Trained on a large multilingual corpus (Chinese and other languages), 192-dim embedding. Choose this for non-English or mixed-language content — it separates non-English speakers far better than the English-only model. Its voiceprints sit further apart, so it needs a larger threshold: recommended ClusterThreshold ≈ 0.8.

enums.name: SpeechToTextTask
enums.summary: The Whisper task: plain transcription or speech translation to English.

values.name: Transcribe
values.summary: Transcribe the speech in its source language.

values.name: Translate
values.summary: Translate the speech to English text (any supported source language in, English out).

enums.name: VLMTask
enums.summary: The task a Florence-2 vision-language model performs on each processed frame. The task selects the natural-language prompt fed to the model and how its output is interpreted (free text vs. grounded regions).

values.name: Caption
values.summary: Generate a short one-sentence caption describing the image (Florence-2 <CAPTION>).

values.name: DetailedCaption
values.summary: Generate a more detailed caption of the image (Florence-2 <DETAILED_CAPTION>).

values.name: MoreDetailedCaption
values.summary: Generate a paragraph-length, highly detailed caption (Florence-2 <MORE_DETAILED_CAPTION>).

values.name: ObjectDetection
values.summary: Detect objects and report a category label with a bounding box for each (Florence-2 <OD>).

values.name: DenseRegionCaption
values.summary: Detect regions and report a short description with a bounding box for each (Florence-2 <DENSE_REGION_CAPTION>).

values.name: Ocr
values.summary: Read all text in the image as a single string (Florence-2 <OCR>).

values.name: OcrWithRegion
values.summary: Read text in the image and report each text block with a quadrilateral region (Florence-2 <OCR_WITH_REGION>).

values.name: PhraseGrounding
values.summary: Ground the phrases of a caption supplied in TextInput to image regions (Florence-2 <CAPTION_TO_PHRASE_GROUNDING>).

enums.name: WhisperModelSize
enums.summary: The Whisper (GGML) model variant. Larger models are more accurate but slower and use more memory; quantized variants (Q5/Q8) trade a little accuracy for a smaller footprint and faster CPU inference.

values.name: Tiny
values.summary: Tiny model (~75 MB). Fastest, lowest accuracy. Good for real-time CPU transcription.

values.name: Base
values.summary: Base model (~142 MB). A good real-time CPU default.

values.name: Small
values.summary: Small model (~466 MB). Noticeably more accurate; real-time with a GPU or a fast CPU.

values.name: Medium
values.summary: Medium model (~1.5 GB). High accuracy; typically needs a GPU for real-time.

values.name: LargeV3
values.summary: Large v3 model (~3 GB). Highest accuracy; GPU strongly recommended.

values.name: LargeV3Turbo
values.summary: Large v3 Turbo model (~1.6 GB). Near-large accuracy at a fraction of the cost.

values.name: LargeV3TurboQuantized
values.summary: Large v3 Turbo model, Q5_0-quantized (~547 MB). Recommended quantized accuracy/speed balance.

enums.name: ZoneExitReason
enums.summary: The reason a tracked object exited a polygon zone.

values.name: Movement
values.summary: The object moved from inside the zone to outside it in the current frame.

values.name: TrackExpired
values.summary: The object's track expired while it was last observed inside the zone.

enums.name: AmplifyClippingMethod
enums.summary: Audio amplify effect clipping method.

values.name: WrapNegative
values.summary: Push overdriven values back from the opposite side.

values.name: WrapPositive
values.summary: Push overdriven values back from the same side.

enums.name: AudioCompressorMode
enums.summary: Audio compressor mode.

values.name: Compressor
values.summary: Compressor changes the amplitude of all samples above a specific threshold with a specific ratio.

values.name: Expander
values.summary: Expander changes the amplitude of all samples below a specific threshold with a specific ratio.

enums.name: AudioDynamicCharacteristics
enums.summary: Specifies the knee characteristic for dynamic audio processing (compressor/expander). Controls how abruptly the gain change is applied around the threshold.

values.name: HardKnee
values.summary: Hard knee. Gain reduction is applied immediately and fully once the signal crosses the threshold. Produces a more aggressive, noticeable compression/expansion effect.

values.name: SoftKnee
values.summary: Soft knee. Gain reduction is applied gradually as the signal approaches and crosses the threshold. Produces a more transparent, natural-sounding compression/expansion effect.

enums.name: AudioEffectID
enums.summary: Audio effect ID.

values.name: ChebyshevBandPassReject
values.summary: Chebyshev band pass and band reject filter.

values.name: ChebyshevLimit
values.summary: Chebyshev low pass and high pass filter.

values.name: Pitch
values.summary: Pitch shift audio effect using soundtouch.

values.name: RemoveSilence
values.summary: Remove silence from audio streams by automatically detecting and removing silent sections.

values.name: CsoundFilter
values.summary: Csound-based audio filter for advanced audio synthesis and processing.

values.name: RSAudioEcho
values.summary: RS Audio Echo effect from rsaudiofx plugin.

values.name: AudioLoudNorm
values.summary: Audio loudness normalization effect from rsaudiofx plugin.

values.name: AudioRNNoise
values.summary: RNN-based audio noise reduction effect from rsaudiofx plugin.

values.name: EbuR128Level
values.summary: EBU R128 loudness level measurement from rsaudiofx plugin.

values.name: HRTFRender
values.summary: Head-Related Transfer Function spatial audio rendering from rsaudiofx plugin.

values.name: WeightedChannelMix
values.summary: Weighted channel mixing for dual-mono audio (CD+G karaoke). Mixes left and right channels with adjustable weights and outputs to both speakers.

enums.name: AudioPanoramaMethod
enums.summary: Specifies the panning algorithm used for stereo balance/panorama adjustment.

values.name: Psychoacoustic
values.summary: Psychoacoustic panning using equal-power (constant-power) law. Maintains perceived loudness when panning between channels. Recommended for most use cases.

values.name: Simple
values.summary: Simple linear panning. Directly scales channel volumes proportionally. May cause a perceived volume dip when panning to center.

enums.name: AudioResamplerFilterInterpolation
enums.summary: Specifies how the sinc filter table is interpolated during audio resampling. Controls the tradeoff between filter accuracy and memory usage.

values.name: None
values.summary: No interpolation. Uses the nearest filter table entry. Fastest but lowest quality.

values.name: Linear
values.summary: Linear interpolation between filter table entries. Good balance of speed and quality.

values.name: Cubic
values.summary: Cubic interpolation between filter table entries. Best quality with slightly higher CPU cost.

enums.name: AudioResamplerFilterMode
enums.summary: Specifies how the sinc filter table is stored for audio resampling. Controls the tradeoff between memory usage and CPU cost.

values.name: Interpolated
values.summary: Use an interpolated filter table. Lower memory usage but requires interpolation at runtime.

values.name: Full
values.summary: Use a full precomputed filter table. Higher memory usage but avoids runtime interpolation.

values.name: Auto
values.summary: Automatically choose between interpolated and full modes based on the memory usage threshold.

enums.name: AudioResamplerMethod
enums.summary: Specifies the resampling algorithm used for sample rate conversion. Higher-quality methods produce better audio but require more CPU.

values.name: Nearest
values.summary: Nearest-neighbor resampling. Fastest but lowest quality, may produce audible artifacts.

values.name: Linear
values.summary: Linear interpolation. Low CPU cost with basic smoothing between samples.

values.name: Cubic
values.summary: Cubic interpolation. Moderate quality with smooth curve fitting between samples.

values.name: BlackmanNuttall
values.summary: Blackman-Nuttall windowed sinc filter. High quality with excellent stopband rejection.

values.name: Kaiser
values.summary: Kaiser windowed sinc filter. Highest quality with near-optimal stopband attenuation. Default method.

enums.name: ChebyshevBandPassRejectAudioEffectMode

enums.summary: NDI video codec hint sent to the connected sender. Controls whether the sender is asked to use hardware or software encoding.

values.name: Hardware
values.summary: Hint the sender to use hardware encoding (HX2/HX3 via H.264/HEVC). Requires hardware decoder support on the receiving device. If the device shows "Video decoder not found", switch to Software.

values.name: Software
values.summary: Hint the sender to use software encoding (full-bandwidth NDI / SpeedHQ). Higher bandwidth but no hardware decoder required on the receiver. Use when the device cannot decode H.264/HEVC HX streams.

values.name: None

enums.name: RTSPBufferMode
enums.summary: RTSP buffer mode for jitter buffer control. Controls how the jitter buffer in rtspsrc handles incoming RTP packets.

values.name: None
values.summary: No buffering. Packets are passed through immediately without reordering. This provides the lowest latency but may result in out-of-order packets. Best for ultra-low latency applications where some packet loss is acceptable.

values.name: Auto
values.summary: Automatic buffer mode selection based on stream characteristics. GStreamer will automatically choose the best buffering strategy. Recommended for most applications.

values.name: Slave
values.summary: Slave mode. The jitter buffer will adjust its buffering based on a master clock. Used for synchronized playback across multiple streams.

values.name: Buffer
values.summary: Buffer mode. Provides packet reordering and buffering for smooth playback. Adds some latency but provides the most stable playback.

values.name: Synced
values.summary: Synced mode. Synchronizes the jitter buffer with RTP timestamps. Balances latency and stability for synchronized multi-stream scenarios.

enums.name: RTSPNTPTimeSource
enums.summary: NTP time source for RTSP timestamp synchronization. Determines which clock source to use for NTP timestamp calculations.

values.name: NTP
values.summary: Use NTP time from RTCP packets. The most accurate method when the RTSP server provides NTP information.

values.name: RunningTime
values.summary: Use the system clock. Uses the local machine's clock for timestamp calculations.

values.name: Clock
values.summary: Use the global pipeline clock. Synchronizes with other elements in the GStreamer pipeline. Recommended for multi-stream synchronized playback.

values.name: AV1

enums.name: LUTInterpolationMode
enums.summary: Specifies the method used for interpolating values between defined points in a 3D space. Each method offers different trade-offs between computational complexity, accuracy, and smoothness.

values.name: Nearest
values.summary: Uses values from the nearest defined point without any actual interpolation. Fastest method but produces discontinuous results at boundaries between regions. Best used when computational speed is critical and discontinuities are acceptable.

values.name: Trilinear
values.summary: Interpolates values using all 8 vertices of the surrounding cube. Performs three linear interpolations along each axis, hence "trilinear". Produces continuous results but may show artifacts at sharp transitions. Computational complexity: O(8) - requires 7 linear interpolations.

values.name: Tetrahedral
values.summary: Interpolates using 4 points forming a tetrahedron within the cube. Divides the cube into 5-6 tetrahedra and selects the appropriate one. Provides better handling of diagonal gradients compared to trilinear. Computational complexity: O(4) - requires 3 linear interpolations.

values.name: Pyramid
values.summary: Interpolates using 5 points forming a pyramid within the cube. Combines aspects of tetrahedral and trilinear methods. Good balance between accuracy and computational cost. Computational complexity: O(5) - requires 4 linear interpolations.

values.name: Prism
values.summary: Interpolates using 6 points forming a triangular prism within the cube. Useful for datasets with strong directional bias. Better preservation of sharp features along one primary axis. Computational complexity: O(6) - requires 5 linear interpolations.

enums.name: PNGEncoderCompressionLevel
enums.summary: PNG encoder compression levels for the rspngenc GStreamer element. Compression levels range from 0 (no compression) to 9 (maximum compression).

values.name: None
values.summary: No compression - fastest encoding, largest file size.

values.name: Minimal
values.summary: Minimal compression - very fast encoding, large file size.

values.name: Low
values.summary: Low compression - fast encoding, moderately large file size.

values.name: Light
values.summary: Light compression - good encoding speed, moderate file size.

values.name: MediumLow
values.summary: Medium-low compression - balanced encoding speed and file size.

values.name: Medium
values.summary: Medium compression - balanced encoding speed and file size.

values.name: MediumHigh
values.summary: Medium-high compression - slower encoding, smaller file size (default).

values.name: High
values.summary: High compression - slow encoding, small file size.

values.name: VeryHigh
values.summary: Very high compression - very slow encoding, very small file size.

values.name: Maximum
values.summary: Maximum compression - slowest encoding, smallest file size.

enums.name: PNGEncoderFilterType
enums.summary: PNG encoder filter types for the rspngenc GStreamer element. Filter types are used to preprocess the image data before compression to improve compression efficiency for different types of image content.

values.name: None
values.summary: No filtering - fastest processing, good for simple images (default).

values.name: Sub
values.summary: Sub filter - transmits the difference between each byte and the value of the corresponding byte of the prior pixel.

values.name: Up
values.summary: Up filter - transmits the difference between each byte and the value of the corresponding byte in the previous scanline.

values.name: Average
values.summary: Average filter - uses the average of the two neighboring pixels (left and above) to predict the value of a pixel.

values.name: Paeth
values.summary: Paeth filter - computes a simple linear function of the three neighboring pixels (left, above, upper left), then chooses as predictor the neighboring pixel closest to the computed value.

values.name: High422
values.summary: High 422 profile - professional broadcast and production quality.

values.name: High444

enums.name: HEVCAMFHeaderInsertionMode
enums.summary: Header insertion mode for HEVC AMF encoder. Controls when and how VPS (Video Parameter Set), SPS (Sequence Parameter Set), and PPS (Picture Parameter Set) headers are inserted into the HEVC bitstream. These headers contain critical information needed to decode the video stream.

values.name: None
values.summary: No automatic header insertion. Headers are only included at the beginning of the stream. This mode results in the smallest file size but requires the decoder to retain the initial headers throughout playback.

values.name: GOP
values.summary: Insert headers at every GOP (Group of Pictures) boundary. Headers are repeated at the start of each GOP, making the stream more resilient to seeking and streaming errors. Recommended for streaming applications where random access is important.

values.name: IDR
values.summary: Insert headers before every IDR (Instantaneous Decoder Refresh) frame. IDR frames in HEVC are complete pictures that don't reference any other frames. This provides the most robust stream but with slightly larger file size. Best for broadcast, live streaming, or when maximum error resilience is needed.

enums.name: HEVCAMFLevel
enums.summary: Represents the profile level settings for the AMF HEVC encoder. HEVC levels define constraints on bitrate, frame size, and decoding complexity. Higher levels support larger resolutions, higher frame rates, and increased bitrates. The level should be chosen based on target device capabilities and content requirements.

values.name: Auto
values.summary: Auto Level - Let the encoder choose the appropriate level based on encoding parameters. The encoder will select the minimum level that satisfies the resolution, frame rate, and bitrate requirements of the encoded content.

values.name: Level_1_0
values.summary: Level 1.0 - Basic mobile/low-power devices. Max resolution: 352x288 (CIF), Max bitrate: 128 Kbps. Suitable for basic mobile streaming and low-bandwidth applications.

values.name: Level_2_0
values.summary: Level 2.0 - Standard mobile devices. Max resolution: 352x480, Max bitrate: 1.5 Mbps. Common for mobile video playback and video conferencing.

values.name: Level_2_1
values.summary: Level 2.1 - Enhanced mobile devices. Max resolution: 640x480, Max bitrate: 3 Mbps. Supports higher quality mobile content and SD video.

values.name: Level_3_0
values.summary: Level 3.0 - SD content. Max resolution: 720x576, Max bitrate: 6 Mbps. Standard for DVD-quality content and SD broadcasting.

values.name: Level_3_1
values.summary: Level 3.1 - HD ready content. Max resolution: 1280x720, Max bitrate: 10 Mbps. Suitable for 720p HD content at standard frame rates.

values.name: Level_4_0
values.summary: Level 4.0 - Full HD content. Max resolution: 1920x1080, Max bitrate: 12 Mbps. Standard for 1080p content at 30 fps.

values.name: Level_4_1
values.summary: Level 4.1 - Full HD high frame rate. Max resolution: 1920x1080, Max bitrate: 20 Mbps. Supports 1080p at 60 fps or higher quality 1080p30. Common for Blu-ray and high-quality streaming.

values.name: Level_5_0
values.summary: Level 5.0 - 4K UHD content. Max resolution: 4096x2160, Max bitrate: 25 Mbps. Supports 4K at 30 fps for streaming applications.

values.name: Level_5_1
values.summary: Level 5.1 - 4K UHD high frame rate. Max resolution: 4096x2160, Max bitrate: 40 Mbps. Supports 4K at 60 fps for premium content.

values.name: Level_5_2
values.summary: Level 5.2 - 4K UHD high bitrate. Max resolution: 4096x2160, Max bitrate: 60 Mbps. For high-quality 4K content with HDR and high frame rates.

values.name: Level_6_0
values.summary: Level 6.0 - 8K UHD content. Max resolution: 8192x4320, Max bitrate: 60 Mbps. Supports 8K at 30 fps for next-generation displays.

values.name: Level_6_1
values.summary: Level 6.1 - 8K UHD high frame rate. Max resolution: 8192x4320, Max bitrate: 120 Mbps. Supports 8K at 60 fps for premium 8K content.

values.name: Level_6_2
values.summary: Level 6.2 - 8K UHD maximum quality. Max resolution: 8192x4320, Max bitrate: 240 Mbps. Maximum quality 8K content with high frame rates and HDR. Requires high-end hardware for playback.

enums.name: HEVCAMFProfile
enums.summary: Represents the profile settings for the AMF HEVC encoder. HEVC profiles define the subset of coding tools and syntax elements that can be used. Note: The comment incorrectly mentioned H264 - these are HEVC/H.265 profiles. However, the enum values appear to be H.264 profiles, which suggests this might need correction. For HEVC, the typical profiles are Main, Main 10, Main Still Picture, etc.

values.name: Main
values.summary: Main Profile - The primary HEVC profile for 8-bit video. Supports 4:2:0 chroma sampling with 8 bits per sample. Most widely supported profile for general use cases. Suitable for SDR (Standard Dynamic Range) content.

values.name: High
values.summary: Main 10 Profile - For 10-bit video content. Supports up to 10 bits per sample for better color depth. Required for HDR (High Dynamic Range) content. Provides smoother gradients and reduced banding artifacts. Note: Value 1 might map to Main 10 in HEVC context.

values.name: ConstrainedBaseline
values.summary: Note: This appears to be an H.264 profile value. HEVC doesn't have a Constrained Baseline profile. This might be a placeholder or require mapping to an appropriate HEVC profile.

values.name: ConstrainedHigh
values.summary: Note: This appears to be an H.264 profile value. HEVC doesn't have a Constrained High profile. This might be a placeholder or require mapping to an appropriate HEVC profile.

enums.name: HEVCAMFQuality
enums.summary: Represents the quality preference settings for the HEVC AMF encoder. This setting controls the trade-off between encoding speed and output quality. AMD AMF uses this to adjust internal encoding decisions and optimizations. Lower values prioritize quality, higher values prioritize speed.

values.name: Speed
values.summary: Prefer Speed (value: 10) - Fastest encoding with acceptable quality. Optimizes for real-time encoding scenarios like game streaming or video conferencing. Uses simplified motion estimation and faster encoding decisions. May result in larger file sizes and slightly reduced visual quality. Best for: Live streaming, screen recording, real-time applications.

values.name: Balanced
values.summary: Balanced (value: 5) - Good compromise between speed and quality. Provides reasonable encoding speed while maintaining good visual quality. Uses moderate complexity algorithms for motion estimation and mode decisions. Suitable for most general-purpose encoding scenarios. Best for: General video encoding, online video platforms, standard content creation.

values.name: Quality
values.summary: Prefer Quality (value: 0) - Maximum quality at the expense of encoding speed. Enables all quality optimizations including advanced motion estimation, sophisticated rate-distortion optimization, and comprehensive mode decisions. Results in best possible quality and compression efficiency. Encoding time can be significantly longer than other modes. Best for: Archival, professional video production, offline encoding.

enums.name: HEVCAMFRateControlMethod
enums.summary: Represents the rate control method settings for the HEVC AMF encoder. Rate control determines how the encoder allocates bits across frames to achieve the desired bitrate or quality level. Different methods suit different use cases. AMD AMF hardware acceleration provides efficient implementation of these modes.

values.name: CQP
values.summary: Constant Quantization Parameter (CQP) - Fixed quality mode. Uses a constant quantization parameter for all frames. Results in consistent quality but variable bitrate. File size is unpredictable as bitrate varies with content complexity. Lower QP values (0-20) = higher quality, larger files. Higher QP values (30-51) = lower quality, smaller files. Best for: Archival, editing, when consistent quality is more important than file size.

values.name: CBR
values.summary: Constant Bitrate (CBR) - Maintains a fixed target bitrate. Encoder adjusts quality dynamically to maintain the specified bitrate. Results in predictable file sizes and bandwidth usage. Quality may vary significantly between simple and complex scenes. Includes a small buffer to handle short-term variations. Best for: Live streaming, broadcast, bandwidth-limited scenarios.

values.name: VBRPeak
values.summary: Peak Constrained Variable Bitrate (VBR) - Variable bitrate with maximum limit. Allows bitrate to vary based on content complexity up to a peak value. Provides better quality than CBR for complex scenes while respecting bandwidth limits. Average bitrate is typically lower than the peak, saving bandwidth/storage. Maintains a buffer to smooth out bitrate variations. Best for: Streaming services, VOD platforms, general video distribution.

values.name: VBRLatency
values.summary: Latency Constrained Variable Bitrate (VBR) - Low-latency variable bitrate. Optimized for minimal encoding delay while allowing bitrate variation. Uses smaller buffers than standard VBR to reduce latency. Provides better quality than CBR with faster response than peak-constrained VBR. May have less optimal rate distribution compared to VBRPeak. Best for: Real-time communication, game streaming, interactive applications.

enums.name: QSVH264LookAheadDownsampling
enums.summary: Enum for Intel QSV Look Ahead Downsampling options, determining the downscaling factor for frames. Controls how frames are downscaled during look-ahead analysis to reduce memory usage and improve performance. Look-ahead analysis examines future frames to optimize encoding decisions.

values.name: Unknown
values.summary: Unknown downscaling factor. Let the Intel driver choose the appropriate downsampling based on resolution and performance.

values.name: Off
values.summary: No downscaling. Full resolution analysis provides best quality but requires more memory and processing. Recommended for content where quality is paramount and system resources are abundant.

values.name: TwoTimes
values.summary: Downscale by 2x. Analyzes frames at half resolution (1/4 pixels), balancing quality and performance. Good compromise for 1080p and higher resolution content. Reduces memory usage by approximately 75%.

values.name: FourTimes
values.summary: Downscale by 4x. Analyzes frames at quarter resolution (1/16 pixels) for maximum performance. Suitable for 4K content or when encoding speed is prioritized over quality. Reduces memory usage by approximately 94%.

enums.name: QSVH264Profile
enums.summary: Enum for H.264/AVC profile options for Intel Quick Sync Video encoding. Profiles define the set of encoding tools and syntax elements available to the encoder. Higher profiles generally offer better compression but require more capable decoders.

values.name: Unknown
values.summary: Unknown profile. Allows the Intel QSV driver to automatically select the most appropriate profile.

values.name: Baseline
values.summary: Baseline profile (BP). Simplest H.264 profile with lowest computational requirements. Supports only I and P slices (no B-frames), no interlacing, no CABAC. Ideal for low-power devices, video conferencing, and mobile streaming. Maximum level: 5.2, supports up to 4K resolution.

values.name: Main
values.summary: Main profile (MP). Adds support for interlaced video, B-frames, and CABAC entropy coding. Widely supported profile offering good compression efficiency. Commonly used for standard definition broadcast and DVD content. Intel QSV provides excellent performance/quality balance with this profile.

values.name: High
values.summary: High profile (HiP). Most advanced H.264 profile with best compression efficiency. Adds 8x8 transform, custom quantization matrices, and separate Cb/Cr control. Recommended for HD content, Blu-ray, and high-quality streaming. Intel QSV fully supports High profile with hardware acceleration.

enums.name: QSVHEVCProfile
enums.summary: Enum for HEVC/H.265 profile options for Intel Quick Sync Video encoding. Profiles define the set of coding tools and bit depth support for HEVC encoding. Intel QSV HEVC support requires 6th generation Core processors (Skylake) or newer.

values.name: Unknown
values.summary: Unknown profile. Allows the Intel QSV driver to automatically select the most appropriate profile.

values.name: Main
values.summary: Main profile. Standard HEVC profile supporting 8-bit video with 4:2:0 chroma subsampling. Most widely supported HEVC profile with excellent compression efficiency. Suitable for most consumer video content and streaming applications. Intel QSV provides full hardware acceleration for Main profile.

values.name: Main10
values.summary: Main 10 profile. Extends Main profile with support for 10-bit video depth. Provides better color accuracy and reduces banding artifacts. Commonly used for HDR content and professional video production. Requires Intel 7th generation Core processors (Kaby Lake) or newer for QSV support.

values.name: MainSP
values.summary: Main Still Picture profile. Optimized for encoding still images or intra-only video sequences. Uses only intra prediction (no inter-frame compression). Useful for applications requiring frame-accurate editing or image sequences. Lower compression efficiency but faster random access to any frame.

values.name: REXT
values.summary: Range Extensions profile (RExt). Advanced HEVC profile supporting extended color formats and bit depths. Includes support for 4:2:2 and 4:4:4 chroma formats, up to 16-bit depth. Used for professional video production and high-end content creation. Intel QSV support for RExt profiles varies by GPU generation.

enums.name: QSVPreset
enums.summary: Enum for Intel Quick Sync Video preset options, representing quality/speed trade-offs. Presets control the complexity of encoding algorithms and analysis performed. Lower values (slower) provide better quality at the cost of encoding speed.

values.name: VerySlow
values.summary: Very slow preset (1). Maximum quality with extensive motion estimation and analysis. Uses most advanced Intel QSV features including look-ahead and RDO. Best for final production encodes where quality is paramount. Encoding speed: ~0.3-0.5x realtime on typical Intel integrated graphics.

values.name: Slower
values.summary: Slower preset (2). High quality with comprehensive motion search and advanced features. Balances quality improvements with reasonable encoding time. Suitable for high-quality archival and distribution. Encoding speed: ~0.5-1x realtime on typical Intel integrated graphics.

values.name: Slow
values.summary: Slow preset (3). Good quality with enhanced motion estimation and rate control. Enables most quality-improving features while maintaining decent speed. Good choice for high-quality streaming content. Encoding speed: ~1-2x realtime on typical Intel integrated graphics.

values.name: Medium
values.summary: Medium preset (4). Balanced quality and speed, default setting for most use cases. Uses standard Intel QSV motion estimation and rate control algorithms. Recommended starting point for most applications. Encoding speed: ~2-4x realtime on typical Intel integrated graphics.

values.name: Fast
values.summary: Fast preset (5). Prioritizes encoding speed with acceptable quality loss. Reduces motion search range and simplifies mode decisions. Suitable for real-time streaming and live encoding scenarios. Encoding speed: ~4-8x realtime on typical Intel integrated graphics.

values.name: Faster
values.summary: Faster preset (6). High-speed encoding with further quality trade-offs. Minimal motion estimation and simplified rate control. Good for preview generation or low-latency applications. Encoding speed: ~8-15x realtime on typical Intel integrated graphics.

values.name: VeryFast
values.summary: Very fast preset (7). Maximum encoding speed with basic quality. Uses fastest available Intel QSV algorithms and minimal analysis. Best for real-time applications where latency is critical. Encoding speed: ~15-30x realtime on typical Intel integrated graphics.

values.name: Film

enums.summary: FFMPEG EXE video encoder.

values.name: Auto
values.summary: Video encoder will be detected using output format.

values.name: CAVS
values.summary: Chinese AVS (Audio Video Standard) (AVS1-P2, JiZhun profile) (encoders: libxavs ).

values.name: FLV1
values.summary: FLV / Sorenson Spark / Sorenson H.263 (Flash Video).

values.name: H264
values.summary: H.264 / AVC / MPEG-4 AVC / MPEG-4 part 10. H264 MF will be used. Standard: ITU-T H.264, ISO/IEC 14496-10. Profiles: Baseline, Main, High, High 10, High 4:2:2, High 4:4:4. Max resolution: 4096×2304 (Level 5.2), 8192×4320 (Level 6.2). Bit depth: 8-bit, 10-bit (High 10 profile). Use case: Universal video codec, streaming, broadcast, Blu-ray.

values.name: H264_MF
values.summary: H.264 Media Foundation encoder. Platform: Windows 7+ (requires Media Foundation). Hardware acceleration: Uses GPU if available. Performance: Good balance of speed and quality. Limitations: Limited configuration options compared to x264.

values.name: H264_X264
values.summary: H.264 / AVC / MPEG-4 AVC / MPEG-4 part 10. x264 will be used. FFMPEG.exe provided with SDK do not contains x264 encoder, please use FFMPEG build with x264. Encoder: x264 (open-source, best-in-class H.264 encoder). Quality: Excellent, industry standard for H.264 encoding. Features: Full H.264 spec support, extensive tuning options. Performance: CPU-based, slower than hardware encoders. License: GPL (requires custom FFMPEG build).

values.name: H264_QSV
values.summary: H.264 / AVC / MPEG-4 AVC / MPEG-4 part 10. Intel QuickSync will be used. Hardware: Intel CPU with Intel HD Graphics (2nd gen Core i3/i5/i7+). Platform: Windows, Linux (requires Intel Media SDK). Performance: Very fast, hardware-accelerated. Quality: Good, slightly lower than x264 at same bitrate. Power: Low power consumption, ideal for laptops.

values.name: H264_NVENC
values.summary: H.264 NVENC encoder. Hardware: NVIDIA GPU (GTX 600 series or newer, Quadro, Tesla). Performance: Extremely fast, dedicated hardware encoding. Quality: Good, optimized for streaming and real-time encoding. Features: B-frames, look-ahead, temporal AQ, spatial AQ. Limitations: Concurrent session limits on consumer GPUs.

values.name: H264_AMF
values.summary: H264 AMF (ATI/AMD) encoder. Hardware: AMD GPU (RX 400 series or newer, Radeon Pro). Technology: AMD Advanced Media Framework (AMF). Performance: Fast hardware encoding, low CPU usage. Quality: Good for real-time applications. Platform: Windows, Linux (limited support).

values.name: H264_OpenH264
values.summary: H.264 / AVC via OpenH264 (Cisco). Encoder: libopenh264 (BSD-licensed, royalty-free). Quality: Moderate, suitable for real-time communication. Features: Constrained Baseline, Main, High profiles; CAVLC/CABAC. Performance: CPU-based, lighter than x264. Use case: Default software H.264 encoder when x264 is not available.

values.name: HEVC
values.summary: H.265 / HEVC (High Efficiency Video Coding). HEVC Media Foundation will be used. Standard: ITU-T H.265, ISO/IEC 23008-2. Efficiency: 25-50% better compression than H.264. Profiles: Main, Main 10, Main Still Picture. Max resolution: 8192×4320 (8K UHD). Use case: 4K/8K video, HDR content, next-gen streaming. Note: Requires Windows 10+ with HEVC Video Extensions.

values.name: HEVC_X265
values.summary: H.265 / HEVC. x265 will be used. FFMPEG.exe provided with SDK do not contains x265 encoder, please use FFMPEG build with x265. Encoder: x265 (open-source HEVC encoder). Quality: Excellent, best software HEVC encoder. Features: HDR10, HLG, Dolby Vision support. Performance: CPU-intensive, slower than H.264. License: GPL (requires custom FFMPEG build).

values.name: HEVC_QSV
values.summary: H.265 / HEVC (High Efficiency Video Coding). Intel QuickSync will be used. Hardware: Intel 6th gen (Skylake) or newer with HD Graphics. Performance: Fast hardware encoding with low power usage. Features: 10-bit support (7th gen+), HDR. Quality: Good for real-time encoding. Platform: Windows, Linux (Intel Media SDK required).

values.name: HEVC_NVENC
values.summary: HEVC NVENC encoder. Hardware: NVIDIA GPU (GTX 960/GTX 750 SE or newer). Performance: Very fast hardware encoding. Features: 10-bit encoding, HDR10, B-frames. Quality: Good for real-time applications. Limitations: Session limits on consumer GPUs.

values.name: HEVC_AMF
values.summary: HEVC AMF (ATI/AMD) encoder. Hardware: AMD GPU (RX 400 series or newer). Performance: Hardware-accelerated HEVC encoding. Features: 10-bit support on newer GPUs. Use case: Real-time encoding, streaming. Platform: Windows, limited Linux support.

values.name: MJPEG
values.summary: Motion JPEG. Compression: Intra-frame only (each frame is a JPEG image). Quality: High quality, but large file sizes. Performance: Fast encoding/decoding, low complexity. Use case: Video editing, digital cameras, webcams. Features: Frame-accurate editing, no temporal compression.

values.name: MPEG1Video
values.summary: MPEG-1 video. Standard: ISO/IEC 11172-2. Resolution: Up to 4095×4095, typically 352×240/288. Bitrate: Up to 1.856 Mbps (VCD). Use case: Video CD (VCD), legacy compatibility. Note: Obsolete for modern use, poor compression efficiency.

values.name: MPEG2Video
values.summary: MPEG-2 video. Standard: ISO/IEC 13818-2, ITU-T H.262. Profiles: Simple, Main, High (4:2:2, 4:2:0). Resolution: Up to 1920×1152 (HDTV), 720×480/576 (DVD). Use case: DVD, broadcast TV, early HDTV. Features: Interlaced video support, closed captions.

values.name: MPEG4
values.summary: MPEG-4 part 2. Standard: ISO/IEC 14496-2. Profiles: Simple, Advanced Simple (ASP). Features: B-frames, quarter-pixel motion, GMC. Use case: DivX/Xvid video, early mobile video. Note: Superseded by H.264/AVC (MPEG-4 Part 10).

values.name: ProRes
values.summary: Apple ProRes (iCodec Pro). Variants: ProRes 422 (Proxy, LT, Standard, HQ), ProRes 4444. Quality: Visually lossless, 10-bit/12-bit support. Use case: Professional video editing, broadcast mastering. Platform: Primarily macOS, limited Windows support. Note: Large file sizes, optimized for editing performance.

values.name: Theora
values.summary: Theora. Developer: Xiph.Org Foundation. License: BSD-style, royalty-free. Based on: VP3 codec. Quality: Comparable to early H.264 implementations. Use case: Open-source video, Ogg container. Status: Largely obsolete, replaced by VP8/VP9.

values.name: VP8
values.summary: On2 VP8. Developer: Google (acquired from On2). License: BSD, royalty-free. Quality: Similar to H.264 Baseline profile. Use case: WebM format, web video, WebRTC. Container: WebM, Matroska.

values.name: VP9
values.summary: Google VP9. Developer: Google. License: BSD, royalty-free. Efficiency: 20-50% better than VP8, competitive with HEVC. Features: 4K/8K support, HDR, wide color gamut. Use case: YouTube, web video, royalty-free alternative to HEVC. Performance: Slower encoding than H.264/VP8.

enums.name: VideoMode
enums.summary: FFMPEG EXE video mode.

values.name: CBR
values.summary: Constant bitrate (CBR). Maintains a fixed bitrate throughout the entire video. Pros: Predictable file size, good for streaming. Cons: Quality varies with scene complexity, inefficient for simple scenes. Use case: Live streaming, broadcast requirements.

values.name: ABR
values.summary: Average bitrate (ABR). Targets an average bitrate over the entire video. Pros: Better quality distribution than CBR, predictable file size. Cons: May exceed target bitrate in complex scenes. Use case: General purpose encoding, VOD streaming.

values.name: Quality
values.summary: Quality-based encoding (VBR). Maintains consistent quality by varying bitrate. Pros: Optimal quality-to-size ratio, efficient encoding. Cons: Unpredictable file size, not suitable for streaming. Use case: Archival, local playback, high-quality masters. Note: Uses CRF (Constant Rate Factor) for x264/x265 or similar quality metrics for other codecs.

values.name: Lossless
values.summary: Lossless encoding. Preserves all original video data without compression artifacts. Pros: Perfect quality, suitable for editing and archival. Cons: Very large file sizes, high bitrate requirements. Use case: Professional editing, archival masters, intermediate files. Note: Not all codecs support lossless mode.

enums.name: NVENCErrorCode
enums.summary: NVENC error codes.

values.name: Success
values.summary: This indicates that API call returned with no errors.

values.name: NoEncodeDevice
values.summary: This indicates that no encode capable devices were detected.

values.name: UnsupportedDevice
values.summary: This indicates that devices pass by the client is not supported.

values.name: InvalidEncoderDevice
values.summary: This indicates that the encoder device supplied by the client is not valid.

values.name: InvalidDevice
values.summary: This indicates that device passed to the API call is invalid.

values.name: DeviceNotExist
values.summary: This indicates that device passed to the API call is no longer available and needs to be reinitialized. The clients need to destroy the current encoder session by freeing the allocated input output buffers and destroying the device and create a new encoding session.

values.name: InvalidPointer
values.summary: This indicates that one or more of the pointers passed to the API call is invalid.

values.name: InvalidEvent
values.summary: This indicates that completion event passed in ::NvEncEncodePicture() call is invalid.

values.name: InvalidParameter
values.summary: This indicates that one or more of the parameter passed to the API call is invalid.

values.name: InvalidCall
values.summary: This indicates that an API call was made in wrong sequence/order.

values.name: OutOfMemory
values.summary: This indicates that the API call failed because it was unable to allocate enough memory to perform the requested operation.

values.name: EncoderNotInitialized
values.summary: This indicates that the encoder has not been initialized with ::NvEncInitializeEncoder() or that initialization has failed. The client cannot allocate input or output buffers or do any encoding related operation before successfully initializing the encoder.

values.name: UnsupportedParameter
values.summary: This indicates that an unsupported parameter was passed by the client.

values.name: LockBusy
values.summary: This indicates that the ::NvEncLockBitstream() failed to lock the output buffer.

values.name: NotEnoughBuffer
values.summary: This indicates that the size of the user buffer passed by the client is insufficient for the requested operation.

values.name: InvalidVersion
values.summary: This indicates that an invalid struct version was used by the client.

values.name: MapFailed
values.summary: This indicates that ::NvEncMapInputResource() API failed to map the client provided input resource.

values.name: NeedMoreInput
values.summary: This indicates encode driver requires more input buffers to produce an output bitstream.

values.name: EncoderBusy
values.summary: This indicates that the HW encoder is busy encoding and is unable to encode the input. The client should call ::NvEncEncodePicture() again after few milliseconds.

values.name: EventNotRegistered
values.summary: This indicates that the completion event passed in ::NvEncEncodePicture() API has not been registered with encoder driver using ::NvEncRegisterAsyncEvent().

values.name: GenericError
values.summary: This indicates that an unknown internal error has occurred.

values.name: IncompatibleClientKey
values.summary: This indicates that the client is attempting to use a feature that is not available for the license type for the current system.

values.name: Unimplemeted
values.summary: This indicates that the client is attempting to use a feature that is not implemented for the current version.

values.name: ResourceRegisterFailder
values.summary: This indicates that the ::NvEncRegisterResource API failed to register the resource.

values.name: ResourceNotRegistered
values.summary: This indicates that the client is attempting to unregister a resource that has not been successfully registered.

values.name: ResourceNotMapped
values.summary: This indicates that the client is attempting to unmap a resource that has not been successfully mapped.

values.name: Pan
values.summary: Specifies the camera's pan setting, in degrees. Values range from –180 to +180, with the default set to zero. Positive values are clockwise from the origin (the camera rotates clockwise when viewed from above), and negative values are counterclockwise from the origin.

values.name: Tilt

values.name: Roll
values.summary: Specifies the camera's roll setting, in degrees. Values range from –180 to +180, with the default set to zero. Positive values cause a clockwise rotation of the camera along the image-viewing axis, and negative values cause a counterclockwise rotation of the camera.

values.name: Zoom

values.name: Exposure
values.summary: Specifies the exposure setting, in log base 2 seconds. In other words, for values less than zero, the exposure time is 1/2n seconds, and for values zero or above, the exposure time is 2n seconds. For example: Value: Seconds: -3 1/8 -2 1/4 -1 1/2 0 1 1 2 2 4

values.name: Iris
values.summary: Specifies the camera's iris setting, in units of f(stop) * 10.

values.name: Focus
values.summary: Specifies the camera's focus setting, as the distance to the optimally focused target, in millimeters. The range and default value are specific to the device.

values.name: ScanMode
values.summary: The ScanMode property specifies the scanning mode of the camera sensor. The property value specifies whether interlace mode should be enabled. A value of 0 indicates that the interlace mode is enabled, and a value of 1 indicates that the progressive (or non-interlace) mode is enabled.

values.name: Privacy
values.summary: The Privacy property specifies whether to prevent video from being acquired by the camera sensor. The property value specifies whether privacy mode is enable or disabled. A value of 0 indicates that the camera sensor can capture video images, and a value of 1 indicates that the camera sensor is prevented from capturing video images.

values.name: PanTilt
values.summary: The PanTilt property specifies absolute pan and tilt settings. The property value is a pair of integers that specify a camera's absolute pan and tilt settings. These values are expressed in arc-second units. One arc second is 1/3600 of a degree. Acceptable values range from −180*3600 to +180*3600 arc seconds. If a pan or tilt value is not provided, the default is 0. When making a pan request, specify a positive value to rotate the camera to the right and specify a negative value to rotate the camera to the left. When making a tilt request, a positive value tilts the camera up and a negative value tilts the camera down.

values.name: PanRelative
values.summary: The PanRelative property specifies a camera's rotation around the vertical axis. The property value specifies a camera's relative pan setting. The size of the value represents the desired pan speed; a higher value represents a higher speed.

values.name: TiltRelative
values.summary: The TileRelative property specifies a camera's vertical tilting status. The property value specifies a camera's relative tilt setting. The size of the value represents the desired tilt speed; a higher value represents a higher speed.

values.name: RollRelative
values.summary: The RollRelative property specifies camera rotation around the image viewing axis. The property value specifies a camera's relative roll setting. The size of the value represents the desired rotation speed; a higher value represents a higher speed.

values.name: ZoomRelative
values.summary: The ZoomRelative property specifies the zoom status of the camera. The property value specifies a camera's relative zoom setting. The size of the value represents the desired zoom speed; a higher value represents a higher speed.

values.name: ExposureRelative
values.summary: The ExposureRelative property specifies the electronic shutter speed. The property value specifies a camera's relative exposure setting. Step size is hardware-dependent. To determine the step size, you can make a get request on the Exposure property.

values.name: IrisRelative
values.summary: The IrisRelative property specifies a camera's aperture setting. The property value specifies a camera's relative iris setting. Both the iris step size and the iris step default value are implementation-specific.

values.name: FocusRelative
values.summary: The FocusRelative property specifies the focus setting of the camera. The property value specifies a camera's relative focus setting. The size of the value represents the speed at which the focal point changes; a higher value represents a higher speed.

values.name: PanTiltRelative
values.summary: The PanTiltRelative property specifies horizontal or vertical rotation of the camera and can specify both simultaneously.

values.name: FocalLength
values.summary: The FocalLength property retrieves focal length information for a camera.] The property value specifies a camera's focal length.

values.name: AutoExposurePriority
values.summary: The AutoExposurePriority (Low light compensation checkbox in a dialog) property specifies whether the device can dynamically vary the frame rate. The property value specifies whether frame rate can be dynamically varied by the device. 0 - frame rate must remain constant. 1 - frame rate can be dynamically varied by the device.

enums.name: VideoInterpolationMode
enums.summary: Specifies the interpolation algorithm used when resizing or scaling video frames.

values.name: NearestNeighbor
values.summary: Uses the nearest pixel value for interpolation, resulting in a blocky appearance but fast processing.

values.name: Bilinear
values.summary: Uses a weighted average of the four nearest pixels, providing smoother results than nearest-neighbor but can still appear blurry.

values.name: Bicubic
values.summary: Uses a weighted average of 16 nearest pixels, offering higher quality and smoother transitions than bilinear, but is computationally more intensive.

values.name: Lancroz
values.summary: A more advanced interpolation method that provides sharp, high-quality results, often used for downscaling images.

values.name: Hue

values.name: Saturation

enums.name: VideoResizeMode
enums.summary: Specifies the algorithm used for resizing video frames.

values.name: CropOnly
values.summary: Resizes the video by cropping, maintaining the original aspect ratio but potentially cutting off parts of the frame.

values.name: NearestNeighbor
values.summary: Resizes using the nearest neighbor algorithm, which is fast but can result in a blocky or pixelated appearance.

values.name: Bilinear
values.summary: Resizes using bilinear interpolation, providing smoother results than nearest neighbor but may still appear soft.

values.name: Bicubic
values.summary: Resizes using bicubic interpolation, offering higher quality and sharper results than bilinear, but is more computationally intensive.

values.name: Lancroz
values.summary: Resizes using the Lanczos algorithm, known for producing high-quality results with good sharpness and minimal artifacts, especially for downscaling.

enums.name: SUBTITLE_INFO
enums.summary: Represents subtitle information for a media stream, typically used in DVD/Blu-ray subtitle tracks. This structure is designed for interop with native media frameworks and contains essential metadata about subtitle tracks including language and naming information.

values.name: Offset
values.summary: Gets or sets the byte offset of the subtitle data within the media stream. This value indicates where the subtitle data begins relative to the start of the stream.

values.name: IsoLang
values.summary: Gets or sets the ISO 639-2 language code as a 4-byte array. This follows the standard 3-letter language code format (e.g., "eng" for English, "fra" for French) with an additional null terminator byte. The language code helps media players display appropriate subtitle options to users.

values.name: TrackName
values.summary: Gets or sets the human-readable name of the subtitle track as a 512-byte array. This can include descriptive information such as "English (SDH)", "Director's Commentary", or "Forced Subtitles". The array is null-terminated and typically encoded in UTF-8.
