enums.name: MFAudioEncoderSettings
enums.summary: Contains audio encoder configuration settings for Media Foundation Transform encoding.

values.name: Encoder
values.summary: Gets or sets the audio encoder type to use for encoding.

values.name: Bitrate
values.summary: Gets or sets the audio bitrate in kilobits per second (kbps). Higher values produce better quality at the cost of larger file sizes.

values.name: AmplifyLevel
values.summary: Gets or sets the audio amplification level multiplier. A value of 1.0 means no amplification, values greater than 1.0 increase volume, and values less than 1.0 decrease volume.

enums.name: MFVideoEncoderSettings
enums.summary: Contains comprehensive video encoder configuration settings for Media Foundation Transform encoding. Includes settings for bitrate control, quality, H.264 profile and level, quantization parameters, and advanced codec options.

values.name: Encoder
values.summary: Gets or sets the video encoder type to use for encoding.

values.name: AvgBitrate
values.summary: Specifies the average encoded bit rate, in bits per second. This property applies only to constant bit rate (CBR) and variable bit rate (VBR) encoding modes.

values.name: MaxBitrate
values.summary: Specifies the maximum bit rate, in bits per second. This property applies only to constant bit rate (CBR) and variable bit rate (VBR) encoding modes.

values.name: Quality
values.summary: Specifies the quality level for encoding. This property controls the quality level when the encoder is not using a constrained bit rate. Default is 65, valid range is 0-100.

values.name: CABAC
values.summary: Enables or disables CABAC (context-adaptive binary arithmetic coding) for H.264 entropy coding. CABAC provides better compression efficiency than CAVLC but requires more processing power.

values.name: H264Profile
values.summary: Gets or sets the H.264 encoding profile (Baseline, Main, High, etc.).

values.name: H264Level
values.summary: Gets or sets the H.264 encoding level which defines resolution, bitrate, and frame rate constraints.

values.name: RateControlMode
values.summary: Gets or sets the rate control mode (CBR, VBR, quality-based, etc.).

values.name: InterlaceMode
values.summary: Gets or sets the video interlace mode (progressive, interlaced, etc.).

values.name: CustomAspectRatioX
values.summary: Gets or sets the custom aspect ratio X component. Set to 0 to use the source aspect ratio.

values.name: CustomAspectRatioY
values.summary: Gets or sets the custom aspect ratio Y component. Set to 0 to use the source aspect ratio.

values.name: AdaptiveMode
values.summary: Gets or sets the adaptive encoding mode for dynamically adjusting encoding parameters.

values.name: LowLatencyMode
values.summary: Low-latency mode is useful for real-time communications or live capture, when latency should be minimized. However, low-latency mode might also reduce the decoding or encoding quality. The encoder is expected to not add any sample delay due to frame reordering in encoding process, and one input sample shall produce one output sample. B slices/frames can be present as long as they do not introduce any frame re-ordering in the encoder.

values.name: MaxKeyFrameSpacing
values.summary: Gets or sets the maximum spacing between key frames (IDR frames) in frames. Also known as the GOP (Group of Pictures) size.

values.name: QualityVsSpeed
values.summary: Specifies the tradeoff between encoding quality and speed. This property is valid in all rate control modes. Default is 33, valid range is 0-100. Lower values favor speed, higher values favor quality.

values.name: MPVGOPSize
values.summary: Specifies the maximum number of pictures from one group-of-pictures (GOP) header to the next GOP header. Default is 50. This setting is specific to MPEG video encoding.

values.name: QPUsed
values.summary: Indicates whether quantization parameter (QP) values are being used for encoding control. When true, the QP field values are applied.

values.name: QP
values.summary: Specifies the quantization parameter (QP) for video encoding. Contains QP values for I, P, and B frames.

values.name: MinQP
values.summary: Specifies the minimum quantization parameter (QP) for video encoding in variable-QP mode. Default is 0, valid range is 0-51.

values.name: MaxQP

deploymentGuides.title: Android MAUI Deployment Guide
deploymentGuides.summary: Deploy VisioForge SDK to Android devices using .NET MAUI framework.
deploymentGuides.content:
# Android MAUI Deployment Guide

## Overview

VisioForge SDK supports Android 5.0 (API 21) and later for mobile video applications.

## Prerequisites

- **Visual Studio 2022** with MAUI workload
- **Android SDK API 34** or later
- **Android device or emulator** (API 21+)

## NuGet Packages

> **Pick the wrapper package for the SDK you licensed.** The snippets below show
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks`, but this guide applies to all four: use
> `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture` for camera, screen and IP-camera recording,
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer` for playback, `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit` for
> timeline editing. Media Blocks is the low-level pipeline layer. The native
> redist packages are the same whichever you choose.

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks" Version="2026.11.6" />
</ItemGroup>

<ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-android'))">
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Android" Version="2026.11.5" />
  <ProjectReference Include="..\AndroidDependency\VisioForge.Core.Android.X10.csproj" />
</ItemGroup>
```

**Important**: Android requires Java bindings via `AndroidDependency` project reference.

## Project Configuration

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TargetFramework>net10.0-android</TargetFramework>
  <SupportedOSPlatformVersion>21</SupportedOSPlatformVersion>
  <ApplicationId>com.yourcompany.appname</ApplicationId>
</PropertyGroup>
```

## Permissions

Add to `AndroidManifest.xml`:

```xml
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.CAMERA" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />
```

### Runtime Permissions (API 23+)

```csharp
using Microsoft.Maui.ApplicationModel;

if (OperatingSystem.IsAndroidVersionAtLeast(23))
{
    await Permissions.RequestAsync<Permissions.Camera>();
    await Permissions.RequestAsync<Permissions.Microphone>();
    await Permissions.RequestAsync<Permissions.StorageWrite>();
}
```

## Deployment

### Build APK

```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0-android
```

### Build AAB (Google Play)

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-android -p:AndroidPackageFormat=aab
```

## Code Example

```csharp
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sources;

public async Task StartCameraAsync()
{
    var pipeline = new MediaBlocksPipeline();
    var camera = new VideoCaptureDeviceSourceBlock(0);
    var renderer = new VideoRendererBlock(pipeline, videoView);

    pipeline.Connect(camera.VideoOutput, renderer.Input);
    await pipeline.StartAsync();
}
```

## Troubleshooting

- **Camera not found**: Check permissions and device capabilities
- **Build failed**: Ensure AndroidDependency project is included
- **App crashes on launch**: Check API level compatibility (min API 21)

## Next Steps

- [MAUI mobile cross-platform](../project-types/maui-mobile.md)
- [iOS deployment](ios-maui.md)

deploymentGuides.content:
# iOS MAUI Deployment Guide

## Overview

VisioForge SDK supports iOS 13.0 and later for iPhone and iPad video applications.

## Prerequisites

- **macOS** with Xcode 14 or later
- **Visual Studio 2022 for Mac** or **VS Code** with MAUI extension
- **.NET 10.0 SDK** or later
- **Apple Developer account** (for device deployment)

## NuGet Packages

> **Pick the wrapper package for the SDK you licensed.** The snippets below show
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks`, but this guide applies to all four: use
> `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture` for camera, screen and IP-camera recording,
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer` for playback, `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit` for
> timeline editing. Media Blocks is the low-level pipeline layer. The native
> redist packages are the same whichever you choose.

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks" Version="2026.11.6" />
</ItemGroup>

<ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-ios'))">
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.iOS" Version="2026.11.5" />
</ItemGroup>
```

## Project Configuration

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TargetFramework>net10.0-ios</TargetFramework>
  <SupportedOSPlatformVersion>13.0</SupportedOSPlatformVersion>
  <CodesignKey>iPhone Developer</CodesignKey>
</PropertyGroup>
```

## Permissions

Add to `Info.plist`:

```xml
<key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app requires camera access for video recording</string>

<key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app requires microphone access for audio recording</string>

<key>NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app requires photo library access to save videos</string>

<key>NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app needs to save captured videos to your photo library</string>
```

## Deployment

### Build for iOS Simulator

```bash
dotnet build -c Debug -f net10.0-ios /p:_DeviceName=:v2:udid=<simulator-uuid>
```

### Build for Physical Device

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-ios /p:ArchiveOnBuild=true /p:CodesignKey="iPhone Developer" /p:CodesignProvision="YourProvisioningProfile"
```

### Deploy to TestFlight

1. Build IPA with Release configuration
2. Upload to App Store Connect
3. Submit for TestFlight review

## Code Example

```csharp
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sources;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sinks;

public async Task StartRecordingAsync()
{
    var pipeline = new MediaBlocksPipeline();

    // Front camera
    var camera = new VideoCaptureDeviceSourceBlock(1);

    // Save to MP4
    var sink = new MP4SinkBlock(Path.Combine(
        Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.MyDocuments),
        "recording.mp4"));

    pipeline.Connect(camera.VideoOutput, sink.VideoInput);
    pipeline.Connect(camera.AudioOutput, sink.AudioInput);

    await pipeline.StartAsync();
}
```

## Troubleshooting

- **Code signing failed**: Verify provisioning profile and certificate
- **Camera not available**: Check Info.plist permissions
- **App rejected**: Ensure all privacy descriptions are clear and specific
- **Crash on device**: Check minimum iOS version (13.0+)

## Distribution Checklist

- [ ] Valid provisioning profile
- [ ] Code signing certificate installed
- [ ] Info.plist permissions descriptions
- [ ] App icons (all sizes)
- [ ] Launch screen
- [ ] Test on physical device
- [ ] TestFlight beta testing
- [ ] App Store review guidelines compliance

## Next Steps

- [MAUI mobile cross-platform](../project-types/maui-mobile.md)
- [Android deployment](android-maui.md)
- [Mac Catalyst](maccatalyst-maui.md)

deploymentGuides.content:
# iOS Native Deployment

## Overview

VisioForge SDK supports iOS native development without MAUI, using Xamarin.iOS or pure iOS projects.

## Prerequisites

- **macOS** with Xcode 14 or later
- **Visual Studio 2022 for Mac** or **VS Code**
- **.NET 10.0 SDK** or later
- **Apple Developer account** (for device deployment)
- **CocoaPods** (if using native dependencies)

## NuGet Packages

> **Pick the wrapper package for the SDK you licensed.** The snippets below show
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks`, but this guide applies to all four: use
> `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture` for camera, screen and IP-camera recording,
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer` for playback, `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit` for
> timeline editing. Media Blocks is the low-level pipeline layer. The native
> redist packages are the same whichever you choose.

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks" Version="2026.11.6" />
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.iOS" Version="2026.11.5" />
</ItemGroup>
```

## Project Configuration (Xamarin.iOS)

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TargetFramework>net10.0-ios</TargetFramework>
  <SupportedOSPlatformVersion>13.0</SupportedOSPlatformVersion>
  <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
  <CodesignKey>iPhone Developer</CodesignKey>
</PropertyGroup>
```

## Info.plist Permissions

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>CFBundleDisplayName</key>
    <string>MyVideoApp</string>

    <key>CFBundleIdentifier</key>
    <string>com.company.myvideoapp</string>

    <key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key>
    <string>This app requires camera access for video recording</string>

    <key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
    <string>This app requires microphone access for audio recording</string>

    <key>NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription</key>
    <string>This app requires photo library access to save videos</string>

    <key>NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription</key>
    <string>This app needs to save captured videos to your photo library</string>

    <key>MinimumOSVersion</key>
    <string>13.0</string>
</dict>
</plist>
```

## Code Example (UIKit)

```csharp
using UIKit;
using Foundation;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sources;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sinks;

[Register("ViewController")]
public class ViewController : UIViewController
{
    private MediaBlocksPipeline? _pipeline;
    private UIView? _videoView;

    public override void ViewDidLoad()
    {
        base.ViewDidLoad();

        // Create video view
        _videoView = new UIView(View.Bounds);
        View.AddSubview(_videoView);

        // Request camera permission
        AVFoundation.AVCaptureDevice.RequestAccessForMediaType(
            AVFoundation.AVAuthorizationMediaType.Video,
            (granted) => {
                if (granted)
                {
                    InvokeOnMainThread(InitializeCamera);
                }
            });
    }

    private async void InitializeCamera()
    {
        _pipeline = new MediaBlocksPipeline();

        // Use front camera (index 1) or back camera (index 0)
        var camera = new VideoCaptureDeviceSourceBlock(1);
        var renderer = new VideoRendererBlock(_pipeline, _videoView);

        _pipeline.Connect(camera.VideoOutput, renderer.Input);
        await _pipeline.StartAsync();
    }

    public override void ViewWillDisappear(bool animated)
    {
        base.ViewWillDisappear(animated);
        _pipeline?.StopAsync().Wait();
        _pipeline?.Dispose();
    }
}
```

## Deployment

### Build for iOS Simulator

```bash
dotnet build -c Debug -f net10.0-ios
```

### Build for Physical Device

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-ios \
  /p:ArchiveOnBuild=true \
  /p:CodesignKey="iPhone Developer" \
  /p:CodesignProvision="YourProvisioningProfile"
```

### Deploy via Xcode

1. Open `.csproj` in Visual Studio for Mac
2. Select physical device
3. Click Run
4. App will be code signed and deployed

## Code Signing

### Development Certificate

1. Open Xcode → Preferences → Accounts
2. Add Apple ID
3. Manage Certificates → + → iOS Development
4. Download provisioning profile

### Distribution Certificate

For App Store or TestFlight:

1. Create Distribution Certificate in Apple Developer Portal
2. Create App Store provisioning profile
3. Build with Release configuration

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-ios \
  /p:CodesignKey="iPhone Distribution" \
  /p:CodesignProvision="YourAppStoreProfile"
```

## Troubleshooting

- **Code signing failed**: Verify certificate and provisioning profile installed
- **Camera not working**: Check Info.plist has NSCameraUsageDescription
- **App crashes on launch**: Verify minimum iOS version (13.0+)
- **Linker errors**: Add `--linkskip=VisioForge` to Additional mtouch arguments

## TestFlight Distribution

1. Archive build with Release configuration
2. Upload IPA to App Store Connect
3. Submit to TestFlight
4. Add internal/external testers
5. Distribute

## Next Steps

- [MAUI iOS deployment](ios-maui.md)
- [Mac Catalyst](maccatalyst-maui.md)
- [SwiftUI integration](https://docs.microsoft.com/xamarin/ios)

# Linux/Ubuntu Deployment Guide

## Overview

VisioForge SDK supports Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 11+) for both headless server applications and desktop apps with Avalonia UI.

## Prerequisites

- **Ubuntu 20.04** or later (or Debian 11+)
- **.NET 10.0 SDK**: `wget https://dot.net/v1/dotnet-install.sh && bash dotnet-install.sh --channel 10.0`
- **GStreamer**: `sudo apt-get install gstreamer1.0-tools gstreamer1.0-plugins-base gstreamer1.0-plugins-good gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad gstreamer1.0-plugins-ugly gstreamer1.0-libav`

## NuGet Packages

> **Pick the wrapper package for the SDK you licensed.** The snippets below show
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks`, but this guide applies to all four: use
> `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture` for camera, screen and IP-camera recording,
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer` for playback, `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit` for
> timeline editing. Media Blocks is the low-level pipeline layer. The native
> redist packages are the same whichever you choose.

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks" Version="2026.11.6" />
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Linux.x64" Version="2026.10.26" />
</ItemGroup>
```

## Project Configuration

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
  <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
  <RuntimeIdentifier>linux-x64</RuntimeIdentifier>
</PropertyGroup>
```

## Deployment

### Self-Contained Deployment

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -r linux-x64 --self-contained true
```

Copy `bin/Release/net10.0/linux-x64/publish/` to target server.

### Make Executable

```bash
chmod +x MyApp
./MyApp
```

## Code Example

```csharp
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sources;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sinks;

// Headless video transcoding
var pipeline = new MediaBlocksPipeline();
var source = new UniversalSourceBlock("input.mp4");
var sink = new MP4SinkBlock("output.mp4");

pipeline.Connect(source.VideoOutput, sink.VideoInput);
pipeline.Connect(source.AudioOutput, sink.AudioInput);

await pipeline.StartAsync();
await pipeline.WaitForCompletionAsync();
```

## Troubleshooting

- **libgstreamer missing**: Install GStreamer packages
- **Permission denied**: Use `chmod +x` on executable
- **Display not found**: For headless servers, set `DISPLAY=:0` or run without GUI

## Next Steps

- [Docker deployment](linux-docker.md)
- [Avalonia UI for Linux desktop](../project-types/avalonia-cross.md)

# Mac Catalyst MAUI Deployment Guide

## Overview

Mac Catalyst allows iOS apps to run natively on macOS. VisioForge SDK supports Mac Catalyst for bringing your iOS video apps to the Mac.

## Prerequisites

- **macOS 11.0** or later
- **Xcode 14** or later
- **.NET 10.0 SDK** or later
- **MAUI workload**: `dotnet workload install maui`

## NuGet Packages

> **Pick the wrapper package for the SDK you licensed.** The snippets below show
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks`, but this guide applies to all four: use
> `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture` for camera, screen and IP-camera recording,
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer` for playback, `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit` for
> timeline editing. Media Blocks is the low-level pipeline layer. The native
> redist packages are the same whichever you choose.

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks" Version="2026.11.6" />
</ItemGroup>

<ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-maccatalyst'))">
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.macCatalyst" Version="2026.11.5" />
</ItemGroup>
```

## Project Configuration

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TargetFrameworks>net10.0-maccatalyst</TargetFrameworks>
  <SupportedOSPlatformVersion Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-maccatalyst'))">14.0</SupportedOSPlatformVersion>
</PropertyGroup>
```

## Critical: Native Library Copying

**Mac Catalyst requires manual copying of .dylib and .so files to MonoBundle directory.**

Add this MSBuild target to your .csproj:

```xml
<Target Name="CopyNativeLibrariesToMonoBundle" AfterTargets="Build" Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-maccatalyst'))">
  <Message Text="Copying native libraries for Mac Catalyst..." Importance="High" />
  <PropertyGroup>
    <AppBundleDir>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).app</AppBundleDir>
    <MonoBundleDir>$(AppBundleDir)/Contents/MonoBundle</MonoBundleDir>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <MakeDir Directories="$(MonoBundleDir)" Condition="!Exists('$(MonoBundleDir)')" />
  <Copy SourceFiles="@(None->'%(FullPath)')" DestinationFolder="$(MonoBundleDir)"
        Condition="'%(Extension)' == '.dylib' Or '%(Extension)' == '.so'">
    <Output TaskParameter="CopiedFiles" ItemName="CopiedNativeFiles" />
  </Copy>
  <Message Text="Native libraries copied successfully" Importance="High" />
</Target>
```

## Permissions

Add to Info.plist (same as iOS):

```xml
<key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app requires camera access for video recording</string>

<key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app requires microphone access for audio recording</string>
```

## Deployment

```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0-maccatalyst
```

## Troubleshooting

- **Native libs not found**: Verify `CopyNativeLibrariesToMonoBundle` target executed
- **Code signing**: Mac Catalyst requires proper signing for distribution
- **Entitlements**: Add camera/microphone entitlements

## Next Steps

- [iOS deployment](ios-maui.md)
- [macOS native](macos-desktop.md)

# macOS Desktop Deployment Guide

## Overview

VisioForge SDK supports macOS 11+ (Big Sur and later) for both Apple Silicon (ARM64) and Intel (x64) Macs.

## Prerequisites

- **macOS 11.0** or later
- **.NET 10.0 SDK** or later
- **Xcode Command Line Tools**: `xcode-select --install`

## NuGet Packages

> **Pick the wrapper package for the SDK you licensed.** The snippets below show
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks`, but this guide applies to all four: use
> `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture` for camera, screen and IP-camera recording,
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer` for playback, `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit` for
> timeline editing. Media Blocks is the low-level pipeline layer. The native
> redist packages are the same whichever you choose.

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks" Version="2026.11.6" />
</ItemGroup>

<ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-macos'))">
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.macOS" Version="2026.11.5" />
</ItemGroup>
```

## Project Configuration

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TargetFramework>net10.0-macos</TargetFramework>
  <RuntimeIdentifiers>osx-arm64;osx-x64</RuntimeIdentifiers>
  <SupportedOSPlatformVersion>11.0</SupportedOSPlatformVersion>
</PropertyGroup>
```

## Deployment

### Build for macOS

```bash
# Apple Silicon
dotnet publish -c Release -r osx-arm64

# Intel
dotnet publish -c Release -r osx-x64
```

### Create App Bundle

For proper macOS app:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <CFBundleName>MyVideoApp</CFBundleName>
  <CFBundleDisplayName>My Video App</CFBundleDisplayName>
  <CFBundleIdentifier>com.company.myvideoapp</CFBundleIdentifier>
  <CFBundleVersion>1.0</CFBundleVersion>
</PropertyGroup>
```

## Permissions

Add to `Info.plist`:

```xml
<key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app requires camera access for video recording</string>

<key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app requires microphone access for audio recording</string>
```

## Code Example

```csharp
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sources;

var pipeline = new MediaBlocksPipeline();
var source = new VideoCaptureDeviceSourceBlock(0); // Camera index
var sink = new MP4SinkBlock("recording.mp4");

pipeline.Connect(source.VideoOutput, sink.VideoInput);
await pipeline.StartAsync();
```

## Troubleshooting

- **Framework not found**: Install .NET SDK for macOS
- **Camera permission denied**: Check System Preferences → Security & Privacy
- **Code signing required**: For distribution, sign with Apple Developer certificate

- [Mac Catalyst deployment](maccatalyst-maui.md)

deploymentGuides.title: Windows Desktop Application Deployment (WPF/WinForms)
deploymentGuides.summary: Complete guide for deploying VisioForge SDK in Windows desktop applications using WPF, WinForms, or Console with .NET Core/.NET Framework.
deploymentGuides.content:
# Windows Desktop Application Deployment

## Overview

Deploying VisioForge SDK to Windows desktop applications (WPF, WinForms, or Console) is straightforward using NuGet packages. This guide covers both .NET (.NET 6-10) and .NET Framework (4.7.2+) deployment.

## Prerequisites

- **Visual Studio 2022** or later (or JetBrains Rider)
- **.NET 10.0 SDK** or later (for .NET apps)
- **.NET Framework 4.7.2+** Developer Pack (for .NET Framework apps)
- **Windows 10/11** (x64 architecture)

## Quick Start

### Step 1: Create Your Project

```bash
# WPF (.NET)
dotnet new wpf -n MyVideoApp

# WinForms (.NET)
dotnet new winforms -n MyVideoApp

# Console (.NET)
dotnet new console -n MyVideoApp
```

### Step 2: Add NuGet Packages

Add the required VisioForge packages to your `.csproj` file:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <!-- Core SDK (choose one based on your needs) -->
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks" Version="2026.11.6" />

  <!-- Windows platform binaries -->
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />

  <!-- FFmpeg/Libav codecs (compressed version) -->
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Libav.Windows.x64.UPX" Version="2026.11.3" />
</ItemGroup>
```

### Step 3: Configure Project Settings

Ensure your project targets x64 architecture:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <OutputType>WinExe</OutputType> <!-- or Exe for console -->
  <TargetFramework>net10.0-windows</TargetFramework>
  <PlatformTarget>x64</PlatformTarget>
  <UseWPF>true</UseWPF> <!-- For WPF apps -->
  <!-- <UseWindowsForms>true</UseWindowsForms> --> <!-- For WinForms apps -->
</PropertyGroup>
```

### Step 4: Build and Run

```bash
dotnet build
dotnet run
```

## NuGet Package Details

> **Pick the wrapper package for the SDK you licensed.** The snippets below show
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks`, but this guide applies to all four: use
> `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture` for camera, screen and IP-camera recording,
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer` for playback, `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit` for
> timeline editing. Media Blocks is the low-level pipeline layer. The native
> redist packages are the same whichever you choose.

### Core SDK Packages

Choose the SDK package based on your use case:

| Package | Version | Use Case |
|---------|---------|----------|
| `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks` | 2026.11.6 | Modern pipeline-based processing |
| `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture` | 2026.11.6 | Video capture and encoding |
| `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer` | 2026.11.6 | Media playback |
| `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit` | 2026.11.6 | Video editing and conversion |

### Required Platform Packages

```xml
<!-- Required for Windows x64 -->
<PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />

<!-- FFmpeg/Libav codecs (compressed) -->
<PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Libav.Windows.x64.UPX" Version="2026.11.3" />
```

### Optional Packages

```xml
<!-- Optional Packages -->
<ItemGroup>
  <!-- Computer Vision (OpenCV) -->
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.OpenCV.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />

  <!-- AWS S3 Integration -->
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.AWS.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />

  <!-- Industrial Camera Support -->
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Basler.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Spinnaker.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />
  <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.AlliedVision.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />
</ItemGroup>
```

## Deployment Methods

### Method 1: Framework-Dependent Deployment (Recommended)

Requires .NET Runtime installed on target machine. Smaller deployment size.

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained false
```

**Output**: `bin\Release\net10.0-windows\win-x64\publish\`

**Deployment**: Copy entire publish folder to target machine. User needs .NET 10 Runtime.

### Method 2: Self-Contained Deployment

Includes .NET runtime. Larger but doesn't require .NET installation.

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true
```

**Output**: Includes all DLLs and runtime (~120-150 MB)

### Method 3: Single-File Executable

Bundles everything into one .exe file:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <PublishSingleFile>true</PublishSingleFile>
  <SelfContained>true</SelfContained>
  <RuntimeIdentifier>win-x64</RuntimeIdentifier>
</PropertyGroup>
```

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release
```

**Note**: VisioForge native DLLs are extracted to temp directory at runtime.

## Platform-Specific Configuration

### Windows-Specific Features

- **DirectShow Backend**: Available on Windows only for legacy capture devices
- **Hardware Encoding**: Support for NVIDIA NVENC, Intel QuickSync, AMD VCE
- **DeckLink**: Blackmagic DeckLink capture card support

### Architecture Requirements

- **x64 Required**: VisioForge SDK requires 64-bit Windows
- **x86 Support**: Limited codec support, not recommended for production

### Application Manifest

For Windows 10/11 compatibility, add this manifest:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <ApplicationManifest>app.manifest</ApplicationManifest>
</PropertyGroup>
```

`app.manifest`:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<assembly manifestVersion="1.0" xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:asm.v1">
  <compatibility xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:compatibility.v1">
    <application>
      <!-- Windows 10/11 -->
      <supportedOS Id="{8e0f7a12-bfb3-4fe8-b9a5-48fd50a15a9a}"/>
    </application>
  </compatibility>
  <trustInfo xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:asm.v2">
    <security>
      <requestedPrivileges>
        <requestedExecutionLevel level="asInvoker" uiAccess="false"/>
      </requestedPrivileges>
    </security>
  </trustInfo>
</assembly>
```

## Code Example

### Media Blocks SDK - Simple Video Player

```csharp
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sources;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.VideoRendering;
using VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoCapture;

public partial class MainWindow : Window
{
    private MediaBlocksPipeline? _pipeline;

    private async void PlayButton_Click(object sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        // Create pipeline
        _pipeline = new MediaBlocksPipeline();

        // Create source (file, RTSP, HTTP, etc.)
        var source = new UniversalSourceBlock("video.mp4");

        // Create video renderer
        var renderer = new VideoRendererBlock(_pipeline, videoView);

        // Connect blocks
        _pipeline.Connect(source.VideoOutput, renderer.Input);

        // Start playback
        await _pipeline.StartAsync();
    }

    private async void StopButton_Click(object sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (_pipeline != null)
        {
            await _pipeline.StopAsync();
            await _pipeline.DisposeAsync();
            _pipeline = null;
        }
    }
}
```

## Troubleshooting

### Issue: Missing DLLs

**Symptom**: Application crashes with "DLL not found" error

**Solution**:
- Ensure all NuGet packages are restored: `dotnet restore`
- Check platform target is x64: `<PlatformTarget>x64</PlatformTarget>`
- Rebuild in Release configuration

### Issue: GStreamer Initialization Failed

**Symptom**: `GStreamer initialization failed` exception

**Solution**:
- Verify `VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Windows.x64` package is installed
- Check Windows Event Viewer for detailed error messages
- Ensure x64 architecture (not AnyCPU or x86)

### Issue: Codec Not Available

**Symptom**: "Codec H.264 not available" error

**Solution**:
- Install `VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Libav.Windows.x64.UPX` package
- For additional codecs, install full `Libav.Windows.x64` (non-UPX) package

### Issue: Antivirus False Positive

**Symptom**: Antivirus blocks VisioForge DLLs

**Solution**:
- Add exclusion for your application folder
- Consider code signing your application for distribution
- Use digital signatures from trusted certificate authority

## Performance Optimization

### Hardware Acceleration

Enable hardware encoding/decoding when available:

```csharp
var encoderSettings = new H264EncoderSettings
{
    HardwareAcceleration = true // NVIDIA/Intel/AMD GPU
};
```

### Memory Management

Dispose pipelines properly to free resources:

```csharp
await using (var pipeline = new MediaBlocksPipeline())
{
    // Use pipeline
} // Automatically disposed
```

## Distribution Checklist

- [ ] Build in Release configuration
- [ ] Test on clean machine without Visual Studio
- [ ] Verify x64 architecture
- [ ] Include Visual C++ Redistributable if needed
- [ ] Test with Windows Defender enabled
- [ ] Consider code signing for production deployment
- [ ] Include license file and SDK documentation

## Next Steps

deploymentGuides.title: Avalonia UI Cross-Platform Deployment
deploymentGuides.summary: Deploy VisioForge SDK with Avalonia UI for true cross-platform desktop and mobile applications.
deploymentGuides.content:
# Avalonia UI Cross-Platform Deployment

## Overview

Avalonia UI enables cross-platform apps with a single codebase. VisioForge SDK integrates seamlessly with Avalonia for Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and iOS.

## Project Approaches

Avalonia supports **two project patterns**:

1. **Single Multi-Target Project** - One project targeting multiple platforms (recommended)
2. **Separate Platform Projects** - Individual projects per platform (Xamarin style)

This guide covers the **multi-target approach**.

## Prerequisites

- **.NET 10.0 SDK** or later
- **Avalonia templates**: `dotnet new install Avalonia.Templates`

## NuGet Packages (Multi-Target Project)

> **Pick the wrapper package for the SDK you licensed.** The snippets below show
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks`, but this guide applies to all four: use
> `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture` for camera, screen and IP-camera recording,
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer` for playback, `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit` for
> timeline editing. Media Blocks is the low-level pipeline layer. The native
> redist packages are the same whichever you choose.

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <AvaloniaUseCompiledBindingsByDefault>true</AvaloniaUseCompiledBindingsByDefault>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- Conditional TargetFrameworks based on build OS -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('Windows'))">
    <TargetFrameworks>net10.0-windows;net10.0-android;net10.0-ios</TargetFrameworks>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <PropertyGroup Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('OSX'))">
    <TargetFrameworks>net10.0-ios;net10.0-android;net10.0-macos</TargetFrameworks>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <PropertyGroup Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('Linux'))">
    <TargetFrameworks>net10.0;net10.0-android</TargetFrameworks>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Avalonia" Version="12.0.5" />
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks" Version="2026.11.6" />
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.Core.UI.Avalonia" Version="2026.11.6" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Windows-specific -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-windows'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Libav.Windows.x64.UPX" Version="2026.11.3" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- macOS-specific -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-macos'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.macOS" Version="2026.11.5" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Android-specific -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-android'))">
    <PackageReference Include="Avalonia.Android" Version="12.0.5" />
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Android" Version="2026.11.5" />
    <ProjectReference Include="..\AndroidDependency\VisioForge.Core.Android.X10.csproj" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- iOS-specific -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-ios'))">
    <PackageReference Include="Avalonia.iOS" Version="12.0.5" />
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.iOS" Version="2026.11.5" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

## Desktop-Only Project Configuration

For desktop-only apps (simpler):

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <OutputType>WinExe</OutputType>
  <TargetFramework Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('Windows'))">net10.0-windows</TargetFramework>
  <TargetFramework Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('OSX'))">net10.0-macos</TargetFramework>
  <TargetFramework Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('Linux'))">net10.0</TargetFramework>
  <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
  <BuiltInComInteropSupport>true</BuiltInComInteropSupport>
  <AvaloniaUseCompiledBindingsByDefault>true</AvaloniaUseCompiledBindingsByDefault>
</PropertyGroup>
```

## XAML Integration

Use VisioForge Avalonia video view control:

```xml
<Window xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
        xmlns:vf="clr-namespace:VisioForge.Core.UI.Avalonia;assembly=VisioForge.Core.UI.Avalonia">
    <Grid>
        <vf:VideoView x:Name="VideoView" />
    </Grid>
</Window>
```

## Code Example

```csharp
using Avalonia.Controls;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sources;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.VideoRendering;

public partial class MainWindow : Window
{
    private MediaBlocksPipeline? _pipeline;

    public MainWindow()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private async void PlayButton_Click(object sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _pipeline = new MediaBlocksPipeline();
        var source = new UniversalSourceBlock("video.mp4");
        var renderer = new VideoRendererBlock(_pipeline, VideoView);

        _pipeline.Connect(source.VideoOutput, renderer.Input);
        await _pipeline.StartAsync();
    }
}
```

## Platform-Specific Deployment

### 1. Windows Desktop

**Build:**
```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0-windows
```

**Publish:**
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-windows -r win-x64 --self-contained
```

**Requirements:**
- Windows 10 or later
- x64 architecture

**Notes:**
- No file copying required
- Native libraries via NuGet

---

### 2. Linux Desktop

**Build:**
```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0
```

**Publish:**
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0 -r linux-x64 --self-contained
```

**Requirements:**
- GStreamer 1.0 installed: `sudo apt install gstreamer1.0-plugins-base gstreamer1.0-plugins-good gstreamer1.0-libav`

**Notes:**
- Uses system GStreamer
- No native library packages needed

---

### 3. macOS Desktop

**Build:**
```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0-macos
```

**Publish (Intel):**
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-macos -r osx-x64 --self-contained
```

**Publish (Apple Silicon):**
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-macos -r osx-arm64 --self-contained
```

**Requirements:**
- macOS 13.0+ (Ventura)

**Notes:**
- No file copying required
- Native libraries via NuGet

---

### 4. Android

**Build APK:**
```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0-android
```

**Build AAB:**
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-android -p:AndroidPackageFormat=aab
```

**Requirements:**
- Android SDK API 21+
- AndroidDependency project reference

**Permissions (AndroidManifest.xml):**
```xml
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.CAMERA" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE" />
```

**Notes:**
- **CRITICAL**: Must include AndroidDependency ProjectReference
- Runtime permissions required (API 23+)

---

### 5. iOS

**Build:**
```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0-ios
```

**Publish for Device:**
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-ios \
  /p:ArchiveOnBuild=true \
  /p:CodesignKey="Apple Development"
```

**Requirements:**
- macOS with Xcode 14+
- Apple Developer account
- Provisioning profile

**Permissions (Info.plist):**
```xml
<key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app requires camera access for video recording</string>

<key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app requires microphone access for audio recording</string>
```

**Notes:**
- Minimum iOS 13.0
- Code signing required

## Troubleshooting

- **Video not rendering**: Check VideoView is properly bound
- **Platform libs missing**: Ensure platform-specific packages are included
- **Linux rendering issues**: Install required GStreamer plugins
- **Android build failed**: Verify AndroidDependency project reference
- **iOS signing errors**: Check provisioning profile and certificate

## Next Steps

- [Windows deployment](../platforms/windows-desktop.md)
- [Linux deployment](../platforms/linux-ubuntu.md)
- [macOS deployment](../platforms/macos-desktop.md)

codeSnippets.title: Code Snippet 1
codeSnippets.code:
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <!-- Conditional TargetFramework based on build OS -->
    <TargetFramework Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('MacOS'))">net10.0-macos</TargetFramework>
    <ApplicationId Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('MacOS'))">com.yourcompany.myblazorapp</ApplicationId>
    <ServerGarbageCollection Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('MacOS'))">false</ServerGarbageCollection>
    <!-- dotnet run starts a macOS bundle through `open`, which shows no output and returns no exit code. -->
    <RunWithOpen Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('MacOS'))">false</RunWithOpen>
    <!-- Release builds osx-x64 and osx-arm64, and a web project's static web assets manifest then lands only in a per-RID folder. -->
    <RuntimeIdentifier Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('MacOS')) and '$(RuntimeIdentifier)' == ''">$(NETCoreSdkRuntimeIdentifier)</RuntimeIdentifier>
    <TargetFrameworks Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('Windows'))">net10.0-windows</TargetFrameworks>
    <TargetFramework Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('Linux'))">net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <!-- A hardcoded x64 target is wrong on Apple silicon. -->
    <PlatformTarget Condition="!$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('OSX'))">x64</PlatformTarget>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks" Version="2026.11.6" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Windows-specific packages -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('Windows'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Libav.Windows.x64.UPX" Version="2026.11.3" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- macOS-specific packages -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-macos'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.macOS" Version="2026.11.5" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Linux uses system GStreamer -->

  <!-- A macOS .app bundle holds no web files, and the bundle is the content root (see Program.cs). -->
  <Target Name="CopyWebAssetsToBundle" AfterTargets="_CreateAppBundle" BeforeTargets="_CodesignAppBundle" Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('MacOS'))">
    <ItemGroup>
      <_BundledWebAsset Include="@(StaticWebAsset)" Condition="'%(StaticWebAsset.AssetRole)' == 'Primary' and !$([System.String]::Copy('%(StaticWebAsset.Identity)').Contains('{0}'))">
        <AssetRelPath>%(StaticWebAsset.RelativePath)</AssetRelPath>
      </_BundledWebAsset>
    </ItemGroup>
    <Error Condition="'@(_BundledWebAsset)' == ''" Text="No static web assets found for the macOS app bundle." />
    <!-- Copy only, never prune: a removed asset does not trigger a re-sign, so the seal goes stale. -->
    <Copy SourceFiles="@(_BundledWebAsset)" DestinationFiles="@(_BundledWebAsset->'$(AppBundleDir)/Contents/Resources/wwwroot/$([System.String]::Copy('%(AssetRelPath)').Replace('#[.{fingerprint}]?', ''))')" SkipUnchangedFiles="true" />
  </Target>
</Project>

deploymentGuides.title: Console Cross-Platform Deployment
deploymentGuides.summary: Deploy VisioForge SDK in cross-platform console applications for servers, automation, and headless video processing.
deploymentGuides.content:
# Console Cross-Platform Deployment

## Overview

VisioForge SDK supports headless console applications for Windows, Linux, and macOS. Perfect for servers, automation, batch processing, and cloud deployments.

## Prerequisites

- **.NET 10.0 SDK** or later
- Platform-specific requirements:
  - **Linux**: GStreamer runtime installed
  - **macOS**: Xcode command-line tools

## NuGet Packages

> **Pick the wrapper package for the SDK you licensed.** The snippets below show
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks`, but this guide applies to all four: use
> `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture` for camera, screen and IP-camera recording,
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer` for playback, `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit` for
> timeline editing. Media Blocks is the low-level pipeline layer. The native
> redist packages are the same whichever you choose.

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <!-- Conditional TargetFramework based on build OS -->
    <TargetFramework Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('MacOS'))">net10.0-macos</TargetFramework>
    <TargetFrameworks Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('Windows'))">net10.0-windows</TargetFrameworks>
    <TargetFramework Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('Linux'))">net10.0</TargetFramework>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks" Version="2026.11.6" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Windows-specific packages -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('Windows'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Libav.Windows.x64.UPX" Version="2026.11.3" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- macOS-specific packages -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-macos'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.macOS" Version="2026.11.5" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Linux uses system GStreamer - no additional packages needed -->
</Project>
```

## Code Example

```csharp
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sources;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sinks;

class Program
{
    static async Task Main(string[] args)
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Starting video conversion...");

        var pipeline = new MediaBlocksPipeline();

        var source = new UniversalSourceBlock("input.mp4");
        var sink = new MP4SinkBlock("output.mp4", new H264VideoEncoderSettings());

        pipeline.Connect(source.VideoOutput, sink.VideoInput);
        pipeline.Connect(source.AudioOutput, sink.AudioInput);

        await pipeline.StartAsync();

        // Wait for completion
        await Task.Delay(-1);
    }
}
```

## Deployment

### Windows
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained
```

### Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -r linux-x64 --self-contained
```

### macOS
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -r osx-x64 --self-contained
dotnet publish -c Release -r osx-arm64 --self-contained
```

## Docker Deployment

### Dockerfile Example

```dockerfile
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/runtime:10.0-noble

# Install GStreamer
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    gstreamer1.0-tools \
    gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
    gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
    gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad \
    gstreamer1.0-libav \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app
COPY bin/Release/net10.0/linux-x64/publish/ .

ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "MyVideoApp.dll"]
```

## Platform-Specific Notes

- **Windows**: Includes native FFmpeg libraries via NuGet packages
- **Linux**: Uses system-installed GStreamer (install via apt/yum)
- **macOS**: Includes native libraries via NuGet package
- **No UI**: Console apps are headless - use file-based sinks or streaming outputs

## Use Cases

- **Batch transcoding**: Convert large video libraries
- **RTSP recording**: Capture IP camera streams to disk
- **HLS streaming**: Generate live HLS streams for CDN
- **Cloud processing**: AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, Google Cloud Run
- **CI/CD pipelines**: Automated video processing in build systems

## Troubleshooting

- **Linux GStreamer errors**: Install all required GStreamer plugin packages
- **Permission denied**: Ensure user has read/write access to input/output paths
- **Out of memory**: Limit concurrent pipelines or increase container memory
- **Codec not found**: Install additional GStreamer plugins (gstreamer1.0-plugins-ugly for some formats)

## Next Steps

- [Linux deployment](../platforms/linux-ubuntu.md)
- [macOS deployment](../platforms/macos-desktop.md)
- [Windows deployment](../platforms/windows-desktop.md)
- [Docker scenarios](../scenarios/)

deploymentGuides.summary: Deploy VisioForge SDK with .NET MAUI for cross-platform mobile and desktop applications from a single codebase.
deploymentGuides.content:
# .NET MAUI Mobile Cross-Platform Deployment

## Overview

.NET MAUI enables building native cross-platform apps with a single codebase. VisioForge SDK supports MAUI for Android, iOS, Windows, and Mac Catalyst.

## Prerequisites

- **.NET 10.0 SDK** or later
- **MAUI workload**: `dotnet workload install maui`
- **Platform-specific tools**:
  - Windows: Visual Studio 2022 with MAUI workload
  - macOS: Xcode 14+ for iOS/Mac Catalyst
  - Android: Android SDK API 21+

## NuGet Packages

> **Pick the wrapper package for the SDK you licensed.** The snippets below show
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks`, but this guide applies to all four: use
> `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture` for camera, screen and IP-camera recording,
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer` for playback, `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit` for
> timeline editing. Media Blocks is the low-level pipeline layer. The native
> redist packages are the same whichever you choose.

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFrameworks>net10.0-android;net10.0-ios;net10.0-maccatalyst</TargetFrameworks>
    <TargetFrameworks Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('windows'))">$(TargetFrameworks);net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0</TargetFrameworks>

    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <RootNamespace>MyApp</RootNamespace>
    <UseMaui>true</UseMaui>
    <SingleProject>true</SingleProject>

    <SupportedOSPlatformVersion Condition="$([MSBuild]::GetTargetFrameworkIdentifier('$(TargetFramework)')) == 'ios'">13.0</SupportedOSPlatformVersion>
    <SupportedOSPlatformVersion Condition="$([MSBuild]::GetTargetFrameworkIdentifier('$(TargetFramework)')) == 'maccatalyst'">14.0</SupportedOSPlatformVersion>
    <SupportedOSPlatformVersion Condition="$([MSBuild]::GetTargetFrameworkIdentifier('$(TargetFramework)')) == 'android'">21.0</SupportedOSPlatformVersion>
    <SupportedOSPlatformVersion Condition="$([MSBuild]::GetTargetFrameworkIdentifier('$(TargetFramework)')) == 'windows'">10.0.17763.0</SupportedOSPlatformVersion>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Maui.Controls" Version="$(MauiVersion)" />
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks" Version="2026.11.6" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Windows-specific packages -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-windows'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Libav.Windows.x64.UPX" Version="2026.11.3" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Android-specific packages -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-android'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Android" Version="2026.11.5" />
    <ProjectReference Include="..\AndroidDependency\VisioForge.Core.Android.X10.csproj" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- iOS-specific packages -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-ios'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.iOS" Version="2026.11.5" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Mac Catalyst-specific packages -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-maccatalyst'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.macCatalyst" Version="2026.11.5" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

## Critical: Mac Catalyst Native Library Copying

**Mac Catalyst requires manual copying of .dylib and .so files to MonoBundle directory.**

Add this MSBuild target to your .csproj:

```xml
<Target Name="CopyNativeLibrariesToMonoBundle" AfterTargets="Build" Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-maccatalyst'))">
  <Message Text="Copying native libraries for Mac Catalyst..." Importance="High" />
  <PropertyGroup>
    <AppBundleDir>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).app</AppBundleDir>
    <MonoBundleDir>$(AppBundleDir)/Contents/MonoBundle</MonoBundleDir>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <MakeDir Directories="$(MonoBundleDir)" Condition="!Exists('$(MonoBundleDir)')" />
  <ItemGroup>
    <_NativeLibraries Include="@(None)" Condition="'%(Extension)' == '.dylib' Or '%(Extension)' == '.so'" />
  </ItemGroup>
  <Copy SourceFiles="@(_NativeLibraries->'%(FullPath)')" DestinationFolder="$(MonoBundleDir)">
    <Output TaskParameter="CopiedFiles" ItemName="CopiedNativeFiles" />
  </Copy>
  <Message Text="Copied @(_NativeLibraries->Count()) native libraries" Importance="High" />
</Target>
```

## Permissions

### Android (Platforms/Android/AndroidManifest.xml)
```xml
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.CAMERA" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE" />
```

### iOS/Mac Catalyst (Platforms/iOS/Info.plist)
```xml
<key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app requires camera access for video recording</string>

<key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app requires microphone access for audio recording</string>
```

## XAML Integration

```xml
<ContentPage xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/dotnet/2021/maui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2009/xaml"
             x:Class="MyApp.MainPage">
    <Grid>
        <Image x:Name="VideoImage" />
    </Grid>
</ContentPage>
```

## Code Example

```csharp
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sources;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.VideoRendering;

public partial class MainPage : ContentPage
{
    private MediaBlocksPipeline? _pipeline;

    public MainPage()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private async void OnStartClicked(object sender, EventArgs e)
    {
        _pipeline = new MediaBlocksPipeline();
        var camera = new VideoCaptureDeviceSourceBlock(0);
        var renderer = new VideoRendererBlock(_pipeline, VideoImage);

        _pipeline.Connect(camera.VideoOutput, renderer.Input);
        await _pipeline.StartAsync();
    }
}
```

## Deployment

### Android
```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0-android
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-android -p:AndroidPackageFormat=aab
```

### iOS
```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0-ios
```

### Mac Catalyst
```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0-maccatalyst
```

### Windows
```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0
```

## Platform-Specific Notes

- **Android**: Requires AndroidDependency project reference for Java bindings
- **iOS**: Requires provisioning profile and code signing certificate
- **Mac Catalyst**: **CRITICAL** - Must use CopyNativeLibrariesToMonoBundle target
- **Windows**: Works like WPF/WinForms, no special requirements

## Troubleshooting

- **Mac Catalyst libs not found**: Verify CopyNativeLibrariesToMonoBundle target executed
- **Android build failed**: Ensure AndroidDependency project is included
- **iOS provisioning**: Check Apple Developer account and certificates
- **MAUI workload missing**: Run `dotnet workload install maui`

## Next Steps

- [Android deployment](../platforms/android-maui.md)
- [iOS deployment](../platforms/ios-maui.md)
- [Mac Catalyst deployment](../platforms/maccatalyst-maui.md)
- [Windows deployment](../platforms/windows-desktop.md)

deploymentGuides.title: Uno Platform Cross-Platform Deployment
deploymentGuides.summary: Deploy VisioForge SDK with Uno Platform for truly cross-platform applications targeting Windows, Android, iOS, and Mac Catalyst.
deploymentGuides.content:
# Uno Platform Cross-Platform Deployment

## Overview

Uno Platform enables single-codebase apps for Windows, Android, iOS, and Mac Catalyst. VisioForge SDK supports Uno for cross-platform video applications.

## Prerequisites

- **.NET 10.0 SDK** or later
- **Uno Platform templates**: `dotnet new install Uno.Templates`
- **Platform-specific tools**:
  - Windows: Visual Studio 2022
  - macOS: Xcode 14+
  - Android: Android SDK API 21+

## NuGet Packages

> **Pick the wrapper package for the SDK you licensed.** The snippets below show
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks`, but this guide applies to all four: use
> `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture` for camera, screen and IP-camera recording,
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer` for playback, `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit` for
> timeline editing. Media Blocks is the low-level pipeline layer. The native
> redist packages are the same whichever you choose.

```xml
<Project Sdk="Uno.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFrameworks Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('windows'))">
      net10.0-windows;net10.0-android;net10.0-ios;net10.0-maccatalyst
    </TargetFrameworks>
    <TargetFrameworks Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('OSX'))">
      net10.0-ios;net10.0-maccatalyst
    </TargetFrameworks>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks" Version="2026.11.6" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Windows-specific packages -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-windows'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Libav.Windows.x64.UPX" Version="2026.11.3" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Android-specific packages -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-android'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Android" Version="2026.11.5" />
    <ProjectReference Include="..\AndroidDependency\VisioForge.Core.Android.X10.csproj" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- iOS-specific packages -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-ios'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.iOS" Version="2026.11.5" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Mac Catalyst-specific packages -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-maccatalyst'))">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.macCatalyst" Version="2026.11.5" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

## Critical: Mac Catalyst Native Library Copying

**Mac Catalyst requires manual copying of .dylib and .so files to MonoBundle directory.**

Add this MSBuild target to your .csproj:

```xml
<Target Name="CopyNativeLibrariesToMonoBundle" AfterTargets="Build" Condition="$(TargetFramework.Contains('-maccatalyst'))">
  <Message Text="Copying native libraries for Mac Catalyst..." Importance="High" />
  <PropertyGroup>
    <AppBundleDir>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).app</AppBundleDir>
    <MonoBundleDir>$(AppBundleDir)/Contents/MonoBundle</MonoBundleDir>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <MakeDir Directories="$(MonoBundleDir)" Condition="!Exists('$(MonoBundleDir)')" />
  <ItemGroup>
    <_NativeLibraries Include="@(None)" Condition="'%(Extension)' == '.dylib' Or '%(Extension)' == '.so'" />
  </ItemGroup>
  <Copy SourceFiles="@(_NativeLibraries->'%(FullPath)')" DestinationFolder="$(MonoBundleDir)">
    <Output TaskParameter="CopiedFiles" ItemName="CopiedNativeFiles" />
  </Copy>
  <Message Text="Copied @(_NativeLibraries->Count()) native libraries to $(MonoBundleDir)" Importance="High" />
</Target>
```

## Permissions

### Android (AndroidManifest.xml)
```xml
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.CAMERA" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE" />
```

### iOS/Mac Catalyst (Info.plist)
```xml
<key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app requires camera access for video recording</string>

<key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
<string>This app requires microphone access for audio recording</string>
```

## XAML Integration

```xml
<Page x:Class="MyApp.MainPage"
      xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation"
      xmlns:vf="using:VisioForge.Core.UI.Uno">
    <Grid>
        <vf:VideoView x:Name="VideoView" />
    </Grid>
</Page>
```

## Code Example

```csharp
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sources;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.VideoRendering;

public sealed partial class MainPage : Page
{
    private MediaBlocksPipeline? _pipeline;

    public MainPage()
    {
        this.InitializeComponent();
    }

    private async void PlayButton_Click(object sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _pipeline = new MediaBlocksPipeline();
        var source = new UniversalSourceBlock("https://example.com/video.mp4");
        var renderer = new VideoRendererBlock(_pipeline, VideoView);

        _pipeline.Connect(source.VideoOutput, renderer.Input);
        await _pipeline.StartAsync();
    }
}
```

## Platform-Specific Deployment

### 1. Windows Desktop (WinUI 3)

Uno on Windows uses **WinUI 3**, not WPF/WinForms.

**Build:**
```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0-windows10.0.19041
```

**Publish (Self-Contained):**
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-windows10.0.19041 --self-contained -r win-x64
```

**MSIX Package (Microsoft Store):**
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-windows10.0.19041 -p:GenerateAppxPackageOnBuild=true
```

**Requirements:**
- Windows 10 version 1809 (build 17763) or later
- Windows App SDK via NuGet (Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK)
- x64 architecture

**Notes:**
- Output uses WinUI 3 controls, not WPF
- Native libraries included via NuGet packages
- No file copying required

---

### 2. Android

**Build APK:**
```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0-android
```

**Build AAB (Google Play):**
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-android -p:AndroidPackageFormat=aab
```

**Install to Device:**
```bash
adb install -r bin/Release/net10.0-android/com.companyname.appname-Signed.apk
```

**Requirements:**
- Android SDK API 21+
- AndroidDependency project reference (for VisioForge Java bindings)
- Permissions in AndroidManifest.xml

**Notes:**
- **CRITICAL**: Must include AndroidDependency ProjectReference
- Runtime permissions required for camera/microphone (API 23+)
- No file copying required

---

### 3. iOS

**Build for Simulator:**
```bash
dotnet build -c Debug -f net10.0-ios
```

**Build for Physical Device:**
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-ios \
  /p:ArchiveOnBuild=true \
  /p:CodesignKey="Apple Development" \
  /p:CodesignProvision="YourProvisioningProfile"
```

**TestFlight Distribution:**
1. Build with Release configuration
2. Archive with code signing
3. Upload to App Store Connect via Xcode or Transporter
4. Submit for TestFlight review
5. Distribute to testers

**Requirements:**
- macOS with Xcode 14+
- Apple Developer account ($99/year)
- Provisioning profile and code signing certificate
- Info.plist permissions (NSCameraUsageDescription, etc.)

**Notes:**
- Minimum iOS version: 13.0
- No file copying required
- Native libraries embedded in app bundle

---

### 4. Mac Catalyst

Mac Catalyst runs iOS apps natively on macOS with desktop-class features.

**Build:**
```bash
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0-maccatalyst
```

**Publish:**
```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -f net10.0-maccatalyst --self-contained
```

**⚠️ CRITICAL FILE COPYING:**
Mac Catalyst requires the `CopyNativeLibrariesToMonoBundle` MSBuild target (shown above in project configuration).

**Requirements:**
- macOS 11.0 (Big Sur) or later
- Xcode 14+
- Code signing for distribution

**Notes:**
- **ONLY platform requiring file copying**
- .dylib and .so files copied to MonoBundle automatically
- Runs as native Mac app with iOS codebase
- Supports Mac-specific features (menu bar, keyboard shortcuts)

## Troubleshooting

- **Mac Catalyst libs not found**: Verify CopyNativeLibrariesToMonoBundle target executed
- **Android build failed**: Ensure AndroidDependency project is included
- **iOS provisioning**: Check signing settings in project properties
- **Video not rendering**: Verify platform-specific packages are installed

## Next Steps

- [Windows deployment](../platforms/windows-desktop.md)
- [Android deployment](../platforms/android-maui.md)
- [iOS deployment](../platforms/ios-maui.md)
- [Mac Catalyst deployment](../platforms/maccatalyst-maui.md)

deploymentGuides.content:
# WPF .NET Core/8+ Deployment

## Overview

WPF on .NET 8+ provides modern, high-performance Windows desktop applications. VisioForge SDK fully supports WPF for video capture, playback, editing, and streaming.

## Prerequisites

- **Visual Studio 2022** or **VS Code**
- **.NET 10.0 SDK** or later
- **Windows 10** or later

## NuGet Packages

> **Pick the wrapper package for the SDK you licensed.** The snippets below show
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks`, but this guide applies to all four: use
> `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture` for camera, screen and IP-camera recording,
> `VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer` for playback, `VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit` for
> timeline editing. Media Blocks is the low-level pipeline layer. The native
> redist packages are the same whichever you choose.

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>WinExe</OutputType>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0-windows</TargetFramework>
    <UseWPF>true</UseWPF>
    <PlatformTarget>x64</PlatformTarget>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks" Version="2026.11.6" />
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Libav.Windows.x64.UPX" Version="2026.11.3" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Optional: OpenCV for computer vision features -->
  <ItemGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Release'">
    <PackageReference Include="VisioForge.CrossPlatform.OpenCV.Windows.x64" Version="2026.11.3" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

## XAML Integration

```xml
<Window x:Class="MyApp.MainWindow"
        xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation"
        xmlns:vf="clr-namespace:VisioForge.Core.UI.WPF;assembly=VisioForge.Core.UI.WPF"
        Title="Video Player" Height="600" Width="800">
    <Grid>
        <vf:VideoView x:Name="VideoView" />
        <StackPanel VerticalAlignment="Bottom" Orientation="Horizontal">
            <Button Content="Play" Click="PlayButton_Click" Margin="5" />
            <Button Content="Stop" Click="StopButton_Click" Margin="5" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Grid>
</Window>
```

## Code Example

```csharp
using System.Windows;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.Sources;
using VisioForge.Core.MediaBlocks.VideoRendering;

namespace MyApp
{
    public partial class MainWindow : Window
    {
        private MediaBlocksPipeline? _pipeline;

        public MainWindow()
        {
            InitializeComponent();
        }

        private async void PlayButton_Click(object sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        {
            _pipeline = new MediaBlocksPipeline();

            var source = new UniversalSourceBlock("video.mp4");
            var renderer = new VideoRendererBlock(_pipeline, VideoView);

            _pipeline.Connect(source.VideoOutput, renderer.Input);
            _pipeline.Connect(source.AudioOutput, renderer.AudioInput);

            await _pipeline.StartAsync();
        }

        private async void StopButton_Click(object sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        {
            if (_pipeline != null)
            {
                await _pipeline.StopAsync();
                _pipeline.Dispose();
                _pipeline = null;
            }
        }

        protected override void OnClosed(EventArgs e)
        {
            _pipeline?.Dispose();
            base.OnClosed(e);
        }
    }
}
```

## Deployment

### Self-Contained Deployment

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained -p:PublishSingleFile=true
```

Output: `bin\Release\net10.0-windows\win-x64\publish\MyApp.exe`

### Framework-Dependent Deployment

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64
```

Requires .NET 10 Runtime installed on target machine.

### MSIX Package (Windows Store)

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <GenerateAppxPackageOnBuild>true</GenerateAppxPackageOnBuild>
  <AppxPackageSigningEnabled>true</AppxPackageSigningEnabled>
</PropertyGroup>
```

## Project Configuration Notes

- **PlatformTarget**: Set to `x64` (required for VisioForge native libraries)
- **UseWPF**: Must be `true` to enable WPF support
- **OutputType**: `WinExe` for GUI applications
- **Nullable**: Recommended to enable for modern C# practices

## Migrating from .NET Framework

If migrating from WPF .NET Framework 4.x:

1. Change `TargetFramework` from `net472` to `net10.0-windows`
2. Remove `packages.config` and add PackageReference items
3. Update NuGet package versions to 2026.11.6
4. No code changes required - VisioForge API is identical

## Troubleshooting

- **Video not rendering**: Ensure VideoView control is properly bound
- **Native DLL not found**: Verify platform is set to x64, not AnyCPU
- **Codec errors**: Install VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Libav package
- **Performance issues**: Enable hardware acceleration in encoder settings

## Performance Tips

- Use GPU-accelerated rendering when available
- Enable hardware video decoding (H264, HEVC)
- Set `VideoView.RenderMode` to appropriate value for your use case
- Dispose pipelines promptly to free resources
